Authors: Chenovick C.
Title: Grace, the Spirits of the Blood, and Mystical Marriage in Aemilia Lanyer-s Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum
Abstract: Aemilia Lanyer-s relationship to the prospective patronesses of her Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum has been the subject of much scholarship. The sheer number of dedicatory verses in Salve Deus have led some to read the volume-s devotional elements as a cynical cover for worldly ambition. At the same time, scholars interested in the potential erotic bonds Lanyer depicts between women have also given the poem-s social ends primacy over its devotional discourses. This essay reevaluates these assumptions by drawing out how Lanyer persistently unifies social and spiritual grace in Salve Deus. Showing how Lanyer draws on spirit-based physiologies to describe the operations of grace in both the patronage poems and in passages on the Passion of Christ, I argue that Lanyer uses physiological beliefs about the spirits of the blood to position divine grace as an embodied force that constitutes the social bonds she creates through her poetry. Authors: Lin Y.; Hu H.; Li B.; Li H.; Zhang Y.
Title: JCF-NMF: Automatic hierarchical multi-view clustering via Joint Convex-Fused Non-negative Matrix Factorization
Abstract: Multi-view clustering has attracted considerable attention due to its ability to integrate information from multiple sources to uncover the intrinsic structure of data. Among various techniques, Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) has been widely employed in multi-view clustering due to its strong interpretability and effectiveness. However, most existing approaches adopt a two-stage paradigm — first learning a common representation and then performing clustering — which focuses mainly on representation-level alignment but fails to fully exploit the consistent cluster structures shared across views. Moreover, decoupling representation learning from clustering often leads to suboptimal performance, and the requirement of predefining the number of clusters further limits their flexibility. To address these issues, inspired by the idea of convex clustering, we propose JCF-NMF, a novel one-step, joint convex-fused NMF framework for automatic hierarchical multi-view clustering. The key innovation of our work is a joint convex fusion penalty applied to the representation matrices of all views. Specifically, an l2-norm regularization is imposed on inter-sample representation differences, which guides them to converge toward a shared cluster structure. This design enables a joint optimization of representation learning and clustering, allowing dynamically updated representations to iteratively refine clustering assignments. As the fusion penalty strength increases, representations from different views gradually merge, forming a multi-granularity hierarchical clustering structure that progresses from fine to coarse levels. This mechanism contributes to the interpretability of the model. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that JCF-NMF consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art multi-view clustering methods. © 2026

Authors: Liu S.; Yang G.
Title: Evolution of cooperation in spatial public goods games via Q-learning with random walks
Abstract: This study investigates the evolution of cooperation in spatial public goods games with overlapping local groups. Considering that learning outcomes depend not only on the update rule itself but also on the information available to learners, we introduce random walks into Q-learning to incorporate multistep spatial information, and a Random Walk Weighted Q-Learning mechanism is constructed. Secondly, under such a mechanism, we conduct numerical simulations. Simulation results indicate that the RWQ mechanism achieves higher cooperation levels than Self-Q, Direct-Q, and Global-Q, and also shows an advantage over Unweighted k-hop-Q in the low synergy region. Further analyses of social state perception and learned Q-value provide additional insight into the mechanism underlying the promotion of cooperation. Finally, we employ sensitivity analyses with respect to the state resolution, information range, random walk decay factor, exploration rate, learning rate, and discount factor, and the results further confirm the robustness of this cooperative advantage. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Cortell-Nicolau A.; Kandler A.
Title: Simulating Shape Variation in Material Culture: The Simumorph R-package
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Archaeologists have devoted a significant amount of effort to define their types, or units of analysis. However, strong disagreements persist even after years of debate. This may occur for many reasons, some intrinsic to the archaeological record itself—since different technocomplexes may involve distinct and not always comparable types—and others related to the discipline’s epistemology, where interobserver bias and differences in theoretical schools and training traditions can play a key role. As a result, most archaeological analyses, usually based on type presence/absence or type frequencies, present uncertainty levels from the start, which are not always due to the archaeological record itself, but to how we analyse that record. In this work, we adopt a materialist view to present an alternative approach where we analyse purely artefact shape without the need for previous categorisation. To do this, we resort to Geometric Morphometrics, widely used in archaeology, and we develop a simulation framework for stepwise artefactual change. We provide the software tools to do this, which have been compiled in the R-package Simumorph, and we showcase its performance in four simulated archaeological scenarios. Here, we base our simulations on the geometric microliths found during the Early and Middle Holocene in the Western Mediterranean, but the framework can be applied to any context where shape variation matters. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Ryu H.J.
Title: Analysis of retail resilience in Seoul's neighborhood commercial districts Amidst the COVID-19 shock
Abstract: This study examines the economic resilience of neighborhood commercial districts in Seoul in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Moving beyond static before–after comparisons, we employ a Panel Interrupted Time Series (Panel ITS) design to separately identify (i) the immediate level shift at the onset of the shock, conceptualized as resistance, and (ii) the subsequent change in the growth trajectory as conditions transitioned toward the endemic phase, conceptualized as recoverability. The results show that structural diversity, operationalized via Shannon's entropy, functions as a key buffering mechanism: it attenuates initial revenue losses and is associated with a steeper post-shock recovery trend. Importantly, we also document pronounced spatial heterogeneity across Seoul's five major sub-markets. Central business districts exhibit heightened exposure and larger initial downturns, while recovery trajectories vary across sub-markets. Taken together, these findings imply that urban management should complement place-based physical upgrading with ecosystem-oriented strategies—specifically, “portfolio diversification” approaches that strengthen sectoral complexity and reduce systemic vulnerability within local commercial ecosystems. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Berrada Rekhami A.; Chnigri Y.
Title: Management control systems and organizational innovation: A bibliometric analysis of the literature (1977–2026)
Abstract: Management control and organizational innovation are widely recognized as major determinants of firm performance and long-term competitiveness in contemporary business environments. Nevertheless, these two dimensions are frequently perceived as conflicting, as management control is traditionally associated with formalization, standardization, and performance monitoring, whereas innovation requires flexibility, experimentation, and organizational adaptability. This apparent tension has led several scholars to question the compatibility between management control systems and innovation processes, encouraging innovative organizations to explore new governance and coordination mechanisms. Against this backdrop, the present study aims to examine the evolution, role, and effectiveness of management control within innovation-oriented organizational contexts. To address this objective, the research adopts a bibliometric approach combined with a structured literature review in order to analyze the scientific production related to management control and innovation. The study investigates the conceptual transformations and practical reconfigurations of management control in response to contemporary organizational changes and emerging managerial challenges. Using 433 scientific articles published in the fields of economics, management, and organizational studies, the analysis identifies the main publication trends, influential authors, dominant research themes, and evolving theoretical perspectives within the literature. The findings reveal a significant and continuous growth in academic interest concerning the relationship between management control and innovation, particularly in relation to organizational agility, strategic performance, digital transformation, and dynamic capabilities. The study also highlights the progressive shift from traditional control mechanisms toward more flexible and interactive forms of management control adapted to innovation-driven environments. Furthermore, this bibliometric review contributes to ongoing debates by identifying emerging research streams and proposing future theoretical and methodological directions for scholars interested in the interaction between management control systems and organizational innovation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Chang R.; Xu Y.; Deng Y.; Zhang Y.
Title: Scope 3 emissions reporting as an instrument for accelerating sustainable aviation fuel deployment
Abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a key near-term option for aviation decarbonisation, but its large-scale deployment is constrained by high production costs. At the same time, governance mechanisms, such as ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and Scope 3 emissions reporting under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, are reshaping incentives across the aviation value chain. This study conducts a systematic literature review of Scope 3 reporting, aviation decarbonisation technologies, and sectoral governance. Based on these insights, it proposes a conceptual financing framework showing how Scope 3 reporting can enable cost-sharing business models for SAF. The framework identifies emerging practices where corporates pay the SAF premium in exchange for Scope 3 credits, airlines cover conventional fuel costs and retain Scope 1 credits, and producers gain demand certainty. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Human-Elephant Conflict and its Impact on the Social Vulnerability of Subsistence Farmers in the Chure Terai Madhesh Landscape, Nepal
Abstract: Asian elephants (Elephas maximus) mainly inhabit fragmented landscapes within their range and frequently clash with humans, rendering subsistence farmers socially vulnerable. However, the extent of this vulnerability in Nepal is not well understood. In this study, we explored the social aspects of human–elephant conflict (HEC) and its impact on subsistence farmers by interviewing 1,060 affected households in Nepal’s Chure Terai Madhesh Landscape. Data were analyzed using the Social Vulnerability Index based on the five capitals of the Sustainable Livelihood Framework. 60% of respondents perceived an increase in HEC. The most common impacts reported were crop damage (47%), property losses (38%), and human casualties (15%). Among the 19 districts studied, Bardia and Jhapa showed the highest exposure and sensitivity to HEC. Farming households faced moderate to high vulnerability to crop loss caused by elephants. Of the five livelihood capitals, physical capital was the most vulnerable, followed by financial capital; social and human capitals showed the lowest vulnerability. The greater vulnerability of financial and physical capital indicates a reduced adaptive capacity among subsistence farmers. We recommend implementing tailored mitigation strategies, such as physical barriers for protecting crops and property, improving financial support systems, and promoting community-based adaptation measures to diminish the vulnerability of affected subsistence farmers. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Al-Maliki A.J.; Ganji D.D.; Gorji-Bandpy M.
Title: CFD Investigation of Thermal and Electrical Behavior of Photovoltaic Modules Equipped with Heat Sinks and Vortex Generators
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: The Photovoltaic (PV) modules suffer performance losses at high operating temperatures, especially in hot and low-wind conditions, making effective cooling essential. This study numerically investigates a fan-assisted PV cooling duct equipped with heat sinks and vortex generators (VGs) using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The novelty of the work lies in the integrated evaluation of duct height, fin spacing, VG height, inclination angle, and attack angle within a single forced-convection framework. The model was validated against published benchmark data with deviations below 5%. The results demonstrate that the reduction of duct height from 200 mm to 100 mm can decrease the PV surface temperature by 10 °C and among all finned cases, the array with 22 fins exhibited maximum cooling whilst the best compromise between heat-transfer enhancement and pressure drop was provided by using an arrangement with 18 fins in a given area. Thermal performance improved with increasing VG height, but the 40 mm VG gave the greatest heat-transfer coefficient at the cost of relatively high-pressure loss. In the 90° case, VG orientation achieved the highest electrical efficiency at (Re = 11000), achieving an electrical efficiency of 16.9% and maximum achievable electrical power output of approximately 88 W, after accounting for DC fan power consumption, with the 90° VG configuration still showing the highest system electrical power. The 30° scenario, by contrast, resulted in the best thermal efficiency—nearly 80% and the greatest thermal power—over 420 W demonstrating practical merit in providing guidance for selecting PV cooling configurations based on specific electrical-output or thermal-recovery priorities. ©2027 The author(s). Authors: Cao Y.; Tang B.; Li C.; Dai B.; Ling J.; Li Y.; Liu X.
Title: BMHA-Net: A two-branch multiscale hierarchical attention network for depression severity estimation from facial videos
Abstract: Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that imposes a substantial public-health and socioeconomic burden, while conventional assessments based on rating scales and clinical interviews are constrained by subjectivity and limited professional resources, hindering large-scale, low-cost, and consistent assessment. Facial-video-based automated modeling provides a non-invasive alternative for depression severity estimation and has attracted increasing attention because facial dynamics may provide informative behavioral cues associated with depression. However, depression-related visual cues are often subtle, sparsely distributed, and sensitive to head pose, illumination, and inter-subject variability, while existing multi-branch attention designs may introduce additional parameter and computational overhead, making the balance between prediction accuracy and model complexity an important issue. To address these challenges, we propose BMHA-Net, a two-branch multiscale hierarchical attention network that enhances fine-grained facial cues through high-resolution local and shifted-window self-attention, captures global spatial dependencies through low-resolution global attention, and strengthens appearance–geometry complementarity via bidirectional cross-branch interaction and adaptive multi-scale fusion. Experiments on AVEC2014 demonstrate that BMHA-Net reduces MAE from 8.86 to 6.30 (28.9% relative) and RMSE from 10.86 to 8.47 (22.0% relative) compared with the official baseline. Under the same visual-only input setting, BMHA-Net achieves lower FLOPs than several recent vision-based methods with reported computational costs while maintaining competitive regression performance. Additional experiments on DAIC-WOZ further demonstrate its adaptability to pre-extracted visual descriptors under a different depression-score protocol. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Do negative emotions mediate the association between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions to involuntary musical imagery? Testing an OCD-analogue cognitive model of distressing earworms
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Purpose: Distressing involuntary musical imagery (INMI) or “earworms” are often experienced but rarely studied. Due to their similarity with obsessions, research can draw on models of obsessive-compulsive disorder. The present study followed a cognitive model and tested the hypothesis of a positive relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions, mediated by negative emotions. Methods: Individuals with OCD (n = 79) and students without OCD (n = 298) completed the Characteristics of Earworms Questionnaire (CEAR). The central hypothesis was tested using a mediation analysis. Results: The analysis revealed a significant direct effect of negative appraisals on dysfunctional reactions to INMI, but no mediation by negative emotions. Conclusions: These findings support the applicability of the cognitive OCD model to INMI, particularly the relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions. However, the results question whether negative emotions mediate this relationship. If replicated, results may provide a foundation for developing targeted interventions for distressing INMI. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Li Y.; Du H.
Title: Health-promoting effects of sky gardens in high-density cities: Evidence from subjective restorative evaluation, eye tracking, and machine learning
Abstract: Sky gardens are increasingly recognized as health-promoting potential strategies in high-density urban environments, yet how specific spatial elements contribute to restorative benefits remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the relationships between spatial composition, visual attention, and psychological restoration by integrating subjective assessments, eye-tracking data, and machine learning analysis across nine sky gardens in Singapore. The results reveal that restorative effects are primarily driven by natural landscapes, public facilities, and waterscapes, while urban landscapes and high-rise elements tend to undermine restoration. Different spatial elements exhibit distinct restorative roles: natural landscapes support both immediate visual attraction and sustained engagement, whereas waterscapes and people presence mainly enhance short-term attention, and public facilities contribute to longer-term restorative experiences. Importantly, these effects are nonlinear, with identifiable threshold ranges beyond which restorative benefits may diminish. These findings provide evidence-based insights for designing health-promoting sky gardens, emphasizing the need to balance natural landscapes, functional facilities, and visual openness to optimize restorative effects. This study deepens understanding of restorative mechanisms in vertical urban spaces and offers practical guidance for improving environmental quality in dense cities. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wang D.; Zhu L.; Duan Y.
Title: Spatio-temporal heterogeneity in the built environment-urban vibrancy nexus of rail transit station areas and its implications for targeted management: Case study of Xi’an, China
Abstract: Urban Rail Transit (URT) station areas are pivotal nodes for shaping urban structure and fostering Urban Vibrancy. However, the spatio-temporal heterogeneity of the built environment’s impact on urban vibrancy remains underexplored, as existing research predominantly relies on spatially invariant global models, which overlook how the effects of the built environment vary across geographical locations and temporal contexts. To address this gap, this study uses Xi’an Metro Line 2 in China as a case study. Employing multi-source big data, including Location-Based Service (LBS) population heatmaps and Points of Interest (POIs) at a fine-grained grid scale, we utilize a Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR) model to quantitatively deconstruct the spatially varying interactions between built environment’s variables and urban vibrancy across different time periods (morning, noon, and evening).The results first statistically confirm the significant spatial non-stationarity of the built environment’s impacts. Based on this, the study identifies three distinct vibrancy generation archetypes: (1) "endogenous service-oriented" vibrancy, driven by localized built capacity and public services; (2) "exogenous attraction-based" vibrancy, defined by city-level functional synergies and public space quality; and (3) "nodal absorption-oriented" vibrancy, characterized by the efficient absorption of commuter flows through high-density development and functional diversity.These findings empirically challenge the universal applicability of principles within Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) theory. The core contribution of this study, therefore, is its advocacy for a paradigm shift in planning-from a "prescriptive framework" that applies standardized principles to a "diagnostic framework" predicated on the precise identification of local, dominant driving mechanisms. This conclusion provides a solid scientific basis and theoretical guidance for formulating place-based and time-sensitive strategies to enhance station area vibrancy. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wei L.; Chen M.; Chen Y.; Zhang C.
Title: Fast density clustering via layered diffusion
Abstract: Density-based clustering algorithms often encounter difficulties when handling datasets with non-uniform density. To address this issue, we propose a novel clustering algorithm, termed Layered Diffusion Density Clustering (LDDC), which performs clustering through a layer-by-layer diffusion process from centroid points to high-density regions and finally to low-density regions. Specifically, LDDC first categorizes data points into centroid points, high-density points, and low-density points. It then propagates labels from centroid points to neighboring high-density points, after which the labeled high-density points continue diffusing labels to their high-density neighbors. During this process, clusters whose centroid points are connected by dense paths are merged, and label propagation continues until all high-density points have been assigned, thereby forming the cluster backbone. Subsequently, low-density points are incorporated into the corresponding clusters through outward diffusion from the cluster backbone, while the remaining low-density points are grouped together according to their neighbor relationships. Through this layered diffusion strategy, LDDC can effectively identify clusters with arbitrary shapes and non-uniform densities. Experiments on 9 synthetic and 10 real-world datasets demonstrate that, relative to the best-performing competing method for each metric, LDDC achieves average improvements of 16.84%, 13.31%, and 9.48% in ARI, NMI, and ACC, respectively, while maintaining high computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Understanding preferences for explainable AI: A study on LIME variations
Abstract: The current research aims to empirically examine user preferences of four variations of visual explanations from an image classification model. Participants ( N = 23) were recruited from a Midwestern university. The study was a within-subjects design in which participants were asked to rate four local interpretable model-agnostic explanation (LIME) variations from best to worst in an image classification task across 10 trials. A Friedman's test and a Plackett-Luce analysis were conducted to examine participants' rank-order preferences for the variations, and a linear mixed-effects model on eye-tracking data was used to examine on which variations participants expended the most visual effort. Results reveal that, overall, participants preferred images that were non-obfuscated and spent more time fixating on images that highlighted both positive and negative features compared to positive only features. The findings have implications for interface design, particularly for designers aiming to prioritize human-centered preferences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chávez É.
Title: Graft: Navigable graphs grown on spatial-approximation rootstock
Abstract: The best navigable graphs for approximate nearest-neighbor search are built serially: each inserted point searches the partially built graph, and its neighbors are selected from what that search visits — a serial dependency chain in which concurrent insertions contend for shared state and two builds of the same data differ. Graft keeps the search step and removes the mutation: the candidate-producing search needs only some navigable graph, and a much cheaper one suffices. Construction builds a rootstock — a forest of T independently seeded spatial-approximation trees, unioned into a fixed, redundant scaffold — then harvests : every point, in parallel, beam-searches the frozen scaffold with itself as the query, and the expanded vertices are occlusion-pruned into its adjacency list. Both phases are embarrassingly parallel, and the graph is bitwise identical at any thread count. A per-point stopping rule ( patience ) preserves graph quality across a 10× increase in n where a fixed search budget tuned at the smaller scale does not. The build costs 0.5%–5% of n distance computations per point; in paired repeated-build experiments at 106 points its wall-clock time is at parity with tuned Vamana on SIFT, 1.3–3.2× slower on GloVe, and 4–17× slower than the GEMM-based PiPNN. The return is measured in distance evaluations, the hardware-independent cost: at recall 0.95–0.97, Graft is within 5% of Vamana on SIFT, GloVe, and a 1024-dimensional Wikipedia benchmark (1.12× on GIST, 1.3× on Fashion, 14%–20% behind on GloVe’s 0.985–0.99 tail); 20%–22% ahead of PiPNN on GloVe; 9%–39% ahead of HNSW at 107–108 points. A degree-matched random substrate needs 4.7× more distances per query: the scaffold’s routability is necessary. The construction consumes only distance comparisons and applies unchanged to any metric. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Introducing a Conditional Support Framework: How young residents view the Olympic games
Abstract: While cost-benefit frameworks have dominated resident support research, they struggle to explain why governance quality increasingly shapes acceptance. This Research Note introduces the conditional support framework (CSF), which treats resident support as a contingent, revisable stance: granted, withheld, or withdrawn depending on perceived governance quality. Drawing on 74 semi-structured interviews and 14 focus groups (N = 146) with young residents aged 18 to 30 years in Lombardy, Italy, this study examines perceptions of the Milano–Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games. Findings reveal that support is contingent on four governance-related conditions: (a) transport readiness, (b) housing fairness, (c) sustainability credibility, and (d) local inclusion. Economic and reputational benefits were widely acknowledged, yet proved insufficient to secure endorsement when governance performance was questioned. By reframing resident support as governance-dependent rather than purely impact-driven, the CSF extends resident attitude research and offers a transferable lens for future research on tourism legitimacy. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Ren W.; Liu H.; Li L.; Li C.
Title: Research on online multi-step short-term photovoltaic power forecasting based on selective representation-driven concept drift adaptation
Abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for the secure operation and optimal scheduling of power systems. However, PV power data are highly non-stationary due to weather fluctuations, seasonal transitions, and changing operating conditions, which often cause concept drift in real-world scenarios. Most existing methods are developed in offline settings and lack the ability to adapt continuously to evolving data streams. To address this issue, this study proposes an online learning framework for multi-step short-term PV power forecasting. Specifically, a shared-parameter dual-branch Informer concept encoder is designed to capture concept discrepancies between historical and incoming data, while a mixture-of-experts adaptive parameter generator is introduced to produce targeted update parameters for different drift patterns. In addition, a selective segmentation mechanism is incorporated into the TimeBridge backbone to improve the modeling of critical temporal blocks. Experimental results on two real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best overall forecasting performance compared with benchmark methods. The proposed framework provides an effective solution for drift-aware online PV forecasting and offers practical support for enhancing the reliability, stability, and dispatch efficiency of power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Financializing the subsoil: Technical disclosure, extractive governance, and asymmetrical accountability in an emerging copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon
Abstract: This article examines how technical disclosure frameworks contribute to the financialization of mineral resources and shape forms of information disclosure within contemporary extractive governance. Focusing on the Warintza copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon, the study analyzes how geological information, investor-oriented valuation, environmental considerations, and community relations are structured within corporate disclosure practices. The research is based on qualitative documentary analysis of 18 publicly available disclosure documents produced between 2015 and 2024, including a NI 43–101 technical report, investor presentations, corporate reports, and sustainability-related documents. NI 43–101, a Canadian securities regulation designed to inform investors, structures highly detailed technical disclosures while offering only limited treatment of social and environmental dimensions. The findings show that disclosure systems prioritize geological and investor-oriented information through highly structured quantitative frameworks. Resource classification, drilling results, and corporate narratives of project potential translate geological uncertainty into investor expectations and position the deposit within global investment networks. By contrast, environmental and social dynamics are primarily represented through narrative descriptions that remain only partially integrated into investor evaluation. Rather than framing this as a problem of asymmetrical accountability, the article conceptualizes these dynamics as a condition of asymmetrical information disclosure across distinct governance domains. Different regulatory systems produce differentiated informational outputs, structuring what is disclosed, to whom, and with what level of precision. The findings also indicate that the limited disclosure of social conflict and Indigenous opposition may constitute a material gap in the representation of project-related risks within investor-oriented disclosure systems. By examining disclosure practices in an emerging mining region, the study contributes to debates on extractive governance, transparency regimes, and the financialization of natural resources. Title: VoXaaS: Safety-governed service orchestration with risk-aware volunteering for vehicular micro-edge computing
Abstract: Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) enables connected vehicles to collaboratively provide sensing and computing services beyond their primary driving functions. However, existing orchestration approaches mostly optimize Quality-of-Service (QoS) metrics and treat vehicles as generic resource providers, without explicitly considering real-time driving safety. This may result in unsafe service participation under demanding traffic or operational conditions. To address this limitation, we propose VoXaaS (Vehicle-oriented eXecution as a Service), a safety-governed vehicular micro-edge computing framework that regulates service participation according to driving risk, resource availability, and provider reliability. The framework introduces Safety-Aware Volunteering (SAV), a continuous risk-driven mechanism for regulating participation in cooperative service execution. SAV determines service eligibility, contribution type, and contribution capacity while ensuring that safety constraints remain dominant over service optimization objectives. VoXaaS further combines risk-aware provider qualification with trust- and QoS-aware orchestration to support dependable cooperative vehicular services. We evaluate the proposed framework through extensive simulations using realistic vehicular mobility traces and increasing service demand levels. Experimental results show that VoXaaS reduces selected-provider risk by more than 80% compared with QoS-based and trust-based orchestration baselines while completely eliminating unsafe volunteering. Unlike conventional safety-preserving approaches that rely on admission throttling, VoXaaS maintains full task admission under increasing service load. As a result, it achieves the highest task success rate and delivers up to 14% higher throughput than competing approaches while incurring only moderate latency overhead. The results demonstrate that explicit safety governance can significantly improve orchestration dependability while maintaining strong service performance under the evaluated service-load conditions. By tightly integrating safety-aware volunteering, elastic trust regulation, and real-time driving risk into service orchestration, VoXaaS provides a step toward dependable and safety-governed vehicular micro-edge ecosystems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Self-Health Literacy Among Students in Islamic School Science Education: A Comparative Analysis Across Gender, Grade Level, and School Context
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This study explores students’ self-health literacy within Islamic school science education by examining differences across gender, grade level, and school context. Using a cross-sectional survey approach, data were collected from junior high school students through an instrument grounded in the health literacy framework, encompassing access, understanding, processing, and application of health information. Students generally demonstrate a positive level of self-health literacy, with stronger performance in applying health knowledge compared to evaluating information critically. Relationships among all dimensions were found to be interconnected, highlighting the integrative nature of health literacy development. No significant differences emerged across gender and school context, while variations in information access were observed across grade levels. Authors: Wang Y.; Zhu L.; Wang B.; Sun J.; Liu H.; Liu C.
Title: A flexibility-oriented scheduling framework for steel enterprises: an optimization model integrating onsite flexible loads and captive power plants
Abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES), particularly wind and solar, has introduced significant variability and uncertainty to modern power systems, posing challenges for operational stability and economic dispatch. Industrial users, especially in the steel sector, are emerging as promising flexibility providers due to their high electricity consumption and growing electrification. This study proposes a source-load coordinated scheduling model for steel enterprises equipped with captive power plants (CPP), aiming to enhance system flexibility and improve renewable energy integration. Flexible operational models are developed for key energy-intensive processes-electric arc furnaces (EAF), air separation units (ASU), and rolling mills, and integrated with internal generation scheduling within a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework. The model jointly optimizes grid interaction, production-side load shifting, and captive generation dispatch to minimize total system cost and wind power curtailment. A case study based on a representative steel enterprise is conducted to evaluate the proposed approach. The results show that coordinated scheduling can effectively reduce system operating costs and improve wind power utilization. While relatively large improvements are observed when compared with an inflexible baseline, consistent performance gains are also maintained under more practical scenarios with partial flexibility. The findings indicate that coordinated control of industrial loads and captive generation can provide additional system flexibility and support renewable energy integration. The proposed framework offers a modeling perspective for analyzing the role of large industrial users in future low-carbon power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang W.
Title: Neural-network learning and identifiability for mobility-based SEAIR epidemic models
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a mobility-based SEAIR epidemic model that addresses two limitations of existing heterogeneous compartmental models: the neglect of pre-symptomatic transmission, and the absence of symptom-driven mobility reduction. Classical models assume homogeneous mixing and a single infectious stage, which ignores individual heterogeneity in contact behavior and causes systematic overestimation of outbreak size; both shortcomings were consequential during COVID-19. Each individual carries a fixed mobility trait governing their contact rate; the infectious period is split into an asymptomatic stage and a symptomatic stage with reduced mobility. We establish four main results: a closed-form basic reproduction number whose entire stage structure collapses into a single effective infectiousness parameter (with latency dropping out entirely); strict selective depletion of high-mobility susceptibles and stage-dependent differences in infected mobility distributions; a scalar final-size equation together with a unique seed-selected branch that satisfies the shielding inequality of [1]; and unique identifiability of the mobility distribution from the aggregate symptomatic time series, with a length-two Taylor delay relative to the SIR case reflecting the additional latent and asymptomatic stages. Numerical experiments illustrate the analytic results and show how pre-symptomatic transmission, isolation, and mobility heterogeneity affect synthetic epidemic trajectories. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Comparative evaluation of SRF-PLL and instantaneous-power LVRT control for a three-wire grid-connected PV system under ground faults
Abstract: The performance of low voltage ride-through (LVRT) control depends on the voltage information used for synchronisation and current-reference generation, as well as the physical current paths of the converter. In this paper, four synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL) and instantaneous power theory (IPT) implementations are compared on a common 1.504 MW photovoltaic simulation model under single line-to-ground and double line-to-ground faults. The three-wire converter is connected through a delta–grounded-wye transformer. Consequently, its zero-sequence line current is constrained to zero, although ground-fault current is present on the grounded transformer side. The current-control action is therefore confined to the two independent converter axes. The comparison uses conventional and positive-sequence-conditioned SRF and IPT implementations with a shared reactive-current-priority LVRT law, DC-voltage regulation and current-reference limits. For the double line-to-ground case, positive-sequence IPT provides 730.6 kvar at the low-voltage measurement point, compared with 376.1 kvar for instantaneous-voltage IPT, while its nonfundamental current residual decreases from 22.06% to 0.037%. However, the latter controller has a smaller 100 Hz active-power component, demonstrating a trade-off between power oscillation and current quality. Actual transient current reaches 1.234 pu despite a 1.2 pu reference ceiling. Sequence-extraction diagnostics against established DSOGI and DSC methods, together with transformer-side measurements, explain these outcomes. Title: A semantic-aware dual-stream framework for spatiotemporal trajectory-user linking
Abstract: Trajectory-User Linking (TUL) aims to associate mobility trajectories with corresponding users. Current solutions rely heavily on POI identifiers and sequential dynamics, thereby providing narrow spatiotemporal insight. This paradigm yields task-specific representations that lack commonality in human mobility patterns and cross-city transferability. In this work, we propose a Semantic-Aware Trajectory-User Linking framework with city-wise transfer learning, named SATUL. In detail, SATUL leverages pre-trained semantic encoders to embed POI category texts and develops multi-frequency sinusoidal encoding to jointly capture temporal periodicity and spatial continuity. Furthermore, SATUL establishes cross-city transferability through a dual-stream mechanism that pre-trains a shared trajectory encoder across cities via joint domain optimization. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that SATUL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with superior data efficiency, particularly in data-scarce and cold-start scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhang Q.; Li Q.; Li Z.; Gan K.
Title: From generative AI usage to entrepreneurial intention: The sequential roles of task and social self-efficacy
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is rapidly evolving and creating new possibilities for supporting students' entrepreneurial development. However, limited research has examined how GAI usage is associated with entrepreneurial intention (EI) through specific psychological pathways. Drawing on self-efficacy theory, this study examines the relationship between GAI usage and EI, focusing on the mediating roles of task and social self-efficacy. Using survey data from 521 Chinese university students, this study empirically tests the proposed model. The results show that GAI usage is positively associated with students' task and social self-efficacy. However, task self-efficacy (TSE) is not directly associated with EI. In contrast, social self-efficacy (SSE) accounts for a significant indirect association between GAI usage and EI. Moreover, a significant sequential indirect association is observed, linking GAI usage with EI through TSE and SSE. By disentangling the distinct roles of TSE and SSE, this study shows that the association between GAI usage and EI is consistent with pathways that differ in their functions and proximity to entrepreneurial action. The findings also provide practical insights for entrepreneurship education and AI-supported learning environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Short-term emission pathways in India's iron and steel sector: A hybrid framework combining quantitative methods and bottom-up modelling
Abstract: This study presents a hybrid assessment framework to quantify current greenhouse gas emissions and evaluate decarbonization pathways for India's iron and steel industry up to 2030. The framework establishes a sectoral emissions baseline and examines the impact of alternative mitigation scenarios, providing a foundation for long-term decarbonization planning beyond 2030. The industry was categorized into two segments: major integrated steel producers, representing more than 57% of national crude steel output, and other producers, comprising predominantly electric-route and small-to-medium-scale operations. Emission intensity estimates for major producers were derived from reported production and emissions data, whereas emissions from other producers were assessed using a bottom-up, process-based estimation. The study estimated the baseline emission intensity for financial year 2023–24 at 2.31 tCO₂/tcs, with major producers averaging 2.53 tCO₂/tcs and other (secondary) producers operating at a lower intensity of 2.02 tCO₂/tcs. Six scenarios were modelled through 2030, revealing that a combination of 30% scrap use and 50% renewable electricity offer the most effective short-term mitigation, reducing intensity to 1.66 tCO₂/tcs. While emissions from major producers remain largely stable, most reductions are driven by secondary producers, highlighting their greater decarbonization potential. Despite these improvements in carbon intensity, projected growth in steel production is expected to increase total sectoral emissions by approximately 20–74% by 2030, depending on the scenario considered. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Gao L.; Li S.-C.
Title: What Strategies Can Payers Use to Negotiate Medicine Prices Globally? Insights and Lessons for Low-Income Countries from a Scoping Review
Abstract: Objectives No comprehensive global review has synthesized mechanisms, strengths, limitations, and implementation challenges of pharmaceutical pricing policies. This scoping review aimed to examine global pharmaceutical pricing policies and generate policy-relevant insights, particularly for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Methods Electronic searches were conducted in Medline, CINAHL, EconLit, and Embase using predefined inclusion criteria. Gray literature was identified through government publications and World Health Organization reports, and reference lists of relevant studies were screened. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review framework and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews guidelines. Results Searches conducted up to May 2024 and updated in February 2026 identified 88 eligible studies. Reference pricing was the most commonly reported strategy, used in 85% of identified countries, offering simplicity and transparency through price benchmarking. Value-based pricing was widely adopted in high-income countries, aligning prices with health outcomes but requiring strong health technology assessment infrastructure. Managed entry agreements were reported in 56% of countries and were used to improve access to new medicines while mitigating financial risk. Indication-specific pricing was implemented in 9 countries but faced operational challenges. Compulsory licensing in several LMICs improved access to essential medicines at lower cost, although concerns regarding impacts on pharmaceutical innovation were noted. Most countries combined multiple pricing approaches to balance affordability, access, and innovation. Conclusions Although value-based pricing and managed entry agreements are common in high-income settings, simpler approaches such as reference pricing and compulsory licensing may be more feasible in LMICs. Context-specific strategies are needed to balance access, affordability, and sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Agag G.
Title: From waste to Watts: Causal evidence on AI-enabled waste-to-energy and financial performance in tourism and hospitality using an empirics-first investigation
Abstract: This study examines whether artificial intelligence enabled waste to energy adoption improves financial performance in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms and identifies the mechanisms and conditions shaping these effects. Using an empirics first mixed methods design, we combine interviews with 41 managers and a firm year panel of United Kingdom listed tourism, travel, and hospitality firms from 2015 to 2025. Difference in differences models with firm and year fixed effects show that adoption is associated with significantly higher financial performance, particularly at greater levels of adoption intensity. The findings indicate that energy cost savings and operational efficiency partially explain these gains. Performance benefits are also stronger in firms with higher baseline waste intensity and during periods of elevated energy prices. The study demonstrates that AI enabled waste to energy functions as an operational capability that can generate measurable economic value when integrated into organisational routines and governance systems. © 2026 The Author.

Title: AI-assisted analysis of creative thinking opportunities in new Chinese elementary mathematics textbooks
Abstract: Developing students’ mathematical creative thinking has become a central goal of mathematics curriculum reform worldwide. This study examines opportunities for mathematical creative thinking in the three Grade 1 Chinese mathematics textbook editions first implemented under the Compulsory Education Mathematics Curriculum Standards (2022 Edition). Drawing on the Opportunities-to-Learn framework, the study localizes Hadar and Tirosh’s (2019) analytical framework by refining the operational indicators of divergent, convergent, and lateral thinking and extending the framework through the incorporation of cognitive complexity. A human–AI collaborative coding approach was used to analyze 1,473 mathematical tasks. The findings indicate that approximately half of all textbook tasks provide opportunities for mathematical creative thinking, with convergent thinking emerging as the dominant dimension across all three editions, although each edition places emphasis on different indicators of mathematical creative thinking. This study contributes a localized analytical framework for evaluating mathematical creative thinking in curriculum materials and provides implications for textbook design, curriculum reform, and future research on mathematical creative thinking. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Guo T.; Ming B.; Liang Y.; Lu F.; Ma W.; Zhang J.
Title: Role-specific household contact patterns in urban and rural China: Implications for influenza household transmission
Abstract: Background Household contact patterns significantly influence the household transmission dynamics of respiratory pathogens. Previous studies have shown ignoring the heterogeneity of household contact patterns can lead to an underestimation of the relative susceptibility and infectivity of children to influenza. However, there is a lack of studies on household contact patterns across all age groups and family structures in China. Methods We conducted two cross-sectional studies via face-to-face, paper-based surveys in Anhua County, Hunan Province (June–July and October 2021) and Kunming City, Yunnan Province (February–April 2023). Factors associated with household contact patterns were explored using linear mixed-effects models. Role-specific contact matrices were established, stratified by household structures and crowding levels. Additionally, using influenza as a representative example, we developed a discrete-time, individual-based stochastic model to investigate household transmission dynamics initiated by different index case roles and to evaluate various role-targeted vaccination strategies. Results The mean number of household contacts reported by participants was 2.58 (95% CI, 2.50–2.66) in Anhua County and 2.26 (95% CI, 2.19–2.33) in Kunming City. Household contact patterns were mainly associated with family roles, household structures, and the number of bedrooms. Contact duration was significantly longer between father–mother pairs, between mother–child pairs in two-generation households and mother–grandchild pairs in three-generation households, and among siblings. Mothers as index cases generated the highest number of secondary cases, whereas grandfathers caused the fewest. When grandparents or parents were the index cases, transmission most frequently occurred to children or grandchildren, whereas when children or grandchildren were the index cases, infection most commonly spread among siblings. Crowded living environments increased transmission risk, leading to a higher average number of secondary cases across all index case roles. Prioritizing vaccination of children or grandchildren yielded the greatest reduction in secondary cases, with further improvement when mothers were also vaccinated. Although vaccinating grandparents had minimal impact on reducing household transmission, it remained essential for their personal protection. Notably, vaccinating both grandparents and grandchildren together was the most efficient four-dose strategy for reducing infection risk for grandparents. Conclusions Given the heterogeneity of household contact patterns, to reduce household secondary cases, priority should be given to vaccinating children or grandchildren. However, if the aim is to reduce the infection risk among grandparents, directly vaccinating them is more effective. Unlike traditional age-based vaccination strategies, our findings provide a new perspective to optimize vaccine allocation. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Further construction of 8 × 8 bijective S-boxes based on coupled Tent map and permutation particle swarm optimization algorithm
Abstract: Aiming at constructing an 8 × 8 substitution box (S-box) with strong resistance against multiple cryptanalytic attacks, this paper proposes a discrete permutation particle swarm optimization (PPSO) scheme integrating a heterogeneous initialization strategy and a local refinement mechanism. This scheme employs a two-dimensional coupled Tent chaotic map and reference anchor synchronization to construct a heterogeneous initial population, thereby achieving synergistic optimization between random search and algebraic priors. A discrete PPSO algorithm based on finite permutation sequences is designed to ensure that the evolutionary process satisfies bijective constraints. A fitness function that balances multiple cryptographic criteria is constructed to guide the search, and a local refinement strategy is incorporated to enhance the ability to direct the search toward high-performance solution neighborhoods. Experiments demonstrate that the overall cryptographic properties of the newly constructed 8×8 S-box are superior to those of similar constructions. While ensuring that the differential uniformity reaches the best known value of 4, its nonlinearity is as high as 110. The S-box not only satisfies bijectivity and achieves the optimal algebraic degree of 7, but also possesses excellent strict avalanche and bit independence properties, thus achieving a good trade-off among various cryptographic criteria. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

Authors: Mo J.; Zhao E.; Wang Z.; Ge C.; Yang H.
Title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis unravels the molecular basis of conspecific aggression in Pelodiscus sinensis
Source title: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology - Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
Abstract: Aggressive behavior is a critical issue affecting health and survival in aquaculture animals; however, the molecular mechanism of aggression in reptiles has not been fully understood. Using the Chinese softshell turtle (Pelodiscus sinensis) as a model, we established a turtle model of reactive aggression using the intruder experiment to compare aggressive and non-aggressive individuals. Integrated brain transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis revealed enrichment in glutamatergic and GABAergic pathways between aggressive and non-aggressive individuals. Aggressive individuals showed upregulated glutamate receptor genes (GRIA2, GRIA3, GRIK3) and an altered GABAergic system. Correlation networks confirmed coordinated gene-metabolite covariation in these pathways. Drug injection tests demonstrated that NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801 significantly reduced attacks, indicating that glutamatergic signaling is a primary driver of aggressive behavior. These findings highlight conserved excitatory mechanisms in vertebrate aggression with reptile-specific characteristics and offer targets for low aggressiveness breeding in aquaculture. © 2026

Authors: Lu J.; Chen X.; Aziz M.; Yu Y.; Zhang C.; Huang Z.; Chen F.
Title: Architected NiTi alloys with elastically dominated regions for efficient and stable elastocaloric cooling
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Elastocaloric cooling based on stress-induced martensitic transformation (SIMT) in NiTi alloys shows great potential for low-carbon thermal management, but the functional performance–cyclic stability trade-off remains unresolved. Here, an integrated strategy of macro–microstructure fabrication is proposed to mitigate this trade-off by architecting the NiTi alloy into elastically dominated buffering regions and phase-transforming regions. In situ experiments confirm that the designed structure spatially distributes stress and temperature. Microscopic analysis further reveals that preferential longitudinal-direction martensite growth and regular secondary twins can effectively suppress plastic damage accumulation and improve reversibility. As a result, the NiTi structure exhibits significant elastocaloric performance, with a stable coefficient of performance of ∼18.7, a mechanical loss factor (ζloss) of ∼0.11 over 103 cycles, and a first recovery strain of 7.3%. This study demonstrates that macroscopic structural programming can improve elastocaloric functional performance by regulating local stress distribution and transformation behavior, offering a new approach to solid-state cooling materials beyond micro-control material optimization. © 2026

Authors: Hutson S.R.
Title: Uncorrelated Inequalities: A Multiproxy Measure for Household Archaeology
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Inequality has received increased attention in the social sciences since the 1990s, in part because of the harm it causes and because massive inequality is avoidable. Bolstered by the Gini coefficient, a quantitative measure of unevenness in a distribution that enhances comparative studies across time and space, archaeologists have expanded the study of inequality in recent years. Many of these investigations use multiple variables to assess inequality. A challenge of such multi-proxy studies is that simply averaging Gini coefficients for multiple variables can over-represent inequality in societies where variables for inequality are not correlated. This paper provides an experimental measure—the Domain Sensitivity Gini (DSG)—and applies it to a sample of Maya archaeological case studies with extensive domestic excavations. The DSG helps disambiguate societies where wealth variables are aligned from societies where such variables are not aligned. In cases where variables do not align, different forms of wealth are not strongly correlated: a household that is poor in one domain might be wealthy in other domains. The DSG also suggests that inequality is lower than estimates based on averaged variables. This finding is valuable when set within a broader comparative context because it shows that high inequality seen today is not natural and that ancient case studies are relevant. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Iqbal M.
Title: Critical minerals and the U.S. industrial strategy: resource security, environmental justice, and the contradictions of decarbonization
Abstract: The United States has rapidly implemented a critical minerals industrial policy to support the clean energy transition and to advance national and economic security, using the Inflation Reduction Act, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and Defense Production Act to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce reliance on China. This review examines whether this strategy represents decarbonization, a new phase of green industrial policy, green extractivism, a geopolitical resource-security approach, or a contradictory project that advances climate goals while perpetuating inequalities. Drawing on 65 peer-reviewed articles, books, and policy reports, the Critical Minerals Justice Dilemma framework clarifies persistent tensions among decarbonization, supply security, industrial competitiveness, environmental justice, and geopolitical resilience. Evidence from Indigenous sovereignty research, conflict mapping in the Americas, and political economy analysis shows that U.S. policy accelerates green extractivism, overrides Tribal consent through crisis-driven measures, uses techno-legal solutions that undermine democratic governance, and shifts environmental and social burdens to Global South sacrifice zones. The analysis identifies three main gaps: limited theorization of racial capitalism and settler colonialism in domestic contexts, insufficient attention to epistemic justice, and a lack of demand-side political economy. The findings suggest techno-optimistic views on green transitions do not address structural inequalities. Achieving a just strategy requires prioritizing Free, Prior, and Informed Consent, Indigenous co-governance, and demand reduction as central political imperatives rather than technical solutions. Decarbonization within racial capitalism continues to reproduce extractivist inequalities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Exploring the key drivers of biogas adoption: a business model for livestock farmers in developing countries
Abstract: The increasing number of livestock farms, coupled with inadequate waste management infrastructure, has become a growing concern, contributing to environmental pollution and productivity loss. Biogas technology presents a viable solution to address these challenges by transforming waste into a sustainable energy source. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the key factors influencing the adoption intention of biogas technology as a business Model among livestock farmers. Employing a purposive sampling approach, this study gathered data from 336 livestock farmers. To ensure a comprehensive analysis, a combined methodological framework integrating both symmetric and asymmetric techniques was utilized, providing a profound understanding of the determinants impacting the intention to adopt biogas technology. This study observes a notable consistency between the findings derived from PLS-SEM and ANN. The analysis indicates that awareness of consequences (AOC) significantly influences ascription of responsibility (AOR). Additionally, findings indicate that personal norms are significantly shaped by herd mentality, initial cost, AOC, AOR, and self-esteem. Furthermore, herd mentality, personal norms, and self-esteem are significantly associated with biogas adoption. However, no significant association was found between perceived ease of use and personal norms. Meanwhile, findings from the fsQCA revealed eight distinct pathways leading to a strong intention to adopt biogas, highlighting herd mentality and AOC as critical prerequisites. Insights gained from this study will be instrumental for stakeholders involved in shaping policies, making investments, and providing technological assistance for the effective installation and operation of biogas technology. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Guo X.; Ta R.; Li X.; Peng C.; Hu W.
Title: Associations between teaching approaches, epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice: A study across different metacognitive levels
Abstract: This study utilized survey data from 1,257 Chinese eighth-grade students to examine the associations among teaching approaches (i.e., inquiry-based teaching and teacher-directed instruction), epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice. Crucially, these relational patterns were analyzed within different levels of metacognitive ability (high, medium, and low). Specifically, the present study employed multi-group structural equation modeling to examine group-specific patterns of associations among variables across students with different levels of metacognitive ability. Results indicated that positive associations between inquiry-based teaching and the examined variables were mainly observed within the high-metacognitive group, whereas teacher-directed instruction demonstrated positive associations with certain variables across groups. In addition, indirect associations involving utility value in the relationship between teaching approaches and science-related career choice were identified in the high-metacognitive group, while comparable patterns were not observed in the other groups. These findings suggest that the association patterns involving teaching approaches, epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice may differ across metacognitive groups. Authors: Xue Y.; Chen D.
Title: A multi-scale modeling approach for infectious disease: Integrating within-host dynamics to network-based transmission
Abstract: Infectious disease transmission is shaped by tightly coupled biological processes within hosts and social contact patterns between hosts, making cross-scale modeling essential for understanding epidemic dynamics. We develop a data-driven multiscale framework that links within-host viral kinetics to between-host transmission on a dynamic multilayer contact network. Using influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and SARS-CoV as representative pathogens, we infer infection-age-dependent infectiousness from longitudinal viral-load data and integrate the resulting profiles into a stochastic individual-based model with contact layers constructed from empirical demographic and contact data. By comparing infectiousness profiles within the same multilayer transmission framework, we show that epidemic trajectories depend not only on overall transmission potential but also on the timing and duration of infectiousness. Early, concentrated infectiousness produces earlier epidemic peaks and shorter outbreaks, whereas later or prolonged infectiousness delays and extends transmission. Layer-resolved analyses show that setting-specific contributions arise from interactions among contact volume, contact intensity, and infectiousness profiles. Intervention simulations highlight the importance of temporal alignment: case isolation and vaccination are most effective when implemented before or during the pathogen-specific period of high infectiousness, whereas physical distancing reduces epidemic burden by lowering contact opportunities. This framework provides a flexible approach for linking viral-load-derived infectiousness with network-mediated transmission and evaluating targeted epidemic control strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Salimi Aghbolagh N.; Huang H.
Title: Dual-cycle mechanism of project-based learning in engineering soft skills development
Abstract: Given the relatively limited resource conditions and institutional environment of local universities (LUs), how to construct a practical and realistic project-based learning (PBL) implementation framework still requires systematic exploration. This study constructs and verifies a dual-cycle PBL model that integrates institutional context analysis (external cycle) with continuous feedback and reflection (internal cycle). A quasi-experimental sequential mixed-methods design was used. 93 sophomore Chemical Engineering and Technology(CET) students at Chongqing H University were assigned to an experimental group (n=48) and a control group (n=45). The experimental group received a 6-month intervention, using the proposed structured dual-cycle PBL framework. The control group received traditional lecture-based course teaching, with the same project tasks and overall assessment structure. Results showed: (1) The experimental group demonstrated extremely significant improvement in overall soft skills (pre-test M=3.64, post-test M=4.34, Δ =0.70, p<0.001), while the control group showed only a negligible natural growth (Δ≈0.17, p>0.05); (2) Repeated measures analysis of variance confirmed that there were extremely significant Group × Time interaction effects in all four soft skill dimensions (all p<0.001, partial η^2=0.338-0.483, with large effect sizes), which proved that the improvement in skills was associated with PBL intervention measures rather than time factors; (3) Creativity and collaboration skills showed the most significant improvement; (4) Qualitative data indicated that the dual-cycle framework was highly consistent with the application-oriented talent cultivation orientation of the learning unit, and maintained structural stability even under limited resource conditions. The results show that the dual-cycle PBL significantly enhances overall soft skills, with creativity and collaboration improving the most. The proposed dual-cycle framework provides a context-adaptive, structurally stable implementation path for engineering education in LUs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Power quality performance assessment of stand-alone minigrids in Kenya
Abstract: Global rural electrification initiatives have accelerated the deployment of renewable energy-based minigrids. However, their performance is highly susceptible to weather dynamics, which adversely affect power quality and service delivery. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of power quality in autonomous minigrids. The assessment was conducted on eleven autonomous minigrids in remote regions of Kenya. Structured questionnaires were administered across all sites, while detailed power quality logging was performed at six selected sites using a Fluke 1777 power quality analyzer for one week per site. Novel integrated fuzzy framework was developed using Weighted Sum Method (WSM), Fuzzy AHP, and AHP + CRITIC to compare overall minigrid performance. Robustness of the final ranking was tested via one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis (±20% weight perturbation) and Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations, 95% CI). Results revealed significant variations, the highest average power factor was recorded at Ndeda Island (0.89), while Illaut (0.61) and Remba Island (0.51) exhibited very poor power factors. Frequency variations at Locheromoit (0.52), Ndeda (0.59), and Remba (1.2) exceeded EN 50160:2010 and IEEE 519-2022 thresholds. Substantial prolonged interruptions were observed at Hadado (1.2 hrs/week) and Illaut (2.59 hrs/week). Unlike Wasini that achieved the highest FTPQI (0.93), Illaut registered the lowest FTPQI (0.29). Wasini and Illaut demonstrated 100% rank stability under ±20% perturbation. Spearman correlations between WSM vs. AHP+CRITIC and FAHP vs. AHP+CRITIC were 0.89 and 0.94, respectively. The findings demonstrate that fuzzy power quality indices are critical for diagnosing specific failures, particularly poor power factor, frequency instability, and prolonged interruptions in autonomous minigrids. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Disparity Considerations in an Alternative Eligibility Criterion for Medicare Medication Therapy Management Programs With Machine Learning
Abstract: Objectives Current eligibility criteria for Medicare Medication Therapy Management (MTM) programs may disadvantage racial and ethnic minorities. As health plans increasingly apply predictive modeling to guide MTM eligibility, these tools risk perpetuating existing disparities. This study examined whether hospitalization and emergency room (ER) costs could serve as an alternative eligibility criterion to improve minority representation in MTM enrollment and whether machine learning models reflect racial and ethnic differences. Methods A 10% random sample of fee-for-service Medicare beneficiaries in 2019 was analyzed. The outcome was inclusion in the top quartile of hospitalization and ER costs. Racial and ethnic differences were assessed using a multivariable logistic regression. Five machine learning algorithms (regularized logistic regression, support vector machines, neural networks, random forest, and gradient boosting trees) were developed, with their predictions combined in a consensus model. A multivariable fractional logistic regression was used to test whether predicted probabilities reproduced observed racial and ethnic differences. Results The analytic sample included 1 848 654 beneficiaries. Black beneficiaries were significantly more likely than non-Hispanic White (White) beneficiaries to be in the top cost quartile (odds ratio [OR] = 1.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.07-1.12), whereas Asian (OR = 0.66, 95% CI = 0.63-0.69) and Other racial groups (OR = 0.87, 95% CI = 0.85-0.89) were less likely. No significant Hispanic-White difference was observed. Machine learning models largely reproduced these patterns. Conclusions Hospitalization and ER costs represent a potential alternative MTM eligibility criterion that may enhance inclusion of Black beneficiaries but underrepresent other minority groups. This study highlights the importance of equity-focused design in predictive tools. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Li Z.; Ma M.; Yavuz M.
Title: Reservation-based intersection scheduling using dynamic programming with dominance pruning
Abstract: Scheduling connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) at reservation-based intersections faces a fundamental trade-off: existing methods sacrifice either optimality for computational efficiency or real-time applicability for optimal solutions. We bridge this gap by proposing a dynamic programming (DP) algorithm with dominance pruning ((Formula presented.)) that simultaneously achieves optimal batch formation, polynomial-time complexity, and superior solution quality. (Formula presented.) introduces a novel dominance rule that eliminates suboptimal child nodes by comparing analytically derived lower bounds, enabling batch-based processing of CAVs while guaranteeing optimality. Unlike existing approaches that assume predetermined batches or sacrifice optimality, (Formula presented.) integrates optimal batching decisions directly into the scheduling algorithm. The proposed method achieves a substantial improvement over existing exact algorithms with (Formula presented.) worst-case and (Formula presented.) best-case time complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that (Formula presented.) reduces computation time by 91% and 99% compared to a state-of-the-art DP algorithm and Gurobi solver, respectively, while consistently delivering superior performance in makespan, average delay, and maximum delay metrics across diverse traffic scenarios. Furthermore, (Formula presented.) outperforms heuristic algorithms in achieving better solution quality and comparative computational efficiency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that (Formula presented.) ’s dominance rule remains effective across varying mean headways, CAV counts, and batch proportions, with performance benefits extending beyond simple batch processing to complex traffic patterns. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: Navigating travel paradoxes: Gen Z coping responses and implications for destination management
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Paradoxes involve contradictory yet interdependent poles that persist rather than disappearing when one side is chosen. Tourism routinely exposes travelers to such tensions, but traveler-level paradoxes and the responses used to navigate them remain underexamined. Using the early tourism-recovery period of 2022 as the empirical context, this study examines paradoxical tensions perceived by young adult Gen Z student travelers and how they respond to them. A two-stage qualitative design was employed. Study A recruited 98 Norwegian Gen Z student travelers, of whom 95 provided useable responses; Study B recruited 48 Gen Z student travelers from the United Kingdom and the United States, of whom 46 provided useable responses. Online open-ended essays were analyzed using thematic analysis, with constant comparison used as an iterative coding technique. Four persistent traveler-perceived tensions emerged: personal travel fulfillment versus environmental responsibility, community economic benefit versus community livability, business recovery versus service-capacity strain, and travel maximization versus travel restraint. Responses clustered into four types: integrative or balancing, prioritization, avoidance or resignation, and externalization or delegation. These responses did not permanently resolve the paradoxes; instead, they temporarily stabilized the tension, privileged one pole, reproduced it, or displaced responsibility. The study therefore positions the 2022 recovery period as an external intensifying condition that made enduring tensions especially visible and connects traveler paradox management to destination governance and shared responsibility. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Abbasi S.; Jalilian A.
Title: A robust energy management model for unbalanced microgrids under electricity price uncertainty considering central inverters and demand response for voltage unbalance mitigation
Abstract: The increasing penetration of unbalanced loads, such as single-phase electric vehicles, in microgrids (MGs) can lead to significant Power Quality (PQ) issues, requiring demand response and ancillary services for mitigation. In this regard, an energy management model for renewable energy resources (RES) and energy storage (ES)-based buses is proposed, in which central inverters are used to support PQ and coordinate energy trading. An unbalanced IEEE 13-bus test system is used to evaluate the proposed framework, with particular emphasis on voltage unbalance mitigation and energy management. The results show that the proposed strategy reduces the voltage unbalance Indicator (VUI) from approximately 4% to below the 2%, with only a 0.35% increase in operating cost. In addition, a robust optimization approach is employed to address electricity price uncertainty, and Monte Carlo simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework under uncertain operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
