Authors: Xu X.; Jiang G.; Huang X.; Chen Q.; Tian Y.; Wen N.
Title: GenAI support to the rescue: Mitigating employees’ psychological stress following tourism service recovery
Abstract: Growing evidence suggests that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has a notable impact on employees' attitudes and behaviors, yet its potential to mitigate psychological stress remains underexplored. Combining conservation of resources (COR) theory with the “computers are social actors” (CASA) paradigm, this study investigates whether and how GenAI support (emotional versus informational) reduces tourism employees' post-recovery psychological stress. The results show that: (1) GenAI support effectively alleviates such stress following tourism service recovery; (2) emotional (vs. informational) support exerts a stronger stress-alleviating effect, which is serially mediated by social presence and emotional energy; (3) framing GenAI as an assistant (vs. a friend) further amplifies the relative effectiveness of emotional over informational support. This study enriches the understanding of GenAI's benefits and extends the workplace support literature. It also offers actionable insights into leveraging digital support tools to manage employee stress in tourism workplaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Direct Technology Diffusion in Higher Education: Evidence from Doctoral Students
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This study compares direct and indirect technology diffusion in higher education, focusing on plagiarism detection software in Indian doctoral education. Using a quantitative survey of research scholars, the study finds that direct diffusion significantly improves outcomes. Similarity levels decreased substantially under direct diffusion, indicating more accurate application of plagiarism rules. Additionally, direct diffusion reduced the time required and lowered costs considerably. The findings suggest that direct access empowers users, minimizes intermediary-related inefficiencies, and enhances both effectiveness and efficiency. Authors: Zhou W.; Kim Y.
Title: Long-term impact of ChatGPT-4 on music students' creative and analytical skills: A follow-up study
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative AI into education has raised important questions about its long-term influence on higher-order thinking. Building on our earlier study that examined the one-off impact of ChatGPT-4, the present follow-up study investigated its sustained effects on music students’ creative and analytical skills. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 74 undergraduate music students assigned to an experimental group ( n = 36) and a control group ( n = 38). Across a 24-week intervention, creativity and analytical skills were assessed at 12 repeated measurement points. Data were analyzed using latent growth modeling, multivariate analysis of covariance, cross-lagged panel modeling, epistemic network analysis, and a first-order Markov chain model. Results indicated that the experimental group began with higher initial levels and demonstrated steeper growth trajectories, reflecting a Matthew effect, while the control group displayed compensatory tendencies. Cross-lagged analyses revealed that analytical reasoning strongly predicted subsequent creativity in the experimental group, and network analysis confirmed stable co-occurrences between creative and analytical moves. Transition modeling further showed recursive cycles of idea generation, revision, evaluation, and structural reasoning. These findings suggest that ChatGPT-4 fosters an integrated interplay of creativity and analysis, offering music educators worldwide practical strategies for designing AI-mediated learning that balances innovation with critical rigor. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Huang T.; Wang W.
Title: Assessment innovation in management education: Authentic assessment evaluation to develop workplace-ready graduates
Abstract: Authentic assessment is increasingly seen as essential in management education for aligning assessment tasks with the complex, collaborative, and uncertain, multi-stakeholder demands of modern workplaces. This paper argues that, despite its popularity, the impact of authentic assessment on graduate preparedness remains poorly understood. To address this, the paper builds and evaluates an integrative model relating authentic assessment design, feedback and reflection, perceptions of assessment value, professional self-efficacy, and perceived workplace outcomes among management students. Drawing on literature about authentic assessment, experiential learning, situated cognition, assessment for learning, and employability, the paper frames authentic assessment as a holistic pedagogical system. A cross-sectional survey of 412 undergraduate and postgraduate students in business and management at four universities provides the empirical basis. The instrument was honed through expert review and a pilot test, and analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and validity checks, correlations, and hierarchical regression and mediation tests. The findings show that authentic assessment design strongly correlates with workplace readiness, especially when dialogic feedback, reflection, and professional self-efficacy are present. External audience group projects, live case analysis, simulations, and portfolio-based evaluation proved effective with clear criteria and guided post-task reflection. The paper contributes a process model and actionable design principles for educators to enhance employability through meaningful assessment, advancing the discourse on management education. © 2026

Title: Exploring the Inherent Affordability for Movement in Past Landscapes
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: The aim of this paper is to demonstrate a method for exploring the conditions inherent to mobility within a landscape, as a means of broadening our understanding of the role of human movement in archaeology. Specifically, it is based on the application of a tool, Omniscape, developed in the field of ecology, which to date has barely been utilised in archaeology. As we shall attempt to demonstrate, it holds great potential to overcome some of the common limitations in the digital modelling of mobility in archaeology. After briefly reviewing these limitations, we outline the operating principles of Omniscape and illustrate the type of results it produces using three ideal control surfaces. Finally, an archaeological case study regarding the distribution of burial mounds in an area of NW Iberia is presented, to illustrate possible ways of utilising the results for tackling specific archaeological questions. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Li Z.; Li F.S.
Title: Time for challenge, money for relaxation: The resource-activity fit in tourism
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Although money and time are essential resources that influence consumer decision-making, research has mostly ignored how resource concept activation affects tourists' decisions in the context of tourism. Drawing on mental simulation theory, this study investigates how activating time versus money resource concepts influences tourists' preferences for different types of tourism activities. Across three experiments, the results show that when the concept of time is activated, tourists report stronger preferences for challenging activities, whereas when the concept of money is activated, they report stronger preferences for relaxing activities. Outcome-focused simulation mediates the relationship between time activation and challenging activity preference, whereas process-focused simulation mediates the relationship between money activation and relaxing activity preference. These indirect pathways are further conditioned by maximization: the time-related pathway becomes stronger as maximization increases, whereas the money-related pathway becomes weaker. The results offer practical implications for tourism destinations that can tailor marketing strategies based on tourists’ decision-making tendencies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Blast Furnace Slag as an Alternative to Natural Mineral Materials in Pavement Engineering: A Review; [Доменный шлак как альтернатива природным минеральным материалам в дорожном строительстве: обзор]; [Жол құрылысында табиғи минералдық материалдарға балама ретіндегі домна қожы: шолу]
Abstract: The presented literature review contains the results of the analysis of scientific articles for 2000-2026 years, considering the use of blast furnace slag in various areas of road construction. It has been established that there are clear differences between the application options for different types of blast furnace slag. Air-cooled blast furnace slag (ACBFS) is more often used as a coarse or fine aggregate for cement concrete and asphalt concrete, and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) is used as an additional binder or as a mineral/reactive filler. When using blast furnace slag in the production of concrete, the highest results in a number of studies were achieved when replacing 20-40% of the aggregate with slag, although this indicator was not a universal optimal value. In some articles, it was pointed out that the use of blast furnace slag as part of the base of a highway or for soil stabilization was associated with an increase in CBR. Some authors point to a reduction in the consumption of Portland cement when using complex binders containing granular blast furnace slag. Data on the improvement of water resistance, fatigue resistance, Marshall stability, and rutting resistance of asphalt concrete with the introduction of ACBFS and GGBFS in various proportions are also presented. Pretreatment of porous ACBFS was also important: selective crushing and related separation methods reduced water absorption, crushing value, and the proportion of weak porous particles. The main practical conclusion is that BFS should not be treated as a single interchangeable material. Its use should be selected according to slag type, particle quality, the component being replaced, and the required pavement property. Further studies should examine whether improvements achieved by slag pretreatment at the aggregate level are retained in concrete, asphalt mixtures, and pavement-base materials under long-term service conditions. © 2026, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. Title: Low-Temperature All-Solid-State Batteries
Abstract: Reliable battery operation in sub-zero environments is critical for polar exploration, military missions, and space applications. However, conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face inherent limitations at low temperatures by intrinsic hurdle of poor ionic mobility in liquid electrolytes. All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), which replace liquid electrolytes with non-flammable and non-freezing solid electrolytes, are considered promising alternatives because these solid electrolytes provide high ionic conductivity at low temperatures, superior temperature stability, and exceptional safety. ASSBs still face practical limitations at extremely low temperatures due to degradation caused by interfacial side reactions and mechanical instabilities that increase resistance and polarization. Addressing these challenges is critical to realize the advantages of ASSBs and enable their practical deployment in low-temperature applications. This review provides an overview of historical developments, critical challenges, and recent progress in advancing the low-temperature performance of ASSBs. The key components of ASSBs, including solid electrolytes, cathodes, and anodes, are systematically investigated to develop strategies for improving ASSBs at low temperatures. By highlighting future perspectives, we emphasize both the potential and necessity of ASSBs to overcome the intrinsic limitations of LIBs and ensure reliable energy storage in harsh environments. Title: Solvent-ion synergistic engineering of hierarchical hydrogels for multifunctional all-weather ionic skins
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Resolving the intrinsic conflict among optical transparency, mechanical robustness, environmental adaptability, and conductivity remains a formidable challenge for hydrogel-based ionotronics. Herein, a novel “Solvent-Ion Synergistic Engineering” strategy is proposed to construct a hierarchical triple-network hydrogel (GAAE-Zr) that successfully overcomes these trade-offs. The design integrates a covalently crosslinked poly(acrylamide-co-2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid elastic backbone, dynamic Zr4+ coordination bonds for toughening without coloration, and an ethylene glycol/water binary solvent system for anti-freezing and anti-dehydration. Through this architecture, the resulting hydrogel exhibits exceptional toughness (elongation > 1500%, tensile strength 286 kPa) and broad-spectrum adhesion, while maintaining glass-like transparency (> 90%). Simultaneously, the reconfigured hydrogen-bonding network significantly depresses the freezing point to −49.5 °C and locks in moisture for long-term stability. Leveraging these merits, the GAAE-Zr hydrogel is demonstrated as a high-fidelity strain sensor with stable conductivity (up to 0.74 S/m) for thermally stable wireless human-machine interaction, and is further implemented as a fully encapsulated triboelectric nanogenerator delivering an instantaneous power density of 220 mW m−2. This work establishes a versatile material platform and a new design paradigm for next-generation wearable electronics requiring multifunctional integration and all-weather operational reliability. © 2026

Authors: Muthia A.; Utari D.; Soesilo T.E.B.
Title: Environmental health conditions associated with childhood stunting during the first 1000 days of life
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Child stunting is increasingly recognized not only as a nutritional disorder but also as a complex environmental health issue. Household environmental determinants, particularly safe potable water and advanced sanitation infrastructure, exert a fundamental influence on minimizing children's susceptibility to environmental health hazards that compromise linear growth trajectories. Using the transtheoretical model as a behavioral framework, the study objectives were to examine how household environmental conditions, including access to improved drinking water and sanitation, together with maternal environmental health-related behaviors, are associated with child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life in Indonesia. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the fifth wave of the Indonesian Family Life Survey. Maternal behaviors related to nutrition, healthcare utilization, and environmental conditions were operationalized as proxies for advanced stages of behavioral change. Child stunting was defined using height-for-age z-scores based on the World Health Organization Child Growth Standards. A binary logistic regression model was utilized to evaluate the multivariate associations linking maternal behavioral patterns, socio-environmental covariates, and socio-demographic indicators to the latent risk of linear growth retardation in children. FINDINGS: The prevalence of stunting among children aged 0 to 23 months was 30.32 percent. Low birth weight and higher birth order significantly increased the odds of stunting. Maternal behaviors reflecting progression to the action and maintenance stages were protective, including routine antenatal care attendance, with an odds ratio of 0.642, and delivery assisted by a skilled birth attendant, with an odds ratio of 0.707. Findings indicate that higher maternal educational attainment, improved sanitation facilities, and safe drinking water sources significantly decreased the likelihood of stunting. In contrast, maternal under nutrition elevated the associated risk by 26.5 percent. CONCLUSION: Household environmental conditions constitute fundamental determinants of child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. Maternal progression toward advanced stages of stunting prevention behavior, reinforced by adequate health services and enabling environments, plays a critical role in reducing stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. The findings underscore the efficacy of the transtheoretical model as a robust conceptual paradigm for mitigating childhood stunting. By integrating maternal behavioral stages of change with healthcare access and environmental determinants, the research delineates a nuanced, stage-sensitive and contextually grounded architecture for analyzing early childhood growth dynamics. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Prioritizing resilience criteria and indicators in urban disadvantaged areas using the Best-Worst Method (BWM)
Abstract: Urban disadvantaged areas are highly vulnerable to natural hazards due to physical, social, economic, and institutional deficiencies. These areas-such as historic residential area, decayed residential areas, informal settlements, and social housing-experience distinct challenges that necessitate tailored resilience strategies. Considering Iran's high hazard proneness, strengthening resilience in such areas is an urgent priority. Existing resilience literature often adopts a generalized, city-wide perspective, lacking the granularity for effective local-level resource allocation in diverse disadvantaged areas. This study aims to identify and prioritize resilience criteria and indicators across the four types of disadvantaged areas. A comprehensive literature review extracted potential resilience criteria, refined and validated using the Delphi method with 16 experts engaged via snowball sampling. The Best-Worst Method (BWM), an MCDM approach, weighted and ranked criteria for each area type. Results show economic capacity is most critical in informal settlements. Physical-environmental aspects (building quality, infrastructure) dominate historical and decayed areas. Institutional dimensions (governance, accountability, policy support) are most influential in social housing resilience. Cross-area comparison reveals shared and context-specific determinants, underscoring the need for integrated, area-sensitive resilience planning. Findings offer a framework for urban planners to prioritize targeted interventions, balancing physical upgrades with social empowerment, economic capacity building, and institutional strengthening for sustainable and inclusive resilience. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Solar Photovoltaic Adoption in East Java Non-Profit Organizations
Abstract: Non-profit organizations in East Java need dependable electricity for service continuity, daily operations, and cost control, yet face capital, regulatory, behavioral, and tropical-climate barriers to rooftop solar photovoltaic adoption. This study combines a focused literature review, bibliometric mapping of 25 verified domain studies selected from 79 unique Scopus records, a random-effects synthesis of five Global Solar Atlas locations, and a 50,000-iteration Monte Carlo model for a common 12 kWp system. The 25 studies met predefined adoption, finance/policy, governance/behavior, and tropical-performance criteria and passed metadata verification. Modeled annual output ranges from 17.231 to 18.227 MWh; pooled yield is 4.03 kWh/kWp/day (95% CI: 3.92–4.14). Median NPV is IDR 40.7–54.9 million, with a conditional positive-NPV probability of 86.4–92.5%. Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate, tariff escalation, capital cost, avoided electricity value, and self-consumption as the dominant drivers of NPV. The five-city results are screening evidence, not a representation of all tropical climates or roofs. A 30% grant or blended-finance contribution raises positive-NPV probability above 99.8% and reduces median payback to 5.8–6.2 years. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. All rights reserved.

Authors: Sun M.; Lu G.; Huang Z.; Quan S.; Zhang Y.; Tan Y.
Title: Hybrid scheduling for serverless function workflows in edge computing system
Abstract: Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) computing paradigm enables fine-grained resource scheduling through decomposing complex workflows into a series of functions deployed in edge computing systems by a containerized manner. The temporal constraints of these workflows are required to be satisfied, where delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant workflows are scheduled through a priority-aware mechanism. We focus on resource-constrained edge nodes which are characterized by limited energy supply and computing capability. It is challenging to achieve the optimal trade-off between response delay and energy consumption through optimally deployed functions on edge nodes for scheduling unpredictable incoming workflows. This issue is formulated as an online deadline-aware function deployment model in terms of the Lyapunov optimization technique with efficient stability queues. A Markov decision process is formulated by continuously updating system states, selecting scheduling actions, and evaluating corresponding rewards. We develop a Deep Q-Learning based Workflow Scheduling (denoted as DQLWS) technique to achieve adaptive hybrid workflow scheduling, while considering long-term response delay and energy efficiency. Extensive experiments are conducted in terms of different proportions between delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant workflows, delay-energy weighting settings, scalability of edge node quantity and long-term scheduling performance. Evaluation results show that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in multiple comparison dimensions, including response delay, energy consumption, temporal violation rate, and algorithm stability, and thus achieves near-optimal scheduling solutions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Missing in action: unaddressed cost-of-illness studies in Colombia – A 30-year review; [Estudios sobre el costo de la enfermedad no abordados en Colombia: una revisión de 30 años]
Abstract: Introduction. Cost studies aim to answer questions about resource use and allocation. They provide information on the magnitude of the resource use of an illness paid for by patients, providers, health insurers or systems. Objective. To systematically review cost-of-illness (COI) studies conducted in Colombia over the past 30 years to identify neglected disease areas using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) classification. Materials and methods. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in MEDLINE, Scopus, and EMBASE up to February 2025, using standardized search terms related to cost-of-illness and Colombia. Eligible studies reported direct medical costs associated with diseases. Studies focused on cost-effectiveness, caregiver costs, or non-peer-reviewed literature were excluded. Data were extracted using a standardized form and adjusted to 2023 Colombian Pesos (COP) using the national Consumer Price Index. Studies were classified according to GBD Level 1 and 2 categories. Results. Of 257 studies screened, 44 met inclusion criteria. Mostly focused on non-communicable diseases, particularly hemophilia A, which had the highest average annual cost per patient. Rheumatologic and neurological disorders also showed high per-patient costs. Communicable diseases with significant costs included HIV/AIDS and drug-resistant infections. Pediatric studies were limited, with ICU-treated respiratory illnesses being most costly. Mental disorders, maternal and neonatal conditions, and several injury subgroups were largely unaddressed. Only 2 of the top 10 causes of DALYs in Colombia had corresponding COI studies. Conclusions. COI literature in Colombia remains fragmented and limited in scope. Standardized methodologies and targeted research are needed to guide equitable health policy and resource allocation. © 2027, Instituto Nacional de Salud. All rights reserved.

Title: Navigating the successful digital transformation of correctional services: Challenges, good governance, and a hybrid framework
Abstract: Digital transformation initiatives are essential for advancing correctional services toward digital maturity in Macao. However, the absence of a well-defined overarching strategy presents a significant impediment to the effective implementation of reforms. Due to the fact that the intelligent construction of the penal system has not yet been integrated with the extant eGovernment, the governance of the correctional system and its capabilities necessitate rigorous enhancement. Good governance encompasses legitimacy, accountability, transparency, capacity, fairness, responsiveness, participation, and consensus, which are widely considered core principles of public administration and are well-suited to linking the vision of digital transformation and smart correction initiatives. Based on the practice of eGovernment in Macao, which aspects can facilitate the digital transformation of correctional services to enhance the modernization of governance systems and capabilities, and achieve good governance? This study employs qualitative research methods, including a comprehensive literature review, secondary data collection, and analysis of legal documents, regulations, and sentencing policies within the Macao penal system. A SWOT-Plus analysis is conducted to assess potential internal and external trends and identify extant challenges. A hybrid framework is proposed that incorporates the incentives for eGovernment and the fundamental principles of good governance, including key governance beliefs and values such as organization, process, regulation, and culture. The findings also outline a series of expected impacts on correctional services that navigate the transformation ideology and foster successful implementation, thereby coordinating the vision of smart government. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Inclusive education as organizational inclusion: Creating inclusive business schools through co-curricular learning
Abstract: Knowing how to create inclusive business schools is crucial for the development of leaders navigating the workforce. This research examines co-curricular First-Year Experience (FYE) programming as an approach to supporting student integration, learning, and experiences. Using a quasi-experimental design, two studies examined academic performance and perceived transition success, belonging, self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and time management behaviours across in-person and online learning contexts. In Study 1, in-person students demonstrated higher academic performance and perceived transition success than online students. At the end of the semester, online and in-person students were comparable in outcome expectations, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management. General belonging was lower among online students across the two measurement occasions however, this difference was already present at baseline and did not change significantly over time. General belonging, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management were positively associated with perceived transition success, whereas outcome expectations were not a significant unique correlate. Study 2 identified exploratory within-format patterns across co-curricular in-person, bespoke in-person, and bespoke online course formats, with university belonging emerging as a significant correlate of perceived transition success across all three. Together, these findings position co-curricular and bespoke FYE approaches as promising frameworks for supporting inclusive business education while highlighting the central role of belonging in students’ transition experiences. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Local Knowledge for Ecological Restoration: Motivations and Barriers in Urban Protected Areas in Mexico
Abstract: Local knowledge is recognized as an important part of ecological restoration, and local communities have become more actively involved in recent years. Because participants hold diverse worldviews, their experiences can support ecological restoration. This study explored motivations and barriers to restoration based on the experiences of local participants in urban protected areas in the Valley of Mexico. We collected data through a survey and interviews. Local participants in restoration were mainly motivated by nature conservation and air purification. The main barriers to restoration were drought and fires. Participants’ restoration goals varied and were less aligned with protected-area objectives. Additionally, more experienced participants were more likely to identify restoration goals than less experienced participants. Overall, participants acquired knowledge through experience and undertook diverse efforts to address constraints. This suggests that learning from restoration activities, as a form of local knowledge, is important for identifying context-based barriers. From a socio-ecological perspective, this research discusses the need to establish context-based ecosystem targets and shared goals among stakeholders, as well as the importance of local knowledge for improving ecological restoration. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Deterministic branch-and-bound global MPPT using surrogate-derived power bounds for partially shaded PV arrays
Abstract: Partial shading fragments the power–voltage characteristic of series-connected photovoltaic (PV) arrays into multiple local peaks, rendering conventional trackers ineffective and exposing the reliance of metaheuristic global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) methods on random initialization and empirical tuning coefficients. This paper proposes TSB-GMPPT, a deterministic tanh-surrogate branch-and-bound GMPPT algorithm that eliminates both dependencies. A control-oriented hyperbolic-tangent surrogate of the PV I–V characteristic admits a non-iterative Lambert W asymptotic approximation for the maximum power point voltage. During discovery, a single saturation-region measurement per candidate is sufficient to construct a calibrated optimistic bound, safely pruning the search space before final peak localization. An offline polynomial calibration recovers the remaining parameters from short-circuit current. During discovery, an optimistic branch-and-bound rule maintains an upper power bound for each unconfirmed layer and permanently discards candidates that cannot exceed the incumbent confirmed power, contracting the admissible search space without exhaustive probing. A five-state finite-state machine governs initialization, shading-topology detection, discovery, winner refitting, convergence, and adaptive reinitialization. Experimental validation using a Chroma 62150H solar array simulator and a dSPACE DS1104 platform on five-module benchmark cases and additional eight-module complex multi-peak shading cases demonstrates average tracking efficiencies of 99.94% under partial shading and 99.98% under uniform irradiance, with corresponding average convergence times of 0.25 s and 0.21 s, respectively, for the five-module test set. Further validation under eight-module complex multi-peak shading cases and dynamic irradiance transitions confirms rapid re-tracking, accurate GMPP identification, and robust operation under realistic operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Fabrication of bioactive hydrogels stabilized by gluten amyloid fibrils and ε-polylysine: Effects of fibril morphology and blending ratios
Abstract: The introduction of ε-Polylysine (PL) provides additional functional activities for hydrogels. However, it simultaneously impairs their mechanical properties to a certain extent. To address this trade-off, we hypothesized that gluten protein amyloid fibrils (GAFs) with distinct topological morphologies—long rigid fibrils (LRF), long flexible fibrils (LFF), and fibril networks (FN) differentially modulate PL hydrogels through site-specific molecular bridging and spatial cross-linking. Driven by strong electrostatic attraction and hydrogen bonding, GAFs and PL underwent ratio dependent systemic reorganization and assembly. The physicochemical properties of GAFs/PL hydrogels were primarily governed by the combined regulation of GAFs morphology and blending ratios. Specifically, at the same GAFs/PL ratio, FN exhibited superior spatial connectivity, contributing to enhanced water immobilization within the hydrogel network. Meanwhile, LRF and FN were more effective in constructing continuous force transmission pathways, thereby improving hardness and dynamic viscoelasticity. These findings demonstrate that the functional performance of GAFs/PL hydrogels can be tailored by selecting appropriate fibril morphologies and blending ratios according to specific application requirements. However, the network formed by LFF was more susceptible to deformation, resulting in a relatively limited mechanical reinforcement effect on the hydrogel skeleton. Ultimately, this study aims to clarify the assembly pathway driven by the cooperative contribution of GAFs and PL. This study provides a theoretical foundation and design strategies for developing food-grade composite materials with tunable mechanical properties and bioactive functionalities. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Peterson B.
Title: Aemilia Lanyer and the Body
Abstract: Scholars have consistently turned to representations of the body in Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum to consider issues of genre, religion, gender, race, social status, poetics, and poetic authority. Yet, despite scholars- frequent attention to topics of corporeality and embodiment, “the body” has not been recognized in Lanyer studies as a central subject of inquiry. The introduction to this special issue surveys how the corpus naturale has undergirded Lanyer scholarship over the past fifty years. Whereas previous studies have identified the body-s importance at discrete moments or in specific mechanisms in Lanyer-s poetry, this introduction emphasizes how the form and content of Salve Deus is fundamentally rooted in the body and bodily experience. This special issue, thus, reconceptualizes the categories of “women writers” and “women-s writing,” highlighting how we might consider the female body not as a historical identity but rather as a formal model in early modern English literature. Authors: Fan J.; Yang H.; Pan X.; Tan Z.; Liu X.; Chen G.; Xu J.; Tan J.; Chen X.; Pan F.
Title: Amplified strain partitioning driven by multiple heterostructures enables superior strength-ductility in Ti-reinforced Mg composites
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The strength-ductility trade-off remains a long-standing challenge for magnesium matrix composites (MMCs). Herein, we develop a novel strategy to fabricate multi-heterostructured MMCs with simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement, using a Ti/Mg-6Zn-1.5Mn composite prepared via ultrasonic-assisted semi-solid stirring, homogenization heat treatment, and hot extrusion. The constructed multi-level heterostructures consist of three key features: (i) non-uniform coarse/fine grain (CG/FG) mixed structure, (ii) nanophases with density differences between FGs and CGs, and (iii) Ti particles preferentially distributed adjacent to the nanophases. The composite exhibits exceptional comprehensive mechanical properties, with an ultimate tensile strength of 366 MPa, yield strength of 239 MPa, elongation of 20.6%, and a superior strength-ductility product of 66.29 MJ/m3. The excellent performance originates from multi-heterostructure-driven amplified strain partitioning, which induces hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening and hardening via geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation. Meanwhile, activated non-basal slip systems enable efficient intergranular slip transfer for uniform plastic deformation, and CGs effectively delay plastic instability and suppress crack propagation. This work provides new insights into the deformation mechanisms of heterostructured MMCs and offers a feasible pathway for developing advanced lightweight structural materials. © 2026

Authors: Bansah K.J.
Title: Mechanization, gender, and livelihoods in artisanal and small-scale mining: a technofeminist political ecology perspective
Abstract: This study examines the gendered impacts of mechanization in artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM), a sector increasingly shaped by excavators, washing plants, motorized pumps, trommels, and leaching techniques. Drawing on field investigations in mining communities in southwestern Ghana, the study shows that technological adoption in ASM is not gender neutral. While mechanization has improved efficiency and productivity, it has simultaneously displaced women from core mining activities where they historically played essential economic roles. As a result, women are increasingly relegated to ancillary and informal tasks that generate lower and often unsustainable incomes while exposing them to heightened environmental and health risks. These intersecting experiences show how mechanization can simultaneously produce economic displacement and continued environmental vulnerability for women in ASM. To explain these dynamics, the study develops and applies a Technofeminist Political Ecology (TPE) framework as an original analytical lens. Integrating insights from technofeminism and feminist political ecology, TPE conceptualizes technology not as a neutral tool of progress but as a social and political force that restructures labor, redistributes environmental risk, and reconfigures gendered vulnerabilities within extractive economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Reconstructing the Life History of Double Perforated Ivory Beads from the Swabian Aurignacian: A Combined Traceological and Experimental Approach
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Aurignacian ivory beads provide valuable insights into ivory-working techniques, labour investment, production organisation, and the symbolic behaviour of Early Upper Palaeolithic people. Although decades of research have led to a detailed understanding of the chaîne opératoire of these iconic beads, systematic approaches for identifying and interpreting manufacturing- and use-related traces remain limited. Using 74 double perforated ivory beads (DPIBs) from Archaeological Horizon IV at Hohle Fels Cave as a case study, we integrate taphonomic, typological, morphometric, and traceological analyses with experimental replication to develop an analytical framework for reconstructing the manufacture and use of archaeological ivory beads. Our results suggest that DPIB production followed a broadly shared production sequence while allowing flexibility in the order and execution of individual manufacturing steps. The archaeological evidence indicates that the beads were produced, used, and discarded on site. Experimental replication further provides a basis for evaluating labour investment and identifying surface modifications associated with manufacture and use. The observed morphological variability may reflect differences in production practices related to variation in skill, individual behaviour, and the involvement of multiple craftspeople. The analytical approach presented here is transferable and can be applied to other archaeological ivory bead assemblages. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Analysis of environmental and social impacts of quarry mining for bridging stakeholder perception gaps–a case study from Padukka, Sri Lanka
Abstract: This study investigates stakeholder perceptions of the environmental and social impacts associated with the China Harbour Aggregate Quarry in the Padukka Division of the Colombo District, Sri Lanka. Despite growing concerns about the impacts of quarrying on host communities, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how different stakeholder groups perceive and experience these impacts in the Sri Lankan context. A mixed-methods case study design integrated qualitative and quantitative approaches to examine stakeholder perspectives. The study involved 31 community members near the quarry, 3 quarry site professionals, and 4 officers from a technical services company, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews with all stakeholder groups and structured questionnaires comprising open- and closed-ended questions administered to community members. Thematic analysis was used to analyze interview and open-ended questionnaire data, while descriptive analysis was applied to closed-ended questionnaire responses. Findings indicate that vibration was the dominant impact, reported by all community participants (100%), with concerns about noise, water dry out, dust, and occasional flyrock events. Community responses revealed high perceived annoyance (93.5%) and opposition to the mining site (87.1%), although all respondents were unwilling to relocate, highlighting sociopsychological constraints. Comparative analysis revealed convergence and divergence between community perceptions and quarry personnel perspectives, with mitigation measures implemented but challenges persisting due to spatial constraints, communication gaps, and disputed compensation claims. The study contributes context-specific evidence on stakeholder perceptions of quarrying impacts and provides practical insights for strengthening community engagement, impact mitigation, and socially responsible quarry management in Sri Lanka. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Work–life conflict and psychological well-being among working women: A qualitative study from counselors’ perspectives
Abstract: Women's increasing participation in the workforce has intensified their exposure to multiple and competing role demands arising from work, family, and personal responsibilities. These overlapping demands may generate work-life conflict and affect psychological well-being. Although previous studies have examined these issues, much of the existing literature has relied on quantitative approaches, with limited qualitative evidence drawn from counsellors who work directly with affected women. This study explored counsellors' perspectives on work-life conflict and psychological well-being among working women. A qualitative research design was employed using semi-structured interviews with seven professional counsellors who had experience handling cases involving working women. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, and the interview data were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. Three emergent themes were also identified: normalisation of working beyond office hours, the importance of personal boundaries and emotional regulation, and counselling as emotional release rather than problem solving. The findings indicate that working women's psychological well-being is shaped by the interaction of workplace demands, family responsibilities, emotional strain, coping resources, and support systems. This study contributes qualitative insights into counselling practice and highlights the relevance of Role Conflict Theory and Boundary Theory in understanding the psychosocial experiences of working women. Title: Growth, skin quality and stress of farmed Morelet’s crocodiles (Crocodylus moreletii) housed communally or individually during the finishing stage
Abstract: This study evaluated the effect of housing type (communal versus individual enclosures) during the finishing stage on growth, skin quality, and chronic stress of farmed Morelet's crocodiles (Crocodylus moreletii). A total of 292 subadult crocodiles were included: 164 housed individually and 128 communally. Growth variables (total length, belly width, and live weight), skin quality, and corticosterone concentrations were assessed at the beginning and end of the finishing stage. The market price for the skin was determined at the end of the finishing stage. Crocodiles housed in communal enclosures showed greater total length, live weight, and growth gain (P < 0.05). In contrast, crocodiles housed individually exhibited greater skin quality with greater commercial value (P < 0.05), as well as lower corticosterone concentrations, at the end of the finishing stage (P < 0.01). Correlation between percentages of TL gain and LW gain was higher in CE (r = 0.74) than in IE (r = 0.31). The coefficient of determination was greater in CE (R2 = 0.54) than in IE (R2 = 0.09). However, variance was greater in CE (TL = 0.08; LW = 3.2) than in IE (TL = 0.04; LW = 2.4). These results suggest a trade-off between growth and skin quality, as well as a different stress response depending on housing type. While communal housing promoted greater growth, individual housing favored more homogeneous growth and skin quality, and reduced the chronic stress response. However, interpretations regarding animal welfare should be made cautiously, as corticosterone was used as one indicator of chronic stress and does not reflect overall welfare status. Authors: Özen S.
Title: A non-explosive alpha-series recurrence framework for modelling mortality jump arrivals
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Catastrophic mortality jumps disrupt long-term trends, yet existing jump models assume either constant jump probability or i.i.d. recurrence times, ignoring how jump-timing patterns evolve. The Lee–Carter framework is extended with a non-explosive alpha-series recurrence process, letting inter-jump durations shift with event order, nesting the stationary renewal process as a special case. Jump years are identified from the total-population mortality index and modelled as a common event sequence, with female and male dynamics linked through sex-specific effects and correlated innovations; the discretised likelihood uses exact recurrence-duration probabilities, including right-censoring after the most recent jump. Applied to Denmark, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the UK, and the USA with a 2019 calibration cutoff, the model reveals substantial cross-country heterogeneity in jump recurrence and favourable forecast performance. For a term-life portfolio, alternative arrival mechanisms yield similar expected liabilities, while their relative differences become more visible in tail-capital measures, indicating that recurrence assumptions matter more for tail-risk assessment than for mean liability levels. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Mapping Healthy Days Scores to EQ-5D-5L Utilities: Development and Validation of an Algorithm Using Population Survey Data
Abstract: Objectives To develop and validate an algorithm for estimating EQ-5D-5L utility scores from the nonpreference-based Healthy Days (HD) instrument using direct and indirect mapping approaches. Methods Data were drawn from the Queensland Preventive Health Survey for 2022 ( N = 12 491) and 2023 ( N = 12 679). Survey-weighted ordinary least squares (OLS), Tobit, beta, majorize-minimize, and ordinal logistic regression models were evaluated. Algorithms were developed using an 80% random training sample from the 2022 data, tested in the remaining 20%, and externally validated using 2023 data. Predictive performance was assessed using root mean square error, mean absolute error, differences between predicted and observed mean utilities, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, body mass index, smoking status, and utility quartile. Results Moderate correlations were observed between unhealthy days measures and EQ-5D-5L utilities (Pearson’s r: −0.53 to −0.56). Predictive accuracy was broadly similar for the OLS, beta, and ordinal logistic models. The OLS model including physically unhealthy days, mentally unhealthy days, activity limitation days, self-rated health, age, and sex was selected as the preferred algorithm. It demonstrated strong and stable predictive performance across samples (root mean square error ≤ 0.117 and mean absolute error ≤ 0.066 in validation samples). All models overestimated utilities in the lowest utility quartile. Conclusions The HD instrument can be mapped to the EQ-5D-5L with favorable predictive accuracy in population survey data. The proposed algorithm provides a pragmatic approach for estimating mean utilities for quality-adjusted life-year calculation when only HD data are available, although caution is warranted in populations with very low baseline health status. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Xu S.; Li M.; Huang Q.; Tian Y.
Title: Decoupled reverse Kullback–Leibler: Rethinking knowledge distillation loss for bridging GNNs and MLPs
Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) excel at handling graph-structured data but are often prohibitively expensive for low-latency applications. Cross-architecture graph knowledge distillation (GKD) addresses this by training efficient Multi-layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to mimic GNN performance. Interestingly, while existing methods predominantly use forward Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence, we find that the two terms of reverse KL exhibit optimization properties that are better matched to the GKD objective. However, its conventional form suffers from tightly coupled fitting and regularization terms with fixed weights, limiting its flexibility. To overcome this, we propose Decoupled Reverse KL (DRKL), which introduces hyperparameters to independently adjust the weight of each term, enabling more effective adaptation to diverse prediction scenarios. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DRKL outperforms both standard forward and reverse KL losses across multiple metrics. Furthermore, DRKL serves as a plug-and-play loss that can enhance the GKD frameworks evaluated in this work without added computational cost, delivering improved performance, robustness, and fast inference. Title: Beyond topology-driven graph convolution: Node patch convolutional network for node representation learning
Abstract: Attributed graph node representation learning is crucial for tasks such as node classification in attributed networks. Conventional GNNs, whether coupled or decoupled, are mainly topology-driven and struggle to capture attribute correlations among non-neighboring nodes. Existing CNN-based graph methods alleviate this limitation by selecting relevant nodes but remain sensitive to node ordering and often fail to integrate attribute and topology views effectively. In this paper, we propose a CNN-based graph representation learning framework namely node patch convolutional network (NPCN) that constructs node-centric patches from both attribute and topology perspectives. Moreover, a tailored patch augmentation and the corresponding readout mechanism are adopted to enhance the node representation learning. A patch consistency constraint further stabilizes the learned representations. Experiments on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms representative approaches. Moreover, computational efficiency analysis shows that NPCN achieves competitive performance with lower training overhead compared with Transformer-based graph representation learning methods, making it a practical solution for attributed graph node classification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Energy trading and demand response strategies for energy flexible manufacturing systems under temporary electricity shortages: A noise-robust multi-agent reinforcement learning approach
Abstract: This paper investigates the energy management of energy flexible manufacturing systems (EFMS) under temporary electricity shortages (TES). TES disrupt the real-time balance of energy supply and demand. Meanwhile, multi-source measurement noise can degrade dynamic state estimation and affect scheduling decisions. To address these challenges, a hybrid approach integrating a generalized loss cubature Kalman filter (GLCKF) and a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm is proposed. First, a dynamic pricing model based on the real-time demand-supply ratio, retail price, and feed-in tariff is designed to keep local trading prices within the grid price bounds. Second, GLCKF is used to suppress the effects of non-Gaussian measurement noise and random outliers. The resulting state estimates are used by MADDPG to jointly optimize real-time energy trading and demand response (DR) strategies. The framework is evaluated using a simulated four-EFMS cluster over a one-day scheduling horizon. The case incorporates industrial load profiles, photovoltaic generation, energy storage parameters, and time-of-use electricity prices. Comparative results show a 53.76% reduction in state-estimation root mean square error relative to CKF-MADDPG under the selected mixed-Gaussian noise setting. The results indicate that the framework improves economic performance and supports supply-demand balance in the tested TES scenarios. © 2026

Authors: Tasias K.A.; Nenes G.
Title: Optimizing equity and efficiency in the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem
Abstract: This study addresses the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem, formulated as the strategic prepositioning of a heterogeneous aerial firefighting fleet across capacity-constrained airbases. A novel bi-objective model is proposed that simultaneously optimizes efficiency (aggregate risk-weighted accessibility) and equity (minimized regional service disparities). The model employs an enhanced spatial accessibility method with a distance-decay function to evaluate coverage effectiveness and distribution fairness. A multi-objective genetic algorithm is implemented to generate Pareto-approximate solutions, revealing quantifiable trade-offs. Applied to a national-scale case study in Greece using 25 years of wildfire data, results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides significantly wider coverage than current practices, thereby extending protection to underserved regions while reducing redundant overlap. Sensitivity analyses confirm robustness across various real-world conditions, such as different budget levels and aircraft availability. This transferable tool enables policymakers to make data-driven decisions by quantifying the balance between response effectiveness and social fairness in wildfire-prone regions. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Sour grapes or strategic choice? Socially disadvantaged tourism entrepreneurs' pursuit of ‘break out’
Abstract: While structural conditions impacting immigrant entrepreneurs' ‘break out’ are well-documented in tourism research, the underlying psychological processes remain underexplored. Informed by self-determination theory and adaptive preferences, this ethnographic study conducted between December 2024 and May 2025 explores how socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs negotiate structural constraints and individual agency while pursuing ‘break out’. Drawing on 345 h of ethnographic observation, digital data from two focal Nepali tourism entrepreneurs in Hong Kong SAR, and longitudinal object-oriented interviews with nineteen stakeholders, it reveals a psychological mechanism where frustration of basic psychological needs triggers adaptive preferences, hindering ‘break out’ efforts. It also shows how tourism's experiential nature enables entrepreneurs to counter stigma and negotiate autonomy. Practically, the findings highlight the need for psychologically informed support that goes beyond traditional skill-based training. Authors: Aydogmus O.; Tunc H.
Title: A unified instance selection approach based on distributional similarity for machine learning
Abstract: In this study, we propose a unified instance selection approach, applicable to both regression and classification tasks, that selects a reduced dataset whose distribution matches that of the original, thereby preserving its key statistical and structural properties. Our central contribution is to analytically show that the instance selection problem, aiming to ensure distributional similarity measured via the Wasserstein distance, is exactly equivalent to the balanced k-medoid problem when the compression ratio is integer-valued. We further extend this equivalence to arbitrary (non-integer) ratios with explicit bounds on the resulting approximation error. This equivalence allows the instance selection problem to be addressed directly with existing balanced k-medoid solvers. To this end, we employ a Lloyd-style alternating (EM-type) constrained k-medoid algorithm, obtained by extending an existing constrained clustering method. Extensive experiments across binary classification, multi-class classification, and regression tasks confirm the method's effectiveness: it significantly outperforms the task-specific baseline at most reduction ratios on all seven multi-class datasets (Wilcoxon, p<0.05), outperforms the boundary-focused baseline on the majority of binary settings—most clearly on the higher-dimensional datasets—and attains lower error on four of five regression datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Sesele K.
Title: Holding the periphery: Women, territorial holding labour, and the post-extractive labour-sending economy
Abstract: Post-extractive scholarship has focused predominantly on mines, mining towns and industrial transition, with limited attention to labour-sending territories historically incorporated into extraction through labour circulation and social reproduction. Drawing on qualitative interviews with 21 participants engaged in informal livelihood activity in Viljoenskroon, South Africa, this paper focuses analytically on nine women to examine how such territories continue to function after extractive employment contracts. The findings identify seven interlocking mechanisms through which women sustain households, livelihoods and community continuity under conditions of constrained accumulation, weakened institutional incorporation and infrastructural decline. The paper conceptualises the territorial condition produced through these relations as the extractive periphery and the feminised work through which its continuity is maintained as territorial holding labour. It argues that as extractive employment contracts, reproductive labour that historically subsidised extraction through the reproduction of labour increasingly subsidises its territorial aftermath through the reproduction of continuity. This extends post-extractive analysis beyond sites of production and social reproduction analysis beyond households and labour power to the reproduction of territorial continuity. The findings also challenge continuity as evidence of successful transition: apparent resilience may conceal the transfer of unresolved adjustment costs into women’s income, time and labour. Transition policy must therefore account for labour-sending territories and for who bears the costs through which their continuity is sustained. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: An integrated framework of emergy analysis and LMDI for assessing sustainability: a case study of tobacco production system
Abstract: To tackle the challenges of resource consumption and environmental pressure in agricultural production systems, quantifying sustainability performance and identifying its driving mechanisms are critical. This study introduces an integrated framework based on emergy analysis and the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI), covering production investigation, system analysis, sustainability evaluation, and driver exploration, and ultimately guiding targeted production recommendations. The results reveal that tobacco energy output rose from 3.5 × 10^16 J in 2004 to 5.1 × 10^16 J in 2013, before declining to 3.3 × 10^16 J in 2021. Total emergy input exhibited a similar pattern, peaking at 2.2 × 10^22 sej in 2013. From 2004 to 2021, the environmental sustainability index increased from 0.46 to 0.54, while the environmental loading ratio decreased from 3.36 to 3.00, indicating a steady improvement in sustainability. Significant spatial variability was observed across provinces. LMDI decomposition revealed that economic efficiency contributed significantly to the sustainability improvement (0.53), while changes in renewable resource dependency offset -0.52 of this gain. Based on this framework, targeted strategies are proposed to optimize curing energy utilization, refine fertilizer management, and enhance economic efficiency. These findings offer practical support for promoting the sustainable transformation of the tobacco production system. © The Author(s) 2027. Published by Higher Education Press. Title: Electrospray preparation of Fe-PMMA films for one-drop analysis of thiocyanate a tobacco biomarker as a case study

Title: Semi-Asynchronous Efficient Hierarchical Federated Learning for heterogeneous resources
Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of cloud–edge–device collaborative computing, Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) has become a promising paradigm for large-scale distributed model training. Title: Artificial intelligence disclosure and the value relevance of earnings

Title: Routine Distributional Analysis of Health Inequality Impact by Socioeconomic Group: Technical Feasibility Study in Queensland, Australia
Abstract: Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility of routine distributional analyses of healthcare interventions in Australia, by adapting a Health Inequality Impact Calculator for Queensland. Title: Mixed methods research: Critical review and guidelines for stronger design, integration, and contribution
Abstract: Mixed methods research has a prominent place in tourism and hospitality scholarship, yet adoption has advanced faster than methodological selectivity, which leaves many studies combining qualitative and quantitative strands without explaining why both strands were necessary, how the strands were related, or what integrated inference their combination alone made possible. Drawing on a critical review of 222 mixed methods studies published in leading tourism and hospitality journals, this article identifies dominant patterns, strengths and weaknesses, and underused possibilities. Title: Fostering creativity through interdisciplinary teaching: A meta-analysis of effectiveness
Abstract: Interdisciplinary teaching is widely promoted to cultivate students’ creativity, yet empirical findings remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis synthesized 55 quantitative studies (70 effect sizes, 7490 students) from 2013 to 2024, applying random-effects models using Hedges’ g. Creativity outcomes were decomposed into three theoretically grounded dimensions: creative thinking process, creative practice ability, and creative personality and psychology. Results indicated a large overall positive effect ( g + = 1.090, 95% CI [0.913, 1.266]), with very high heterogeneity ( I 2 = 96.017%). Dimensional analysis revealed significant variations: the strongest effects on creative practice ability ( g + = 2.164), followed by creative thinking process ( g + = 1.253), while effects on creative personality and psychology were smaller ( g + = 0.478). Moderator analyses revealed that educational stage, dominant subject, pedagogical approach, intervention duration, and group activities significantly influenced outcomes, while class size and instructional setting did not. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Biorefining of whole cotton plant residues for bioethanol production with greenhouse gas emission reduction and social carbon benefits
Abstract: This study evaluated the potential of cotton-processing residues, including leaves, bolls, linters, and stalks, as feedstocks for bioethanol production using ethanol-based organosolv pretreatment. Biomass samples were pretreated with 65 % (v/v) ethanol at 120, 150, and 180 °C for 30 and 60 min, followed by enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation. Organosolv pretreatment altered biomass composition through partial removal of hemicellulose and enrichment of glucan in the recovered solids, which was associated with improved enzymatic digestibility and ethanol production. The highest hydrolysis efficiencies reached 75.4 %, 80.2 %, 83.0 %, and 79.9 % for leaves, bolls, linters, and stalks, respectively. Correspondingly, the highest ethanol yields were obtained from leaves (70.8 %) and stalks (61.1 %) after pretreatment at 180 °C for 30 min, while maximum yields of 42.3 % and 42.6 % were achieved for bolls and linters, respectively. The results demonstrated that pretreatment severity significantly influenced both hydrolysis and fermentation performance, although the optimal conditions varied among biomass fractions. Greenhouse gas reduction calculations estimated that replacing gasoline with E85, E10, and E5 ethanol–gasoline blends could reduce emissions by 55.7 %, 4.9 %, and 2.4 %, respectively. In addition, the social cost of carbon analysis indicated substantial reductions in the social cost of carbon emissions, with the highest benefit obtained from boll-derived bioethanol due to its greater production potential. These findings demonstrate that cotton-processing residues represent a promising lignocellulosic resource for bioethanol production while supporting agricultural waste valorization and greenhouse gas mitigation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Cross-modal vision transformer with energy-system priors for interpretable operational pattern discovery
Abstract: The identification of the repeating operating conditions for energy assets — namely, the limited range of states through which any turbine or building passes — forms an essential component of condition monitoring; however, since operating labels are seldom available at scale, the process has to be unsupervised. Progress is hampered by two issues: one-dimensional sequence encoders do not explicitly represent pairwise lag, recurrence, and transition structures that can separate states with similar marginals; moreover, physics-blind clustering can collapse into trivial magnitude groups that lose temporal coherence. We present PRISM, a cross-modal vision transformer that reads the operational segment both as a smoothed picture derived from the signal via the vision transformer branch and as an unprocessed sequence of signals through the selective state-space branch, connecting the two derived perspectives using cross-attention with prior biasing. We present an idealized conditional identifiability result under explicit multi-view and bounded-switching assumptions, while the envelope prior provides only a qualitative complexity rationale. On five public benchmarks involving buildings (the Building Data Genome 2 and REFIT) and wind turbines (Kelmarsh, Penmanshiel, CARE-to-Compare), PRISM brings fault and anomaly detection to a mean AUROC of 0.922 and exceeds the leading contrastive baseline by 0.031 (3.1 percentage points), while improving silhouette from 0.489 to 0.571. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The impact of entrepreneurship education on sustainable entrepreneurial intentions: A quasi-experimental study
Abstract: In this paper, we examine how a semester-long sustainability-oriented entrepreneurship course shapes sustainable entrepreneurial intention (SEI) through individual sustainability orientation (ISO). Grounded in an adaptation of the Theory of Planned Behaviour, ISO is conceptualized as a multidimensional construct encompassing sustainability-oriented (SO) values, SO motivation, awareness of sustainability issues, and SO self-efficacy, dimensions expected to mediate educational effects on SEI with different temporal sensitivities. We implemented a quasi-experimental design across two graduate introductory entrepreneurship courses at two Canadian universities: one redesigned around sustainability mechanisms (treatment, N = 112) and one covering standard content (comparison, N = 47). Pre- and post-test surveys were conducted. Results show no direct effect of the treatment on SEI and no change in SO values, which were high at baseline. However, the treatment significantly increased students’ sustainability awareness, self-efficacy, and, unexpectedly, motivation. Among these, changes in awareness and self-efficacy were positively associated with changes in SEI. These findings indicate that semester-long interventions can reliably influence proximal cognitions (awareness and self-efficacy), while deeper dispositions such as values, and to a lesser extent motivation, likely require longer-term or more immersive exposure. Theoretically, this study conceptualizes ISO as a temporally layered construct that helps explain why prior findings on education–SEI links are mixed. Methodologically, it demonstrates the value of coupling quasi-experimental designs with pedagogical reporting. Practically, it highlights workable mechanisms, such as sustainability-anchored projects, sustainable business modeling, and impact-oriented pitches, that strengthen awareness and SO self-efficacy. These insights encourage moving beyond outcome-level evaluations toward understanding how entrepreneurship education can foster SEI. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Assessing the techno-economic performance of membrane-based carbon capture and storage in South African coal-fired power plants
Abstract: South Africa relies heavily on coal for electricity generation, making its power sector a major contributor to carbon dioxide emissions. Carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies have been proposed as pathways to mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and environmental impacts. This study presents a techno-economic evaluation of a membrane-based carbon dioxide capture system tailored for a South African coal-fired power plant. This study presents a techno-economic evaluation of a membrane-based carbon dioxide capture from a South African coal-fired power plant. The work involves firstly simulating a supercritical coal power plant with a capacity to produce a gross power of 804 MW. Coal characteristics and local ambient conditions in a specified region of South Africa are considered. The resulting flue gas composition and state are determined from the simulation. In a second stage, a membrane system is proposed for carbon capture from the power plant flue gas. To optimise the process, a superstructure-based model is applied. The capture efficiency is set at 90% whilst the product stream consists of 95% carbon dioxide. The cost of the membrane process, transport and storage and ultimately the cost of electricity, is determined. The study shows that an optimal membrane-based carbon capture and storage system in South Africa would result in an additional 10.6% efficiency penalty. The cost of electricity would increase by 131.9% to 152.5 US$/MWh. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic graph attention networks for multi-regional load forecasting in modern power systems with missing data
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy and multi-regional power system operation creates new challenges for short-term load forecasting (STLF), particularly under missing data, dynamic spatial dependencies, and uncertainty. Existing approaches often separate data imputation from forecasting, rely on static spatial structures, and provide deterministic predictions, limiting their applicability in risk-aware power system operation. This paper proposes an Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Graph Attention Network (UA-DGAT) for multi-regional load forecasting under incomplete and uncertain data conditions. The proposed framework integrates probabilistic masked self-attention imputation, uncertainty-aware dynamic graph attention, and multi-scale temporal modeling based on discrete wavelet transform within an end-to-end architecture. Unlike conventional pipelines, UA-DGAT explicitly propagates imputation uncertainty, spatial dependency uncertainty, and predictive uncertainty throughout the forecasting process. Extensive experiments on NYISO and ISO-NE datasets demonstrate that UA-DGAT achieves superior performance in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting metrics, reducing MAE and RMSE while attaining approximately 87% prediction interval coverage. Ablation studies verify the contribution of each component and confirm the significant role of uncertainty-aware conditioning. Furthermore, the proposed framework maintains robust forecasting performance under missing data rates up to 50%, with particularly improved resilience under block missing patterns. The results demonstrate that uncertainty-aware modeling of data reconstruction and spatial dependency learning enables more accurate, reliable, and risk-aware load forecasting for modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Exploring the linkage between entrepreneurial education and entrepreneurial intentions among university students in Morocco
Abstract: The Moroccan labor market continues to struggle with the incorporation of its university graduates and the interest in entrepreneurship as an employment option is growing. Higher education institutions are an essential part of developing students' entrepreneurial competencies and intentions. This research investigates the effects of entrepreneurship education on students' entrepreneurial intention as based on the Theory of Planned Behavior. The research also investigates how attitudes toward entrepreneurship, perceived behavioral control, subjective norms, creativity, proactive behavior, and family background influence entrepreneurial intention. A self-administered questionnaire was used to collect data from 226 students at the Faculty of Economics and Management at Beni Mellal, Morocco, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that entrepreneurship education is positively related to entrepreneurial intention both directly as well as indirectly through attitudes toward entrepreneurship and perceived behavioral control; also, creativity and family background were found to positively influence entrepreneurial intention. In contrast, subjective norms and proactive behavior do not show a significant effect in this context. These findings highlight the importance of entrepreneurial education in strengthening students' entrepreneurial orientation while suggesting that social influences and individual proactivity may operate differently within the Moroccan context. The study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence from a developing country context and offers implications for policymakers and educators seeking to enhance entrepreneurship education programs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Unpacking the pathways: Self-regulation’s mediating effect on students’ self-efficacy and mathematics achievement
Abstract: This research design aims to investigate the influence of self-regulation as the mediating variable on the relationship between self-efficacy and mathematics achievement of the participants who are Grade Nine students at the selected public high schools in the Philippines for the school year 2024 – 2025. The survey measured key constructs, including self-efficacy and self-regulation, while mathematics achievement was evaluated using first quarter mathematics grades. The study included a total of 845 valid responses from Grade Nine students. The data collected were treated using frequency count, percentage, weighted mean, standard deviation, Pearson’s r, and multiple regression analysis. The analysis of the findings revealed moderate levels of students’ self-efficacy and self-regulation in planning and monitoring, while levels of adjusting and reflecting were high. Moreover, there was a significant weak positive correlation between self-efficacy and mathematics achievement, a weak positive for self-efficacy and self-regulation, and a weak positive for self-regulation and mathematics achievement. It is determined that the students’ self-regulation partially mediates the relationship between students’ self-efficacy and mathematics achievement, indicating that self-efficacy enhances mathematics performance not only directly but also indirectly by fostering self-regulatory behaviors. Title: Will this time be different? Just transition pathways in eastern and Southern Africa’s critical minerals sector
Abstract: The global energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for critical minerals required for renewable energy technologies like solar panels, wind turbines, and battery storage systems. However, the future translation of mineral reserves into equitable socio-economic development in the region depends on policy frameworks and governance systems that promote inclusive participation, recognition, and benefit-sharing. This paper examines pathways for inclusive economic transformation, analyzing the conditions required to ensure mining-affected communities benefit equitably from the critical minerals boom. We employ a justice-centered framework of distributional, procedural, recognition and restorative justice to analyze five countries (Democratic Republic of Congo, South Africa, Zambia, Malawi, and Burundi) through stakeholder interviews with 43 actors and document and policy analysis, including Malawi and Burundi, whose emerging sectors are largely absent from the peer-reviewed record. Across the five cases the four dimensions are not encountered as separate problems. Findings suggest that employment opportunities do not always reach local populations, revenue mechanisms face transparency challenges, consultation processes have limited influence over outcomes, customary tenure is inconsistently recognized, and environmental legacies often persist without adequate remediation. Ensuring that the substantial economic opportunities created by critical mineral demand are realized inclusively will require simultaneous interventions across all four justice dimensions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
