Title: Employment subcenters and polycentric urban development in the Greater Dhaka Region, Bangladesh
Abstract: Although a significant number of studies have focused on urban growth patterns in Dhaka, the spatial structure of employment and its roles in shaping polycentric urban development is poorly understood. Specifically, how employment subcenters (ESCs) emerge and organize under conditions of informal and infrastructure-led urban growth typical of Global South megacities remains unclear. Hence, this study poses the question of how ESC formation is related with the construction and development of a polycentric urban employment structure in the city and how their hierarchical spatial organization shapes intra-urban agglomeration. To answer this question, the spatial distribution of employment in the Greater Dhaka Region during the 2011-2013 study period was analyzed based on fine-scale employment data from the 2013 economic census together with Local Moran's I (LMI) within a grid-based framework. An optimal grid size and shape were used to detect ESCs, including their location, hierarchy, spatial extent, geographical distribution, spatial characteristics and processes. The study found 59 ESCs, including one rank 1 center, four rank 2 centers, 18 rank 3 centers, and 36 rank four centers. The findings reveal a core-dominant but dispersed polycentric employment structure, in which high-ranked ESCs concentrated within approximately 20 km of Dhaka's historical core and low-ranked ESCs developed along major transportation corridors in peripheral areas. The findings suggest that the employment structure observed during the study period reflected a hierarchical, corridor-oriented pattern influenced by market forces and infrastructure-led urban processes rather than by planned decentralization, with weak metropolitan coordination strengthening the continued dominance of the historical core. Title: Thermal history and stress redistributions achieving reduced crack susceptibility in laser-directed energy-deposited Al2O3/GAP/ZrO2 eutectic ceramics by circular oscillation scanning
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Crack control remains a major challenge in laser-directed energy deposition (LDED) of oxide eutectic ceramics because of their intrinsic brittleness and thermal-stress accumulation. In this work, emissivity-calibrated in-situ infrared thermometry and thermo-mechanical simulation were used to reveal how circular oscillation scanning (COS) reduces the crack susceptibility of LDED Al2O3/GAP/ZrO2 eutectic ceramics. Compared with linear reciprocating scanning, COS produced a wider high-temperature zone, stronger interlayer reheating, and milder recooling. At the representative mid-height location, the average cooling rate from peak temperature to melting point decreased from 330.91 to 173.82 °C/s, while the reheating-induced temperature rise increased from 167.38 to 1076.03 °C. Stress analysis showed that COS reduced crack susceptibility mainly by weakening the continuous bottom-centered tensile-stress band and localizing higher-stress regions near the side areas, rather than by simply lowering the local stress peak. This stress redistribution was consistent with the observed transition from bottom-initiated vertical cracking to side-localized, laterally limited cracking. The COS parameter study further revealed a trade-off between thermal coverage and tensile-stress concentration. These findings provide guidance for scan-path design and crack control in LDED of oxide eutectic ceramics. © 2026

Title: A coupled oxidation-damage model for cross-layer ablation failure in HfC/SiC bilayer coatings on C/C composites
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: HfC/SiC bilayer coatings provide exceptional ultra-high-temperature ablation protection for Carbon/Carbon composites. However, the complex cross-layer chemo-mechanical interactions, specifically between the oxidation-induced cracking of the HfC outer layer and the active oxidation of the SiC inner layer, remain poorly understood. In this work, a comprehensive oxidation-damage coupling ablation model is proposed based on continuum damage mechanics and chemical reaction kinetics. Oxyacetylene ablation experiments were conducted to characterize the ablation depths and layer-specific damage evolution. To handle the severe material discontinuity at the bilayer interface, an interfacial node-decoupling method is implemented, ensuring multiphysics continuity while preserving the independent chemical kinetics. The proposed model is successfully validated against experimental results with an average relative error of 15.7%. The numerical results clarify a mutually exacerbating failure mechanism: Stress-driven HfC cracking creates preferential oxygen pathways that accelerate localized SiC depletion, while the resulting material loss undermines the mechanical support of the overlying HfC layer. Furthermore, parametric analysis uncovers a non-monotonic evolution of the anti-ablation performance when varying the SiC layer thickness (10–30 μm). A thicker SiC layer imposes a more severe mechanical constraint that prematurely drives outer-layer microcracking, whereas it provides a superior secondary oxygen barrier during extended ablation. Title: Determining the robust drivers of CO2 emissions in Africa: Machine learning and panel econometric evidence on the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis
Abstract: One of the primary greenhouse gases linked to global warming is carbon dioxide. This study investigates the determinants of carbon dioxide emissions in 29 African countries over the period 1990–2023 using a two-stage machine learning and econometric framework. In the first stage, Classification and Regression Trees, Random Forests, and Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithms are employed to identify the most important drivers of carbon dioxide emissions. The results indicate that Random Forests provide the highest predictive performance among the machine learning models. In the second stage, the variables identified by the machine learning analysis are incorporated into second-generation panel estimators that account for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity. Specifically, long-run and short-run relationships are examined using the Common Correlated Effects Autoregressive Distributed Lag estimator, while Augmented Mean Group, Common Correlated Effects Mean Group estimators, and Fixed Effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors are employed as robustness checks. The findings reveal that oil consumption is positively associated with carbon dioxide emissions, whereas renewable energy consumption is negatively associated with carbon dioxide emissions. The results provide limited but supportive evidence for the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis, with income and income-squared terms exhibiting the expected signs and the estimated turning point falling within the observed income range. Robustness analyses based on oil-exporting and non-oil-exporting country groups, as well as an alternative carbon-intensity measure, confirm the central role of fossil fuel dependence and renewable energy adoption in shaping environmental outcomes across Africa. These findings highlight the importance of accelerating renewable energy deployment, reducing reliance on fossil fuels, improving energy efficiency, and promoting sustainable development strategies to achieve long-term environmental sustainability in African economies. © 2026 The Authors. Title: The perceived legitimacy of costly punishment in the evolution of cooperation under private reputation
Abstract: Indirect reciprocity promotes cooperation by allowing reputation to serve as a social currency for future benefits. However, the role of costly punishment under private reputation remains less understood. Under private reputation, independent assessments may lead observers and punishers to hold different views about the same recipient. This raises the question of how an observer evaluates punishment when the punished recipient appears to have a good reputation. We introduce the perceived legitimacy of costly punishment into a private-reputation model of indirect reciprocity. We first analyze the core dynamics among unconditional cooperators, unconditional defectors, and discriminating punishers, and then test whether the cooperative state is stable against the full set of action-rule mutants, including antisocial punishers. Our results show that costly punishment promotes cooperation only when its perceived legitimacy lies within an appropriate range. In this regime, discriminating punishers and unconditional cooperators can coexist stably, producing high cooperation and social payoff. However, insufficient legitimacy prevents punishers from disciplining defectors, whereas excessive legitimacy allows strategies that punish high-reputation individuals to invade, linking the model to antisocial punishment. Finite-population Markov analyses further confirm that the main qualitative dynamics are robust to small punishment execution and assessment errors. These findings show that, under private reputation, the perceived legitimacy of costly punishment determines whether punishment sustains cooperation or facilitates antisocial punishment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: The effect of social robot authority on epistemic vigilance in early childhood
Abstract: Social robots are increasingly deployed as tutors and learning partners, yet their authority cues may discourage children from questioning or verifying information. The same task and outcome measures were used as in Study 1. The results showed that cognitive authority significantly decreased children’s verification behavior, but there was no significant effect of role authority or child age. Title: FedLoop: Personalized federated learning with closed-loop feature rectification
Abstract: While Personalized Federated Learning (pFL) has emerged as a promising solution to statistical heterogeneity, existing methods predominantly rely on static client-level adaptation. However, uniform adaptation ignores instance-level heterogeneity, inevitably leading to the under-fitting of outliers and the catastrophic forgetting of well-aligned samples. To address this, we introduce FedLoop, a novel paradigm that shifts from static parameter tuning to dynamic, instance-aware feature rectification. FedLoop establishes a closed-loop feedback mechanism that explicitly decouples rectification into direction and magnitude, utilizing prediction uncertainty as a real-time feedback signal to dynamically modulate the rectification intensity. Notably, our method adds personalization through a local rectifier that is excluded from aggregation, so instance-level adaptation does not alter the aggregated global backbone. Extensive experiments across computer vision, time-series, and NLP benchmarks demonstrate that FedLoop significantly outperforms state-of-the-art pFL methods. Crucially, it achieves rapid convergence with negligible computational overhead and maintains superior robustness even under sparse client participation, effectively resolving the long-standing dilemma between local personalization and global utility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Tian H.; Chen W.; Cheng Y.; Li K.; Lv D.
Title: Mechanism-guided soft sensing of NOx emissions in CFB boilers under heterogeneous noise and multiscale dynamics
Abstract: Accurate soft sensing of NOx emission concentration in coal-fired boilers is important for clean combustion control. However, real CFB operating data contain heterogeneous noise, multiscale dynamic responses, and stage-dependent dominant variables, which hinder extraction of NOx-formation dynamics and degrade soft-sensing accuracy. To address these issues, a NOx emission soft sensing method is proposed. First, training samples consistent with practical disturbances are constructed from differences in the statistical distributions of process variables. Representation consistency between noisy and original data is then constrained in the latent space to reduce abnormal-disturbance effects on basic features. After obtaining basic representations, a variable-scale prior weight matrix is designed using data characteristics and CFB combustion mechanisms. This matrix is combined with data-driven scale weights to fuse multiscale features and extract dynamic information better matched to the actual combustion process. To capture dynamic changes in variable effects, learnable proxy vectors aggregate NOx-related key segments with reduced sequence interaction cost. Variable gating then generates variable weights from proxy temporal representations, dynamically identifying dominant process variables across operating stages. Experiments on practical operating data from a 350 MW CFB unit show that the proposed method achieves an R2 of 0.953 on the test set. Under compound disturbances comprising random, abnormal, and drift noise, the R2 remains 0.896, indicating strong noise robustness. SHAP analysis and internal-weight visualization show that the identified key variables and their time-varying effects are generally consistent with CFB combustion mechanisms. Overall, the proposed method improves the accuracy, robustness, and interpretability of NOx emission soft sensing, and provides a practical auxiliary tool for NOx emission monitoring in CFB boilers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Design implications of ground properties and operating conditions for geothermal cooling in hot-humid and arid regions: A case study of Bahrain
Abstract: This study assesses the feasibility of geothermal cooling for residential buildings in hot-humid and arid regions, using Bahrain as a representative case. Unlike studies relying on commercial software, this evaluation utilizes a fundamental analytical approach based on ASHRAE guidelines to explicitly demonstrate how individual parameters influence system sizing. Vertical borehole ground-coupled heat pump systems were modeled using local climatic data and subsurface thermal properties. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis was performed to isolate the impact of ground thermal conductivity, diffusivity, borehole spacing, system operating duration, and circulating water temperature on the required heat exchanger length. The analysis identifies ground thermal conductivity and circulating water temperature as the primary drivers for minimizing system footprint, yielding borehole length reductions of up to 46%. The study also quantifies the competing long-term effects on the ground heat exchanger: localized thermal buildup expands the required heat exchanger length by 39% over time, whereas natural groundwater flow provides a stabilizing 36% reduction. Techno-economic analysis indicates that despite elevated capital expenditure driven by drilling cost, geothermal cooling can substantially reduce power consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, while mitigating local ambient temperatures by rejecting heat into the ground. The findings provide a transparent, physics-based design framework that demonstrates the technical viability of geothermal cooling in high-ambient-temperature regions, provided that long-term ground thermal saturation is managed. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Grinding Charcoal for Rock Painting: A Methodological Framework for Particle-Size Analysis in Rock Art Micro-Samples
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Research on the materiality of rock art has shifted attention from images as finished products to the technical and social processes involved in their making. Within this framework, pigment grinding is a crucial but still methodologically elusive aspect of painting production, despite its potential to inform technological choices, labor investment, and variability in painting practices. In this paper, we propose an experimental and archaeometric approach to the study of charcoal grinding in rock art micro-samples. By combining experimental archaeology, optical microscopy, and particle analysis, we develop a model linking charcoal particle area to grinding time. We apply this method to study black rock paintings from the Oyola archaeological site, in northwestern Argentina, where charcoal was identified as the main black pigment. The results show that microscopically measurable differences in particle areas make it possible to distinguish varying degrees of grinding among paintings that are macroscopically and chemically similar. Title: EV-PV-capacitor integration in distribution systems with reliability-cost trade-off: A utility-prosumer perspective
Abstract: This paper proposes a generalized framework for the integrated planning of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS), Photovoltaic (PV) systems, and capacitors in distribution networks using a sequential optimization strategy aligned with practical planning dependencies. The three-stage approach addresses multi-stakeholder economics and reliability–cost trade-offs. To establish the planning baseline, Stage-1,determines EVCS locations that minimize total network losses using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Stage-2 employs Multi-Objective PSO (MOPSO) to size PV systems by jointly optimizing conflicting utility and prosumer Net Present Values (NPVs), considering bill savings, export revenue, lifecycle costs, loss reduction, interruption savings, deferral benefits, FiT expenses, and PV degradation, with the optimal solution selected using Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Stage-3 applies a similar framework to co-optimize capacitor number, size, and placement, balancing investment costs with reliability. Validation on the 33-bus system under probabilistic uncertainties in load, solar irradiance, and EV charging shows reduced losses, improved economic performance, and enhanced stability and reliability. Results demonstrate that the coordinated EV-PV-capacitor solution reduces active power losses by 59.0%, improves minimum voltage by 6.2%, and reduces SAIFI, SAIDI, and AENS by 17.9%, 20.4%, and 30.3%, respectively. Title: Driving sustainable development goal alignment through green consumption marketing and public mind
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable development demands synchronized efforts across socioeconomic and environmental domains, specifically targeting poverty alleviation, food security, and environmental stewardship. Although sustainable consumption patterns and ecological marketing act as established catalysts for environmental transitions, the specific socio-civic pathways translating micro-level pro-environmental behaviors into macro-level policy alignment remain underexplored. To bridge this gap, the study objectives were to evaluate the direct and indirect pathways through which green consumption behavior and green marketing drive local alignment with the sustainable development goals through the mediating role of the public mind among residents in Nonthaburi Province, Thailand. METHODS: A quantitative survey design was executed to gather data from 400 residents across administrative districts in Nonthaburi Province using proportionate stratified random sampling. The researchers collected primary data through structured questionnaires employing a 5-point Likert scale. Analytical procedures encompassed descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling to validate construct relationships and assess overall structural model fit. FINDINGS: The results of structural equation modeling indicate that both green consumption behavior and green marketing significantly influence the realization of local sustainable development goals, operating through both direct pathways and indirect pathways mediated by public consciousness. The public mind demonstrated the strongest direct influence on sustainable development goals realization (β = 0.69, p < 0.01), followed by direct impacts from green consumption behavior (β = 0.35, p < 0.01) and green marketing (β = 0.28, p < 0.01). Additionally, green consumption behavior was the primary driver of public mind activation (β = 0.37, p < 0.01), surpassing green marketing (β = 0.27, p < 0.01). The validated structural model accounted for substantial variance in sustainable development goals alignment (R^2 = 0.97) and the public mind (R^2 = 0.77). CONCLUSION: Green consumption behavior and green marketing are critical precursors to cultivating a collective public mind, which bridges individual eco-conscious actions with macro-level alignment of Sustainable Development Goals. Municipal authorities ought to embed the mobilization of public ecological awareness into environmental governance policies. Furthermore, this structural framework offers a scalable model adaptable to other rapidly urbanizing provinces in Southeast Asia. Title: Explaining Strategies to Reduce the Occurrence of Medication Errors at Older Adults with Polypharmacy
Abstract: Objective: Age-related changes make the older susceptible to multiple chronic diseases and, consequently, an increase in the number of medications consumed. The present study aimed toexplain strategies to reduce the incidence of medication errors at illiterate and low-literate older adults with polypharmacy from the perspectives of the older, caregivers, and pharmacists. Method: The present study is a qualitative study that was conducted with 23 semi-structured interviews with three different groups of participants including illiterate and low-literate older adults with polypharmacy, caregivers of the older (informal caregivers of the older such as family members), and pharmacists from August 2022 to Murch 2024 in Tabriz, Iran. Participants were selected using purposive sampling method and interviews were conducted based on a designed interview guide. Conventional content analysis method was used to analyze the data. Findings: The inductive content analysis process extracted 6 main categories from 32 subcategories. The average age of the older participants in the study was 67.53 years. From the perspective of the study participants, strengthening self-care and health-oriented behaviors and beliefs, using techniques to optimize medication management, caregiver responsibility and support, effective education, effective interaction between the older and the physician-pharmacist, and an efficient healthcare system can be effective in reducing the incidence of medication errors in the older. Title: Meta-operation-assisted optimization for execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning
Abstract: Existing robotic disassembly sequence planning (RDSP) studies mainly optimize operation ordering under precedence constraints, whereas robot configurations and local operation parameters are typically treated separately or represented by fixed or simplified operation costs. To bridge this gap, this paper formulates an execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning (EP-RDSP) problem that jointly considers disassembly sequencing, robot configuration selection, and disassembly operation parameter optimization. In contrast to task-level RDSP, EP-RDSP evaluates a plan through the coupled effects of its operation sequence, selected inverse kinematics (IK) configurations, joint-space transitions, and local operation parameters. EP-RDSP contains heterogeneous and tightly coupled decisions, making direct optimization of the full mixed decision space computationally challenging. To address this challenge, a meta-operation-assisted (MOA) optimization framework is proposed to support multiobjective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA)-based search. The framework exploits meta-operation knowledge for operation-parameter generation before online optimization, allowing MOEA to focus on globally coupled planning decisions such as operation ordering, IK candidate selection, and joint-configuration and speed-ratio decisions. Experiments on 15 generated problem instances show that, across the four underlying optimizers and three instance scales, the MOA variants reduce the mean online runtime required to reach the target hypervolume (HV) by 16.45%–83.01%. Under fixed online time budgets, the MOA framework improves the mean HV by 31.13%–80.04% relative to five comparison methods and achieves the lowest mean inverted generational distance (IGD) on 14 of the 15 instances. Title: Dual-Objective Design of Broadband Rectenna and Anchor Node Optimization for Energy Harvesting and High-Accuracy UWB Localization
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Wireless sensor networks and portable devices face two major challenges: sustainable energy supply and high-precision indoor localization. While far-field wireless power transfer (WPT) offers energy solutions, it suffers from low power density and environmental sensitivity. To mitigate these drawbacks, the proposed system incorporates polarization diversity and a wideband impedance matching strategy. Simultaneously, GPS fails in indoor environments, driving the need for ultra-wideband (UWB) localization to achieve centimeter-level accuracy. This paper presents a dual-objective framework to tackle both issues. First, it designs a broadband antenna array (1–20 GHz) with multi-polarization reception, combined with an optimized matching network and Schottky-based rectifier to enhance RF-to-DC conversion under low power. Second, it introduces an anchor placement optimization algorithm for UWB that uses probabilistic target behavior models to minimize positioning errors. Simulation results confirm that the energy harvester remains effective across various incident angles and frequencies, while the localization error is consistently reduced to around one centimeter. The integrated approach provides a comprehensive solution for next-generation WSNs, overcoming power management bottlenecks while elevating localization accuracy to approximately one centimeter. © 2027 The author(s). Authors: Chen Z.; Liao H.; Chen J.; You D.
Title: Complementary recommendation with abductive correction in incremental development
Abstract: Complementary cloud API recommendation, which suggests APIs frequently co-invoked with a given set of APIs, plays a crucial role in enabling efficient incremental development. Existing approaches primarily model API complementarity from co-invocation behaviors but often overlook weak complementary relationships revealed through functional co-occurrence. Moreover, most methods follow a one-step paradigm, directly generating recommendations from learned relationships without further abductive refinement, thereby limiting accuracy. To address these issues, we propose a Complementary Recommendation method with Abductive Correction, named CRAC. CRAC is built on three key ideas: (1) developing a path-based modeling approach that unifies both strong complementary (from co-invocation) and weak complementary (from functional co-occurrence) relations into a unified framework; (2) introducing complementary projection and higher-order reasoning modules that capture complementary and non-substitutable relationships while enforcing complementary-but-not-substitutable constraints; (3) designing an abductive correction mechanism that refines recommendation results through abductive tasks and losses, with an over-correction strategy to ensure effective correction. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that CRAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Further ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of weak complementarity modeling and abductive correction in enhancing complementary recommendation performance. Title: TikTok as a stage: How short video creators’ identity performance drives engagement with tourism experiences
Abstract: Destinations are increasingly collaborating with short-form video creators to engage consumers. Through Goffman's dramaturgical lens, this study explores how creators' performed identities in travel videos relate to audience responses. Combining machine learning and AI-powered analyses of over 10k short-form videos and 176k viewer comments with a controlled experiment, we identified four identities that creators performed in these videos (the “showman,” “diarist,” “docent,” and “photographer”) and classified them at scale. Results showed that identity performance is associated with distinct configurations of audiences' behavioral engagement. The “docent” generated more audience engagement than other identities, including audiences' learning, endorsing, and intending to participate dimensions. Guided by the knowledge gap theory, a subsequent experiment showed that the “docent” identity increased engagement by sparking curiosity. Title: Recursive self-regulation in genAI-assisted experiential learning: A task-contingent model
Abstract: Existing literature on generative AI (genAI) in business education has examined students’ attitudes, motivation, and the ethics of genAI use, alongside ongoing debate about whether genAI over-reliance may diminish self-regulated learning (SRL). Within this structured, reflective learning context, students indicated evaluative judgement and metacognitive regulation, providing preliminary evidence that scaffolded genAI activities can elicit active rather than passive engagement. Title: Brazilian Expert Consensus on the Use of Equity and Acceptability in Health Technology Assessment: A Delphi Panel
Abstract: Objectives To achieve consensus among Brazilian experts on the concepts of equity and acceptability within the context of health technology assessment (HTA) in Brazil and to identify guidance for their practical application across assessment stages, operationalization methods, and strategies for evidence generation and use. Methods A 2-round online Delphi panel with Brazilian HTA experts assessed agreement on predefined literature-based concepts of equity and acceptability and explored perspectives on HTA stages, methods, and evidence generation and retrieval strategies. Results Participants were experienced HTA professionals, and consensus on the concepts of equity and acceptability was reached in the first round, exceeding the predefined threshold of 80% agreement. These dimensions were considered cross-cutting throughout the HTA process, with priority given to technology assessment, clinical guideline development, and implementation stages. Evidence search methods and cost-effectiveness analyses were prioritized for equity, whereas qualitative evidence and mixed methods were prioritized for acceptability. Strategies including secondary data analysis, primary data collection, and standardized filter use were prioritized for both dimensions. Title: Complex adaptive governance for sustainable tourism villages: Explanatory insights from combined polycentric and chaos theoretical perspectives
Abstract: Sustainable tourism villages face complex governance challenges because they must simultaneously support economic development, protect local culture, preserve ecological resources, and respond to changing social conditions. Existing studies have examined sustainable tourism governance mainly from administrative, community-based, or institutional perspectives, but less attention has been given to how distributed authority interacts with nonlinear adaptive dynamics in village-level governance systems. To address this gap, this study develops an integrated framework that combines polycentric governance theory and chaos theory. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that institutional diversity has the strongest association with sustainable tourism village governance, followed by decentralization and local autonomy, bifurcation and cosmology, community participation, flexibility and adaptability, edge of chaos and the butterfly effect, and self-organization and strange attractors. The model yields a very high coefficient of determination, which suggests a close within sample fit between the proposed constructs and the observed perception data. This result is interpreted cautiously because the study is cross-sectional and several constructs are conceptually proximate. The study contributes to governance theory by showing that sustainable tourism village governance can be understood as both polycentric and complex-adaptive. Practically, the findings suggest that policymakers and tourism village managers should strengthen multi-actor coordination while maintaining flexibility to respond to uncertainty and local change. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Retreat in monastery stay tourism: the role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ connectedness and behavioural intention

Abstract: Monastery stay tourism is an emerging niche within spiritual and transformative tourism, offering immersive experiences that facilitate personal and emotional growth. Despite its rising popularity, limited research has explored how such experiences shape tourists' emotional bonds, identity formation, and revisit intention. Title: Exploring the acceptance of science teachers toward simulator-based technology
Abstract: Teacher acceptance of technology is crucial for enhancing the effectiveness of learning in the digital era. This study aims to explore the acceptance of simulator-based technology among science teachers and to compare the perspectives of experienced and inexperienced teachers. A quantitative descriptive approach was used, adopting the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology 2 (UTAUT2) model. The analysis was conducted to test the influence of Performance Expectancy (PE), Effort Expectancy (EE), Social Influence (SI), Facilitating Conditions (FC), Hedonic Motivation (HM), and Habit (HA) on Behavioral Intention (BI) and Use Behavior (UB). Data were collected through a survey of middle school science teachers in Surakarta, Indonesia. The results revealed positive acceptance of the simulator, with differences between the two groups. Perceived ease of use (EE) and facilitating support (FC) influence behavioral intention (BI), whereas habit (HA) and hedonic motivation (HM) play a significant roles in use behavior (UB), especially among experienced teachers. The results revealed positive acceptance of the simulator, with significant differences between the two groups. Overall, experienced teachers demonstrated higher mean scores across all UTAUT2 indicators. Performance Expectancy (PE) and Facilitating Conditions (FC) were found to consistently influence Behavioral Intention (BI) across almost all groups. However, Effort Expectancy (EE) and Social Influence (SI) were more significant for inexperienced teachers, whereas Habit (HA) significantly influenced BI only for experienced teachers. For Use Behavior (UB), Behavioral Intention (BI), Facilitating Conditions (FC), Hedonic Motivation (HM), and Habit (HA) emerged as strong predictors, particularly for the experienced group. These findings imply the need for adaptive implementation strategies; experience-based training, infrastructure enhancements, and user-friendly simulator design are recommended to enhance the acceptance and utilization of technology among science teachers. Authors: Blessing M.A.; Will M.
Title: Blowing Leaves in Archaeology—The Multidimensionality of Technological Complexity in Human Origins Research
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Technological complexity has been a continuous trope in archaeological research from its beginnings in the nineteenth century. Based on a concept of unidirectional cultural evolution, archaeological material was ordered along a linear progression from simple to complex. While creating hierarchies of extant populations based on the complexity of their tools is not overtly practiced in archaeology anymore, the same is not true for the deep past. The concept of behavioural modernity and research on human cognitive evolution is still partly founded on technological complexity. The turn away from technological complexity to symbolic behaviour in pursuing questions surrounding behavioural modernity and humanness was less a reaction to criticisms of the concept but served to maintain the hierarchical ranking between modern humans and extinct hominins. Here, we propose an alternative view on technological complexity that attempts to overcome linear hierarchies and lingering progressivist notions. By reviewing several measures of complexity alongside their analytical units and underlying definitions, we show that technological complexity is not suitable for creating a single hierarchy of artefacts, assemblages, or hominin species. The multitude of existing definitions, methods, and measures does not imply a fundamental flaw in these approaches but exemplifies the multidimensionality of technological complexity. We propose a new way of understanding multiple, justified measures for technological complexity through a heterarchical structure that allows various kinds of ranking to exist depending on context, need, scale, or function, including the potential for competing or even contradictory hierarchies. A heterarchical perspective on technological complexity asks ‘How were technologies or hominins complex?’ rather than ‘How complex were technologies and hominins relative to another?’ This approach can shed persistent historical bias and overcome simplistic dichotomies such as ‘us’ and ‘them’ in deep-time archaeology that hinder our ability to engage with questions about the becoming of humans in a meaningful way. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Multi-objective optimization and decision-making for renewable energy production and enhancement of wind turbine selection in Morocco
Abstract: Selecting an appropriate wind turbine for a specific location requires the simultaneous evaluation of energy output, cost, and site-specific deployment constraints. This research introduces a comprehensive framework that integrates simulation, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), and hybrid deep learning to enhance the selection of turbines for various sites. One year of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis version 5 (ERA5) reanalysis data and geographical information from satellite and elevation datasets was used to model the energy output of 40 commercial turbines in 15 Moroccan cities. A weighted scoring procedure was developed to evaluate turbines based on their capacity factor, annual energy production (AEP), capital and operating expenditures (CAPEX/OPEX), topographical constraints, and proximity to infrastructure. Two hybrid models, convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) and convolutional neural network-Transformer (CNN–Transformer), were trained on structured inputs that included meteorological, topography, and spatial data to enhance decision assistance. The CNN–Transformer model outperformed the CNN–LSTM model in predictions and closely aligned with the expert rankings derived from simulations. Constraint-aware filtering and cost-performance trade-offs were employed to enhance the final turbine suggestions. The findings demonstrate the efficacy of integrating physics-based simulation with machine learning for large-scale energy planning at specific locations. This framework supports future upgrades to renewable energy systems, including AI-based digital twins, real-time monitoring, and use across more locations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wu E.L.; Kuo H.-C.
Title: The influence of gender, socioeconomic, and domain competencies on students’ creative thinking across four high-performing educational systems
Abstract: This study explores the multidimensional construct of students’ creative thinking by analysing the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment data from four educational systems: Chinese Taipei, Hong Kong, Macao, and the Czech Republic. These jurisdictions are uniquely characterised by high student performance in reading, mathematics, and science, while their average creative thinking scores fall below the OECD benchmark. The study examines the predictive power of gender, socioeconomic status (SES), and academic proficiency in Reading, Mathematics, and Science on students’ performance across four creative thinking (CRT) domain contexts: Written Expression, Visual Expression, Social Creative Problem-Solving, and Scientific Creative Problem-Solving. Evidence shows that female students consistently outperformed male students across all four creative thinking domains, while SES demonstrated a modest but consistently positive association with creative thinking performance. Academic competencies also contributed significantly to CRT but exhibited distinct domain-specific predictive patterns. Reading competence was the strongest and most consistent predictor, particularly for Written and Visual Expression. Science competence showed stable positive associations across domains, whereas Mathematics contributed most strongly to Social and Scientific Creative Problem-Solving but was negatively associated with Visual Expression. These findings indicate that academic competencies contribute differently across creative thinking domains. Representative item-level analyses further illustrated task-specific predictive patterns, while the complete item-level analyses are reported in the Supplementary Material. These findings support a domain-sensitive view of creative thinking, in which academic competencies show differential associations with creative performance depending on the domain and task context, and further offer practical implications for creativity assessment and educational practice. Title: Measuring head motion across deceleration levels in automated driving: Quantifying comfort
Abstract: Passenger-centred comfort measures are needed to enable adaptive driving styles in automated vehicles, particularly where comfort begins to decrease. This study examined passengers' head motion during automated braking at a crosswalk. Data from thirty-four participants were analysed, who experienced three deceleration levels (−1.5, −2.5, −3.5 m/s2) and two pedestrian visibility conditions, reflecting how quickly the AV braked after the pedestrian appeared, rating comfort respectively. As expected, head pitch and translational acceleration increased with deceleration intensity, while pedestrian visibility had no effect on head motion, even though faster AV responses were previously found more comfortable, suggesting this reflects passengers' judgement of the AV's response rather than head stability. Head-motion measures did not add predictive value beyond vehicle kinematics, likely because comfort ratings were similar across conditions. In this scenario, head-motion mainly reflected physical response to braking rather than subjective evaluation. Future research should test head-motion measures in more complex driving conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Inozemtsev S.; Iarmolatii A.
Title: Behavioral Economics as a Driver of Healthcare System Reform: Methodological Approach
Abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to develop and apply the Behavioral Economics in Health index as a methodological tool for assessing the role of behavioral strategies in healthcare reform, with particular attention to their impact on healthcare expenditure, life expectancy, and system-level adaptation in countries with varying levels of institutional maturity and economic capacity. Methods The research used system-dynamics-based simulation modeling using behavioral and economic parameters, followed by statistical analysis of the results. Results The AnyLogic simulation results showed that, under an intensive behavioral integration scenario for 2024 to 2034, per-capita health expenditure decreased by USD 200 in Ukraine and USD 190 in Poland. In these countries, the initial levels of behavioral integration were the lowest—0.51 and 0.59, respectively—and the 10-year increase was 0.30. This fact ensured a steady reduction in expenditure throughout the entire modeling period without significant fluctuations. In Denmark, where the initial behavioral integration level was higher (0.88), the decrease amounted to only USD 26 per person, indicating a limited effect of further behavioral interventions in an already prevention-oriented healthcare system. Conversely, in the United States, where the integration index was even higher (0.91), expenditure increased by USD 20.72 per capita. Conclusions These findings indicate that the maximum economic effect of behavioral strategies is achieved in countries with low initial levels of integration and limited resources. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhai P.; Su Y.; Cao Y.; Wu L.; Zhang F.; Teng C.
Title: Delay-aware feasibility control for quadrotor path following
Abstract: Safe quadrotor path following under input delay is formulated here as a quantitative feasibility problem in which delayed actuation directly reduces the transverse acceleration authority available for path recovery. The proposed framework establishes an explicit chain from bounded thrust-channel delay and rotor-level actuator limits to a recoverability margin, a curvature-aware path-speed law, and a second-order Lyapunov invariant tube. A delay-matched nonlinear disturbance observer is incorporated to reduce the disturbance-related residual, while a command-rate-limited closed-form speed governor regulates path progression only when curvature demand and delay-induced authority loss approach the available recovery budget. The resulting controller requires no online optimization and is implemented through the same full SE(3) plant, rotor allocation, thrust–attitude mapping, and actuator constraints used in the numerical benchmarks. Across four simulation scenarios, including a certification-oriented case and more demanding nominal, stress, and curvature-varying conditions, the proposed method preserves the implemented feasibility margin while avoiding unnecessary uniform speed reduction. In the stress case, with a delay reserve of 0.703 m/s2 and a certified transverse acceleration radius of 5.724 m/s2, the proposed controller maintains zero negative-margin duration, whereas the fixed-speed disturbance-observer controller and the delay-ignorant proportional–derivative controller exhibit negative-margin durations of 12.76% and 20.56%, respectively. The proposed controller attains a root-mean-square transverse error of 0.195 m at a mean path speed of 3.682 m/s, illustrating the intended safety–progression trade-off rather than minimizing tracking error at the expense of recoverability. These results demonstrate that input delay can be treated not merely as a stability perturbation but as a quantifiable loss of rotor-backed recovery authority that can be compensated through explicit feasibility-based progression regulation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Zhu C.; Wang F.; Wang S.; Li T.; Chen H.; Feng X.
Title: LMC-DETR: A lightweight detection model for foreign object detection on power lines
Abstract: To address the dual requirements of model lightweighting and detection accuracy in foreign object detection for drone-based power-line inspection, this paper proposes a lightweight multi-scale context-aware detection model, termed LMC-DETR. Specifically, a Context-aware Global Block (CGB) is introduced into the backbone network, which integrates multi-scale receptive field fusion with global context recalibration, thereby achieving significant reduction in parameters while enhancing feature extraction capabilities. In the neck network, a Multi-scale Context Fusion Framework (MCFF) is designed to construct an intelligent feature pyramid, wherein two cooperative submodules, Fusion-U and Fusion-D, collaborate. Attention-guided upsampling and downsampling mechanisms are employed to substantially improve the quality of multi-scale feature fusion. Furthermore, a Squeeze-and-Excitation Channel (SEC) module incorporates a lightweight Efficient Squeeze-and-Excitation (ESE) attention mechanism for adaptive channel-wise feature recalibration, effectively suppressing background noise while accentuating critical feature representations. Experimental evaluations on a public power line foreign object dataset demonstrate that the proposed LMC-DETR achieves a detection accuracy of 85.0% APIOU=50. Compared to the baseline, LMC-DETR reduces the number of parameters (15.1M) and computational cost (44.1 GFLOPs) by 23.7% and 22.5%, respectively, striking a favorable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Consequently, the model shows promise for real-time drone inspection scenarios, pending further validation on edge hardware. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Gaze aversion and emotional mimicry deficits in individuals with schizophrenia during naturalistic interaction
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Individuals with schizophrenia exhibit a range of verbal and nonverbal impairments during social interaction, which contribute to reduced interaction quality and broader social dysfunction. To optimize clinical interventions, it is essential to identify the mechanisms underlying these deficits. Building on previous findings demonstrating reduced emotional mimicry in schizophrenia, the present study examined whether gaze aversion is associated with instances of failed mimicry during naturalistic conversation. In a within-partner design, interacting partners (n = 20) each engaged in one conversation with an individual with schizophrenia (n = 20) and one with a matched healthy control (n = 20). Prior analyses using OpenFace-based video coding revealed diminished emotional mimicry in the schizophrenia group. In the present study, the same video recordings were reanalyzed using FaceReader to extract gaze direction. We specifically examined gaze aversion during the interaction and, more critically, during episodes of failed mimicry, defined as instances in which participants did not reciprocate their partner's smile. Results indicated that although individuals with schizophrenia did not display significantly greater overall gaze aversion across the entire interaction, they exhibited significantly greater gaze aversion when their partner was smiling. This pattern was associated with a higher proportion of failed mimicry accompanied by gaze aversion in the schizophrenia group compared to controls. These findings suggest that reduced visual attention may represent one mechanism contributing to emotional mimicry deficits in schizophrenia. Clinical implications are discussed, along with the potential role of stigma in exacerbating these processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Yeleliere E.; Frimpong Boamah E.
Title: Locked in: How formal institutional design sustains extractivism and ecological decline in Ghana’s mining–water sector
Abstract: Mining-related water pollution persists despite repeated legislative reforms and regulatory interventions. Yet, existing explanations largely attribute this persistence to weak enforcement, political patronage, or socioeconomic pressures driving artisanal small-scale mining (ASM). We argue instead that the problem is fundamentally one of institutional design. Drawing on institutional theory and institutional grammar analysis, we examine how Ghana's mining-water legislation allocates authority and embeds incentive structures that shape environmental governance. We find that the legislative framework privileges regulative over constitutive institutional elements, producing governance arrangements that are procedurally elaborate yet functionally weak. At the same time, it embeds economic and political incentives that favor extractivism while providing comparatively weak social and regulatory incentives for environmental stewardship, reinforcing fragmented authority, symbolic governance, and executive overreach. These institutional arrangements generate intertwined common-pool resource and public-bad dilemmas that lock Ghana's mining-water sector into a gilded trap, in which short-term extractive gains systematically outweigh long-term socioecological sustainability. The findings suggest that persistent mining-related water pollution is not simply a failure of enforcement but a consequence of institutional architectures that privilege extractivism while weakening environmental governance. In reconceptualizing the gilded trap as an institutionally produced condition, the paper demonstrates how imbalances between constitutive and regulative institutional elements generate symbolic governance and position the state as an active producer, rather than merely a failed regulator, of extractivist outcomes. © 2026 .

Authors: Hu X.; Li H.; Zhu H.; Zhang J.
Title: Decoding interfacial differences between regioisomeric organic dyes: The role of alkyl-chain conformational accessibility
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Long alkyl chains in dye-sensitized solar-cell sensitizers are commonly regarded as aggregation-suppressing substituents, although their conformational accessibility may influence interfacial organization. Here, DFT, TD-DFT, CREST/xTB conformational sampling, and projected density-of-states (PDOS) analysis were combined to examine the regioisomeric dyes T5-1 and T5-2, for which IPCE maxima of approximately 60% and 85%, respectively, have been previously reported. The T1–T4 reference series shows that π-extension red-shifts absorption while introducing trade-offs in adsorption and charge-transfer descriptors. For T5-1/T5-2, frontier-orbital energetics and alkyl-free dye–TiO₂ coupling are comparable; however, the low-energy T5-1 ensemble favors syn-type chain dispositions, whereas T5-2 has a thermally accessible anti conformer. Thus, conventional backbone-centered electronic descriptors alone do not fully account for their distinct interfacial behavior. Selected interface models associate the T5-2 motif derived from the anti-conformer with more-upright adsorption, stronger local chain-mediated contacts, and larger LUMO resonance broadening. This organization provides a structural basis for reduced electrolyte accessibility and a lower propensity for interfacial charge recombination, while retaining strong dye–TiO₂ electronic coupling. These findings highlight alkyl-chain conformational accessibility as an important factor linking molecular connectivity to interfacial behavior in the T5-1/T5-2 regioisomeric dye pair. Authors: Liu Z.; Liu S.; Wang Y.; Chen Y.; Deng H.; Tan Z.; Zhao X.; Chen Y.; Zhu M.
Title: Broad-spectrum chromaticity and high color fastness of polyimide fibers via intrinsic coloration
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Due to the exceptional thermal stability, radiation resistance, and mechanical properties, polyimide (PI) fibers are widely used in various extreme environments. However, the intrinsic monochromatic golden hue and chemically inert surface of PI fiber give rise to a natural barrier to dyeing and low color fastness. Herein, a facile and transformative intrinsic coloration strategy for the dyeing of PI fibers is proposed by directly incorporating a perylene-based chromophore monomer into the backbone of PI. By tuning the concentration and categories of perylene derivatives, various intrinsic colors of PI fibers are afforded, constructing a diverse chromatic PI fiber library with a broad color gamut (spanning from warm tones to slate-grey). Significantly, the strategy successfully overcomes the long-standing trade-off between dyeing and mechanical integrity. Moreover, the incorporation of perylene-based chromophores exhibits excellent structural compatibility with the PI backbone, acting as reinforced components rather than stress-concentrating defects. Consequently, the fibers exhibit simultaneous enhancements in mechanical properties and exceptional color fastness against harsh environments. This work establishes a cost-effective and scalable paradigm for the functionalization of PI fibers, contributing to the expanding application of PI fibers in high-end textiles and smart wearables. © 2026

Authors: Albaba M.; Yeşilata B.
Title: Electrical performance assessment of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid power system for EV charging applications
Abstract: The integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure with renewable-based autonomous power systems presents a promising approach for distributed energy deployment. This study evaluates the electrical performance of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid system designed to supply EV charging and lighting loads in Urla, Izmir, Türkiye. Optimal system sizing is performed using HOMER, followed by detailed electrical modeling and time-domain simulations in ETAP under realistic operating conditions. The system comprises photovoltaic arrays, a wind turbine, battery energy storage with bidirectional converters, supplying EV charging and lighting loads. A deterministic time-scheduled load profile is adopted to ensure reproducibility. Scenario-based analyses across multiple operating conditions, including reduced solar irradiance, wind turbine outage, and load curtailment, are conducted over three representative days corresponding to winter, summer, and transitional conditions. Results demonstrate sustained power balance and full supply reliability, achieving 0% unmet load across all scenarios. Voltage levels remain within tight operational limits, confirming electrical stability, while battery state-of-charge profiles indicate adequate energy availability and effective storage utilization. The findings validate the operational feasibility and electrical robustness of the proposed system under variable generation and dynamic loading conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zeng Y.; Liu Y.; Mei L.
Title: Curriculum greenwashing in business statistics education: Institutional decoupling in responsible management education
Abstract: Business schools increasingly state commitments to responsible management education (RME), yet institutional commitment may not be consistently reflected in pedagogical change. This study examines curriculum greenwashing as a possible divergence between RME language in curriculum artifacts and corresponding evidence in teaching practice and student learning, without assuming deliberate intent. Drawing on institutional theory and decoupling, we test whether signatory status in the Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME) is associated with declarative, procedural, and consequential integration in undergraduate business statistics courses. Longitudinal multilevel data were collected from 215 students and 45 faculty members across 30 institutions across three waves. PRME status was positively associated with RME content in syllabi, whereas associations with reported teaching and student learning gains were not detected. Faculty-reported practices were positively associated with student learning gains. The PRME status × faculty quantitative teaching self-efficacy interaction was positive but did not reach conventional statistical significance; exploratory probing indicated a positive PRME association only at high self-efficacy. The study contributes a three-level audit framework for evaluating how institutional RME commitment is reflected across curriculum representation, reported teaching practice, and student learning, while underscoring the value of evidence beyond syllabus language alone. © 2026

Title: Recurrent and eroding challenges in creative tourism: A longitudinal study of entrepreneurial resilience among urban handicraft artisans
Abstract: Despite the growing importance of creative tourism in emerging economies, the temporal nature of the challenges facing artisans—and the resilience strategies they employ—remains poorly understood. Grounded in the processual entrepreneurial concept, this study explores how handicraft artisans understand the challenges they face and how they enact resilience in response. Adopting a longitudinal interpretivist approach, the study examines the entrepreneurial resilience of urban handicraft artisans in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, across a period of compounding crises, including the pandemic, political instability, and socioeconomic volatility. The study identifies a novel “recurrent–eroding” dichotomy as a framework for understanding challenge temporality and three resilience enablers, namely personal resources, social support networks, and operational responses. Theoretically, the study introduces new typologies of entrepreneurial challenges and extends resilience theory in creative tourism. Practically, it provides critical insights for policymakers, advocating for institutional shifts from crisis-response measures to strengthening accountable support mechanisms, market linkages, and protections for cultural work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Embodied cognition and the luxury hospitality experience of in-flight wine in premium cabins
Abstract: This study explores how first- and business-class passengers experience in-flight wine as luxurious, even though flying reduces taste and smell. Drawing on embodied cognition theory, we argue that passengers do not simply judge wine by its quality. They build a sense of luxury by noticing how the airline tries to compensate for sensory limits, by feeling that the service fits their bodily experience, and by responding emotionally. We surveyed 500 premium-cabin passengers and used two analytical approaches: structural equation modeling and necessary condition analysis. The results show two related paths to luxury: a cognitive path, in which the service feels consistent with the passenger's bodily state, and an affective path, in which the service creates positive emotions. For first-class passengers, both paths had to reach a minimum level for luxury to emerge. For business-class passengers, the cognitive path was more important, and positive emotions were less essential. These findings help airlines design in-flight wine service that still feels luxurious despite the sensory challenges of air travel. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liang Y.; Chen R.; Zeng Y.; Yin S.
Title: Beyond participation: Creativity and entrepreneurial mindset across instructional modes and learner-level digital conditions in entrepreneurship education
Abstract: Entrepreneurship education is often examined as a uniform educational exposure, although its associations with student development may depend on instructional mode and learner-level digital conditions. This study compares six entrepreneurship education formats and examines their associations with two self-perceived outcomes—creativity and entrepreneurial mindset—while assessing whether these relationships vary by perceived digital literacy and functional social media use. Drawing on survey data from 1181 graduating students at a multidisciplinary university in Guangdong, China, we use propensity score matching to improve comparability between participants and non-participants on observed characteristics and estimate interaction models to assess conditional relationships. The results indicate that entrepreneurship education is more consistently associated with entrepreneurial mindset than with creativity. Business plan competitions, training programs, and practical workshops generally show comparatively strong associations, particularly relative to entrepreneurship courses, although public lectures are also notably associated with entrepreneurial mindset. Perceived digital literacy displays a selective and format-dependent moderating relationship with creativity but does not consistently moderate the relationship with entrepreneurial mindset. Functional social media use shows no stable moderation in the primary binary models, while supplementary continuous-measure models reveal some operationalization-sensitive patterns. These findings indicate that entrepreneurship education is best understood as a heterogeneous set of learning experiences whose associations with student development vary across instructional modes, developmental outcomes, and learner-level digital conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Design-based estimation and central limit theorems for local average treatment effects for RCTs

Abstract: There is a growing literature on design-based methods to estimate average treatment effects for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) using the underpinnings of experiments. Consistent, conservative variance estimators based on model residuals are provided, and simulations show that the estimators yield confidence interval coverage near nominal levels. Title: Optimal telepresence experience in heritage tourism: A multidimensional scale and its impact on tourist behavior
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly being integrated into on-site heritage tourism, yet little is known about how visitors evaluate hybrid experiences combining physical heritage environments with VR-mediated reconstructions. Theoretically, the study advances immersive tourism research by conceptualizing and validating OTE as a higher-order experiential construct for hybrid technology-enhanced heritage experiences. Title: Designing sustainability communication across behavioral effort levels: How AI-generated micro-videos shape pro-environmental intentions
Abstract: The sustainability communication literature treats communication formats as functionally substitutable, overlooking how effectiveness may depend on the effort required to perform targeted behaviors. Drawing on processing fluency theory, this research uses perceived behavioral effort and procedural demands as an organizing lens for examining message effectiveness. Focusing on AI-generated micro-videos, the study examines how different formats influence hotel guests’ perceptions and pro-environmental intentions. Across three experiments, Study 1 demonstrated that dynamic AI-generated videos outperformed static signage, although the effect could not be attributed solely to AI generation. In Study 2, instructional clips enhanced perceived message fluency and task–technology fit for lower-effort behaviors, but not pro-environmental intentions. In Study 3, instructional clips significantly enhanced all three outcomes for higher-effort, rule-based behaviors. The study enriches sustainability communication theory by highlighting the value of explicit instructional guidance and offers actionable recommendations for designing hospitality sustainability initiatives in unfamiliar tourism service settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chen N.; Huo L.
Title: A new three-layer metapopulation networks model coupling online-offline social interactions with epidemic spread
Abstract: The dissemination of epidemic-related information can effectively enhance public awareness of preventive measures and decrease infection risks. However, information dissemination through multiple channels, including both online and offline sources, and the dynamics of information dissemination across these channels are influenced by individual mobility. To address this gap, this study develops a three-layer metapopulation network coupled model that integrates online information dissemination, epidemic spreading, and offline information dissemination. The proposed model systematically investigates the patterns of information dissemination through both online and offline channels, as well as the epidemic reaction–diffusion process driven by individual migration. Furthermore, the social interactions dynamics of both information channels are influenced by migration, manifested as migrated individuals acquire offline information in destination patches and establish online connections with individuals residing there. Theoretical analysis using the Microscopic Markov Chain Approach (MMCA) derives epidemic thresholds, while Monte Carlo (MC) simulations validate the model and examine factors influencing propagation dynamics. Results indicate that migration enhances individuals’ offline information acquisition, and accelerates cross-patch online information dissemination. Both online and offline information interactions exert inhibitory effects on epidemic spread, effectively increasing the infection threshold and reducing the outbreak scale. Furthermore, increasing the connectivity and dissemination rate of online information, particularly the information dissemination via weak relationships between patches, can effectively inhibit epidemic outbreaks. Notably, when the suppression effect of information on the epidemic is weak, population migration facilitates epidemic spread. In contrast, when the suppression effect is strong, migration-driven information dissemination significantly reduces the probability of infection, thereby further suppressing the outbreak. Title: Analogy Versus Behavioral Ecology in the Study of Human Evolution
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: In a recent critique published in this journal (Ben-Dor, M. & R. Barkai, 2026, Paleolithic dietary flexibility? Methodological considerations in analogy-based reconstructions of Paleolithic energetic returns, Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory 33, article 47, pp. 1–27), the authors characterize behavioral ecology approaches to the study of foraging efficiency as being fundamentally constrained by their reliance on conventional analogy-based reasoning. This characterization, however, misrepresents the aims and theoretical and methodological foundations of these approaches. Rather than relying on simple analogies, behavioral ecology models evaluate how interactions among variables such as prey behavior, encounter rates and contexts, seasonal variation in the macronutrient composition of game tissues, technology, pursuit success rates, opportunity costs, and other ecological and economic factors influence foraging efficiency across diverse habitats and among a wide range of societies. By explicitly identifying and testing the mechanisms that generate variation in economic returns, these approaches provide a rigorous and theory-driven alternative to conventional analogy-based interpretations. We also identify several problems with Ben-Dor and Barkai’s claim that proboscideans constituted high-ranked prey during the Lower and Middle Pleistocene. These include a selective use of relevant data, assumptions that lack sufficient empirical support, methodological shortcomings in the treatment and interpretation of the available evidence, and reliance on inadequately controlled archaeological datasets. Given these limitations, we find little support for their claim that proboscideans represented a frequent and easily acquired prey resource during the Pleistocene. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Pastoral Belonging and Educational Opportunity for Mongolian Herder Women
Abstract: As part of the UN’s International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralism (2026) the Gender Working Group stresses the importance of equality in pastoralism. For herder women themes of family, work, schooling and marginality resonate across African and Asian drylands. As environmental, economic and development pressures impact herding women are essential to its continuity. In Mongolia, a prominent pastoralist nation, the role of rural women in household decision-making, livelihood production and community contributions has received little study. In a series of interviews in two rural districts this study explores the practice and knowledge of female herders with a focus on their daily lives. Findings reflect pastoralism in a time of social and livelihood transition. Nature, livestock and tradition were valued whilst family and work responsibilities were arduous. Reflecting perceived challenges and opportunities, experienced herders encouraged daughters to pursue education. Whether growing up in the socialist era or appreciating today’s conveniences, women’s commitment to herding is a vital part of the country’s past nomadic heritage and future direction. As social roles and environmental uncertainty reconfigure pastoralism, female herders are at the forefront of changing rural communities in Mongolia. Authors: Ferdowsi A.; Aral A.
Title: Distributed neuromorphic computing with temporal co-optimization of spiking dynamics
Abstract: Neuromorphic processors and event-based sensors enable always-on perception, yet training their computational building blocks, namely spiking neural networks (SNNs) across heterogeneous edge devices, is constrained by bandwidth, latency, and energy. This paper studies the systems problem of distributing continuous-time SNN training when computation and communication are driven by sparse spike events. Building on a previously developed exact event-driven single-device learner (ExactTrain) as a local training primitive, we develop distributed protocols, an AER communication abstraction, and the associated convergence, traffic, and system analyses. In particular, we formulate: (i) FedSNN, a federated protocol that matches centralized exact-gradient training under full participation and a one-full-local-gradient regime, (ii) SplitSNN, a split protocol that partitions a model across devices and exchanges address-event representation (AER) spike and error packets, and (iii) HybridSNN, a two-tier split/federated hierarchy that exposes an explicit accuracy-communication trade-off.Experiments on the N-MNIST and DVS Gesture benchmarks evaluate centralized equivalence, split and hybrid traffic, matched-configuration and byte-accounted baseline comparisons, scalability, sensitivity to non-IID data and partition location, and trace-driven network emulation with injected bandwidth limits, jitter, and packet loss. The results reveal that the proposed protocols preserve the timing benefits of exact event-driven local learning while replacing dense activation exchange with sparse spike/error traffic whose scaling is predictable from event rates and cut connectivity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Individual entrepreneurial orientation in Spanish university students: The role of critical thinking disposition and intellectual styles in entrepreneurship education
Abstract: This study proposes a model that links students' disposition toward critical thinking (DTCT), Type I intellectual styles (oriented toward creativity, cognitive complexity, and autonomy) and Type II intellectual styles (oriented toward structure, conformity, and rule adherence), and individual entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) in higher education. A cross-sectional survey was administered to 208 students enrolled in entrepreneurship-related courses at a Spanish public university, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results show that DTCT is a strong positive predictor of IEO; Type I intellectual styles are positively related to both DTCT and IEO, whereas Type II styles display negative relations with entrepreneurial orientation. DTCT improves the effect of Type I styles on IEO, but not with Type II styles. These findings suggest that strengthening DTCT is a central pathway through which entrepreneurship education can enhance students' IEO. The study argues that entrepreneurship courses should explicitly treat DTCT and IEO as learning outcomes and intentionally adapt tasks, scaffolding, and assessment to diverse intellectual style profiles in order to support more inclusive and opportunity-oriented entrepreneurial learning. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Integrated system dynamics modeling for sustainable fisheries provisioning services
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Fisheries provisioning services deliver food production, livelihoods and ecosystem functions, but are increasingly under pressure from environmental degradation, declining fishery resources and socio-economic stressors. Traditional paradigms in fisheries governance often exhibit a deficiency in accounting for the multidirectional feedback loops linking ecological systems with socio-economic dynamics. The objectives of this study were to develop an integrated system dynamics model to assess interactions between these dimensions and identify management options to improve fisheries provisioning services through long-term scenario simulations. METHODS: A system dynamics model was integrated, consisting of social, environmental, and economic sub-models using primary and secondary data from 2018-2023. The model includes population, fishermen, floating net cages, alternative employment, willingness to be a fisher, water quality and aquatic conditions, fish restocking, capture fisheries production, fisheries productivity, fish processing innovations, income, costs, and fisher's income. The model was verified and validated using the mean absolute error and average variation error metrics. Subsequently, predictive simulations were projected to 2045 under current, moderate, and optimistic scenarios. FINDINGS: Actual capture fisheries production declined by 88.9 percent, from 588,100 kilograms in 2018 to 65,035 kilograms in 2023 and was projected to decline to 31,179 kilograms by 2045 under current conditions. Under the moderate and optimistic scenarios, the number of floating net cages was modeled with an annual reduction rate of 30% and 35%, respectively. Production recovery commenced in 2027 under the moderate scenario and in 2026 under the optimistic scenario. Furthermore, target water quality conditions were achieved by 2041 and 2037, respectively, while fisher's net income reached positive values by 2034. CONCLUSION: The integrated system dynamics model underscores the potential for the sustainability of fishery production services through coordinated actions across social, environmental, and economic dimensions. The faster realization of target outcomes under the optimistic scenario highlights that proactive, coordinated interventions effectively expedite ecological restoration, fisheries output, and socioeconomic progress. This model offers a decision-support framework for assessing long-term fisheries management strategies. © 2027 The author(s).
