Title: Teaching AI governance in management education: A serious game for accountable decision-making under uncertainty
Abstract: Management education increasingly needs ways to prepare students for AI governance, yet students have limited opportunities to practise the organisational judgement involved in deployment decisions. This paper presents “Leading in the Age of AI”, a card-based serious game in which student teams assume asymmetric C-suite roles, make AI deployment decisions under constraints, and document their reasoning in Model Cards adapted from AI documentation practice. Conceptually, the paper frames AI governance education as accountable decision-making under uncertainty: students negotiate competing priorities, allocate scarce safeguards, respond to disruption, and prepare written accounts for scrutiny. The paper contributes a reusable game design, a pedagogical adaptation of Model Cards as justification artefacts, and design patterns for management-education contexts involving accountable decisions under uncertainty. An exploratory evaluation across two undergraduate cohorts used matched pre-test/post-test data (N=67), post-session evaluations, and descriptive artefact analysis of team-produced Model Cards (n=15). Students evaluated the activity positively and reported immediate confidence gains across knowledge, ethics, and governance composites (dz=0.44 to 1.00), while quiz gains were modest and not statistically significant. Model Card analysis suggests the activity generated inspectable governance reasoning, while leaving causal learning, retention, and transfer for future research. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Lehto X.; Lee Y.J.; Chen J.
Title: Dance as destination infrastructure: Toward a progress agenda
Abstract: Tourism destinations increasingly seek embodied, multisensory, and culturally meaningful experiences whose significance extends beyond immediate consumption. Yet tourism management still has a limited vocabulary for explaining how embodied cultural practices generate value across destination systems. This Progress paper uses dance as a focused and theoretically revealing case to address this gap. Rather than treating dance merely as entertainment, heritage representation, or event programming, we conceptualize it as relational, embodied cultural infrastructure through which patterned movement can organize encounters, carry cultural meaning across generations, and contribute to the character and capabilities of destinations. Drawing on tourism's anthropological lineage and interdisciplinary dance scholarship, we develop the Dance Ecosystem for Destinations—a seven-biome framework that distinguishes encounter-level value realization, portfolio-level accumulation and circulation, and cross-cutting technological mediation. The framework expands tourism management's conceptual and diagnostic capacity by linking these biomes to questions of experience design, stewardship, governance, value distribution, and evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effects of a design thinking education program for kindergarteners: A mixed-methods study
Abstract: Children as young as three can engage in oral and visual planning when creating tangible objects from materials, yet it remains unclear whether such design competencies can be systematically strengthened in early childhood to cultivate future design thinkers and innovative creators. To evaluate a research-informed design thinking (DT) education program, we conducted a mixed-methods study. The quantitative component involved a quasi-experiment with 133 children ( M age = 5.22, SD = 0.86) from a Chinese kindergarten (intervention group: n = 68; business-as-usual comparison group: n = 65), where the intervention group received an eight-week DT program. Each child’s DT competence was assessed immediately before and after the intervention, followed by play-based interviews with 12 children (six per group). Child-level analyses indicated a statistically significant improvement in overall DT competence favoring the intervention group (Cohen’s d=0.38). However, gains were uneven across specific DT dimensions. Children showed more apparent gains in Empathize, Define, and Prototype, whereas no significant gains were observed in Ideate and Test. Furthermore, the youngest children appeared to show larger gains, whereas gender did not significantly moderate the intervention effects. Qualitative interviews provided insight into the cognitive processes underlying these developmental variations. Together, these preliminary findings may inform DT education research and practice in early childhood settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Social-ecological resilience and environmental justice in Bangladesh: A multi-site analysis of sand mining governance
Abstract: As global demand for sand reaches an estimated 50 billion tonnes annually, the pressure on fluvial and coastal ecosystems has created a significant sustainability crisis. This study examines the environmental and socioeconomic impacts of sand mining in Bangladesh, a deltaic country where rapid urbanization has transformed sand into a multi-billion-dollar industry. Combining Social-Ecological Systems (SES) and Environmental Justice (EJ) frameworks, the research uses a qualitative case study approach across three ecologically distinct sites: Chandpur (river confluence), Sandwip (estuarine island), and Cox's Bazar (mainland coast). Data from 39 semi-structured interviews and field observations show that unregulated extraction is reported and observed as coinciding with a self-reinforcing (positive) feedback loop of increased riverbank erosion and habitat loss that respondents associate with harm to the livelihoods of marginalized fishers and farmers. The results reveal a triple failure of justice: distributive (unequal erosion burdens), procedural (exclusion from leasing decisions), and recognitional (marginalization of local ecological knowledge). Additionally, an analysis of the Balumohal and Soil Management Act (2010) uncovers critical institutional issues, including political patronage and poor coordination between the Department of Environment and local authorities. By highlighting community stories of adaptation and displacement, this study contends that sustainable resource management must shift from top-down, revenue-focused models to participatory, justice-driven frameworks that safeguard the resilience of rural social-ecological systems. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Integrating theory of planned behavior and value-belief-norm framework to explain voluntary carbon offsetting intentions in aviation: Evidence from Vietnamese air passengers
Abstract: The aviation industry faces growing environmental criticism for its high greenhouse gas emissions, necessitating both technological and behavioral solutions to mitigate climate change. This study examines passengers’ willingness to pay for voluntary carbon offsetting programs by developing and empirically testing an integrated model combining the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Values-Beliefs-Norms (VBN) framework. Using data from 342 Vietnamese airline passengers, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze both direct and indirect relationships among key constructs. Within the TPB framework, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control are strong predictors of the intention to participate in voluntary carbon offsetting, with perceived behavioral control exerting the largest effect. Mediation analysis reveals that attitudinal and normative pathways bridge moral and cognitive antecedents with behavioral intention, underscoring the complementary roles of rational and moral motivations. The integrated TPB-VBN model demonstrates considerable explanatory power, providing a useful framework for understanding pro-environmental behavior in aviation. Title: Carbon coordination-driven regulation of reactive species pathways in Fe-N-C catalysts for enhanced activity and stability
Abstract: Fe-N-C catalysts featuring Fe-N4 active sites are promising yet exhibit structurally similar Fe-N4 first-shell coordination environments that evolve distinct reaction pathways with unclear origins. Herein, carbon coordination in Fe-N4 single-atom is found to reprogram interfacial electronic and spin structures, enabling bifurcated reactive species evolution and reshaping activity-stability trade-off. Specifically, M-FeNC catalyst exhibits superior activity compared to M-HFeNC (0.2998 vs 0.266 min−1), yet inferior stability (67.6% vs 87.5%) after ten cycles, with high-valent iron species predominating in M-FeNC and 1O2 prevailing in M-HFeNC. 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that FeN4C10 possesses a balanced electronic distribution, facilitates well-matched spin exchange and promotes PMS coupling. This configuration enables efficient 1O2 generation while minimizing structural reconstruction, thereby preserving high catalytic stability. In contrast, FeN4C12 exhibits enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized HOMO-LUMO coupling, which favors high-valent iron formation, but induces pronounced Fe-N bond fluctuations and local carbon reconstruction, ultimately compromising stability despite high activity. Furthermore, CPET-driven high-valent iron species-mediated polymerization pathway for phenolic pollutants was unveiled. This work provides molecular-level insight into how carbon coordination regulates reactive species pathways and thereby governs the activity-stability balance in Fe-N-C catalysts, establishing essential design principle for rational catalyst engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Speech-driven dialogic question generation for preschool picture book reading: a cognitive-level-aware spoken interaction system using pre-trained language models
Abstract: The quality of preschool children's language development depends largely on the cognitive level of questioning strategies employed during shared reading interactions; however, existing intelligent dialogic reading systems predominantly rely on fixed question scripts and lack the capacity for dynamic adaptation to narrative context and children's cognitive needs. Title: Validity and Reliability of the Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle Method for Determining Masticatory Preference in Children Before Premolar Transition

Abstract: Objective: To evaluate the validity and reliability of Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle (PFMA) method with a modified device compared to the clinical method as the gold standard for determining masticatory preference side in children. The outcome measures were the validity and reliability of the PFMA method compared to the clinical method as the gold standard. Conclusion: The Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle with a modified device proved to be a method with good validity and a useful tool as a screening test to identify the masticatory preference side. Abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) faces an intrinsic trade-off between activity and selectivity, primarily due to the lack of well-defined and functionally differentiated active sites. Herein, a SubPc/Ag–ZnIn2S4 (SubPc/Ag–ZIS) S-scheme heterojunction is constructed by coordinating subphthalocyanine (SubPc–Br) onto Ag cluster-decorated ZnIn2S4. Distinct from conventional dual-site catalysts, this work achieves atomic-precision site differentiation via boron coordination chemistry, where the electron-rich B–Ag site activates O2, and the B–S site lowers the H2O2 desorption barrier. More importantly, the interfacial potential difference drives directional migration of the activated ·O2− intermediate from B–Ag to B–S, establishing an unprecedented “activation–migration–desorption” relay pathway. Femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) confirms that this dual-site synergy significantly prolongs the charge carrier lifetime, providing a favorable kinetic foundation. The optimal catalyst delivers a H2O2 production rate of 1200 μmol g−1 h−1 with a 2e− ORR selectivity of 78%. In the presence of tetracycline (TC) wastewater, hole-driven TC degradation (reaching 93.5% within 60 min) further inhibits charge recombination and synergistically increases the hydrogen peroxide generation rate to 1579.8 μmol g−1 h−1. This work establishes a boron coordination chemistry-driven dual-site relay catalysis strategy, offering a new paradigm for integrating efficient H2O2 photosynthesis with pollutant degradation. © 2026

Authors: Khedhiri S.
Title: Predictors of Death Related to Drug Use Disorder and Interpersonal Violence in North Africa
Abstract: Fatal interpersonal violence and deadly drug use disorder are serious social issues resulting from criminal behavior, which require effective intervention policies. Prior research on African countries is limited, and the potential association between the two issues, as described in the literature, has not been investigated. In this study, a statistical analysis was performed with R packages to identify factors that predict the death patterns related to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence, and to show empirical evidence for the association between drugs and violence in North Africa. Data on annual counts of deaths attributed to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence between 1990 and 2023 were collected, and a bivariate copula modeling approach was adopted to account for the dependence of the two counts. The findings show that socioeconomic factors, including per-capita gross domestic product, youth unemployment rate, and urban population, are significant predictors of these death counts, and statistical tests show a positive relationship between deaths related to drug use disorder and deaths caused by interpersonal violence. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Environmental performance of hydrogen production via eucalyptus biomass gasification and natural gas steam reforming: A life cycle assessment approach
Abstract: A life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted to compare hydrogen production via steam methane reforming (SMR) of natural gas and eucalyptus biomass gasification under Brazilian conditions. Three scenarios were evaluated for the production of 1 kg of hydrogen: (i) SMR, (ii) SMR with carbon capture and storage (SMR-CCS), and (iii) Gasification-WGS (eucalyptus gasification with water–gas shift reaction). The ReCiPe 2016 midpoint method was applied, with normalization used to identify the most relevant impact categories. Global warming potential (GWP) was confirmed as the most critical category by both midpoint and endpoint results. SMR generated 10.13 kg CO2-eq, SMR-CCS 6.40 kg CO2-eq, and Gasification–WGS 1.30 kg CO2-eq per kg of hydrogen, corresponding to reductions of 36.8% and 87.2% relative to conventional SMR, respectively. Carbon capture reduced the climate impact of the fossil route but did not result in net-negative emissions. SMR-CCS showed higher burdens than conventional SMR in seventeen of the eighteen impact categories assessed, most markedly in water consumption (14.1-fold) and land use (8.5-fold), the latter arising from the biomass-fired cogeneration supplying MEA regeneration heat. Gasification-WGS achieved the lowest climate impact but did not dominate across all indicators: it outperformed conventional SMR in nine of the eighteen categories and underperformed in the remaining nine, most notably in land use (37-fold), water consumption (3.8-fold), marine eutrophication (2.3-fold) and freshwater ecotoxicity (2.2-fold). The comparison therefore describes a trade-off in which the biomass route exchanges carbon and fossil resources for land, water and nutrient pressure. Overall, the results indicate that the preferred pathway depends on which environmental priority dominates in a given region: eucalyptus gasification offers the largest climate and fossil-resource benefit, while carbon capture on the fossil route delivers a smaller climate gain at the cost of increased impacts in nearly every other category. By addressing both climate mitigation and resource sustainability, this study provides guidance for policymakers and industry in developing low-carbon hydrogen pathways adapted to regional conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Jin S.; Ma J.; Ma J.; Dang L.; Chen B.
Title: TacFG-9: A tactile-vision-language dataset for factorized fine-grained tactile semantics
Abstract: Tactile semantics provide essential physical cues for understanding object properties during robotic interaction. However, existing tactile-language datasets primarily rely on coarse tactile semantics and lack systematic annotations for fine-grained tactile semantics, which makes it difficult to generate semantically faithful descriptions under partial tactile observations. To address this issue, we introduce TacFG-9, a fine-grained tactile-vision-language dataset constructed through a three-level, nine-dimensional annotation framework. Each TacFG-9 sample combines a tactile observation, visual context, a verified caption, and structured tactile semantic labels organized from material identity to local perceptual cues. To scale TacFG-9 while maintaining annotation reliability, we use model-assisted expansion to explicitly identify samples with uncertain or semantically inconsistent predictions and route them to targeted human review. Building on TacFG-9, we further propose TacRAGate, a similarity-gated tactile captioning framework for reliable fine-grained description generation. TacRAGate uses retrieved verified captions and fine-grained tactile attribute labels as evidence, estimates evidence reliability using the top-1 retrieval similarity, and accordingly switches among Direct Retrieval, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Low-Evidence Generation. Experiments demonstrate that the structured tactile-vision-language supervision in TacFG-9 improves tactile representation learning, while TacRAGate produces more semantically faithful tactile descriptions than existing tactile captioning methods under partial observations. Title: Trends in molecular gastronomy
Abstract: Molecular gastronomy, a fusion of food science and culinary art, applies scientific principles to modify and transform ingredients and culinary techniques. By understanding the physical and chemical mechanisms and properties of food, scientists and researchers create various innovative foods with different, unique textures, flavors, and appearances. Recent trends in molecular gastronomy highlight the importance of eco-conscious practices by incorporating plant-based ingredients, microbes, and novel techniques to generate novel foods. Additionally, advancements in food technology, such as 3D printing, allow customization of food products with novel ingredients and complex geometric structures with personalized nutritional food products, have also evolved and developed. This paper mainly aims to focus on the recent advancements in molecular gastronomy and the recent trends in foods, with different technologies also being discussed. Different methodologies, which include foam and emulsion, gelation, smoke infusion, specification techniques, and methodologies, have been implemented in food products to improve product sustainability, product consistency, and public acceptance toward the product. Various products, such as encapsulated products, nano products, 3D printed products, functional foods, and novel foods, have also been developed with the emerging molecular gastronomy techniques. The benefits and challenges of molecular gastronomy foods and the new culinary future trends have been discussed with molecular gastronomy. © 2026

Authors: Liu J.; Fang Y.; Tao Y.; Jiang B.; Khairuddin U.; Lee Y.; Liu Q.
Title: EIMa: Efficient and robust local feature matching with interleaved Mamba
Abstract: The trade-off between accuracy and efficiency remains a fundamental challenge in feature matching. Although recent Mamba-based detector-free matchers such as JamMa achieve remarkable performance in outdoor scenes with low inference latency, their lightweight parameterization and reliance on purely sequential modeling constrain generalization capabilities, leading to significant degradation in complex indoor environments. To address this limitation, we propose EIMa, a novel feature matching framework that effectively balances accuracy and computational efficiency. First, we propose an interleaved scan strategy that spatially interweaves tokens from both views at the feature level to promote high-frequency cross-view interactions. Second, we design a sparse omnidirectional scan scheme coupled with a lightweight global aggregator, which substantially reduces the scan sequence length while preserving a global receptive field. Finally, we introduce an aggregated attention mechanism that synergizes with these scan paradigms to strengthen cross-view global modeling, thereby significantly enhancing generalization in challenging scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EIMa achieves a superior performance-efficiency trade-off, providing an efficient and robust solution for lightweight local feature matching. Title: A bi-objective optimization model to plan vaccination campaigns aided by temporary centers
Abstract: Vaccination campaigns have saved thousands of lives and reached even the world's most remote areas. However, the COVID-19 pandemic significantly changed the strategies for such campaigns. It is now crucial to rigorously consider new factors when planning the operational aspects of these campaigns, particularly for last-mile vaccine dispensing. First, a large share of the population must be vaccinated, with emphasis on vulnerable groups at higher risk. Second, if the virus is highly contagious and capable of asymptomatic transmission, implementing public health measures at vaccination sites becomes paramount. To address these challenges, we propose a bi-objective optimization model to support healthcare decision-making. It defines a schedule for locating temporary vaccination centers and assigning populations to permanent and temporary sites over a planning horizon. Moreover, we formalize and validate a minimum set of properties for a function-based prioritization mechanism to ensure consistent prioritization. One objective prioritizes vaccinating vulnerable groups according to our novel function-based approach, while the other minimizes the operational costs of temporary centers. In the complex environment of a pandemic, the strategic integration and use of temporary and permanent vaccination centers is vital for creating a robust and responsive vaccination strategy. Temporary centers, whose locations are determined by the model, improve access for hard-to-reach groups, contribute to minimizing crowding at permanent sites, and lower infection risks. Our results, demonstrated through a case study, show that the model effectively allocates resources and generates various vaccination plans that cater to different priority levels assigned to each objective, thereby offering valuable decision support. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Abstract: The present study investigates the phonological and morphological changes of Persian loanwords during their localization process in Ottoman Turkish, as well as the influence of the Persian language on Ottoman Turkish, using a descriptive-analytical approach. To this end, data comprising approximately 6,000 Persian loanwords were collected and analyzed through a comprehensive examination of dictionaries, glossaries of definitions and allusions, thematic dictionaries, and encyclopedias compiled in Anatolia during the Ottoman period.Using Microsoft Excel and computer-assisted analysis, the frequency and percentage of occurrence of common phonological and morphological processes were calculated. The findings reveal that among the phonetic and phonological processes examined—including vowel harmony, phonemic over-differentiation, assimilation, metathesis, insertion, deletion, lenition, and weakening—vowel harmony, one of the most prominent characteristics of Turkish as an agglutinative language, exhibits the highest frequency.In the morphological domain, where the processes of compounding and derivation were analyzed, derivation was found to be the most frequent process. Despite the typological differences between Persian and Turkish, the linguistic interaction between these two languages has been extensive. This interaction has resulted in a remarkably asymmetrical influence, reflected in the substantial number of Persian loanwords found in Ottoman Turkish. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Ionized magnesium in serum measured using a blood gas analyser: Agreement with whole blood, short-term stability and preliminary reference interval in healthy adults
Abstract: Objectives Ionized magnesium (iMg) is the biologically active fraction of circulating magnesium, yet its use in routine practice remains limited. This study evaluated serum iMg measurement using a blood gas analyser, focusing on agreement with whole blood, short-term pre-analytical stability, and factors associated with iMg concentrations in healthy adults. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 60 healthy individuals were included. iMg was measured in paired whole blood and serum samples using a blood gas analyser. Agreement between matrices was assessed using Spearman correlation, Passing–Bablok regression, and Bland–Altman analysis. Serum stability was evaluated at 4 and 24 h under refrigerated conditions. Multivariable linear regression was used to identify factors associated with iMg concentrations. A preliminary reference interval was estimated according to CLSI EP28-A3c. Results Serum and whole blood iMg showed strong correlation (ρ = 0.727; p < 0.001) with minimal systematic bias, although variability between matrices was observed. Serum iMg remained within acceptable limits at 4 h but exceeded the maximum permissible instability at 24 h. The preliminary reference interval for whole blood iMg was 0.53–0.68 mmol/L, with a corresponding interval in serum of 0.49–0.71 mmol/L. In multivariable analysis, total magnesium was the only variable independently associated with iMg concentrations (β = 0.658; p < 0.001). Conclusions Serum iMg measured using a blood gas analyser may represent a feasible alternative matrix under controlled pre-analytical conditions. However, its limited stability requires timely analysis. These findings support a stepwise approach to magnesium assessment, in which iMg may be considered as a reflex test in patients with low or near-low total magnesium concentrations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Continuity and Discontinuity in Artefact Distributions from Multi-Period Archaeological Sites
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Artefact finds recovered by metal detecting and reported by members of the public are a growing source of archaeological information, with over 1.2 million finds recorded to date by the Portable Antiquities Scheme in England and Wales. Heritage schemes in many other European countries where hobby detecting for archaeology is legal likewise report growing numbers of finds. Using point pattern analysis, this paper presents a worked-out set of computational methods to study diachronic processes within artefact assemblages at field or local (e.g. parish) levels. We present a simulated ‘toy’ example to illustrate the methodology and test it with two large artefact assemblages from the counties of North Yorkshire and Norfolk that differ in terms of finds record quality and known contextual archaeological landscape information. The proposed approach and example code can be reapplied to other archaeological point patterns. It formalises a spatial statistical workflow that produces an assessment regarding landscape persistence and reuse, and which can be used, for example, to assist fieldwork or planning decisions by identifying areas for further research. The case studies highlight the considerable need for formal analytical workflows in public finds research, which can be easily deployed at different sites and local assemblages. Moreover, while the proposed workflow has been designed with public finds scatters in mind, it is scale-agnostic and can be reapplied to investigate a range of archaeological phenomena from monument distributions across a larger region to investigating artefact scatters within an excavated area. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Perceived authenticity of AI-generated tourism video and destination attractiveness: An entity-referent correspondence perspective
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Grounded in the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how three authenticity dimensions of AI-generated destination portrayals, true-to-ideal, true-to-fact, and true-to-self, relate to destination attractiveness via parallel and sequential pathways of place imagination and mental simulation. Analysis of 406 participants exposed to an AI-generated tourism video reveals that true-to-ideal and true-to-fact authenticity show significant direct effects on destination attractiveness, whereas true-to-self authenticity operates entirely indirectly, consistent with a meaning-making route. For parallel mediation, true-to-ideal and true-to-self authenticity exert significant indirect effects via both mediators, whereas true-to-fact authenticity does so only through place imagination. The sequential pathway from place imagination to mental simulation receives consistent support across all dimensions. Theoretically, this study advances the ERC framework from a static typology to a processual account by delineating the distinct cognitive routes of each referent and highlighting both the conceptual promise and measurement challenges of operationalizing true-to-self authenticity as perceived communicative sincerity in algorithmically generated portrayals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Micro-foundations of destination supply: A configural analysis of herders’ livelihood strategies in grassland tourism
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Based on the revised Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis was used to investigate the combinatorial effects of social, human, cultural, policy, physical, natural, and financial capital on herders' livelihood strategies in Chen Barag in the Hulunbuir Grassland, to identify the key drivers of herders’ adoption of a tourism livelihood. The results identify six differentiated livelihood configuration types. Traditional pastoral livelihoods are associated with resource-constrained configurations and high thresholds for tourism participation under ecological, market, and institutional conditions. Conversely, mixed livelihoods are associated with configurations involving productive resource release, locational advantages, cultural commodification, and intergenerational labour division, while governance tensions between institutional arrangements and diversified livelihood needs may create additional constraints. These findings highlight the joint importance of asset-related thresholds and institutional conditions in shaping differentiated tourism participation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Bridging single-species models to ecosystem-based maximum sustainable yield for environmental sustainability in marine fisheries
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: Maximum sustainable yield remains a central biological reference concept in fisheries management. Its reliability is shaped by model assumptions, uncertainty, ecological interactions, and environmental change. The study objectives were to reconstruct the mathematical progression of maximum sustainable yield, from single-species deterministic models to ecosystem-based, multispecies formulations. The critical narrative review synthesizes the paradigm shift in ecological modeling, tracing its trajectory from equilibrium-based single-species frameworks to holistic, ecosystem-aware formulations. Classical production models are compared with age-structured, stock-recruitment, bioeconomic, precautionary, and multispecies approaches. The assumptions, data needs, uncertainty, and management implications are evaluated. Eight fisheries cases are used to illustrate contrasts in data availability, assessment methods, harvest rules, ecosystem awareness, and shared-stock governance. These cases are treated as illustrative examples rather than a representative validation sample. Evidence shows that trophic interactions can alter species-specific and system-level reference points. The direction of change depends on food-web structure, selectivity, interaction strength, environmental productivity, and management objectives. Environmental variation can also affect growth, recruitment, natural mortality, habitat capacity, and species interactions. Accordingly, biological reference points require adaptive updating when stock productivity exhibits nonstationarity, precluding their interpretation as rigid constants amidst shifting environmental conditions. Economic objectives, social needs, and conservation goals must also be distinguished from biological yield objectives. A five-dimension readiness framework is proposed as a preliminary hypothesis-generating heuristic. Alternative weighting schemes indicate that some borderline classifications are sensitive to assumptions. Independent validation and inter-rater testing are therefore required before operational use. While substantial data constraints persist across multiple Indonesian fisheries, these limitations must not be regarded as the sole impediment to comprehensive management. Governance, enforcement, fleet structure, socioeconomic incentives, habitat condition, and climate variability can independently affect performance. Greater use of adaptive monitoring, precautionary harvest rules, uncertainty analysis, and ecosystem indicators is therefore recommended. Multispecies assessment should be prioritized where trophic or technical interactions materially influence stock dynamics. Maximum sustainable yield is best retained as an analytical reference point rather than a literal catch target. Environmentally sustainable application requires precautionary, adaptive, and ecosystem-based governance frameworks dynamically aligned with local empirical data quality, ecological conditions, and institutional capabilities. Title: Cognitive appraisal of illegitimate tasks and research creativity: dual reflective processing pathways in graduate education
Abstract: Although graduate students frequently encounter illegitimate tasks—assignments perceived as inconsistent with their research roles—little is known about how such tasks influence research creativity and through what cognitive mechanisms. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), a dual-pathway model is proposed in which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity through problem-solving pondering and affective rumination, with supervisor–student relationship quality as a moderator. Data were collected from 389 graduate students in Chinese universities using a two-wave survey design, and the hypothesized moderated mediation model was tested using hierarchical regression analyses supplemented by the PROCESS macro. The results indicate that illegitimate tasks exert opposing indirect effects on research creativity through distinct reflective cognitive pathways. Illegitimate tasks were associated with increased affective rumination, which interfered with sustained creative engagement. However, under high-quality supervisor-student relationships, illegitimate tasks were more strongly related to problem-solving pondering, which facilitated creative thinking. Supervisor-student relationship quality further shaped how illegitimate tasks were interpreted and which reflective pathway was activated. These findings clarify the cognitive mechanisms and relational conditions through which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity and contribute to understanding how task legitimacy shapes creative thinking in graduate research contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hasegawa T.
Title: Applied economic reasoning in air transport management: A question- and concept-level analysis of an airport business course
Abstract: Economic reasoning underpins business decision-making. Yet how it is taught and assessed in air transport management education remains underexplored. Drawing on final-exam data from an Airport Business course for non-specialists at a Japanese university, this study identifies aspects of assessed economic reasoning that appeared relatively more demanding. At the question level, the higher-difficulty side concerned airport network financing, restructuring, and public support, whereas the lower-difficulty side addressed charge pass-through, the club-good characteristics of small-airport services, and concession-contract risks. At the concept level, government failure, incentives, and user-pays lay on the higher-difficulty side, while demand and costs, price discrimination, and public, private, and club goods fell on the lower-difficulty side. This concept-level pattern did not follow a simple foundational–advanced distinction, with positions varying across institutional contexts and concept co-occurrence. These patterns remained broadly stable in supplementary analyses assessing sensitivity to question selection. The findings add a question- and concept-level perspective to research on air transport management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Digital Literacy through a Web-Based Application: Addressing Polarization and Promoting Social Integration among Islamic Senior High School Students

Abstract: Digital literacy encompasses not only technical skills but also an understanding of social dynamics such as polarization and the need for social integration in digital environments. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of a web-based Mobile Polarization and Social Integration application in improving students’ digital literacy. A quasi-experimental design with a control group was employed, involving students from an Islamic senior high school. Data were collected using a validated test and analyzed through comparative statistical methods. Title: Enhancing college students’ reflective thinking through online visualized collaborative argumentation: An exploratory study
Abstract: In this era of technological advancements, how to better support students in argumentation-based computer-supported collaborative learning using emerging interactive technology to develop their reflective thinking has become an important issue in talent development. This study was embedded in the Cognition of Multimedia Learning course, and involved a pre- and posttest experiment with 56 college students to investigate the effects of visualized collaborative argumentation on their reflective thinking. The relationships between students’ argumentation and changes in their reflective thinking were also examined. Moreover, the differences in cognitive performance in argumentation among students with different levels of change in reflective thinking were explored using epistemic network analysis. The findings revealed that visualized collaborative argumentation significantly enhanced students’ reflective thinking. Especially, the higher the students’ level of engagement in rebuttal, the greater the impact on their reflective thinking. Moreover, according to the changes in reflective thinking behavior scores, K-Means cluster analysis determined a high-level change group (N = 33) and a low-level change group (N = 23). The findings revealed that the high-level change group outperformed the low-level change group in cognitive performance. Students with high-level change in reflective thinking are more adept at illustrating ideas through examples or attributes to avoid unclear understanding by others; they are more able to make direct rebuttals and evaluations, or to ask counter-questions; they show more rigor in deduction, pursuing the sufficiency of evidence; and they are good at using divergent thinking to break through thinking limitations. This exploratory study suggests that online visualized collaborative argumentation may have potential for supporting college students’ reflective thinking. The findings offer preliminary implications for the design of instructional strategies aimed at fostering reflective thinking development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Structural integration of inert porous media as a primary mitigation strategy for firewood stoves: Toward decoupling combustion intensification from emissions
Abstract: Residential wood combustion in energy-vulnerable contexts creates a critical trade-off between thermal comfort and air quality, while many conventional emission-control technologies require electricity, maintenance, or active control. This study evaluates the structural integration of inert porous media (IPM) within a commercial residential wood stove as a passive primary mitigation strategy. Combustion cycles, conducted following an adapted EPA Method 5G protocol, compared the baseline stove with the IPM-integrated prototype. IPM operation showed a tendency toward a more intensive fuel-conversion regime together with thermal redistribution toward the stove enclosure. Median thermal efficiency was 29.3 % higher, while exhaust-gas temperature decreased by 6.0 % and outer lateral-wall temperature increased by 18.8 %. Despite the higher burning rate, PM2.5 and CO mass emission factors showed directional decreases of 65.5 % and 30.9 %, respectively; HC remained essentially unchanged, whereas NOx increased. Particle-number emission factors were lower across most of the measured 0.253–35.15 µm size range. Useful-energy normalization strengthened the environmental benefit, with PM2.5 and CO decreasing by 76.3 % and 33.4 % per unit of useful heat delivered; HC shifted toward a lower burden, whereas the NOx increase was attenuated but remained. Overall, the findings support a pollutant-specific tendency toward decoupling combustion intensification from incomplete-combustion emissions and identify structural IPM integration as a promising passive strategy for improving residential wood-heating performance without auxiliary energy input, particularly where affordability and operational simplicity constrain advanced emission-control technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tran T.
Title: Inner-supportive destinations for psychologically vulnerable solo travelers: A framework of narrative reconstruction and reintegrative stabilization
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: This study examines how inner-supportive destination experiences support psychological reconstruction among solo visitors reporting self-identified emotional disruption. Drawing on constructivist grounded theory and 30 in-depth interviews with domestic solo visitors to Da Lat, Vietnam, the research identifies a process through which pre-travel emotional disruption is gradually reorganized through destination experience. Findings show that participants did not travel merely for leisure or stress relief, but because burnout, grief, relational rupture, life transition, or identity uncertainty had unsettled their self-understanding. Inner-supportive affordances, including temporal deceleration, sensory softness, perceived safety, and supported solitude, reduced defensive pressure and created conditions for regulated emotional exposure. This exposure enabled narrative re-authoring, through which distressing experiences were reinterpreted and integrated into a more coherent self-understanding. Based on these accounts, the study proposes the inner-supportive destination framework, explaining how destination affordances, regulated emotional exposure, narrative re-authoring, participant-attributed reintegrative stabilization, and boundary conditions relate within a contingent process. Theoretically, the study extends destination marketing and management by distinguishing narrative reconstruction from restoration, healing, or emotional elevation. Practically, it offers guidance for designing vulnerability-sensitive destinations that support autonomy, low-pressure engagement, and safe solitude without making therapeutic claims. The findings invite broader applications of inner-supportive design across wellness, cultural, nature-based, and urban retreat contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Choe Y.; Kim H.
Title: A stock-and-flow perspective on destination brand equity across the PyeongChang Olympic period: Evidence from a two-wave panel
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: This study examines how destination brand equity was distributed across the PyeongChang 2018 Olympic period. A matched panel of 502 U.S.-based target-market respondents evaluated South Korea approximately three months before and three months after the Games. The post-event measure intentionally captured evaluations attributed by respondents to hosting the Games and is therefore interpreted as an early event-attributed response rather than a causal Olympic effect. Separate-wave latent profile analyses, supported by focused four-versus-five-state validation, retained five ordered destination-brand-equity states. Average destination brand equity was higher at the post-event observation (mean difference = .340), but this positive net difference coexisted with substantial between-person heterogeneity. A fixed-criterion regression-to-the-mean benchmark reproduced the small residual net direction but not the observed volume of gross bidirectional redistribution, while reliable-change analysis indicated that most respondents did not exceed a conservative change threshold. After baseline adjustment, media consumption and hosting appraisal were positively associated with the post-event score, whereas their interaction was not significant. The findings show why aggregate brand tracking and individual-level diagnostics should be interpreted jointly and distinguish early event-attributed responses from durable mega-event legacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From airplanes to classrooms: A cross-domain literature review of seating assignment models and methods
Abstract: Seating assignments play an important role in customer-focused managerial decisions, yet existing studies are frequently limited in scope to isolated application domains. This paper addresses this fragmentation through the first systematic cross-domain seating assignment literature review, analyzing publications via bibliometric analysis and examining assignment methods (including optimization techniques) across transportation (airplanes and trains), dining establishments, entertainment venues, and classrooms. Co-citation analysis reveals that research communities operate in separate networks despite addressing similar challenges using mathematical programming, heuristic approaches, stochastic simulation, and other operational research methods. Our cross-domain synthesis identifies technique transfer opportunities previously invisible due to research silos, such as applying restaurant group-seating strategies to airline passengers traveling together or entertainment venue considerations to dining table assignments. The review concludes that limited real-world implementation stems partly from researchers' inability to access successful approaches from adjacent fields, highlighting opportunities to advance seating assignment methods through integrated frameworks. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Authors: Yang H.-K.; Wang C.; Li J.-Z.; Song S.-L.; Jiang Y.-M.; Ning H.; Wang H.-Y.
Title: Multi-layered texture-heterogeneous architecture enabling strength-ductility synergy in Mg laminates
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Achieving strength-ductility synergy in Mg alloys remains challenging because their inherent plastic anisotropy leads to a trade-off between texture-induced strengthening and strain accommodation. Here, we designed and fabricated texture-heterogeneous Mg laminates by accumulative roll bonding, comprising five alternating layers of Mg-Al-Zn with a strong basal texture (hard layer) and Mg-Al-Sn-Ca with a weaker basal texture (soft layer). Two texture-heterogeneous laminates with different stacking architectures have been constructed, i.e., hard-soft-hard-soft-hard (HSH-5L) and soft-hard-soft-hard-soft (SHS-5L). HSH-5L exhibits a yield strength of 192 MPa and fracture elongation of 22%, representing improvements of 8.1% and 27%, respectively, compared with SHS-5L. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction, digital image correlation, and finite element simulation indicate that the improved mechanical response is associated with enhanced interfacial constraints and higher strain gradients in HSH-5L. These conditions facilitate <c+a> slip near interfaces and provide more nucleation sites for strain bands (SB). As deformation proceeds, dense SBs mainly dominated by basal <a> slip gradually intersect. The intersection regions induce local stress concentration and activate additional non-basal slip, which in turn restricts the further propagation of SBs and thereby contributes to sustained strain hardening in the HSH-5L sample. By contrast, in the SHS-5L sample, basal <a> slip initiates and propagates rapidly during deformation, forming long-range SBs that lead to local deformation instability and premature fracture. These findings provide insights for the design of heterogeneous Mg laminates with high strength and ductility. © 2026

Authors: Vu L.H.
Title: From trust and generational education to climate action: Global empirical evidence on shaping climate beliefs and policies; [از اعتماد و آموزش نسلی تا اقدا مهای اقلیمی؛ شواهد تجربی جهانی دربارة شکلگیری باورها و سیاستهای اقلیمی]
Abstract: Public support for climate action depends not only on economic incentives and information, but also on deeper social and institutional foundations. This study investigates how trust shapes individuals’ climate change perceptions and their willingness to support mitigation policies, particularly through higher environmental taxes. Using individual-level data from the fourth round of the Life in Transition Survey, combined with country-level macroeconomic indicators from the World Bank, the analysis covers 37 countries over the period 2022–2023. We estimate baseline models using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), with all regressions weighted by national population to ensure cross-country representativeness. A key contribution of the study is the distinction between generalized trust and multi-level institutional trust, including trust in the presidency, central government, regional government, and local government. The results show that both forms of trust are positively and robustly associated with stronger beliefs that climate change is real and primarily driven by human activity, as well as with greater willingness to support environmental taxation. Institutional trust, in particular, exhibits a stronger relationship with policy support, highlighting its central role in shaping acceptance of financially costly climate measures. Beyond trust, the findings underscore the importance of intergenerational education. Mothers’ education is more strongly associated with climate perceptions, while fathers’ education shows a closer link to willingness to pay for environmental policies, suggesting differentiated family-based transmission channels. © 2026, University of Tehran. Authors: Begade S.
Title: Inferring Behavioural Landscape Systems in Palaeolithic Archaeology: Unsupervised Spatial Learning as a Framework for Formal Inductive Inference
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Interpretations of Palaeolithic landscapes have frequently relied upon a priori site typologies, functional classifications, and environmentally deterministic frameworks that risk circular reasoning, typological reification, and underdetermined behavioural inference. This study develops and applies an explicitly inductive framework for identifying behavioural landscape structure without imposing pre-defined functional or categorical assumptions. Using a multivariate dataset of 158 georeferenced open-air Palaeolithic occurrences from the Vidarbha region of eastern Maharashtra, India, the analysis integrates topographic, hydrological, and raw-material accessibility variables alongside a kernel-derived archaeological persistence measure within an unsupervised spatial learning workflow. Unsupervised spatial learning refers here to the application of clustering algorithms requiring no predefined class labels to spatially referenced archaeological datasets, distinguishing this exploratory inferential mode from confirmatory supervised prediction. Cluster robustness was evaluated through multiple internal validation diagnostics, including elbow analysis, silhouette optimisation, gap statistic assessment, sensitivity testing, and cross-algorithm comparison. Results reveal reproducible multivariate landscape configurations best understood as probabilistic behavioural landscape systems rather than discrete functional site types or deterministic settlement categories. These findings demonstrate that coherent archaeological landscape organisation can be detected inductively prior to typological assignment, while clarifying persistent zones of temporal palimpsest formation, proxy limitation, and interpretive ambiguity inherent to open-air records. The study argues that unsupervised spatial learning is most productive when positioned as an epistemic support framework that formalises pattern discovery, stabilises inductive reasoning, and preserves the interpretive centrality of archaeological expertise, contributing to a more transparent and methodologically accountable approach to behavioural inference in Palaeolithic landscape research. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Tang Y.; Yang Y.; Li J.; Cao F.; Gong Z.; Zhu H.; Li J.; Rao W.-F.; Bai Y.
Title: Simultaneous giant electrostrain and wide-temperature stability in PNZST ceramics via antiferroelectric phase boundary regulation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Antiferroelectric (AFE) ceramics are promising candidates for precision actuators, but the trade-off between giant electrostrain and wide-temperature stability has severely limited their practical applications. Here, we propose a dual-pathway phase boundary regulation strategy in perovskite AFE systems to synergistically optimize electrostrain magnitude and temperature stability by designing the electric-field-induced AFE-ferroelectric (FE) transition sequence under coupled temperature-electric-field conditions. Using the prototype system of Pb0.99Nb0.02[(Zr0.75Sn0.25)xTi1−x]0.98O3 (PNZST-100xZS), our results show that PNZST-99ZS and PNZST-97ZS exhibit giant electrostrains of 0.98% and 0.77%, respectively. Remarkably, over a wide temperature range of 25–155 °C, they maintain low electrostrain fluctuations of only 16.12% and 9.21%, significantly better than previously reported materials. The excellent performance stems from the electric-field-induced orthorhombic AFE (AFEO)-rhombohedral FE (FER) transition at low temperatures and the tetragonal AFE (AFET)-FER transition at high temperatures. Between these two temperature regions, the diffuse AFEO-AFET transition bridges the two field-induced pathways, ensuring a smooth evolution of the electrostrain response across the entire operating temperature range. This work provides a new route to high-performance AFE actuator materials with both large electrostrain and wide-temperature stability. © 2026

Abstract: Grammarly is one of the most widely used software applications for the automatic detection of grammatical errors in texts translated from Persian into English. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Grammarly and to propose suggestions for improving its performance. To achieve this objective, a corpus consisting of English translations of booklets introducing works of resistance literature was analyzed. After grammatical errors had been identified by the researchers (human evaluators), the electronic versions of the booklets were submitted to Grammarly for error detection. The identified errors were then categorized, and the results obtained by the researchers were compared with those generated by the software. Following the qualitative and quantitative analyses of the errors and the presentation of the findings, recommendations were made to enhance Grammarly’s effectiveness. According to the findings, of the 98 instances identified by Grammarly as errors, 16 were not actual errors. In four cases (4.9%), Grammarly failed to correctly identify the type of error. The software demonstrated its weakest performance in the detection of spelling errors and the misuse of masculine and feminine pronouns. Overall, Grammarly exhibited a high level of effectiveness, correctly identifying 82.8% of the errors. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. All rights reserved.

Authors: Liu P.; Lu H.; Xu G.; Han C.; Shang M.; Song X.
Title: Synergistic enhancement of coercivity and saturation magnetization in Sm-Co alloys via multi-element doping
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Multi-element doping represents the most effective approach for enhancing the performance of permanent magnetic alloys. However, the complex interdependencies among diverse doping elements, broad concentration ranges, and intricate element-matrix interactions present significant challenges in establishing appropriate composition-property relationships, impeding efficient development of high-performance multicomponent alloys. To address this fundamental limitation, this study introduced a data-driven framework incorporating high-throughput identification of key elemental features governing magnetic properties. Principal component and feature sensitivity analyses quantified feature contributions to distinct magnetic characteristics and evaluated comprehensive weighting factors for multi-objective optimization. This integrated methodology enabled efficient and appropriate design of multi-element doped alloys targeting simultaneous enhancement of competing magnetic properties. Demonstrated by the Sm-Co-based systems, the framework concurrently enhanced both saturation magnetization and coercivity, which effectively resolved the trade-off between these properties through multi-element doping. Experimentally validated designs across multiple matrix types exhibited superior comprehensive magnetic properties, with quantitative confirmation of the model predictions. The present study provides a novel strategy that is in principle broadly applicable for designing multicomponent alloys that overcome inherent property trade-offs. © 2026

Title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Asciminib in Patients With Chronic Phase Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Previously Treated With 2 or More Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Colombia
Abstract: Objectives To assess the cost-effectiveness of asciminib in adult patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia who have been treated with 2 or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors, from a third-party payer perspective in Colombia. Methods A nonhomogeneous partitioned survival model was developed using ASCEMBL trial and matching-adjusted indirect comparisons. Outcomes included overall survival, progression-free survival, and safety. Overall survival was modeled using exponential functions based on 6-month major molecular response rates. Quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were estimated using phase-specific utilities. Direct medical costs were obtained from national public databases (2024-2025) and expressed in 2025 USD (USD 1 = COP 4053). A 30-year time horizon was applied. Base case compared asciminib with bosutinib and ponatinib. Scenario analyses included nilotinib and dasatinib because they are rarely used in third line in Colombia. Sensitivity analyses explored ponatinib dose deescalation, generic drug pricing, asciminib price thresholds, relative dose intensity, and alternative overall survival assumptions. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Asciminib was dominant compared with bosutinib and ponatinib, yielding more QALYs (0.41 and 0.20) and lower costs (−USD 47 334 and −USD 88 554). Scenario analyses including nilotinib and dasatinib favored asciminib, with higher QALYs (0.32 and 0.25) and lower costs (−USD 43 785 and −USD 6400). Results remained robust across analyses, including ponatinib dose deescalation, generic pricing, relative dose intensity, and alternative overall survival assumptions. Conclusions Asciminib was a dominant treatment option for patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia who have been treated with 2 or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors, offering clinical and economic advantages over other pharmacological treatments. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Papadimitriou A.; Pan Z.
Title: Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) in business and management education for developing AI and prompt literacy
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into organizational practice has created an urgent need for business and management education to move beyond tool exposure toward meaningful skill development. This study develops and implements a Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) approach that embeds GAI within active learning environments to support students' AI literacy and prompt literacy. A central feature of the approach is the use of structured scaffolds, particularly the RACE framework (Role–Action–Context–Explanation), which guides students in designing prompts, evaluating AI outputs, and linking responses to theoretical concepts. The approach was implemented in an undergraduate Organizational Behavior course (n = 93) using an explanatory mixed-methods design. Quantitative results indicate significant improvements in both AI literacy and prompt literacy, including gains in knowledge, application, and ethical awareness. Qualitative findings show that students engaged with AI iteratively and reflectively, using it as a “co-thinker” to refine prompts, assess output quality, and connect AI-generated insights with course theories. Cognitive and metacognitive engagement emerged as dominant, while collaborative and ethical dimensions, though less prominent, contributed to students’ developing awareness of responsible AI use. The findings demonstrate that structured, pedagogically guided AI integration transforms AI from a passive information source into an active learning scaffold. The SAIL approach, supported by RACE, offers a practical and transferable pathway for educators seeking to prepare students to navigate AI-augmented professional environments with critical, reflective, and responsible judgment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Xu Y.-Y.; Chen J.-Y.; Zhang W.-T.; Zhang H.-R.; Min F.
Title: Multi-behavior popularity-aware recommendation
Abstract: Recommender systems (RSs) face a persistent challenge known as popularity bias, which is characterized by the systematic over-recommendation of popular items and under-recommendation of long-tail or new items. This issue has been addressed in existing single-behavior recommendations, which mainly focus on mitigating popularity bias in the final interaction (such as purchasing). Multiple behaviors of users typically exhibit sequential dependencies across multiple stages (e.g., browsing → adding to cart → purchasing). However, existing multi-behavior recommendations fail to sufficiently leverage these relationships to effectively address popularity bias. In this paper, we propose a multi-behavior popularity-aware recommendation to alleviate the above problem. We explore the role of user sequential behavioral relationships in alleviating popularity bias from two perspectives: items and users. From the perspective of items, we redefine popularity under multi-behavior. We calculate the item popularity by counting the number of user-item interactions, such as browsing, adding to cart, and purchasing. From the user’s perspective, we calculate the user’s attention to the item popularity and divide all users into conservatives and trend-followers by their attention. Subsequently, we design a popularity-matching loss to influence the recommendation probability. It represents the matching degree between the two kinds of followers’ preferences and the popularity of the target item. Finally, we rank the probabilities of all target items and provide a recommendation list for the user. Experimental results on five well-known datasets indicate that compared with twenty-four state-of-the-art models, the proposed model is superior in terms of NDCG, Recall, and APT. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Budget Impact Analysis of System-Level Costs Associated With Topical Janus Kinase Inhibitor Therapies for Moderate Atopic Dermatitis in Germany
Abstract: Objectives German statutory health insurance budgets are driven by escalation to advanced systemic therapies for atopic dermatitis (AD). Effective and affordable novel options for adults with AD are needed to reduce the economic burden. Our objective was to estimate the 5-year budget impact of adopting the topical Janus kinase inhibitor, 1.5% ruxolitinib cream, for adults with moderate AD, affected body surface area ≤ 20%, and clinical eligibility for systemic therapy from a German population perspective. Methods We developed a budget impact model that compares the current systemic treatment mix with a forward-looking intervention scenario in which 1.5% ruxolitinib cream is adopted for adult AD from 2026 onward. Uptake increases linearly to 25% by 2030 and proportionally displaces systemic therapies. Ruxolitinib cream costs were modeled based on real-world evidence. Direct costs included drug acquisition and nondrug medical costs; the societal perspective incorporated out-of-pocket costs and productivity losses. Results The systemic-eligible population was estimated at 330 600 patients in 2025, growing to 402 200 by 2030. Among those were 90 000 patients treated with 1.5% ruxolitinib cream in 2030. Over 2026 to 2030, costs were €39.8bn with ruxolitinib cream versus €44.1bn with current systemic treatments, yielding a cumulative budget impact of €4.3bn. Statutory health insurance savings accounted for 80% (€3.4bn) of those savings. Conclusions Under the modeled uptake and displacement assumptions, ruxolitinib cream could represent a cost-mitigating option that could reduce the economic burden of AD. Postlaunch evidence on utilization, persistence, and therapy switching is needed to validate and refine budget impact estimates. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Waiting for Uganda’s first commercial ‘Pearl Sweet’ oil: Discourses on social and environmental impacts and safeguards
Abstract: Uganda discovered approximately 3.5 billion barrels of commercially recoverable oil reserves in 2006 and is poised to become a major oil producer in Sub-Saharan Africa. In assessing progress towards full–scale oil production, expected by the end of 2026, Uganda’s President referred to the country’s commercial crude oil as “pearl sweet”, highlighting its medium-to-heavy, highly waxy characteristics, relatively low sulphur content, and ease of refining. Despite the anticipated economic benefits, considerable debate persists regarding the potential social and environmental impacts of oil development and the adequacy of safeguards ahead of full–scale production. Drawing on experiences from established oil–producing countries, this paper examines how environmental and social impacts are framed, how safeguards are prioritised, and what this implies for Uganda’s emerging oil sector. Anchored in environmental justice and political ecology, the study adopts a sequential integrative design combining a systematic literature review with empirical insights from twelve purposively selected stakeholders in Uganda’s oil-producing districts and national regulatory institutions. The literature review used Boolean search strings that connected terms within conceptual blocks using OR and combined blocks using AND, following a PRISMA-guided process across Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar and institutional data bases. Of 1800 records identified, 95 key sources were retained for analysis. The findings indicate that, although Uganda has initiated several safeguards measures including oil–spill preparedness training, buffer zone enforcement, afforestation, and resettlement programs – implementation remain fragmented, under–resourced, and heavily centralised. Comparative analysis further indicates limited integration of international climate frameworks, including the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement, into national oil governance. We argue that Uganda’s challenge is not simply the absence of safeguards, but the persistence of centralised, uneven, and under–resourced governance arrangements that constrain the translation of international safeguard commitments into effective national practice. This study contributes to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land), while also intersecting with SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Psychological safety as a driver of student learning outcomes in team-based learning environments: The mediating role of teamwork quality
Abstract: With the rise of constructivist approaches, team-based learning (TBL) has gained popularity as an instructional design in the field of management education. The extant research indicates that the positive effects of TBL on student learning outcomes, which many studies report, might depend on individual as well as social-contextual drivers. In this paper, we introduce psychological safety and the quality of teamwork processes as two important social-contextual drivers of student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Based on research on team processes and TBL, we argue that psychological safety fosters student learning outcomes because of its positive effect on intrinsic motivation and group interaction. We further hypothesize that the relationship between psychological safety and student learning outcomes is mediated by the quality of teamwork processes within the student teams. A field study based on a computerized business simulation involving 169 undergraduate management students, nested within 44 teams, at a German university supports our hypotheses. We contribute to research on constructivist learning and TBL by introducing psychological safety as an important driver and the quality of teamwork processes as a mediating mechanism for student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Our study also has practical implications for the design, support, and facilitation of psychologically safe team-based learning environments. © 2026

Title: The power of gastronomic cultural capital: How local food culture shapes residents' recommendation intention
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: While destinations increasingly leverage cultural capital for competitiveness, research predominantly focuses on top-down promotions of monument-centered heritage, neglecting the distinct social logic of gastronomic culture. Grounded in cultural capital theory, this study aims to examine how Hong Kong's tea restaurants food culture translates into residents' recommendation intentions toward culturally diverse individuals. It untangles the core inquiries: how everyday food culture fosters attachment; how this attachment subsequently shapes cultural identity and confidence; and how nostalgia and knowledge moderate these psychological pathways. Additionally, it identifies which specific tea restaurant's food culture dimensions serve as the primary drivers. Utilizing an empirical sample of 615 Hong Kong residents, this research adopts a PLS–SEM–ANN approach. The PLS–SEM analysis confirms that cultural identity and confidence act as pivotal mediators, while the complementary ANN analysis reveals that gastronomic identity, exceeding mere sensory flavour, is the predominant driving dimension. Empirically, nostalgia amplifies the culture–attachment link, and knowledge strengthens the attachment–confidence relationship. These findings advocate for a paradigm shift in destination marketing: beyond institutional campaigns, mobilizing residents as active cultural transmitters is crucial for gastronomic tourism, establishing a scalable mechanism for everyday cultural capital transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Incentivized sadism: The impact of intrinsic and extrinsic reward on sadistic aggression
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: In two studies (one correlational, one experimental; total N = 419), we tested whether dispositional sadism is related to the anticipation of experiencing pleasure (instead of guilt) during and after aggressing, and whether this anticipation motivates aggressive behavior. We also tested whether individuals higher in sadism are less likely to use dissonance reduction strategies for behaving aggressively (and feeling pleasure while doing so). Study 1 looked at how dispositional sadism is related to the anticipation of intrinsic and extrinsic rewards of behaving aggressively. Study 2 looked at whether offering a meager extrinsic reward for behaving aggressively (i.e., financial compensation) increased the experience of pleasure and decreased the experience of guilt during and after aggression – a dissonance reduction strategy – and whether this effect was reduced for people high (vs. low) in sadism. Results revealed that dispositional sadism positively predicts (1) the expectation of reward and lack of guilt after behaving aggressively (Study 1), (2) aggressive behavior in an animal-killing paradigm (Study 2), and (3) hedonic pleasure and lack of guilt while doing so (Study 2). Notably, these affective correlates of sadism were not maintained after aggression, suggesting that hedonic gains are short-lived. The effects of introducing a financial incentive for behaving aggressively were inconsistent across the main studies and a preliminary pilot study (reported in Supplementary Materials), and should be interpreted with caution. Overall, the current studies portray dispositional sadism as a trait primarily associated with intrinsic motivation for aggressive behaviour, driven by its emotional benefits — at least in the moment. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Hematological and biochemical profiling of iron deficiency anemia among adolescent girls: A cross-sectional study from rural areas of the Jungle Mahal, West Bengal, India
Abstract: Background Iron deficiency anemia (IDA) is a major public health concern among adolescents, adversely affecting physical growth, cognitive abilities, and maternal future health. Our study evaluated the incidence of anemia and the hematological and biochemical parameters of iron deficiency among adolescent girls in the Jungle Mahal area of West Bengal, India. Methods A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted between May 2022 and June 2025 among 372 adolescent girls. Blood samples were analyzed for hemoglobin, complete blood count, and iron-status biomarkers, including serum iron (μg/dL), ferritin (μg/dL), TIBC (μg/dL), UIBC (μg/dL), and transferrin saturation (%). Results The overall prevalence of anemia was 52.42%, with rates of 11.3% in early, 34.9% in mid, and 53.8% in late adolescence. Serum iron (28.84 ± 26.29), transferrin saturation (16.88 ± 6.50), and serum ferritin (13.63 ± 0.34) were significantly lower in the severe IDA group compared to the control group. However, TIBC (412.77 ± 197.53) and UIBC (386.95 ± 192.55) were substantially higher. RBC and HCT have a significant positive correlation with Hb ( r = 0.866 and 0.923, respectively). RDW-CV and PWD showed negative correlations ( r = − 0.273 and − 0.508) with Hb. Conclusion The present study reveals that anemia affects a small proportion of adolescent girls in early and mid-adolescence, but is more frequent in late adolescence. The burden of anemia among rural adolescent girls could be reduced by strengthening community-based screening, nutrition education, iron supplementation, and awareness programmes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The power of morality: The effect of moral appeals on tourists’ attitudes in rural tourism destinations
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Rural tourism has become an important tool for rural-revitalization and poverty alleviation, which has been increasingly framed as a moral narrative in public discourse. However, destination marketing often prioritizes utilitarian attributes while overlooking the role of moral appeals. Drawing on affective events theory, this study employs two experiments to examine the effects of moral appeals on tourists' attitudes, the underlying mechanism, and boundary conditions. The findings reveal that moral appeals significantly enhance tourists' visit intention and perceived value of rural destinations, with anticipated guilt mediating this relationship. Notably, these effects are more pronounced in low-quality destinations than in high-quality ones. Specifically, in rural destinations with low quality, high-intensity moral appeals are more effective than low-intensity ones in enhancing tourists’ visit intention and perceived value. This study contributes to the literature on rural tourism marketing and highlights the strategic value of moral appeals, particularly for rural destinations with limited resources. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Adaptive dynamic Q-factor continuous wavelet transform for natural frequency extraction in fault-originated transient signals
Abstract: This paper presents an adaptive dynamic Q-factor continuous wavelet transform (ADQ-CWT) algorithm for accurate natural frequency identification in power system fault transient analysis. The proposed approach dynamically adjusts the Q-factor of the analysing wavelet by modifying its centre frequency and time-decay parameter, thereby optimising the trade-off between time and frequency resolution across multiple scales. To further enhance temporal localisation and suppress redundant low-frequency components, multi-resolution analysis (MRA) filtering is integrated into the framework. The algorithm is validated through electromagnetic transient simulations conducted in EMTP-RV using the IEEE 34-bus distribution network. The evaluation considers three representative aspects: variations in network topology, fault types, and fault locations. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm consistently identifies natural frequencies with high precision, yielding deviations below 0.1 % from the theoretical values. Moreover, the algorithm exhibits strong robustness to changes in system configuration and fault conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
