Title: The effects of risk perception based on local or global information in suppressing the spread of infectious diseases
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: This paper aims to investigate the role of individuals’ perceptions of infection risk in suppressing the spread of infectious diseases. It also examines whether global or local information is more effective in preventing infections. We developed an agent-based model in which 100000 individuals are connected in a small-world network. Infection information for the entire population was classified as global information, and infection information for the surroundings of a specific individual was classified as local information. The degree of response to infection risk information was measured using a normalized tunable sigmoid function. Higher sensitivity to infection risk increases the implementation of preventive measures, which reduces the spread of infectious disease. The use of global information on infection risk has been shown to be more useful in suppressing infections in general. However, if infected people around us can be recognized immediately and personal quarantine is quickly followed, the use of local information has been shown to be the most cost-effective way to end infections. Our study emphasizes the importance of individuals recognizing and responding to infected people around them to effectively control the spread of infectious diseases. It demonstrates that higher sensitivity to infection risk leads to better adherence to preventive measures, which in turn reduces disease transmission. These findings suggest that individual awareness and behavior play a critical role in managing infectious diseases. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: Feedback-Free Photonic Reservoir Computing via Time-Concatenated Dimensional Expansion and Hybrid Pruning
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) offers an efficient framework for temporal processing by combining nonlinear mapping with short-term memory. However, conventional implementations are often hindered by the high hardware costs of spatial arrays or the speed and integration bottlenecks associated with feedback delay lines and input masking in time-delayed RC. In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a single-node photonic reservoir computing system without physical delay lines and input masking operations. To enhance the representational capability of the single-node system, we introduce a time-concatenated dimensional expansion technique to construct a high-dimensional state space. Furthermore, a hybrid pruning strategy is employed to quantitatively optimize the trade-off between computational resources and forecasting performance. Our results demonstrate a feedback-free photonic reservoir computing framework that combines physical photonic feature generation with digital state construction and optimization for temporal processing tasks with diverse dynamical characteristics.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Authors: Nwafor S.C.; Tsakeni M.
Title: Think-pair-share strategy integrated with Google Classroom: Investigating its effect on students with different cognitive styles for learning about electrolysis
Abstract: While acknowledging that students organise, process and perceive information in different ways, empirical studies report that students perform poorly in chemistry, and the topic of electrolysis, in particular. Some of these studies suggest integrating technology into science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. A think-pair-share instructional strategy, integrated with Google Classroom (TPSISIGC) was useful for increasing students' achievement and active learning. This study examined the effect of the TPSISIGC on students' achievement in electrolysis for different cognitive styles and the challenges students encounter when electrolysis is taught using the TPSISIGC. The study involved secondary school chemistry students and used a quasi-experimental research design. Students in the experimental group were taught electrolysis utilising TPSISIGC, and the control group was exposed to the lecture method. Data were collected using the Electrolysis Achievement Test (EAT), Group Embedded Figure Test (GEFT), and a questionnaire titled Student Challenges When Taught Electrolysis Using Think-Pair-Share Integrated with Google Classroom (SCETPSIGC). The instruments were validated by three experts, and reliability indices of 0.88, 0.85, and 0.80 were established for EAT, GEFT, and SCETPSIGC, respectively. The data collected were analysed using mean, standard deviations and ANCOVA. The study findings reveal that TPSISIGC, compared to the lecture method, significantly improved students' achievement on the topic of electrolysis. Although no significant difference was found between students with field-dependent and field-independent cognitive styles when they were taught about electrolysis using TPSISIGC, there was a significant interaction effect between cognitive styles and treatment on secondary school students' achievement on the topic of electrolysis. Moreover, inadequate teacher training, too little time, unstable internet connectivity and unstable power supply were some of the challenges students encountered while using TPSISIGC. The researchers concluded that TPSISIGC is an inclusive strategy that enhances the achievement of both field-dependent and field-independent students and that the effectiveness of instructional strategies can vary and depends on students' cognitive styles. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Towards a digital skills framework for the energy sector: Evidence from the Australian LNG industry
Abstract: Digital innovations have become increasingly widespread in almost every industry, and Australia’s energy sector has not been immune to this. It therefore follows that the coordination of energy exports like liquified natural gas (LNG) across government, industry, and community stakeholders will be largely dependent on the ability of these constituents to share digital information between and among each other in useful timeframes. However, the success of these integrated data systems will hinge on the ability of the energy sector’s workforce to use these technologies effectively, but it is increasingly coming into focus that the industry’s workers have very uneven levels of proficiency with digital technologies. By synthesizing earlier digital skills frameworks from other industries and adding qualitative evidence distilled from 42 interviews with a broad range of employees throughout a midsize Australian LNG company, this paper puts forward a digital skills framework for the energy sector which identifies five skill areas that will be required in 2030: (1) data analytics, (2) digital communication and collaboration, (3) digital security, (4) digital ethical and social responsibility, and (5) digital innovation. The required level of proficiency that will be required in 2030 for each of these skill areas is then assessed for different discipline groups throughout the industry. We conclude by explaining how the presented framework can be used as an assessment tool for identifying skill gaps throughout the energy sector, and exploring the policy-related implications of the findings. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Heterointerface-grain boundary defect engineering enables high-performance and mechanically robust Bi2Te3-based thermoelectric nanocomposites
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The simultaneous optimization of thermoelectric (TE) performance, mechanical robustness, and device-level applicability remains a long-standing challenge for the practical deployment of Bi2Te3-based TE materials in power generation and solid-state cooling. Herein, we report a high-performance TE nanocomposite, Bi0.3Sb1.7Te2.99S0.01 + 0.7 wt.% ZrO2, which concurrently exhibits enhanced TE properties and mechanical strength, enabling reliable device fabrication. By integrating heterogeneous interface engineering with deliberately constructed grain-boundary defect architectures—including twin boundaries, staggered lamellae, and antisite defect layers—a cooperative regulation of charge and phonon transport is achieved across multiple length scales. This defect-mediated transport modulation markedly enhances the Seebeck coefficient and power factor, while suppressing both electronic and lattice thermal conductivities, thereby effectively mitigating the intrinsic trade-off between TE efficiency and mechanical integrity. Consequently, the optimized nanocomposite delivers a peak zTmax of ∼1.46 at 350 K and an average zTave of ∼1.23 over 300–500 K, in addition to a Vickers hardness of 1.17 GPa and a compressive strength of 218 MPa. Importantly, a seven-pair TE device achieved a maximum conversion efficiency of ∼6.8% at a temperature difference of 200 K and a maximum cooling temperature difference of ∼63.4 K at 300 K. This study demonstrates that heterointerface–grain boundary defect engineering provides an effective and scalable strategy to simultaneously advance TE performance, mechanical reliability, and device-level functionality in Bi2Te3-based TE nanocomposites. © 2026

Title: Bridging governance and sustainability in the Global South: NGO-led urban transition pathways in Mashhad, Iran
Abstract: Urban areas in the Global South face growing challenges of centralized governance, rapid urbanization and environmental degradation, which demand more inclusive and sustainable planning approaches. This article investigates how civil society organizations, particularly professionally oriented NGOs, can influence urban governance and contribute to sustainability-oriented transitions. The study examines the case of CharTabaqeh, a non-governmental organization in Mashhad, Iran, that contested the construction of the Southern Beltway and played an important role in the policy process that ultimately contributed to the project's transformation into the Mountain Park. Drawing on document analysis and observation, the research adopts a qualitative case study approach. The findings reveal that CharTabaqeh acted as a transition intermediary by creating participatory spaces, mobilizing citizens, and connecting community concerns with formal decision-making processes. The organization also promoted a shift toward more sustainable and resilient urban development by advocating for the preservation of ecological assets and the development of public green space in place of a car-oriented infrastructure project. Moreover, the NGO's strategic use of digital platforms during the COVID-19 pandemic facilitated civic mobilization, strengthened coalitions and amplified advocacy efforts at local and national scales. These results demonstrate that NGOs can act as catalysts of sustainable urban transitions by bridging community interests with policy processes, reframing development trajectories and leveraging digital technologies within centralized governance contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Leveraging avatar fingerprinting: A multi-generator photorealistic talking-head public database and benchmark
Abstract: Recent advances in photorealistic avatar generation have enabled highly realistic talking-head avatars, raising security concerns regarding identity impersonation in AI-mediated communication. To advance this challenging problem, the task of avatar fingerprinting aims to determine whether two avatar videos are driven by the same human operator. However, current public databases in the literature are scarce and based solely on old-fashioned talking-head avatar generators, not representing realistic scenarios for the current task of avatar fingerprinting. To overcome this situation, the present article introduces AVAPrintDB, a new publicly available multi-generator talking-head avatar database for avatar fingerprinting. AVAPrintDB is constructed from two audiovisual corpora and three state-of-the-art avatar generators (GAGAvatar, LivePortrait, HunyuanPortrait), representing different synthesis paradigms, and includes both self- and cross-reenactments to simulate legitimate usage and impersonation scenarios. Building on this database, we define a standardized and reproducible benchmark for avatar fingerprinting, considering public state-of-the-art avatar fingerprinting systems and exploring novel methods based on Foundation Models (DINOv2 and CLIP). We also conduct a comprehensive analysis under generator and dataset shift. Our results show that, while identity-related motion cues persist across synthetic avatars, current avatar fingerprinting systems remain highly sensitive to changes in the synthesis pipeline and source domain. The AVAPrintDB, benchmark protocols, and avatar fingerprinting systems are publicly available to facilitate reproducible research. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: González F.A.I.
Title: Cushioned but hollowed out: coal’s end and the demographic legacy of Spain’s mining communities
Abstract: Between 2018 and 2020 Spain closed almost its entire coal sector, abruptly and in a handful of mining districts, under a just-transition agreement that retired displaced miners early. I ask what the closures did to the population of the mining municipalities and whether the cleaner air they left behind drew anyone in Comparing the municipalities that the government classified as most affected by the mine closures with non-mining municipalities on the same pre-closure population path, I find that the two move together until the closures and then diverge: the mining municipalities lose about three percent of their population by 2022. The loss is larger where coal mattered more and survives randomization inference. It did not arrive as unemployment, which fell relative to controls because early retirement converted dismissal into pension, and it was not offset by newcomers: in-migration to the areas whose air improved most does not respond, an improvement that was small in this low-pollution setting. The transition therefore delivered justice to workers without securing the territory. Read through the lens of territorial justice, income protection for the displaced is necessary but not sufficient for the sustainable development of extractive regions, and the social and cultural costs of a hollowing community, together with the lagged effects on services and on the young, lie beyond what the quantitative record yet shows. Title: Augmented reality as a digital scaffold for slow travel: The roles of cultural competence and tourist engagement at a heritage site

Abstract: Heritage sites are designed to foster in-depth cultural experiences for tourists at destinations and are well suited for promoting slow travel. However, cultural differences and tourist’ limited awareness often hinder its practice. Grounded in zone of proximal development theory, this study reveals that the perceived enjoyment of AR is positively associated with cultural competence, but only for highly engaged users. Title: RFEP-SI-Fed: Fuzzy risk-entropy prediction safety island with federated reinforcement learning for low-carbon dispatch of nitrogen-hydrogen-ammonia coupled multi-park integrated energy systems
Abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy requires multi-park integrated energy systems (IESs) to coordinate electricity, heat, cooling, hydrogen, ammonia, and nitrogen while retaining local operational data and screening safety-critical actions before execution. This study proposes RFEP-SI-Fed, which integrates a six-carrier N2-H2-NH3 dispatch model, risk-weighted fuzzy-entropy assessment with Green/Yellow/Red Safety Island control, and FedProx-based PPO coordination. In the original three-park representative-day benchmark, aggregate operating cost decreased from 46,640 to 38,960 CNY/day (16.5%) and aggregate carbon-trading cost decreased from 5460 to 3590 CNY/day (34.2%) relative to the NoMonitor baseline. Warning coverage ranged from 92.1% to 94.7%, the average warning lead time was 22.4 min, and the complete configuration achieved a 96% survival rate in the reported ablation evaluation. The extended evaluation used three independent training seeds, six program-generated out-of-distribution scenarios, 3-, 6-, and 12-park systems, communication-delay and client-dropout tests, optimizer comparisons, and parameter screening. From 3 to 12 parks, mean server-side aggregation latency increased from 11.45 ± 2.92 to 40.79 ± 6.62 ms, while mean cost per park increased by 2.42%. One- to three-round aggregation delays increased paired mean cost by 4.57–5.66%. Across the tests of six limited scenarios, the complete framework is consistently constrained within the predefined risk envelope, which demonstrates that the proposed method realizes a clear trade-off between safety and economic cost. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The Integration of Islamic Religious Values in the Ritual Mantras of Pinisi Boat-Making as Instructional Material for Literature Learning in Islamic Schools

Title: Enhancing communication competence and managerial skills through virtual reality based experiential learning in management education
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising pedagogical modality in higher management education, offering immersive, risk-free environments that simulate the complexity of real-world organizational interactions. This study investigates whether, and to what extent, VR-based experiential learning is associated with students' communication competence and managerial self-efficacy, drawing on Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory and Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory. Using a cross-sectional survey design complemented by platform-generated usage logs, we analyzed survey and behavioral data from 412 postgraduate and undergraduate management students across three program types at a research-intensive business school. Ordinary least squares regression served as the primary analysis, supplemented by instrumental-variable estimation (IV/2SLS), generalized method of moments (GMM), and propensity score matching to address potential endogeneity and selection bias. Bootstrap mediation analyses indicated that experiential learning depth and reflective practice partially mediate the associations between VR intensity parameters and both outcomes. Heterogeneity analyses revealed stronger associations among executive-education participants and where instructor facilitation quality was high. Findings were robust to alternative specifications and sample-trimming procedures. The study contributes a multi-method framework for integrating immersive technology into business-school curricula and offers actionable recommendations for curriculum designers, institutional administrators, and educational-technology policymakers. © 2026

Title: Is green product trade a pathway to better air quality in China?
Abstract: This study evaluates whether green product trade can serve as an effective pathway to improving air quality in China. Using panel data for 28 provinces from 2010 to 2021, we are the first to jointly examine the impacts of green trade on six major air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, NOx, and CO2) while simultaneously identifying both its temporal dynamics and spatial spillover effects within a unified empirical framework. We construct an integrated green-product trade database combining the APEC, OECD, and World Bank classifications and employ System GMM and the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) to address spatial-temporal dependence. The results show that a 1% increase in green trade reduces PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations by approximately 1.1%. Moreover, green imports in neighboring provinces generate strong spatial spillovers, lowering local PM2.5, PM10, CO, and SO2 emissions by about 5%. We also find that green imports exert significantly stronger pollution-reduction effects than green exports, suggesting an import-driven technology-upgrade mechanism typical of developing economies. These findings provide robust evidence that green trade contributes to China's environmental improvements and offer important policy insights for emerging economies seeking to leverage green globalization for sustainable, lower-emission development. Title: Equity in print: Unveiling GEDSI construction in an Indonesian junior high school english textbook
Abstract: This study investigates how Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) are represented in English for Nusantara Grade Seven, an Indonesian government-issued English textbook developed under the Merdeka Curriculum. While previous textbook studies have predominantly focused on binary gender representation, limited research has examined disability and social inclusion through a multimodal critical discourse analysis (MCDA) framework. Addressing this gap, the present study analyzes how verbal and visual elements jointly construct meanings related to gender equality, disability, and inclusion. Using Kress and van Leeuwen's MCDA framework, the study examined the entire 264-page textbook and identified Chapters 1 and 2 as the only sections containing explicit GEDSI-related representations. The analysis focused on ideational, interpersonal, and textual meanings embedded in images, comic strips, and written passages. The findings reveal partial efforts toward inclusive representation. Female and male characters are portrayed in both domestic and public roles, indicating attempts to challenge traditional gender stereotypes. The textbook also includes characters with physical disabilities, particularly wheelchair users, and presents them as socially active participants in school and family life. However, representations remain limited in scope. Physical disabilities dominate the portrayals, while cognitive, sensory, and invisible disabilities are absent. In addition, female characters with disabilities are less visible and less empowered than male characters with disabilities, reflecting intersectional inequality. Although the textbook promotes positive messages of diversity and participation, GEDSI representation appears only in selected chapters and is not consistently integrated throughout the textbook. Title: When crowds converge: Link between events and crime
Abstract: This study draws on environmental criminology to conceptualize planned events as bounded opportunity contexts that temporarily reshape urban activity. Using high-dimensional fixed-effects Poisson models and a panel of 154,561 events in Houston, Texas, we estimate reduced-form associations across event attributes and offense types. The event-crime association is statistically detectable but economically modest. Formal comparisons reveal selective offense heterogeneity, with the Crimes Against Society coefficient exceeding the Violent Crime coefficient. Public opportunistic crime also shows stronger associations than private opportunistic and non-opportunistic crime, but not Other Crime. Event size exhibits significant heterogeneity, with the largest events showing stronger associations than those in all lower-attendance categories. Event type, day-type context, duration, and recurrence are not statistically distinguishable. Adjustment for contemporaneous foot traffic attenuates the event coefficient. Title: A hierarchical scheduling strategy for achieving multi-source energy complementarity in self-powered systems
Abstract: Ensuring long-term, stable operation of self-powered systems considering the stochastic and fluctuating nature of ambient energy remains a pivotal challenge, as existing multi-source harvesting architectures are confined to static, non-responsive paradigms. This work presents a self-powered wireless sensing system that transitions the field toward automatic, priority-driven management through a hardware-enforced, quadruple-buffered power scheduling strategy. The core of this strategy is a scheduling protocol that orchestrates energy flow in the following order: real-time photovoltaic (PV) energy, PV-stored energy, real-time thermoelectric-vibration hybrid energy, and auxiliary-stored energy. This is implemented via a dedicated circuit that enables automatic stored energy release and seamless source switching (<20 ms). A critical enabling feature is the electrical isolation between the primary and auxiliary power paths, which prevents mutual interference and resolves the impedance mismatch inherent in conventional static topologies. Experimentally, the system achieves 93 min of operation from a 10-min charge under controlled conditions, surpassing standalone PV-only and thermoelectric-only systems by 47.6% and 116.3%, respectively. Its practical viability is demonstrated by 75 min of stable field operation and consistent performance over a 10-day continuous test, with an overall system efficiency of 75%. This work provides a robust, maintenance-free power solution, demonstrating significant potential for sustainable wireless sensing in intelligent transportation and broader Industrial Internet of Things applications. © 2026 Author(s).

Title: Decarbonizing dairy processing with grid-connected hybrid renewable energy systems: a surrogate-assisted multi-objective framework

Authors: Ivanov D.
Title: Impacts of a global energy crisis on supply chain performance, ripple effects, and viability
Abstract: We simulate impacts of a global energy crisis on supply chains (SCs). First, we articulate the specific features that frame a global energy crisis as a unique type of SC large-scale systemic shocks characterized by a long-term disruption existence, disruption propagations (i.e., the ripple effect), a combination of immediate and delayed effects, cross-industry ripple effects, and mutual interrelations of SC and economic impacts. Second, we demonstrate how simulation-based methodology can be used to examine and predict the impacts of global energy crises on SC performance using the example of the Strait of Hormuz blockage and anyLogistix software. The major observation from the simulation experiments is that global energy crisis impacts resemble the COVID-19 pandemic patterns and ripple effects in 2020–2022 with reduced logistics capacities, delivery delays, and production shutdowns, supplemented by inflation effects observed in tariff turbulences in 2025. Other important factors influencing the shock impacts and propagation mechanisms are the duration of the energy crisis and SC viability. We observe that viable SCs with greater variety in production, supply, logistics, and energy structures are better able to absorb shocks. The outcomes of this research can be used by decision-makers to predict the operational and long-term impacts of global energy crises on SCs and to develop viability strategies. Our models are readily available to be used in practice for SC stress testing. They offer recommendations on proactively building adaptability and reconfiguring in response to disruptions to survive in a world without a reliable energy supply, incorporating large-scale systemic shocks into operational models. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Complexity and Economic Value of Care Provided in Humanitarian Relief Clinics for Displaced Persons at the Mexico-US Border, 2020-2022
Abstract: Objectives Millions of people rely on humanitarian organizations for medical care. We characterized the complexity and economic value of care provided by a humanitarian relief organization for displaced persons at the Mexico-US border. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of clinical encounters by a humanitarian relief organization in Tamaulipas, México, near US ports of entry from 2020 to 2022. We used records from a sample of medical encounters to assign ICD-10 and Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) billing codes for each encounter, procedure, or service. We derived an estimate of economic value for these encounters in 2020 US dollars by mapping the CPT billing codes to Medicaid reimbursement rates in Texas, and we compared these with a locally derived estimate using a fee schedule from the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social. We stratified economic value estimates by demographics, site of care, and type of medical service. Results From 23 339 clinical encounters representing 13 963 unique patients (59.5% female; median age 30 years), the most common codes were office visits: CPT 99202 (“office visit with a history”) comprised 43.9% of all encounters. The most common procedure was obstetric ultrasound, present in 341 (1.5%) of all clinical encounters. The value of care was $39.18 per encounter, which was within 5% of the locally derived estimate. Evaluation and management services accounted for 95.4% of the value. Conclusion This approach of assigning diagnosis and billing codes to clinical encounters provides an estimate for the value and complexity of clinical services provided by humanitarian relief organizations at the México-US border. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Sung Y.
Title: Translanguaging as an epistemic mechanism in Korean immigrant parents’ mediation of mathematical meaning
Abstract: This study investigates how Korean immigrant parents draw on translanguaging practices to mediate mathematical meaning with their elementary-aged children during home mathematics interaction. Using video-based, ethnographically informed observations of six sessions across three parent-child dyads, the analysis examines how parents coordinated Korean and English alongside gesture, diagrams, and tools to make mathematical relationships more visible, interpretable, and open to negotiation in real time. In this study, translanguaging is conceptualized as the epistemic mechanism through which mathematical meaning is mediated. The findings suggest that parents used translanguaging to diagnose procedural and structural mismatches, make unfamiliar terminology more accessible, bridge semantic and structural relationships across concepts, reorganize algebraic representations, and coordinate geometric action through multimodal guidance. The most salient form of this mechanism appeared in diagnostic interactions, where bilingual contrast and multimodal coordination made otherwise implicit mismatches visible and available for repair. The study contributes to translanguaging research in mathematics by respecifying translanguaging not only as a resource for participation but as an epistemic mechanism through which mathematical structure is made visible and available for reorganization. The study also suggests that Korean-English interaction provides an analytically productive context for examining how typologically associated linguistic resources become interactionally available in mathematical activity. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Makhetha E.; Maharajh R.
Title: Underground movements: Zama Zama Mobility, Precarity, and community resilience in South Africa’s Platinum Belt
Abstract: This article examines the lived experiences of unregulated artisanal miners, locally known as Zama Zamas, who mine within and around abandoned platinum mines in South Africa’s North West province, a region rich in critical minerals. While artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) in abandoned gold mines has been the subject of considerable academic inquiry, similar activities in platinum mining areas remain understudied. This study seeks to address this gap by situating ASM within the broader discourse on Africa’s critical minerals agenda and contributing to both academic and policy debates on its strategic role. Drawing on a mixed-methods approach, the paper investigates how Zama Zamas navigate precarious and often dangerous working conditions, patterns of circular and transnational migration, and exclusion from formal mining economies. It further reveals the social and economic networks and adaptive local strategies that foster resilience and community cohesion amid institutional abandonment and uncertain regulation within the critical mineral extraction sector of derelict mines. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Enhancing graph link prediction with sequential latent variable diffusion models
Abstract: Predicting interactions between nodes, known as link prediction, is a fundamental task in graph machine learning. This task is critical due to its widespread application in domains such as recommendation engines, social network analysis, drug discovery, and sequential data analysis. Deep generative approaches, such as Graph Auto-Encoders (GAEs) and Variational Graph Auto-Encoders (VGAEs), along with their derivatives, have set benchmarks by addressing challenges related to edge partitioning during training, the complexity of prediction functions for node pairs, and the proficiency in reconstructing data through latent spaces. Despite the prominence of these models in link prediction, in this work, we reveal their limitations through analytically investigations. Specifically, their reliance on a single set of latent variables often fails to capture the full spectrum of complex interactions and potential links between nodes. Moreover, we mathematically demonstrate that integrating multiple latent variables can substantially enhance a model's expressive capacity. To address this, we propose a methodology that enriches model expressiveness by leveraging a sequence of latent variables to perform multi-step latent refinement. Our approach involves constructing a parameterized forward process and a reverse reconstruction model to optimize the probability of accurately reconstructing the adjacency matrix, which follows a diffusion-inspired multi-step refinement scheme. Evaluations on diverse datasets, both homophilic and heterophilic, supported by detailed visualization analyses, confirm that our approach significantly improves the detection of potential links and the handling of complex node features within graph structures. Authors: Wang T.; Tian Z.; Li H.; Wang Z.; Li T.
Title: Experimental comparison of dual-stage organic Rankine cycle and organic Rankine flash cycle for low-temperature geothermal power generation
Abstract: Organic Rankine cycle (ORC) has gained increasing attention in thermal power generation, but with a relatively low efficiency due to the irreversible loss of the evaporation process. In order to improve the performance of ORC, dual-stage ORC (DORC) and organic Rankine flash cycle (ORFC) were proposed. Previous numerical studies have demonstrated that DORC and ORFC can indeed enhance the system performance. However, experimental verification is lacking. This study designed and established an experimental setup to achieve the switching of the DORC and ORFC systems via valve start-stop operation, using R245fa as the working fluid. The power generation performance of ORFC is tested and compared with that of the DORC. Experimental results reveal that the working fluid of ORFC undergoes incomplete evaporation before entering the scroll expander, which can effectively reduce the irreversible loss of between the heat source and the working fluid. Compared with DORC, ORFC achieves a higher specific power output due to the further reduction the injection temperature. The thermal efficiency of ORFC is almost the same as that of DORC. Nevertheless, ORFC exhibits lower net power generation and exergy efficiency due to higher power consumption of the working fluid pumps. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Siringoringo L.P.; Romagnoli A.
Title: Overcoming geothermal development barriers in Indonesia: A narrative policy review of sedimentary basin-based geothermal development
Abstract: Indonesia possesses the world's largest geothermal resource potential, yet its utilization remains disproportionately low. This study conducted a narrative policy review and strategic assessment using the SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) framework to identify the key barriers to geothermal development and formulate strategic recommendations using the TOWS (Threats, Opportunities, Weaknesses, Strengths) matrix. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach based on a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2011 and 2026. The analysis identified four major constraints to conventional volcanic geothermal development: high exploration risk and capital expenditure (CAPEX), land-use conflicts with protected forests, electricity tariff policies linked to coal-based generation costs, and persistent social resistance (NIMBY/Not in My Backyard syndrome). The findings indicated that diversifying geothermal development toward non-volcanic back-arc sedimentary basins, particularly through co-production with mature Oil and Gas (O&G) fields, provided a practical pathway to reduce exploration risk, lower infrastructure costs, minimize permitting conflicts and social resistance, and improve project economics. This approach could potentially reduce the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) to below USD 0.07/kWh. Based on the TOWS analysis, the study recommended a dual-track geothermal development strategy combining continued volcanic exploration with accelerated sedimentary basin development, supported by binary-cycle technology, brownfield O&G infrastructure reuse, Feed-in Tariff (FiT) reform, and international green financing. Collectively, these strategies could strengthen investment attractiveness and accelerate Indonesia's transition toward its Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2060 target. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Career plateau and multifaceted turnover pathways in the airline industry: Evidence from full-service and low-cost carrier cabin crew
Abstract: This study examines how career plateau influences stress, burnout, and multifaceted turnover intentions among airline cabin crew members by comparing full-service carriers (FSCs) and low-cost carriers (LCCs). Career plateau was categorized into hierarchical and job content career plateaus, and their psychological and behavioral impacts were assessed. Data were collected through a survey of 382 Korean cabin crew members with at least three years of experience and in-depth interviews with 14 participants. Quantitative results showed that a job content career plateau significantly heightened stress, leading to burnout. LCC crew members reported stronger turnover intentions, whereas burnout among FSC crew members did not necessarily translate into turnover intentions, suggesting that its effects may be constrained by organizational and labor market conditions. Qualitative findings revealed coping strategies such as goal adjustment and highlighted carrier-specific interpretations of turnover. Social support moderated the burnout–turnover link, buffering negative outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: 'In Every River, in Every Lake': Impacts of Beaver Population Change on Indigenous Livelihoods and Wellbeing in the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, Western Canadian Arctic
Abstract: Ecosystem transformation driven by climatic, environmental and societal factors poses interlinked ecological and social challenges for many Indigenous communities. For Inuvialuit communities in and around the lower Mackenzie Delta, in the western Canadian Arctic, recent changes in the population of beavers (Castor canadensis) have disrupted subsistence harvesting activities and travelling routes, exacerbating stresses linked to the cost of living and increasing the exposure of active harvesters to risk. Drawing on interviews with 25 Inuvialuit knowledge holders from the three communities of Inuvik, Tuktoyaktuk, and Aklavik, we investigated concerns around beaver population change in the western Arctic and the impact of this change on Inuvialuit livelihoods and wellbeing. Beyond the direct impact of beavers, the issues associated with ecosystem transformation pose challenges for Inuvialuit collective identity, the continuity of knowledge and connections to the land. While beaver population change was widely attributed to the local effects of a warming climate, participants also pointed to the effects of social transformations over recent decades. Ecological changes interact with social factors to produce complex and wide-ranging consequences for Indigenous communities. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: A simulation-informed machine learning framework for integrated energy and thermal comfort assessment in adaptively reused heritage courtyard buildings under hot-arid climates
Abstract: Adaptive reuse of heritage courtyard buildings as boutique hotels creates a complex balance between energy performance, thermal comfort, and cultural conservation in hot-arid regions. However, existing studies commonly address energy performance and thermal comfort separately and often depend on computationally intensive simulation workflows. This study develops a simulation-informed machine-learning surrogate framework for simultaneous prediction of end-uses energy consumption and thermal comfort indicators in adaptively reused heritage courtyard buildings. A comprehensive hourly dataset was generated from full-year simulations of twelve heritage courtyard buildings modelled in DesignBuilder using representative meteorological data for the hot-arid climate of Kashan, Iran. Building-specific heat-transfer characteristics represented by overall heat-transfer coefficient values, geometric attributes, operational parameters, indoor environmental conditions and weather were used as predictors. Seven end-uses energy outputs, namely cooling electricity, heating gas, lighting, appliance energy, system fan energy, system pump energy, and auxiliary energy, were evaluated alongside three thermal comfort indicators: predicted mean vote, predicted percentage of dissatisfied, and comfort percentage. Twenty-eight machine-learning algorithms were attempted, of which 22 successfully converged and were assessed using a leave-one-building-out validation strategy to evaluate cross-building generalization. In addition, an independently simulated heritage building, excluded from all training and validation procedures, was used for external testing to further assess model transferability. Model performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination, root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean squared error, and predictor importance was examined using a Shapley-value-based feature-importance analysis. Ensemble Bagged Trees achieved the highest predictive performance for eight of the ten evaluated outputs, while the two system-level end-uses, system fans and system pumps, were predicted less accurately (coefficients of determination of 0.397 and 0.839, respectively). Thermal comfort analysis revealed substantial seasonal discomfort, ranging from cold winter stress to severe summer overheating, while annual comfort levels remained below the adopted comfort benchmark. The Shapley-value-based analysis indicated that climatic variables (e.g., solar irradiation and outdoor temperature) and building-scale geometric/envelope variables (e.g., orientation, façade area, window-to-wall ratio, and envelope thermal properties) were among the most influential predictors across the evaluated outputs. Although courtyard-specific geometric parameters were not included as explicit inputs, building-scale variables partly reflect the influence of courtyard configuration. The independent test case further demonstrated the framework's ability to predict several energy and thermal comfort outputs for a previously unseen building, while indicating lower transferability for some system-level end-uses. Although the framework is based on simulation-generated rather than measured data, it provides a computationally efficient basis for preliminary retrofit assessment and scenario exploration. Overall, the framework enables integrated and interpretable assessment of energy performance and thermal comfort to support heritage-sensitive retrofit planning in hot-arid climates. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Plug-and-play watermarking method for diffusion models via distribution alignment
Abstract: Generative models are widely distributed to multiple users, raising significant concerns about tracing malicious content dissemination. While watermarking is a common solution, existing methods struggle to support scalable multi-user scenarios and maintain watermark integrity under adversarial manipulations. To address these issues, we propose a plug-and-play watermarking method for diffusion models based on distribution alignment, enabling effective detection and per-user traceability. Specifically, watermarks are embedded directly into latent representations without altering diffusion model parameters, allowing seamless deployment and replacement across different users. Our method leverages the connection between latent representations and generated images to ensure high watermark accuracy. Furthermore, we enforce distribution constraints to couple watermark integrity with image utility. This mechanism ensures that generated content inherently carries the watermark while neutralizing malicious bypass attempts. Experimental results demonstrate our method’s high effectiveness, achieving average true positive rates exceeding 95% for both detection and traceability under various complex distortions. Crucially, the framework thwarts Quality-Constrained Evasion (QCE) by forcing the semantic quality of tampered images to drop to unusable levels (CLIP score < 0.2). Collectively, our method provides a robust and secure plug-and-play framework for tracing the source of generated content in generative AI deployment scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Zwitterionic Ionogels Resolving the Trade-Off Between Mechanical Strength and Autonomous Self-Healing for Iontronics
Abstract: Simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness and autonomous self-healing in ionogels remains a fundamental challenge for durable, skin-like electronics. Conventional approaches often improve mechanical strength by introducing rigid or densely cross-linked polymer networks, but such strategies inevitably restrict polymer chain mobility and hinder dynamic bond reconfiguration required for healing. Here, a zwitterionic side-chain engineered tough ionogel (ZESTI) is developed to overcome this trade-off through molecular-level design. Hydrophilic zwitterions are covalently grafted onto a hydrophobic polyurethane backbone to preferentially interact with the ionic liquid through ion–dipole interactions and thereby regulate its distribution. This architecture simultaneously facilitates dipole–dipole interactions for mechanical reinforcement and ion–dipole coordination for efficient self-healing under ambient conditions. As a result, ZESTI exhibits an exceptional combination of tensile strength (10.40 MPa), stretchability (1606%), toughness (56.03 MJ m−3), and ambient self-healing efficiency exceeding 83%, while maintaining high ionic conductivity via enhanced ion hopping. When constructed as a self-reporting packaging interface, ZESTI provides stable protection and state perception under sharp contact and restores signal output after mechanical damage through self-healing. This work offers a generalizable design strategy that reconciles mechanical toughness with dynamic functionality in ionogels, establishing a general design paradigm for next-generation self-sustaining iontronic devices. Title: Alginate-induced structural modification of high-moisture extruded soy and pea protein scaffolds for cultivated meat applications
Abstract: Producing plant-based scaffolds through high-moisture extrusion offers a promising approach for cultivated meat. However, the influence of hydrocolloid incorporation on scaffold structure and functionality remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated alginate incorporation during high-moisture extrusion of pea and soy protein concentrates and evaluated its effect on structure, material properties, and cell distribution.Protein source was associated with differences in processing behavior and extrudate appearance, with soy exhibiting higher specific mechanical energy and darker extrudates than pea. Increased directional alignment was observed in pea extrudates upon alginate addition, whereas soy extrudates only showed moderate structural changes. Mechanical characterization of soy extrudates showed increased stiffness and cohesion compared to pea extrudates, while alginate-containing formulations generally reduced stiffness and increased deformability, potentially reflecting both alginate incorporation and the associated reduction in protein content. Protein extraction differed between pea and soy protein and was altered by alginate addition, indicating changes in protein accessibility, potentially reflecting both altered protein-polysaccharide interactions and the decreased protein content. Scaffold preparation altered surface morphology, with observed increased porosity upon ethanol treatment, especially in alginate-containing scaffolds. Cell experiments showed heterogeneous cell distribution, with observed localized cell accumulation in grooves and cavities.Overall, differences between protein sources were observed in processing behavior, structure, mechanical properties, and protein solubility, while alginate addition altered these properties to varying extents. These findings provide first insights into how formulation composition and scaffold preparation may influence scaffold architecture and cell distribution, for cultivated meat applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Global and Regional Prevalence of Areca Nut Consumption among Children and Adolescents – A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Source title: Pesquisa Brasileira em Odontopediatria e Clinica Integrada
Abstract: Objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis (SRMA) aimed to pool the estimates of prevalence of areca-nut consumption among children and adolescents. Materials and methods: A comprehensive search was done in “PubMed”, “EMBASE”, “Scopus”, and CINAHL databases till 31st December 2024 using search terms “Areca nut” OR “Betel nut” OR “Areca catechu”, “Arecas” AND “Children” OR “Youth” OR “Juvenile” OR “Child” OR “Minor” OR “Teenagers” OR “Adolescent”. Cross-sectional and cohort studies that reported the prevalence of areca nut consumption among children and adolescents, and studies published in English were included. Variables extracted were year, country, age and sex, sample size, prevalence (maximum recall), sex specific prevalence, and type of population. Results: A total of 1447 publications were identified using a systematic search of various databases. Title and abstract screening were performed for 722 publications after removing duplicates (n = 725). Six publications were identified from other websites. Full text screening was performed for 106 publications, which yielded 66 estimates. Males have a significantly higher prevalence than females (OR: 2.6). The pooled prevalence of areca-nut consumption was 29.1 (95% CI: 23-35.3; n = 66) with high heterogeneity. Multiple meta-regression analyses were done, which showed no significant influence of age, male: female ratio, publication year, and the risk of bias score on the overall estimates. Sensitivity analysis showed that the overall estimates were not changed drastically when one study was eliminated successively. Conclusion: Three out of 10 children and adolescents had the habit of consuming areca nuts. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). All rights reserved.

Title: Differentiated impacts of urban expansion patterns on ecosystem services and their socio-ecological drivers: Evidence from the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration in China
Abstract: Urban expansion can alter ecosystem services (ES), yet the effects of different expansion patterns and their socio-ecological drivers remain insufficiently understood. The study focused on the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration (PRD) to understand how different geometric expansion types influence regional ES. The Landscape Expansion Index (LEI) was used to identify interior-filling, edge-spreading, and leap-frogging expansion, while the InVEST model assessed changes in habitat quality, carbon sequestration, soil retention, water yield, and food production. A Random Forest model was further employed to identify the relative importance of ten socio-ecological drivers under different expansion patterns. The results showed a clear spatial gradient, with interior-filling concentrated in the urban core, edge-spreading dominant in the middle belt, and leap-frogging more common in peripheral areas. Carbon sequestration, habitat quality, and food production declined over 2000–2020, with net changes of −11.86 × 108 gC, −21.67 × 104, and −17.12 × 105 t, respectively, while soil retention decreased by 7.73 × 106 t. Water yield increased by 7.24 × 107 mm despite declines during the early periods. Edge-spreading generated the largest absolute ES losses because of its extensive spatial footprint, whereas interior-filling produced the highest ES loss intensity per unit area. The driving mechanisms also differed among patterns: edge-spreading was more sensitive to topography and precipitation, while interior-filling was more strongly associated with socioeconomic factors. Leap-frogging had smaller regional effects but may increase local risks such as habitat fragmentation, soil erosion, and reduced ecological connectivity. These findings suggest that urban growth should be managed according to expansion patterns, with ecological land around urban fringes protected during edge-spreading, ecological safeguards strengthened during interior development, and green infrastructure improved in areas affected by leap-frogging expansion. Title: The American touch: Evaluating the reach of U.S. soft power in India; [رویکرد آمریکایی در ارزیابی دامنة قدرت نرم ایالات متحده در هند]
Abstract: The study assesses the reach and effectiveness of U.S. soft power in India from 2010 to 2025. It also explores how cultural, educational, economic, and diplomatic tools have shaped Indian perceptions of the United States. In this study, using Joseph Nye's soft power theory, qualitative content analysis was combined with quantitative data from Pew surveys and secondary indicators, including educational exchange, aid flows, and trade figures. According to the findings, U.S. influence in India is impressive but unbalanced, with it being strongest in the areas of technology, education, and entertainment, but limited by historical mistrust, cultural sensitivities, and geopolitical complexities. Initiatives such as Fulbright exchanges, immigrant engagement and economic cooperation have fostered goodwill, but apparent inconsistencies in U.S. policy and moral messages continue to limit deep appeal. In conclusion, sustained and creative engagement – based on credit, equality, and shared prosperity – is essential to transforming U.S. cultural appeal into a lasting strategic influence in India's evolving multipolar fabric. © 2026, University of Tehran. Title: Tailor-Made Nanoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks Via Molecular Engineering for Bilirubin-Specific Capture from Liver Failure Patients’ Blood
Abstract: This work innovatively formulated a molecular engineering strategy for nanoframeworks, achieving precise customization of their nanoporous architectures. This work developed a nanoscale bilirubin-specific capture trap, physically overcoming the critical trade-off between bilirubin removal and protein loss. Title: Bi-level coordinated day-ahead dispatch of an electricity–gas–heat–hydrogen integrated energy system with endogenous hourly vehicle-to-grid pricing interaction
Abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy and large-scale EV integration poses new challenges to the optimal scheduling of regional integrated energy systems (RIESs) by intensifying source-load uncertainty and affecting operational flexibility and economic performance. To address this issue, a bi-level optimal dispatch model is developed to coordinate the economic interaction between the RIES operator and EV users through price-based source-load interaction. The upper-level RIES operator minimizes its net operating cost, while the lower-level EV users minimize their net charging/discharging cost. Three EV participation modes, namely disorderly charging, orderly charging, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G), are compared to quantify their impacts on load smoothing, multi-energy coordination, and system-user economics. Scenario generation and reduction are used to construct expected renewable profiles, while Monte Carlo sampling provides heterogeneous EV travel inputs for the deterministic day-ahead bi-level dispatch. Under the zero-degradation-cost setting, the V2G strategy reduces the RIES operator net cost, EV user net cost, and combined resource cost by 5.56%, 47.74%, and 10.99%, respectively, compared with disorderly charging. When battery degradation compensation is considered, the EV-side economic benefit decreases but remains positive; for example, the EV user cost reduction decreases to 42.41% at a degradation cost of 0.10 CNY/kWh. The proposed strategy balances the interests of EV users and the RIES operator while improving load smoothing and flexible coordination of multi-energy flows. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chandran S.; Ramachandran T.; Sivakumar D.; Ambika A.
Title: The impact of environmental, economic, and social sustainability under intensive agriculture
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Intensive agriculture has substantially increased agricultural productivity but is increasingly associated with environmental degradation, resource depletion, and socio-economic challenges. The study objectives were to evaluate the sustainability impacts of intensive agricultural practices across environmental, economic, and social dimensions in Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu, India, with particular emphasis on resource utilization, ecological stress, and the factors influencing sustainable agricultural development. METHODS: Primary data were collected during 2025 from 663 eligible farmers selected through multistage stratified random sampling across eight taluks of Namakkal District using a structured questionnaire. Farms were classified as traditional or intensive based on cultivation practices. Relationships among the study variables were examined using correlation analysis, analysis of variance, regression analysis, and non-parametric statistical tests. FINDINGS: The findings revealed a strong positive relationship between landholding size and family size (correlation coefficient = 0.7214), indicating close structural and demographic linkages within farming systems. Intensive agriculture was significantly associated with land expansion (correlation coefficient = 0.658), environmental pollution (correlation coefficient = 0.519), and declining health conditions among farming communities (correlation coefficient = 0.412). Approximately 63 percent of respondents reported land degradation, while 65 –78 percent reported salinity and nutrient depletion, reflecting perceived ecological stress. The regression model explained 7.1 percent of the variation in agricultural production (coefficient of determination = 0.071), indicating modest explanatory power. Questionnaire reliability was satisfactory (Cronbach's alpha = 0.824), supporting the internal consistency of the survey instrument. CONCLUSION: Intensive agriculture is associated with higher short-term agricultural productivity but is also associated with environmental degradation, increases health risks, and places greater pressure on natural resources. These findings may inform strategies to improve the environmental, economic, and social dimensions of agricultural sustainability through sustainable soil management, balanced agrochemical application, efficient irrigation, and policy support. While the study is limited to a single district and cross-sectional data, it provides empirical evidence to inform future longitudinal and multi-regional investigations. ©2026 The author(s). Authors: Mou X.; Xiao Y.; Huang M.; He W.; Zhao W.; Li Q.

Title: Competition-aware information fusion for cascade popularity prediction
Abstract: Estimating the final size of an information cascade from its early prefix is difficult on open social platforms, where concurrent cascades often compete for overlapping user attention. Existing methods have improved prefix-based prediction with structural, temporal, and continuous-time representations, but external diffusion information is still often treated as generic context. The target-specific competitive environment available at prediction time is therefore not explicitly represented. We propose COMPETE, a competition-aware information fusion framework for macroscopic cascade popularity prediction under historical observability. COMPETE constructs a leakage-free local competition field from cascades visible at the prediction time. It combines structural-anchor and dynamic-burst views to represent the target cascade, selects locally relevant competitors by representation similarity, user overlap, and temporal concurrency, and couples the resulting competitive representation with the endogenous state for popularity estimation. In this formulation, surrounding cascade activity is represented as a target-specific field rather than a coarse context vector. Experiments on four public datasets show that COMPETE outperforms representative baselines in most settings. Additional analyses show that local competition is useful mainly when the observable environment contains stable external signals, which makes prediction-time competition a practical information source for cascade popularity prediction. The source code is publicly available on GitHub . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fu H.; Liang J.; Liang F.; Zhang G.; Han J.
Title: FEDS: Feature and Entropy-Based Distillation Strategy for efficient learned image compression
Abstract: Learned image compression (LIC) offers strong rate–distortion performance, but many high-performing models remain too heavy for deployment. This paper introduces Feature and Entropy-based Distillation Strategy (FEDS), which transfers knowledge from a strong offline teacher to a lightweight student through output supervision, intermediate feature alignment, and entropy-guided latent supervision. The latent objective ranks teacher channels by entropy and transfers the channels with the largest expected coding cost under the student's limited channel budget. On Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC, the student stays close to the teacher, with BD-rate gaps of only 1.24%, 1.17%, and 0.55%, while reducing parameters by 63% and decreasing encoding/decoding time by about 73%. Additional channel-selection, alignment, bit-rate robustness, and transformer-family ablations confirm that FEDS provides an effective compression–efficiency trade-off. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Pan Y.; Zhang A.; Qi C.; Wang Y.; Chen X.; Wang W.; Wang X.; Liu Y.
Title: Pore-confined synthesis of ultra-small Pt nanozymes on gold nanobipyramids for electrochemical detection of cancer cell-derived H2O2
Abstract: Accurate quantification of H2O2 released by tumor cells is important for characterizing cancer-associated oxidative stress, yet conventional biosensors often face an intrinsic trade-off between catalytic activity and structural stability. Herein, we present a rational strategy for real-time electrochemical monitoring of cancer-associated oxidative stress species through the in-situ fabrication of ultrasmall Pt nanozymes confined within the mesoporous silica shell of gold bipyramids (AuPt@SiO2). In this architecture, the Au core provides conductive nucleation and anchoring sites, the mesoporous SiO2 shell regulates Pt growth and affords structural stabilization and molecular-sieving protection, and Pt serves as the catalytic center for H2O2 reduction. The resulting AuPt@SiO2 nanozyme exhibited pronounced peroxidase-like activity with a favorable Michaelis-Menten constant (Km) of 6.08 mM toward H2O2. After integration into a Nafion-based sensing interface, the enzyme-free sensor provided complementary linear ranges of 0.25-60 mM by cyclic voltammetry and 1-2100 μM by amperometry with a detection limit at 0.3 μM of H2O2. The electrochemical sensor based on AuPt@SiO2 also demonstrated excellent repeatability and exceptional stability, retaining over 85% of its initial response after 30 days. Importantly, this platform enabled label-free monitoring of phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-triggered H2O2 efflux from MGC-803 gastric cancer cells and differentiated their oxidative-stress phenotype from that of normal gastric epithelial cells. The apparent H2O2-equivalent response normalized to cell number was approximately 1.72 × 10−13 M per cell. This work highlights the potential of confined nanozymes for high-performance H2O2 sensing and precise pathological profiling at the single-cell level. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Beyond green claims: a social-ecological assessment of cruise tourism sustainability
Abstract: Cruise tourism sustainability discourse prioritises vessel level innovation, marginalising destination level social ecological impacts. To address this, we develop a structured literature based conceptual model of cruise mobility as a coupled global and local social ecological system. Supported by AI assisted extraction and synthesis of multidisciplinary literature, this paper constructs a governance-oriented framework. The analysis identifies two interacting dynamics: a reinforcing expansion loop where revenues stimulate infrastructure and deepen dependency, and a degrading acceptance loop where cumulative stress erodes tolerance. Presented as heuristic formalisation devices, these loops help explain why vessel efficiency alone cannot prevent destination level degradation. We translate these findings into a five-pillar governance framework featuring capacity thresholds, social monitoring, economic diversification, power rebalancing, and multi-level coordination. This shifts attention from ship focused compliance towards destination embedded sustainability governance. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Yadem Lamien M.H.; Farzaneh H.
Author full names: Yadem Lamien, Mohammed Hussien (59525273700); Farzaneh, Hooman (15848542900)
Title: Optimal planning of rooftop PV systems participating in local energy markets: evidence from Japan's electricity market
Abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems integrated into community-based local energy markets (CBMs) offer a promising solution for urban energy transitions by enabling local consumption of surplus energy. This study develops a comprehensive modeling framework to investigate (1) the impact of CBM dynamics on the optimal sizing and configuration of rooftop PV systems, and (2) the potential of the proposed system to mitigate feed-in-tariff (FiT)–related challenges, especially renewable energy curtailment due to limited grid capacity. The developed model is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) framework to identify rooftop PV configurations that maximize total social welfare in residential areas operating and trading within a CBM, distinguishing it from previous studies that primarily focus on technical, spatial, economic, or aesthetic aspects of rooftop PV planning. The developed CBM-based Rooftop PV system optimization model is validated using data from the Japan Electric Power Exchange (JEPX) market, combined with electricity load and meteorological data from Fukuoka City in Kyushu, a major island in Japan, which has frequently experienced challenges associated with FiT-induced renewable energy curtailment. Four market scenarios with varying FiT and CBM fees are considered to assess their impact on rooftop PV spatial deployment and electricity transactions. The results reveal that rooftop PV deployment is highly sensitive to FiT levels and CBM dynamics, and CBM further enhances local utilization. The results highlight that lower FiT levels combined with CBM can reduce subsidy burdens while promoting intra-community energy exchange and more efficient use of rooftop PV systems in urban systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Al-Hattami H.M.; Al-Sinawi S.
Title: Ethical reasoning and responsible use of ChatGPT in higher education: Integrating technology acceptance and moral cognition
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT into higher education has raised important questions about how students evaluate the ethical implications of AI-assisted academic practices and whether those evaluations are linked to intentions to use these tools responsibly. While previous research has largely focused on technology adoption and acceptance, it has paid less attention to the relationship between ethical reasoning and intentions to use these tools responsibly. This study develops and tests an integrated framework that combines the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and moral cognition theory to examine how technology perceptions and academic and cognitive factors relate to students’ ethical reasoning and intentions to use ChatGPT responsibly. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design among business and management students in Oman and analysed the data using structural equation modelling. The findings indicate that perceived ease of use, academic pressure, and moral disengagement are positively associated with ethical reasoning, whereas perceived usefulness is not significantly associated with ethical reasoning. Ethical reasoning is positively associated with behavioural intention to use ChatGPT responsibly. In contrast, ChatGPT usage does not significantly moderate the relationship between academic pressure and ethical reasoning. These findings suggest that students’ responsible-use intentions are associated with their ethical evaluations of ChatGPT-assisted academic practices, while conventional technology acceptance perceptions and usage frequency alone offer a more limited explanation of ethical reasoning. The study contributes to emerging research on responsible generative AI use by extending TAM beyond conventional adoption outcomes and integrating it with a moral cognition perspective. It highlights the relationship between ethical reasoning and responsible-use intentions while distinguishing ethical evaluation from technology acceptance and usage frequency. The findings also provide context-specific evidence from Omani higher education, while recognising the limitations of the cross-sectional design, self-reported measures, and a context-specific sample. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Social inequalities and occupational disease in Colombia: An ecological analysis of the 2021 ENCSST and associated determinants; [Desigualdades sociales y enfermedad laboral en Colombia: análisis ecológico de la ENCSST 2021 y determinantes asociados]
Abstract: Introduction. Occupational disease represents a growing public health challenge in Colombia, characterized by marked territorial inequalities associated with socioeconomic, organizational, and exposure-related factors. Objective. To describe the prevalence of occupational disease in Colombia and to identify the associated socioeconomic, organizational, and exposure-related factors across the country's six regions. Materials and methods. An exploratory ecological study was conducted using regional data from the 2021 National Survey of Working Conditions and Health (ENCSST) and socioeconomic indicators from DANE and DNP. Spearman correlations were estimated between occupational disease prevalence and variables related to exposure, organizational conditions, and structural determinants. A multiple linear regression model was developed to identify factors associated with regional variation. Results. The prevalence of occupational disease showed substantial disparities, ranging from 36 cases per 100,000 workers in the Pacific region to 2,289 per 100,000 in the Amazon region. Implementation of the Occupational Health and Safety Management System (SG-SST) was significantly inversely associated with prevalence ( β = -6.04 ; 95% CI: -7 to -5 ; p = 0.002 ). Exposure to biological hazards ( β = 6.29 ; 95% CI: 5-7.62; p = 0.002 ) and multidimensional poverty ( β = 1.06 ; 95% CI: 0.652-1.47; p = 0.008 ) were positively associated with higher prevalence. The model explained 50 of the regional variation. Conclusions. Occupational disease in Colombia reflects profound territorial inequalities driven by the interaction between social vulnerability, occupational exposure, and organizational capacity. Strengthening the Occupational Health and Safety Management System, implementing differential epidemiological surveillance, and reducing structural gaps are key priorities to decrease the burden of occupational disease in the country. © 2027, Instituto Nacional de Salud. Author full names: Chapman, Sian (57199654457); Roy, David (57192113395); Baker, William (56103706800); Hotko, Katie (57216943296); Hamilton, Amy (57205702241); Burke, Katie (56261924100)
Title: Supporting initial teacher education student creativity and critical thinking using active constraints in assessment: A scoping review
Abstract: Assessment design plays a critical role in shaping student learning in higher education, particularly in disciplines where creativity is both a learning outcome and a pedagogical approach. In Initial Teacher Education (ITE), this role is intensified, as assessment tasks often function as the primary site of learning for time-poor students and simultaneously model pedagogical practice for future teachers. While constraints are frequently embedded within assessment tasks, their role in supporting creativity remains under-theorised and inconsistently articulated in the literature. This scoping review examines how constraints are used within assessment tasks that aim to foster creativity and/or critical thinking in social sciences, humanities, education and creative arts courses in higher education in order to consider implications for enhancing creativity through assessment tasks in ITE. Using a scoping review framework, 28 empirical studies published since 2000 were identified and analysed thematically. Six key themes emerged: the role of prior experience, constraints as catalysts for creativity, task design and flexibility, rubrics and scaffolding as support structures, the domain-specificity of creativity, and the presence of “invisible architectures” in task design. Findings indicate that constraints function as powerful pedagogical mechanisms when they are intentionally designed, aligned with disciplinary practices, and calibrated to student readiness. However, many studies prioritise creative outcomes without sufficiently detailing the task conditions that shape them. Drawing on these findings, the paper positions constraints as active contributors to assessment design and introduces a design-oriented framework to support educators in making constraints explicit and pedagogically purposeful. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Artificial intelligence and generative AI in entrepreneurship education: A systematic review of competency development, entrepreneurial intention, and the sustainability disconnect
Abstract: Entrepreneurship education increasingly deploys artificial intelligence (AI), yet claims that it builds entrepreneurial competence and advances sustainability rest on an unexamined evidence base. This review asks what that evidence supports, and what it does not. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus and Web of Science searches yielded 21 empirical studies with approximately 7800 unique participants across 14 countries. Studies were stratified as generative, broader or analytical AI, quality was appraised item by item with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and every conclusion was tested by sensitivity analysis. CIMO logic specified the question; TCM-ADO organised the synthesis. AI was positively associated with entrepreneurial intention in every study that measured it, but its magnitude cannot be established: the largest estimates come from the lowest-quality studies, and few report uncertainty estimates. Competency development, the assumed mechanism, rests almost entirely on non-generative AI studies and is untested for generative systems. Self-efficacy operates as a boundary condition, raising an equity concern no study measures. Nominal relevance to the Sustainable Development Goals is widespread, yet none measured a sustainability outcome or named an environmental goal. It supplies a stratified, quality-weighted evidence base and shows that closing the sustainability gap requires theory and instruments, not more intention surveys. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chen Z.
Title: Toward vulnerability-friendly destinations: A relational framework for inclusive destination governance
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourism research has generally located vulnerability in particular travelers and treated inclusion as an extension of accessibility provision. This paper reframes vulnerability as a relational destination-level condition produced, intensified, or reduced through interactions between heterogeneous human capacities and destination-system demands. A structured integrative conceptual synthesis connects public health equity, human factors engineering, and tourism management. The resulting framework explains how unequal exposure creates person-system mismatch, how destination arrangements produce vulnerability through recurring interfaces, and how inclusive-governance capability operates both preventively by shaping system properties and responsively by coordinating intervention. Risk redistribution is specified as a distinct mechanism that follows risk reduction and the allocation of responsibility, workload, and cost, and concerns the pooling, transfer, or absorption of residual risk by actors with greater capacity. Five recurring exposure interfaces and four intervention dimensions are organized in an analytical matrix. The framework distinguishes proximal outcomes (participation, safety, dignity, trust, and wellbeing) from conditional destination outcomes such as legitimacy, loyalty, and competitiveness. The paper extends relational vulnerability logic to the destination-system level and provides a research agenda for inclusive destination governance. © 2026
