Title: Investigating the interplay between public art, urban design, and national identity: Case of the UAE
Abstract: Public art and culturally responsive urban environment play a crucial role in shaping national identity, particularly in culturally diverse and rapidly evolving societies like the UAE. This study examines how different forms of public art, their integration into urban spaces, and digital platforms influence perceptions of national identity. Grounded in Social Identity Theory, Place Attachment Theory, and Public Space Theory, it employs structural equation modeling (SEM) and thematic analysis using data from 543 respondents across UAE emirates. The SEM model explains 40.3% of the variance in Perceived National Identity (PNI), emphasizing the significant role of public art and digital platforms in cultural engagement. Mediation analysis highlights the importance of interactive experiences in strengthening cultural connections, while thematic analysis identifies cultural integration, community involvement, and sustainability as key themes. Findings suggest that combining traditional Emirati artistic elements with modern digital technologies enhances inclusivity and engagement. However, the limited direct impact of urban design on national identity highlights the need for culturally relevant elements to maximize its effectiveness. By integrating quantitative and qualitative insights, this study offers clear implications for policy and practice by recommending participatory planning, integration of heritage-based design elements and use of digital platforms to enhance cultural visibility and engagement. It provides a practical framework for urban planners, cultural policymakers, and designers to develop inclusive public spaces that reinforce national identity in the UAE. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Yin B.; Wu X.-R.; Lian R.
Title: AI-assisted interactive narrative as an integrative-learning design task: Student appraisal in preservice teacher education
Abstract: Research on generative AI in education often asks whether these tools improve learning outcomes. Collaborative design raises a prior question: how should teaching organize AI-supported work so that disciplinary knowledge, creativity, collaboration, and human judgment come together? Integrative learning names that aim: connecting disciplinary knowledge with situated experience and synthesizing insights across cases. Integration matters in teacher education, where preservice teachers must apply principles to ambiguous professional situations. We examined an AI-assisted interactive-narrative (AI-IN) assignment in which preservice teachers designed branching professional-ethics games through a whole-part-whole sequence: course-wide orientation, collaborative development of a focal case with AI-supported possibility generation, and cross-case reintegration. We used self-reports from a 480-person primary cohort and an independent 257-person same-course cohort to ask how students appraised the design, whether the learning ratings shared residual covariance in a one-factor model, and which conditions accompanied appraisal. Allowing residual covariance between the two perceived-learning ratings improved the one-factor model in both cohorts (scaled Δχ²(1) = 11.99 and 14.20, respectively; both p < .001); the localized association was stable across sensitivity analyses. This localized covariance may reflect perceived-learning content or shared-method influences, including wording and placement; it establishes neither learning gains nor a distinct latent domain. In the primary cohort, favorable appraisal accompanied clearer roles, efficient collaboration, greater contribution, better challenge-engagement balance, and positive AI attitudes. Students reported challenges in translating ethics into plots, selecting platforms, and managing workload. AI-IN offers a testable design proposition for integrative learning: AI supports possibility generation while students retain responsibility for selection, verification, ethical judgment, and synthesis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Spectral clustering based on neighborhood relationships and the number of nearest neighbors k
Abstract: Spectral clustering has become a mainstream method for clustering complex data due to its strong adaptability to non-convex distributions, high-dimensional data, and manifold structures. The performance of spectral clustering is directly determined by the quality of the similarity matrix, yet conventional methods often rely on globally fixed parameters, making it difficult to accommodate local structural variations in the data, which can easily lead to degraded clustering results. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel spectral clustering algorithm based on neighborhood relationships and the number of nearest neighbors k(SC-k). The algorithm constructs an ε-neighborhood graph that integrates mean and variance, uses the average distance between a sample and its k nearest neighbors as a local scaling parameter, and designs a new Gaussian kernel similarity measure. This ensures both sparsity and reasonableness of the similarity matrix while reducing sensitivity to the parameter k. Title: Experimental validation of an E-GOA-Based MPPT for PV-SEPIC systems under challenging irradiance conditions
Abstract: In photovoltaic systems, partial shading and rapidly changing irradiance create multiple peaks in the power-voltage (P-V) characteristic, making global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) challenging. The grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA) provides a population-based search mechanism for GMPPT but remains sensitive to search boundaries and algorithm parameters. This work establishes, through simulation and hardware experiments, an enhanced GOA (E-GOA) for MPPT of PV-SEPIC systems. In the proposed implementation, the search space is defined directly by the converter duty cycle, with each search agent corresponding to a candidate operating point within the prescribed limits. The search process is reinitialized when the relative variation in PV output power exceeds a predefined threshold. The search dynamics are re-tuned through the social-force parameters and a linearly decreasing control coefficient to balance exploration and exploitation. E-GOA was evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink using a 162 W PV array under ten uniform irradiance levels, ten mismatched patterns and four dynamic scenarios. The methods were benchmarked against PSO, GWO, FA and P&O over 1000 independent runs using tracking efficiency, RMSE, MAE and STD. E-GOA tracked the MPP at 1000 W/m2 in 0.33s, compared with 0.55 s for FA, 0.64 s for PSO and 0.91 s for GWO. Under mismatched irradiance, E-GOA achieved average tracking efficiencies of 94.21-97.25%, compared with 86.65-95.89% for PSO and 53.46-85.21% for P&O. Experimental validation showed that E-GOA achieved tracking efficiencies ranging from 98.99% to 99.95% across the tested scenarios. The measurement uncertainty of the experimental acquisition chain was also quantified. These results confirm the effectiveness of E-GOA for fast and reliable GMPPT. © 2026

Authors: Hao Y.; Xu H.; Li X.
Title: Motivations in Chinese costume travel photography: An evolutionary psychology perspective
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourist photography has shifted from passive sightseeing to active narrative construction. Existing research has revealed the proximate motives of such behavior centered on identity construction, but the ultimate motives remain underexplored. Using a qualitative research design, this study explores motivations in Chinese costume travel photography by applying three interpretive lenses derived from evolutionary psychology, namely performative affiliation, temporary status, and scripted exploration. The findings indicate that participants' motivations are satisfied in Chinese costume travel photography as follows: temporary immersion and affiliation are gained from symbolic imitation and contextual co-performance; contextualized status enhancement is acquired by enacting ideal identities and collecting digital validation; and novelty seeking is met through experiences grounded in symbolic imagination and pre-arranged scripts. This study provides insights into the ultimate drivers of tourists’ surface motivations and the possible satisfaction mechanisms of deep evolutionary motives in Chinese costume travel photography. It also offers practical insights for tourism experience design and marketing by focusing on the satisfaction of deep motives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Herzlinger G.; Galanidou N.
Title: The Acheulean Large Cutting Tool Assemblage from Rodafnidia, Lesvos: A 3D Morpho-technological Cross-regional Comparative Analysis
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: The Acheulean, a key Lower Palaeolithic technocomplex characterised by iconic large cutting tools (LCTs), is one of the most extensively studied phenomena in prehistoric archaeology. Yet its vast chrono-spatial distribution, together with the persistent tension between technological homogeneity and variability, has hindered the construction of robust cultural phylogenetic scenarios for its evolution and dispersal. One way to address this challenge is to develop regional- and continental-scale syntheses of industrial traits based on standardised analytical protocols. Such protocols can help overcome differences in site context, artifact recovery, chronology and publication standards that reflect diverse geographic, chronological and academic traditions. In tune with this we integrate technological and computational archaeological analyses under open science principles to conduct a comparative study of Acheulean variability and cultural phylogeny at the Eurasian crossroads of the Aegean and the southern Levant. Our point of departure is Rodafnidia, a Middle Pleistocene locality on the island of Lesvos, Greece, where excavations have revealed stratified Acheulean knapped stone tool assemblages. We present a comprehensive morpho-technological analysis of an LCT assemblage composed of handaxes and cleavers from Rodafnidia. The analysis evaluates contextual integrity and examines the relationship between technological procedures and morphological features across well-provenanced stratified artifacts and surface finds. Given the scarcity of Acheulean assemblages in the Balkan Peninsula and western Anatolia, we compare the Rodafnidia material with five handaxe assemblages from ‘Ubeidiya, Gesher Benot Ya’aqov (GBY), Ma’ayan Barukh, Holon, and Nahal Hesi, as well as with nine cleaver assemblages from GBY. Together, these reference assemblages span different chrono-cultural stages of the Levantine Acheulean. The results reveal a high degree of homogeneity within the Rodafnidia assemblage, indicating consistent technological preferences and recurrent morphological outcomes. At the same time, the morpho-technological configuration identified at Rodafnidia differs from any pattern recognised among the studied Levantine assemblages. Our research protocol underscores the value of integrated comparative morpho-technological analyses for investigating the complex evolutionary and cultural dynamics of Acheulean hominin populations. More broadly, our findings contribute to a nuanced understanding of Middle Pleistocene Acheulean variability and cultural phylogeny in this part of the Mediterranean, while demonstrating a scalable approach that can be applied across the Acheulean world. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Homer S.T.
Title: From fragmentation to integration: Rethinking the measurement of responsible management education
Abstract: Responsible Management Education (RME) has become a central agenda within business schools, as institutions seek to prepare graduates capable of addressing complex sustainability and societal challenges. Despite its growing prominence, approaches to evaluating RME remain fragmented, with studies measuring diverse educational, institutional and societal outcomes using inconsistent conceptualisations and indicators. This study systematically reviews the contemporary literature to examine how RME is currently measured and develop a more coherent conceptual framework for evaluation. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature review of 62 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2016 and 2026 using the Scopus database—an AI-assisted, human-in-the-loop thematic synthesis identified and consolidated 328 measurement-related concepts. The synthesis identified five complementary measurement domains: implementation, learning, behaviour, performance and impact, alongside five stakeholder groups: students, educators, institutions, industry and society. Building on these findings, the study proposes the Integrated Responsible Management Education Measurement Framework (IRMEF) as a multidimensional conceptual evaluation architecture that organises these domains and stakeholder perspectives. Rather than representing an empirically validated measurement model, the IRMEF provides a common conceptual vocabulary for organising existing approaches and guiding future evaluation and empirical validation. It provides a foundation for greater theoretical coherence and methodological consistency while supporting business schools, accreditation bodies, and policymakers seeking more balanced, multidimensional, and contextually appropriate approaches to RME evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Peng C.; Jing Q.; Zhang R.; Chen M.; Yu R.
Title: Hierarchical contrastive learning for multi-modal representation in Alzheimer's disease diagnosis
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis increasingly relies on the integration of multi-modal data, including structural magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. However, existing methods often inadequately explore the discriminative information within each modality and fail to fully capture complementary interactions between modalities. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical contrastive learning method which can fully utilize the intra-modal and inter-modal information, guiding the model to learn a well-structured feature space to improve the performance of diagnosis. Specifically, our method first introduces intra-modal alignment, which enforces supervised contrastive constraints within each modality, thereby effectively exploiting discriminative information between different clinically diagnosed groups. Secondly, we innovatively propose a clinical label-guided inter-modal alignment method to exploit the complementary interactions between modalities, leading to more discriminative and coherent representations. Furthermore, a dynamic learning strategy is employed between the intra-modal and inter-modal alignments to ensure the stability of the training process and achieve the comprehensive hierarchical contrastive learning. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches, validating its efficiency in learning discriminative multi-modal representations for AD related diagnosis. Authors: Guo R.; Wang Y.; Gong T.; Li C.
Title: Advancing family bonding: A conditional framework from immersion to communitas
Abstract: A gap still exists between mobile social media-embedded modern family tourism and family relationship improvement. From a communitas perspective, this study proposes a conditional immersion-communitas relationship improvement framework to address this gap. Evidence from multi-wave surveys, an eye-tracking experiment, focus group interviews, and multiple field experiments shows that: (1) social media notification management is a key precondition for relationship improvement; compared with notification-off, visual, or auditory models, haptic notifications better sustain relationship improvement through the full chain mediation of immersion and communitas; (2) happiness experience type (eudaimonia vs. hedonia) moderates the immersion maintenance mechanism, with hedonia family members relying more on notification management; (3) family structure (intragenerational vs. intergenerational) also moderates the process: the positive effect of communitas on family relationship improvement is stronger in intergenerational families than in intragenerational ones. This study advances understanding of modern family tourism and offers practical implications for both individual management and external intervention. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Combating human trafficking in Vietnam: How does the 3P+P framework influence policies and laws?
Abstract: Human trafficking remains among the greatest human rights violations globally, and Vietnam—as both a source country and a transit country—has undergone substantial legal and policy reform over the past fifteen years. This article systematically analyzes the development of Vietnam's legal and policy framework for the prevention and control of human trafficking from 2010 to 2025, applying the 3P+P theoretical framework (Prevention, Protection, Prosecution, and Partnership) as the primary analytical lens. Drawing on doctrinal legal analysis and policy analysis, this study examines domestic legislation, including the 2011 Law on Prevention and Combat of Trafficking in Persons, the 2015 Penal Code (as amended in 2017), and the landmark 2024 Law on Prevention and Combat of Trafficking in Persons, alongside international instruments—notably the Palermo Protocol and the ASEAN Convention Against Trafficking in Persons (ACTIP)—and empirical materials from UNODC, UNDP, and the U.S. Department of State's annual Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Reports. Analysis across three phases (2010–2015, 2016–2020, and 2021–2025) reveals a progressive trajectory from foundational criminalization toward a multisectoral, human rights-centered approach, reflecting both endogenous developmental priorities and exogenous normative pressures. Key findings indicate that while Vietnam has achieved meaningful normative alignment with international standards—particularly in victim protection, legal aid, and regional cooperation—critical implementation gaps persist, including inadequate victim identification, weak interagency coordination, the absence of corporate supply chain accountability, and delayed legal responses to emerging exploitation forms such as online scam operations. This study offers the first longitudinal 3P+P analysis of Vietnam's complete 2010–2025 legal and policy trajectory, including the 2024 Law, highlighting the persistent gap between normative progress and implementation outcomes. Accordingly, the article proposes concrete legal amendments: incorporating “abuse of a position of vulnerability” into Article 150 of the Penal Code, formalizing NGO legal status in specialized law, and establishing a corporate accountability regime for forced labor in supply chains. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Kumar A.
Title: From distraction to engagement: An applied examination of the IMPACT framework in technology-rich management education
Abstract: Student perceptions of instructional effectiveness in technology-rich management education remain actively studied amid concerns about classroom distraction in digitally mediated environments. This study introduces IMPACT—an integrative pedagogical framework composed of Incentive, Measurement, Project-based Learning, Accountability, Critical Reflection, and Technology. It presents an exploratory, multi-course demonstration across four management courses spanning the MBA, Executive MBA (EMBA), and Executive Postgraduate Diploma in Management (EPGDM–VIL) programs, delivered in face-to-face and synchronous online modes. Implementation was examined using institutional course-evaluation data (N = 202 of 203 enrolled students), and a thematic close reading of open-ended comments informed by reflexive thematic analysis. Across all four courses, student perceptions of instructional effectiveness were uniformly high on standardized nine-item instrument (weighted averages ≥ 6.0 on a seven-point scale). Qualitative themes aligned with the framework's design intent: practical relevance, structured project workflows, visible progress indicators, and technology-mediated tools, alongside integrative configuration as a framework-level property. Findings support consistent implementation across heterogeneous settings and association with positive student perceptions, but do not support causal claims about engagement. The study contributes design-oriented vocabulary identifying integrative configuration, operational workflow, and multi-mode portability as the framework's primary contributions. Limitations include single-institution, single-instructor, construct–measurement mismatch, and the absence of comparative or pre/post designs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Spatio-temporal cross attention involved dual graph convolution network for traffic flow prediction
Abstract: Traffic flow prediction is a critical task in intelligent transportation systems. The main challenge lies in the existence of complex, intertwined and dynamically evolving spatio-temporal dependencies in real-world traffic networks. Existing methods often rely on inherent static road network graph structures, lacking focus on the key time nodes and effective interaction mechanisms of spatio-temporal dimension information. To address this limitation, we propose a traffic flow prediction model named spatio-temporal cross attention involved dual graph convolution network. Our method adopts a parallel framework to synchronously extract features from both spatial and temporal dimensions. It spatially achieves enhanced learning of global and local dynamic dependencies through a dual graph convolution module, and temporally, it combines a long short-term memory network with a temporal attention module to capture continuous temporal correlations. Then through a cross attention fusion module, it dynamically integrates spatio-temporal information and establishes an interaction mechanism between them. Extensive experiments on four real-world traffic datasets from the Caltrans performance measurement system (PeMS03, PeMS04, PeMS07 and PeMS08) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average performance improvement of 2% to 15% compared with existing baseline models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Xie T.C.; Wang X.L.
Title: The blind spots of in-situ upgrading: Rethinking social infrastructure
Abstract: In-situ upgrading has become a preferred strategy for improving informal settlements worldwide, yet its focus on physical infrastructure often obscures the social infrastructures that sustain everyday life. This study examines how communal spaces—alleyways, rooftops, and other informally produced environments—function as urban commons and how they become vulnerable during upgrading processes. Drawing on Schlager and Ostrom’s bundles-of-rights framework, document analysis, field observations, and 105 interviews, the research traces changes in access, use, management, and ownership of communal spaces during a comprehensive in-situ upgrading project in Nantou, Shenzhen. The findings show that social infrastructure in informal settlements is constituted through shared routines, tacit norms, and collective practices rather than formal design, making it particularly susceptible to enclosure when upgrading prioritizes aesthetic, commercial, or heritage objectives. The study identifies governance displacement as a mechanism through which upgrading reconfigures rights and responsibilities, producing non-physical forms of dispossession even without relocation. By conceptualising social infrastructure as urban commons, the paper advances a framework for recognizing and protecting these often-invisible systems. The findings offer transferable insights for upgrading practices globally, highlighting the need for governance-sensitive, participatory approaches that safeguard the social foundations of community life. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Building on sand: state capacity, livelihoods, and the limits of environmental governance in Cabo Verde
Abstract: Cabo Verde has built an extensive environmental policy framework, ratifying major multilateral agreements and enacting decree-laws that formally regulate the exploitation of natural resources. Yet on Santiago Island, small-scale illegal extraction of development minerals by low-income households continues to cause severe degradation of beaches, watersheds and hillsides. Drawing on fieldwork in two northern municipalities (São Miguel and Tarrafal) and 25 semi-structured interviews with community leaders and sand and gravel extractors, this article investigates why extraction persists despite a dense regulatory architecture. We find that extraction is a survivalist strategy primarily undertaken by women heads of household, for whom environmental regulation represents a direct threat to precarious livelihoods. Mobilising the "environmental state" framework and feminist political ecology (Nightingale, 2006). We argue that state intervention has tightened coastal enforcement but displaced extraction into riverbeds and hillsides, intensifying rather than reducing aggregate environmental pressure. We characterise this as "governing through precarity", an environmental state present in law and on highly visible beaches, though absent in inland sites where the poorest extractors work. By centring the politics of enforcement and social reproduction, the article contributes to global debates on artisanal extraction, gender, and informality in African Small Island Developing States (SIDS). © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Engel W.E.
Title: “Whose Death Killed Death, and Took Away His Sting”: Aemilia Lanyer-s Subtle Art of Death in Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum
Abstract: Historically grounded approaches to the Renaissance “death arts” can be used to illuminate Lanyer-s mobilizing and transforming of standard rhetorical tropes and poetic conceits—most notably the blazon—to reconceptualize and represent the bliss-imbued chiastic movement from Jesus-s incarnation and death by crucifixion to the resurrected Christ-s making possible the prospect of eternal life. Consonant with Lanyer-s participation in the querelle des femmes (the longstanding controversy over women-s ontological and social status in a patriarchally organized world-system), Salve Deus partakes of earlier traditions of female piety like those popularized in The Golden Legend, and also the Christus Mortuus contemplative technique brought to prominence in Reformation England by Katherine Parr. Lanyer-s poem thus provides a rich case study in the death arts to promote a novel, reconfigured form of female piety predicated on a series of stunning memory images of the grotesquely maimed and blood-drenched male body. Title: A Holistic Framework for Paleolithic Projectile Studies: Insights from Swabian Gravettian Fléchettes
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Projectile technology and long-range weapons represent a major innovation in human evolution, shaping subsistence strategies, complex behavior, and advanced planning skills. Given the fast decay of organic remains, the Upper Paleolithic record is dominated by lithic implements, which are often classified as projectiles based primarily on morphological characteristics. However, such typological classifications frequently overlook macro- and microfractures that signal actual projectile use and may vary between different weapon systems. Here, we present the results of a detailed technological and functional analysis of 54 fléchettes from the Gravettian layers of the cave sites Hohle Fels, Brillenhöhle, and Geißenklösterle. Using a holistic approach including multiple analytical approaches spanning from lithic technology, traceology, projectile experiments, and statistics allowed a more comprehensive and robust analysis of possible wear patterns linked to projectile use. The technological analysis focused on the production sequence and morphological variability of the fléchettes, while use-wear analysis was employed to identify macro- and micro traces indicative of projectile use. The observed traces were tested against a reference assemblage of experimentally replicated fléchettes knapped from Jurassic chert and radiolarite, the two primary lithic materials used in the Swabian Gravettian. The experiments tested different propulsion modes, including spear-throwing and bow-and-arrow propulsion, as well as the influence of raw material variability on the formation of macro traces. The results reveal a high overlap of use-wear traces between Ach Valley fléchettes and fléchettes used in experimental spear-throwing while clustering with TCSA values of ethnographic arrowheads. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that fléchettes were likely adapted for projectile use in a long-range weapon system, complementing other Gravettian point types in a modular projectile design that reflects the versatile technological and subsistence organization in the Swabian Gravettian. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Analysis of medical isotope yield based on 232Th(p, x)225Ac reaction
Abstract: Actinium-225 (225Ac) has emerged as a premier medical isotope for targeted alpha therapy (TAT), yet its large-scale production remains impeded by multiple technical challenges. This study aims to develop an optimal thick-target scheme for 225Ac production via proton beam irradiation of thorium targets. Specifically, the FLUKA code was employed to quantify and analyze the impacts of thorium target thickness and incident proton energy on both 225Ac production yield and the maximum deposition power density within the target, thereby identifying the optimal proton energy and corresponding target thickness parameters. The results indicate that irradiating an 18-cm-thick thorium target with 500 MeV protons maximizes 225Ac production efficiency under the constraint of constant proton beam power. This work achieves an optimal trade-off among 225Ac yield, proton energy, and target heat load, thereby providing a critical technical reference for the efficient and scalable production of this pivotal medical isotope. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Speed-Resolved experimental and CFD evaluation of a Low-Power Intake-Air ionization retrofit for diesel combustion and emission control
Abstract: A low-power intake-air ionization attachment was experimentally and numerically evaluated as a retrofit strategy for diesel-engine performance and emission control without fuel reformulation or engine modification. A single-cylinder compression-ignition engine was tested under baseline and staged ionized-air conditions at 300–1500 rpm, with five repeated measurements at each operating point. Each negative-ion module operated at a fixed 12 V DC input (<1 W per module) with device-rated values of approximately −9.5 kV DC high-voltage output, 1.2 x 1013 ions s−1 negative-ion production, and 1.9 x 1012 ions cm−3 at a 2.9-cm reference distance. The staged strategy activated one to five modules as speed increased. At the fully load-matched 1500-rpm condition, brake power and torque remained 1.94072 kW and 12.35 N m in both modes, while fuel mass-flow rate decreased from 2.34 x 10-4 to 2.25 x 10-4 kg s−1. Using an LHV of 42.5 MJ kg−1, BSFC decreased from 0.4341 to 0.4174 kg kW-1h−1 and brake thermal efficiency increased from 19.51 % to 20.30 %. Across the speed range, mean exhaust-gas temperature decreased by 6.8–19.8 °C and CO, HC, and NOx analyzer concentrations were lower under the staged ionization-ON condition. Crank-angle-resolved in-cylinder pressure and ion-current signals were measured, and apparent net and cumulative heat release were derived from the pressure trace. A steady three-dimensional RANS model used displacement-consistent inlet conditions based on the 0.363-L swept volume and eta_v = 0.82. Grid refinement at 1500 rpm used approximately 1.6, 3.2, 6.3, 12.6, and 25.2 million cells; the 6.3-million-cell grid was selected as the production mesh after the monitored solution changed by less than 1 % with further refinement. Residual reduction, monitored-variable stability, and inlet–outlet mass conservation were verified before post-processing. Title: Adaptive energy management of storage-enabled microgrids using emission-aware demand-side flexibility aggregation
Abstract: Microgrids play a key role in distributed energy systems by facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, maintaining system reliability, and creating economic value. However, optimising their operation remains challenging, as it requires balancing conflicting objectives under operational constraints. This paper presents a novel customer-centric adaptive microgrid energy management framework using a two-stage ε-constraint multi-objective optimisation approach to balance competing objectives: minimising operational costs and emissions, enhancing technical performance through load factor improvement, and maximising customer benefits via dynamic reward allocation. The proposed two-stage response mechanism, formulated as a non-convex MINLP, exploits the flexibility of both economic- and comfort-oriented consumers within a coordinated system optimisation framework. The first stage models consumer participation using a coefficient of participation (CoP) and an incentive-based structure, enabling significant load adjustments. In the second stage, the microgrid operator exploits the aggregated flexibility of comfort-oriented consumers to solve the multi-objective problem and generate feasible optimal solutions. To improve computational efficiency, this paper reformulates the model as an MIQP using the Big-M method and McCormick relaxation. The framework is validated against real-world data from an Australian grid-connected microgrid. Results indicate that, relative to a no-flexibility baseline, economic-oriented consumers reduce individual energy consumption by up to 33%, with load factor improvements of up to 10%. The analysis also reveals clear trade-offs among the objectives by generating solutions with an average computation time of approximately 3 seconds per feasible solution, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed coordinated energy management in balancing technical, economic, and social objectives in microgrid operation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Traditional or simplified Chinese? Exploring the use of linguistic variants in tourism linguistic landscape
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: By employing a two-phase mixed-method research design (i.e. survey and interviews), this study investigates residents' and tourists' perceptions of the effectiveness of language variants of Chinese characters in public signage within Macao's tourism landscape. The findings reveal that while simplified Chinese may be favored for its practicality, traditional Chinese retains significant cultural and identity values among residents and enhances the travel experiences by signally authenticity. Additionally, the research highlights perceived cultural erosion among the local community and concerns over prioritizing tourists' needs at the expense of local identity. This study extends linguistic landscape scholarship by illustrating how script variants within a shared language carry distinct practical and symbolic meanings for different stakeholders. Finally, this research proposes an exploratory needs–affect–attachment framework and a theoretically informed model of tourism power relations to conceptualize these dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Uncovering creative metacognition patterns in TVET innovation education: insight from an epistemic network analysis of students’ self-reflective assessments
Abstract: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) increasingly position creativity as a teachable competence in innovation and entrepreneurship education, yet little is known about how Creative Metacognition (CMC) elements are structurally interconnected and activated to facilitate creativity in TVET learners. To address this gap, this study provides an exploratory epistemic network analysis on structural mapping of CMC in TVET innovation and entrepreneurship course. Forty TVET learners completed a three-stage authentic Creative Problem-Solving task focused on venture design for a remote region. Their self-reflective assessments were segmented into 1,506 theory-driven semantic fragments and coded into Creative Strengths (CS), Creative Restrictions (CR), and Creative Contextual Knowledge (CK). Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) was employed to model the co-activation patterns and relational intensity among CMC elements. Results show that students with high scores exhibited a stronger connection between CS and CK, suggesting that contextual knowledge was framed as creative affordances. In contrast, low-scoring students demonstrated a stronger connection between CR and CK, suggesting that situational reasoning was more often associated with perceived barriers and may reflect constrained idea development despite contextual awareness. The study also provides evidence of associations between reflective CMC configurations and creative performance, offering implications for reflective scaffolding and TVET entrepreneurship task design. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Synergistic strength-ductility in wire arc additive manufacturing of Al-Cu-Mg alloys via Sc microalloying and in-situ multi-scale precipitation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) of high-strength 2xxx series Al-Cu-Mg alloys is severely restricted by the intrinsic strength-ductility trade-off, severe mechanical anisotropy, and inadequate microstructure control under non-equilibrium solidification. This work addressed these challenges by developing a novel Sc microalloyed 2024 Al alloy wire and systematically investigating its microstructural evolution and mechanical properties in both as-deposited (AD) and T6-treated conditions. The results indicated that the non-equilibrium solidification during WAAM induced the in-situ transformation of primary Al3Sc into the highly stable Al8Cu4Sc (W-phase) at grain boundaries. The introduction of Sc and Mn synergistically mitigated the conventional bimodal grain structure by inhibiting interlayer recrystallization, reducing the microstructural anisotropy to 9.1%. Following T6 treatment, the intergranular T-phase (Al20Cu2Mn3) networks were largely dissolved and reprecipitated as nanoscale rod-like intragranular T-phase, while the coarse W-phase remained thermally stable at the boundaries. This cross-scale hierarchical microstructure enables a remarkable synergy of strength and ductility. The ultimate tensile strength and yield strength reached 453.0 and 313.9 MPa, respectively, with an extraordinary elongation of 10.1% (a 115% increase compared to the AD conditions). Quantitative calculation indicated that Orowan strengthening from nano-scale T- and W-phases dominated the yield strength (108.2 MPa), while uniform distribution of non-shearable precipitates promoted homogeneous dislocation slip and delayed strain localization, accounting for the improved ductility. This work provides fundamental insight into Sc microalloying in high-Cu Al alloys for WAAM, and offers a facile strategy for developing high-performance additively manufactured aluminum alloys. © 2026

Authors: Bouafif Mansali M.; Bäckström T.
Title: Sequential patterns in turn durations of dynamic speech interaction
Abstract: People’s conversations follow distinct interaction patterns. We examine the role of time in these patterns by visualizing, analyzing, and identifying patterns in transitions between speakers using tools from dynamical systems theory. We map spontaneous conversational activities as paths in state space, calculate the likelihood of state transitions, and evaluate the correlation between the durations of subsequent turns. Our measurements demonstrate that the duration of consecutive turns follows a structured pattern: consecutive turns are highly correlated in length, except for pairs involving at least one short turn. These results advance descriptive knowledge of turn-taking dynamics and may help inform the design and evaluation of conversational systems. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Kazali E.; Kalliontzi E.
Title: Cognitive predictors of narrative retelling in early childhood
Abstract: This study examined the associations between inhibitory control, working memory, inductive reasoning, awareness, and children’s narrative retelling abilities in early childhood. A total of 212 children aged 4–7 years participated in the study. Executive functions were assessed through measures of verbal and visuospatial working memory and inhibitory control, inductive reasoning was assessed using a Raven-like matrix task, and awareness was assessed through perceptual and inferential awareness tasks. Narrative retelling was evaluated using a story retelling task that captured multiple aspects of narrative performance. Correlational analyses indicated moderate associations between inhibitory control, working memory, and several narrative retelling indicators. Narrative retelling performance also increased significantly with age, indicating clear developmental gains from the preschool to the early school years. Structural equation modeling further showed that inhibitory control and verbal working memory were significant predictors of the latent narrative retelling construct, whereas visuospatial working memory and inductive reasoning were not significantly associated with narrative retelling. Awareness showed small but significant associations with certain narrative retelling indicators. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Informal elder care in Malaysia: Cultural norms, motivations and family dynamics shaping adult children’s caregiving roles
Abstract: This qualitative study explores the cultural norms and motivational factors shaping adult children's involvement in informal elder care for ageing parents in Malaysia from a multidisciplinary perspective. Amid rapid population ageing, growing numbers of working adult children undertake informal caregiving responsibilities while balancing employment and family commitments, often in contexts of limited formal support. Within this setting, caregiving arrangements are largely negotiated within families and shaped by deeply embedded social expectations and moral obligations. Drawing on in-depth interviews with thirteen working adult children from middle- to high-income households, the study examines the motivations underpinning caregiving roles as well as the family dynamics and challenges encountered. Thematic analysis identified nine interrelated factors influencing the assumption of caregiving responsibilities: (1) rejection of institutional care, (2) siblings' inability or unwillingness to provide care, (3) a sense of responsibility and perceived capability, (4) parental selection, (5) caregiving as a natural family role transition, (6) religious motivation, (7) caregiving as an opportunity, (8) personal choice, and (9) intergenerational role modelling. Beyond motivational drivers, participants' narratives reveal the emotional, cultural and moral complexities of informal elder care within a collectivist social context, shaped by familial expectations, religious values and caregiving norms. The findings highlight the need for integrated support systems and responsive social policies to reduce caregiver burden and enhance quality of life among working caregivers. By conceptualising informal elder care as a culturally embedded and multidimensional family practice, this study offers insights relevant to counselling, public health, social policy and family studies, while contributing to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3: Good Health and Well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Wu Z.; Chu X.; Cao S.; Chen H.; Zhang A.; Yu B.; Zeng J.
Title: A framework for transmission line ice thickness prediction integrating physics-informed feature engineering, attention networks, and causal inference
Abstract: Accurate prediction of ice thickness on transmission lines is essential for effective anti-icing and de-icing strategies. Existing methods predominantly rely on "black-box" models lacking physical interpretability, and correlation analysis alone cannot distinguish direct causal effects from mediated transmission among meteorological factors. This paper proposes a three-layer progressive analytical framework for high-altitude heavy-icing sites that integrates physics-informed feature engineering, an attention-based prediction network, and causal inference, progressively addressing prediction accuracy, feature-level interpretability, and causal mechanism discovery. A key finding is the synergistic effect between physics-informed feature engineering and the attention mechanism—neither component alone improves prediction accuracy, yet their combination yields a significant performance gain, with the proposed model achieving competitive performance among deep learning methods. Computational analysis further shows that the proposed model achieves a compact parameter count (12,321) and 40× faster inference than Random Forest, while providing interpretability. SHAP cross-model consistency analysis identifies humidity-related features as the dominant predictors across architecturally distinct models, a conclusion driven by data patterns rather than model bias. Causal inference further reveals that humidity exhibits a nonlinear inverted-U effect on ice thickness (peak at ∼82% RH), temperature serves as a necessary threshold condition, and wind speed exerts a modest direct effect (+0.21 mm/(m/s)) that is not mediated by temperature or humidity. These findings provide a scientific basis for a three-tier icing early-warning framework—temperature gating, humidity severity assessment, and wind intensification—rather than relying on temperature alone. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Kaymaz Özcanli A.
Title: Topology-aware gap analysis for national DC fast-charging networks: The case of Türkiye
Abstract: This study evaluates the functional adequacy of DC fast-charging infrastructure using a network-based framework that moves beyond station counts to assess corridor continuity, traffic demand, and targeted expansion strategies. A graph representation of the national intercity highway system integrates public DC fast-charging stations as network seed nodes, and accessibility is quantified through multi-source shortest-path analysis. Minimum Viable Coverage (MVC) criterion and traffic-weighted metrics are used to reflect heterogeneous mobility demand across provinces. The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity, highlighting a disconnect between nominal infrastructure availability and functional long-distance mobility. Inequality analysis shows that the top ten provinces account for approximately 72.8% of national traffic-weighted accessibility, while the bottom 40% contribute only about 2.2%. Sensitivity analysis across inter-charger distance thresholds indicates diminishing marginal gains beyond moderate spacing levels. A gap-based DC expansion scenario further demonstrates that a limited number of strategically placed stations can substantially restore consecutive coverage along previously disconnected highway corridors, yielding relative MVC improvements of up to 62% in structurally underserved provinces. At the national level, the targeted deployment raises primary-corridor MVC from 86.72% to 91.22%, recovering approximately 3,400 km of previously disconnected roadway. Overall, the proposed framework provides a transferable planning tool for improving corridor continuity, supporting targeted charging-infrastructure deployment, and informing the integration of growing EV charging demand into power-system investment decisions in emerging EV markets. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Voltage fluctuation source localization in distribution systems using a signature-based approach with minimal monitoring points
Abstract: Reducing or eliminating voltage fluctuations, a key power quality issue that causes many problems such as flicker, hinges on accurately identifying their sources. The complexity of distribution systems adds further challenges to this task. On the other hand, there is a limitation in providing power quality measurement devices (PQMDs) compared to the number of buses in these systems. Therefore, this paper introduces a simulation-based approach for pinpointing voltage fluctuation sources (VFSs) in distribution systems, specifically for frequencies up to three times the network frequency, using a limited number of PQMDs. The proposed method simulates potential VFS locations and applies a trial-and-error approach, comparing a defined signature from the simulated system with that of the real system to find the closest match to the observed network behavior. Additionally, this method employs a novel carrier signal estimation technique for demodulation and a pulse-wave approximation method for decomposition of rectangular amplitude modulation. To validate the method, simulations were performed under various scenarios on the 15-bus system, the IEEE 33-bus standard test system, and the 70-bus test system. The simulation results demonstrate 99.4%, 97.8%, and 99.5% accuracy in identifying the VFS location in the 15-bus, 33-bus, and 70-bus test systems, respectively, while using only 3, 4, and 14 PQMDs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: DensePSA: Robust image watermarking framework with cross-scale dense structure and patch-wise self-attention mechanism
Abstract: While recent architectural advances in image watermarking have yielded notable performance improvements, they often introduce substantial model complexity and computational overhead, thereby impeding real-world deployment. To address this trade-off, we propose a robust yet lightweight image watermarking framework that integrates cross-scale dense connection with a self-attention mechanism. Specifically, we design a multi-scale dense-connected encoder/decoder architecture that systematically reuses intermediate features across resolutions, enhancing both feature utilization and representational capacity for reliable watermark embedding and extraction. Complementing this design, we incorporate a Patch-wise Self-Attention (PSA) module between convolutional stages. By partitioning high-resolution feature maps into non-overlapping patches and applying an adaptive re-weighting strategy, PSA effectively captures global dependencies with reduced computational cost. This patch-based design preserves global contextual information without incurring the prohibitive complexity associated with conventional attention models on large tensors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both imperceptibility and robustness against common signal-processing attacks, all while supporting real-time inference. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Hakki A.
Title: The reality of Dubai's property price index and a look at the foreseeable future; [تحلیل شاخص قیمت املاک دبی و پیشبینی آیندة آن]
Abstract: The real estate market serves as an important indicator of economic health, reflecting the complex interaction of numerous factors. The study provides a detailed assessment of the real estate sector in the United Arab Emirates, with a particular focus on the Dubai market. Using price data from 2012 to 2024 compared to a base index of 1.00 (equivalent to AED 934,524 for apartments and AED 1,646,567 for villas), the results show a steady upward trend in value. This growth will peak in 2024, when the index will reach 1.58 for apartments and 1.43 for villas. The study uses the Orange-ARIMA forecasting model, according to which the period of market stability will continue until 2028. At this stage, a slight correction is expected, with the forecast indices stabilizing at 1.57 for apartments and 1.37 for villas. As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, the apartment price index fell to a low of 0.99 in the second quarter of 2021, while the villa price index reached its lowest point in the first quarter of 2020, recording 0.99. The research confirms that the Dubai real estate market has remarkable resilience and great potential for sustainable growth. This stability is underpinned by solid economic fundamentals and a predictable political environment. Key drivers include the increasing adoption of advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, which enhances operational efficiency and market transparency. All these factors together reinforce Dubai's unique and leading position as a safe and advanced investment center in the region. © 2026, University of Tehran. All rights reserved.

Authors: Todkar A.; Dhodiya J.
Title: A solution approach for sustainable uncertain multi-objective 5D shortest path problem involving fixed-charge: Application to fish transport system
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Sustainability encompasses the interplay between environmental, economic, and social systems at multiple levels. Vehicles rely on various fuels to meet their energy needs in transportation systems. However, these fuels emit greenhouse gases, leading to environmental pollution. Considering this context, this study investigates a sustainable fixed-charge multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problem. The main goal is to identify the most efficient route that minimizes costs, time, risk, carbon emissions, and distance for travel between sources and destinations. In practical scenarios, the parameters of fixed-charge multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problems often involve uncertainties, which can be anticipated based on human judgment. Liu's uncertainty theory is widely accepted as a legitimate tool for handling such uncertainties. Therefore, zigzag uncertain variables are incorporated into the proposed model to represent uncertain parameters. The study develops the expected and optimistic value models of the fixed-charge uncertain multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problem and provides their corresponding deterministic transformations. Moreover, two multi-objective genetic algorithms namely, aspiration level - based non-dominated sorting genetic algorithms -II and III are used to address the deterministic model. An application of the proposed model is demonstrated through a fish transport system problem. A comparison of the compromise solutions obtained from the mentioned techniques is presented with hybrid genetic algorithm, non-dominated sorting genetic algorithms-II, and III, along with a sensitivity analysis of the objective functions concerning the shape parameter and aspiration level. Finally, the coverage performance measure is calculated to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: PG-DCA: prototype-guided knowledge transfer for imbalanced and heterogeneous data collaboration
Abstract: Collaborative analysis of distributed data requires fusing information from multiple sources whose raw data cannot be centralized, whose label distributions may be highly skewed, and whose local feature mappings may be incompatible. Data Collaboration Analysis (DCA) can align heterogeneous client representations after local dimensionality reduction, but traditional DCA relies on anchors that often lack task-specific semantic structure and are used only after biased local mappings have already discarded important discriminative components. This paper formulates this limitation as Non-IID component loss and proposes Prototype-Guided Data Collaboration Analysis (PG-DCA), a heterogeneity-robust framework based on prototype-guided knowledge transfer. PG-DCA constructs a task-relevant reference by extracting class-level knowledge from client-side statistics, translating it into the observation space, and rebalancing it without moving raw client data. Crucially, this reference is used as a knowledge carrier to guide local mapping before DCA alignment begins. A local-first guidance interface incorporates prototype knowledge into each client’s mapping while retaining the native objective of its chosen structured linear algorithm. The guided representations are then aligned in a common collaborative space to support server-side model training. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 under severe statistical and algorithmic heterogeneity show that PG-DCA reduces component loss and improves collaborative utility, with gains driven by prototype-mediated reference quality and guidance of local mapping. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Sun D.; Mi X.; Hong J.
Title: From diagnosis to explanation: An integrated framework for examining spatially heterogeneous associations between temporary industrial-land use and neighborhood gentrification
Abstract: As Chinese megacities transition to post-industrialism, the socio-spatial consequences of temporary industrial land reuse—a pivotal urban renewal strategy—remain under-theorized. This study integrates Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR), Geodetector, and Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) to examine associations between four functional types of temporary use and a Standardized Gentrification Index (SGI) capturing changes in educational and floating-population composition across 134 Beijing subdistricts. The results reveal differentiated and context-dependent patterns. Technology-oriented use density exhibits a stable and spatially widespread positive association with SGI. Cultural-use area is positively associated with SGI across most subdistricts, whereas cultural-use density is predominantly negative. Production-service area is significant only in a limited set of locations, while consumer-service measures show no statistically significant local MGWR coefficients. Cultural and technology clustering recur as the principal correlates of coefficient heterogeneity, whereas production clustering, transport-accessibility growth, and housing-price change matter in specific relationships. These findings suggest a state-mediated, technology-oriented pathway of demographic upgrading and a more conditional cultural pathway. Methodologically, the framework moves from mapping spatial non-stationarity to interpreting its contextual correlates, providing evidence for differentiated urban-renewal governance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Foraging Theory and the Colonization of Unfamiliar Landscapes: Assessing Late Pleistocene Projectile Point Reduction Strategies
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: How humans perceive risk has long been of interest to the social sciences. The colonization of unfamiliar landscapes by Late Pleistocene hunter-gatherers is a valuable case study that required novel strategies of risk management, technological organization, and ecological knowledge acquisition. Here, we apply evolutionary theory to projectile point reduction in the Tennessee River Valley to model utility thresholds and assess resharpening versus replacement decisions. We evaluate attributes of Clovis and Cumberland points to quantify artifact use-lives and curation intensity using a dataset drawn from the Paleoindian Database of the Americas. Results indicate that Clovis groups practiced a more conservative lithic resource management strategy by resharpening points further to extract greater utility. By contrast, subsequent Cumberland groups more frequently discarded points with variable amounts of utility remaining, suggesting reduced emphasis on resource conservation. We interpret this difference as reflecting the resolution of landscape knowledge barriers. Clovis groups confronted higher search costs in raw material acquisition, whereas Cumberland groups inherited generational knowledge of local lithic resources and became more familiar with known resource distributions. More broadly, our study demonstrates that lithic artifacts, when modeled as patches of utility, provide archaeologists with rare opportunities to test predictions of optimal foraging theory and risk management. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Sithole S.T.M.
Title: Embedding ESG, sustainability and ethics in accounting assessment: Bridging global standards and educational practice
Abstract: The growing prominence of environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, sustainability, and ethical accountability is reshaping expectations of accounting and management graduates. While these competencies are increasingly embedded within global professional standards and competency frameworks, their translation into educational assessment remains underexplored. This study examines how ESG, sustainability, and ethics are embedded in documented assessment across global standards, professional competency frameworks, and Australian university accounting education. Using qualitative comparative document analysis, the study analyses the International Federation of Accountants’ International Education Standards, the competency frameworks of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, and assessment documentation from 104 undergraduate accounting units across 26 Australian universities. The findings reveal partial and uneven alignment. Although sustainability and ethics are explicitly articulated within global and professional frameworks, they are frequently embedded implicitly within technically oriented assessment tasks rather than explicitly assessed as judgement-focused competencies. To explain this pattern, the study introduces the concept of differential assessability, which explains why some professional competencies are more readily translated into assessment than others despite comparable prominence within professional standards. By reframing ESG integration as an assessment design challenge, the study extends assessment theory and offers practical implications for responsible management and accounting education. © 2026

Authors: Hruby J.
Title: Designing ethical negotiation simulations for measurable metacognitive development: Boundary conditions in SCELM
Abstract: Ethical negotiation simulations generate strong engagement but often fail to produce measurable metacognitive development in students. This boundary condition design study argues that the problem is structural: many simulation formats are misaligned with the consolidation phase through which disruption becomes learning. We evaluated two implementations of Structured Cross-Cultural Ethical Leadership through Multilateral Negotiations (SCELM): a multicultural rotating format (N = 84 responses; matched n = 26) and a bilateral intercultural format (N = 39; Battle 1 n = 30) across four high-institutional-distance dyads in this study. Paired t-tests and thematic analyses of 124 reflections (κ = 0.81) were conducted in parallel. The rotating format produced no significant within-person changes across any metacognitive index (all d ≤ 0.17). In contrast, the bilateral format generated greater baseline assumption disruption, as indicated by a significant Welch's t-test (p = .028) and marginally higher role tension (p = .063). Qualitative findings showed that perspective revision occurred primarily during structured intra-team consolidation rather than during negotiations, indicating that immediate post-battle surveys underestimate learning. We propose four educator-facing design principles and a dual-timepoint Assurance of Learning protocol, recommending that perspective-shift outcomes be assessed after structured consolidation rather than immediately following negotiation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Ding H.; Dai C.; Zhou H.; Wu Y.; Ma W.
Title: HAPO: Hierarchical affinity aware propagation for unsupervised graph anomaly detection
Abstract: Graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to identify nodes that deviate from normal structural or semantic patterns and is critical in security-sensitive applications. Existing unsupervised anomaly detection methods based on anomaly scoring are largely grounded in the local homophily assumption and are limited by feature smoothing to aggregating one-hop neighborhoods. Consequently, they lack a global perspective for detecting globally anomalous nodes and tend to misclassify structurally peripheral yet normal nodes as anomalies. Moreover, most existing approaches are not readily applicable to multi-view settings, limiting their effectiveness in graphs with heterogeneous relational semantics. To address these challenges, we propose Hierarchical Affinity-Aware Propagation (HAPO), a unified framework for single-view and multi-view GAD. HAPO combines multi-hop affinity-aware propagation with affinity-guided residual connections to enlarge the receptive field while mitigating over-smoothing, and a multi-classifier hierarchical affinity module to construct robust global affinity representations. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. In particular, HAPO outperforms state-of-the-art methods by more than 10.11% on the single-view Amazon dataset and 9.69% on the multi-view IMDB dataset in terms of AUPRC. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zarezadeh Z.; Gretzel U.
Title: From influence to empowerment: Unpacking capacity building and social learning in virtual communities
Abstract: This study explores how independent travel empowers women travel influencers and how meanings of empowerment are negotiated through interactions with their followers by examining the empowerment process at both individual and social levels. Drawing on capacity building theory and social cognitive theory, it investigates how travel experiences and digital content creation contribute to personal agency, skill development, and socially mediated expressions of empowerment. Using an interpretive paradigm and a netnographic approach, the study analyses the social media practices of 17 female travel influencers. Authors: Continelli E.; Haskovec J.; Pignotti C.
Title: Consensus and flocking with transmission and reaction delays
Abstract: We investigate consensus formation and flocking behavior in multi-agent systems subject to two distinct types of delay: a transmission delay accounting for information exchange between agents, and a reaction delay representing the processing time before agents adjust their states. For a simplified linear two-agent system, we analyze how these delays affect asymptotic stability. We then derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic consensus and flocking in the general multi-agent setting with a nonlinear, globally positive influence function. These conditions require the delays to be sufficiently small relative to the initial data and the decay rate of the influence function. The analysis is based on a Lyapunov functional approach combined with a Grönwall–Halanay-type inequality. Our results establish rigorous sufficient conditions under which collective behavior emerges in delayed multi-agent systems where both communication and reaction lags are non-negligible, with applications to biological, social, and engineered systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Agag G.
Title: Generative AI communications and firm value: Evidence from digital innovation in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms using deep learning
Abstract: This study examines whether firm-initiated generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) communications are associated with firm value in UK-listed tourism, travel, and hospitality (TTH) firms. The final sample includes 177 firms from 2018 to 2024, comprising 68 firms with verified WeChat official accounts and 109 firms retained with zero-valued communication measures. From 105,429 archived posts, we develop a bilingual annotation scheme and supervised deep-learning classifiers to identify GenAI communication and distinguish implementation-salient disclosures from generic mentions. Our preferred measures are share-normalized, capturing both GenAI communication intensity and implementation emphasis relative to total posting activity. Firm- and year-fixed-effects results show that implementation-weighted GenAI communication is positively associated with Tobin's Q and operating performance. Digital innovation partially mediates this relationship, while industry dynamism and complexity strengthen it, but munificence does not. The study contributes a tourism-specific measure of GenAI capability signaling and clarifies the value relevance of implementation-oriented communication in service-intensive digital contexts. © 2026 The Author.

Title: Assessing salinity intrusion risk from coastal flooding through a spatial multi-criteria approach in Satkhira district of Bangladesh
Abstract: Bangladesh's coastal zones face compounding threats from climate change, sea-level rise, and the resulting intensification of salinity intrusion, critically jeopardizing freshwater security, agriculture, and local livelihoods. This study presents a spatial multi-criteria analysis using a Geographic Information System (GIS) integrated with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to systematically assess and map the hazard, vulnerability, and exposure dimensions driving flood-induced salinity intrusion risk in Satkhira District. The comprehensive assessment utilized 17 thematic criteria, revealing distinct spatial patterns of susceptibility. The Hazard analysis demonstrated that 35.21% of the total area is classified under the combined High and Very High zones, predominantly concentrated in the south-western and south-eastern coastal areas. The biophysical vulnerability assessment indicated a high degree of intrinsic sensitivity, with 36.59% of the district categorized as very highly vulnerable. Conversely, the Exposure analysis identified a substantial 28.19% of the land as highly and very highly exposed, reflecting the high density of valuable assets even in inland Upazilas. The final composite risk map reveals that 27.95% of the study area is subjected to either high or very high salinity intrusion risk, with the highest risk observed in Satkhira sadar. These empirically derived risk maps and quantitative findings offer crucial, evidence-based insights for policymakers, providing a foundational tool for the design and implementation of targeted adaptation strategies, sustainable land-use planning, and disaster risk reduction programs in vulnerable deltaic environments globally. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Comparative assessment of distribution network robustness against wind and solar uncertainties using information gap decision theory
Abstract: To address the challenges posed by source‑load multiple uncertainties to the stable operation of power systems, this paper explores adaptive control strategies for energy storage system (ESS) and investigates differences in system sensitivity to uncertainties in wind and solar power generation. Based on Information Gap Decision Theory (IGDT) for uncertainty quantification, a three-layer robust optimization model is formulated to maximize the uncertainty radius under a predefined power loss target. By incorporating the worst condition defined as minimized power generation coupled with maximized load, the original three-layer model is converted into a two-layer model for efficient solution. Furthermore, the Reference Vector Guided Evolutionary Algorithm (RVEA) is employed to solve the model, obtaining a Pareto solution set that reflects the trade‑off between robustness and economy. Simulations based on the IEEE 33‑bus system demonstrate that ESS forms differentiated charging and discharging strategies for different operating scenarios, and the system exhibits higher sensitivity to wind power fluctuations. Authors: Meng X.; Lin J.
Title: AWCRL: Adaptive Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Reliability Learning for resource-constrained proxy-state recognition
Abstract: Multimodal pattern recognition can support the characterization of affective and behavioral states by integrating complementary visual and physiological evidence, but real-world deployment is challenged by unreliable modalities, limited annotations, and constrained computation. We propose Adaptive Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Reliability Learning (AWCRL), a resource-aware framework for recognizing ontology-derived affective proxy states under incomplete or unreliable multimodal evidence. AWCRL estimates modality reliability from unimodal predictions and a lightweight pre-routing pooled consensus, then uses a budget-conditioned router to retain informative tokens before low-rank cross-modal fusion. An explicit weak ontology maps affective and engagement-related cues to four ordinal proxy states — stable, disengaged, cognitive overload, and acute stress — while confidence- and affinity-weighted prototype refinement reduces the influence of uncertain weak labels. Under subject-independent five-fold evaluation on K-EmoCon and AMIGOS, AWCRL achieves 78.6% and 76.2% macro-F1 with mean computation of 0.78 and 0.82 GFLOPs per segment, respectively. Compared with full-token inference at 1.95 GFLOPs, the budgeted setting reduces computation by 60.0% and 57.9%, with macro-F1 decreasing by only 0.8 and 0.7 percentage points. On K-EmoCon, AWCRL also achieves the highest descriptive macro-F1 among the compared methods under complete, missing-modality, and single-modality corruption conditions. These results indicate a favorable recognition–efficiency trade-off under weak supervision and variable multimodal evidence. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Almatar K.M.
Title: Modeling the historical relationship between waterfront development and transport infrastructure: Evidence from Jeddah’s coastal transformation
Abstract: The redevelopment of waterfronts is increasingly perceived as a transport-mediated spatial process as opposed to a design or land-use process. Nevertheless, limited information exists on the impacts of transportation infrastructure on waterfront integration over time, nonlinear dynamics and temporal lag effects, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. This paper examines the history of the relationship between the evolution of transport infrastructure and waterfront spatial integration along the Jeddah coastline in a longitudinal, GIS-based study. The analysis combines network accessibility, pedestrian permeability, land-use intensity gradients, and a composite Waterfront Mobility Integration Index (WMII) across three historical development phases. Normalized indicator trajectories, sensitivity tests, and counterfactual situations are used to analyze the concepts of threshold behavior and time lag. It has been found that accessibility to transport grows more rapidly than other spatial dimensions, and that substantial growth in pedestrian permeability and the continuity of public space is achieved only after accessibility becomes critical, with a time lag. The findings reveal that accessibility is sufficient, though not necessary in waterfront integration, and that pedestrian infrastructure is the mediating variable in the transformation of transport investment into continuous, publicly accessible waterfront environments. The research adds to the transport-waterfront literature by offering a replicable analytical framework on evaluating waterfront change in fast growing coastal metropolitan areas and providing longitudinal evidence of threshold effects and lagged spatial response. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wang J.
Title: Digital Literacy of English Language Teachers in EFL Contexts: The Necessity of Teachers’ Development in the Digital World
Abstract: Digital technologies have significantly reshaped the landscape of language education, influencing both pedagogical practices and teacher professional development. This review article investigates the role of English language teachers’ digital literacy in enhancing teaching efficiency by synthesizing findings from recent empirical and theoretical studies. Drawing on a comprehensive analysis of peer-reviewed journal articles, books, and academic reports published over the past decade, the review explores how digital competence contributes to instructional effectiveness, classroom engagement, and ongoing teacher growth. The literature was systematically selected based on relevance, publication quality, and thematic focus on digital literacy and language education. The synthesis reveals that teachers with higher digital literacy are better equipped to integrate educational technologies, adapt to dynamic learning environments, and foster more interactive and learner-centered classrooms. Authors: Sun L.; Yang Q.; Yu H.; Zheng Y.; Akhtar N.
Title: EgoMamba: Fusing hand-guided spatial cues and multi-scale temporal context for efficient egocentric action recognition
Abstract: Egocentric action recognition requires modeling hand-object interaction regions and their temporal evolution while maintaining high computational efficiency. Existing methods are mainly based on CNNs or Transformers. CNN-based methods are limited in long-range dependency modeling, whereas Transformer-based methods often incur high computational and memory costs. Recent state space models such as Mamba offer an efficient alternative for sequence modeling, but directly applying them to video understanding remains insufficient for capturing action-critical spatial interactions and non-strictly causal temporal context in egocentric scenes. To address these limitations, we propose EgoMamba, an efficient spatiotemporal modeling framework for egocentric action recognition. EgoMamba adopts a spatiotemporally decoupled architecture and introduces lightweight enhancement branches in both the spatial and temporal stages. In the spatial stage, a hand-guided global and local spatial reweighting module highlights core hand-object interaction regions. In the temporal stage, a multi-scale temporal context convolution branch supplements short-, medium-, and long-range temporal cues. We further incorporate a semantic-prior-guided masked pretraining strategy to improve representation learning for key egocentric regions. Experiments on Something-Something V2 and EPIC-KITCHENS-100 show that EgoMamba achieves a favorable trade-off between recognition accuracy and computational efficiency, outperforming various CNN-based, Transformer-based, and existing Mamba-based methods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
