Authors: Li J.; Ge S.S.; Ji R.; Xu K.
Title: Singularity avoidance control of independently steerable and driven mobile robots
Abstract: This paper develops a coordinated singularity avoidance control framework for independently steerable and driven mobile robots by jointly regulating steering geometry and control allocation. A unified model is established by combining the common instantaneous-center-of-rotation consistency constraint with planar rigid-body dynamics, thereby relating steering configuration, chassis motion, and wheel actuation within a common formulation. In the steering layer, a manipulability-gradient correction is combined with a boundary-localized safeguarding mechanism. Positive invariance of a prescribed safe steering set is established under explicit initialization and guard-region regularity conditions, providing a sufficient condition for operational singularity avoidance under the nominal steering dynamics. In the chassis layer, an adaptive disturbance-compensating controller is integrated with a manipulability-dependent damped least-squares allocator. The resulting allocation mismatch is retained in the closed-loop dynamics, and uniform ultimate boundedness of the chassis tracking errors is established under a bounded total disturbance. Numerical studies on representative four-wheel and six-wheel configurations show that the proposed method preserves a positive manipulability margin and substantially limits singularity-induced actuator amplification while allowing a finite transient deviation from nominal geometric consistency. Under actuator, steering-rate, sensing, and steering-lag nonidealities, the four-wheel configuration maintains a minimum scaled manipulability of 0.1705 with a peak commanded wheel torque of 3.818 Nm, while the six-wheel configuration maintains a minimum value of 0.6326 with a peak commanded torque of 4.339 Nm. A gain-sensitivity study further quantifies the trade-off between manipulability preservation and geometric consistency. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Segura-Duque V.; Griffin L.
Title: Hand clearances in ergonomic design: A scoping review of types, methods, and measurements
Abstract: Hand clearances, the space available for hand access and operation, are essential for manual workspace design. However, clearance types lack systematic characterization, unified methods, and standardized criteria for defining adequate space during manual tasks. This scoping review analyzed 26 records published between 1960 and 2026. Ninety-four unique clearances were identified and organized into four categories: Openings, Operational Clearances, Object-Specific Clearances, and PPE Allowances. Four methodological approaches and eight methodological gaps were identified, including reliance on static measurements, inadequate treatment of PPE, small or outdated samples, and limited reporting standards. Widely cited clearance values originate from small, demographically narrow 1960s studies and have propagated with limited re-validation. The review introduces the functional clearance margin as a conceptual proposition describing the additional space beyond hand dimensions required for functional operation rather than fit alone. These findings provide a foundation for developing more representative, dynamic, and standardized approaches to hand clearance design. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Modeling the propagation of risk in large-scale power outages: Integrating ETA, directed-weighted CN, and risk chain mining
Abstract: To understand the systemic propagation and interdependencies of various risk factors in large-scale power outages, a novel risk evolution framework is proposed, incorporating Event Tree Analysis (ETA), directed-weighted Complex Network (CN), and risk chain mining. A network comprising 37 nodes and 130 edges is constructed using data from 29 large-scale power outages spanning from 1965 to 2025. Topological analysis identifies critical propagation nodes, including power plant failures and grid instability. Robustness tests reveal the network's resilience to random disruptions but also expose its vulnerability to targeted attacks. Furthermore, high-risk causal chains are directly extracted and classified from the network, and path mining further uncovers 24 high-risk six-node chains, which are categorized into four distinct propagation patterns. This integrated framework offers a data-driven methodology for characterizing large-scale power outage risks, yielding structurally suggestive priorities to inform prevention and mitigation strategies for power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Hapipi; Stylianides A.J.
Title: Students’ engagement with statements and their understanding of corresponding proofs by contradiction and contraposition
Abstract: Engagement has been shown to influence students’ understanding and achievement, yet little is known about how engagement with statements relates to students’ understanding of corresponding proofs. In this paper, we take a step towards addressing this gap by investigating whether engaging with statements is associated with better understanding of proofs by contradiction and contraposition. Eighty-seven Indonesian undergraduate mathematics education students, organized in four groups, participated in the study. Two groups (n = 43) were randomly selected to first engage with the statements—reflecting on their meaning, judging their truth, and attempting to prove or disprove them—before responding to an instrument designed to measure their understanding of given proofs for the same statements; the other two groups (n = 44) proceeded directly to the instrument. There were six statements overall, three proved by contradiction and three by contraposition. We found that students who engaged with the statements achieved significantly higher mean scores on measures of proof understanding than those who did not, with a medium effect size. Regression analyses confirmed engagement as a significant predictor of students’ understanding for both proof methods, and individual semi-structured interviews with 12 participants provided qualitative support for these findings. Overall, our findings identify engagement with statements as a meaningful factor in students’ proof understanding and suggests that selectively incorporating an engagement stage before introducing key proofs may enhance undergraduate mathematics instruction beyond the typical Definition-Theorem-Proof (DTP) approach. Title: Interface-aware adaptive layer-wise physics-informed neural networks for multilayer large-strain consolidation: a benchmark of architectures, training strategies, and trade-offs
Abstract: Multilayer large-strain consolidation in stratified soils involves nonlinear pore-pressure dissipation, evolving deformation, and material discontinuities, which pose significant challenges for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). This study develops a layer-wise adaptive PINN framework in which soil layers are represented by neural subnetworks coupled through pore-pressure and Darcy-flux continuity conditions. A controlled three-layer benchmark is used to evaluate MLP and KAN architectures, adaptive activation, adaptive weighting, and parameter sharing over three independent random seeds. The framework is further extended to four- and five-layer profiles using Shared MLP, layer-wise MLP, and KAN. Results demonstrate that no single architecture is optimal across all physical responses: parameter sharing improves mean global and settlement accuracy, KAN-based models better control selected local errors, and adaptive strategies alter pressure, settlement, and interface behavior in a metric-dependent manner. The successful four- and five-layer calculations further support the applicability of the same physical formulation as the number of internal interfaces increases, although the preferred architecture changes with the layer arrangement. Overall, pore-pressure accuracy, settlement prediction, interface consistency, and computational cost involve distinct trade-offs, so model selection should reflect the target physical quantity and profile complexity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Workplace management of musculoskeletal and mental health risks: translating evidence into practice
Abstract: There is a large body of research evidence identifying the biomechanical and psychosocial hazards that can affect work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and stress-related mental health problems (MHPs). Using APHIRM survey data from three occupations in the healthcare sector, this project compared hazard ‘riskiness’ profiles: (a) at occupational versus local workgroup levels, and (b) using hazard constructs versus individual hazard items. Title: Do smiling faces change children’s minds? Testing evaluative conditioning in 3–6‑year‑olds
Abstract: This study examined whether preschoolers form preferences for shapes paired with happy or sad faces (evaluative conditioning) and whether the effect varies with age or with the number of different faces paired with each shape. Sixty-one children aged 3–6 years viewed four neutral shapes during a brief conditioning movie. Each shape was assigned to one of four conditions, in which it was paired with a single happy face, a single sad face, five different happy faces, or five different sad faces. Shape preferences were measured before and after the movie, along with memory for the pairings. Children showed clear pre-existing preferences for some shapes, and the pattern differed by age. After accounting for these starting preferences, two additive advantages emerged (for positive over negative faces and for multiple over single faces) and their combination in the shape paired with multiple smiling faces was the only condition to produce a reliable shift from zero. The other three conditions did not produce reliable change, and children’s exact age and memory for the pairings did not predict change. These findings suggest that evaluative conditioning in preschoolers is more selective than typically assumed, with the number of different faces paired with a shape emerging as a key factor. The results also highlight the importance of accounting for children’s pre-existing preferences when measuring acquired evaluative learning. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Urbanisation, gender vulnerability, and ecovocation among migrant women in prostitution
Abstract: This study examines how rapid metropolitan transformation in Jakarta produces structural vulnerability and social inequality among female migrants involved in covert sexual labour within the SPA industry. It investigates the relevance of the right to the city and an eco-vocational educational approach within Population and Environmental Education as critical frameworks for understanding exclusion, agency, and citizenship. Using a qualitative multi-sited case study design, the research draws on in-depth interviews, limited participant observation, and document analysis involving women workers, SPA managers, community actors, civil society representatives, and policymakers. The data were analysed thematically through critical urban studies and feminist perspectives. The findings show that women's involvement in covert sexual labour cannot be understood simply as an individual moral failure or fully voluntary decision. Rather, it reflects constrained agency shaped by unequal labour markets, limited educational capital, family economic responsibilities, debt relations, migration pressures, and regulatory ambiguity surrounding the SPA sector. Participants experienced layered forms of exploitation, symbolic violence, stigma, and disconnected citizenship: they contributed to the city's informal service economy but remained socially marginalised, politically unrecognised, and institutionally underprotected. Urban governance practices tended to intensify this vulnerability by emphasising surveillance, raids, and moral regulation rather than social protection, labour justice, and inclusive public policy. The study argues that the right to the city offers a useful analytical lens for revealing spatial injustice and the denial of substantive citizenship among marginalised women. It further proposes eco-vocational education as a transformative framework for restoring dignity, strengthening capabilities, expanding livelihood alternatives, and promoting more inclusive, just, and humane urban futures. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Energy transition materials, climate knowledge, and the imagined supply chain: Escaping the productive paradox of necessary mining
Abstract: Much scholarship, public discourse, and policymaking on ‘energy transition materials’ (ETMs) imagines a supply chain from material production to climate mitigation, despite the absence of any mechanism ensuring that mined materials will become an electrification technology, let alone replace fossil fuels or avoid warming impacts. Scholarship about energy transition material (ETM) discourse, including criticism, largely neglects this material-discursive contradiction and truncates final analyses to paradoxes productive toward extractive futures. Leveraging a review of 99 peer-reviewed articles published between 2013-2025, this article brings mining scholarship into conversation with climate knowledge politics. It charts the dematerialization of climate knowledge from warming impacts to values negotiated along three spectra (urgency, scale, and sacrifice) and rematerialization reflected in extractive rationales (developmental, Indigenous rights, nature, and futures). Most ETM discourse is enclosed in three narrative boundaries, which lean on the imagined supply chain and foreclose non-extractive possibilities: (1) The contingencies that link climate policy and mining, such as materials science, technological manufacturing and use, are taken for granted; (2) Scalar formulations separate and compare anthropogenic climate change and mining impacts; and (3) ETMs wield climate knowledge itself as a supply chain, dialectically illustrating a problem to its own solution. Pathways to overcome the boundaries can center the materiality of mining and climate change over the abstractions of supply chains and imagined climate benefits, critically reflect on the relationships between material production and technopolitical knowledge, and take seriously actually occurring alternative livelihoods. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wang B.; Gui B.; Zheng L.; Wang Y.; Wang L.
Title: LLM-agent-based explicit-implicit interaction fusion for human-robot collaborative Assembly
Abstract: In human-robot collaboration (HRC), explicit and implicit interactions typically follow distinct workflows: explicit interactions are actively initiated by the operator to convey task objectives, while implicit interactions are continuously perceived and responded to by the system to adapt robot behavior to the current collaboration context. Existing HRC systems often handle these interaction types separately, lacking a unified cognitive and decision-making mechanism, which can lead to interaction conflicts, execution interruptions, or delayed safety responses in complex scenarios. Although large language models (LLMs) demonstrate tremendous potential in reasoning, they have yet to effectively integrate explicit and implicit interactions into robotic decision-making. To address this, this paper proposes an LLM-Agent-based framework for explicit-implicit interaction fusion, which models both types of input within a unified semantic space and incorporates a two-stage fusion decision mechanism in LLM reasoning. This framework helps robots maintain consistent responses to task objectives and mitigate potential collaborative safety risks. Preliminary small-scale experimental results on representative HRC tasks reveal favorable trends in task completion ratio, collaborative safety performance and decision consistency when compared with the baseline scheme without explicit-implicit fusion. The proposed method provides an interpretable and scalable approach for deploying LLM-based HRC systems in real-world settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Presidential Involvement in Legislative Processes in Indonesia: Constitutional Distinctiveness or Structural Anomaly Within a Presidential System?; [La participación presidencial en los procesos legislativos en Indonesia: ¿una particularidad constitucional o una anomalía estructural dentro de un sistema presidencialista?]
Abstract: The lawmaking process in Indonesia, as defined by the 1945 Constitution, features extensive presidential involvement in proposing bills, participating in deliberations, and enacting laws. This departs from most presidential systems, where the executive's role in lawmaking is more limited. This article examines whether Indonesia's model is a distinctive constitutional innovation or an anomaly that strains the separation of powers. Employing a normative legal methodology, it analyses constitutional provisions, implementing statutes, and comparative studies of presidential systems in the United States, South Africa, and Colombia. The analysis shows that Indonesia's model institutionalises intensive executive-legislative cooperation but also generates legal ambiguities, especially in agendasetting, budget formation, veto practice, and emergency legislation. These procedural uncertainties risk governance instability and blur classical boundaries between branches. The article argues that Indonesia represents a "colegislative presidency" that both departs from orthodox presidentialism and enriches comparative typologies of executive-legislative relations. Title: The Effect of Mindful Teaching on Job Satisfaction among L2 Instructors: Examining the Mediating Role of Teacher Self-Efficacy
Abstract: Teacher well-being has become an important concern in higher education due to increasing levels of occupational stress, burnout, and attrition, which may negatively affect instructional quality and student learning outcomes. These challenges are particularly evident in English as a foreign language teaching, where instructors frequently manage intensive workloads, diverse learner needs, and substantial emotional demands. Although previous research has linked mindfulness and self-efficacy to positive teacher outcomes, limited attention has been given to the psychological mechanisms through which mindful teaching contributes to job satisfaction in EFL contexts. Addressing this gap, the present study examined the direct effect of mindful teaching on job satisfaction and investigated the mediating role of teacher self-efficacy in this relationship. The participants consisted of 321 EFL instructors working in English-language preparatory programs in higher education in Türkiye. Data were collected using the Mindfulness in Teaching Scale, the Teacher Self-Efficacy Scale, and the Job Satisfaction Index. The findings revealed a statistically significant positive relationship between mindful teaching and job satisfaction. Teacher self-efficacy was also found to partially mediate this relationship, indicating that mindful teaching contributes to job satisfaction both directly and indirectly through stronger efficacy beliefs. These findings identify self-efficacy as an important psychological mechanism underlying the relationship between mindful teaching and job satisfaction. The study extends current understanding of teacher well-being in EFL higher education by providing empirical support for a mediation model linking mindful teaching, self-efficacy, and job satisfaction. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Fear of psychosis in an OCD analogue sample: Prevalence and associated factors
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) includes heterogeneous presentations, despite the disproportionate research and clinical attention on contamination and symmetry symptoms. Colloquially coined “schizophrenia OCD”, obsessional fears of having or developing a psychotic disorder (or “going crazy”) and associated compulsions have received growing recognition within psychoeducational contexts and patient communities. This preliminary study examined the prevalence and associated factors of fears of psychosis among a university student sample (N = 154). Participants completed an online questionnaire that included symptom checklists assessing psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thoughts and compulsive behaviours, alongside a series of validated measures. Fears of psychosis were commonly endorsed: 77.9% endorsed lifetime unwanted intrusive thoughts, 70.1% endorsed associated compulsive behaviours, and 83.1% reported at least one psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thought or compulsive behaviour. Fears of losing control of your thoughts or actions was the most frequently endorsed intrusive thought (50.6%), whereas fear of developing a psychotic illness (18.3%) was rated most distressing. The most frequently endorsed compulsive behavior was replacing “bad thoughts” with better thoughts (53.2%). Supporting our hypothesis, individuals meeting OCD symptom cut-offs were more likely to endorse psychosis-related fears. Finally, hierarchical regression analyses indicated that health anxiety and negative beliefs about losing control predicted psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thoughts, over and above demographic factors, OCD severity, or other clinically relevant variables. Findings underscore the need for recognition of fears of mental health issues in individuals with OCD and suggest that interventions targeting health anxiety and perceptions of loss of control may be particularly relevant. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Numerical approximation in discrete portfolio optimization using DeFi as a new asset frontier: Risk contribution and correlation dynamics in a minimum-risk portfolio
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The introduction of decentralized finance (DeFi) as an innovative asset class necessitates a reevaluation of the conventional framework for portfolio optimization. Traditional continuous-time models are challenged by the complex and non-linear features of DeFi tokens, such as discontinuous trading, high volatility, heteroskedasticity, and regime-switching behavior. The use of numerical approximation is examined in this article, optimizing portfolios with discrete techniques, including DeFi assets in a framework with low risk. We use and compare several optimization techniques, such as mean variance, Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) and a number of Risk Parity (RP) strategies are at the core of our analysis. We used a dataset of ten well-known DeFi tokens for our empirical investigation. DeFi tokens from 2021 to 2024 show a fundamental trade-off. Concentration-based models (mean-variance and CVaR) generate highly concentrated weights portfolios, leading to extreme volatility, large drawdowns, and prohibitively high portfolio turnover, which would be severely affected by real DeFi transaction fees, such as gas fees. In contrast, Risk Parity models consistently demonstrate superior practical performance. They produce well-diversified portfolios that deliver smoother results and significantly lower compound return paths and more stable rolling volatility and drastically reduced turnover. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Impact of Livelihood Capital on Farmers’ Adoption of Sustainable Crop Residue Management Practices: Empirical Evidence from Punjab Province, Pakistan
Abstract: Sustainable crop residue management can increase agricultural productivity and reduce farming-related carbon emissions, yet adoption of sustainable crop residue management practices (SCRMPs) remains limited. This study investigates how farmers’ livelihood capital shapes SCRMP adoption in Punjab, Pakistan, using survey data from 500 farmers in three agro-ecological zones. A multivariate probit model, weighted with the entropy-TOPSIS method, estimates the effects of human, social, natural, physical, and financial capital on practices including on-farm use, livestock feed, residue retention, and biogas production. Human, social, financial, and physical capital positively influence on-farm residue use, while all five forms of capital significantly promote biogas production. Although livestock feed remains the most common use, many farmers are willing to adopt alternatives such as biofertilizer production and biogas. These findings indicate substantial potential to expand sustainable residue management in the region. Title: Balancing the mechanical-corrosion performance via the in-situ alloying effects of commercial Al-Mg and Al-Zn powders during additive manufacturing
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Corrosion-mechanical performance trade-off is a key issue for engineering application of Al-Mg alloy. The main restriction is the contradicted performance variation and sensitization phenomenon. Current research has achieved prominent progress in performance optimization of casting Al-Mg alloy, by in-situ alloying, post treatment, etc. Whereas, the performance evolution in hot-spot additive manufacturing still needs systematic study. More importantly, the performance is vitally sensitive to microstructure variation, and their intrinsic mechanism still needs clearer elucidation. This work attempts to testify the influence of microstructure evolution on the strengthening-corrosion behaviors. Herein, an economic and efficient alloying approach is adopted by coupling commercial Al-Zn/Al-Mg system. The cooperation of Al3(Sc,Zr) and low-brittleness T-Mg32(Al,Zn,Cu)49 suppresses the sensitization effects and harmonizes the strengthen-deformation behaviors. Therefore, the novel Al-Mg-Zn-Cu alloy achieves a yield strength of 420.4 MPa and an elongation of 11.4%, and they retain 310.9 MPa and 29.4% at 200 °C, respectively. Moreover, the microstructure can restrain intergranular corrosion and promote pitting homogeneity. Zn addition promotes the passive film densifying, and T-phase shows a standard potential close to matrix, thus lowering the corrosion tendency. By regulating the plastic deformation-corrosion behaviors, the comprehensive performance is improved. The findings can provide a supplement for the performance regulation theory of Al-Mg alloy. © 2026

Authors: Hamidi H.; Haji Seyed Javadi F.; Zahedi M.H.
Title: Beyond Digitalization: A Conceptual and Institutional Framework for Digital Transformation in Higher Education
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Digital transformation in higher education has emerged as a strategic priority for universities worldwide over the past decade. Despite the rapid growth of scholarly interest in this field, the existing literature remains conceptually fragmented, disproportionately focused on technological aspects, and limited in providing integrated frameworks to guide digital transformation processes. This study aims to systematically synthesize the digital transformation literature in higher education, identify dominant trends, key dimensions, challenges, and research gaps, and develop an integrated conceptual framework to address these limitations. Using a systematic literature review approach in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, 145 peer-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2026 were analyzed. Data were examined through systematic content analysis across multiple levels, including temporal and geographical trends, methodological characteristics, thematic classifications, and conceptual integration of findings. The results reveal a clear shift in the literature from technology-centered perspectives toward a multidimensional, institutional, and strategic understanding of digital transformation in higher education. Three interrelated dimensions, digital technologies and infrastructure, human resources and digital skills, and leadership, culture, and policy were identified as the core components of effective digital transformation. The findings further highlight persistent research gaps related to organizational readiness, institutional implications, change management, and the contextual localization of digital transformation frameworks, particularly in developing country contexts. In response to these gaps, this study proposes an integrated conceptual framework that conceptualizes digital transformation in higher education as a dynamic four-stage process encompassing readiness and assessment, pilot implementation, scaling and integration, and continuous optimization and innovation. The proposed framework offers both an analytical foundation for future research and a practical reference for university leaders and policymakers seeking to design and implement sustainable digital transformation initiatives. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Hierarchically woven covalent organic framework hydrogels with programmable hydrogen-binding domains for adaptive human–machine interfaces
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Hydrogels are among the most promising materials for wearable sensors in human–machine interaction, but the pursuit of high mechanical strength and resilience in hydrogels often leads to a trade-off with conductivity, which significantly limits their practical applications; thereby, balancing energy dissipation and ion transport in hydrogels remains a critical challenge. Here, we develop molecularly woven hydrogels by non-covalently threading linear polymers into thiadiazole-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs), in which the thiadiazole dihydrazide units in the COFs function as hydrogen-binding domains, fostering multiple non-covalent interactions between the COFs and linear polymers. This unique configuration facilitates energy dissipation while simultaneously enhancing ion transport. The resulting hydrogels exhibit a tensile strength of 0.41 MPa, resilience of 99%, an ionic conductivity of 1.27 ± 0.18 S m−1, and limited crack propagation, ranking among the highest values reported for hydrogel materials. Furthermore, the hydrogel-based sensor demonstrates a rapid strain response of 12.5 ms, excellent cyclic stability, and superior environmental weatherability, enabling accurate monitoring of human activities and gesture recognition for dexterous robotic manipulation. This work holds great promise for developing intelligent human-machine interfaces to perform dangerous and high-precision tasks. © 2026

Title: A density-aware and overlap-driven framework for task allocation in distributed spatial data processing environments
Abstract: The increasing volume of data generated by distributed sensing and Internet of Things (IoT) devices and applications has intensified the need for efficient data and task management in edge and distributed environments. A key challenge in such systems is determining how to allocate tasks that require the processing of multidimensional data across distributed nodes while preserving data locality and limiting communication overhead. In this paper, we propose a density-aware and overlap-driven framework for task allocation in distributed data-processing environments. Tasks and node data regions are represented as multidimensional hyper-rectangles, while each node maintains information about its local data density. The proposed framework employs a scenario-based allocation mechanism based on strict spatial containment, tolerance-based containment, and external execution. Depending on the spatial relationship between a task and the available data regions, as well as the corresponding density conditions, the task can be executed locally, supported through neighboring-node collaboration, offloaded to another node, or reported as unserved when no suitable execution node is available. Candidate nodes for collaboration and offloading are selected using a scoring mechanism that considers spatial overlap and communication latency. To improve adaptability under heterogeneous data distributions, the framework additionally supports adaptive density thresholds and bounded tolerance expansion according to the observed node densities. The proposed approach is evaluated using three heterogeneous real-world datasets: OpenStreetMap (OSM) data from Greece, NYC Yellow Taxi data, and data derived from the National Ambulatory Medical Care Survey (NAMCS). The evaluation examines allocation behavior, execution success, communication requirements, decision overhead, scalability, parameter sensitivity, and deadline-aware admission. The results demonstrate accurate allocation decisions with low decision overhead while highlighting the trade-offs among local execution, neighbor collaboration, and external offloading. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and adaptive approach to multidimensional task allocation and offers a practical basis for distributed data processing in edge and IoT environments. Title: Efficient optimal scale combination selection via granular sequential three-way decision
Abstract: Optimal scale combination (OSC) selection is crucial for knowledge extraction in multi-scale decision systems (MDSs). However, existing multi-scale rough set models typically represent the three regions as unions of equivalence classes, losing the structural information of equivalence classes and hindering rule extraction. Moreover, most OSC selection algorithms adopt a fine-to-coarse backward search strategy, which not only contradicts the human coarse-to-fine cognitive mode but also is inefficient on large-scale datasets due to scale combination explosion. To address these issues, a granular sequential three-way decision model for MDSs (GrS3WD-M) is developed, and then an efficient forward optimal scale combination selection algorithm (FOSC) is designed. First, a two-step trisecting strategy is proposed to accelerate boundary region reduction, and then GrS3WD-M based on granular rough sets is developed to preserve the structural information of equivalence classes. As a result, rules can be directly extracted from equivalence classes in the positive region, while redundant computation during granulation is avoided. Second, the core scale combination is defined, an equivalent computational formula is derived, and an efficient algorithm based on GrS3WD-M and attribute grouping is proposed for its computation. Finally, the outer significance of attributes in MDSs is defined, and an efficient method for computing it is presented. Furthermore, the FOSC algorithm is proposed, which starts from the core scale combination and uses the outer significance as a heuristic to guide a coarse-to-fine forward search. Authors: Desrizal; Widigdo B.; Yulianto G.; Kurniawan F.; Sulistiono
Title: Sustainability assessment for multi-activity coastal areas using an integrated hierarchical decision-making framework
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainability assessments of multi-activity coastal areas generally evaluate each utilization activity independently, leaving interdependencies unaccommodated and risking biased contribution estimates under conventional hierarchical weighting. This constraint carries profound implications for settings where anthropogenic activities vie for finite ecological space, most notably within tropical coastal socio-ecological systems in developing countries. The study objectives were to develop an activity-based sustainability assessment framework integrating hierarchical and network-based multi-criteria weighting to estimate the relative contribution of three activities: small-scale capture fisheries, vannamei shrimp ponds, and coastal tourism, in the coastal area of Pariaman City, Indonesia. METHODS: Assessments covered 36 indicators across four sustainability dimensions: ecological, social, economic, and governance, with a 17-node interdependence network built from 14 indicators showing cross-activity dependencies through shared resources and identified causal pathways. Hierarchical weights for individual activities were derived independently by fifteen experts across three sectoral panels. Additionally, network-based weighting to account for inter-activity interactions was performed by a subset of five cross-sectoral experts. All pairwise comparison matrices satisfied the predetermined consistency threshold. The resilience of the regional index to weighting uncertainty was tested through sensitivity analysis. FINDINGS: Network-based weights ranked vannamei shrimp ponds above small-scale capture fisheries and coastal tourism, but far less dominantly than under hierarchical weighting, which treated ponds as an extreme outlier by ignoring their negative influence on shared water quality and spatial resources. With a near-uniform contribution value of 0.554 across all three activities, the regional index underscores that intervention prioritization requires integrating interdependent cross-activity contributions rather than relying exclusively on standalone activity assessments. The moderately sustainable category held consistently across sensitivity scenarios, although activity contribution order proved more sensitive to weighting uncertainty. CONCLUSION: Accounting for interdependence corrects the hierarchical approach's over-estimation of vannamei shrimp ponds and reveals a greater contribution from small-scale capture fisheries and coastal tourism than independent estimates suggest. The sustainability contribution of a given activity cannot be reliably determined in isolation from cross-sectoral interdependencies, highlighting the primary utility of this framework as a decision-support mechanism for coastal management. Title: Brains on copy-paste mode? A mixed-methods study on the relationship between generative artificial intelligence use and students’ critical thinking skills
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence tools, such as ChatGPT, into higher education has raised important questions about their relationship with students' critical thinking (CT) skills. This study explored these associations among 398 undergraduate students using a mixed-methods design. Quantitatively, participants completed validated measures of critical thinking and a survey assessing frequency of AI use in academic contexts. Correlation analyses indicated a significant negative association between AI use and Analyzing/Organizing skills. Moderation analyses revealed that academic achievement moderated this relationship for Analyzing/Organizing and Evaluating, with higher achievers showing a stronger negative association. No significant effects emerged for gender and age on the remaining CT dimensions. Likewise, qualitative analyses of 200 open-ended responses identified three user profiles: (1) instrumental/uncritical, comprising younger low-achieving male students emphasizing AI speed and utility while reporting reduced verification effort; (2) stable/complementary, comprising older high-achieving students perceiving little change in their evaluative practices; and (3) ambivalent/skeptical-trusting, comprising women with medium achievement, divided between increased skepticism and greater reliance on AI outputs. Supplementary analyses linking Analyzing/Organizing and Evaluating scores to these profiles showed that lower development of both skills consistently aligned with the instrumental/uncritical profile. The interpretive consistency between both analytical strands suggests that the relationship between generative AI use and CT skills is nuanced and profile-dependent, limited in scope to specific dimensions and student groups rather than reflecting a broad negative impact, while highlighting the risks of uncritical reliance and the potential of AI as a complementary academic tool when used reflectively. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Affective Dimensions of Spanish as a Foreign Language (SFL) Education: Exploring the Interplay of Anxiety, Motivation, and Self-Esteem among Secondary School Students
Abstract: This study probed the associations among Spanish as a foreign language (SFL) students’ anxiety, motivation, and self-esteem. Beyond mapping the connections between these affective factors, the research also examined the extent to which students’ motivation and anxiety predicted their self-esteem. The data were collected from 118 secondary school students through three validated instruments, namely the Foreign Language Classroom Anxiety Scale, Foreign Language Self-Esteem Scale, and Motivation towards Foreign Languages Survey. The analysis indicated clear patterns of association, with higher levels of anxiety linked to lower levels of both motivation and self-esteem. The results highlighted the importance of addressing emotional factors in foreign language education and suggested that interventions targeting anxiety reduction and the enhancement of self-esteem and motivation could foster a more supportive language learning environment. By demonstrating how affective factors shape SFL learning, the study offered practical insights for policymakers and language educators seeking to promote students’ emotional well-being and engagement. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Integrating local cultural values into deep learning pedagogy: A framework for teaching science fiction writing in Indonesia
Abstract: This study examines the integration of the Deep Learning curriculum with Javanese cultural values in teaching science fiction writing to high school students. The study is motivated by the importance of developing STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) competencies integrated with the strengthening of cultural identity in the era of globalization. A mixed methods research approach was applied involving 30 students and 2 Indonesian language teachers at SMA Negeri 9 Malang. Data were collected through structured observations, semi-structured interviews, and analysis of student work documents using rubrics developed based on the 6C's dimensions of Deep Learning (Critical Thinking, Creativity, Collaboration, Communication, Character, Citizenship). The research results revealed that the integration successfully actualized all dimensions of Deep Learning at a high level (scores of 4.3-4.8 on a 5-point scale), with the highest achievements in the Collaboration (4.8) and Creativity (4.7) dimensions. Qualitative analysis of student work identified five patterns of Javanese cultural integration, namely: (1) integration of technology with Javanese philosophy, (2) technology as an optimizer of local wisdom, (3) mythology as the basis of technology, (4) collaborative resolution of generational conflicts, and (5) culture as a value system regulating technology. As many as 55% of student works reached the very good category, showing a significant improvement in aspects of creativity and cultural integration. The research conclusion states that the integration of the Deep Learning curriculum with Javanese cultural values not only improves technical competence in writing science fiction but also develops contextual scientific literacy and strengthens students' cultural identity. This model represents a transformative synthesis between global education paradigms and local wisdom relevant to the Indonesian educational context. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Developing Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Gen Z accounting students: The roles of AI Competency, Systematic Thinking Ability, and Design Thinking Ability
Abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in accounting practices have significantly increased the complexity and uncertainty of professional work environments, making Dynamic Risk Management Skills a critical competency for contemporary accounting graduates. This study aims to examine the relationships between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Generation Z (Gen Z) accounting students, with Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability considered as mediating variables. A quantitative research design was employed, collecting data from 571 fourth-year accounting students across Thailand. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that AI Competency is significantly and positively associated with Systematic Thinking Ability, Design Thinking Ability, and Dynamic Risk Management Skills. Moreover, Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability significantly account for the indirect associations between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills. These findings extend theoretical understanding of risk management skill development in accounting education and offer practical implications for curriculum design by emphasizing the integration of AI with higher-order thinking skill development to better prepare graduates for complex and rapidly changing professional environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Modelling Local Strontium Isotope Baselines from Human Isotopic Data Using Machine Learning: Implications for Past Mobility Studies
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Estimating bioavailable strontium isotope baselines is a critical step in archaeological mobility studies. Conventional proxy-based approaches, which rely on environmental samples, such as soils, fauna, plants, or waters, are not always feasible and may be affected by environmental, taphonomic, or sampling-related biases. Here, we introduce MobSr, a machine-learning-based model designed to estimate probable local 87Sr/86Sr baselines directly from human enamel isotope data. The model combines four first-layer classifiers—Naïve Bayes, k-nearest neighbours, support vector machine, and Random Forest—with a Bayesian ensemble layer that integrates classifier outputs and refines local/non-local probability estimates. MobSr was trained on a dataset of approximately 3000 human enamel samples from 86 archaeological sites, using published expert-derived local/non-local classifications. Local isotopic ranges are estimated by analysing posterior probabilities assigned to individual observations. Model performance was evaluated through general cross-validation and through site-specific case studies, including a La Tène period cemetery from the Czech Republic, an Early Medieval cemetery from Finland, and multi-period burial assemblages from Bahrain in the Arabian Peninsula. The results show 87–95% agreement with published local/non-local classifications, depending on the evaluation strategy and treatment of atypical cases. These values quantify concordance with the source-study labels. These findings demonstrate that MobSr can replicate and refine local baseline estimates without requiring additional environmental sampling. The model offers an efficient tool for preliminary mobility assessment and provides a complementary strategy to traditional baseline construction in bioarchaeological research. In addition, the use of a large training dataset enables broader exploration of expert-derived locality assignments across predominantly sedentary populations from different regions and periods. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Beyond copy number: circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA Fragmentomics and structural states in liquid biopsy
Abstract: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf-mtDNA) is commonly treated as a concentration-based biomarker, yet the measured signal is a composite of biologically distinct molecular states that are differentially affected by blood collection, platelet activation, centrifugation, storage, extraction, amplification, and sequencing. This analytical heterogeneity has become more consequential as cf-mtDNA research moves from copy-number assays toward fragmentomics, topology, heteroplasmy, oxidative lesions, and carrier-resolved measurements. Recent multi-cohort studies indicate that fragment size, 5′-end composition, motif diversity, and regional breakage patterns can support cancer detection and tissue-of-origin inference, while clinical chemistry studies demonstrate that routine preanalytical choices can markedly alter the mitochondrial fraction recovered from plasma. This review develops a laboratory-medicine framework in which cf-mtDNA is considered a multidimensional analyte rather than a single abundance variable. We integrate mitochondrial release biology with the extracellular carrier states of mtDNA; explain how TFAM, membrane pores, mitophagy, extracellular vesicles, platelets, and nucleases shape the observed fragmentome; evaluate preanalytical and analytical sources of bias; and assess translational evidence across oncology, critical illness, cardio-renal disease, metabolic inflammation, transplantation, and neuroinflammatory disorders. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing true biological variation from procedure-induced redistribution of cf-mtDNA between soluble, vesicular, platelet-associated, and cell-free mitochondrial compartments. We propose minimum analytical descriptors, quality-control priorities, and validation steps required before cf-mtDNA fragmentomic signatures can become transportable clinical tests. The central implication is that the next phase of cf-mtDNA diagnostics will depend less on measuring more DNA than on measuring the correct molecular fraction with traceable preanalytics, orthogonal characterization, and clinically locked computational models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Shala V.J.; Shala H.
Title: Between criminalization and decriminalization: Homosexuality, gender norms, and sociolegal change in Kosovo
Abstract: Since the mid-nineteenth century, Kosovo has undergone significant social transformation and legal reform, particularly in relation to sexuality and state intervention in private life. This study provides a historical analysis of criminal legislation addressing homosexuality, examining both normative legal frameworks and prevailing social attitudes. At first glance, the fact that approximately 95 of the population of Kosovo identifies as Muslim might suggest the existence of a pronounced social resistance towards homosexuals, as seen in certain countries of the Eastern world. However, empirical research reveals a considerably more intricate social reality. While traditional attitudes toward homosexuality persist, there is no proportionally strong political or social mobilization against the rights of homosexual individuals. Indeed, a significant segment of the population endorses the civil rights of LGBT people in general. The main reason for these attitudes is that national identity often carries more social and political weight than religious affiliation. The research employed a mixed-methods design, integrating a literature review, historical and comparative analysis, two personal communications, and a structured questionnaire survey conducted with 1,050 respondents stratified into three age groups. The χ^2 test of independence was used to assess the associations between attitudes, gender, and age, while Cramer's V measured the strength of these relationships. The findings demonstrate that age exerts a statistically significant influence on attitudes, whereas gender differences are relatively small. The majority of the respondents (74.8%) recognize that homosexuals and lesbians often marry heterosexually to conform to tradition, while 77.3% believe imprisonment would not eliminate homosexuality. Furthermore, the results indicated that more than half (53.2%) oppose renewed punishment for homosexuals, and 52% acknowledge its timeless existence. The findings of this study suggest that attitudes toward homosexuality in Kosovo are shaped by a complex interplay of historical experience, legal change, cultural norms, and contemporary human rights discourse. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Risk perception and preventive control in indoor plant production: food safety practices among Swedish operators of leafy vegetables and microgreens
Abstract: Indoor plant production is often promoted as a controlled production system that can reduce some hazards associated with open-field cultivation. However, ready-to-eat leafy vegetables, herbs, microgreens and sprouts remain vulnerable to microbial contamination through seeds, water, nutrient solutions, growing media, surfaces and human handling. This study investigated how Swedish commercial indoor production operators perceive and manage food safety in their urban soilless production systems. A mixed-methods design was used, combining an online survey of 17 respondents with semi-structured interviews with representatives from eight indoor production operations. Fisher's exact tests showed no statistically significant association between awareness of applicable safety requirements and educational level, certification status, or previous safety training. Interview data showed that food safety management was shaped by three interrelated dimensions: risk perception, preventive control practices, and economic, spatial and regulatory constraints. Some operators interpreted controlled indoor production as inherently low risk, whereas others recognized system specific hazards and reported routines for seed treatment, water testing, cleaning, employee hygiene, documentation and certification. Resource limitations, testing costs, limited space, language barriers and unclear regulatory communication constrained implementation. Because the study did not include observation, audit or microbiological sampling, it addresses perceived safety and reported preventive control rather than verified food safety performance. The findings reinforce that indoor plant production modifies, but does not remove, the food safety risk landscape. Strengthening food safety in this sector requires practical, regulation-aligned training, scalable guidance, and verifiable preventive controls adapted to indoor production systems. © 2026

Title: From Individual Reasoning to Collaborative Engagement: Continuity of Student Problematic in Grade 1 Mathematical Problem Solving
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This qualitative study examined the continuity of student problematic from individual reasoning to collaborative engagement in a Grade 1 mathematics classroom within the Transformative Lesson Study Incorporating Open Approach (TLSOA) context. Seven Grade 1 students were followed across six lessons on addition and subtraction. Data were collected through video and audio recordings, students’ written work, field notes, and photographs, and analyzed using protocol analysis and analytic description. The findings show that student problematic remained observable when students re-engaged with the same mathematical problem in small groups. Student problematic appeared through proposing, questioning, explaining, checking, reconsidering, and coordinating mathematical ideas. The study contributes to understanding how young learners’ mathematical engagement continues across changing social contexts. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

Title: Beyond the final product: AI-Enabled Learner Traces as Assessment Evidence in Project Management Education
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in project management education (PME), especially in digital learning environments where learner activity can be captured as process data. This matters because project management learning involves collaboration, coordination, decision-making, reflection, and professional judgement, which are difficult to assess through final outputs alone. This systematic mapping review examines how AI-generated or AI-mediated learner data are collected, analysed, and used for assessment-related purposes, and identifies the educational implications reported in the literature. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches were conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, ERIC, and IEEE Xplore for studies published between January 2016 and November 2025. Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The review identified five categories of AI-enabled learner data and assessment-relevant evidence: human–AI dialogue and prompt-based interaction logs, adaptive and personalised learning process data, project artefacts and revision traces, reflective, self-report, and course feedback evidence, and standardised task, output, and scoring data. These categories are treated as different layers in the data-to-evidence process rather than as learner traces in a narrow technical sense. Future-oriented conceptual data systems were identified as an emerging possibility but were treated separately from reported learner data and assessment evidence. Across the included studies, data were analysed using natural language processing, machine learning, rule-based techniques, learning analytics, and generative AI/LLM-based prompting, and were used to generate feedback, indicators, recommendations, and scoring support. Reported benefits mainly relate to formative feedback, improved visibility of learning processes, and more timely instructional support. However, the evidence base remains limited and uneven, with important gaps in validity, fairness, transparency, and longer-term educational effects. Overall, AI in PME is used not simply to automate assessment, but to broaden how learner activity is captured, interpreted, and used to support process-oriented assessment and pedagogical judgement. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Helal A.; Hoseyni S.M.
Title: Optimizing renewable energy planning: a Monte Carlo–analytical hierarchy process framework for net-zero transitions
Abstract: As the world pursues net-zero emissions, selecting renewable energy technologies presents a complex challenge balancing technical, economic, environmental, and social factors. Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods support decisions by comparing alternatives against multiple criteria. However, traditional MCDM approaches, reliant on fixed inputs, often fail to capture real-world variability in energy planning, yielding less reliable outcomes. This study introduces a novel Monte Carlo–Analytical Hierarchy Process (MAHP) framework that integrates AHP's structured evaluation with Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) to model uncertainty in criteria weights and alternative scores. The MAHP framework was applied to support Sheffield's 2030 net-zero target by evaluating five renewable energy technologies: solar PV, onshore wind, biomass, hydropower, and geothermal. Thousands of simulations were conducted to reflect different stakeholder priorities, covering technical, environmental, social, economic, and equal-weighting scenarios. The analysis demonstrated that technology rankings are highly sensitive to stakeholder priorities, underscoring the need for adaptable planning approaches, and showing that no single technology consistently dominates when priorities are balanced. Overall, the results support a hybrid mix centred on solar PV, onshore wind, and hydropower for Sheffield. This framework strengthens renewable energy planning by moving beyond single deterministic rankings and instead quantifying how robust each recommendation is under uncertainty and shifting priorities. By making ranking stability and trade-offs explicit, MAHP enhances the credibility of technology selection and provides decision-makers with clearer evidence to support defensible net-zero strategies in dynamic urban contexts. More broadly, probabilistic ranking supports portfolio planning by identifying consistently competitive technologies, reducing over-commitment when stakeholder priorities and evidence are uncertain. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Synthesis, physicochemical characterization, and alkyd-enamel performance of cobalt phthalocyanine pigment
Abstract: Cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc)-containing pigment was prepared by heating phthalic anhydride, urea, and cobalt(II) chloride with boric acid and magnesium acetate tetrahydrate at 200 °C for 2 h and evaluated in PF-115 alkyd enamel. A 40.000 g portion of the crude product yielded 16.400 g of dry pigment-containing material after acid treatment, neutralization, washing, and drying (41.0% purification mass recovery); the chemical yield and purity of CoPc were not established. Powder X-ray diffraction showed changes after acid treatment but did not permit an unambiguous α/β polymorph assignment. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) bands supported a phthalocyanine-related framework, whereas absorptions at 1772 and 1722 cm−1 indicated possible residual carbonyl-containing compounds. Ultraviolet–visible absorption of a sample prepared in dimethyl sulfoxide showed features in the 600–700 nm region. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) showed an unresolved signal near 337.9 mT (effective g = 1.9996) without uniquely identifying its origin; scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy provided local, semi-quantitative elemental information. Enamels containing 4.5 wt% pigment matched the reported first-grade GOST 6465-76 numerical limits, with gloss values of 54% and 50% and hiding-power values of 60 and 40 g m−2 for light-blue and blue coatings, respectively. The results support use of the recovered pigment fraction as a colorant in the tested alkyd formulations, while its chemical yield, bulk purity, and polymorph identity remain unresolved. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Network science in sports
Abstract: Network science has become a central methodological framework for the study of complex systems, with applications across social, biological, and technological domains. Its strength lies in formalizing such systems as collections of interacting units, whose collective behavior depends not only on the properties of the individual components, but also on the structure, dynamics, and evolution of their interactions. In this Review, we analyze how this framework, rooted in statistical physics, is being applied to the study of sports systems. Sports provide a particularly suitable domain for network modeling, as performance emerges from interactions among agents, whose actions are constrained by spatial embedding and temporal ordering, and evolve under competitive, adaptive, and out-of-equilibrium conditions. We review the main network representations used in sports, from classical graph-based descriptions to more general frameworks, including spatial, temporal, multilayer, and higher-order networks. Particular attention is devoted to soccer, where network science has had its deepest methodological impact, while applications to other sports such as basketball, volleyball, American football, or badminton serve to illustrate the generality of the underlying principles. Network science provides sports analytics with a rigorous language for quantifying coordination, emergence, adaptation, and collective performance. At the same time, the availability of high-resolution event, tracking, and pose-estimation data makes sports an ideal testbed for validating and refining network models in realistic settings. As a result, the relationship between network science and sports, currently driven primarily by the application of network methods to sport, has the potential to become genuinely bidirectional. In this Review, we not only organize the literature on network methodologies and their applications to sports, but also discuss complementary concepts needed to capture the full picture, including entropy and complexity measures, as well as key ideas from statistical physics and nonlinear dynamics. Finally, despite the substantial progress made so far, the field remains under active development, and we highlight the main open questions that should be addressed in future research. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Evaluating feasibility of an ACT group telehealth-delivered therapy intervention for adolescents with depression
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Increasing rates of adolescent depression call for efficient and accessible interventions that are well received by adolescents. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a third-wave psychotherapy that has been shown to be effective in treating depression in adolescents, delivered both individually and in group settings. Group therapy can help address service provider shortages by enabling a single provider to treat multiple individuals at once. Additionally, telehealth allows greater access to care for individuals who cannot readily travel to a clinic. Telehealth-delivered group therapy combines these two strategies to facilitate adolescents’ access to mental health treatment. We piloted a 10-week group intervention, adapted from ACT for Adolescents with Depression, and explored its feasibility. Adolescent patients with depression (N = 10) ages 14 to 18 (M = 16; SD = 1.49 years), seeking mental health services, participated in the program and completed pre and post assessments. The majority identified as female (70%) and White (60%). The groups were well attended; only one patient dropped out, and one was discharged. The patients reported overwhelmingly overall positive experiences with the program. Group means for depression and anxiety scores in this sample decreased from baseline to end of treatment, psychological flexibility increased by the end of treatment, and no changes were observed in flourishing scores. Overall, the intervention was well accepted. Well-powered research studies with randomized allocation to telehealth delivered ACT and control groups are needed to test this protocol’s effectiveness in treating depression in adolescents as an independent treatment or as adjunct treatment to individual therapy. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Authors: Jin B.; He B.; Zhao Y.; Liu Y.; Ding J.; Meng L.; Shi Y.; Han D.; Sun J.
Title: A multi-objective planning study of distributed photovoltaics based on candidate-node screening and an MO-ISSA method
Abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (DPV) siting and sizing in distribution networks is a high-dimensional discrete optimization problem with coupled objectives. Existing studies usually focus on optimizer improvement or full-bus-set planning, while the coordinated improvement of search-space reduction and Pareto-front quality remains insufficient. To address this issue, a DPV planning framework combining topology-aware candidate-node screening and a Multi-Objective Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (MO-ISSA) is proposed. A Node Comprehensive Importance Index (NCII), integrating inter-community connections, betweenness centrality, and active-power-loss improvement, is constructed to identify candidate nodes before optimization. MO-ISSA is then used to solve a three-objective model considering economic benefit, comprehensive grid vulnerability, and active power loss. Results on the IEEE 33-bus system show that the proposed screening strategy reduces computation time while maintaining planning quality. Compared with NSGA-II, MOPSO, and SSA, MO-ISSA achieves better Pareto-front quality, convergence, and stability. Comparisons with the full-node-space heuristic result, an SOCP-representable deterministic surrogate reference model, and full-node-space standard algorithms further verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The IEEE 69-bus case confirms its applicability to larger distribution networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Efficient IP Lookup Using a B-Tree on Expanded Trie
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: As routing tables continue to increase in size, IP address lookup has become a critical performance bottleneck in packet forwarding. A fundamental challenge arises from the variable-length nature of IP prefixes, which requires longest prefix matching (LPM) to identify the appropriate next-hop router. This paper presents BTET (B-tree on Expanded Trie), an efficient data structure designed to support high-performance IP address lookup. BTET combines the hierarchical organization of B-trees with the Controlled Prefix Expansion (CPE) technique to achieve efficient lookup and update operations. The core of the proposed structure consists of a collection of B-trees, where each expanded prefix is partitioned into multiple segments, and each segment is stored in the B-tree corresponding to its expansion level. Abstract: Background and Aims: Oral sulfate solutions (OSSs) are used for low-volume bowel preparation but have a distinctive bitter taste. This study evaluated the efficacy and tolerability of OSSs compared with polyethylene glycol plus ascorbate (PEG-ASC) and identified patient factors associated with favorable acceptability. Title: A tax-subsidy scheme for efficient investment in renewable generation capacity
Abstract: Electricity markets are central to the energy transition, but current market rules do not always deliver socially desirable outcomes. This paper studies two related inefficiencies in wholesale electricity markets. First, competitive market-clearing based on merit-order dispatch can ignore pollution damages, leading to inefficient spot-market outcomes. We address this distortion by deriving a Pigouvian tax that charges each generator for its marginal contribution to pollution damages. Second, because generation capacity affects future spot prices, producers may strategically distort their long-run investment decisions, particularly in systems with increasingly low-operating-cost renewable generation. To align private investment incentives with social welfare, we derive a generator-specific investment subsidy based on each producer's contribution to aggregate utility. We show that, under the stated behavioral and informational assumptions, the combined tax–subsidy mechanism aligns decentralized dispatch and generation-capacity investment decisions with the social-welfare benchmark while respecting operational constraints. Implementing this mechanism does not require producers to report their complete private cost functions; the tax and subsidy can instead be calculated using existing market submissions and settlement data, verified emission information, and generator-specific counterfactual market re-clearing outcome. An analytical example and numerical experiments illustrate the mechanism and show that strategic capacity investment can exceed the socially optimal level and reduce welfare. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Unbowed: Raiding and Hunting with Paracas Spearthrowers and Slings and the Conspicuous Absence of the Bow in Western South America
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: New weapons such as the bow and arrow often emerge alongside rising population densities and interpersonal conflict. We test this generalization in southern Peru during the violent Final Formative (400–1 BCE) with measurements of 200 obsidian projectile points anchored to precise Bayesian chronologies from Paracas sites in the Palpa valleys. Based on Bayesian regressions against hafted archaeological projectile points, we conclude all Paracas points were spearthrower darts. This agrees with the lack of bows in Paracas burials and in imagery on ceramics and textiles. Conflict was limited to small-scale raids, based on a compilation of sites with slingstones, mace heads, skeletal trauma, and walls. Hunting and herding were focused in the highlands, mapped with a MaxEnt predictive surface of modern prey location. Based on spatial correlations, conflict did not drive settlement patterns; the key factors were hunting grounds, herding pastures, and agricultural suitability. Pending future research, the notable lack of the bow in the region may include later Nasca, Moche, and Chimú populations. This invites us to rethink the conditions that drive and limit the adoption and invention of bows, a uniquely human and purportedly superior projectile technology that no one bothered with during these violent centuries. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: The Fragility of Collective Action in Community Forest Management: Social Feedbacks, Trust, and Cooperation Dynamics
Abstract: In community forest management, cooperation is rarely a one-time decision. It depends on whether local actors continue contributing time, labor, and resources year after year. We examine this problem with a system dynamics model that follows changes in trust, reputation, reciprocity, perceived benefits, and free-riding. The model adapts an earlier structure to the case of ejido La Loma, Mexico. The case material guided several modeling decisions, especially the choice of variables and the interpretation of the scenarios. It did not, however, provide enough information for full empirical calibration. The simulations show that trust and reputation may sustain cooperation even as participation declines. Over time, however, the loss of active members can weaken monitoring and place collective action at risk. One result is particularly relevant: a favorable starting point does not guarantee long-term stability. Title: Genetic engineering of cyanophages for harmful cyanobacterial bloom treatment—A mini review
Abstract: Harmful cyanobacterial blooms (HCBs) are a prominent worldwide environmental concern. Proliferation of HCBs outpaces the development of mitigation and management technologies. Recently, cyanophages began to emerge as a potential abundant resource that can be harnessed for target-specific HCB treatment. However, there exist two major technical barriers in applying cyanophage-based treatment to HCB mitigation: host specificity and lysogenic life cycle. This minireview attempts to parse documented studies that developed or applied genetic engineering approaches or technologies to tackle the barriers through expanding host range and bypassing or abolishing the lysogenic life stage. We summarized representative technical approaches that may be extrapolated from bacteriophage to cyanophage, discussed genes and pathways that regulate host binding and infection or determine the switch between lytic and lysogenic lifecycles, identified existing knowledge and technological gaps and challenges, and proposed some attainable solutions and future perspectives for this fast-growing field of engineered cyanophage-mediated HCB remediation. © 2026 .

Title: A comparative investigation of physics-driven machine learning architectures for consolidation analysis
Abstract: Physics-driven machine learning has emerged as a powerful framework for forward and inverse modeling of partial differential equations (PDEs), with increasing applications in geotechnical engineering. However, the relative performance of different physics-driven learning strategies remains problem-dependent, and their suitability for typical geotechnical problems has not been systematically established. This study systematically compares four physics-driven machine learning paradigms for consolidation analysis by combining Multi‑Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) with physics-informed neural networks (PINN) and the discrete-time deep energy method (DTDEM). The paradigms are evaluated for forward and inverse consolidation problems in one and three dimensions, with particular attention to convergence, computational cost, parameter inversion, accuracy, and robustness to noise. For forward problems governed by PDEs, although the energy-form DTDEM converges in fewer epochs than the strong-form PINN under both MLP and KAN architectures, its higher per-epoch cost results in a longer total wall-clock training time. A similar trade-off applies to KAN relative to MLP where the higher per-epoch cost can offset the benefit of faster convergence in terms of epochs. In terms of solution accuracy, replacing MLP with KAN improves both accuracy and training-loss convergence under the strong-form PINN framework, while under the DTDEM framework this advantage is not consistent. For parameter inversion, the DTDEM-based energy formulation is ineffective for parameter inversion because treating material parameters as additional optimization variables make the functional unbounded from below, resulting in divergent training. In contrast, within the strong-form framework, KAN substantially improves parameter-inversion accuracy and robustness to noisy data compared with MLPs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: UHPLC-HRMS-based untargeted lipidomics for differentiating halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages
Abstract: The integrity of the halal food supply chain is continually challenged by fraudulent adulteration, particularly in processed meat products where visual identification of ingredients is impossible. This study used untargeted lipidomics based on ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-HRMS) combined with chemometric analysis to differentiate halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages. Five sausage formulations were prepared: 100% beef, 100% pork, 100% dog meat, and 50:50 mixtures of beef–pork and beef–dog meat. Lipid profiles were acquired in both positive (ESI+) and negative (ESI−) ionization modes. Principal component analysis (PCA) clearly separated the five sausage formulations, indicating distinct lipidomic profiles. Partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) further differentiated the sample groups and identified several putative lipid biomarkers based on variable importance in projection (VIP) scores. Among these, PG(16:0/18:2) and PE(6:0/14:1) + H detected in pork samples were consistent with previous reports and may serve as candidate biomarkers for halal authentication, while PC(18:0p/17:1) + H and PC(13:0/21:2) + H were identified as putative lipid biomarkers characteristic of dog meat sausages. These findings highlight the potential of UHPLC-HRMS-based untargeted lipidomics for differentiating halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages. However, the proposed biomarkers require further validation by targeted MS/MS analysis and independent sample sets before broader application. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Materials–Structure–Hardware–Algorithm Co-Driven Hierarchical Optimization for Flexible Sensors
Abstract: Flexible electronics represent a paradigm shift in modern electronics, with flexible sensors serving as pivotal components in these systems. Despite significant advances driven by innovations in materials, structures, hardware, and algorithms, conventional design approaches that focus on optimizing individual hierarchies have inherent performance trade-offs, limiting further development. This review contends that future performance enhancements can no longer rely solely on breakthroughs in separate components. Still, it must adopt a new co-design paradigm spanning the “materials–structure–hardware–algorithm” hierarchy. In this review, we systematically organized the research landscape and representative advances across these four key hierarchies, analyzed the importance and recent breakthroughs in hierarchical synergy, and established a forward-looking theoretical framework to foster innovation and development in the field of flexible sensing.
