Title: Re-imagining visions as shared societal statements– empirical insights from Indian cities
Abstract: Visions in Indian cities lack commitment from actors and possess low normative power. To address these concerns, we take up the task of examining vision-making with a focus on institutional settings across 31 million-plus populated cities. Ostrom's Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) framework and ADICO grammar tool are used for analysis. We ask how rules-in-use within the vision-making settings are organized and geared towards collective action, and how they affect outcomes, i.e., visions. The analysis underscores three commonalities that hinder collective action, i.e., bureaucratic hegemony and allegiance to sectoral mandates, fragmented actor constellation and weak regulatory power of visions. Within visioning settings, facilitators serve as key agents for ensuring a level playing field. We found that when facilitators are external (i.e., consultants), stakeholder coverage is wider and documentation is exhaustive. In large metropolises and megacities, the visioning process acknowledges stakeholder consultation responsibly. Perhaps fair information exchange and informal monitoring of visions by civil society actors contribute to the politicisation of vision-making. In institutional terms, visions are closer to being a strategy and less to norm-setting. The paper argues that participatory discussions in diverse and heterogeneous settings with the scope of repeat interactions will build homophily and address concerns of structural fragmentation. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Algorithms-Based Monitoring of Vaccine Coverage in Chronic-Disease Cohorts: A Population-Based Evaluation of Regional Immunization Policy in Emilia-Romagna, Italy
Abstract: Objectives This study aims at estimating uptake of risk-based recommended adult vaccinations among major chronic-condition subgroups in Emilia-Romagna Region (Italy) and at quantifying sociodemographic and territorial determinants of vaccine uptake. Methods Retrospective, population-based record-linkage study including all residents aged ≥18 years registered on December 31, 2023 ( N = 3 793 475). Chronic conditions (nonmutually exclusive: diabetes, cardiopathies, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [COPD], chronic kidney disease, cancer, and anatomical asplenia) were identified through multisource algorithms applied to regional administrative databases (2020-2024). Vaccination histories were retrieved from the Regional Vaccination Registry-Real Time (2000-2024); uptake was defined as ≥1 recorded dose. Uptake was modeled via subgroup-specific multivariable logistic regression (sex, age group, citizenship, Local Health Authority). Results Pneumococcal uptake ranged from 28.4% in cancer to 40.7% in COPD and was markedly higher in anatomical asplenia (85.1%). Composite uptake mirrored these patterns (32.6% cancer; 42.0% COPD; 85.5% asplenia). Uptake of other risk-indicated vaccines was low in large subgroups, whereas asplenia showed high meningococcal uptake (MenACWY 67.5%; MenB 65.8%). In multivariable models, Italian citizenship was consistently associated with statistically significant higher odds of composite uptake (OR 1.348-2.527), and male sex increased odds in all subgroups ( P < .001) except for asplenia. Age effects were substantial but condition specific. Residual territorial heterogeneity persisted after adjustment. Conclusions Algorithm-based identification of chronic-disease populations linked to immunization registries enables scalable, risk-stratified monitoring applicable to any chronic-condition subgroup definable through administrative codes. This approach detects strong equity gradients and persistent between-Local-Health-Authority variation, supporting regression-based indicators for subregional benchmarking and targeted strengthening of integrated multivaccine delivery pathways. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Territorializing the sea: fragmented operational control in offshore tin mining on Bangka Island, Indonesia
Abstract: The expansion of offshore tin mining transforms the sea into a space of extraction, yet territorial claims over this space do not necessarily translate into operational control. Studies of territorialization have largely focused on the formation of claims rather than on the processes through which such claims are converted into operational control. This article examines the territorialization of offshore tin mining on Bangka Island, Indonesia, through three interrelated analytical moments: territorial claims, securing access, and operational control. This qualitative study draws on fieldwork comprising interviews with 23 informants and observations, supplemented by a review of relevant literature and an analysis of regulatory documents, corporate reports, and news coverage. The findings show that exploration and regulatory arrangements produce epistemic and legal claims over marine space but do not, in themselves, enable mining operations. Companies and their local networks must still secure access by cultivating and representing support, engaging village institutions and local intermediaries, negotiating benefits, and making personal approaches to key actors. Their success varies across locations, shaped by local power relations, actor legitimacy, and fisher resistance. Consequently, operational control is contingent, partial, fragmented, and continuously negotiated: mining operations can proceed in some locations, whereas elsewhere territorial claims remain in force without being translated into operational control. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Optimized machine learning models for identification of autism spectrum disorder
Source title: International Journal of Cognitive Computing in Engineering
Abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) relies heavily on identifying critical behavioral and clinical markers within high-dimensional datasets. However, standard feature selection methods frequently struggle with premature convergence and suboptimal feature identification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an approach based on an Improved White Shark Optimizer combined with Machine Learning classifiers (IWSO-ML). The proposed approach engineers a dynamic balance between global exploration and local refinement by integrating an adaptive PSO-WSO velocity update, differential evolution, and covariance-based exploitation. To ensure robust search space navigation and prevent local optima entrapment, IWSO-ML incorporates Sobol/Halton chaotic initialization, a shrinking search radius, and stagnation-aware population control. The algorithmic superiority of the approach is first validated against the complex CEC’2022 continuous benchmark suite. The proposed IWSO-ML evaluated clinically across four diverse ASD datasets including adult, children in UCI, and prediction, screening in Kaggle using five distinct classification models (SVM, K-NN, RF, DT, and GNB). Extensive statistical analysis confirm that IWSO-ML consistently outperforms state-of-the-art metaheuristics, including RUN, HHO, IMODE, PSO, SSA, WOA and MFO. Notably, the IWSO-SVM configuration achieved a peak classification accuracy of 99.5%, demonstrating superior convergence speed, narrowed error distributions, and exceptional solution stability. Ultimately, this hybrid architecture provides a highly generalized and computationally efficient feature selection mechanism, establishing a robust foundation for reliable clinical predictive modeling and advanced ASD diagnostics. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Cost-Effectiveness of Peripheral Neuropathy Screening in Patients With Thalassemia: A Hybrid Decision-Markov Model
Abstract: Objectives To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of a systematic screening program for thalassemia-related peripheral neuropathy (ThalPN) compared with standard care in Malaysia. Methods A hybrid decision-Markov model was developed to simulate the lifetime health outcomes and costs for a hypothetical cohort of adult thalassemia patients (both transfusion-dependent and non-transfusion-dependent). The model was populated with data from the Malaysian Thalassemia Registry, a clinical cohort study for prevalence and utility values, and published literature. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratios for the 18 to 29 and 30 to 39 age groups were USD 2951 and USD 3209 per quality-adjusted life-year gained, respectively. Conclusions Incorporating a ThalPN screening program into standard care is a cost-effective strategy. By facilitating early intervention, screening can prevent or slow irreversible disease progression, thereby improving health-related quality of life and potentially reducing long-term costs for this patient population. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Graphitic-shell-mediated interfacial bonding and MWCNT-enabled electrical percolation in superhard cBN composites

Abstract: Conductive superhard cubic boron nitride(cBN)-based composites are difficult to realize because conductive additives often weaken the covalent load-bearing framework. Microstructural, Raman, and transport analyses reveal strongly bonded cBN/diamond interfaces and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-connected carbon-rich pathways. Title: AI-enabled cyberbullying detection from a cyber-physical-social-thinking space integration perspective: Theories, technologies, and challenges
Abstract: Cyberbullying has emerged as a pervasive threat to digital well-being, evolving into a multidimensional phenomenon that spans multiple interconnected spaces. Despite significant progress in detection techniques, existing approaches predominantly rely on textual analysis, limiting their ability to capture the full spectrum of cyberbullying behaviors and contextual dependencies. To address this limitation, this study presents a systematic review with qualitative synthesis of AI-enabled cyberbullying detection through the lens of Cyber-Physical-Social-Thinking (CPST) space integration. Based on 120 included studies, the review develops three principal outputs. First, it develops a fusion-mechanism taxonomy of AI-enabled cyberbullying detection research across cyber, physical, social, and thinking dimensions, organizing how content, contextual, relational, behavioral, and cognitive information is combined to support more comprehensive and context-aware detection. Second, it establishes a quantitative and descriptive landscape of the reviewed literature across CPST-space coverage, modalities, model families, publication trends, social media platforms, dataset characteristics, and evaluation metrics. Third, it develops a four-level conceptual taxonomy that organizes cyberbullying-related information into observable evidence, latent states, behaviors, and outcomes. Building on this evidence-based output, the study synthesizes a CPST-based conceptual reference architecture that organizes heterogeneous data sources, feature representations, information-fusion strategies, and decision-making processes, while distinguishing the differing empirical maturity of the four spaces. The review further synthesizes state-of-the-art AI technologies, including natural language processing, computer vision, network analysis, affective computing, and multimodal learning, in relation to their roles in cross-space information integration. Title: Behavior of Children with Down Syndrome During Preventive Dental Care: An Observational Study
Source title: Pesquisa Brasileira em Odontopediatria e Clinica Integrada
Abstract: Objective: To compare behavior guidance techniques (BGTs) applied to children with and without Down Syndrome (DS) during preventive dental care. Material and Methods: This observational, cross-sectional study included 40 children aged 2-6 years with and without DS. The Melamed´s Modified Behavior Scale was evaluated during the preventive procedure and the Frankl's Behavior Rating Scale (FBRS) was classified after dental care. The BGTs applied were evaluated by direct observation. Friedman and Mann-Whitney U tests and Spearman's Correlation Coefficient were applied. Results: A total of 76 attempts were required to perform the dental procedure for children with DS and 42 for children without DS. Conclusion: There was a difference between groups in relation to the behavior evaluated by the physiological method. Authors: Geng J.; Zhang H.; Mao Y.; Chen Y.; Wang N.; Zhao Q.; Kang Y.; Hou Z.; Zhu L.
Title: Dislocation network-induced multiple deformation mechanisms enabling a near-α titanium alloy with high strength-ductility synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Overcoming the intrinsic strength-ductility trade-off remains a central challenge in developing advanced titanium (Ti) alloys, as conventional strengthening strategies invariably sacrifice ductility. Here, we propose a dislocation engineering strategy that deliberately constructs ordered dislocation networks in the TA18 alloy, achieving exceptional strength-ductility synergy. These ordered geometric architectures are robustly stabilized by sessile jogs originating from specific crystallographic interactions between <a> and <c+a> dislocations. During early deformation, the networks subdivide grains into fine deformable units, providing massive initial strain hardening by impeding mobile dislocations via the dislocation jog dragging effect. With progressive strain, inhomogeneous local stresses drive the sweeping out of jogs, dynamically transforming the static networks into glissile dislocation arrays and dense dislocation walls. This critical structural evolution triggers a fundamental transition to a “transport-dominated” plasticity regime, activating potent hetero-deformation-induced strengthening and indirect slip transfer. These findings establish a scalable paradigm for designing high-performance Ti alloys via dislocation architecture control. © 2026

Title: Resurgence of large-scale influenza A (H1N1) outbreaks: Modeling the interplay of transmission, loss of immunity, and vaccination
Abstract: Influenza is a highly transmissible respiratory virus that can cause devastating pandemics. The 2009 influenza pandemic, caused by a strain of A(H1N1) virus, resulted in millions of cases and hundreds of thousands of deaths worldwide. In the following years, many regions experienced waves driven by environmental conditions, waning immunity, and other factors. More dramatically, several locations saw unpredicted large resurgent outbreaks, yet the mechanisms behind these severe resurgences remain poorly understood. Despite an extensive literature of epidemic models aimed at explaining and predicting H1N1 dynamics, mathematical frameworks specifically designed to address why these large outbreaks recur years after an initial epidemic are still lacking. Here we address this gap by proposing a mechanistic model with time-varying rates of infection, loss of immunity, and vaccination. In particular, we explore two mathematical functions to model dynamic loss of immunity, capturing how viral evolution may reduce the duration of immune protection. Numerical simulations show that the model reproduces key features of H1N1 case data, and that delayed resurgence is associated with longer immunity periods and higher vaccine efficacy. We also fit the model to data from Brazil, Turkey, Iran, New Zealand, the United States, Colombia, South Africa, and Croatia, demonstrating its ability to capture resurgence patterns. Fitted infection rates exhibited a wide range of temporal profiles, from regular annual cycles to higher-frequency oscillations and gradual changes, suggesting that transmission is driven by factors beyond seasonal influences. The model also inferred dynamic loss-of-immunity rates, representing different effects of antigenic drift. To our knowledge, this is the first mechanistic modeling study specifically aimed at investigating large resurgent H1N1 epidemics across multiple locations. Our findings highlight the need for context-specific models and surveillance systems that account for the complex interplay among environmental drivers, population immunity, and viral mutation driving H1N1 dynamics. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Hu S.-G.; Liu Y.-Y.; Wang X.-X.; Wu Z.-H.
Title: Beyond positive attitude: What motivates stem undergraduates to engage in classroom discussions?
Abstract: Fostering active participation in classroom discussions remains a persistent challenge in higher education, particularly in STEM fields where lecture-based instruction remains prevalent. While positive attitudes are often considered an important predictors of participation in classroom discussions, this study examines a broader set of psychological factors associated with STEM undergraduates’ intention to participate in classroom discussions. We propose and test an integrated model incorporating attitude, subjective norms, perceived need, and self-efficacy. Using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) on data from 550 undergraduates from engineering-focused universities, the study examines the motivational factors associated with participation intention and willingness to recommend classroom discussions. Perceived need and self-efficacy showed the strongest statistical associations with both outcomes. Subjective norms were positively associated with participation intention but not willingness to recommend, whereas attitude did not demonstrate a significant unique effect in the full model. Additional analyses suggest that this pattern reflects the stronger explanatory role of perceived need when considered alongside students’ general evaluations of classroom discussions. These findings highlight the importance of perceived learning value and confidence in predicting students’ participation in classroom discussions and provide context-specific implications for discussion-based teaching in engineering education. Authors: Neog B.; Gogoi A.P.
Title: Landscapes of extraction: Youth, coal and contested livelihoods in Tinsukia, Assam
Abstract: The article explores the diverse and intersecting forms through which youth encounter, experience, and respond to coal mining in Tinsukia, Assam’s easternmost resource-rich district. Drawing on qualitative ethnographic fieldwork in the Ledo and Margherita coalfields, it examines how extractive economies reshape youth livelihoods, aspirations and vulnerabilities in a landscape marked by environmental devastation, informalization of labour, and uneven development The article focuses on three connected processes: the erosion of traditional livelihoods and ecological relations; entry into precarious and informal mining-related work; and the emergence of critique and resistance. Rather than treating youth as a homogeneous category, the article analyzes how their positions are not fixed but fluid. It shows how their positions differ according to access to land, labour, networks, and political resources, while also shifting between economic dependence, negotiation, and opposition. The article contributes to political ecology and extractive-frontier scholarship by foregrounding youth perspectives from a Northeast Indian coal belt and by showing how development is experienced simultaneously as livelihood opportunity and socio-environmental harm. Title: High-thermal-conductivity GFRP for dry-type air-core reactors: thermal-electrical performance and trade-off analysis
Abstract: Dry-type air-core reactors suffer from localized overheating due to the limited thermal conductivity of conventional glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) insulation. Enhancing the thermal conductivity of GFRP provides a potential approach for improving reactor heat dissipation; however, excessive incorporation of thermally conductive fillers may compromise electrical insulation reliability. This study establishes an integrated material-to-equipment evaluation framework to investigate the thermal-electrical trade-off of high-thermal-conductivity GFRP (HTC-GFRP) for dry-type air-core reactors. HTC-GFRP samples with different alumina contents were prepared, and their thermal conductivity, dielectric properties, AC flashover voltage, and breakdown strength were experimentally characterized. The results demonstrate that increasing alumina loading effectively enhances thermal conductivity by promoting the formation of thermally conductive pathways, whereas excessive filler incorporation leads to deterioration of insulation performance. Considering both thermal enhancement and electrical insulation reliability, a favorable thermal conductivity range of approximately 0.75–0.95 W/(m·K) was identified. Furthermore, multiphysics simulations of a 10 kV dry-type air-core reactor reveal that increasing the GFRP thermal conductivity from 0.35 to 1.3 W/(m·K) reduces the maximum operating temperature by approximately 3 °C. These results demonstrate the thermal-electrical trade-off of HTC-GFRP and provide quantitative guidance for balancing heat dissipation capability and insulation reliability in dry-type air-core reactors. © 2026

Title: Beyond transactions: Cultural role enactment, positive emotional response, and supportive behavioral intention in Northeast China
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Grounded in dramaturgical, performative identity, and cultural memory theories, this study develops and validates a three-dimensional measure of Cultural Role Enactment and examines its associations with emotional and supportive outcomes in rural bazaars (Ganji) in Northeast China. Positive Emotional Response is associated with stronger Affective Attachment and Supportive Behavioral Intention, while greater attachment is also related to stronger supportive intentions. Bootstrapped indirect effects support the theoretically specified associations, and Ganji Familiarity strengthens the association between Cultural Role Enactment and Positive Emotional Response. Abstract: Language learning strategies refer to deliberate behaviors, processes, and approaches through which learners receive, process, and use new information in a structured and purposeful manner, thereby promoting self-directed learning, self-regulation, and learner responsibility. Title: Correlations between cerebrospinal fluid and plasma levels of GABA, glutamate, dopamine, and related metabolites, and their concentrations across neurological disorders
Abstract: Background Neurotransmitters play critical roles in both central and peripheral nervous system function. However, the correlation between cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma levels of neurotransmitters remains incompletely understood, limiting the interpretation of peripheral measurements as surrogates for central neurochemical changes. This study aimed to investigate the correlations between CSF and plasma levels of GABA, glutamate, dopamine, and related metabolites, and to explore their expressions across common neurological disorders in a real-world clinical setting. Methods A total of 181 paired CSF and plasma samples from patients with neurological disorders and 67 plasma samples from healthy controls were analyzed. Concentrations of GABA, betaine, L-DOPA, histamine, glutamine, glutamate, dopamine, and choline were quantified using LC–MS/MS. Correlations between CSF and plasma concentrations were assessed using Pearson correlation analysis. Age- and sex-related effects were evaluated in healthy controls, and differences among disease groups were analyzed after classifying patients into neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs), CNS demyelinating diseases (CNS DDs), CNS tumors, and CNS infections. Results GABA, histamine, betaine, glutamate, and choline exhibited higher concentrations in plasma than in CSF, whereas glutamine concentrations were higher in CSF. Except for betaine and glutamate, all other neurotransmitters showed statistically significant but weak CSF–plasma correlations ( r = 0.15–0.7, p < 0.05). In healthy controls, plasma histamine, betaine, glutamate, and choline levels were higher in males. Plasma GABA levels in all disease groups were consistently lower than controls, and plasma glutamine levels in NDDs, CNS DDs, and CNS tumors were significantly higher than those in controls. By contrast, there were no significant differences in CSF levels among different disease groups, except that glutamate was higher in the CNS tumor group than in the other disease groups. Conclusions Most plasma neurotransmitters and their metabolites do not reliably reflect their CSF levels, which may provide important context for interpreting peripheral neurotransmitter biomarkers in CNS diseases. Title: Environmental risks of pest management practices in smallholder coconut plantations
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: Oryctes rhinoceros, the coconut rhinoceros beetle, remains one of the most damaging pests of coconut (Cocos nucifera) across South and Southeast Asia, the Pacific, and increasingly, new invasion fronts in the Americas. Although climatic alterations may redistribute the geographic footprint of the hazard, predictive assessments underscore non-linear and variable outcomes. Regional expansions in vulnerable or suitable extents are largely contingent upon the analytical scenario and structural parameters of the model utilized. This reinforces the case for treating its management as an environmental, not solely agronomic, concern. The study objectives were to characterize how smallholder-level management choices translate into differentiated environmental and health risk. Smallholder coconut plantations, which supply most world coconut production, are disproportionately exposed because of fragmented land holdings, limited capital, and constrained extension access. This review evaluates the translation of management interventions into distinct environmental and health hazards by systematically reviewing evidence on coconut rhinoceros beetle biology, intervention efficacy, smallholder socioeconomic dynamics, and insecticide risk literature through a standardized four-tier risk framework. Smallholders commonly rely on chemical control options such as organophosphates and pyrethroids. These options carry documented risks: non-target toxicity, soil and water contamination, and occupational exposure. In the absence of beetle-specific metrics, elevated occupational exposure risks are inferred from prevailing normative practices in smallholder agriculture concerning the omission of protective equipment. Biological and cultural alternatives include O. rhinoceros nudivirus, Metarhizium anisopliae, Bacillus thuringiensis, botanical larvicides, and pheromone-based trapping. These present a substantially lower environmental risk profile: laboratory bioassays report 90 to 100 percent larval mortality for Metarhizium isolates from East Java, comparable to the up to 98 percent larval and 90 percent adult mortality reported for a granular carbamate alternative, indicating technical efficacy is not the limiting factor, with field-deployed monitoring documented in Jepara and Bengkulu. Uptake of these lower-risk options is nonetheless constrained less by technical efficacy than by production economics, extension access, and the fragmented governance of smallholder replanting and pest-management programs. The evidence suggests that attenuating this risk burden is predominantly constrained by the disparity between existing lower-risk technological interventions and their operational uptake, among other compounding determinants. Risk-management strategies must therefore be designed around smallholder economic and institutional realities rather than efficacy data alone. Title: Intervening Impersistence on the St. Johns River, Florida

Title: Activating slightly stronger adsorbed CO2 on CeO2 with concentrated sunlight to enable ethylene and propylene synthesis
Abstract: Harnessing solar light to convert CO2 and H2O into multi-carbon (C2+) fuels constitutes a critical strategy toward achieving carbon neutrality. This necessitates the development of photocatalytic systems and catalysts capable of breaking the linear activity-selectivity trade-off, which ultimately rests on a fundamental understanding of the key factors controlling C1–Cn (n ≥ 2) coupling selectivity. Herein, with CeO2 and Pr6O11 selected as model catalysts, we clarify that the decisive factor governing C2+ production is interfacial CO2 adsorption strength/coverage, rather than interfacial photogenerated charge carrier density or H2O dissociation/adsorption. Therefore, a solar‑concentrating photocatalytic system was designed to activate slightly stronger adsorbed CO2 with high local coverage, ultimately achieving substantial generation of C2+ products by a *CO–free formaldehyde self–condensation pathway, whereas almost no multi‑carbon products were observed under conventional photocatalytic reaction systems. Intriguingly, within this system, CeO2, despite its inferior photoelectric response and H2O activation capability compared to Pr6O11 and the Pr6O11/CeO2 composite, delivered the highest C2+ yield and molar selectivity. Over 56 h, it produced 109.69 μmol of C2H4 (19.79%) and 31.0 μmol of C3H6 (5.59%). These findings establish that, in concentrated solar light catalytic systems, the formation of C1–Cn bonds is closely related to interfacial CO2 adsorption behavior, and that slightly stronger CO2 adsorption strength is clearly beneficial for the generation of C2+ products. This insight advocates a new design paradigm under concentrated solar catalytic systems, focused on modulating CO2 adsorption strength/coverage rather than that of the *CO intermediate, moving beyond the traditional practice of avoiding either strong or weak binding. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Cost-Utility Analysis of Sentinel Node Biopsy Versus Selective Neck Dissection for Node-Negative Early-Stage Oral Cancers: A Health Economic Evaluation from the Indian Healthcare System Perspective
Abstract: Objectives To conduct a cost-utility analysis comparing sentinel node biopsy (SNB) with selective neck dissection (SND) for clinically node-negative early-stage oral cancer from the Indian healthcare system perspective. Methods A hybrid decision-tree-Markov model compared SNB with SND over a 10-year horizon, incorporating 18 clinical pathways, time-trade-off utilities from an Indian population, and costs from Indian settings. Model and R code construction were assisted by a large language model (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) with author verification. Effectiveness was measured in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs). A lifetime-horizon scenario (cohort age 55-100; 45 cycles) confirmed SNB dominance with incremental cost −INR 5466 and incremental QALYs 0.1767. Results were robust across deterministic and scenario analyses. Conclusions SNB is a cost-effective alternative to SND for clinically node-negative early-stage oral cancer in Indian tertiary cancer centers with appropriate technical expertise, dominating in the deterministic base case and remaining cost-effective in 78.5% of probabilistic iterations at the India-specific threshold. Title: Stage-aware deep learning with adversarial data synthesis enables prospective season-scale A/H1N1 influenza forecasting in China
Abstract: Accurate influenza forecasting is essential for public health preparedness, yet many models require future covariates, provide limited interpretability, and degrade under post-pandemic regime shifts. We propose a Stage-Aware Multimodal Neural Network (SAMNN) that integrates multimodal temporal features using configurations adapted to heterogeneous transmission regimes and supports season-ahead scenario forecasting using adversarially synthesized covariates. Using 13 years of national A/H1N1 surveillance data from mainland China (2011∼2024), SAMNN was evaluated across three epidemiologically distinct seasons spanning ∼20-fold differences in peak intensity. SAMNN achieved R  2  values of 0.82–0.95, 0.82-0.97, and 0.55-0.97 for 1-week-, 2-week-, and 4-week-ahead forecasting, respectively, and generally maintained competitive performance relative to five baseline models across forecast horizons. SHAP attribution showed that epidemiological signals dominated predictions, with context-dependent contributions from climatic and social-context features. To support prospective scenario forecasting, we used an adversarial synthetic covariate-generation pipeline to produce season-ahead forecasts for 2024/25 using information available at the prespecified forecast origin. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: 40 years of equity sensitivity: A theoretical and meta-analytic review of relations, roles, and remaining questions
Abstract: Organizational scholars have studied equity sensitivity (ES) for nearly half a century. Yet, a lack of synthesis in the ES literature suggests important questions remain regarding our understanding of the concept, its nomological network, the theoretical role(s) it may play in shaping employee attitudes and behaviors, and its relations to adjacent theories of equity and organizational justice. In the current work, we address these questions via a theoretical and meta-analytic review of the ES literature encompassing 117 articles, 144 samples, and 36,177 participants. In synthesizing the literature, we (1) describe and alleviate existing tensions surrounding the construct's conceptualization, (2) provide empirical insights regarding the construct's associations and relative importance in the prediction of key workplace outcomes, and (3) present an integrative model of ES's potential theoretical moderating role in equity and justice relationships. Our work provides clarity regarding ES's nomological network and offers critical directions for future scholarship. Specifically, we draw special attention to opportunities for new work exploring ES's potential as a key linking mechanism among equity and organizational justice theories. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Microclimate shifts driven by Lake Urmia shrinkage and their implications for urban cooling demand and carbon emissions under future climate scenarios
Abstract: Lake Urmia, one of the world's largest hypersaline lakes, has experienced dramatic shrinkage over recent decades, raising concerns regarding its impacts on regional climate, urban thermal environments, and energy sustainability. This study investigates microclimate shifts driven by Lake Urmia desiccation and evaluates their implications for urban cooling demand and carbon emissions under future climate scenarios. An integrated framework combining multi-temporal remote sensing observations, climate data, urban thermal indicators, and energy-emission modeling was employed to quantify relationships among lake shrinkage, land surface temperature, urban heat island intensity, cooling demand, and carbon emissions. Results show that Lake Urmia's surface area declined from 5420 km2 in 1990 to 610 km2 in 2025, representing an 88.7% reduction. This hydrological decline was accompanied by substantial thermal amplification, with mean Land Surface Temperature increasing from 28.4°C to 36.4°C and maximum Land Surface Temperature rising from 34.8°C to 47.1°C. Vegetation degradation was also pronounced, with the mean Normalized Difference Vegetation Index decreasing from 0.46 to 0.23. Concurrent urban expansion intensified thermal stress, increasing surface urban heat island intensity from 1.8°C to 4.7°C in Urmia and from 2.1°C to 5.2°C in Tabriz. Correlation analysis revealed strong relationships between lake area and LST (R = −0.87), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and Land Surface Temperature (R = −0.81), Land Surface Temperature and Urban Heat Island intensity (R = 0.79), and LST and cooling demand (R = 0.84). Future climate projections indicate temperature increases of 1.4°C, 2.6°C, and 4.1°C by 2050 under the SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5 scenarios, respectively, resulting in projected increases in cooling demand of 18–36%. Given Iran's electricity sector's fossil-fuel dependence, rising cooling demand is expected to increase carbon emissions. These findings highlight Lake Urmia desiccation as a coupled hydro-climatic–urban-energy challenge requiring integrated restoration, climate adaptation, and sustainable energy strategies. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Ji L.; Chang Y.
Title: What prevents community gardens from long-term survival? A five-year case study in Suzhou, China
Abstract: Community gardens are increasingly recognised as important instruments of urban micro-regeneration, yet their long-term sustainability remains fragile under project-based governance. This study traces the five-year evolution (2021–2025) of maintenance barriers in a government-initiated community garden in Suzhou, China. Using a longitudinal mixed-methods design, this paper tracks the community garden across three stages (inception, growth and struggle) through three phases of Likert-scale surveys and semi-structured interviews, supplemented by Participatory Action Research (PAR). The findings reveal a marked divergence in barrier trajectories. Individual technical constraints declined as residents accumulated horticultural knowledge, with the mean score for ‘lack of gardening knowledge and skills’ falling from 4.00 in 2021 to 1.83 in 2025. By contrast, team and institutional barriers intensified: ‘lack of an internal leader’ rose from 4.07 to 4.83, ‘unclear garden tasks’ from 3.20 to 4.33, and ‘Inadequate support from local authorities’ from 3.53 to 4.83, reaching the ceiling value of 5.0 for several individual respondents in 2025. The withdrawal of external facilitators exposed a governance vacuum that residents themselves labelled the ‘Three-Ignores’ ( san-bu-guan ) condition, in which fragmented responsibilities among Residents’ Committees, Property Management Companies and Homeowners’ Committees, together with unfulfilled budgetary commitments, produced systemic deterioration. At the same time, a significant demographic shift towards a volunteer team composed exclusively of elderly residents weakened the garden’s collective resilience. Sustaining community gardens requires a shift in urban management from temporary ‘project logic’ to more durable ‘governance logic’, including formal exit strategies, clearer responsibility arrangements and the incorporation of community assets into established administrative and budgetary systems. Title: Hamiltonian dynamics of Boolean networks
Source title: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: This article examines the impact of Hamiltonian dynamics on the interaction graph of Boolean networks. Three types of dynamics are considered: maximum height, Hamiltonian cycle, and an intermediate dynamic between these two. The study addresses how these dynamics influence the connectivity of the graph and the existence of variables that depend on all other variables in the system. Additionally, a family of unate Boolean networks capable of describing these three Hamiltonian behaviors is introduced, highlighting their specific properties and limitations. The results provide theoretical tools for modeling complex systems and contribute to the understanding of dynamic interactions in Boolean networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Modeling the Relationship Between Physical Activity, Mental Health, and Cognitive Abilities with the Mediating Role of Perceived Social Support in Older Adults
Abstract: Objectives: Aging is one of the most significant demographic phenomena of the twenty-first century, and identifying factors affecting the physical and mental health of older adults is crucial. This study aimed to examine the relationship between physical activity, mental health, and cognitive abilities with the mediating role of perceived social support in older adults. Materials and Methods: This correlational descriptive study with path analysis was conducted among older adults aged 60 years and above (Mean = 67.63, SD = 6.02) in Sanandaj, Iran, in 2024. Using a convenience sampling method, 280 participants were recruited. Data were collected using the Physical Activity Questionnaire, the Quality of Life Questionnaire (mental health domain), the Cognitive Abilities Questionnaire, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. Data analysis was performed using SPSS-24 and AMOS-24. Results: Path analysis indicated that physical activity (Mean = 10.32, SD = 5.26) had significant direct effects on perceived social support (Mean = 40.87, SD = 11.33; β = 0.378, P < 0.001), cognitive abilities (Mean = 69.09, SD = 15.34; β = 0.351, P < 0.001), and mental health (Mean = 18.86, SD = 5.53; β = 0.189, P = 0.002). Cognitive abilities and mental health also had significant direct effects on perceived social support. Mediation analysis confirmed the significant mediating role of perceived social support in the relationships of cognitive abilities (β range = 0.061-0.453, 95% CI range [0.022- 0.573], P < 0.001) and mental health (β range = 0.054-0.153, 95% CI range [0.010-0.224], P < 0.001) with physical activity. Conclusions: These findings confirm that strengthening perceived social support can serve as a key mediating pathway that enhances the impact of mental health and cognitive abilities on physical activity among older adults. Perceived social support plays an important mediating role in amplifying the effects of physical activity on mental health and cognitive functioning in this population. Accordingly, health-promotion programs and public health policies should simultaneously focus on fostering supportive social interactions and encouraging regular physical activity in order to improve the psychological well-being and cognitive performance of older adults. © (2027), (Negah Institute for Social Research and Scientific Communication). Title: Consumer awareness, participation, and accessibility in sustainable electronic waste management
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid increase in electronic waste has created increasingly complex environmental and health challenges, especially in developing countries like Indonesia. The study objectives were to examine how household awareness and accessibility of electronic-waste management facilities are associated with consumer participation, controlling for socioeconomic factors, demographics, and the region's spatial characteristics. METHODS: This study uses a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design to examine household consumers living near electronic waste management facilities in Indonesia. To analyze the data, Spearman's rank correlation was employed to evaluate variable relationships, ordinary least squares regression to estimate the associations of awareness and accessibility with participation levels, Kruskal-Wallis test to examine group differences, and Geographic Information System-based spatial analysis to describe the spatial patterns of facility distance, accessibility, and electronic waste management participation. FINDINGS: Consumer awareness of the consequences of electronic waste showed a significant positive correlation with the intention to manage electronic waste, with a correlation coefficient of 0.340, but showed no significant correlation with actual behavior, with a correlation coefficient of only 0.067. Accessibility showed a significant positive correlation with both intention and actual behavior, with correlation coefficients of 0.197 and 0.416, respectively. Accessibility had the largest reported regression coefficient for actual behavior ( β = 0.449 ), followed by awareness of consequences ( β = 0.182 ). The Kruskal-Wallis test confirmed significant differences in intention and actual behavior across accessibility levels, with chi-square values of 11.67 and 35.91, respectively. Spatial analysis using the nearest neighbor method produced a nearest neighbor ratio of 0.60 with a z score of -10.01. Spatial analysis revealed that highly aware and active residents are significantly clustered rather than randomly dispersed, with the vast majority residing within a functional catchment area defined by 10 to 30 kilometer distances or 10 to 30 minute travel times from e-waste facilities. CONCLUSION: The findings underscore the need for electronic waste management policies that prioritise facility accessibility and spatially based approaches to strengthen community participation within a circular economy framework. Title: Comparative diagnostic utility of cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in multiple sclerosis
Abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis depends on clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data; the need for confirmatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers for differential diagnosis is a crucial step. Objective We aim to investigate and compare the diagnostic value of CSF markers (e.g., chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)) compared to the established supportive diagnostic oligoclonal bands test (OCBs) in MS. Methods We collected 62 CSF samples from suspected MS patients with T2-Hyperintense lesions and investigated OCBs and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for NfL, CHI3L1, and GFAP. Results The CSF levels of NfL ( p < 0.001) and CHI3L1 ( p < 0.001) were significantly elevated in the MS group compared to the non-MS group, in contrast to GFAP ( p = 0.17). Diagnostic criteria for MS diagnosis was excellent for OCBs (Area under curve (AUC) = 0.978, p < 0.001; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.929–1.000), good for CHI3L1 (AUC = 0.838, p < 0.001; 95% CI: 0.738–0.939), acceptable for NfL (AUC = 0.729, p = 0.003; 95% CI: 0.602–0.855) and poor for GFAP (AUC = 0.604, p = 0.173; 95% CI: 0.477–0.762). Conclusion Among the studied biomarkers, CHI3L1 showed potential as an adjunctive biomarker for discriminating MS from non-MS patients. Its diagnostic accuracy was higher than that of NfL in our cohort, but GFAP has limited diagnostic accuracy, which could restrict its use in MS diagnosis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Optimal timing for staged vaccination campaigns: Insights from scenario tree-based stochastic optimization
Abstract: We develop a mathematical modeling framework to address the challenge in launching an effective staged vaccination campaign during a typical viral infection season to avoid an overwhelmed healthcare system for the entire season. Using the COVID-19 pandemic following its acute phase as a motivating example, our model takes into account the willingness of the public to receive vaccines, as well as the uncertainty of vaccination delivery and administration, to achieve the objective of optimizing the timing and distribution of the vaccination campaign, subject to the constraint that hospitalized cases do not exceed healthcare capacity. The integration of a dynamic transmission model with a scenario tree–based stochastic optimization framework enables the evaluation of future scenarios characterized by uncertainty in vaccination rates, contact mixing, and public adherence to safety measures. Accounting for these future scenarios facilitates the identification of strategies to dynamically adjust the timing and scale of vaccine and contact mixing during distinct phases of the viral season. Our study demonstrates that a well–timed, well–phased vaccination campaign, along with other public health interventions, can prevent overcrowding in hospitalization in a typical viral infection season. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Analytic hierarchy process-based criterion weighting for water resources management projects
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Prioritizing water resources projects requires decision-makers to balance hydrological performance, engineering feasibility, environmental and social sustainability, and economic value under limited budgets and implementation resources. Conventional evaluation frameworks are frequently bound to specific project typologies or geographical contexts, thereby constraining their direct applicability across heterogeneous project portfolios. The study objectives were to develop an analytic hierarchy process-based multi-criteria decision-making framework for deriving criterion weights for water resources management project assessment, using Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as the empirical context. METHODS: The framework was developed by synthesizing water resources management principles, practical project-assessment considerations, and relevant multi-criteria decision-making literature. The evaluation model comprised four principal dimensions and 18 operational sub-criteria. The Analytical hierarchy process framework was employed to analyze expert judgments elicited from six senior water resources and irrigation specialists, each possessing a minimum of 20 years of professional experience. Individual judgments were subsequently evaluated for consistency and aggregated using the geometric mean. Local weights were calculated using the eigenvector method and combined with the corresponding main-dimension weights to obtain global priorities. FINDINGS: Engineering and Implementation Feasibility received the highest main-dimension weight (32.58 percent), followed by Economic performance (25.84 percent), Environmental and Social Sustainability (21.87 percent), and Water Resource and Hydrological Performance (19.71 percent). At the global level, cost effectiveness ranked first (13.99 percent), followed by Structural Scale (11.58 percent), Foundation Suitability (10.60 percent), and Storage and Hydrological Adequacy (8.93 percent). These four sub-criteria accounted for 45.10 percent of the total weight. Accounting for 81.88 percent of the total weight and encompassing elements across all four dimensions, the top 11 sub-criteria demonstrate that comprehensive assessment necessitates an integrated approach spanning technical, economic, hydrological, environmental, and social dimensions. CONCLUSION: By establishing a transparent architecture for criterion organization and context-specific priority derivation, the framework facilitates water resources project evaluation. Integrated with empirical performance data and explicit scoring protocols, it underpins the formulation of robust project screening, portfolio comparative analysis, and budgetary prioritization procedures. The reported weights represent the judgments of the study panel and should be recalibrated for other locations, project types, and stakeholder groups. Subsequent applications of this framework should formulate a structured operational scoring rubric while comprehensively evaluating parameter sensitivity, model robustness, and project-ranking stability. Title: Coupling composition design with defect engineering: An oxygen-doped Ti-Zr-Nb strain glass alloy with enhanced high-temperature shape memory effect
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-temperature shape memory alloys (HTSMAs) are critical for temperature-sensitive applications, yet the trade-off between high transformation temperatures and large recoverable strains remains a long-standing challenge. This study addresses this limitation by deploying a composition control and defect engineering strategy to regulate the martensitic transformation in HTSMAs via a strain glass while preserving elevated transformation temperatures. By introducing 1 at.% oxygen as point defects, a Ti47Zr47Nb5O1 strain glass alloy with a freezing temperature of about 462 K was fabricated. The microstructure consists of a strain‑glass‑dominated β matrix with minor residual α″ martensite. The low Nb content destabilizes the β phase, enabling the alloy to retain a high transformation temperature of about 745 K. Enabled by the strain glass state and the remarkable theoretical transformation strain derived from the addition of high-content Zr with large atomic radius, this alloy exhibits nearly full recoverability for pre‑strains up to about 5%, and achieves a shape memory recovery strain of ∼5.7% at a pre‑strain of 10%, outperforming most reported HTSMAs. Title: Robust incomplete multi-view clustering via adaptive similarity graph completion and dual-tensor decomposition
Abstract: Incomplete multi-view clustering (IMC) is crucial for real-world applications such as image retrieval, text classification, and subtype recognition, where multi-modal data frequently suffer from missing values and severe noise due to acquisition limitations or transmission losses. However, most existing methods rely on raw data completion, single-tensor constraints, and isolated multi-step processing paradigms. These approaches not only struggle to simultaneously preserve cross-view consistent principal components and filter out view-specific variations, but their phased nature also introduces irreversible error accumulation. To overcome these bottlenecks, this paper proposes a novel unified framework named Dual-Tensor Graph Completion for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering (DTGC-IMVC). Specifically, to eliminate reconstruction noise at the data feature level, an adaptive similarity graph completion mechanism is introduced to directly recover the similarity graph within the self-representation. Meanwhile, a dual-tensor architecture seamlessly integrating the tensor nuclear norm and the Schatten-p norm is constructed to rigorously capture high-order cross-view consistent features and effectively sparsify noise and view-specific components. Furthermore, a unified multi-source denoising strategy constrained by the L2,1-norm is introduced. Comprehensive experiments on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of clustering performance and robustness. Title: Strategic deployment of seasonal thermal energy storage for decarbonizing remote northern communities in Canada: A multidimensional evaluation framework
Abstract: Remote northern communities face major energy-transition challenges due to extreme climates, prolonged heating seasons, geographic isolation, dependence on imported fossil fuels, and limited energy infrastructure. Seasonal Thermal Energy Storage (STES) can address the mismatch between renewable heat availability and winter heating demand, but technology selection must account for environmental, geological, logistical, economic, and socio-technical constraints alongside conventional engineering performance. This review evaluates seven STES technologies using a northern-specific multidimensional framework integrating thermodynamic performance, technical maturity, economic performance, constructability and logistics, permafrost compatibility, and community implementation capacity. The framework operationalizes this assessment through non-compensable feasibility screening and TOPSIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis using a literature-informed technology-performance matrix, an equal-weight reference, two contrasting northern deployment archetypes, and weight- and score-sensitivity analyses. Results show that suitability depends on the interaction between technology characteristics and deployment context rather than engineering performance alone. Tank Thermal Energy Storage (TTES) exhibits the most robustly favourable profile across the evaluated scenarios and sensitivity analyses, whereas Pit Thermal Energy Storage (PTES), Borehole Thermal Energy Storage (BTES), and Rock Thermal Energy Storage (RTES) are more context dependent. Phase Change Material (PCM) and Thermochemical Energy Storage (TCES) offer high theoretical storage potential but remain limited by large-scale operational validation, while Aquifer Thermal Energy Storage (ATES) is conditional on suitable hydrogeological conditions. The proposed framework shifts STES selection from performance-based ranking toward context-driven decision support, providing developers, utilities, engineering practitioners, and community decision-makers with a transparent and reproducible methodology for identifying robust candidates, context-sensitive alternatives, and critical deployment constraints before detailed site-specific assessment in northern Canada and other circumpolar regions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Two pathways at once: An investigation of how reactance and ethicality shape student learning with AI
Abstract: Generative AI tools promise to expand student agency in management education, yet the same tool can help and hurt learning inside a single classroom. We argue this contradiction is the signature of two psychological pathways running in parallel. Drawing on the cognitive-affective-conative framework, we develop a dual-pathway serial mediation model in which a cognitive pathway runs from psychological reactance through autonomy perceptions to effectiveness judgments, while an affective pathway runs from ethical perceptions through emotional engagement to effectiveness judgments. Ninety-seven undergraduate management students participated in two AI-enhanced activities with different chatbot tools across one semester. Both pathways operated as predicted. More surprising was how the cognitive pathway changed across exposures. At first use, reactance traveled through autonomy, consistent with self-determination theory. By the second activity, reactance bypassed autonomy and suppressed effectiveness directly. The affective pathway remained stable across exposures. For management educators, ethical framing before a student's first AI encounter may do more work than redesigning the tools themselves to preserve student choice. As a single-cohort study using two researcher-built chatbots, the results are preliminary and point to hypotheses for multi-site replication rather than population estimates. © 2026

Authors: Zhao W.; Zhang B.; Wang Y.; Li B.; Liu K.
Title: Mitigating feature degradation in deep Forward–Forward networks
Abstract: The Forward–Forward (FF) algorithm is a promising alternative to Backpropagation (BP) using layer-wise optimization. However, due to its local learning nature, FF suffers from feature degradation, which can be more severe than in BP for deep networks. To bridge this gap, we propose Sustained Forward (SF), which employs a dual-mechanism approach to achieve sustained feature propagation. Specifically, Cross-layer Gradient Momentum (CGM) propagates cross-layer gradient momentum to enrich the learning signal, and Local Feature Reconstruction (LFR) reconstructs local features to compensate for information loss. Extensive experiments on common benchmarks demonstrate that SF achieves significant performance improvements (e.g., over 6% on CIFAR-100), substantially narrowing the gap to BP. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Resilience Optimization Strategy for Cyber-Physical Distribution Systems Under Coordinated Fake-Base-Station and Physical Attacks
Abstract: Driven by the deployment of intelligent terminals and advanced communication technologies, modern distribution networks have fundamentally evolved into cyber-physical distribution systems (CPDSs). Consequently, these systems face an escalating exposure to sophisticated, coordinated cyber-physical attacks. To address this critical vulnerability, a tri-level defender-attacker-operator optimization model is proposed in this paper to enhance CPDS resilience against coordinated fake-base-station (FBS) and physical attacks. The coordinated attack process is modeled by jointly considering physical line disruptions, cyber-induced RCS communication failures, and their coupled impact on post-attack self-healing. To render the resulting complex tri-level formulation computationally tractable, a hybrid framework is developed, which integrates an improved column-and-constraint generation method with M²SITRI. Comprehensive simulations conducted on modified IEEE 33-node and IEEE 123-node distribution test systems verify both the effectiveness of the proposed resilience-enhancement model and the computational efficiency of the hybrid solution method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based predictive model for prognosis in cerebral hemorrhage patients after hyperbaric oxygen therapy
Abstract: (Figure presented.) Intracerebral hemorrhage is a common and critical neurological emergency, and the inconsistent results of hyperbaric oxygen therapy make predicting outcomes challenging. Therefore, a reliable predictive model for outcomes is needed to improve treatment plans. This study used interpretable machine learning to determine key risk factors linked to adverse outcomes in cerebral hemorrhage patient post-hyperbaric oxygen therapy. To improve prognostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making, we analyzed the data from 401 patients with intracerebral hemorrhage who received hyperbaric oxygen therapy at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jiaxing, China, using multivariate logistic regression and machine learning to develop predictive models, with model performance assessed via 10-fold cross-validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations values aided in model interpretation and in the development of a logistic regression-based nomogram. Based on the modified Rankin scale, patients were stratified into two prognostic groups: a good prognosis group (modified Rankin scale < 3, n = 265) and a poor prognosis group (modified Rankin scale ≥ 3, n = 136). Significant differences in various factors were observed between the groups. Independent risk factors identified included the Glasgow coma scale score, computed tomography hemorrhage volume, activities of daily living score, treatment modality, intraventricular bleeding, and rebleeding. Among the models tested, the random forest algorithm yielded the highest predictive performance (the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.99). The study identified key predictors, including activities of daily living score, computed tomography hemorrhage volume, and Glasgow coma scale score, as factors influencing hyperbaric oxygen therapy outcomes in intracerebral hemorrhage patients. Random Forest model demonstrated strong predictive capability, with SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis providing insights into individual risk factors. Overall, these findings are crucial for improving clinical decision-making and personalized treatment. © 2026 Medical Gas Research

Authors: Cherif R.; Lawton P.
Title: Spatial analysis of the 15-minute city concept in three historically distinct urban areas across metropolitan greater Cairo
Abstract: This paper explores how the 15-min city concept plays out in Greater Cairo by examining three neighbourhoods: Agouza, Madinaty, and Badya. To do so, it draws on a systematic approach that includes selecting case studies, identifying key service categories, extracting POI and street-network data, mapping service areas in ArcGIS, and presenting the results through service area analysis and thematic mapping. To complement this, accessibility was assessed through four measures: cumulative opportunities, land-use entropy, functional redundancy, and space syntax (integration) metrics. The findings show that access in Cairo depends not just on distance but also on the diversity of available services, the degree of proximity between services, and the way streets connect different areas. Cycling makes a clear difference in widening reach and reducing accessibility inequalities and fragmentation. The findings suggest that, in addition to clinics and schools, social anchors such as souqs, ahwa, and cultural places emerge as vital parts of daily urban life. The paper argues that in Cairo, the 15-min city concept, whether built from scratch or adapted to existing urban fabrics, should not be treated as a universal recipe but as a flexible framework. The concept is part of a longer lineage of planning ideals, adopted in the planning of several areas of Cairo, from the Garden City movement to New Urbanism. It should build on the city’s own urban vocabularies, shaped through layered urban planning and lived experiences, which continue to define how urban spaces and services are used and valued within the 15-min radius or beyond. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Xu J.-J.; He X.-Q.; Chen Z.-S.; Lin M.-Q.
Title: Ghost-ResDSCNet:lightweight residual depthwise separable convolution with spatial pyramid pooling for power quality disturbance classification
Abstract: The increasing complexity of power quality disturbances (PQDs) calls for lightweight yet accurate classification methods suitable for edge deployment. This paper proposes Ghost-ResDSCNet, a multi-scale deep network that first converts voltage signals into time–frequency spectrograms via short-time Fourier transform. A residual depthwise separable convolution backbone performs efficient feature extraction, Ghost modules reduce computational cost by cheap feature generation, and a spatial pyramid pooling module captures multi-scale contextual information. On a 21-class synthetic PQD dataset, Ghost-ResDSCNet achieves an average accuracy of 99.34% on clean signals, along with 99.26%, 99.11%, and 95.80% under 40 dB, 30 dB, and 20 dB SNR respectively, with only 0.12M parameters, outperforming MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet. On a real-world five-class dataset, it attains 100.00% accuracy on clean and 40dB signals, and 99.96% and 94.02% under 30dB and 20dB SNR. Grad-CAM++ visualization confirms that the model focuses on physically interpretable time–frequency regions. The results demonstrate an effective trade-off among accuracy, robustness, and efficiency for real-time PQD monitoring in edge computing. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Reconciling rheology, stretchability and thermal conductivity in thermal interface materials through dynamic polymer interactions and multimodal filler networks
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Thermal interface materials (TIMs) used for heat dissipation of high-power electronics must combine good dispensability, high stretchability, and high thermal conductivity to maintain efficient heat dissipation during assembly and thermo-mechanical cycling. However, achieving these properties in one system remains challenging because the high filler loadings needed for efficient heat transport typically increase viscosity and reduce stretchability. Here, we report a polyurethane-siloxane TIM that integrates dynamic polymer interactions with a multimodal aluminum filler network to overcome this trade-off. Disulfide exchange and abundant urethane hydrogen bonding promote rapid stress relaxation and network rearrangement, while ternary particle-size-graded aluminum fillers improve packing efficiency and interparticle contact, forming effective thermal conduction pathways. As a result, the TIM exhibits low viscosity (234.13 Pa s), pronounced thixotropic behavior, high stretchability (elongation at break of 304.58%), and high thermal conductivity (8.13 W m−1 K−1). Integrating the TIM into a chip, we demonstrate the reduced operating temperature and thermo-mechanical reliability of the chip under cyclic and prolonged operation. This design offers a promising strategy for next-generation TIMs requiring both processability and mechanical reliability. © 2026

Authors: Lu T.; Liu H.; Wang T.; Sun K.; Lin T.; Jia Z.; Wang H.; Yu S.; Song Y.; Zhang X.
Title: Toward ammonia-to-NOx ratio control in an ammonia/diesel dual direct-injection engine under low-load conditions
Abstract: An excessive ammonia-to-NOx ratio (ANR) under low-load operation poses a challenge to the efficient operation of aftertreatment systems in ammonia-fueled engines. In this study, experiments were conducted on a single-cylinder ammonia/diesel dual direct-injection (DDI) engine to investigate the effects of ammonia substitution ratio (ASR), intake pressure, dual-fuel injection pressure, and injection timing (−28 to −12°CA ATDC) on NH3 emissions, NOx emissions, and the ANR under a low-load condition of 4 bar indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP). The results show that increasing ASR is the dominant factor driving the increase in the ANR. When the ASR was maintained below 60%, coordinated optimization of intake pressure, dual-fuel injection pressure, and injection timing under the late diesel injection strategy reduced the ANR to 1.1–1.25 while maintaining a high indicated thermal efficiency (ITE), thereby reducing the ANR to a level compatible with the efficient operating window of the aftertreatment system, and engine-out N2O emissions showed no evident deterioration. Furthermore, by substantially advancing diesel injection timing (−340 to −220°CA ATDC) to establish a thermally favorable in-cylinder environment before ammonia combustion, the ANR could be further reduced to below 1.0. However, a trade-off between ASR and ITE together with a marked increase in engine-out N2O emissions was observed under this strategy. The study systematically elucidates the regulation characteristics of key combustion control parameters on the ANR under low-load conditions and proposes practical ANR control strategies for ammonia/diesel DDI engines. The findings provide new insights into the optimization of ammonia utilization and energy conversion efficiency, and offer useful guidance for in-cylinder combustion control with aftertreatment requirements in ammonia-fueled engines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jiang Q.; Zhao X.-L.; Zhang H.; Wu W.-H.; Ng M.K.
Title: A convolutional low-rank continuous tensor representation for multi-dimensional data recovery
Abstract: Convolutional low-rank methods have been widely used in image processing and computer vision due to their ability to capture local spatial structure. However, existing convolutional low-rank methods are limited to rectangular meshgrids at a fixed scale, which restricts their applicability to emerging real-world spatial-irregular data, such as semantic spatial sub-regions and spatial transcriptomics. To overcome this limitation, we propose a convolutional low-rank tensor representation for spatial arbitrary-shape multi-dimensional data. Specifically, by representing the latent tensor through an implicit neural representation, we impose a new tensor nuclear norm (low-rank regularization) on the sampled domain by inferring the inside/outside data entries and develop a new ARbiTrary-shape Convolutional Tensor Nuclear Norm (ART-CTNN). Compared with classic convolutional low-rank tensor representations, ART-CTNN offers two key advantages: it unifies the exploration of the convolutional low-rank prior for spatial arbitrary-shape data, and it can exploit convolutional low-rankness at arbitrary resolutions beyond the original sampling grid, allowing regularization at a suitable scale. Extensive experiments on both regular and irregular datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the recovery performance of complex spatial details and structures, while further enhancing downstream clustering performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Enhancing accounting students’ writing performance through problem-based learning: Evidence from a vocational higher education context
Abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) has gained momentum in English for specific purpose (ESP) education, yet little is known about how PBL functions in vocational higher education settings for accounting for students' writing. This study investigated the effectiveness, benefits, and challenges associated with accounting students' writing performance. This study employs a mixed-methods design involving 60 students from one of the state polytechnics in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. The experimental group (N=30) experienced PBL, and the control group (N=30) received conventional learning. Data were collected through writing tests to investigate students' improvement in their writing performance, and interviews to explore students' perceptions of benefits and challenges. The results of the writing test were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics via SPSS, and the interview results were analyzed using thematic analysis. The quantitative results reveal that there is a significant difference in the writing performance of accounting students who were taught by using PBL and those who were taught by using conventional learning, with PBL being better than conventional learning. It can be concluded that PBL is effective at enhancing accounting students' writing performance. The qualitative results of the interviews revealed that the accounting students mentioned the benefits of PBL, including improvement in students' writing skills, development of students' problem-solving skills, development of students' critical thinking, team collaboration, and real accounting problem connections. However, they listed the challenges of PBL, which include difficulty relating to the varied ideas and a lack of experience with the problems. Future research is recommended to extend the study duration to better capture the lasting impacts of PBL, offering a more comprehensive understanding of this approach. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Title: Enhanced adaptive SRF-PLL-based robust synchronization and control of grid-integrated PV-battery systems for seamless mode transition under distorted grid conditions
Abstract: Synchronization problems, harmonic distortion, and power regulation problems are likely to occur in grid-integrated SPVA-BES microgrids serving nonlinear loads due to changing grid conditions. A dual-mode approach, EAFF-SRF-PLL, has been introduced for the grid-integrated SPVA-BES microgrid, which operates in both grid-connected and standalone modes. In the synchronization loop, adaptive gain scheduling, along with a frequency feed-forward estimation technique, has been used to maintain phase-locking capability under distorted, unbalanced, and nonlinear grid conditions. A supervisory energy management strategy controls the BDDC and grid-connected VSC based on the battery SOC status and BES availability. The performance of the controller is tested under harmonic distortion, varying loads, irradiation, unbalanced voltages, frequency deviations, PV unavailability, and mode transitions. The results of CHIL experiments employing an STM32F407G-DISC1 controller with an OPAL-RT OP4512 real-time simulator include the following: a synchronization time of 5 ms, a phase ripple of 0.78%, and a grid current total harmonic distortion of 2.7%. Compared with traditional SRF-PLL and DDSRF-PLL, the proposed algorithm achieves better synchronization accuracy and transient response. Authors: Si L.; Li L.; Yuan W.; Ma Z.
Title: Link prediction in multiplex social networks based on information transmission graph neural networks
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: Social networks are omnipresent graph-structured data where entities and interactions between them can be modeled as nodes and edges, respectively. In recent years, graph neural networks (GNNs) have evolved as a mainstream and powerful model for handling graph data. Link prediction, which can foretell missing or potential links, is a crucial task in social network analysis. However, most existing methods focus on monolayer networks and usually ignore that multiplex networks have richer information, which often results in poor performance on link prediction. Therefore, this paper proposes an information transmission-based GNN (IT-GNN) model for link prediction in multiplex social networks. IT-GNN first learns the representation of each node in a multiplex network from itself and its neighborhood. Specifically, the neighborhood information of a node is learned from its 1-, 2- and 3-hop neighbors in combination with the three new ways of information transmission. Then, the embedding of a node pair is obtained based on these representations. In this regard, the final representations of potential links in the target layer, which are used to determine the existence of potential links, are generated by fusing their embeddings from all layers. Extensive experiments on seven real-world networks demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed model. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: Impacts of tourism development on residents’ quality of life: A dual spillover perspective
Abstract: Tourism development can influence residents’ quality of life through bottom-up spillover (i.e., mediation) across life domains and through spatial spillover across regions. However, existing research has not integrated these micro and macro perspectives. This study develops an innovative theoretical framework to account for both spillover effects simultaneously. Using a constructed panel dataset from England and Wales, which integrates national longitudinal survey data, tourism statistics, socioeconomic indicators and geographic information, we apply dynamic spatial lag X panel models to verify the above framework. Results indicate that tourism development affects overall life satisfaction only indirectly, through spatial spillover effects mediated by different life domains, depending on the tourism indicators employed, underscoring the complexity of its impacts and the need for multifaceted tourism policymaking. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Transformational entrepreneurship education in the AI era: Reframing entrepreneurial readiness through AI literacy and digital entrepreneurial capability
Abstract: Artificial intelligence integration is reshaping entrepreneurship education and increasing the need for pedagogical approaches that prepare students to act under digital uncertainty. Drawing on Transformational Learning Theory, Growth Mindset Theory, and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examines how Transformational Entrepreneurship Education and AI Literacy contribute to Entrepreneurial Readiness directly and through Digital Innovation Skills and Digital Growth Mindset, the complementary dimensions through which Digital Entrepreneurial Capability is conceptually expressed. Survey data from 698 Indonesian university students were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, followed by semi-structured interviews with 24 students. The findings show that Transformational Entrepreneurship Education was positively related to AI Literacy, Digital Innovation Skills, Digital Growth Mindset, and Entrepreneurial Readiness. AI Literacy was also positively related to both capability dimensions and Entrepreneurial Readiness. Both dimensions significantly mediated the relationships of Transformational Entrepreneurship Education and AI Literacy with Entrepreneurial Readiness, while the corresponding direct effects remained significant. Qualitative findings showed that reflective AI engagement, iterative experimentation, feedback, and persistence supported capability development, whereas passive AI reliance and limited scaffolding constrained capability translation.
