Authors: Setyowati M.S.; Hanum R.K.
Title: The effect of agricultural taxes and local agricultural policies on enhancing food security and environmental sustainability
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Indonesia is currently working towards sustainability in line with Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger). Anticipated demographic growth to 10.8 billion by the year 2050 is expected to place unprecedented strain on global food security and production systems. The study objectives were to examine the biophysical factors, production inputs, economic conditions, socio-technological factors, agricultural business management, and agricultural tax policies regional agricultural policies and, ultimately, agricultural productivity. METHODS: This quantitative study employed structured questionnaires administered to a sample of 200 farmers in Surabaya. The instrument used a one-to-five Likert scale covering biophysical factors, economic factors, tax policy, tax morale, and agricultural productivity. Data was analyzed using partial least squares-structural equation modeling version 3. The analytical procedure comprised three distinct phases: first, evaluating the outer model for convergent and discriminant validity; second, conducting reliability assessments; and third, testing the inner model via bootstrapping to determine the coefficient of determination, the effect size, and hypothesis significance. Hypothesis significance was determined using t-statistic values of at least 1.96 and p-values of no more than 0.05. FINDINGS: Four hypotheses were rejected: economic factor on regional agricultural policy (p-value 0.557), agricultural taxation policy on tax morale (p-value 0.072), tax awareness on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.058), and tax morale on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.208). The findings reveal that regional agricultural policies are substantially driven by three key dimensions: biophysical factors (beta coefficient of 0.251, probability value of 0.000), production inputs (beta coefficient of 0.253, probability value of 0.002), and agricultural business management (beta coefficient of 0.228, probability value of 0.007). Agricultural tax policy significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.229, probability value of 0.000), while tax administration efficiency also significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.345, probability value of 0.000) and tax morale (beta coefficient of -0.634, probability value of 0.000), since clarity on procedures, benefits, and regulations fosters public responsibility and awareness of taxpayer obligations and rights. CONCLUSION: Elevating agricultural output demands comprehensive frameworks characterized by active farmer participation, supportive regulatory policies, targeted outreach regarding tax frameworks, and enhanced coordination between industry stakeholders and governmental bodies. Regional agricultural policies and tax awareness significantly influence agricultural productivity. These findings offer practical insights for policymakers aiming to strengthen agricultural governance and tax compliance frameworks in support of sustainable rural development. Title: Moral responsibilisation in destination management: The strategic framing of civic practices by DMOs
Abstract: This paper examines moral responsibilisation as an emerging destination governance mechanism through which destination management organisations (DMOs) and local stakeholders mobilise visitors to support sustainability goals. Drawing on an intrinsic qualitative case study of the Danish DMO, Wonderful Copenhagen , we develop a practice theory-based model showing that responsibilisation extends beyond narrative persuasion to include the organisational and material reframing of civic conduct. Analysis of interviews, participant observation, documents, and netnography identifies four interrelated stages: interpellation, involvement, intervention, and institutionalisation. Together, these stages connect inspirational messaging with participatory experiences, reward schemes, and decentralised service design. The findings also reveal tensions around the relevance, inclusivity, and feasibility of emerging civic practices. Resistance to responsible subject positions stems from stakeholders’ differing interpretations, negotiations, and disengagement from DMO-prescribed roles. The study advances the understanding of responsibilisation as a practice-based mode of governance and offers insights that may inform destination managers in varied tourism contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: DNA authentication of shark meat products from a major Chinese e-commerce platform reveals trade-name opacity and traceability limitations
Abstract: Shark meat products are subject to a variety of regulatory and conservation frameworks, yet their characterization at the retail level is often constrained by the use of umbrella terms and limited species-specific information. In this context, the present study was designed as an exploratory case study examining shark meat products commercialized through a major Chinese e-commerce platform within a defined sampling period. Product descriptions, labeling information (including trade name, processing type, product presentation, declared production origin, and price), and molecular species identification obtained through DNA barcoding were jointly examined to characterize shark-derived products marketed through the platform. A total of 63 products were screened, and 165 tissue samples were analysed using COI and cytb markers. All products were marketed under generic umbrella terms, without scientific nomenclature, and prepackaged products showed variable labeling completeness. Molecular analyses detected at least one shark taxon in 61 of the 63 products examined, whereas the remaining two products contained billfish and batoid taxa. At the tissue level, 160 of 165 samples (97%) were assigned to shark taxa. Across all analysed samples, molecular identification revealed 12 species-level taxa, comprising 10 shark species (Alopias pelagicus, A. superciliosus, Carcharhinus brevipinna, C. limbatus, C. sorrah, Galeocerdo cuvier, Isurus oxyrinchus, Mustelus griseus, Prionace glauca, and Sphyrna lewini), one batoid species (Rhynchobatus australiae), and one billfish species (Istiophorus platypterus), together with three genus-level assignments including shark and billfish taxa (Scoliodon sp., Carcharhinus sp., and Kajikia sp.). The identified taxa include species listed as Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, and Critically Endangered according to the IUCN Red List. The two products containing non-shark taxa represented cases of non-conformity between molecular identity and the available product information and therefore warrant discussion in relation to labeling practices. Overall, the findings illustrate the utility of molecular approaches for documenting species composition in online retail settings and provide an exploratory baseline for future investigations into species-level transparency, product information practices, and shark product commercialization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Pastoral Nomads at a Crossroads: Investigating the Resilience of the Bakarwal Community to Climate and Socio-Ecological Challenges
Abstract: Environmental shifts influence the livelihoods of Bakarwal pastoral nomads as they traverse the varied terrains of the Western Himalayas. Climate fluctuations and socio-ecological stressors markedly affect their resilience. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study examines how environmental factors and livelihood pressures interact among these nomads. By integrating scientific analysis of long-term climate patterns with qualitative data from 239 Bakarwal families, the research investigates their adaptive strategies and internal capacity. Results show that a 1 °C rise in winter and early summer temperatures, coupled with decreased rainfall in winter and transit habitats, affects mobility and resource availability, including fodder and water. The study highlights the importance of traditional knowledge, flexible transhumance practices, and eco-friendly methods in enhancing resilience. However, socio-ecological challenges, including limited institutional support and marginalization, threaten the sustainability of their pastoral lifestyle. The research situates livelihood resilience within the dynamic interactions of environmental and cultural systems. By simultaneously evaluating climate and socio-ecological factors, it affirms the enduring value of traditional wisdom and the resilience of pastoral systems in preserving ecological integrity and fostering sustainable development. It underscores the need for inclusive, community-driven policies and adaptive strategies to strengthen resilience and sustain pastoral livelihoods. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Touchable cultural heritage: How alternative touch experience facilitates visitors’ cultural inheritance behavior
Abstract: Touch is a fundamental human need, yet in cultural heritage tourism, it is strictly restricted to protect fragile artifacts. While essential for preservation, touch restrictions limit multi-sensory experience and impede deeper cultural participation. This research addresses this touch dilemma by introducing alternative touch experiences, wherein tourists touch surrogate objects (e.g., artifact replicas) that simulate the haptic attributes of authentic artifacts. Across four studies with qualitative, experimental, and field evidence, we found that alternative touch experiences enhance tourists’ psychological closeness to heritage, which in turn fosters cultural inheritance intentions and actual behaviors (e.g., cultural learning, cultural knowledge sharing, and donation to protect heritage). However, this touch effect diminishes when artifacts carry negative (vs. positive) superstitious associations. These findings offer a new theoretical perspective on enabling embodied experience within the traditionally sensory-restricted context, and highlight the role of sensory engagement in facilitating heritage appreciation and cultural inheritance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Sustainable urban planning in conflict-affected cities: Governance, displacement, and hierarchical sustainability in Marib, Yemen
Abstract: Sustainable urban planning frameworks presuppose institutional stability and regulated development, yet their applicability to conflict-affected cities remains theoretically underexamined. This qualitative case study examines how sustainability is interpreted and prioritised in Marib city, Yemen, an urban centre experiencing rapid growth amid armed conflict and mass internal displacement. Drawing on a framing analysis of global sustainability frameworks, semi-structured interviews with 16 city stakeholders, and structured observations in seven neighbourhoods, the study identifies a structural mismatch between global sustainability paradigms and local planning practice. Whereas international models assume balanced domain integration, the evidence from Marib reveals a context-conditioned hierarchy in which governance capacity and essential service provision operate as preconditions structuring environmental management, economic activity, and technological uptake. Locally, environmental sustainability is reduced to basic service continuity; social sustainability is dominated by displacement-driven absorptive pressures; economic sustainability narrows to livelihood survival; and technological adoption is fragmented and institutionally constrained. The paper advances a context-conditioned, hierarchical model of urban sustainability that challenges the implicit universality of parallel-domain planning approaches and calls for planning paradigms that recognise institutional capacity as foundational in fragile urban contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Revisiting the Agropastoral Landscape of Çatalhöyük East Through Agent-Based Modeling (9100–8100 BP)
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Understanding the complex interplay between external climatic forcing and internal socioecological dynamics remains a major challenge in the study of early sedentary societies. While unilinear frameworks frequently link systemic shifts to external climate triggers, these perspectives tend to neglect the internal dynamics and non-linear feedback loops of complex socioecological systems (SES). This research sheds new light on established narratives by investigating the 1000-year coevolution of agropastoral practices and landscape dynamics at Çatalhöyük East (ca. 9100–8100 BP). We employ a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM), integrating the MedLanD (MML) platform with the Macrophysical Climate Model (MCM) via an original sequential simulation design. This methodological novelty allows us to quantify how cumulative land-use legacies and their environmental costs shaped the community’s later options. Our results indicate that while the agricultural strategy effectively sustained high population density, it simultaneously pushed the system toward a rigidity trap. The model demonstrates how short-term adaptive successes generate structural limits in landscape capacity. These findings suggest that the settlement’s eventual reorganization was not a simple response to external climatic forcing but rather an emergent outcome of internal socioecological stress. By reframing the trajectory of Çatalhöyük through a complex systems lens, this study emphasizes that resilience must be understood as a dynamic process shaped by the long-term interaction of human agency and landscape evolution. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Forte M.; Ortoleva J.K.
Title: Performing Power and Transitional Space: the Use of Acoustics and Multimodal AI in Etruscan Painted Tombs
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: This article presents a new multimodal AI and acoustic methodology using two 5th c. BCE Etruscan painted tombs at Tarquinia, Italy, the Tomba del Gallo and the Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri as case studies. Via the integration of AI computer vision–based visual saliency analysis, architectural affordance modelling, acoustic data, and agent-based perceptual trajectories, the study suggests that each tomb affords distinct experiential strategies. The Tomba del Gallo privileges visual sequencing, threshold control, and gaze discipline, whereas the Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri potentially induces perceptual disorientation and immerses the visitor into a sensory and spatial environment that has the possibility of inducing trance-like experiences. A central contribution of the study is the reinterpretation of subterranean funerary spaces as possible transitional spaces, where architectural and symbolic devices mediate between life and death, order and chaos, memory and transformation, and sensory manipulation operate as core ritual technologies. Ultimately, we argue that when combined with scientifically documented acoustic data, AI enables archaeology to move beyond representational interpretation toward the experimental modelling of ritualised experiences in the ancient Mediterranean. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Adaptive ADMM-based optimal power flow for distribution systems via dynamic penalty strategy
Abstract: To mitigate voltage fluctuations caused by intermittent distributed generation (DG), this paper proposes a reactive power optimization strategy based on an Improved Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (I-ADMM). The model coordinates switchable capacitor banks (SCBs), on-load tap changers (OLTCs), and the reactive power capabilities of DGs to balance voltage quality and active power losses. Simulation results on the IEEE 33-bus system show that the proposed I-ADMM reduces total voltage deviation by 18.71% and 25.94%, and decreases branch losses by 9.51% and 10.67% compared with T-ADMM and C-OPF, respectively. In addition, a multi-period validation under time-varying DG and load conditions shows that the proposed method maintains effective performance across representative operating periods while preserving voltage security. Additional validation on a modified IEEE 69-bus system further confirms the scalability of the proposed method. These results demonstrate improved computational efficiency and the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive penalty strategy for distributed OPF under representative time-varying operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang H.; Shan Q.; Zhang J.; Xiao P.; Liu A.
Title: An audio-visual fusion emotion generation model based on neuroanatomical alignment
Abstract: In the field of affective computing, traditional methods for generating emotions predominantly rely on deep learning techniques and large-scale emotion datasets. However, deep learning techniques are often complex and difficult to interpret, and standardizing large-scale emotional datasets are difficult and costly to establish. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a novel framework named Audio-Visual Fusion for Brain-like Emotion Learning(AVF-BEL). In contrast to conventional brain-inspired emotion learning methods, this approach improves the audio-visual emotion fusion and generation model through the integration of modular components, thereby enabling more lightweight and interpretable emotion learning and generation processes. The framework simulates the integration of the visual, auditory, and emotional pathways of the brain, optimizes the fusion of emotional features across visual and auditory modalities, and improves upon the traditional Brain Emotional Learning (BEL) model. The experimental results indicate a significant improvement in the similarity of the audio-visual fusion emotion learning generation model compared to single-modality visual and auditory emotion learning and generation model. Ultimately, this aligns with the fundamental phenomenon of heightened emotion generation facilitated by the integrated impact of visual and auditory stimuli. This contribution not only enhances the interpretability and efficiency of affective intelligence but also provides new insights and pathways for advancing affective computing technology. Authors: Mountacer M.; Youssef N.
Title: Training and Institutional Guidelines in Teachers’ Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Bibliometric Analysis, Empirical Evidence, and Implications for Quality Education and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly shaping educational practice, yet teachers’ professional adoption remains uneven. This study examines the roles of AI-related training and institutional guidelines in teachers’ use of GenAI and situates the findings within the broader context of quality education and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A cross-sectional survey of 208 Moroccan teachers was analyzed using descriptive statistics, bivariate tests, and binary logistic regression, complemented by a concise bibliometric overview of GenAI research trends. AI-related training was significantly associated with professional GenAI use, whereas institutional guidelines were not significant after adjustment. The findings emphasize the importance of sustained professional development and provide evidence for strengthening responsible GenAI integration in education, particularly in support of SDG 4 on quality education. © 2026, Yayasan Bumi Publikasi Nusantara. Authors: Mansfield J.; Rennie L.J.
Title: The role of creativity and imagination in scientific endeavour
Abstract: Creativity and imagination (C&I) are integral, but often overlooked, aspects of scientific endeavour. If scientists aim to innovate and develop new knowledge about the world around us, C&I are essential, yet how C&I are used in science is poorly understood. This lack of clarity about how C&I are defined, and how they are used, results in uninformed views about the nature of scientific endeavour. Here, we propose a conceptual Framework for an informed view of C&I to support the understanding of science through both research and teaching. We define our understanding of scientific endeavour, then define creativity in science through the generation of new thoughts, processes and products in intentional and unintentional ways which are effective in the context in which the creativity was applied. Imagination complements creativity and is defined as the ability to form mental images in the absence of the senses. During scientific endeavour, C&I work in conjunction with critical thinking and manifest as dispositions and actions when questioning, planning, doing and reflecting in science. Nineteen aspects of scientific endeavour are identified and the roles of C&I for each aspect are illustrated. The result is a characterisation of the role of C&I in scientific endeavour that makes creative and imaginative thoughts and actions explicit. This conceptualisation of an informed view provides a Framework for science educators who are tasked with researching, teaching and assessing, students’ understanding about the role of C&I in scientific endeavour. We close with implications for science education and research. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. A software solution — a Python module for fuzzy inference and visualization has also been implemented, expanding the capabilities of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate that the developed system correctly ranks transport enterprises by risk level. Verification on five theoretical cases (TK1-TK5) confirmed the model's ability to generate an Integrated Safety Assessment (ISA) from 0 to 1, effectively distinguishing between exemplary compliance and systematic critical violations. For instance, a critically problematic scenario (TK4) received a low ISA of 0.34, signaling the need for immediate intervention, while a case with systematic violations (TK5) scored 0.55, near the predefined acceptability threshold of 0.5. ©2027 The author(s). Authors: Pan A.
Title: The AI-augmented collaborative learning model: A conceptual framework for integrating generative AI in business and management education
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) amplifies four tensions in business and management education: the threat to pedagogical coherence, the literacy-to-competency gap, pervasive ethical risks, and the assessment crisis. A first wave of practice-oriented frameworks – including the Human-Centric AI-First (HCAIF) framework and the Leeds Model – offers actionable roadmaps but lacks the theoretical architecture needed to explain the systemic classroom dynamics GenAI introduces. This conceptual paper addresses that gap by developing the AI-Augmented Collaborative Learning (ACL) Model, a second-wave framework organised around three research questions: (RQ1) which theoretical lenses explain the classroom dynamics that generative AI creates in business and management education; (RQ2) how can these be synthesised into an integrated pedagogical framework whose pillars address the four systemic challenges; and (RQ3) how can human-AI collaboration be operationalised as an assessable pedagogical meta-skill. Using Socio-Technical Systems Theory, Activity Theory, Actor-Network Theory, Constructivist and Experiential Learning Theories, and the AI-TPACK framework, the ACL Model specifies four interlocking pillars – Pedagogical Intentionality, Developmental Scaffolding, Ethical Guardrails, and Authentic Assessment. The paper's primary theoretical contribution is to relocate the unit of analysis from the individual student to the student-AI network and to define collaborative intelligence as the resulting meta-competency. A six-proposition validation agenda guides testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Dirksmeier P.; Göb A.
Title: Why conversations constitute neighbourhood cohesion: A mixed-methods approach to substantiating cause and effect
Abstract: Communicating is a meaningful practice for building neighbourhood cohesion by fostering a sense of connection, mutual support and belonging among residents of a geographically defined neighbourhood. In our paper, we highlight the role of regular contact and conversations with neighbours for generating neighbourhood cohesion. Following a mixed-methods approach, we combine qualitative instruments from two case studies focusing on neighbourhoods in Hanover with quantitative data from a panel survey conducted in Hanover and Magdeburg, Germany. The residents’ statements clearly show that talking to each other influences their socio-spatial orientation towards the neighbourhood as a point of reference, thus promoting attitudes and practices to strengthen neighbourhood cohesion. Based on these results, the causal model confirms the effect of conversations on neighbourhood cohesion, which is mediated by the factor of trust. Combining the two types of data helps to understand and explain why neighbourhoods are relevant for peaceful coexistence: they enable low-threshold interaction and thus the experience of belonging and integration. It remains open whether and to what extent neighbourhood cohesion can be scaled up, which requires comparisons with other cities and city types as well as different neighbourhoods to identify regional and international differences. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Gavin C.; Temeljotov Salaj A.
Title: Navigating CSRD compliance: Challenges in sustainability reporting for the real estate sector
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the challenges faced by the Norwegian real estate sector in complying with the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), addressing a critical gap in understanding how these regulations impact sustainability reporting practices. The research seeks new insights into the barriers to implementing CSRD-compliant reporting, contributing to a deeper understanding of the sector's readiness and areas requiring improvement. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, utilizing a scoping literature review to map existing knowledge and semi-structured interviews with industry stakeholders to supplement findings. Data were collected from peer-reviewed articles, master's theses, and interviews with key stakeholders, and analyzed using thematic coding and qualitative analysis. The results reveal that the main challenges include limited knowledge of sustainability matters, difficulties in conducting Double Materiality Assessments (DMA), high costs, poor data systems, and administrative burdens. These findings provide evidence that while some companies proactively prepare for CSRD compliance, many, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), struggle due to resource constraints and a reliance on manual processes. This highlights significant implications for improving digital solutions and stakeholder collaboration. This research offers a novel perspective on sustainability reporting in the Norwegian real estate sector, providing valuable insights into the sector's preparedness and key barriers. The study's findings contribute to advancing digital reporting practices and support for SMEs, highlighting areas for future research and potential policy development to ease the transition to CSRD compliance. Title: Multi-modal knowledge-level representation learning for structure-oriented patent citation prediction
Abstract: Patent citation prediction aims to identify prior patents that challenge the novelty of new patent applications. A citation is valid when the technical components in the new application are functionally and structurally similar to those disclosed in the prior patent. This component structure is conveyed through two modalities: the claim text and the patent figures. Existing methods predominantly rely on text and struggle to capture the graph-structured nature of patent components. We propose a Multi-Modal Knowledge-Level Patent Representation Framework. First, we construct a multi-modal component graph that links text-derived triples with figure-derived visual components via reference numerals. Second, we introduce a knowledge-level attention mechanism operating at the triple level, coupled with cross-modal attention that injects figure-grounded structure into token embeddings, jointly aligning the modalities and suppressing noise arising from legal characterizations in patent text. Finally, we introduce a re-ranking module that performs structure-oriented similarity reasoning over the fused representation. We introduce PatCite, the first citation dataset categorizing samples into “tree-structured” and “graph-structured” types. Under the dynamic full-corpus protocol, our method achieves macro Recall@1/Recall@10 of 14.4%/43.8% on PatCite, with a Recall@1 gain of 5.0 percentage points over the strongest fine-tuned baseline. © 2026

Title: Impact of heritage status on market prices of townhouses in Central Rio de Janeiro
Abstract: This study investigates the effects of differentiated heritage protection regimes on townhouse property values in central Rio de Janeiro, contributing original evidence to a largely unexplored field in Brazil. Based on a sample of 86 townhouses, it applies a traditional hedonic pricing model (OLS), a Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR), and a Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression with Spatial Autoregressive Error (MGWRSAR), which account for spatial heterogeneity and residual autocorrelation. To overcome data limitations, the analysis employs a bootstrap procedure to improve the robustness of inference. Results indicate that only properties under the least restrictive protection (“monitored”) display statistically significant price premiums. However, rather than reflecting a simple inverse relationship between restrictions and market value, this finding points to the importance of regulatory legibility, enforcement consistency, and perceived investment risks. The discussion highlights how flexible and intelligible protection regimes may foster market confidence, while ambiguous or overly rigid frameworks can undermine the effectiveness of heritage policy. The study also underscores a structural barrier to evidence-based policymaking: the lack of public access to transaction-level data in Brazil. This constraint limits empirical evaluation and transparency, both in academic research and in public administration. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Beyond compliance: Community development committees and the transformation of resource governance in Tanzania
Abstract: Resource-rich countries worldwide often face persistent imbalances in the redistribution of resource wealth. Although mineral extraction generates substantial revenues, these funds are typically centrally managed and redistributed, leaving host communities, who bear the social and environmental burdens of extraction, impoverished and marginalized. In Tanzania, despite provisions allowing Local Government Authorities to levy a 0.3% service charge on mining revenues and receive Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) contributions intended to support local development, means of engaging host communities remain a challenge. Community Development Agreements (CDAs) have been identified as potential instruments to safeguard the interests of host communities. However, despite their widespread promotion, a critical gap remains in understanding how communities can effectively engage in, negotiate, and implement CDAs, particularly in contexts marked by power asymmetries. Communities are often poor, with limited knowledge of mining and the broader extractive industry, and with no access to decision-making power. This study addresses the gap by examining Community Development Committees (CDCs) as an inclusive, participatory institutional mechanism through which communities can effectively articulate their development priorities. Using semi‑structured interviews with 36 key informants across the mining value chain, including central government officials, mining representatives, and local communities, the study finds the CDC model as an effective approach for strengthening community voice, enhancing transparency, improving negotiations, and monitoring project implementations. Although grounded in Tanzania’s mining sector, the study offers insights relevant to other resource dependent economies seeking to foster more equitable social contracts. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Enhancement of power system steady-state stability through allocation of quantum-inspired grey wolf optimization algorithm-based multiple D-STATCOM Units
Abstract: Modern distribution networks suffer from power losses and voltage instability under various loading conditions. Mitigating these operational issues requires optimal allocation of custom power devices, such as Distribution Static Compensators (D-STATCOMs). To address this challenge, this study develops a quantum-inspired grey wolf optimization (QGWO) algorithm for allocating D-STATCOMs to ensure steady-state stability, improve bus voltage profiles, and reduce power losses. Distinct from existing variants, QGWO models search agents as probabilistic quantum state vectors, utilizing a fitness-driven amplitude scaling and dynamic phase angle adaptation. Using the backward-forward sweep (BFS) load-flow method, the performance is evaluated across base-load, load-increment, and single-phase fault scenarios on practical 44- and IEEE 69-bus test systems. The voltage stability margin (VSM) is utilized to determine maximum loading factors. For the 44-bus system, buses 22, 29, and 41 with capacities of 637.69 kVAR, 503.75 kVAR, and 351.01 kVAR are found as the optimal locations and sizes. With these units, power losses are reduced by 50.894% under the base-load scenario. For the IEEE 69-bus system, buses 11, 17 and 61 with capacities of 358.69kVAR, 254.02kVAR and 1206.75kVAR reduce power losses by 42.76% under the base-load scenario. Using VSM, the maximum loading factor is found as 1.53 and 2.65 for 44- and 69-bus systems. Statistically, the proposed QGWO achieves the lowest mean power loss, with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests confirming its advantage over PSO, APSO, GWO, and CGWO. Weight sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the optimal solution remains invariant to changes in objective-function weights. Economically, cost-benefit sensitivity analyses confirm the financial viability of the project. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy for flashforwards: Randomized multiple baseline single case experimental design in social anxiety disorder
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Background and objectives: Negative mental imagery in social anxiety is common and can involve memories of adverse events or catastrophic future anticipations (i.e., “flashforwards”). Laboratory research has shown that such imagery can be modulated by dual-tasking interventions, which is used in Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy. Methods: Using a replicated sequential single-case experimental design, we examined whether EMDR therapy for flashforwards reduces social anxiety and avoidance of fear-related situations, relative to baseline, in eight individuals with social anxiety disorder. Participants were recruited from a specialized treatment center after unsuccessful CBT or because of treatment complexity (e.g., comorbidity) and were randomly assigned to varying baseline durations before EMDR therapy. Outcome variables were daily social anxiety and avoidance. Randomization tests were conducted for each case separately to test whether EMDR therapy compared to a baseline phase resulted in less daily 1) social anxiety and 2) social avoidance for individual participants and for the total sample. Results: The preregistered randomization tests did not show statistically significant between-phase differences in daily social anxiety, daily social avoidance, or weekly social anxiety severity. Exploratory, unplanned permutation distancing tests, conducted to examine the possible influence of serial dependency, indicated lower scores during the intervention phase across all three outcomes. At the individual level, these exploratory analyses indicated reductions in daily social anxiety for six participants, in daily social avoidance for three participants, and in weekly social anxiety severity for five participants. Aggregated effect-size estimates were medium for daily social anxiety, small for daily social avoidance, and small to medium for weekly social anxiety severity. Limitations: Limitations include modest serial dependency, absence of an active treatment control condition, absence of long-term follow-up measurements, and inclusion of one participant without a clearly identifiable flashforward, although treatment adhered to the prespecified Stage 1 treatment protocol. Conclusions: The preregistered analyses did not provide confirmatory evidence that EMDR therapy for flashforwards reduced social anxiety or avoidance. However, the descriptive findings, effect-size estimates, and exploratory analyses showed a pattern consistent with possible reductions in social anxiety, while findings for avoidance were weaker and less consistent. These results should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered controlled studies. Authors: Wang Y.; Che M.; Wei Y.
Title: Effective algorithms for tensor-train decomposition via the UTV framework
Abstract: The tensor-train (TT) decomposition is widely used to compress large tensors into a more compact form by exploiting their inherent data structures. A fundamental approach for constructing the TT format is the well-known TT-SVD method, which performs singular value decompositions (SVDs) on the successive unfolding matrices sequentially. But in practical applications, it is often unnecessary to compute full SVDs. In this article, we propose the TT-UTV method, a general framework that incorporates the family of UTV-type algorithms to compute the TT decomposition. As an extension of TT-SVD, it can choose rank-revealing UTV factorizations for the extraction of core tensors, enabling more efficient handling of large-scale intermediate unfolding matrices. We further analyze the error propagation of each step within the TT-UTV framework, and derive a tight overall error bound. Based on this analysis, we recommend distinct sweep patterns for the ULV and URV cases, and formulate the rank-adaptive algorithms with prescribed accuracy. Numerical experiments on various datasets, including magnetic resonance imaging data completion, demonstrate their good performance in practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Quasi-real-time degradation-aware energy management for standalone PV-battery microgrids under uncertainty
Abstract: Energy management in standalone photovoltaic-battery microgrids requires balancing supply reliability, forecast uncertainty, and battery degradation within tight computational budgets. This paper proposes an integrated, quasi-real-time energy management framework that couples nonlinear rolling-horizon model predictive control with three complementary mechanisms: (i) a variable-resolution dispatch layer that adapts the optimization granularity to system dynamics, (ii) an operating reserve formulation based on short-term energy-mismatch forecasts produced by dedicated Long Short-Term Memory recurrent neural networks (LSTM-RNN) for load, photovoltaic generation, and reserve estimation, and (iii) an online battery degradation assessment algorithm compatible with the optimization layer. The framework is evaluated on a standalone microgrid in Ouarzazate, Morocco, using one-second-resolution data over three representative weeks. The results reveal that the integrated degradation-aware framework does not uniformly improve dispatch performance, but rather establishes an explicit trade-off between supply reliability and battery lifetime. Under the tested configuration, the joint framework extends expected battery lifetime by approximately 218% compared to the uncertainty-only strategy (from 4.51 to 14.36 years averaged across three weeks), at the cost of a 50% relative increase in unmet load (from 19.22% to 28.78%), providing microgrid operators with a quantifiable, tunable mechanism to prioritize battery preservation when operationally justified. The proposed online cycle detection algorithm is cross-verified against pyLife's rainflow-based reference implementation across all 30 evaluated dispatch cases, showing a mean absolute cycle-count deviation of 2.68%, confirming its consistency with reference rainflow methods and its suitability for real-time embedded deployment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Dual-view contrastive learning for heterogeneous graph representation
Abstract: Representation learning on heterogeneous graphs relies on exploiting both diverse semantics and intricate structural relations. However, the common approaches struggle to simultaneously account for distant semantic interactions and fine-grained structural patterns. Therefore, we introduce a novel Heterogeneous Graph Representation Learning method via a dual-view contrastive structure (HGRL). Specifically, the Schema-aware Graph Abstraction Module (SGAM) captures relational dependencies using a type-aware graph neural network augmented with adaptive residual pathways to learn structural representations. Moreover, the Mamba-based Semantic Reasoner (MSR) utilizes a globally-enhanced Mamba backbone with multi-scale fusion and directional positional encodings to model high-order semantic dependencies. Furthermore, we design a dynamic bidirectional contrastive learning framework that aligns the semantic and structural views, where each view serves as a form of learnable augmentation and mutual supervision for the other, thereby fostering robust and mutually-enriched representations. Comprehensive experiments on six benchmark datasets show that HGRL achieves competitive or superior performance relative to representative state-of-the-art methods across node classification and clustering tasks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Enhancing Real-World Physics Problem-Solving Skills through Mind Map-Based Scaffolding: The Role of Metacomponents among Pre-University Students

Abstract: Physics problem-solving is essential in physics education, yet many pre-university students struggle to apply concepts to real-world contexts. A quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test non-equivalent group design involved 253 students at Universiti Malaysia Sabah. The experimental group used mind maps to define problems, organize information, and plan strategies with guided scaffolding, while the control group received conventional lectures. Data from open-ended RWPPS assessments showed that the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group, with improvements across all metacomponent sub-skills, especially monitoring. Title: Declining cocoa and intensifying artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM): examining changing labour structures and livelihoods in rural Ghana
Abstract: Ghana’s cocoa frontier increasingly overlaps with mechanised artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), creating competition over land and labour. This article examines how declining cocoa production and intensifying ASGM reorganise a local labour regime and reshape rural livelihood pathways in Juaboso District, Western North Region. It draws on 40 semi-structured interviews with cocoa farmers, ASGM workers and institutional actors, alongside observations at four ASGM sites, conducted in 2024. The analysis combines the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework for the 21st Century (SLF-21) with a labour-regime lens. The findings show that cocoa decline and political arrangements governing access to land, machinery, finance and licences create uneven openings for mining. Landowners and operators can convert cocoa land and capture mining rents, while young, often migrant, workers enter hazardous and insecure work. At the same time, ASGM expansion reduces labour availability for cocoa production, increases labour costs for cocoa farmers and degrades land and water used by farming households. Mining income can meet urgent household needs and, in some cases, support farming, but these gains coexist with risks that are shifted onto workers, non-mining farmers and younger generations. These risks are unevenly distributed across generations, with younger people likely to bear a greater burden through depleted land and water resources, and the health and educational consequences of mining-centred livelihood pathways. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Urban transformation in heritage cities through the perceptions of experts- A case of Varanasi, India
Abstract: This study presents responses to questionnaires submitted to 30 experts from diverse professional backgrounds about one of the oldest settlements in India, i.e., Varanasi. Expert interviews provided diverse perspectives on the challenges of urban settings and their transformation. To decipher the subjective responses, this data was analysed using MAXQDA24, a data analysis tool that facilitates quick analysis, coding, and presentation of large qualitative datasets. The expert highlights that the visual representation of the city, including its religious, educational, and historical significance, is highly prominent. Additionally, the study suggests the establishment of a city-level heritage body to a) maintain heritage properties, b) plan different neighborhoods for different perceptual experiences to segregate the footfall, and c) involve the local community. Title: Severity-based adaptive control strategy for BESS frequency regulation and SoC management
Abstract: This paper proposes a severity-based adaptive control strategy for BESS-based primary frequency regulation (PFR) and state-of-charge (SoC) management. Conventional adaptive droop controllers commonly use decoupled gain structures, fixed nonlinear curves, or multi-parameter logistic functions, which complicate tuning and may increase unnecessary battery cycling. The proposed controller introduces a unified Δf–SoC map in which a single concavity parameter β shapes the frequency-severity response. A multiplicative SoC weighting function enforces dynamic participation limits, while a hybrid β-adaptation mechanism distinguishes sustained volatility from high-RoCoF events. A frequency-gated restoration loop is added to recover SoC without interfering with critical frequency support. The controller is evaluated through SFR-model simulations and IEEE 9-bus multi-machine studies, supported by sensitivity analysis, stability verification, and battery degradation assessment. Results show that the proposed method provides a balanced trade-off between frequency regulation and battery utilization. In the continuous stochastic case, it reduces BESS energy throughput and total degradation damage compared with the benchmark controllers. In the severe IEEE 9-bus step disturbance, it achieves the lowest RMS frequency deviation and maximum deviation among the tested methods. These results confirm that the proposed strategy improves large-disturbance frequency support while preserving battery lifetime and maintaining stable operation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Intra-Matrix Flexible Optical-Electronic Configuration Algorithms for Energy-Efficient Large Language Model Inference
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Low-energy, low-precision inference is an important enabler for scalable deployment of large language models (LLMs). Optical-electronic computing offers high bandwidth, low latency, and potentially high energy efficiency, making it a promising approach for future LLM deployment. However, existing optical and hybrid optical-electronic inference systems typically use uniform hardware configurations, such as fixed optical power or a fixed electronic-photonic partition across layers. Fine-grained allocation of optical power and optical-electronic computation remains underexplored for photonic LLM inference. Here, we propose three flexible configuration algorithms: Flexible Optical Power Allocation (FOPA), Flexible Weak-Column Allocation (FWCA), and Joint Optical Power and Weak-Column Allocation (JOWA). Using a diagonal Hessian estimator without constructing the full Hessian matrix, these methods jointly optimize optical-electronic resources under predefined energy budgets. Evaluations on Llama 2-7B and DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Base show estimated energy savings of 40.11%-60.85% relative to FP16 inference on the NVIDIA H100 and 5.34%-38.12% relative to uniform optical-power and weak-column baselines, while maintaining an acceptable perplexity increase. Evaluations using a Tianshu-hardware-calibrated simulator show corresponding estimated energy savings of 39.91%-53.67% and 5.02%-26.76%, respectively. These results indicate that fine-grained resource allocation can improve the energy-accuracy trade-off of hybrid optical-electronic systems for LLM inference.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Title: Socio-ecological Landscape Contexts and Ecosystem Services in the Argentine Dry Chaco: From Agroexpansion to Inhabited Forests (2000–2020)
Abstract: Landscape transformation driven by agribusiness expansion in the Dry Chaco is among the most pressing socio-ecological challenges globally, yet biophysical, ecosystem-service (ES), and sociodemographic dynamics are typically analyzed separately, obscuring how territorial configurations shape landscape change. To address this gap, this study proposes the Socio-Ecological Landscape Context (SELC) framework — a spatially explicit approach that integrates biophysical metrics with sociodemographic variables to define territorial units and interpret how they mediate ES supply over time. We applied it to Santiago del Estero Province in the Argentine Dry Chaco, analyzing landscape transformation (patch count and edge density) and ES supply (a rapid multicriteria assessment assigning potential supply values to land-cover types) over two decades (2000–2020), using satellite imagery (MapBiomas Chaco Collection 4), deforestation records, and census data. Cluster analysis identified six SELCs: First Wave Agroexpansion, Second Wave Agroexpansion, Concentrated Population, Inhabited Dry Forest, Hilly Arid, and Alluvial Plain. Closed woody vegetation declined by 12.6% points (from 66.6% to 54.0%), while the number of forest patches rose by 44%, indicating progressive fragmentation. Two contrasting patterns emerge: dynamic SELCs (First and Second Wave Agroexpansion, Concentrated Population) show marked declines in key ES, whereas persistent SELCs maintain higher ES levels over time. A sparse rural population shows a modest but consistent positive association with ES supply. These findings suggest that similar land-cover compositions can yield divergent socio-ecological outcomes depending on landscape configuration and modes of inhabitation, supporting biocultural conservation approaches that recognize peasant and Indigenous communities as active contributors to landscape multifunctionality. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Blastocystis sp. in human populations: Pooled prevalence and subtype distribution from a systematic review and meta-analysis
Abstract: Blastocystis is widely detected in human populations, yet prevalence estimates vary substantially across geographic regions, population settings, and diagnostic approaches. We systematically reviewed cross-sectional surveys published from 2015 to 2025 that investigated non-disease-selected human populations. Across 137 eligible survey units from 47 countries, 562,327 participants and 26,697 positive detections were included. The crude participant-level positivity was 4.7%, whereas the random-effects pooled prevalence across published surveys was 17.9% (95% CI: 13.9%–22.6%; 95% PI: 0.7%–87.5%; I2 = 99.7%). Regional pooled estimates were 44.2% in Africa, 36.7% in the Americas, 8.4% in Asia, and 7.2% in Europe; however, these comparisons should be interpreted descriptively because substantial residual heterogeneity and study-level confounding remained. Population-group differences were not statistically significant ( P = 0.074), while the three broad diagnostic-strategy groups were summarized descriptively because multimodal protocols were heterogeneous. Sensitivity analyses restricted to population-based surveys and community/household surveys yielded pooled estimates of 15.8% and 13.0%, respectively. Among 62 studies reporting molecular subtype information, 5220 isolates were assigned single subtypes, while 658 mixed-subtype detections from 18 studies were summarized separately. ST3, ST1, and ST2 were among the predominant reported subtypes. These findings summarize available published surveillance data rather than a population-weighted global burden estimate and highlight the need for standardized sampling frameworks, harmonized molecular workflows, and integrated One Health investigations to clarify Blastocystis epidemiology and transmission ecology. Title: Business simulation games and ethical decision making confidence and intentions: The role of self-efficacy, reflective practice, and teamwork
Abstract: This study examines the potential associations between experiential learning via participating in a business simulation game and business students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. While simulation games have been widely recognized for their effectiveness in developing business competencies, their associations with ethical decision making confidence and intentions in a non-ethics related environment remain underexplored. Our findings suggest that participation in simulation games is associated with higher levels of students' teamwork and reflective practice capabilities that, in turn, were found to be positively associated with their ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Moreover, students who participated in simulation games reported higher self-efficacy which, however, was not found to have a significant relationship with ethical decision-making confidence and intentions. Our findings highlight the potential value of integrating experiential learning tools, such as simulation games, into business education suggesting an association with improvements in students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Title: Integrated assessment of the environmental and social impacts of bauxite mining in the Boké Prefecture
Abstract: Since the 2011 mining reforms, Guinea has experienced a rapid increase in bauxite extraction, particularly in the Boké Prefecture. While this growth has significantly stimulated the nation's economy, the aggregated socio-environmental and territorial consequences of bauxite extraction at the local level remain insufficiently documented in peer-reviewed literature, especially through comprehensive, community-level empirical analyses that links spatial transformations to residents’ experiences of displacement. This study argues that existing compensation and governance frameworks do not match the territorial extent of bauxite mining impacts, resulting in ongoing livelihood insecurity even in cases of formal resettlement. The research employs a mixed-methods approach, integrating field surveys, direct observations, interviews, and focus group discussions with 83 participants from four impacted communities. It also incorporates a diachronic analysis of land use and land cover (LULC) derived from Landsat imagery spanning 1973 to 2024. The study follows Cernea’s Impoverishment Risks and Reconstruction framework. Findings indicate a marked increase in mining areas (from 0 to 68 km²) and exposed soils near Sangarédi, accompanied by a substantial decline in vegetation cover (–28%). These spatial changes align with local perceptions of deteriorating air and water quality, farmland loss, and heightened livelihood insecurity, despite observable investments in social infrastructure. In Kanfarandé, the expansion of port infrastructure has precipitated significant territorial changes, even absent direct mining activities. Overall, the research shows that current compensation and governance mechanisms remain inadequate to address the cumulative and indirect impacts of bauxite exploitation, underscoring the need for integrated, participatory, and territorially informed governance frameworks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Bi-level optimization of harmonic mitigation and energy trading in distribution networks with connected microgrids using PV-inverters and active power filters
Abstract: The widespread deployment of power electronic-based devices in modern distribution networks introduces significant power quality challenges, necessitating effective mitigation strategies at the distribution level. Title: Seven Sisters tourism under siege: Hybrid neural insights into stakeholder resilience
Abstract: Tourism stakeholders in insurgency-affected destinations navigate persistent insecurity that shapes their perceptions, adaptive behavior, and support for tourism in nonlinear ways. Title: Multi-Level collaborative optimization for Multi-Modal media manipulation detection and grounding
Abstract: The proliferation of manipulated multi-modal content threatens the credibility of social media. Although existing detecting and grounding multi-modal media manipulation (DGM4) methods exploit image-text complementarity, they optimize classification and localization largely independently, overlooking structured collaboration between the two tasks. To address this limitation, we propose a multi-level task collaboration (MLTC) framework that progressively promotes detection and grounding interaction at the feature, semantic, and decision levels. At the feature level, cross-modal alignment and interaction construct modality-specific bridge representations, enabling classification and grounding within each modality to reason over a shared multi-modal evidence space. At the semantic level, the proposed cross-granularity semantic fusion (CGSF) module learns shared semantic importance weights to coordinate global classification semantics and local grounding evidence, encouraging consistent manipulation-aware evidence selection across different granularities. At the decision level, focusing on the dense spatial nature of visual grounding, we introduce cross-granularity decision fusion (CGDF), which integrates image-level manipulation confidence and patch-level localization responses to produce a manipulation probability map (MPM). The manipulation-aware grounding refinement (MAGR) module further introduces the MPM as a bounded soft prior during query-based evidence aggregation, strengthening manipulation-relevant patch contributions while preserving the baseline visual evidence for robust bounding-box prediction. On the entire DGM4 test set, MLTC achieves an AUC of 94.94%, a multi-label mAP of 90.72%, an image-grounding IoUmean of 79.63%, and a token-grounding F1 score of 76.85%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Congestion management in electric distribution systems through flexibility services: a bibliometric and analytical review
Abstract: Electricity systems are rapidly evolving toward decentralized architectures with high shares of variable renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources (DERs), increasing congestion in medium- and low-voltage networks. This paper presents a structured mixed-source review combining bibliometric mapping and targeted analytical synthesis on flexibility services for congestion management in electric distribution systems. Analysis of the quality-controlled Q3 corpus (n = 1827) identifies China as the leading national contributor and substantial collective European participation, with 79.6% of records published from 2018 onward. Author-keyword mapping reveals five streams: distribution-network optimization, market-based congestion management, uncertainty-aware active-network operation, flexibility-service coordination, and demand-response smart-grid control. Novelty lies in keeping the validated bibliometric corpus separate from an independently assembled, question-driven evidence base until interpretation. The analytical synthesis shows that distributed locational marginal pricing (DLMP), particularly in iterative formulations, can internalize network constraints and provide locational signals for DER coordination, although its effectiveness depends on adequate network modeling, uncertainty treatment, and flexible-demand participation. The review also identifies converging trends toward multilayer coordination between transmission system operators (TSOs) and distribution system operators (DSOs), local flexibility procurement, and digital platforms for ancillary-service provision. Across jurisdictions, explicit remuneration, interoperable data, and coordinated governance recur, but uneven implementation precludes causal comparisons or effectiveness rankings. The paper concludes by identifying research gaps related to cost–benefit validation, regulatory standardization, data interoperability, and large-scale implementation in distribution systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: CONSUMER HEALTH ENTOMOLOGY-A FORTIORI INDUSTRIAL SCIENCE OF EMERGING PUBLIC HEALTH SIGNIFICANCE, WITH EMPHASIS ON ITS COMMERCIAL, BEHAVIOURAL AND SOCIAL CONSIDERATIONS
Abstract: Among various subsets of entomology, medical entomology focuses on vector-borne diseases and suggests methods for its control. However, the lacunae of information on contribution of the product originators, attributes of consumers in integrated vector control led to the emergence of a new discipline called Consumer Health Entomology (CHE). It is a novel concept addresses gaps in traditional medical entomology by focusing on the direct and indirect impact of insects on consumers involving three pillars of action viz., Protection, Prevention and Awareness. In the era of globalization, where consumer needs evolve rapidly, it bridges the gap between laboratory and field research applied in every-day life of humans, promoting sustainable and consumer-friendly pest control solutions. CHE fosters collaboration among researchers, public health officials, and industries to develop effective, accessible products. Empowering consumers with knowledge and innovative solutions, CHE paves the way for a healthier future. Its success requires collaborative efforts of researchers, public health officials, and individuals. © 2027, The Entomological Society of India. All rights reserved.

Authors: Miyagawa H.; Suzuoki T.
Title: Exhaust emission control strategies for lean-burn NH3/H2-fueled spark ignition engines
Abstract: Ammonia-fueled engines are attracting increasing interest as a carbon-free energy conversion technology; however, their exhaust typically contains unburned ammonia (NH3), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and nitrous oxide (N2O), and achieving their simultaneous removal under oxygen-rich conditions remains a major challenge. This study investigates emission control strategies using SCR catalyst for a NH3/H2-fueled spark-ignition engine, with emphasis on the linkage between engine-out exhaust characteristics and SCR performance. Engine experiments demonstrate that the engine-out ammonia-to-NOx ratio (ANR) can be systematically controlled through mixture composition, specifically via the equivalence ratio and H2 energy fraction, providing a practical control index for aftertreatment. Using Fe- and Cu-zeolite SCR catalysts, ANR-dependent conversion characteristics are quantified over a wide temperature range. Both catalysts exhibit a temperature-dependent optimal ANR at which near-complete simultaneous removal of NH3 and NOx is achieved, reflecting competition between SCR reactions and NH3 oxidation. To address sensitivity to ANR variability, two complementary and distinct approaches are demonstrated: (i) a control-based strategy employing periodic ANR swing to exploit NH3 storage in zeolite catalysts, and (ii) a catalyst-design-based strategy using a tandem Fe/Cu SCR configuration. Both approaches achieve catalyst-out NH3 and NOx concentrations below 10 ppm. For the tested Fe/Cu tandem system at a nominal catalyst-inlet gas temperature of 450 °C, simultaneous high NH3 and NOx conversions were observed at all tested ANR points between 1.25 and 1.62. In addition, the effects of catalyst configuration and temperature on N2O formation and decomposition are clarified, highlighting trade-offs between operational robustness and greenhouse gas mitigation. The results present proof-of-concept emission-control approaches under the selected steady-state conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yao H.; Chen Z.
Title: How autonomy-supportive environments and growth mindset foster creativity efficacy in middle school students? Evidence from a large-scale survey in China
Abstract: This study examines the associations between multi-source autonomy-supportive environments, growth mindset, and creative self-efficacy among Chinese middle school students, with particular attention to the mediating role of growth mindset and individual heterogeneity in these associations. Using large-scale survey data from 6146 middle school students in Suzhou, China, and drawing on Bandura's (1997) social cognitive theory and Self-Determination Theory, we employed structural equation modeling and quantile regression to investigate these relationships. The SEM results indicate that teacher, parental, and peer autonomy support are all positively associated with creative self-efficacy, with teacher and peer support showing stronger total associations than parental support. Growth mindset mediated all three associations, with the indirect effect proportion being highest for teacher autonomy support, followed by parental autonomy support and peer autonomy support. Quantile regression analyses revealed meaningful heterogeneity across the creative self-efficacy distribution: teacher and parental autonomy support showed stronger associations at lower quantiles, peer autonomy support peaked at moderate quantiles, and all associations weakened at higher quantiles. These findings contribute to the cross-cultural understanding of how multi-source autonomy-supportive environments relate to creative self-efficacy in a collectivist educational context, and offer practical implications for differentiated educational interventions targeting students at different levels of creative self-efficacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Maiese K.
Title: Oxidative stress, aging, metabolism, SIRT1, and the gut microbiota: the neurocardiac basis of cognitive loss
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease and cognitive loss have a neurocardiac basis. Poor vascular perfusion can impair cognitive function in both Alzheimer’s disease and multiple sclerosis. However, a treatment gap exists because current approaches do not adequately address the shared underlying cellular mechanisms responsible for cognitive dysfunction in these conditions. Current treatments for cognitive impairment in diseases such as cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and diabetes often fail to fully address the shared underlying cellular mechanisms. Consequently, the prevailing precision treatment strategy, which focuses on managing symptoms and preventing disease progression, is insufficient. This highlights the urgent need for innovative approaches capable of targeting these common cellular pathways across these diverse conditions. Novel investigations into oxidative stress, cellular senescence, programmed cell death with apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and autophagy, cellular metabolism with apolipoprotein E and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonism, silent mating type information regulation 2 homolog 1 (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), mitochondrial dynamics, and the gut microbiome offer the potential to address the risk factors and clinical treatments for cardiovascular disease and cognitive loss. These pathways are exquisitely dependent upon one another and require in-depth knowledge of the modulatory cellular mechanisms for effective translation to clinical care. © 2026 Medical Gas Research

Authors: Wang L.; Wu X.; Sun Z.; Dou Y.
Title: Physics-constrained spatiotemporal modeling for temporal localization in structured multichannel acoustic signals
Abstract: Temporal localization in structured multichannel acoustic signals, such as first-arrival picking in geophysical logging, is a fundamental yet challenging task. Traditional signal processing methods rely heavily on manual heuristics, while existing data-driven deep learning approaches often overlook the inherent physical priors of multichannel arrays, resulting in a trade-off among accuracy, stability, and real-time performance in field applications. To address these challenges, we propose FA-Picker, a physics-constrained spatiotemporal modeling framework for first-arrival picking. This model explicitly incorporates the depth dimension to construct a three-dimensional input data volume, enabling the capture of joint spatiotemporal features across multiple receivers and consecutive measurements. Moreover, an end-to-end multi-task architecture is designed, where coarse first-arrival segmentation guides continuous arrival-time regression. A dual-constraint mechanism is introduced, combining soft loss-based guidance with hard physical constraints, ensuring that the localized temporal points strictly comply with the underlying wave propagation laws. Furthermore, to alleviate the scarcity of high-quality labeled data, we exploit the highly structured characteristics of multichannel acoustic arrays to develop a comprehensive synthetic data generation workflow that simulates diverse formation variations and acquisition environments. Experimental results on field datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed modeling and data augmentation strategies, showing the superior performance of FA-Picker in practical first-arrival picking tasks. The code is available at: https://github.com/longw0110/Synthetic-workflow-for-FA-Picker. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: When tourism competitiveness becomes human development: The conditioning role of institutional quality in Central and Eastern Europe
Abstract: Why do destinations with similar levels of tourism competitiveness experience different human development outcomes? Integrating Sen's Capability Approach with the Tourism Competitiveness Theory Hypothesis, this study examines the institutional conditions under which tourism competitiveness becomes meaningful for human development. Tourism competitiveness is conceptualized as a resource-generating capacity, while institutional quality represents a macro-level condition shaping its conversion into human development. Using annual data for eleven Central and Eastern European countries (2000–2023), we estimate heterogeneous panel autoregressive distributed lag models, error-correction dynamics, and Granger-type causality tests. Results show a positive long-run relationship between tourism competitiveness and human development, with stronger institutional quality associated with larger developmental returns. A trajectory analysis identifies four tourism–development pathways and interprets their differences through institutional quality. The study extends tourism competitiveness theory beyond destination performance by explaining why comparable competitive capacities can generate different human development outcomes across institutional contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ji X.; Zhang X.
Title: Can AI-generated images match human-generated images in inspiring travel? A visual feature analysis of audience perceptions and visit intention
Abstract: Generative AI tools can now create photorealistic destination images at low cost, yet whether such images motivate travel as effectively as human-generated images remains unclear. Drawing on the heuristic-systematic model, this research examines differences between AI-generated and human-generated tourism images through three studies. Study 1 shows that AI-generated images receive higher ratings of perceived aesthetics but lower ratings of perceived authenticity, narrative transportation, and visit intention than human-generated images. Study 2 identifies 19 computable visual indicators across three dimensions and finds that AI-generated images exhibit stronger visual schema characteristics, whereas human-generated images show richer visual structure. Study 3 uses XGBoost and SHAP analysis to identify the visual features associated with different psychological responses. These findings connect computational visual analysis with tourism consumer research by identifying differences in audience responses to AI-generated and human-generated images and the visual features associated with those responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Data centres and the new strategic infrastructure governance: From cloud ESG to compute sovereignty
Abstract: Data centres have moved from the background of the digital economy to the foreground of energy, climate, industrial and national-security politics. Artificial intelligence is intensifying this shift through growing demand for compute, electricity, cooling, land, hardware and critical materials. Yet governance remains largely organised around facility-level metrics that treat data centres as bounded technical assets rather than strategic infrastructure embedded in grids, water systems, supply chains, communities and security architectures. This article develops the CLOUDS framework—Coherence, Lifecycle materiality, Operational locality, Utility burden, Digital sovereignty, and Social licence and public purpose—as a diagnostic architecture for evaluating data centres as system-shaping infrastructure. It also develops capacity extraction: the process through which heterogeneous inputs such as electricity, water, land, permits, institutional trust and community tolerance are rendered as a single quantity called capacity and converted into compute whose higher-value layers may remain controlled elsewhere. The framework is developed through an integrative review and tiered empirical design spanning Chile, Australia, Querétaro, Ireland and Singapore. It is proposed for testing rather than presented as validated. Two findings are central. First, instrument incoherence can arise without regulatory capture when no institution can govern trade-offs across electricity, water, planning and public value. Second, hosting is not sovereignty: physical location alone creates no assured claim on compute access, workload priority, crisis continuity or higher-value layers. The policy implication is strategic infrastructure bargaining over both system capacity and the institutions governing its conversion into compute. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Puente-Díaz R.; Cavazos-Arroyo J.
Title: Feelings of ease in generating ideas: My loyal companion that guides my mental action but does not help me generate more creative ideas
Abstract: The ability to generate creative ideas is an important skill for education. This study examined how feelings of ease in generating ideas act as a cue that allowed individuals to have information to monitor their mental action and make important metacognitive decisions while generating creative ideas. Participants were asked to generate four ideas to help deal with the problem of empty work offices during and after the pandemic of COVID-19. After generating each idea, participants reported their feelings of ease and evaluated the creativity of each idea. Participants then reported their confidence in the ideas generated and selected their most creative idea. Results showed negative, curvilinear trajectories of feelings of ease and self-evaluations of the creativity of each idea. Feelings of ease in generating ideas were positively related to self-evaluations and the decisions to continue generating ideas and negatively related to choosing the first idea as the most creative. In addition, feelings of ease were indirectly and positively related to post-task confidence through their relationship with self-evaluations. These findings provided initial, empirical evidence that feelings of ease acted as cues to inform relevant judgments and decisions in the process of ideation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bongo M.F.
Title: Modified DEA-SBM efficiency-based diversion risk proxy assessment with peer similarity for decision support in aircraft diversion management
Abstract: Aircraft diversion is a critical component of aviation safety management, requiring close coordination among pilots, air traffic controllers, and airline operations teams. Although established procedures guide the process, diversions remain complex and time-sensitive due to operational and logistical constraints, and there is no universal framework for selecting the most suitable alternate airport. This paper proposes a decision support system to assist diversion decision-making through a modified data envelopment analysis–slack-based measure (DEA-SBM) efficiency-based proxy model. The model evaluates the efficiency-based diversion risk proxy (EDRP) index for airports using relevant input and output variables associated with the diversion process. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model, three real diversion cases in the Philippines are used as baseline scenarios. The resulting model outputs are consistent with the actual diversion decisions implemented in operational practice. This alignment provides empirical support that the model can function as a reliable decision support tool for diversion management, particularly in replicating observed operational judgment under real-world constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
