Authors: Asare P.Y.
Title: Task value, effort regulation and critical thinking: Towards a unified learning configuration in financial management education
Abstract: Financial Management requires students to integrate motivational, behavioural, and cognitive competencies to solve financial problems. However, existing research has predominantly examined these learner characteristics independently, providing limited understanding of how they coexist to shape learning. This study adopted a person-centred approach to identify distinct learning configurations based on task value, effort regulation, and critical thinking among Business students studying Financial Management. A cross-sectional survey design was employed to collect data from 168 students using validated measures, and Latent Profile Analysis identified naturally occurring learning profiles. Four distinct learning configurations emerged: Low Learning Orientation (10.1%), Developing Learning Orientation (11.9%), Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation (31.0%), and Integrated Learning Configuration (47.0%). The Integrated Learning Configuration represented the largest group. Notably, the Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation profile reflected students with stronger task value and effort regulation relative to critical thinking. This finding suggests that valuing learning and regulating effort alone may be insufficient for developing higher-order financial reasoning. Profile membership differed by programme of study but not by sex or age. The study advances management education by conceptualising learning in Financial Management as an integrated configuration of motivational, behavioural, and cognitive dimensions rather than isolated learner characteristics, informing pedagogical connoisseurship in practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Serafin T.; Nitka W.
Title: Data-driven calibration sample selection and forecast combination in electricity price forecasting: An application of the ARHNN method
Abstract: Calibration sample selection and forecast combination are two simple yet powerful tools used in forecasting. They can be combined with a variety of models to significantly improve prediction accuracy, at the same time offering easy implementation and low computational complexity. While their effectiveness has been repeatedly confirmed in prior scientific literature, the topic is still underexplored in the field of electricity price forecasting. In this research article we apply the Autoregressive Hybrid Nearest Neighbors (ARHNN) method to three long-term time series describing the German, Spanish and New England electricity markets. We show that it outperforms popular literature benchmarks in terms of forecast accuracy by up to 10%. We also propose two simplified variants of the method, granting a vast decrease in computation time with only minor loss of prediction accuracy. Finally, we compare the forecasts’ performance in a battery storage system trading case study and propose a new automated trading strategy. We find that using a forecast-driven strategy can consistently achieve a substantial share of theoretical maximum profits while trading, demonstrating business value in practical applications. © 2026

Authors: Mohammadi P.; Dahmardeh M.
Title: Gender Representation and Intercultural Competence in Iranian EFL Coursebooks from the 1960s to 2020s
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the representation of gender and intercultural competence in the images and texts of 15 Iranian secondary school English coursebooks, published over six decades. Gender representation was investigated using the framework proposed by Dahmardeh and Kim (2020), and the scale developed by Solhaug and Kristensen (2020) was used as the criteria for investigating intercultural competence. The data were coded and counted using manifest content analysis. The results showed that Iranian English coursebooks mentioned males and females unequally in their texts across different decades, with one gender being represented more in each decade. Regarding gender representation in the images, males were represented more than females in almost all decades. The representation of males and females in the books published in the 1970s was almost equal, followed by extreme and sudden changes in gender representation in the 1980s. However, the books published in and after the 2000s presented a balanced picture of males and females. The coursebooks dealt with intercultural competence in their texts and images very rarely, limiting this concept to religious issues and neglecting other aspects. In fact, the coursebooks addressed only one category out of the 11 categories. Finally, the study ends with implications for coursebook authors, materials designers, teachers, students, and teacher trainers. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. All rights reserved.

Title: Perceived social entrepreneurship education and entrepreneurial intention in times of crisis: Where moral obligation matters
Abstract: Social entrepreneurship education is widely promoted; however, the reflection of students' educational experience in social entrepreneurial intention remains insufficiently understood, particularly in institutionally fragile contexts. Drawing on survey data from 299 Lebanese university students, this study tests a moderated mediation model grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). Specifically, it examines whether personal attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control mediate the relationship between students' perceived social entrepreneurship education experience and entrepreneurial intention, and whether moral obligation conditions these pathways. More positive perceptions of the educational experience are associated with stronger intention indirectly through personal attitude and perceived behavioural control, while subjective norms show no significant effect, reflecting weakened normative reference points under prolonged crisis. Moral obligation operates selectively, strengthening the attitudinal pathway while leaving the control and the normative pathways unchanged. This study extends the mediated view of educational influence to social entrepreneurship education in a crisis setting, suggests that moral obligation may function as a conditional ethical amplifier, and shows how institutional fragility can affect the salient dimensions of TPB. In fragile settings, such education should cultivate reflective attitudes and moral engagement alongside structural reforms that enable normative support for socially oriented careers. © 2026

Authors: Zhang R.
Title: Emotional preferences in LoRA-driven AI-generated urban vitality spaces: A study using discrete choice models
Abstract: China's transition toward urban stock renewal has heightened the focus on the emotional quality of urban vitality spaces. While AI generative design offers new approaches, whether AI-generated images as visual representations for specific spaces can meet people's emotional needs remains insufficiently examined. This study examines whether AI-generated visual representations of such spaces evoke image-based emotional preferences comparable to those for real photographs, and identifies which spatial attributes drive these preferences. Using THE BOX in Beijing as a case, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion models generated visual representations of seven chosen scenes. Emotional preferences were measured through validated scales completed by 115 participants. A discrete choice model was used to compare participants' preferences between photographs of the real space and AI-generated images and identified influential attributes. Results showed that participants with design-related backgrounds preferred real photographs. Positive affect toward AI-generated images was the strongest predictor of preference. Real-scene color, natural elements, and uniqueness reduced the odds of choosing AI-generated versions, whereas AI-generated form and structure, natural elements, and changeability increased them. The study contributes a replicable workflow linking generative AI with emotional preference measurement, offering a structured approach for evidence-based design review. The findings are preliminary due to the single case, modest sample, and reliance on static images. Future work should extend to diverse urban contexts and multimodal evaluation. © 2026 The Authors.

Author full names: Aguirre-Suárez, T. (60994559300); Pérez-Chiquito, M. (60994192400); Cochea-Tomalá, H. (60994192500); Escandón-Panchana, P. (57200918370)
Title: A bibliometric and systematic analysis of artificial intelligence and the transition towards smart geotourism
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: The rapid digital transformation of tourism has positioned artificial intelligence as a key enabler of destination intelligence, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable tourism management. Although artificial intelligence has become increasingly important in smart tourism research, its application to geotourism remains fragmented, particularly regarding geoheritage conservation, geodiversity management, and territorial planning. Employing a retrospective approach, this study delineates the developmental trajectory of artificial intelligence applications in sustainable tourism while interrogating their integration into the paradigm of smart geotourism. An integrated bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review were conducted to evaluate scientific developments and empirical applications of artificial intelligence within geotourism contexts. Such findings delineate a burgeoning field of inquiry structured through the convergence of three intersecting axes: technological advancement, analytical intelligence, and visitor-focused experiential paradigms. The review study identified four principal domains through which artificial intelligence contributes to geotourism: predictive analytics, smart destination management, geoheritage interpretation, and environmental monitoring and geoconservation. The findings further highlight significant regional differences in technological adoption and reveal a limited integration between artificial intelligence, geoheritage conservation, and sustainable territorial governance. Based on these findings, the study proposes a smart geotourism framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning within a unified conceptual structure. By delivering an integrated appraisal of artificial intelligence within geotourism, this study contributes to extant scholarship by conceptualizing artificial intelligence beyond its technical dimensions—positioning it as a fundamental enabler of empirical territorial planning, destination analytics, and the sustainable preservation of geological resources. The study objectives were to propose an integrated conceptual framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning to support the development of smart geotourism. © 2027 The author(s). Authors: Mohammadi V.; Sadeghi Bigham B.
Title: Trust fusion: a weighted multi-perspective framework for ECG anomaly detection in IoMT
Abstract: Continuous electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments faces a fundamental precision–sensitivity trade–off. Standalone reconstruction–based detectors achieve high specificity but miss subtle anomalies, while geometric detectors capture rare patterns but generate excessive false alarms. This paper presents a hybrid Trust Fusion framework that resolves this trade–off through linearly weighted integration of an LSTM–Autoencoder, a 6–band Isolation Forest, and Z–score statistical validation, augmented by a clinically motivated Label–Free Adaptive Recovery mechanism that reclassifies borderline missed arrhythmias closest to the decision boundary. Title: The adopter's conundrum: Institutional drivers and performance outcomes of innovation in travel distribution

Title: Scenic spot crowd flow prediction: Combining large language model semantic understanding and spatio-temporal network
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of tourist flows is crucial for urban planning, transportation management, and overcrowding prevention. Tourism demand is highly sensitive to external stimuli, often leading to abrupt and irregular fluctuations that are difficult to quantify using existing methods. To address this issue, we propose an event-aware dynamic spatiotemporal network (EAD-STN) that integrates large language model embeddings with dynamic spatiotemporal graph modeling. External factors are encoded into high-dimensional representations to capture their impacts on visitor demand. The model further incorporates both dynamic spatial adjacency and LLM-derived semantic adjacency among attractions, enabling a more comprehensive characterization of inter-attraction relationships. Experiments on real-world datasets from Beijing and Shanghai demonstrate that EAD-STN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Authors: Bisht A.
Title: Silent Valleys: Unraveling the Causes and Strategic Pathways for Reverse Migration in Hilly Regions of Uttarakhand
Abstract: This study examines out-migration and the prospects for sustainable reverse migration in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand, addressing three objectives: identifying the main drivers of migration, synthesizing reinforcement strategies to reduce distress migration and support return, and linking causes and responses within a human-environment systems perspective. We conducted a scoping review of 68 studies (2010–2025) using a structured screening and synthesis process. Findings show that migration results from interacting economic, infrastructural, geographical, policy, and social pressures rather than a single employment factor, with reinforcing feedback effects such as land abandonment, declining agricultural viability, weakened local services, and heightened human-wildlife conflict that can intensify future migration. The study synthesizes an evidence-graded portfolio of interventions: livelihood diversification, agri-value-chain strengthening, digital access and skills, climate-resilient infrastructure, community-based and eco-tourism, and improved local service delivery and governance support, contributing an integrated conceptual framework linking drivers, feedback loops, and intervention levers for coordinated, place-based mountain-region planning. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Experimental study on high-pressure constant-volume combustion of ultra-lean methane-air mixtures under different ignition delay times
Abstract: Low-concentration coal mine gas is typically characterized by low combustion rate and significant heat losses. Studies on ultra-lean methane-air combustion under high-pressure constant-volume and turbulent conditions remain limited. This study experimentally investigates turbulent combustion characteristics and heat losses under elevated initial pressures, where turbulence intensity is regulated by adjusting the ignition delay time t d. Results reveal that varying t d non–monotonically affects both flame development and rapid combustion stages. While turbulence plays a primary role in shortening the rapid combustion duration, its intensification does not monotonically reduce heat losses, since the flow field influences both the convective heat transfer coefficient and the temperature difference between combustion products and chamber walls. At t d = 1 s, weak turbulence attenuates the promoting effect of temperature rise on flame development, with the most pronounced effect observed at P 0 = 0.5 MPa and 0.7 MPa. Further turbulence intensification yields a greater reduction in combustion duration than that resulting from the combined effect of temperature rise and weak turbulence. Within initial pressures of 0.3–0.7 MPa, the coupled effects of temperature rise and turbulence reduce the combustion duration by 20.6%–54.0% and increase P max by 10.3%–19.2% relative to quiescent combustion. An initial pressure of 0.6 MPa is found to minimize heat losses for the 6 vol% methane–air mixture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mapping the intellectual structure of digital transformation research in SMEs: A decade of performance-oriented studies
Abstract: Despite their vital contribution to worldwide economic progress, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are vulnerable to environmental fluctuations, resource limitations, and swift technological shifts. In this context, digital transformation has emerged as a critical strategic mechanism through which firms seek to enhance competitiveness, resilience, and organizational outcomes. Although this topic has attracted considerable scholarly attention in recent years, the available literature is dispersed across different academic fields, theoretical viewpoints, and methodologies, making it difficult to gain a holistic understanding of the area's intellectual organization and progression. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to examine digital transformation and firm-level outcomes in small business contexts from January 2016 to January 2026. Bibliographic data were retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix through its Biblioshiny interface and VOSviewer. A final dataset of 186 peer-reviewed journal articles was examined using descriptive statistics, keyword co-occurrence analysis, bibliographic coupling, citation analysis, thematic mapping, and research trend analysis. The results indicate a strong and accelerating publication trend, with an annual growth rate of 17.46, particularly since 2020, highlighting the increasing strategic importance of digital technologies in response to economic disruptions and uncertainty. The analysis identifies four major thematic clusters: (1) performance-oriented outcomes, (2) technology - and capability-driven transformation, (3) organizational and sustainability-related performance, and (4) strategic and Industry 4.0-oriented transformation. In addition, emerging themes include digital readiness, dynamic capabilities, and business model innovation. While the literature frequently associates digital transformation with improved organizational outcomes, the findings also reveal persistent heterogeneity in results and highlight substantial risks and failure rates, especially among resource-constrained firms. By mapping the intellectual foundations, thematic structure, and evolution of this research domain, the study provides an integrative overview that supports theory development and informs future empirical research. The results also offer valuable insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers who seek to understand and guide digital transformation initiatives in small business contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: From giant components to communities: community-level insights for prioritizing interventions within large clusters of HIV-1 transmission networks
Abstract: Large clusters in HIV-1 molecular networks contain a substantial proportion of people living with HIV and dominate local epidemics; however, their large size and complex structure pose a challenge for effective public health interventions. We developed an analytical framework to partition the large cluster into small groups for precise intervention. In the HIV-1 CRF07_BC molecular transmission network in Guangzhou, China (2008-2020), a giant component (681 members) was partitioned into 34 communities with dense internal and sparse external links. All 378 inter-community links involved high-centrality members from Community 1 ( P < 0.001) and phylogenetic analysis identified Community 1 as the most likely ancestral source of the giant component (marginal probability = 0.989). Exponential random graph models (ERGMs) revealed significant homophily effect among members with specific characteristics in the giant component and its large communities, highlighting potential outbreaks within specific subgroups. Partitioning giant components into communities may be a promising approach to help develop community-level interventions and could improve the effectiveness of interventions targeted at large clusters. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Liu Y.; Tian Y.
Title: Influence of threshold-activated linear decay behaviors on information propagation in social networks
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: The social propagation of behaviors is influenced not only by interpersonal interactions, but also by individual psychological dynamics. This study presents a threshold-activated linear decay behaviors (TALDB) that incorporates both social and psychological factors to investigate propagation phenomena in social networks. Through edge-based partition theory and numerical simulations, the results demonstrate that TALDB can induce a range of phenomena, including continuous phase transitions, discontinuous phase transitions, and static behaviors. As the values of behavioral parameters increase, the behavioral intensity weakens, leading to a shift from continuous to discontinuous to static phase transitions. The findings reveal a phase transition crossover in how TALDB changes: the high-intensity behaviors promote the propagation of behaviors, while the weak behaviors delay propagation, decreasing gradually and more slowly. These insights extend the theoretical understanding of how individual psychology affects propagation dynamics in social systems, providing a mechanism for targeted interventions in complex networks. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: A method for predicting essential proteins in heterogeneous networks based on discrete quantum walk
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: Essential proteins are an important material basis for life activities, and their accurate identification is crucial for understanding cellular functions and biological mechanisms. Although there are already various experimental and computational methods for detecting essential proteins, most of them are limited to a single network or local features, making it difficult to integrate heterogeneous network information, and they lack accuracy and robustness in complex networks. Therefore, we propose a heterogeneous network essential protein prediction algorithm based on discrete-time quantum walk (HNDQW). This algorithm first constructs a protein–domain heterogeneous network according to the original protein–protein interaction (PPI) network and the known relationships between proteins and domains. Then, it constructs a quantum weighted transition matrix of the heterogeneous network by integrating network topological features and multi-source biological information. Finally, it constructs a discrete-time quantum walk model and performs quantum walks on the heterogeneous network. The average probability of reaching each vertex is selected to represent the essentiality score of the protein node. By ranking the proteins, the top-ranked proteins are selected as candidate essential proteins. In addition, to evaluate the performance of the algorithm, we compare this method with 13 other different methods on three datasets, DIP, Krogan and Gavin. The experimental results show that this method achieves recognition accuracies of 94.12%, 63.35%, 56.82% and 51.26% among the top 1%, 15%, 20% and 25% of candidate proteins, respectively. It also performs well under multiple evaluation metrics, with prediction accuracy exceeding that of the other 13 methods, and can effectively identify essential proteins. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: Domain-adaptive probabilistic broad learning with evidence fusion for multimodal biomedical vigilance estimation
Abstract: In multimodal biomedical data analysis, wearable physiological signals provide complementary neural and oculomotor measurements for safety-critical vigilance monitoring. Joint analysis is complicated by differences between electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-movement (EM) streams in their distributions, dimensionalities, noise characteristics, and informativeness across subjects. Existing single-modal and static fusion methods do not jointly address cross-subject distribution shifts and sample-specific evidence uncertainty. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a domain-adaptive probabilistic broad learning system with pseudo-view enhanced Dempster–Shafer evidence fusion (PBLS-DS) for multimodal biomedical vigilance estimation. PBLS-DS embeds marginal source–target alignment in closed-form BLS output optimization and transforms deterministic scores into normalized evidence assignments for Dempster fusion. In this formulation, the term probabilistic refers to evidence or belief assignments rather than calibrated posterior probabilities. Its fusion mechanism constructs a lightweight joint EEG–EM view and combines evidence through evidence-concentration discounting, sample-dependent subset selection, and Dempster fusion. Experiments on SEED-VIG show that PBLS-DS outperforms representative supervised learning, domain adaptation, and deep transfer learning baselines across multiple evaluation metrics while retaining low measured training and inference costs. Post-hoc contribution analyses further characterize complementary oculomotor and frequency-dependent EEG information. PBLS-DS therefore formulates wearable vigilance estimation as a multimodal biomedical pattern-recognition task under the evaluated cross-subject protocol. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The impact of technological developments on the changing role of HR(M): A scoping review and research agenda
Abstract: Due to technological developments, jobs disappear, new jobs arise, and existing jobs change. This leads to opportunities and challenges regarding human resource management (HRM) and the role of the HR function in the future of work. In this article, we explore how technological developments such as the use of smart technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and robotics influence HRM and the role of the HR function. Through a scoping review, we highlight the influence of technological developments across macro (societal), meso (organization/HRM) and micro (individual workers) level work themes. We specifically focus on the dynamic interplay between technological developments and HRM. At the meso level, the analysis zooms in on how technological developments influence HRM at the strategic, tactical, and operational levels within organizational contexts. Our findings inform a future research agenda comprising avenues aimed at deepening our understanding of the challenges and opportunities associated with technological change in the context of HRM. More specifically, we propose future research to explore how the HR function can prepare the organization, itself, and other stakeholders, including line managers and workers, for the impact of technological developments to enhance HRM for the greater good. Title: Robust hybrid graph fusion for multi-modal relation extraction via information bottleneck denoising
Abstract: Mainstream Multi-modal Relation Extraction (MRE) methods often suffer from performance degradation. This is due to inherent inconsistencies, or ”modal incongruity, between visual and textual modalities, leading to inaccurate predictions. To address this critical challenge, we propose IBHF, a novel framework that actively denoises multi-modal inputs to purify robust relational signals. The core of IBHF is its pioneering Hybrid Multi-modal Graph (HMG). This structure synergistically fuses a heterogeneous graph, which captures fine-grained pairwise interactions, with a hypergraph that models key high-order group semantics. Critically, we devise an innovative graph denoising framework, IB-GD. It applies the Information Bottleneck (IB) principle to a unique contrastive learning objective. This strategy compels the model to learn a representation that is highly informative for the MRE task but minimally dependent on the noisy input. This process effectively mitigates the negative impact of modal inconsistencies. Our unified framework is applicable to both entity-entity (EE-MRE) and the more challenging entity-object (EO-MRE) extraction tasks. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets, MNRE and MORE, demonstrate the superior performance of our IBHF. Notably, on the more challenging MORE dataset, IBHF achieves an F1-score of 72.59%, setting a new state-of-the-art with a significant margin of 2.34%. On the MNRE dataset, IBHF also delivers SOTA-level performance, reaching the highest accuracy and an F1-score of 89.91%. By combining a hybrid graph structure with an IB-based structural denoising strategy, IBHF offers a robust and effective paradigm for handling noisy, real-world multi-modal data. Copyright © 2026. Title: A tri-objective goal programming approach to generator maintenance scheduling

Title: Tracking fitness, comparing bodies: Social comparison and exercise activity among college students
Abstract: Wearable fitness trackers are widely used by college students to monitor exercise and promote healthy habits. Previous research has predominantly identified the positive role that fitness trackers have in users' exercise behavior. Guided by Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory, this study explored both positive and negative behaviors associated with wearable fitness trackers. A total of 253 college students completed a cross-sectional survey that examined associations among exercise tracking, exercise-related social media use, social comparison, exercise-related outcomes, mental health, and disordered eating. This study found students who tracked exercise behavior reported higher levels of exercise involvement, motivation, and positive exercise outcomes. Tracking was also associated with increased upward and downward social comparison, which can be harmful for some students, particularly for those who have been treated for an eating disorder. How often students share tracked exercise behavior on social media was not significantly related to most outcomes, suggesting frequency alone may not capture its relationship to mental health. Title: Empowering LLMs for biomedical information extraction with RAG-ICL and DFPO
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for biomedical information extraction (IE), but their application to named entity recognition (NER) and relation extraction (RE) remains limited by prototype selection, preference alignment, and structured-output validity. In this study, we formulate LLM-based biomedical IE as a structure-constrained pattern recognition problem and propose a framework centered on two complementary adaptation mechanisms. Retrieval-Augmented In-Context Learning (RAG-ICL) performs inference-time prototype selection by retrieving and reranking instance-specific demonstrations, enabling LLMs to use more relevant contextual examples without parameter updates. Dual-Phase Fine-tuning with Preference Optimization (DFPO) performs training-time parameter alignment through supervised fine-tuning, MFPEA-based structured preference data, DPO-Positive optimization, and post-finetuning. In addition, Dual-Mode Correction and Review (DMCR) is used as an auxiliary output-side verification module to improve parsability and reduce malformed structured predictions. Experiments across biomedical NER and RE benchmarks show that RAG-ICL improves over zero-shot and random/fixed ICL baselines, while DFPO consistently enhances extraction performance over supervised fine-tuning and representative biomedical IE systems. Further analyses demonstrate the importance of compact, relevant demonstrations, the incremental contribution of DFPO stages, and the practical trade-off between inference-time and training-time adaptation. These results suggest that decomposing LLM-based biomedical IE into prototype selection, preference-aware decision alignment, and structural verification provides an effective and coherent framework for schema-constrained biomedical text recognition. © 2026

Title: How to deal with AI technology anxiety and its negative consequences? The role of strengths-based leadership
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into hospitality operations, employees’ AI technology anxiety has emerged as a salient managerial concern. Title: Newly graduated nurses' experiences in internal medicine and surgical clinics after the earthquake
Abstract: Aim: To explore the experiences of newly graduated nurses working in internal medicine and surgical units in earthquake-affected regions. Background: The 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye severely disrupted healthcare services and increased the need for healthcare professionals in affected regions. Little is known about the experiences of newly graduated nurses as they begin their careers in disaster-affected settings. Methods: This qualitative descriptive phenomenological study used semi-structured interviews with 10 newly graduated nurses working in internal medicine and surgical units between February and August 2025. The interviews were conducted online, recorded, transcribed, thematically analysed, and reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research guidelines. Results: Six main themes and 14 sub-themes were identified: (1) assignment process and decision-making, involving perceived ease of appointment, obligation, family guidance, and social responsibility; (2) physiological and environmental challenges, including health, housing, basic needs and transportation problems; (3) psychological challenges, including adaptation difficulties, post-traumatic fears, and empathic burden from traumatic narratives; (4) social life challenges, characterised by limited social opportunities and gradual development of a new social life; (5) professional experiences, including inexperience, working with disaster-affected colleagues, and caring for earthquake-affected patients; and (6) recommendations for supporting newly graduated nurses. Conclusions: Beginning professional practice in a disaster-affected region created substantial environmental, psychological, social, and professional challenges for newly graduated nurses. These findings support the need for structured preparation and support to facilitate their adaptation to such settings. Implications for nursing and health policy: Newly graduated nurses assigned to disaster-affected regions should receive disaster preparedness training, structured orientation, and psychological and institutional support. Workforce planning should also ensure access to experienced nurses who can support newly graduated staff in high-risk settings. Title: Emotions in flipped and lecture-based math courses
Abstract: Background: Emotions play an important role in learning. Activating teaching methods, such as flipped learning, can provide positive learning experiences but also pose emotional challenges to students. Aims: This intensive longitudinal study investigated 1) how students’ emotional valence before a learning event, learning mode (individual, peer, teacher-led), teaching implementation (lecture-based vs. flipped), and physiological arousal (electrodermal activity, EDA) during the learning event related to emotional valence after a learning event, and 2) how EDA varies across within-event segments and teaching implementations during learning events. Sample: Participants were 69 students enrolled in an engineering mathematics course implemented either as lecture-based (n = 34) or flipped learning (n = 35). Methods: Students reported their emotional states via a smartphone application and wore smart rings to measure EDA. A series of multilevel binomial logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models were analyzed across 546 learning events, totaling 827 h of data. Results: Positive pre-event emotional valence predicted positive post-event emotional valence. Teacher-led events were associated with more positive post-event emotional valence than individual events, particularly in the lecture-based group. The main effect of the teaching implementation was not significant. EDA did not show robust associations with post-event emotional valence; however, lecture-based events showed a clearer decline in EDA across event segments than flipped learning events. Conclusions: The results highlight the importance of supporting social and individual learning processes and examining physiological arousal as a temporal learning-event process rather than a simple proxy for post-event emotional valence. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Neuroendocrine and circuit remodeling under chronic social stress
Abstract: Social stress has emerged as one of the most impactful environmental risk factors contributing to psychiatric disorders in modern societies. Although acute stress responses are adaptive mechanisms that promote survival and homeostasis, chronic social stress induces maladaptive neurobiological changes that culminate in pathological behavioral phenotypes. Accumulating evidence from rodent studies demonstrates that chronic social stress reshapes neural circuits and disrupts neuroendocrine regulation. In this review, we summarize and compare major rodent models including early life stress, social isolation, chronic social defeat stress, and chronic subordinate colony housing, and synthesize how these paradigms differentially engage the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis and monoaminergic systems, including serotonergic, noradrenergic, and dopaminergic circuits, as well as emerging modulators such as endocannabinoids and neuropeptide Y. Because these paradigms engage distinct developmental windows and have been validated predominantly in males, we explicitly evaluate outcomes as a function of age at exposure and sex. We further integrate these neurochemical alterations into a synaptic and cell-type-specific framework of cortico-limbic circuit remodeling linking excitation/inhibition imbalance and astrocytic dysregulation to the divergence between susceptible and resilient phenotypes. We introduce allostatic load as an integrated framework linking cumulative, paradigm-specific stress burdens to vulnerability and resilience, and highlight active, compensatory neuroendocrine and circuit-level mechanisms that confer resilience. We propose that chronic social stress represents not a simple neurotransmitter deficit, but a dysregulation of neural circuits and neuroendocrine plasticity, providing a systems-level perspective of stress-related mental illness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Newcomers help most after being helped, veterans do not: Evidence from Stack Overflow
Abstract: Whether people who receive help online go on to help others is an open question. Prior observational studies report mixed results, and designs that ignore prior user activity may overstate reciprocity. We develop a matched difference-in-differences survival analysis of over 21 million Stack Overflow questions, comparing users whose questions were answered with propensity-score-matched users whose questions were not. We don't ask broadly whether reciprocity works in general, but locate the narrow conditions under which it affects user behavior. Users whose questions were answered helped others slightly more often (increment at answer arrival, hazard ratio [HR] = 1.049, 95% CI [1.044, 1.054]). The response depended on tenure: new users responded most (HR = 1.071 in the first week, 95% CI [1.056, 1.086]), while the longest-tenured users did not respond measurably. The tenure gradient is the most robust pattern we find. Timing mattered too, though far more fragilely: users answered within 30 to 60 min responded most strongly, while answers under 30 min show no elevation. Most of our data predate 2020, and the generalized reciprocity effect among new users does not survive a split at 2020, so these estimates largely reflect a pre-generative-AI baseline. We review gratitude, moral obligation, social expectation, and incentive displacement as possible psychological mechanisms but cannot measure them. On Stack Overflow, generalized reciprocity is less a general driver of cooperation than a recruitment channel for contributions from new users: designers gain most by getting newcomers’ questions answered. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Factors associated with installed photovoltaic capacity in Australia across small, medium, and large-scale systems
Abstract: Australia, as a global leader in photovoltaic deployment, has attracted significant research attention, has attracted significant research attention into factors associated with PV installation patterns. Previous studies have highlighted the role of early adopters, family wealth, and education, and have identified financial parameters (such as investment cost, internal rate of return, and net present value), social parameters (including household income and demographics), and environmental factors as relevant correlates of PV adoption. However, how these correlations vary across different system sizes, small, medium, and large, has not been systematically examined using historical data. In this study, historical time-series data on installed PV capacity in Australia, categorized by system-size groups across five states from 2013/14 to 2024/25 are collected, and the correlation of 4 groups of economic, market, financial, and affordability variables with PV installed patterns is examined. The results indicate that different system-size categories exhibit distinct association patterns. Small-scale adoption shows higher correlations with electricity prices and unit costs, medium-scale systems are more correlated with income and affordability indicators, and large-scale systems are more correlated with long-term financial returns and market incentives. The main contribution of this study is a systematic comparison of association patterns across PV system-size categories, highlighting how selected parameters are differently correlated with Installed PV capacity across system sizes and states. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Negotiation impasses as meaningful outcomes: How AI is changing the cost structure of walking away
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is often expected to improve negotiation by strengthening information processing and analytical consistency. We argue that its effects on impasses are more selective. Extending the impasse cause, type, and resolution (ICTR) model, we distinguish two pathways. The first pathway is analytical augmentation: AI can reduce unwanted impasses caused by misunderstanding, poor option generation, and coordination failure. The second pathway runs through behavioral flexibility: Humans sometimes reach mutually acceptable agreements through aspiration adjustment, face-saving, and relational repair. Systems configured to apply stable decision thresholds and optimize focal-party outcomes without relational objectives reduce this flexibility and can thereby increase forced impasses. Which pathway dominates depends on AI's role as advisor or counterpart; its objective, training, and prompt; and whether agreement primarily requires analytical problem solving or interpersonal flexibility. These predictions concern system behavior, not whether AI experiences fatigue or social pressure: systems can be designed to respond to relational cues without experiencing them. Wanted impasses depend on both parties' underlying preferences, which AI does not change; AI instead helps negotiators recognize incompatibility sooner and justify walking away more openly. AI therefore changes the composition and meaning of impasses rather than uniformly increasing or decreasing agreement. Remaining impasses may reveal genuine incompatibility, but they may also reflect misspecified objectives or failures to encode principals' relational and economic costs. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Ultrasonic vocalizations in mice: Effects of sex, age, and environmental conditions
Abstract: Ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) are key communicative signals in rodents, reflecting developmental stage, sex, and social context. Most studies on female mice USVs focus on their effects on male behavior or pup interactions, while few address vocalizations unrelated to reproduction or maternal care. The present study aimed to fill this gap by characterizing USVs in C57BL/6 mice of both sexes at different developmental stages and under distinct contexts. Neonatal (PND 3–4), postnatal (PND 13–14), adolescent (PND 30–45), and adult (PND 90) mice were evaluated in various contexts. Our results reveal a dynamic transitional pattern in USV production. Neonates of both sexes emitted a high number of calls, which markedly declined after the postnatal period, indicating a behavioral shift in communication. Sexual dimorphism emerged in adulthood, as females partially recovered vocalization rates, whereas males maintained low emission levels after adolescence. Although no significant differences in USVs were detected between stressed and non-stressed adolescents, some stressed individuals completely ceased vocalizing, suggesting a strong individual variability in response to acute stress, independently of sex. In adulthood, males and females exhibited distinct vocal strategies depending on the social or non-social context. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of USVs as sensitive markers of developmental, sex-dependent, and context-specific communicative behaviors, providing valuable insights for refining animal models in behavioral neuroscience. © 2026

Authors: Szymkowiak A.; Madias K.
Title: Do users trade performance for eco-visibility? Digital pollution awareness and stated preferences for social media platform configurations
Abstract: Digital platforms face growing pressure to demonstrate environmental responsibility, yet users’ preferences for eco-visible features remain underexplored relative to functional attributes. Using a full-factorial rating-based within-subject conjoint survey with a UK sample (N = 345) recruited to match national census distributions of age, sex, and ethnicity, combined with hierarchical linear modelling, this study decomposes willingness to use social media platforms across four attributes: media quality, loading speed, eco-visibility, and advertising frequency. Results show that technical attributes — media quality (relative importance = 34.9%) and loading speed (34.5%) — jointly dominate eco-visibility (8.1%), revealing a persistent performance-over-sustainability hierarchy in elicited trade-off preferences. A full 4 × 4 cross-level moderation analysis incorporating all 16 attribute-by-moderator interactions with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction identifies advertising receptivity — rather than green self-identity or environmental awareness — as the strongest individual-difference moderator, showing a dual pattern: it simultaneously attenuates the reduced-ads utility and amplifies the loading-speed premium. Green self-identity attenuates the media-quality premium but does not amplify eco-visibility utility; none of the eco-visibility moderations — by green self-identity, social comparison orientation, or digital environmental attitude — is confirmed. Exploratory benefit segmentation identifies three preference profiles — Technical Optimizers, Eco-Aware Pragmatists, and Ad-Averse Minimalists — revealing a sign reversal in eco-visibility utility across profiles. Theoretical and practical implications for sustainable platform design, multiple-comparison practices in conjoint moderation research, and green digital marketing are discussed. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Fecker D.
Title: Why they come (back): Motive clusters of seasonal employees and their multiple workplace commitments
Abstract: This study develops seasonal employee typologies for the Alpine tourism and hospitality sector by connecting motives for seasonal work with varying levels of different workplace commitments and return intention. Conceptualizing the destination as an analytical lens rather than merely context, this study examines how employees’ social, economic, and leisure motives affect their commitment to the organization, coworkers, job, and destination. Drawing on survey data from 381 hospitality employees in an Alpine destination in Austria, cluster analysis, analysis of variance, and post hoc tests were applied. The analysis identified four employee clusters (lifestyle seekers, dedicated professionals, practical earners, and social contributors) that significantly differ in their motivational profiles, commitment patterns, and demographic characteristics. The findings demonstrate that commitment among seasonal employees extends beyond the organization and differs across motive-based segments. These differences may shape guest interactions and service delivery, ultimately impacting service quality, visitor satisfaction, and overall destination performance. By integrating a motive-based segmentation with a multi-target commitment perspective, this study advances research on seasonal tourism employment and underscores how destination-specific contexts impact employee attitudes and behaviors. The results offer insights for adapting recruitment and retention strategies to distinct employee profiles in seasonal hospitality settings. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Scale-armor-inspired rigid-soft-coupled heterogeneous structures: Additive manufacturing and tribological mechanisms
Abstract: Biological scale armor offers a natural strategy for reconciling lightweight design with wear resistance through rigid-soft synergy. However, the pronounced mismatch in composition and mechanical properties between rigid and soft materials often causes interfacial incompatibility and stress concentration, hindering the precise fabrication and tribological optimization of bioinspired rigid-soft coupled structures. Inspired by the wear-resistant and drag-reducing structure of desert lizard scales, we construct a bioinspired rigid-soft coupled structure (BRSCS) by multimaterial additive manufacturing and systematically investigate how structural parameters affect its friction and wear behavior. The results indicate that incorporating a flexible constituent phase promotes deformation accommodation and subsurface loading redistribution, thereby improving the tribological performance of the material under sliding conditions. Compared with pure rigid resin, the BRSCS reduces the coefficient of friction ( COF ) by 25.7% and the wear rate by up to 62.6% under a representative normal load of 20 N and the present dry reciprocating sliding conditions. Combined mechanical, dynamic mechanical, and wear-morphology analyses indicate that the tribological response is associated with the evolution of the interfacial contact states under different rigid-soft configurations. This work provides structural-design guidance for additively manufactured polymer-based bioinspired materials with potential lightweight structural and wear-resistant applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Fang J.; Pan Y.
Title: Not alone: How group photos enhance audience responses to virtual influencers
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Although marketers increasingly use virtual influencers to engage consumers, concerns about authenticity continue to limit their effectiveness. This research examines whether group photos can make virtual influencers appear more socially connected and authentic, thereby improving audience responses. We propose that, compared with no-person images or solo photos, group photos provide visual social cues that place virtual influencers in recognizable interpersonal contexts and make them appear more socially connected in shared experiences. Across one large-scale field study and two experiments, we test this proposition. Study 1 draws on a large-scale Instagram dataset of 17,878 posts from 109 virtual influencers collected between 2023 and 2026, with the main analyses based on 8558 non-video posts and finds that group photos receive higher post engagement than no-person images and solo photos. Study 2 provides controlled experimental evidence consistent with this effect and suggests that perceived social connectedness and perceived authenticity sequentially account for the relationship between group photos and favorable post evaluations. Study 3 identifies virtual influencer type as an important boundary condition: group photos are more effective for human-like virtual influencers, whereas this advantage weakens for cartoon-like virtual influencers. These findings contribute to research on virtual influencer humanization and authenticity by showing that visual social connectedness can make virtual influencers appear more socially embedded, more authentic, and more favorably evaluated. The results also offer actionable insights for marketers and content creators seeking to design virtual influencer content that elicits more favorable audience responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Pursuit and burnout: How goal orientation influences academic pressure in students
Abstract: This study comprehensively investigated the relationship between students' goal orientation and their corresponding experience of academic pressure, emphasizing how distinct motivational frameworks impact psychological stress within modern academic settings. Recognizing that goal-driven behavior can simultaneously inspire exceptional achievement and inadvertently heighten emotional strain, this research aimed to shed light on how students' varied motivational orientations structurally align with their perceived academic demands. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed to capture these dynamics, involving a sample of 225 college students systematically selected through simple random sampling techniques. Data collection was facilitated using two standardized and highly reliable instruments: the Academic Stress Scale and the Achievement Goal Questionnaire-Revised (AGQ-R). Descriptive statistics were utilized to examine the general baseline trends in students' goal orientation and stress levels, while Spearman's rank-order correlation determined the exact nature, strength, and direction of the relationship between the two primary variables. Findings revealed that students generally demonstrated a high level of goal orientation, with a particularly strong emphasis placed on mastery-oriented goals. Concurrently, participants reported notable academic pressure stemming from intense personal expectations and the perceived social importance of academic success. Crucially, a significant positive correlation emerged between goal orientation and academic pressure, demonstrating that increased achievement motivation is frequently accompanied by heightened student stress. These results clearly indicate that while a strong goal orientation contributes positively to students' engagement and drive, it may also manifest as severe emotional strain if not properly balanced. Understanding this complex psychological dynamic is essential for designing supportive academic environments, offering vital insights for educators, counselors, and institutional policymakers aiming to cultivate a holistic learning climate that encourages high achievement without compromising long-term student health. Authors: Qi B.; Sheng T.; Xu S.; Dong F.
Title: Impact of distributor zone design on flow uniformity in metal foam cooling flow fields of PEMFC
Abstract: In a proton exchange membrane fuel cell, the distributor zone of a metal foam cooling flow field directly affects coolant distribution among the cooling branches and the resulting temperature uniformity. Based on the optimized structural parameters of the main metal foam cooling flow field, a three-dimensional numerical model incorporating the core components of a single cell and the distributor zone was developed. This study systematically investigated how three key design parameters, namely distributor zone shape, circular hole diameter, and number of circular holes, regulate coolant flow uniformity. The circular structure was retained as the baseline configuration because of its favorable thermal characteristics and geometric adjustability. The results showed that the optimal circular hole diameter was 1.5 mm, yielding an average mass flow deviation of 26.05 %. With this diameter fixed, the configuration with 14 circular holes exhibited the lowest average mass flow deviation and coefficient of variation among the examined cases, at 17.93 % and 27.26 %, respectively, thereby achieving the best trade-off between flow uniformity and hydraulic resistance. This study clarifies how the structural parameters of the distributor zone regulate coolant distribution and provides key technical support for the integrated design and performance optimization of cooling systems at the stack level. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A hierarchical federated learning trusted collaboration and auditable mechanism based on DAG–consortium chain hybrid ledger
Abstract: Hierarchical federated learning (HFL) reduces wide-area communication by introducing edge aggregation, but it also creates additional trust boundaries: malicious or low-quality client updates may contaminate edge models, edge-side admission and aggregation decisions are difficult to verify, and conventional training logs provide limited support for end-to-end accountability. At each edge, a bounded client trust score combines historical reputation, exponential timeliness, alignment with a clean root update, and contribution quality. The score drives dynamic admission, median-norm clipping, and a hybrid aggregation rule that combines coordinate-wise trimmed mean with trust–sample weighted averaging. Meanwhile, client-, edge-, and global-level commitments are linked into a cross-layer evidence chain: the DAG layer records high-frequency update metadata, whereas a permissioned consortium blockchain anchors lower-frequency governance and audit records. Experiments with three random seeds on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 cover 20/50/100 clients, multiple robust baselines, label-flipping, backdoor, free-rider, collusion, Sybil, and adaptive attacks. Under 30% label flipping, the proposed method achieves (Formula presented) final accuracy on MNIST and exhibits dataset-dependent trade-offs on Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10. At 100 clients, it reduces accounted cross-layer tensor communication from 127.44 to 95.12 MB/round, at the cost of increasing round time from 7.38 to 10.05 s. A Hyperledger Fabric v2.5.14 prototype further processes 6400 audit-record submission attempts with a 99.734% success rate; with a 256-B payload and concurrency 10, it reaches 32.70 tx/s with 304.25 ms mean commit latency. Title: AI-driven cultural and creative packaging design and user purchase intention: AI-disclosure perspective based on SEM-ANN hybrid analysis
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Generative AI has introduced new possibilities for cultural and creative packaging design. This study examines how cultural symbol compatibility, design innovation, and aesthetic experience are associated with purchase intention through functional value, emotional value, social value, and epistemic value. Perceived factual disclosure and perceived narrative disclosure are further incorporated as moderators. A combined SEM-ANN approach is used to examine the linear relationships and nonlinear predictive importance of the study variables. The results indicate that the three perceived design attributes are indirectly associated with user purchase intention through multiple consumption-value pathways, although statistical support varies across the specific indirect effects. The principal theoretical contribution is to identify AI disclosure as a differentiated boundary condition in the conversion of consumption value into purchase intention. Perceived factual disclosure does not significantly moderate the relationships involving functional value or social value. Perceived narrative disclosure is associated with a weaker relationship between emotional value and purchase intention and a stronger relationship between epistemic value and purchase intention. Title: Coupled convection–radiation heat transfer and optimization in microscale fin structures
Abstract: With the increasing power density of electronic devices, effective thermal management is essential for maintaining performance and reliability. Although air-cooled heat sinks have been extensively investigated, studies have primarily focused on structural optimization and convective heat transfer, while the contribution of surface radiation has received comparatively limited attention in microscale thermal management. This study investigates a backside-integrated air-cooled heat sink, with particular emphasis on the coupled effects of forced convection and surface radiation at the microscale. Comparative analysis shows that the parallel plate fin structure provides the best heat dissipation performance, while fin optimization reveals a trade-off between heat transfer enhancement and flow resistance. Furthermore, increasing the inlet velocity effectively enhances convective heat transfer and reduces the chip temperature, but the cooling benefit gradually diminishes beyond approximately 1.2 m/s, whereas flow-related energy consumption continues to increase. Meanwhile, radiative heat transfer is strongly influenced by flow conditions and input power, with surface emissivity playing an increasingly important role under low velocity and high input power conditions. At an inlet velocity of 0.2 m/s, increasing the emissivity from 0.05 to 0.95 reduces the maximum chip temperature by approximately 10.8 °C at 0.1 W and 33.3 °C at 0.3 W. At ε = 0.95 and v = 0.2 m/s, the radiative contribution reaches 32.0%, 34.3%, and 36.4% at input powers of 0.1 W, 0.2 W and 0.3 W, respectively. These results demonstrate that appropriate matching of inlet velocity and surface emissivity can effectively regulate heat dissipation while reducing reliance on excessive airflow. Title: Digital echoes of death and dying distress among family members of intensive care unit patients: A qualitative study
Abstract: Objectives: To explore how ICU family members experience and articulate death and dying distress through social media narratives. Methods: This study employed a qualitative design informed by the socioecological model and a constructivist epistemological perspective. Data were drawn from publicly available posts on REDnote (also known as Xiaohongshu), a popular Chinese social media platform, using a keyword-based search targeting ICU-related experiences. After screening for relevance, 317 posts comprising 124,906 Chinese characters were retained for analysis. Reflexive thematic analysis was conducted following Braun and Clarke's six-phase approach, emphasizing researchers' active role in co-constructing themes through iterative engagement with the data. Results: Eight themes were identified across three socioecological levels: at the microsystem, emotional volatility and multi-dimensional distress reflected intense emotional experiences and endurance; at the mesosystem, shared burdens, concentrated family responsibilities, and support beyond blood ties captured family dynamics under strain; at the macrosystem, digital spaces, institutional barriers, and financial pressures shaped broader sociocultural experiences of death and dying distress. Conclusion: This study provides new insights into the distress of ICU family members facing death and dying. It highlights that such distress is not solely an individual psychological reaction, but an experience of endurance shaped by family relationships and broader social and institutional contexts. Implications for clinical practice: These findings suggest that nursing interventions could adopt a systems-oriented approach to support family functioning, address relational and institutional challenges, and extend support beyond the bedside to include digital spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: When culture meets citizenship: The moderating role of instructional leadership
Abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of organizational culture and instructional leadership in shaping the organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) of high school teachers, as well as to explain the social mechanisms underlying this relationship. Specifically, this study answers questions regarding the extent to which organizational culture influences teachers' OCB, the role of instructional leadership in this relationship, and why statistically significant patterns emerge in the context of school organizations. The qualitative stage was carried out through semi structured interviews to deepen and explain the quantitative findings. The results show that organizational culture has a significant effect on teachers' OCB, while instructional leadership has no significant direct or moderating effect. This indicates that cultural factors play a more dominant role than formal leadership practices in influencing teachers’ discretionary behaviors.Qualitative findings explain that teachers' OCB develops as a result of the internalization of collective values, trust, and peer relationships that are deeply rooted in school culture, while instructional leadership is perceived more as an administrative practice than an empowering pedagogical relationship. This study makes a theoretical contribution by repositioning organizational culture as the main mechanism of social exchange in the formation of teachers' OCB, as well as emphasizing the contextual and contingent nature of instructional leadership in educational organizations. In addition, the study highlights the importance of strengthening value-based school culture to sustain teachers’ professional commitment and collaboration. Title: Reliability and Validity of Swedish Versions of the Diabetes Self-Management Questionnaire and the Diabetes Distress Scale
Abstract: Objectives Self-management is essential in diabetes care but can be demanding. Diabetes distress may impair glycemic control, increase complications, and reduce quality of life. This study evaluated the psychometric properties of the Swedish versions of the Diabetes Self-Management Questionnaire (DSMQ) and the Diabetes Distress Scale (DDS-17). Methods Adults with type 2 diabetes ( n = 192) participated in this cross-sectional study with a test-retest design. The instruments were translated using forward-backward translation and tested with Cronbach’s alpha (α), intraclass and Spearman’s correlation coefficients, and confirmatory factor analysis. Results Cronbach’s α for the DSMQ was 0.82 (subscales 0.10-0.79). The subscale Healthcare use had an α of 0.10. Cronbach’s α for the DDS was 0.93 (subscales 0.85-0.89). Test-retest reliability measured with the intraclass correlation coefficient showed an agreement of 0.87 for the DSMQ and 0.84 for the DDS. Convergent validity tested with Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient showed a small correlation between the DSMQ total score and HbA1c ( r = −0.23). The DDS showed a moderate correlation with the Perceived Stress Scale ( r = 0.38). Structural validity was assessed with confirmatory factor analysis and showed an acceptable fit for the tested 3-factor solution of the DSMQ (comparative fit index 0.899, Tucker-Lewis Index 0.858, root mean square error of approximation 0.082, and standardized root mean square residual 0.060) and for the proposed 4-factor solution of the DDS (comparative fit index 0.917, Tucker-Lewis Index 0.900, root mean square error of approximation 0.091, and standardized root mean square residual 0.063). Conclusions The DSMQ appears reliable and valid, with reservations regarding 1 subscale, whereas the DDS-17 appears both reliable and valid, demonstrating satisfactory psychometric properties for the Swedish type 2 diabetes population. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A graph model for conflict resolution incorporating movement willingness intensity under linguistic uncertainty
Abstract: In the graph model for conflict resolution (GMCR), decision-makers (DMs) are required to express their preferences over feasible conflict states. Under uncertainty, however, such preferences are often difficult to quantify precisely and are more naturally represented by linguistic preference relations. To address this issue, this study develops a linguistic GMCR framework. Four linguistic stability concepts, namely linguistic Nash stability, linguistic sequential stability, linguistic symmetric metarationality, and linguistic general metarationality, are defined in logical form for general multi-DM conflicts. Corresponding matrix-based representations are then derived to facilitate stability computation. To capture heterogeneity in DMs’ willingness to transition between states, the framework is further extended by introducing a two-degree linguistic preference structure with two flexible formulations of the linguistic satisficing threshold. This extension distinguishes strong and mild transition willingness and yields three classes of linguistic stability, namely general linguistic stability, strong linguistic stability, and weak linguistic stability. The proposed framework is applied to the Elmira groundwater contamination conflict to demonstrate its practical applicability. Sensitivity and comparative analyses show that the two-degree linguistic framework identifies differentiated stability patterns that cannot be captured by single-threshold approaches, thereby providing a more refined basis for conflict diagnosis and resolution under linguistic uncertainty and heterogeneous transition willingness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: What drives versus what is required: Sufficient and necessary conditions for consumer intention in an unfamiliar wellness service
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Despite the growing importance of wellness and health tourism, little is known about how individuals who have never experienced thermal spa treatments form intentions toward such services. This study addresses this gap by mobilizing an extended Theory of Planned Behavior framework enriched with subjective knowledge and expected health benefits. Based on a large-scale survey of French non-users, we combine Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling and Necessary Condition Analysis to examine both enabling and constraining mechanisms of intention formation. The results show that all predictors contribute positively to intention, with subjective norm emerging as the most influential factor. However, the necessity analysis reveals a markedly different causal structure: only subjective norm, expected health benefits, and perceived behavioral control establish threshold conditions that must be satisfied for higher levels of intention to occur. In contrast, subjective knowledge and attitude, although significant, do not operate as indispensable conditions. These findings reveal an asymmetry between the factors that raise intention and those that set the threshold for it. They suggest that, in this context, intention depends on socially mediated validation, not on individual evaluation alone. For managers, the priority is the conditions that must be met for intention to form - social legitimacy, credible health benefits, and feasibility - rather than interventions, such as information or persuasion, that intensify intention only once those conditions are in place. © 2026 The Authors

Title: MLLM-based dual-stream synergistic model for multimodal aspect-based sentiment analysis
Abstract: Multimodal aspect-based sentiment analysis (MABSA) aims to determine the sentiment polarity associated with specific aspects in image–text content. While various approaches have been proposed to integrate multimodal information, most existing methods face two key challenges: (i) cross-modal interaction modeling may hinder the learning of syntactic structures; and (ii) external knowledge is often underutilized to enrich aspect context. To address these issues, we propose an MLLM-based dual-stream synergistic model (LLM-DSS). Specifically, to balance cross-modal interaction and syntactic structure learning, we adopt a parallel dual-stream architecture. We construct a knowledge-enhanced multimodal stream and a syntax-enhanced text stream and we use a synergistic alignment mechanism to promote cooperative modeling across streams. This design structurally decouples syntactic learning from cross-modal interaction, and we further design a Multi-View Syntactic Fusion (MSF) module to strengthen syntactic modeling. To supplement aspect context, we use an MLLM to generate aspect-related external knowledge and introduce a Context-aware Knowledge Filter (CKF) module to remove redundant knowledge. Experiments on two public MABSA datasets show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Yang Q.; Lu K.; Fang X.
Title: MAGE: A structural-prior-guided graph-language multimodal framework for business process anomaly detection
Abstract: Business process event logs record activities, resources, timestamps, and other process attributes, and therefore provide the basis for trace-level anomaly detection. Existing methods often lack a unified reference for normal behavior and do not explicitly coordinate structural deviations with semantic information. We propose MAGE, a structural-prior-guided graph-enhanced language embedding framework for business process anomaly detection. MAGE first constructs structural priors solely from normal traces in the training set, including normal directly-follows relations, trace-length statistics, and adjacent-event resource-switching statistics. It then compares each trace with these priors to generate structural deviation signals and constructs both an activity-resource-time-slice heterogeneous graph and a structure-aware textual representation. A heterogeneous graph Transformer extracts structural representations, while a LoRA-adapted Qwen3 model extracts semantic representations. Gated cross-attention fuses the two modalities for trace-level anomaly classification. The structural prior and graph self-supervised pretraining use only normal training traces, whereas the final multimodal classifier is jointly optimized on labeled training samples. Experiments on synthetic logs and public real event logs with controlled anomaly injection show that MAGE achieves the highest mean F1-scores of 0.872 and 0.860, respectively, among the compared methods under the evaluated settings. Ablation results further indicate that the structural prior, heterogeneous graph encoding, structure-aware prompting, and cross-modal fusion each contribute positively to F1-score under the evaluated settings. Together, these findings provide evidence for combining normal-process structural constraints with language-based semantic information in trace-level business process anomaly detection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Collective communication behavior driven by emotion: A systematic meta-analysis of the relationship between emotional arousal and rumor spreading
Abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to quantify the relationship between emotional arousal and rumor spreading. To this end, it integrated 30 empirical studies (55 effect sizes, N = 32,082) and employed a three-level meta-analytic model. Meta-regression examined the moderating effects of emotional valence, rumor-spreading channel, measurement dimension, and participants’ country, gender, and educational background. Results indicated a significant positive correlation between emotional arousal and rumor spreading (r =.294, p <.001). Moderation analysis further revealed that emotional valence significantly moderated this relationship (QM (1) = 4.20, p <.05), and positive emotional arousal showed a stronger correlation with rumor spreading. Additionally, participants’ country significantly moderated the relationship between emotional arousal and rumor spreading (QM (1) = 5.453, p <.05). The correlation between emotional arousal and rumor spreading was stronger among samples from developing countries relative to those from developed countries. Participants’ gender, educational background, rumor-spreading channel, and measurement dimension did not exert significant moderating effects. This indicates that rumor spreading is a collective social behavior, and its variation is significantly contingent on macro-level factors. Consequently, rumor governance represents a collective social endeavor. Theoretically, this meta-analysis identified emotion as a core construct correlated with rumor spreading, validating and expanding upon the existing theoretical framework. Title: Why identity matters for development
Abstract: This paper argues that while development economics has moved beyond income-based metrics toward a broader capabilities framework, it remains insufficiently attentive to the role of social identity in shaping life chances. Drawing on evidence from global gender disparities and caste-based inequalities in India, the paper demonstrates how identity-blind policies risk reinforcing structural hierarchies. Authors: Song L.; Li J.; Guan S.; Kong Y.
Title: Instance-Prototype Affinity Learning for Non-Exemplar Continual Graph Learning
Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNN) endure catastrophic forgetting, undermining their capacity to preserve previously acquired knowledge amid the assimilation of novel information. Rehearsal-based techniques revisit historical examples, adopted as a principal strategy to alleviate this phenomenon. However, memory explosion and privacy infringements impose significant constraints on their utility. Non-Exemplar methods circumvent the prior issues through Prototype Replay (PR), yet feature drift presents new challenges. In this paper, our empirical findings reveal that Prototype Contrastive Learning (PCL) exhibits less pronounced drift than conventional PR. Drawing upon PCL, we propose Instance-Prototype Affinity Learning (IPAL), a novel paradigm for Non-Exemplar Continual Graph Learning (NECGL). Exploiting graph structural information, we formulate Topology-Integrated Gaussian Prototypes (TIGP), guiding feature distributions toward high-impact nodes to augment the model's capacity for assimilating new knowledge. Instance-Prototype Affinity Distillation (IPAD) safeguards task memory by regularizing discontinuities in class relationships. Moreover, we embed a Decision Boundary Perception (DBP) mechanism within PCL, fostering greater inter-class discriminability. Evaluations on four node classification benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving a better trade-off between plasticity and stability.
