Title: Home economics and sustainable futures: A systematic literature review
Abstract: This study aims to systematically examine the development, thematic structure, and research trends in Home Economics from 2015 to 2024, with an emphasis on its contribution to a sustainable future. Through the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach with Scopus indexed article data sources, a total of 22 articles were analyzed using a combination of thematic synthesis methods and bibliometric visualization through the VOSviewer tool to identify developing research patterns, relationships, and clusters. The results of the analysis show that Home Economics research has shifted its focus from traditional discussions of household skills to a multidisciplinary approach that emphasizes sustainable education, family economic literacy, health, and social responsibility. The keyword mapping process uncovered to have five major clusters—education, sustainability, health, students, and digital literacy—that intersect to have within the broader framework of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD). Quantitatively, publication trends show a significant increase over the past three years (2021–2024), reflecting to have the increasing global interest in issues concerning welfare and sustainability in the field of education. The main findings also suggest that Home Economics is increasingly being positioned as a transformative discipline that integrates economic literacy, environmental awareness and social responsibility. Theoretically, the results of this study expand the framework of Home Economics as a humanistic and ecological science, while practically, the implications confirm the need for contextual, collaborative, and project-based curriculum and pedagogy innovations to address the challenges of the 21st century. These implications are important for curriculum developers, educators, and policymakers in integrating sustainability values into the education system. In conclusion, this study confirms that Home Economics has a strategic role in shaping a sustainable future through education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Event-centric human value understanding in news-domain texts: An actor-conditioned benchmark across multi-scope event contexts
Abstract: This work presents NEVU, a benchmark for actor-conditioned, event-centric, and direction-aware human value recognition in news-domain texts. NEVU evaluates whether models can infer values from event-structured evidence, attribute them to the correct social actors, and determine their aligned or contradictory direction. Built from 2865 English news articles, NEVU represents news at four semantic levels, from subevents to composite events and full articles. Using a hierarchical taxonomy of 54 fine-grained and 20 coarse-grained values, the benchmark contains 46,589 semantic units, 72,905 annotated unit–actor pairs, and 168,061 directed value instances. NEVU is constructed through a staged LLM-assisted annotation and verification pipeline, with targeted human verification for unresolved cases. Candidate-level acceptance and agreement are further examined through a multi-group assessment. The experiments show that prompting-only models remain limited, whereas LoRA-tuned open-weight models substantially improve performance, with overall Micro-F1 gains of 29.77 and 8.21 percentage points over the strongest prompting-only open-weight and proprietary baselines, respectively. These gains primarily reflect learnability under the NEVU reference-label setting. NEVU provides a structured benchmark for systematic evaluation and supervised adaptation of actor-conditioned human value recognition in English news. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Title: Politicization of duan lolat culture as an electoral strategy in the 2024 regional elections in Tanimbar Islands Regency, Indonesia
Abstract: This study examines how Duan Lolat culture was politicized as an electoral strategy during the 2024 Regional Head Election in the Tanimbar Islands Regency, Maluku, Indonesia. The research employs a qualitative-interpretive case study approach to understand the transformation of customary kinship relations into instruments of political mobilization within the context of local democracy. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with twelve key informants consisting of political actors, customary leaders, election organizers, and community members, supported by limited participant observation and document analysis. The data were analyzed using thematic coding techniques and triangulation procedures to ensure credibility and analytical consistency. The findings reveal that Duan Lolat culture has experienced a functional shift from a form of social capital grounded in solidarity and reciprocity into a political instrument for electoral mobilization. The study identifies three principal mechanisms of politicization: structural informality, relational emotionality, and material-symbolic hybridity. Through these mechanisms, customary kinship networks were strategically utilized by political elites to construct symbolic legitimacy, strengthen emotional loyalty, and mobilize electoral support based on kinship obligations rather than programmatic political preferences. The study also identifies a normative gap referred to as kosong, namely a regulatory space between customary law and formal electoral regulations that enables identity-based political mobilization to operate informally beyond institutional oversight. These findings indicate that while local democracy in Tanimbar procedurally functions in a stable manner with relatively high voter participation, substantively it remains vulnerable to identity polarization, patronage politics, and cultural manipulation. This research contributes to the broader literature on identity politics, social capital, and hybrid governance by demonstrating how indigenous cultural systems can be transformed into symbolic and political resources within local electoral contestation in Indonesia. Authors: Sacco P.L.; Fancourt D.
Title: Operationalising the arts exposome
Abstract: A recent arts exposome framework identified 50 transdiagnostic causal mechanisms (emotional, cognitive, self-referential, arousal–stress, inflammatory–epigenetic, social, and behavioural) by which arts engagement may affect mental health, organised around patterned daily exposure to active ingredients across diverse modes of arts engagement. Translating this structure into testable predictions depends on two operational prerequisites that current research has under-addressed. First, the active ingredients must be decomposed into mechanism-aligned exposure dimensions: aggregating activities as varied as receptive consumption, active participation, and cultural attendance under “arts engagement” averages mechanistically different effects and yields findings that the framework cannot localise to specific processes. Second, mechanism tractability is unevenly distributed across measurement modalities. Stress–HPA–immune mechanisms are well-served by peripheral measurement, including transcriptomic markers such as the Conserved Transcriptional Response to Adversity. Aesthetic and reward mechanisms are tractable through central measurement and autonomic indices of aesthetic emotion, but not through peripheral biomarkers. Affiliative mechanisms face validity challenges in peripheral measurement that may require pharmacological probes or behavioural proxies. Neither prerequisite suffices alone: a valid biomarker linked to a heterogeneous exposure measures something the framework cannot interpret, and a well-specified exposure linked to an inappropriate modality deteriorates evidence quality. These refinements are best understood as minimum conditions for identifying the core ingredients that matter most for each mechanism, since individual and contextual variation continue to moderate activation in real-world settings. Together, they identify where mechanism research can deliver near-term advances, where alternative methods are needed, and how the framework can move from theoretical mapping toward ecologically grounded testable inference. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: The impact of AI-based information system integration embedded with ESG considerations on perceived overall organizational performance
Abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI)-based information system integration, conceptualized as a perceived integration capability embedded in organizational workflows, is associated with perceived overall organizational performance. It focuses on the mediating roles of dynamic capability activities, employee AI action readiness, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices, defined as routinized monitoring, disclosure, and governance activities. Using survey data from 496 employees in firms with AI systems, the proposed framework is tested through structural equation modeling and supplemented by machine-learning-based predictive analysis. The results indicate that AI-based information system integration is associated with perceived overall organizational performance mainly through indirect pathways. It is positively associated with employees’ awareness of AI-supported sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring activities and with their readiness concerning the practical applicability of AI-supported information in daily work, both of which are associated with stronger ESG practices and higher perceived overall organizational performance. Its direct association with ESG practices is positive but weaker than the indirect pathways through dynamic capability activities and employee AI action readiness. Bootstrapped analyses support parallel and sequential indirect effects, while multi-group analyses show that the overall relationship pattern is stable across small and medium-sized enterprises and large enterprises. This study contributes by shifting attention from AI adoption to the perceived integration of AI into organizational workflows and by identifying dynamic capability activities, employee AI action readiness, and ESG practices as complementary pathways linking AI integration to perceived overall organizational performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Chefs, kitchens, and stars: A literature review of fine dining in hospitality and management studies
Abstract: Fine dining represents a niche within the restaurant industry, yet it has garnered significant attention from both scholars and practitioners. Fine dining, due to its distinctive characteristics - such as extreme creativity and innovation, adherence to strict institutional logics, a rigorous system of social evaluation from customers and critics, and the juxtaposition of artistic logics and commercial logics - is a compelling setting for hospitality and management scholars. However, fine dining literature is quite fragmented. Drawing on a thematic analysis of 101 articles, this literature review provides scholars with five thematic clusters that emerged: (1) Work environment and career path; (2) Creativity and innovation; (3) Social evaluation and institutional logics; (4) Customer experience and engagement; (5) Entrepreneurship and business model innovation. Title: Graph-informed learning of interpretable interaction dynamics in collective motion
Abstract: Inferring interaction mechanisms from collective-motion trajectories is challenging because effective interaction partners are typically unobserved, and motion updates arise from the coupled effects of neighbor selection and response rules. We propose Graph-informed Learning of Interaction Dynamics (GILD), an interpretable framework for homogeneous collective-motion systems. GILD jointly learns a state-dependent neighbor selector and a physically structured response rule through closed-loop rollout training. We evaluate GILD on six simulated collective-motion systems with diverse neighbor-selection mechanisms, response rules, and motion constraints. Across these systems, GILD achieves strong closed-loop prediction performance and reproduces the main trajectory-level and group-level behaviors of the simulated dynamics. Post-hoc analyses show that the learned selector weights are broadly consistent with rule-defined neighbor-selection mechanisms, and that the learned response modules can be distilled into compact symbolic expressions capturing the dominant functional structures of the underlying dynamics. Ablation experiments support the effectiveness of the main components of GILD. Experiments with response-noise perturbations further reveal model-dependent robustness and sensitivity under noisy trajectory generation. These results suggest that GILD provides a predictive and interpretable route for modeling collective-motion dynamics when interaction mechanisms are not directly observable. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Li B.; Kim N.; Zhang H.
Title: Virtual reality as a catalyst for change: Promoting communication intention, policy support and interaction with migrant workers in Singapore
Abstract: Migrant workers are vital to the host country's development, yet they often remain socially invisible and face barriers to social integration. Drawing on narrative persuasion and indirect contact perspectives, this research examines how immersive storytelling relates to empathy and supportive orientations toward migrant workers through two laboratory experiments in Singapore. Study One (N = 125) compared narrative delivery via virtual reality (VR), 360-degree video, and text. VR generated the highest immersion, and a sequential path indicated that greater immersion was associated with stronger identification with the protagonist, followed by greater empathy; empathy was associated with stronger willingness to interact with migrant workers, greater policy support, and higher future supportive behavioral intentions. Study Two (N = 87) focused on a key VR design choice, avatar perspective, by comparing self-versus other-embodiment in the VR experience. Self-embodiment increased self-presence, while greater self-presence was sequentially associated with immersion, identification with the protagonist, and empathy, followed by the same pattern of supportive outcomes. Together, the studies show that both modality and within-VR self-representation shape empathy-based pathways toward supportive orientations, offering actionable guidance for designing immersive interventions that promote understanding and support for marginalized groups. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Lv L.; Xie Z.; Gao H.; Xu S.; Xie H.; Chen W.; Kang S.
Title: Text-augmented patch–scene collaborative network for joint hyperspectral and LiDAR classification
Abstract: Remote sensing (RS) image classification is an important technique for land-cover understanding and environmental monitoring. Combining hyperspectral imagery (HSI) with light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data has become a promising strategy for improving land-cover recognition. However, most existing approaches still focus on visual representation learning and make limited use of scene-level context and category-related semantic knowledge. Relying only on image features makes it difficult to associate visual patterns with land-cover semantics, especially for categories with similar appearances. Moreover, most methods focus on spectral–spatial feature extraction from local patches while overlooking potential scene dependencies among land-cover types. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Text-Augmented Patch–Scene Collaborative Network (TAPSCN), a multilevel information fusion framework for joint HSI and LiDAR classification. TAPSCN integrates patch-level cross-modal cues, scene-level structural context, and category-level textual priors for scene-aware semantic classification. First, an Interactive Patch Fusion Module (IPFM) employs spectral-channel attention and geometric-spatial attention to accommodate the heterogeneous characteristics of HSI and LiDAR data, respectively. A two-stage asymmetric cross-modal mutual-guidance strategy further enhances collaborative representation learning across modalities, yielding robust local patch representations. Subsequently, a Global Scene Guidance Module (GSGM) models whole-image context through visual state-space modeling. By collaboratively optimizing local patch information and global scene semantics, GSGM improves the discrimination of complex scenes and easily confused classes. Finally, a Text Augmentation Alignment Module (TAAM) constructs semantic priors from class-level textual prompts. Through the joint optimization of strong vision–text alignment and weak semantic reconstruction, TAAM guides visual features to capture high-level semantic knowledge associated with land-cover classes, thereby enhancing their semantic discriminability. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that TAPSCN achieves superior classification accuracy while maintaining moderate parameter complexity. Title: Redistribution meets decarbonisation: Exploring universal basic income through an ecological macroeconomic integrated assessment model
Abstract: The dual challenge of climate change and rising inequality calls for policies capable of delivering both ecological sustainability and social equity. Within the field of Ecological Macroeconomics (EM), integrated assessment models (IAM) with biophysical and socio-economic linkages provide a promising approach to explore policy trade-offs ex ante. This paper contributes to this literature by employing the Within Limits Integrated Assessment Model (WILIAM), an EM-IAM that combines a macroeconomic multi-regional input–output structure with explicit representations of energy and material flows, biophysical constraints, and climate damages. We assess a policy mix designed to support a just low-carbon transition in 21 European countries over the period 2025–2050, including a universal basic income (UBI) financed through a wealth tax, alongside a carbon tax aimed at internalising the external costs of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. We examine the interactions between redistribution and emissions within a unified modelling framework that accounts for household heterogeneity, economic rigidities and ecological limits. Our results show that the policy mix substantially reduces income inequality and improves social outcomes. However, the introduction of UBI generates rebound effects through increased consumption, which can be partially mitigated in the presence of carbon pricing. These findings highlight a potential trade-off between equity and environmental objectives. We discuss the mechanisms driving these dynamics and explore policy design implications, including the role of complementary measures to decouple well-being from material throughput. The paper illustrates the value of EM-IAMs for analysing complex policy interactions and advancing the integration of social and ecological dimensions in macroeconomic modelling. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Gong Y.; Huang J.; Bao L.; Li H.; Liu J.; Jing P.; Xiong J.; Tang X.
Title: Teacher emotional support, question openness and student oral participation: The role of positive emotion across stages in AI-observed STEM and non-STEM classes
Abstract: Background: Student oral participation is essential for engagement and learning, yet participation tends to decline in large-class and STEM contexts where social risk and cognitive demands are higher. Existing studies often relied on self-reported or small-scale observations, which may introduce subjective bias and are labor-intensive, limiting large-scale evidence on how instructional practices influence participation across contexts. Aims: This study examines how teacher emotional support and question openness influence student oral participation through student emotion, and whether these effects vary across educational stages and disciplinary contexts. Sample: Data were collected from 1455 face-to-face classes in China. Methods: Artificial intelligence-based techniques were used to capture fine-grained classroom interactions. Structural equation modeling and multigroup analyses were conducted to examine the mediating role of student positive emotion and to compare pathway patterns across educational stages and disciplinary contexts. Results: Teacher emotional support was primarily associated with student oral participation via student positive emotion, whereas question openness showed a more direct association with participation. The indirect role of emotional support through positive emotion became stronger across educational stages, suggesting a compensatory function in secondary education where baseline participation tends to decline. Students in STEM classes were less emotionally responsive to teacher support but showed a stronger association between positive emotions and oral participation. Conclusions: Emotional support is a context-sensitive intervention rather than a universally effective strategy. By combining large-scale AI-based observation with cross-stage and disciplinary comparisons, this study contributes methodological advances for classroom interaction research, although cross-cultural validation of AI-based measures is needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Contreras S.A.
Title: Making critical-mineral sourcing visible: recorded-origin evidence from U.S. federal procurement
Abstract: Critical-mineral security depends not only on extraction and processing capacity but also on state visibility. Governments struggle to govern a mineral dependence they cannot observe in their own records, even when fragments of that information are held privately across agencies. This article asks how far the United States federal government’s recorded sourcing of the critical-mineral commodities it buys can be seen in its own contract data. Using approximately one thousand federal contract awards for selected critical-mineral commodity classes over fiscal years 2018–2026, we measure domestic-versus-foreign sourcing at the contract level in USAspending / Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS) records. Country of product origin is recorded for about 94% of awards and for nearly all obligated dollars, enough to support a bounded sourcing profile in this narrow universe. Among awards with recorded origin, foreign sourcing is a minority, about 9%, but it is policy-relevant: China is the largest foreign source by dollar value, concentrated in two large manganese awards, while Germany is the most frequent by award count. Bullion and coinage flows must be separated from strategic-materials procurement, or they inflate the universe twenty- to forty-fold. Two preliminary findings, a selective-onshoring trend and a defense-logistics sourcing effect, do not survive the complete data. The analysis covers U.S. federal procurement only and measures recorded procurement sourcing rather than upstream mine origin or total national dependence. Its contribution is to make one layer of critical-mineral governance, the state’s own recorded purchasing, observable, and to clarify what that layer can and cannot show for public oversight. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang S.; Cui H.; Duan M.; Li X.; Qu Y.; Zhang Y.
Title: Structure-aware prompt learning with large language models for drug–drug interaction prediction
Abstract: Drug–drug interactions (DDIs) are a major cause of adverse drug reactions and clinical safety risks, highlighting the need for accurate and clinically meaningful prediction methods. While most existing approaches primarily formulate DDI prediction as a binary classification task, systematic exploration of predicting specific interaction types remains limited, despite its higher clinical relevance. Meanwhile, although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong reasoning capabilities, their application to pharmaceutical prediction tasks remains limited and rarely leverages structural drug information. To address these gaps, we propose ProDDI, a structure-aware prompt engineering framework for DDI prediction. Specifically, we design a novel prompt generation module that incorporates multi-path subgraphs from the drug interaction network and molecular structure sequences into prompt templates. This enables the model to capture both high-order relational semantics and fine-grained chemical structures. In addition, a low-rank adaptation strategy is adopted to ensure efficient fine-tuning. Experiments on DrugBank and OGB-biokg datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of ProDDI. Notably, ProDDI also exhibits strong generalization and robustness under cold-start and noisy conditions, making it a promising paradigm for advancing LLM-based drug knowledge discovery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Ramkumar J.; Anand K.; Ramesh A.
Title: Development and experimental analysis of a novel impulse turbine compounded naturally aspirated High-Speed diesel engine
Abstract: Despite decades of research and development proving the technical advantages of turbocharging, several gasoline and diesel engines, especially the single-cylinder engines, remain naturally aspirated. Commercially available single-cylinder engines are rarely turbocharged due to inherent technical challenges and cost-to-performance trade-offs. The pulsating exhaust flow typical of single-cylinder engines causes efficiency losses in conventional turbocharger reaction turbines, which are designed for steady or near-continuous exhaust flow. Thus, the benefits of charging and exhaust energy recovery are not realised in many engines, especially single-cylinder engines. Even in the case of two-cylinder and three-cylinder engines, the benefit of charging is not fully realised, as adapting a turbocharger to these engines involves several compromises in energy extraction by the turbine due to the pulsated exhaust flow, in matching the turbine and the compressor, and in matching the turbine and the engine. Consequently, the best-suited compressor or the most effective turbine is not designed individually for these engines, since matching both to the engine compromises the system’s effectiveness. Thus, commercially available single-cylinder engines are rarely turbocharged, supercharged, or turbo-compounded. Therefore, neither the advantage of charging is realised nor the potential for exhaust energy recovery is capitalised, leaving these engines underutilised and underperforming despite their potential. In this work, a novel impulse turbine capable of extracting work from the pulsating exhaust flow typical of a single-cylinder engine was designed and developed for a commercially available single-cylinder diesel engine, based on simulations and theoretical calculations. Furthermore, a turbocompounding layout was developed to adapt the novel impulse turbine for the single-cylinder engine. Subsequently, an experimental analysis was conducted to evaluate the performance of the impulse turbine. Experimental results showed that the impulse turbine delivered 1.2 kW of power at 3000 rpm, increasing the naturally aspirated (NA) engine brake power output by 12 %. The turbine efficiency was about 80 %, and the net brake power output of the NA engine with the impulse turbine was 11.5 kW at 3000 rpm. The present study demonstrates the potential to improve the performance of single-cylinder engines by effectively extracting thermal energy from exhaust gas through impulse turbo-compounding. Title: An integrated framework for total nitrogen load allocation and multidimensional assessment reconciling equity and environmental efficiency in large river basins
Abstract: Total nitrogen (TN) load governance is crucial for safeguarding river and nearshore water environments. However, translating basin reduction goals into equitable and efficient spatial targets remains challenging due to socioeconomic, hydrological, and biogeochemical heterogeneities. This study develops an integrated framework coupling process-based water quality modelling (SWAT) with Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) to reconcile environmental efficiency with regional equity. Applying this framework to the Liao River Basin in China, this study generated multiple allocation schemes reflecting different socioeconomic priorities and evaluated their performance across TN compliance, abatement costs, food production, and social equality. Results show that under the 30% reduction target, schemes integrating efficiency reduced total basin abatement costs by 0.1%–6.5% and increased crop yields by 0.4%–2.4% relative to the equity-only scheme, although they widened regional disparities in economic and livelihood burdens. Sensitivity analyses indicate that the economic advantages of efficiency-integrated schemes weaken under the 40% reduction target due to nonlinearly escalating marginal abatement costs, and remain sensitive to source allocation within individual catchments. The scheme performance assessment accounting for multiple uncertainties reveals that the optimal schemes depend on the total reduction target and specific policy priorities, including objective weighting and policy-weighted scenarios prioritizing food security, cost control, or social equality. Ultimately, this framework explicitly quantifies multidimensional tradeoffs and provides a practical basis for formulating load management strategies across varying reduction targets and policy priorities. © 2026

Title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of the feasibility and acceptability of a school-based intervention to reduce student anxiety during the transition to middle school
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of a school-based intervention to reduce anxiety and related impairment during the transition to middle school. Thirty-eight students were randomly assigned to receive the Transitioning Emotionally and Academically to Middle School Successfully (TEAMSS, n = 20) program, a group cognitive behavioral intervention, or Enhanced Usual Care (EUC, n = 18), a study generated resource list and usual school counseling. Students (mean age 10.4; 85.7% White; 50% female) had elevated anxiety symptoms and/or a primary anxiety disorder. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed via recruitment, retention, attendance, intervention satisfaction, and intervention adherence. Exploratory student outcomes of anxiety and constructs targeted in TEAMSS (e.g., behavioral avoidance, academic organizational and social skills) were assessed at post intervention (10 weeks after the initiation of treatment) and at the end of the academic year (follow-up). Results revealed student recruitment challenges; enrolled participants found the intervention acceptable and helpful. Student attendance at the group meetings was high. Clinician adherence to the intervention indicated room for improvement. At post and follow-up assessments, students in both groups showed significant reductions in anxiety and improvements in functioning, but there were few statistically significant between-group differences. Within group effect sizes were medium to large and favored TEAMSS on several measures assessing changes in areas targeted in TEAMSS (e.g., maladaptive cognitions, social skills); however, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the overall absence of group differences on most measures. Title: Research trends and conceptual foundations of religious moderation: A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Although the concept of religious moderation has received increasing scholarly attention in recent years, comprehensive and globally integrative syntheses remain limited. In many Western scholarly traditions, similar ideas are often articulated through related concepts such as religious tolerance, pluralism, liberal pluralism, or collaborative secularism, resulting in fragmented conceptual discussions across disciplines and regions. This study therefore aims to map the development, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of research on religious moderation within global academic discourse. This study employs a hybrid approach combining Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database, where the keyword “religious moderation” was searched in article titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search identified 901 publications (2009–2026). After applying the PRISMA screening procedure, 235 articles met the inclusion criteria and were selected for analysis. Bibliometric mapping was conducted using VOSviewer to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, institutional affiliations, and thematic patterns within the field. The findings indicate that research on religious moderation has experienced gradual growth and increasing global visibility. However, the distribution of scholarly contributions remains highly concentrated in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia and Malaysia, suggesting that the concept has not yet diffused widely across Western, Middle Eastern, and African academic traditions. This geographical concentration reveals significant opportunities for comparative, cross-cultural, and interdisciplinary research. This study also, through an analysis of 235 articles indexed in Scopus, found several studies on the indicators and principles of religious moderation, which play an important role in fostering harmony amid social differences and diversity. In addition, the study proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework linking religious moderation to broader domains including social cohesion, conflict resolution, interfaith relations, family dynamics, and education, highlighting its relevance for sustaining inclusive and resilient communities. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Hauser C.S.; Fourati M.
Title: Fostering institutional trust and organ donation: Evidence from a randomized informational intervention in Tunisia
Abstract: Organ transplantation saves lives and improves the quality of life of patients who would otherwise depend on costly and invasive treatments. The technology is becoming available in low- and middle-income countries, but the gap between the demand for and the supply of organ transplants remains large. In a randomized controlled trial at a Tunisian university, we evaluate an expert-led intervention designed to inform about organ donation and strengthen trust in medical institutions. The intervention consists of a short video testimonial from a heart transplant survivor, a presentation led by a medical doctor and a short Q&A session. We find that the intervention significantly increases deceased donor registration, with suggestive evidence of positive spillover effects on the control group. The survey data provides little support for changes in attitudes and social expectations as potential mechanisms. Instead, it reveals large and statistically significant increases in medical and legal knowledge, religious beliefs supportive of donation, and institutional trust among treated students. Finally, we show that treatment effects on organ donor registration are driven by male students and those whose families likely support organ donation. Targeting older segments of the population may further increase the impact and cost-effectiveness of this intervention. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Biological effects of ionizing radiation combined with extremely low frequency magnetic fields among occupationally exposed X-ray technicians
Abstract: The human body is susceptible to ionizing radiation penetration resulting in cancer and other adverse health outcomes. One potent ionizing radiation source that has uses in medicine is X-rays. Globally, about 2.3 million and in Pakistan about 26,046 registered medical technicians are exposed to X-rays. Along with X-rays, these X-ray technicians are also potentially exposed to extremely low frequency magnetic field (ELF MF) from X-ray machines and other electrical devices. This study investigated the individual and combined effects of X-rays and ELF MF in the form of molecular mechanism including disruption of antioxidant enzyme activities, generation of reactive oxygen species, and the DNA damage. A total of 250 healthy workers were enrolled in this study; divided into ionizing radiation exposed and un-exposed groups. Along with exposure to ionizing radiation and ELF MF, information about exposure to potential confounding factors and effect modifiers was also collected. The results showed a statistically significant increased risk of DNA damage in the X-ray exposed group 20.3 ± 11.2 compared to un-exposed group 10.3 ± 5.85, p < 0.001. Also, antioxidant enzymes activities were statistically significantly higher in the exposed group Vs. un-exposed group for CAT: 12.1 ± 4.53 Vs. 9.67 ± 4.99; p < 0.001 and MDA: 9.36 ± 6.55 Vs. 5.92 ± 4.58; p < 0.001. However, the increase for SOD was not statistically significant (7.75 ± 5.58 Vs. 7.45 ± 4.83; p= 0.648). The combined exposure of ionizing radiation and ELF MF (≥0.4 μT) increased the impact for DNA damage only where changes in all the antioxidant enzymes were not meaningful. The age was statistically significantly associated with DNA damage and SOD activity. Also, the risk increased with dose-response (duration of employment) and highest DNA damage was observed in workers with work experience of ≥10 years. The study findings are useful in reporting the adverse health effects of exposure to occupational X-rays radiation and also in educating the laboratory technicians about the potentially harmful parts of their work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Meng S.; Zheng H.; Pu A.; Yan X.; Wei J.
Title: Multi-scenario CTR prediction with LLM-augmented semantic graphs and anti-polarization experts
Abstract: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction is a core task in recommendation systems. However, existing multimodal CTR methods still rely heavily on interaction-driven graphs, which are often too sparse to capture deeper semantic relations between users. To address this limitation, we propose APEX-GraphMoE, a unified framework centered on LLM-enhanced LightGCN (LLN). LLN introduces an LLM-as-graph-builder paradigm, in which fine-tuned large language models aggregate multimodal user behaviors and construct semantic user–user edges to enrich the graph beyond explicit interactions. Building on this core paradigm, we further introduce HUBM and APG to address two additional challenges caused by strong semantic graph signals. HUBM performs task-aware multimodal refinement to preserve the contribution of image and text features during downstream optimization, while APG stabilizes adaptive routing in MMoE and alleviates expert polarization. Experiments on the large-scale AntM2 C dataset, containing approximately 10 million samples across five scenarios, show that APEX-GraphMoE improves AUC by 2.89% and reduces expert-usage variance by 50.21% over strong baselines.We further conduct auxiliary validation on MM-CTR1 M to provide preliminary cross-dataset evidence, while keeping AntM2 C as the primary benchmark. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of LLN as the core source of semantic topology enhancement, with HUBM and APG serving as complementary supporting mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Effects of black soldier fly larvae meal on hepatic metabolism and intestinal health in juvenile southern catfish (Silurus meridionalis): Insights from non-targeted metabolomics
Source title: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology - Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
Abstract: To investigate the effects of replacing fishmeal (FM) with black soldier fly larvae meal (BSFLM) on hepatic metabolism and intestinal health in juvenile southern catfish (Silurus meridionalis), six isonitrogenous and isoenergetic diets were formulated with graded replacement levels of 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% and fed to fish for 8 weeks. Intestinal antioxidant parameters, serum immune factors, hepatic free amino acids, and non-targeted hepatic metabolomics were analyzed. No significant differences were observed among groups in intestinal superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutaredoxin (GSH-PX), total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC), or malondialdehyde (MDA) (ANOVA, all P > 0.05). Serum interleukin-10 (IL-10) showed a significant linear increase with increasing BSFLM inclusion (P = 0.021), indicating dose-dependent anti-inflammatory immunomodulation. Hepatic free amino acid profiling revealed that ornithine decreased significantly with increasing replacement (P = 0.012), S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) peaked in the H50 group (36.59 vs. 24.00 in H0, P = 0.006), proline decreased significantly (P = 0.030), taurine and cysteine were significantly elevated in the H50 group (P = 0.007 and 0.022, respectively), and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) declined significantly (P = 0.004). Non-targeted metabolomics revealed a three-phase metabolic trajectory: 10–20% replacement represented an adaptation phase characterized by decoupling of central nitrogen metabolism from anabolism; 30% constituted a transition phase with synergistic integration of energy metabolism, carbohydrate utilization, and glucuronidation detoxification; 40–50% represented a stress/dysregulation phase, marked by a coordinated stress module containing norepinephrine and pyroglutamic acid, with 2-furoic acid emerging as a potential stress biomarker at 50% inclusion. The number of differentially abundant metabolites increased from 7 in the H10 group to over 60 in the H50 group. KEGG pathway enrichment confirmed activation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis at low levels, while high levels enriched oxidative stress-related pathways including glutathione metabolism, ferroptosis, and ABC transporters. Collectively, these findings indicate that BSFLM replacement should not exceed 30% in juvenile southern catfish diets to balance sustainable protein utilization with maintenance of metabolic homeostasis and overall health. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Liu X.; Tian M.; Dong Z.; Ou X.; Shi F.; Lai J.
Title: Risk-based collaborative planning for cyber–physical–social distribution systems against extreme weather
Abstract: Extreme weather can simultaneously damage distribution lines and communication facilities, weakening coordinated resource operation and increasing load-shedding risk. Such disruptions are particularly consequential in cyber–physical–social systems (CPSS) supporting distribution system operation, where power delivery depends on cyber connectivity and prosumer participation. To address this interdependence, a risk-based collaborative planning framework traces fragility-based failures through communication service to prosumer market access and adaptive post-event operation. Within this framework, peer-to-peer (P2P) trading serves as a communication-dependent mechanism for energy exchange among accessible prosumers rather than as an independent planning objective. A two-stage mean–CVaR model coordinates the distribution system operator’s (DSO) investment in communication backup and active-power transfer capacity with prosumer investment in renewable generation and energy storage. As cyber–physical conditions deteriorate, the model shifts from grid-connected coordination to communication-supported island operation and ultimately to local self-supply. A nested progressive hedging and alternating direction method of multipliers (PH-ADMM) algorithm coordinates scenario decisions and the interfaces between the DSO and prosumers. Studies on modified IEEE 33-node and 123-node systems show that communication survivability materially affects investment decisions and feasible post-event energy coordination. The framework provides a scalable basis for resilience-oriented collaborative planning in communication-dependent distribution systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Schurr A.; Moyal A.; Ritov I.
Author full names: Schurr, Amos (55512477300); Moyal, Adiel (57213839331); Ritov, Ilana (6701818465)
Title: The complex role of perspective taking in negotiations
Abstract: To reach an agreement, successful negotiators typically need to understand two things: what they themselves are willing to accept, and what the other side is willing to accept. Understanding the other party's threshold requires perspective taking. In negotiations over goods or services, these judgments shape perceptions of the bargaining zone: the range of outcomes both parties would prefer to walking away without an agreement. The present paper examines how negotiators form perceptions of the bargaining zone. These perceptions have important downstream consequences, influencing everything from the offers negotiators make to the agreements they reach. We review work on how negotiators form perceptions of what their counterpart is willing to accept. Perspective taking can help negotiators estimate the lowest price a seller would accept or the highest price a buyer would pay. However, it can also lead negotiators to erroneously internalize the other party's perspective as if it is relevant to their own valuation. As an example, we demonstrate that buyers are willing to pay more for the same good when the seller gives up an entire endowment rather than only part of it, although the seller's end state should not affect buyer's willingness to pay for the good. These findings show how taking the other party's perspective can shape valuations, fairness judgments and negotiations outcomes. We conclude by discussing implications for multi-issue bargaining and strategic framing, highlighting how psychological heuristics and social context interact to shape outcomes in complex real-world situations, such as salary negotiations and real estate transactions. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: How Sociodemographic Factors Shape Community Well-Being in Sustainable Tourism Destinations
Abstract: Tourism significantly contributes to the livelihoods of host communities, influencing their social, environmental, and economic development. However, residents’ diverse demographics and attitudes often shape their perceptions of tourism, affecting the level of support or opposition within these communities. Such demographic factors may influence how individuals perceive tourism’s benefits and drawbacks, leading to regional variations in engagement. This study examined the relationship between sociodemographic factors, New Silk Road (NSR) infrastructure, community well-being, and tourism sustainability in destination areas. Specifically, it analysed correlations among NSR infrastructure, demographic variables, tourism impact (TI), quality of life (QOL), place image (PI), and support for tourism development (STD). Data were collected during the NSR infrastructure project in Turkistan, Kazakhstan. The findings indicated that 24 of 28 relationships between variables were statistically significant, demonstrating strong associations. Additionally, post-hoc analysis revealed significant differences in satisfaction with non-material aspects of life—affected by respondents’ income, occupation, and parental status—providing valuable insights for policymakers to develop targeted strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Fang L.; Liu H.; Tong B.; Zhao Y.; Gan X.; He C.
Title: Toward intelligent safety science: a paradigm-oriented framework for AI-enabled reconstruction of safety theories and models
Abstract: Modern socio-technical systems are increasingly interconnected, dynamic, and uncertain, which challenges safety research that relies mainly on retrospective accident explanation. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied to risk identification, fault diagnosis, early warning, and decision support, its role in safety research is still often fragmented and limited to tool enhancement. This paper proposes Intelligent Safety Science (ISS) as a paradigm-oriented framework for organizing AI-enabled safety research. The framework aims to explain how AI can help extend classical safety theories from post-accident analysis toward earlier understanding and management of evolving risks. To develop this framework, the paper identifies three AI-enabled extension paths for classical safety theories: dynamic upgrading, real-time enhancement, and proactive transformation. It then abstracts a Perception-Reasoning-Decision-Intervention (PRDI) structure as a conceptual-methodological framework for linking risk observation, risk analysis, safety response, and feedback. Based on PRDI, ISS is characterized by four capability dimensions—predictability, holism, adaptability, and generativity—and four supporting elements: data, model, knowledge, and interaction. Scenario-based analyses of complex industrial systems, urban critical infrastructure, and human-machine collaborative environments further illustrate how ISS can be adapted to different sectoral conditions. This study provides a theoretical framework for clarifying the role of AI in safety science and offers a basis for future empirical research on intelligent safety systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Navigating blue economy research conflicts for improved societal outcomes
Abstract: The Blue Economy aims to balance economic prosperity, environmental stewardship, and social equity through sustainable ocean development. Its rapid expansion—spanning fisheries, aquaculture, maritime transport, and energy—has intensified competition for marine resources and space, often generating conflict and cumulative impacts on ecosystems and communities. These tensions are driven by uncertainty about outcomes, as well as differing stakeholder values and perceptions. To realize the goals of the Blue Economy, robust research is needed. However, research institutions working in contested marine spaces may face reputational, ethical, and strategic risks. These include navigating tensions among ocean users, developers, policymakers, and the public. From an organisational perspective, deciding whether to engage in such research requires balancing potential benefits against risks to integrity, partnerships, and long-term goals. This paper introduces the Conflict Navigation Grid, a decision-support framework that enables research organisations to systematically evaluate the risks and benefits of proposed projects. The Grid helps identify initiatives that provide strong organisational, community, environmental, and policy value while also assessing whether reputational, operational, or personal risks are manageable. It distinguishes projects that align with institutional values and capacities from those where the potential harms outweigh uncertain returns. By adopting this systematic decision framework, organisations can confidently make decisions in the face of conflict, thereby managing risk and achieving improved societal outcomes. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wang Y.; Nie L.
Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of an age-space structured epidemic model with partial immunity, nonlinear infection rate, and combined transmission pathways from hosts and environment
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: To account for the complex challenges of spatial heterogeneity, inevitable human mobility, and dual transmission pathways (human-to-human and environment-to-human) in epidemic dynamics, we propose a novel age-space structured model incorporating partial immunity and nonlinear incidence. The model explicitly includes the infection age structure of both infected individuals and environmental pathogens to capture variations in infectivity during the transmission process. First, the well-posedness of the model solution is rigorously established using the Banach fixed-point theorem. Next, by applying the Laplace transform, we derive the next-generation operator L, then the basic reproduction number is defined as its spectral radius. Furthermore, under a spatially homogeneous scenario, R0 is obtained in exact analytical form. The global asymptotic stability of the disease-free and endemic steady states is then established by analyzing the distribution of the roots of the characteristic equations and constructing appropriate Lyapunov functionals. Numerical simulations visually elucidate complex spatio-temporal-age dynamics and quantify the effectiveness of interventions. In particular, restricting the mobility of infected individuals and improving vaccine efficacy significantly curb transmission. Fitting to cholera case data from Somalia, we find that neglecting either age structure or spatial heterogeneity leads to significant biases in case number estimates, underscoring their indispensable role in accurate forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Shiny by Design: Establishing Diagnostic Criteria for Intentional Burnishing on Prehistoric Bone Artifacts
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: The identification of intentional burnishing on prehistoric osseous artifacts remains a persistent methodological challenge. Bone surfaces are highly reactive and readily record microwear traces but are susceptible to taphonomic alteration. This study investigates how the use of different burnishing materials affects the morphology of bone surfaces and the formation of diagnostic microwear traces to develop a methodologically grounded classification for identifying intentionally burnished surfaces on archeological osseous artifacts. Experimental observations are evaluated in relation to existing knowledge of use-related, manufacturing, and postdepositional surface modifications. The analysis is based on a microwear framework that integrates multiscalar observations (low- and high-magnification microscopy and scanning electron microscopy) with quantitative three-dimensional surface texture analysis. Both microscopy and quantitative data derived from confocal microscopy reveal clear differences among bones burnished with different agents, highlighting agent-specific topographic patterns. The experimentally derived reference dataset was subsequently applied during microwear analysis of selected prehistoric bone points from Lake Lubāns (Latvia) and the Wiele 33 site (Poland) to assess the analytical applicability of the proposed protocol. The results of our study demonstrate the diagnostic potential of the created classification of wear traces to distinguish intentional burnishing on archaeological osseous artifacts and to discriminate between intentional, use-related, and taphonomic surface modifications. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Jedinger A.
Title: A dual-process motivational approach to understanding antisemitism: The role of authoritarianism, social dominance orientation, and conspiracy mentality
Abstract: Antisemitism remains a persistent challenge in contemporary societies, yet its psychological underpinnings are not well understood. Building on the dual-process motivational (DPM) model of ideology and prejudice, this study examined the extent to which antisemitism is rooted in broader ideological dispositions - right-wing authoritarianism (RWA), social dominance orientation (SDO), and conspiracy mentality. Using a nationwide online survey of German adults ( N = 457), bivariate and multivariate analyses indicate that conspiracy mentality is the strongest correlate of antisemitic attitudes, followed by individual differences in SDO. These findings support the view that antisemitism is embedded within a broader ideological belief system characterized by anti-egalitarian and conspiratorial worldviews. The role of conspiratorial worldviews as a potential distinct motivational pathway to prejudice within the DPM model is discussed. © 2026 The Author.

Author full names: Brady, William J. (57222282207); Yu, Chen-Wei (57941423800); Ornstein, Nicholas (60896643700); Sun, Bolun (60895903900); Jackson, Joshua Conrad (57056837000)
Title: Artificial intelligence systems distort upstream selection in human social learning
Abstract: Humans are social learners who depend on observing others to acquire knowledge, norms, and behaviors, a capacity that underlies cumulative cultural evolution. Social learning unfolds in two stages: upstream selection determines what information becomes visible, and downstream selection determines what learners copy from that visible sample. Downstream selection occurs through biases such as conformity bias (copying what appears common) and prestige bias (copying those who appear highly respected). These downstream biases can be adaptive when upstream selection yields a sample that reflects the population's true distribution, so that what appears common is actually common and those who appear respected are actually competent. We argue that digital technologies disrupt this condition, creating an upstream selection problem. Engagement-based algorithms amplify the tails of the distribution, surfacing rare and extreme content, whereas generative AI collapses it toward the mode (of the population or the user), erasing the surrounding diversity. Crucially, in each system the optimization signal shapes both visibility and prestige. For engagement-based algorithms, the signal is engagement: creators who post extreme content become more visible and, through the likes, shares, and followers, appear more prestigious. For generative AI, the signal is statistical typicality: it makes a modal answer dominant and, with no alternatives shown, makes the model that produced it appear more prestigious. These distortions can give rise to emergent group-level phenomena, including pluralistic ignorance and illusory consensus. Synthesizing evidence across psychology, cultural evolution, and computational social science, we provide a framework for how digital technologies disrupt social learning and outline interventions for restoring functional cultural transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Wang Z.Q.; Li X.T.; Yan J.X.; Qu Z.; Zhang Z.J.; Zhang P.; Zhang Z.F.
Title: Overcoming the strength–ductility trade-off of chemically complex alloys via local chemical fluctuations
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Tailoring the ordered structures within chemically complex alloys (CCAs), represents an effective strategy for addressing the strength-ductility trade-off dilemma in conventional metals, such as steels, aluminum alloys, and titanium alloys. In this study, a novel strategy is proposed in a CoCrNiAl dual-phase CCA, where prolonged low-temperature annealing is utilized to tailor local chemical fluctuations (LCF). This process promotes enhanced ordering degree of the matrix, resulting in an enhancement in strength without loss of uniform elongation. Comprehensive microstructural analysis reveals that LCF modulates dislocation activity and deformation mechanisms by altering local energy fluctuations (LEF). Specifically, the enhancement of atomic ordering increases the antiphase boundary (APB) energy, thereby increasing the resistance to dislocation glide. Meanwhile, elemental segregation reduces the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the matrix, enhancing its work-hardening capacity. These novel findings provide deeper insight into the influence of ordered structures on both the strength and work-hardening capacity of face-centered cubic CCAs at room temperature. © 2026

Title: More alike than unalike: Contextually aligned authority arguments amplify sustainable choices across cultures
Abstract: Most research is conducted in Western societies, with few studies from Latin America. This oversight has led to a narrow understanding of the effectiveness that various sustainability-oriented interventions have in countries with different cultural values. As consumers play a vital role in mitigating climate change issues, this behavioral field experiment investigates whether reliance on the authority and commitment-consistency principles from social influence increases individuals' inclination to choose sustainably, and whether the effectiveness of these principles is culturally contingent. Participants from Ecuador and Norway (N = 346) were randomized to one of three conditions (control vs. authority vs. commitment-consistency), with the latter two conditions containing a message tailored to its associated social influence principle. After replying to some survey items, participants made a choice between a more (vs. less) sustainable option. A chi-square test revealed that both social influence conditions jointly boosted choice likelihood of the more sustainable option relative to the control condition, supporting our initial preregistered hypothesis. However, contrary to our second preregistered hypothesis, a regression-based simple moderation analysis using the PROCESS macro (Model 1) showed no country moderation in the effectiveness of these social influence principles; instead, the results were largely attributable to the authority condition alone, which was considerably more effective than both other conditions across countries, regardless of participants' trust in authorities and their need for consistency. Our findings demonstrate the superiority of contextually aligned authority arguments as a viable way to foster pro-environmental behaviors. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Rebelo P.; Rosa S.
Title: Optimal resource control of a food chain with weak Allee effect and antipredator behaviour
Abstract: The aim of this paper is to study a nonautomonous food chain model with three trophic levels: producers (plants), primary consumers (herbivores) and secondary consumers (carnivores). The model includes some realistic biological assumptions such as carrying capacity, seasonal reproduction, rigid social structure and the inclusion of antipredatory behaviour. Results concerning existence, uniqueness, positivity, uniform boundedness of the solution and local stability analysis of the (uncontrolled) model are presented. An optimal control problem related to primary consumer’s biomass is formulated. Existence and uniqueness of the optimal control is proved. Numerical simulation of both uncontrolled and controlled cases is presented. A study on the control efficiency is also presented. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Li Y.; Chen R.; Tran K.T.
Title: 2D time-domain SH-wave full-waveform inversion for geotechnical site characterization: a practical comparison of optimization strategies
Abstract: Engineering-geological site investigation requires reliable identification of shallow subsurface structures, interfaces, and weak zones, whereas conventional methods such as boreholes and coring remain spatially discrete. Two-dimensional time-domain SH-wave full-waveform inversion (SH-FWI) provides a nondestructive, in situ, and spatially continuous approach for recovering shear-wave velocity (Vs) and density, two parameters directly relevant to engineering-geological interpretation. This study presents a practical evaluation of steepest descent (SD), L-BFGS, and Gauss–Newton (GN) within a unified 2D time-domain SH-FWI framework, focusing on their effects on Vs and density recovery using one synthetic model and two representative engineering-geological field cases with contrasting near-surface conditions. In the field cases, the inversion-derived density results are quantitatively compared with laboratory-measured borehole core densities through depth-dependent and layer-wise statistical analyses, thereby providing practical evidence for assessing the applicability of different optimization strategies in engineering-geological site characterization. The results show that all three methods can recover the main engineering-geological framework, including shallow hard layers, weathered limestone transitions, localized weak intervals, and competent bedrock. GN provides the highest inversion resolution and fastest convergence but at substantially greater computational cost and memory demand. SD serves as a stable first-order baseline but tends to produce smoother models and slower convergence. L-BFGS provides a practical compromise among inversion reliability, borehole-density consistency, and computational affordability under the tested field conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate that SH-FWI can provide useful and spatially continuous information for shallow engineering-geological characterization, and the recovered Vs and density models can further support the derivation of stiffness-related parameters for subsequent engineering-geological analysis and application. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Duan Y.; Ma K.; Fu X.; Li S.; Chen R.; Zhao J.; Wang X.; Meng Y.H.; Zhang S.; Guo Y.
Title: Transparent and mechanically robust fish gelatin hydrogels through covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation by dialdehyde carboxymethyl chitin nanofibers
Abstract: Polysaccharide reinforcement enhances the mechanical strength of fish gelatin (FG), narrowing its performance gap with mammalian gelatins (bovine and porcine gelatins). However, the improved mechanical strength is often accompanied by reduced optical transparency due to interfacial incompatibility-induced aggregation, phase separation, and light scattering. Herein, a covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation strategy based on dialdehyde carboxymethyl chitin nanofibers (dCMCh-NF) was developed to optimize protein–polysaccharide interactions in FG hydrogels. At a low loading of 0.1 wt%, dCMCh-NF effectively reinforced the FG network. The FG/dCMCh8-NF hydrogel exhibited a hardness of 695.52 ± 4.51 g, significantly higher than that of pure FG (497.30 ± 19.19 g) and comparable to that of mammalian gelatin. Meanwhile, its light transmittance reached 85.70 ± 1.32%, markedly exceeding that of FG/CMCh-NF (71.37 ± 0.47%). Structural characterization and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that aldehyde groups on dCMCh-NF formed Schiff-base linkages with FG as the primary interaction, while hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions served as secondary stabilizing forces. This dual crosslinking suppressed local aggregation, reduced phase separation, and facilitated the formation of a homogeneous and compact network, thereby minimizing light scattering. This work establishes covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation as an effective strategy for overcoming the inherent transparency-strength trade-off in polysaccharide-reinforced FG hydrogels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A novel strategy for high conductivity and dimensional stability sulfonated polyimide proton exchange membranes for direct methanol fuel cells
Abstract: The trade-off between proton conductivity and dimensional stability of sulfonated polyimide (SPI) proton exchange membranes (PEMs) greatly limits their practical application in direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs). Herein, a strategy for regulating the proton conductivity and dimensional stability of copolymer membranes through the coupled regulation of the degree of sulfonation (DS) and fractional free volume (FFV) is proposed. By introducing bulky fluorene groups as side chains to regulate the FFV, a series of SPI PEMs with different DS and FFV were prepared. It is found that an appropriate balance between DS and FFV is critical for achieving high proton conductivity and dimensional stability. In particular, the BSPI-50 membrane achieves a proton conductivity of 113 mS·cm−1 at 80 ℃ while maintaining a low swelling ratio of 35.2 %. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that FFV can be tuned by adjusting the content of fluorene units, as increased side-group content weakens intermolecular interactions between polymer chains. An appropriate balance between DS and FFV facilitates the formation of well-connected hydrophilic nanochannels, thereby promoting proton transport while maintaining dimensional stability. The BSPI-50 membrane delivers a peak power density of 72.97 mW·cm−2 in single cells and exhibits durability over 100 h of continuous operation, with a minimal voltage decay rate of 0.7 mV·h−1. This work demonstrates that the combined regulation of DS and FFV provides an effective approach to balancing proton transport and dimensional stability, enabling the development of SPI PEMs with excellent overall performance for DMFCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Pang X.; Chen L.; Mu Y.
Title: Wedge-index based butterfly counting in bipartite graphs
Abstract: Butterfly counting is a key metric in the analysis of bipartite networks. Existing butterfly counting techniques are primarily classified into two categories: layer-priority-based and vertex-priority-based methods. Both approaches compute the number of butterflies in bipartite graphs by enumerating wedges from the neighbor lists of vertices. The state-of-the-art algorithms typically adopt vertex-priority-based techniques, where priorities are assigned to vertices, enabling the enumeration of fewer wedges during the butterfly counting process.In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient wedge-based index for bipartite graphs, referred to as the WB-index (Wedge-based Bipartite Index), designed to accelerate butterfly counting. We introduce two variants of the WB-index based on the two primary butterfly counting principles. By performing a single traversal of the WB-index, we can compute three types of butterfly statistics: the total number of butterflies in the bipartite graph, the number of butterflies for each vertex, and the number of butterflies for each edge. These three computations are implemented by the algorithms BFC-WB, VBFC-WB, and EBFC-WB, respectively. Furthermore, when the bipartite graph undergoes changes, butterfly counting can still be performed efficiently by maintaining the index without the need for reconstruction, especially for medium-scale graphs. Experimental results show that BFC-WB substantially improves butterfly counting efficiency compared with state-of-the-art vertex-priority algorithms, achieving speedups of 66× to 103×. © 2026

Title: Beyond decontamination: Investigating the effect of gamma irradiation on natural dyes in a historical wool carpet
Abstract: This study investigates the viability of gamma irradiation as a treatment process for historical textiles, focusing on the dyes of a 19th–century wool carpet. The effect of irradiation doses (1–10 kGy) on blue-, red-, and yellow-dyed fibers was evaluated by multiple techniques, including colorimetric, spectroscopic, chromatographic, thermal, and morphological analyses along with theoretical calculations. Colorimetric measurements showed that color changes were hardly perceptible (ΔE* < 3) for all samples after 10 kGy irradiation. XRF results indicated that the red and yellow fibers were mordanted with aluminum, whereas the blue dye was applied directly. Dye characterization using the LC-PDA-MS method revealed the presence of indigo carmine in the blue fibers, cochineal in the red fibers, and a mixture of weld and cochineal in the yellow fibers. The irradiation at 10 kGy significantly decreased the extractability of red and yellow color components. As no new peaks corresponding to degradation products were detected in the chromatograms, the reduced extractability was attributed to radiation-induced solid-state molecular reorganization, consistent with the Raman and SEM findings. The thermal characteristics of the dyed fibers were almost unaffected by irradiation. Furthermore, theoretical evaluations of the experimental findings were performed using global reactivity descriptors, charge distributions, and local reactivity regions obtained via optimized geometries, MEP mapping, and Fukui functions, respectively. The findings demonstrate that gamma irradiation up to 10 kGy is a safe treatment for historical wool carpets, causing no significant visual or molecular damage to the color components, while even enhancing the stability of certain dyes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Trustworthy artificial intelligence in advanced manufacturing
Abstract: Additive manufacturing is relying more and more on artificial intelligence for prediction, control, and real-time decisions. Deployment, however, is still difficult. The main reason is that the underlying thermal, flow, and microstructural behavior can shift as the process changes, which makes reliable model performance hard to maintain. This review examines how trustworthy artificial intelligence (TAI) can be used to close that gap in digital twins for additive manufacturing across both metallic and ceramic systems. It frames trustworthiness as a technical condition for deployment and translates it into an AM-specific operational framework. From that point onward, it examines how current workflows handle reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, explainability, robustness, generalizability, fairness, and transparency. A structured evaluation of sixty studies in metallic and ceramic additive manufacturing systems reveals a distinct trend. Robustness and generalizability receive much more attention than transparency, explainability, and fairness. The coverage is also stronger in metallic systems than in ceramic ones. To move beyond binary classification, the review further applies a structured evidence-depth rubric that distinguishes absent coverage, limited or implicit evidence, method-level evidence, and operational evidence for each TAI attribute. We further show that trustworthy deployment depends on more than predictive accuracy. It also depends on physically consistent models as well as updates that account for uncertainty. Decision support has to remain interpretable as well. Model transfer across machines and materials should be treated as controlled adaptation, where reusable physics, sensing, and validation elements are separated from material-specific features that require recalibration. The validation path must also support qualification and industrial deployment, leading to a more cohesive digital twin framework. It brings together physics-based models, reduced-order models, learning-based surrogates, multimodal sensing, and trust-aware evaluation. The main finding is that trustworthiness is the missing technical link between digital twins that can be confidently used in advanced manufacturing and promising AI-enabled demonstrations. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Evolution and lifecycle mapping of research methods based on the Boston Matrix in library and information science from 1995 to 2025
Abstract: Developing an evolution framework for research methods is essential for advancing Library and Information Science (LIS), but existing research method schemas remain fragmented and limited. This study proposes an automated framework combining AI-driven methods to mine, classify, and a temporal analysis based on the Boston Matrix to map the lifecycles of research methods. Using a comprehensive dataset of 31,913 articles from 21 LIS journals (1995–2025) as a validation corpus, the framework integrates semantic clustering for bottom-up entity extraction with generative top-down ontology mapping. This approach dynamically maps methods into a four-stage lifecycle schema: mainstream, emerging, marginalized, and mature, revealing distinct evolutionary trajectories and the broader computational turn within LIS. Validated through quantitative threshold testing and qualitative evaluation, the proposed framework significantly reduces manual coding subjectivity and enhances replicability. By empirically comparing the subfields of librarianship and information science, this study accounts for inherent thematic variations and uncovers their distinct paces of methodological adoption. Ultimately, this study offers a robust automated framework for longitudinal methodological tracking, theoretically demonstrating how diverse AI-driven and traditional methods synergistically coevolve and assume distinct scholarly roles within the emerging AI4Science paradigm. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Han L.; Qiao Y.; Jia F.; Zhao Y.; Jia C.
Title: RumorGAL: Graph-anchored LLM for domain-generalized rumor detection
Abstract: Rumor detection models must remain robust to breaking events that are unseen during training. Although large language models (LLMs) offer strong generalization potential, their text-centric nature makes them vulnerable to spurious textual patterns in noisy social media discussions and leaves them without explicit awareness of how rumors propagate through conversation threads. To address these limitations, we propose RumorGAL, a graph-anchored LLM framework for domain-generalized rumor detection. The framework first employs a graph neural network (GNN) to derive graph-anchored structural prefixes from the propagation graph, providing structural guidance for the LLM. It then identifies high-quality textual evidence from noisy discussions through an evidence density-guided mining strategy. Finally, a hierarchical reasoning mechanism organizes both the structural prefixes and textual evidence into a unified reasoning process, enabling the LLM to ground its predictions in both propagation patterns and informative content. Across the three transfer settings, RumorGAL achieves robust performance, improving average accuracy over the strongest baseline, zero-shot GPT-4.1, by 5.27 percentage points under the domain generalization setting. When compared with domain adaptation methods, it surpasses the best domain adaptation method in two out of three tasks, with improvements of 3.1 and 0.5 percentage points in F1 score for the rumor class, respectively. These findings suggest that an LLM-as-primary, GNN-as-auxiliary design, which couples structure-aware guidance with evidence-grounded reasoning, is a promising approach to robust and interpretable rumor detection. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yuan L.; Zhu J.
Title: The security unlock: How rural social pension makes people more entrepreneurial?
Abstract: Previous literature on the determinants of entrepreneurship has not explored the role of social pension. Leveraging variation in the roll-out timing of a universal rural pension program across Chinese counties, our analysis, at both the individual and aggregate levels, reveals that pension provision led to an increase in entrepreneurship among the younger generation. We show that this effect operates through two primary channels: an intergenerational transfer channel and a local demand channel. Specifically, the pension program mitigates upward transfers from adult children to elderly parents, while boosting local consumer demand, which exerts a demand-side “pull” effect on enterprise establishment. Our findings may shed new light on the interplay between pension, intergenerational resource allocation, and entrepreneurial activity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
