Title: Sex-divergent vulnerability to chronic peripheral LPS challenge in aged ApoE4 mice: Male systemic fragility versus female central neuroinflammation
Abstract: Inflammageing links chronic inflammation to biological aging, contributing to senescence and multimorbidity common in the elderly. In neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, inflammatory processes play a causal role in accelerating neurodegeneration. Interestingly, apolipoprotein E (APOE), particularly the APOEε4 allele, is a major genetic risk factor for neurodegeneration, acting as a key immunomodulator with sex differences. This is especially relevant given the lack of clear prevention strategies for APOEε4 carriers. Therefore, this study characterized the sex-specific neuroinflammatory and cognitive vulnerability of APOE4 genotype under a chronic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge in senescence-transition stage. Male and female homozygous apoE4 mice (15–16 months old) were administered intraperitoneal doses of 0 or 0.25 mg/kg LPS three times per week for a total of 17 doses. Body weight was monitored, and behavioural assessments were conducted from the 12th injection until the 17th. Serum and tissues were collected to assess hippocampal, cortical and systemic markers of inflammation, antioxidant-related genes, genes implied in myelin dynamics, and neurotrophin-related transcripts. Findings revealed basal sex-dependent divergent phenotypes with specific responses under LPS challenge. Under LPS treatment, males exhibited higher systemic fragility, with significantly increased mortality, which may have conditioned cognitive outcomes. Females showed greater central alterations related to neuroinflammation along with altered expression of myelin-related transcripts. However, the results suggest a stablished tolerance to LPS. These results highlight how chronic systemic inflammation during ageing in an APOE4 genotype background shapes sex-divergent pathological trajectories, underscoring the need to address sex-specific therapeutic strategies. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Lemmens A.
Title: Algorithmic fairness as a human–technology interaction problem
Abstract: Algorithms shape high-stakes decisions across society. While promising efficiency, algorithms also raise fairness concerns. This article proposes that algorithmic fairness is best understood as a human–technology interaction problem rather than a purely technical challenge. Algorithms can reproduce human biases, amplify them through feedback loops, or create new forms of unfairness through objectives, proxies, and seemingly neutral variables. Yet they can make decision processes more explicit, disparities more visible, and actively mitigate discrimination. Fairness depends not only on statistical properties but also on how algorithms are designed, used and experienced by those affected by their decisions. This article therefore offers an interdisciplinary perspective that integrates insights from social justice, psychology, computer science, judgment and decision-making, and management. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Jeong D.; Min S.
Title: Multi-material topology optimization of tunable multifunctional microstructures with nonlinear magnetic and thermal fields
Abstract: Multi-material microstructures provide a versatile means for tailoring multiple macroscopic properties beyond those of monolithic materials. Achieving reliable magnetic performance while ensuring efficient heat dissipation is essential for magnetic devices and motivates the concurrent design of magnetic and thermal responses. In this context, multifunctional material systems offer an expanded design space for meeting such combined requirements. However, most existing studies on magnetic fields remain limited to single-material systems. To address this limitation, a novel multi-material inverse homogenization framework is proposed to facilitate microstructure design by considering both magnetic and thermal fields. In this approach, micromechanics-based homogenization is employed to evaluate effective properties. A discrete-material-optimization-based interpolation scheme was adopted to represent the spatial distribution of two-phase ferromagnetic materials with inherent trade-offs between magnetic permeability and thermal conductivity and was further modified using exponential interpolation to improve numerical characteristics. To obtain balanced multifunctional designs, a global criterion method was introduced to integrate multiple physical performance criteria into a unified objective function. Several numerical examples were presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results showed that multi-material designs under multi-field conditions offer apparent benefits over their single-material or single-field counterparts and that considering magnetic nonlinearity leads to distinct design outcomes. Furthermore, systematic performance tuning was achieved through material volume fraction control, and directional magnetic responses were realized by introducing an additional orthotropy constraint. This study provides insights into the engineering design of hybrid material systems, highlighting the potential of multi-material and multi-field approaches for achieving controllable and application-relevant functional performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Chen J.; Xia S.; Ma Z.
Title: The role of attention and norm perception in online comments’ impact on attitudes toward sunscreen: An eye-tracking approach
Abstract: Social media platforms have become a major source of health information, where user-generated comments often shape attitudes toward health behaviors. Yet, the mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. This study examines the role of selective attention and perceived norms in the influence of online comments on attitudes toward sunscreen use. Using a between-subject eye-tracking experiment (N = 177), participants viewed a simulated YouTube live-stream video promoting sunscreen misinformation accompanied by either pro- or anti-sunscreen comments. Attention to comments was measured objectively (time viewed, fixation counts) and subjectively (self-reported attention). Results reveal that prior attitudes and behaviors predict selective attention in distinct ways: individuals with more positive attitudes attended more to pro-sunscreen comments, whereas more frequent sunscreen use was associated with more attention to anti-sunscreen comments. Mediation analyses indicate that attention to comments influences perceived norms differently across conditions. In the pro-sunscreen condition, greater attention predicted stronger perceived proximal network norms, which were strongly associated with attitude change. In contrast, in the anti-sunscreen condition, attention predicted weaker perceived social media norms but did not alter proximal norms. Across models, changes in proximal network norms were the most robust predictor of attitude change. Findings highlight the importance of examining selective attention to better understand online comment effects and reveal nuanced normative pathways. The study advances selective exposure and social norm literature in online comment contexts and underscores the value of eye-tracking for objectively measuring visual attention to online comments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From smart cities to smart villages: Evolution, domains, and policy implications for smart rural development
Abstract: Smart villages have evolved from early parallels with urban smart city models into a comprehensive, multidimensional framework that integrates digital infrastructure, agriculture, local enterprises, tourism, and sustainability. This expanded framework recognizes the unique characteristics and potentials of rural areas, moving beyond the urban-centric logic of technology adoption. This review aims to examine the conceptual evolution of smart village research, track emerging methodological trends, and analyze global implementation trajectories. In the early stages, many studies concentrated on definitional debates and approaches that were primarily centered on technology. However, more recent perspectives have begun to emphasize the importance of integrating technological innovation with social innovation, community empowerment, participatory governance, and environmental stewardship. Methodological approaches have also advanced significantly, shifting from conceptual reflections and single-case studies toward more diverse methods including comparative studies, bibliometric mapping, and participatory action research. These evolving methods enable a deeper and more nuanced understanding of smart village dynamics. Regional approaches demonstrate distinct emphases: European initiatives focus on service revitalization and smart specialization; Asian and African strategies prioritize connectivity, renewable energy access, and digital inclusion; while Latin American programs increasingly integrate climate-smart agricultural practices. Despite regional differences, common challenges remain, including the persistent rural digital divide, fragmented coordination among multiple stakeholders, issues of financial sustainability, and the emergence of new forms of inequality. Policy directions increasingly stress the importance of place-based strategies, building local capacities, establishing supportive governance structures, and fostering inclusive participation. The review concludes by identifying critical areas for future research, such as the creation of unified evaluation metrics, conducting longitudinal impact assessments, and embedding smart village initiatives within broader rural development and climate resilience agendas. Overall, smart villages represent dynamic and promising pathways for driving innovation-led, inclusive, and sustainable rural transformation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Authors: Dehghani A.; Salaripour A.
Title: From design attributes to social life: Modelling conviviality in urban underground spaces
Abstract: From being infrastructure utilities, urban underground spaces (UUS) have developed into multipurpose public spaces that combine commercial, cultural, and transit functions. While their technical and spatial contributions to compact urbanism are evident, their capacity to foster conviviality, the experiential quality of inclusiveness, sociability, and shared belonging, is less understood. This study develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework that operationalizes conviviality in UUS by linking seven spatial-perceptual dimensions (safety and security, identity and meaning, accessibility, functionality, environmental comfort, aesthetics, and structure and form) to behavioral mediators of willingness to use and social interaction, culminating in perceived conviviality. Using the Theatre-Shahr underground complex in Tehran as a case study, data were collected through structured surveys and analyzed via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that although environmental factors generally have a positive indirect effect on perceived conviviality, social interaction emerges as the primary mechanism shaping conviviality in urban underground spaces, while willingness to use plays only a complementary and limited mediating role in this process. Among the environmental factors, accessibility, environmental comfort, and safety and security show the strongest effects. In contrast, some variables, particularly identity and meaning and structure and form, do not demonstrate statistically significant effects in certain pathways. These findings suggest that planning and design strategies for urban underground spaces should prioritize environmental qualities that support social interaction, to enhance perceived conviviality. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Enhancing combustion in an ethanol rotary engine via turbulent jet ignition: parametric study and mechanism analysis
Abstract: Enhancing the combustion of ethanol rotary engine (ERE) is crucial for carbon neutrality. This study systematically compares the effects of conventional spark plug ignition mode (CSPIM) and turbulent jet ignition mode (TJIM) on the performance of an ERE. This investigation employs a combined methodology of experimental validation and numerical simulation, systematically analyzes the combustion characteristics of both ignition modes across multiple equivalence ratio conditions. Furthermore, this research elucidates the effect of jet nozzle diameter (JND) on the combustion behavior of the TJIM. The results reveal that TJIM’s effectiveness is governed by the coupling between the energy of the jet flame and the concentration of the mixture in the pre-combustion chamber. It demonstrates superior flame propagation and combustion at equivalence ratios of 1.0 and 1.2 by generating highly turbulent jet flames, but underperforms CSPIM under an equivalence ratio of 0.8 due to reduced jet flame intensity. Furthermore, the optimal JND shifts with the global equivalence ratio — 3.5 mm for lean and 2.0 mm for stoichiometric combustion. The JND governs a trade-off between the mass of fuel in the pre-combustion chamber and the jet flame velocity. While TJIM significantly reduces CO emissions via more complete combustion, it increases NO formation due to higher temperatures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Unconventional plastic accommodation mediated by strain gradients in a multiscale heterostructured Mg alloy at room temperature
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Heterostructures are widely recognized as an effective strategy for achieving strength-ductility synergy in Mg alloys. However, their potential remains insufficiently exploited because most current approaches rely on single-scale structural regulation. In this work, a multiscale heterostructured Mg alloy with through-thickness gradients in grain size, texture, and dislocation density was fabricated via heterothermal rolling. The alloy exhibits a pronounced strength–ductility synergy, with ∼3.3 times higher ductility than that of conventional rolling while maintaining comparable strength. Microstructural characterization reveals that the multiscale heterogeneous architecture rapidly accumulates geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) at the early stage of deformation, establishing a pronounced dislocation density gradient that continuously generates strain gradients along the thickness direction during subsequent deformation. The coupled dislocation and strain gradients promote special boundary formation and activate micro-shear-dominated plasticity. Owing to the through-thickness microstructural heterogeneity, shear bands nucleate heterogeneously across different layers, activating multiple slip systems and accelerating dynamic recrystallization and texture weakening processes that are usually suppressed at room temperature. The recrystallized fraction reaches up to 80% in the necked region, suggesting that the strain gradient can activate high-fraction room-temperature recrystallization and thereby contribute to plastic accommodation in the present heterostructured Mg alloy. Meanwhile, the heterogeneous layers undergo a dynamic soft/hard-domain transition, which sustains strain accommodation and delays strain localization. These findings reveal a strain-gradient-mediated plasticity mechanism and provide a new structural design strategy for overcoming the strength–ductility trade-off in Mg alloys. © 2026

Title: Mental imagery and visuospatial processing in visual communication design education: Examining relationships with creative performance and academic achievement in university students
Abstract: This study investigated the relationships among mental imagery, visuospatial processing, creative performance, and academic achievement in university visual communication design students. A sample of 156 undergraduate students majoring in visual communication design completed the Mental Imagery Test (MIT), Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (RSPM), and Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (TTCT), while their academic performance in design studio, typography, digital imaging, and visual theory courses was assessed through course grades. Results indicated significant positive correlations between mental imagery abilities and both creative performance and academic achievement across all design-related courses. Visuospatial processing, operationalized here as figural-inductive visuospatial reasoning, partially mediated the relationship between mental imagery and academic performance in design studio and digital imaging courses, while creative self-efficacy emerged as an additional mediator for typography performance. Gender differences were minimal, with males showing slight advantages only in spatial transformation tasks. These findings underscore the importance of developing mental imagery and visuospatial skills within visual communication curricula and suggest that targeted cognitive training interventions may enhance both creative output and academic success in design education contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Regulating metallurgical continuity and fracture-path selection through interfacial coupling in multi-material additive manufacturing
Abstract: The growing demand for multifunctional components requires structural and functional properties to be spatially tailored within a single architecture, a capability difficult to achieve using monolithic materials. Multi-material additive manufacturing offers a promising solution, yet its implementation is constrained by the difficulty of forming reliable interfaces between dissimilar alloys. Here, we reveal how interfacial melt-pool coupling governs interface evolution and fracture-path selection in 316L stainless steel/CuSn10 multi-material architectures fabricated by multi-material laser powder bed fusion. Four programmed coupling conditions were produced by varying the cross-boundary scan extension and were operationally classified as decoupled, partially coupled, stably coupled, and over-coupled according to the resulting interfacial morphologies. Stable coupling transformed the sharp and discontinuous boundary into a continuous, chemically heterogeneous transition zone with broadened Fe/Cu redistribution, refined interfacial grains, and locally identified BCC α-Fe within the Cu-rich matrix. This transition suppressed boundary-dominated failure and redirected fracture across both constituent materials, increasing the ultimate tensile strength by 61.7%, from 161.1 to 260.5 MPa, although the elongation decreased from 8.33% to 5.23%, indicating a strength–ductility trade-off. Insufficient coupling preserved lack-of-fusion defects, whereas over-coupling generated pore-bearing Cu-rich regions and shifted failure to a pore-assisted path. Time-resolved synchrotron X-ray imaging further revealed keyhole fluctuation, partial collapse, and pore retention as a plausible pore-formation pathway. Application-oriented multi-material demonstrators with complex geometries were successfully fabricated, supporting the geometric implementation of interface-controlled MM-LPBF. These findings establish a coupling-dependent interface-control principle for balancing metallurgical continuity against defect-assisted damage in multi-material additive manufacturing. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Integrating human–stream interactions into ecological stream assessment: A novel rural–urban socioecological sustainability framework
Abstract: Current assessment tools for streams and rivers focus on ecological functioning while ignoring the social dimension, which varies across rural and urban ecosystems. This study presents the rural–urban socioecological stream sustainability index (hereinafter, RU-SESSI) for assessing stream function across the rural–urban continuum. This index is based on the stream ecosystem services (ES) and biodiversity index (SESBI), which was developed in our previous study to assess stream health. The SESBI was extended into a sustainability subindex by adding two economic indicators, and the framework was complemented by a stream–society interaction subindex comprising accessibility, public safety, and community involvement. Together, these subindices capture stream function through both sustainability performance and human–stream interaction patterns. The framework was refined and validated using the Delphi method, revealing significant differences in the relative importance of most RU-SESSI indicators between rural and urban segments. Applied to the Yarkon Stream in central Israel, the index revealed higher biodiversity and regulating services scores in the rural reach, whereas economic, recreation, and accessibility scores were higher in the urban reach, while public safety and community involvement were comparable between reaches. The urban reach achieved a slightly higher RU-SEES score than the rural reach (6.22 vs. 5.76), with no significant difference in the distribution of weighted indicator scores. The RU-SESSI offers a context-sensitive framework that accounts for unique socioecological dynamics, providing policymakers with valuable insights for tailoring stream management to rural–urban settings and contributing to global water security and sustainability. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: On flat production surfaces associated with Cobb-Douglas-type production models exhibiting variable returns to scale

Title: Benchmarking operational spatial plausibility and temporal compatibility of EEG inverse solutions in the visual P300 network
Abstract: Background: EEG source localization is ill-posed, and competing inverse priors may yield different spatial, temporal, and reliability profiles for visual P300 source estimates. Methods: We benchmarked nine inverse solutions across four families (RAP/TRAP, LCMV/DICS, MNE/dSPM/sLORETA/eLORETA, and Bayesian sparse/hierarchical inference) in 31 participants, 63 sessions, and 2520 trials. Analyses were repeated under an fsaverage template BEM and an alternative spherical conductor model. Outcomes included continuous nearest-ROI distance, 20 mm ROI coverage, 5–40 mm tolerance sensitivity, P3b-window temporal plausibility (300–500 ms with ±25 ms shifts), cross-session reliability, computational cost with setup-versus-inference timing, and source-method×head-model interaction testing. FDR-corrected contrasts, TOST equivalence tests, subject-level bootstrapping, and Aligned-Rank-Transform checks were used. Results: Under fsaverage, LCMV had the highest 20 mm ROI-proximal coverage (21.7%). However, the head-model interaction was significant (p=9.8×10−8), and MNE was the most probable top performer under the spherical model. Cross-session dispersion showed no significant method effect (p=0.866). P3b-timing conclusions were sensitive to the shifted windows, and cross-method agreement was low (mean κ about 0.13). Computational cost ranged from 17.2 to 191.1 s per trial under fsaverage and reached 974.0 s for spherical DICS. Conclusions: The results support uncertainty-aware, multi-constraint method selection rather than a single fixed ranking. © 2026

Authors: Yang Y.; Li J.; Li Y.; Zhang S.; Guo K.
Title: Facilitator or hallucination trap? A social-cognitive account of AI-generated misinformation handling in GenAI-assisted L2 writing
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has demonstrated remarkable potential in second language (L2) learning, yet it is prone to hallucinations. Empirical research on how GenAI-generated misinformation is handled in educational contexts remains scarce. Accordingly, little is known about how these practices shape learning processes and outcomes. Guided by social cognitive theory, the current study frames students' GenAI-assisted L2 writing (using a tailored GenAI writing agent) in a hallucination-prone context in which misinformation was implanted. We examine AI literacy, higher-order thinking resources (i.e., critical thinking and creativity), L2 writing resources (i.e., L2 writing grit and self-regulatory writing strategies), English writing self-efficacy (EWSE), AI-generated misinformation detection (AI-MD), and L2 writing performance within this framework. Using a multi-method approach, combining a qualitative interview study (N = 35), two lab experiments (N = 140), and a large-scale questionnaire survey (N = 406), we find that critical thinking positively predicts GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance via AI-MD, and that negative priming on AI hallucinations significantly improves students’ AI-MD and their GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance, relative to neutral or positive priming. Furthermore, the cross-sectional survey focuses on personal factors and shows that AI literacy significantly predicts EWSE both directly and indirectly through a cognitive–generative pathway involving higher-order thinking resources and a motivational–regulatory pathway involving L2 writing resources. These findings extend social-cognitive accounts of GenAI-assisted L2 writing and inform instruction that helps learners evaluate AI outputs, manage misinformation risks, and sustain their own writing processes. © 2026

Authors: Wang Y.; Wang Z.; Zou Y.; Song Y.; Xia G.; Chen S.; Guo H.; Cao C.; Yang X.; Deng Z.; Li J.; Gong D.; Wang W.; Lyu X.; Tao Z.; Huang X.
Title: Self-disclosure to intelligent virtual agents: A scoping review and the disclosure affordance–actualization–governance framework
Abstract: Intelligent virtual agents (IVAs) have become digital social objects to which people disclose personal, emotional, health-related, and other sensitive information. Yet similar cues—including anthropomorphism, social presence, empathy, gaze, anonymity, and structured questioning—are associated across studies with greater disclosure, refusal, impression management, socially desirable responding, or discomfort. Searches covered four bibliographic databases without publication-year restrictions through March 17, 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar searching on May 20, 2026. This review, reported with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), maps 88 empirical studies and introduces the Disclosure Affordance–Actualization–Governance (DAAG) framework as a middle-range account linking specific empirical findings with broader explanations of IVA-mediated disclosure. DAAG distinguishes sociotechnical interaction ecology; perceived safety from judgment, relational receptivity, expressive latitude, and boundary agency; disclosure actualization; affective, relational, and functional consequences; governance; and evidential reach—the extent to which studies observe perception, behavior, consequences, time, and governance. The literature is most developed for disclosure onset, sensitive reporting, emotional expression, and immediate system acceptance, but remains thin on persistence, reciprocity, subjective–behavioral divergence, correction, revocation, and downstream data use. Recurrent patterns are consistent with IVA cues being interpreted through evaluation risk, partner responsiveness, observability, topic sensitivity, competence, privacy, and control. DAAG is not presented as a validated causal model, but as a framework for explaining when digital social interaction supports, redirects, or appropriately constrains self-disclosure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Perceived need and measured well-being: How well do subjective rankings capture relative poverty?
Abstract: Subjective well-being rankings are widely used to target social protection programs, yet their ability to capture relative welfare and wealth remains debated. This study compares three commonly used subjective ranking methods: self-, peer-, and elite-based poverty rankings, against consumption- and wealth-based measures using a large household survey in Ethiopia, where about 20 households per village were ranked from most to least “needy” by themselves, their peers, and community leaders. We assess concordance between subjective and conventional welfare rankings and explore sources of divergence. Subjective rankings align more with relative wealth than consumption and with total rather than per capita welfare, suggesting they overlook household composition. Among the three subjective ranking methods, elite-based rankings best capture conventional measures, although overall concordance between subjective and welfare-based rankings remains weak. Subjective rankings also better reflect relative deprivation among households exposed to covariate shocks. A composite index combining all three modestly improves concordance with standard metrics. We find suggestive evidence that information asymmetry, favoritism, and welfare dynamics partly explain discrepancies between subjective rankings and conventional welfare measures. These findings offer important insights to improve targeting in data-scarce settings. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Qin S.; Li J.; Qin X.; Fan Q.
Title: Taylor-sparsified differentially private federated learning with support-consensus robust aggregation
Abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative training without sharing raw data, but sparse private updates may still leak information through both support masks and noisy values, while remaining vulnerable to Byzantine attacks. We propose TDP-SRA, a Taylor-sparsified differentially private federated learning framework with support-consensus robust aggregation. Clients select supports using a privatized Taylor utility criterion and release clipped sparse values with Gaussian perturbation, providing client-level privacy accounting for the complete sparse release. The server maintains a temporally smoothed support frequency vector, estimates a consensus support, scores uploads by support agreement and privacy noise normalized residuals, and aggregates server clipped sparse updates via a weighted geometric median in the consensus subspace. We establish client-level Rényi differential privacy and provide sufficient or conditional analyses for support recovery and robust aggregation under explicit support stability, support separation, and effective Byzantine weight assumptions. Experiments on multiple vision datasets under standard, data poisoning, and adaptive support-aware attacks show that TDP-SRA achieves a favorable empirical trade-off among accuracy, privacy, robustness, and uplink communication efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Wang Z.; Yang J.; Qiao X.; Lei L.
Title: Online collective aggression in algorithmic environments: The roles of algorithm awareness, moral outrage, and negative descriptive norms
Abstract: In algorithmic social media environments, filtering, ranking, and recommendation systems shape which online events, comments, and group reactions become visible. However, little is known about whether awareness of these algorithmic processes can reduce online collective aggression. Drawing on a focused application of value-added theory and a multidimensional framework of algorithmic literacy, the present research tested a moderated mediation model in which algorithmic awareness may reduce aggressive participation through attenuated moral outrage, with negative descriptive norms as a boundary condition. Across three experimental studies with emerging adults aged 18–28, participants completed self-developed online collective aggression scenarios. Study 1 (N = 158) showed that experimentally induced algorithmic awareness reduced individuals' tendency toward online collective aggression. Study 2 (N = 306) further found that moral outrage mediated this effect, suggesting that algorithmic awareness may reduce aggressive participation by weakening immediate moralized emotional responses to online events. Study 3 (N = 289) revealed a significant index of moderated mediation: the conditional indirect effect through moral outrage was significant when negative descriptive norms were low but not when they were high. Together, these findings identify algorithmic awareness as a potentially protective cognitive factor whose effects depend on the normative climate inferred from visible cues. They clarify how algorithmic curation, moralized emotion, and normative cues jointly shape aggressive participation. Practically, these findings underscore the need to develop algorithmic literacy education and platform interventions that address both users’ recognition of algorithmic curation and the normative cues conveyed by visible comment environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhang Y.; Qian H.; Luo X.; Liang Y.; Lu P.; Liang Z.; Chen J.; Chen Y.
Title: Life cycle analysis and multi-objective optimization of CCUS-integrated methanol reforming PEMFC-CCHP systems
Abstract: Distributed methanol steam reforming (MSR)-proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) systems have attracted attention due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness. Coupling these systems with combined cooling, heating, and power (CCHP) configurations further enhances energy utilization. However, their strong reliance on fossil fuels leads to substantial carbon emissions. Although integrating carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) mitigates operational emissions, it introduces additional energy penalties, economic costs, and complexity, while its full life cycle environmental benefits remain insufficiently understood. Moreover, conventional single-objective optimization is inadequate to simultaneously balance energy, economic, and environmental performance. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel distributed MSR-PEMFC-CCHP system integrated with CCUS and develops a comprehensive evaluation framework combining life cycle assessment (LCA) and multi-objective optimization. Three configurations—CCHP-C (without carbon treatment), CCHP-S (with CCS), and CCHP-M (with CCUS)—are systematically analyzed to quantify full life cycle environmental impacts and identify optimal trade-offs. Results show the operation stage dominates life cycle emissions, contributing over 80 % in all configurations. Under the adopted inventory assumptions and system boundary, CCHP-M has the lowest total pollutant emissions and global warming potential, whereas CCHP-C has lower acidification and respiratory effect potentials. For CCHP-M, the selected compromise solution, Point D, achieves an energy efficiency of 85.61 % and an LCOE of 0.2463 $/kWh. Compared with the energy-optimal solution, Point K, Point D reduces the LCOE by 2.84 % and lowers life-cycle CO2-equivalent emissions by 2.816 t, or 4.14 %, to 65.153 t, while decreasing energy efficiency by 1.79 %. These results identify the environmental trade-offs among the three carbon-management configurations and the operating compromise within CCHP-M. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effect of CO2 concentration on carbon sequestration and mechanical strength of coal-based solid waste cemented backfill
Abstract: Coal production generates large quantities of coal-based solid wastes (coal gangue, blast furnace slag, and fly ash) and significant CO2 emissions, creating severe ecological challenges in mining regions. This study integrates coal-based solid waste cemented backfilling with CO2 mineral sequestration to manage both solid wastes and CO2. The CO2 uptake and uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) of coal-based solid waste cemented backfill (CSCB) were investigated after 14 days of mineralization curing at CO2 concentrations of 0–10 vol%. Thermogravimetric analysis (TG), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) were used to examine the sequestration mechanism and the associated strength reduction. CO2 uptake increased with CO2 concentration: raising the concentration from 1.5 to 10 vol% increased the uptake from 2.42 to 4.05 wt% (a 67.4% increase), based on a single TG measurement per group. In contrast, UCS decreased from 6.05 MPa (0 vol%) to 0.72 MPa (10 vol%), an 88.1% reduction. Microstructural and mineralogical analyses indicate that CO2 reacts with alkaline phases and hydration products (CH, MH, C-S(A)-H gel, and AFt) to form calcite, gypsum, and possible Mg-bearing carbonate (XRD peaks tentatively assigned to dolomite). The strength loss is attributed to weakening of the alkaline environment, decalcification of C-S(A)-H gel, and carbonation of AFt to gypsum. A concentration of 1.5 vol% provided a reasonable balance, with 2.42 wt% uptake and a 13.2% strength loss. These results show a clear trade-off between carbon uptake and mechanical performance in CSCB. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Pu Y.; Chen H.; Guo Y.
Title: Autonomy-supportive mediation and scam susceptibility: The role of literacy among middle-aged and older adults
Abstract: Although online scams increasingly threaten middle-aged and older adults, existing research has largely focused on individual literacy and short-term interventions, leaving the development and application of scam literacy in everyday contexts less understood. Drawing on parental mediation theory and self-determination theory, this study conceptualizes autonomy-supportive mediation (ASM) as a family-based socialization context for developing aging parents' scam-related literacy. It also considers face concern, a personal orientation reflecting individuals’ motivation to protect their social image from potential social judgment. This study tested two complementary models that distinguish between the foundation of scam literacy (scam knowledge) and its activation (cyber-risk beliefs). Data were collected through a cross-sectional vignette-based survey of 404 middle-aged and older adults in China between February 13 and February 27, 2025, using a volunteer-assisted convenience sampling strategy. The results indicated that higher levels of ASM were linked to lower scam loss, with this association mediated by scam knowledge and moderated by face concern. Moreover, ASM was positively related to cyber-risk beliefs, which were subsequently linked to greater systematic information processing and suspicion toward potential scams. These findings suggest that effective scam prevention depends not only on what individuals know, but also on whether they recognize and respond to risks in real-world situations. This study highlights the importance of autonomy-supportive family communication in combating online scams. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Disaster Management: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses
Abstract: This study presents an examination of artificial intelligence (AI) in the disaster management (DM) cycle to support human decision-making systems. There is an urgent need for holistic application strategies that support disaster risk reduction given the increasing frequency and severity of disaster events. This stems from the growing adoption of AI technologies, including machine learning (ML), deep learning, and natural language processing in transforming disaster management. This is to enable the development of high-performance tools for assessing disaster impacts and addressing un-met human needs. This study reviewed journals and conference proceedings articles from three different academic databases: Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Article selection and query refinement were conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines to support methodological approach. The review explored scholarly perspectives on AI application in DM phases to support human-centered decision-making processes in reducing disaster impacts on human lives. Findings from the review indicate that most existing studies focus primarily on the AI application in the response phase. Despite its potential, integrating AI into disaster management remains challenging, particularly due to widespread misconceptions about adoption of AI, as well as ongoing ethical, trust, and security concerns. This study emphasizes the comprehensive application of AI to enhance planning, encourage proactive measures, and improve response and recovery efforts during disaster events. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: How do children intervene in transgressions? The influence of apology and intervention costs
Abstract: When norms for maintaining cooperative networks are violated, humans try to cope in various ways. However, knowledge is limited regarding how children respond to transgressions. Across two experiments, we examined how 82 six-year-olds, predominantly of Japanese ethnicity (97.6%), choose among punishment, forgiveness, and non-intervention when addressing transgressions from a third-party perspective using a novel paradigm. In addition, we examined how an apology from the transgressor and intervention costs influence children’s moral intervention behaviors. In Experiment 1, Japanese children (N = 41) were presented with a transgressor who either did or did not apologize. Contrary to the previous assumption that children are highly inclined to moral intervention even when it is costly, punishment was the least selected option and non-intervention was the most selected. Children who initially showed reluctance to intervene in transgressions then flexibly adjusted their choice to show forgiveness in response to the transgressor’s apology. In Experiment 2, as in Experiment 1, Japanese children (N = 41) avoided costly punishment and predominantly chose non-intervention. However, when punishment involved no personal cost, children were more likely to choose punishment and less likely to choose no intervention. These findings demonstrate that, when presented with multiple options, 6-year-olds engage less actively in punishment or forgiveness than previous work has suggested, and their intervention strategies are sensitive to social cues and personal costs. This research provides novel insights into the development of moral decision-making in early childhood. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: “The Right to Repair”: A systematic literature review and research agenda for an emerging interdisciplinary field
Abstract: The Right to Repair (R2R) is an important arena in which restrictive repair practices, including limits on access to spare parts, manuals, software, and specialised tools, as well as product designs that inhibit repair, are being contested. Although scholarly interest in R2R is growing rapidly, research remains fragmented across disciplinary and empirical domains, limiting the development of a coherent understanding of its implications for technology-society relations. In response, this paper presents a systematic literature review that maps and synthesises existing research on R2R. Specifically, it (1) consolidates empirical evidence on the implications of R2R; (2) examines how the concept has been theorised across disciplines; and (3) identifies key conceptual and methodological gaps that constrain theoretical and empirical advancement in the field. By organising this literature into coherent thematic domains and tracing the relationships between them, the review argues that the effective realisation of R2R depends on a socio-technical capacity: the practically exercisable ability to repair produced through the interaction between legal entitlements, technological architectures, economic arrangements, and social capabilities. It also reveals disciplinary and geographical imbalances and identifies four tensions structuring future research: formal ownership versus effective control, legal entitlement versus practical repair capacity, universal frameworks versus situated repair practices, and systemic transformation versus continuity. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Integrating fatty acid signatures through machine learning for traceability and nutritional profiling of wild and farmed gilthead sea bream (Sparus aurata)
Abstract: Fatty acid composition of seafood can provide insights into its nutritional value and tools for traceability analysis. In this study, the fillet fatty acid compositions of wild-caught gilthead sea bream and specimens produced under cage-reared and pond-reared aquaculture regimes in Northeast Atlantic waters were evaluated to (i) assess nutritional quality using lipid quality indices and (ii) test the traceability discrimination potential of fatty acids using machine-learning classification (Random Forest) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis. Distinct fatty acid profiles and total lipid contents were observed between all groups. Although wild-caught fish exhibited higher relative abundance of nutritionally important marine fatty acids EPA and DHA, the greater total lipid content of farmed specimens yielded comparable or higher absolute levels of these omega-3 fatty acids. Mid-Atlantic cage-reared fish contained the highest total fatty acid and EPA + DHA contents, whereas coastal cage-reared specimens displayed favorable cardiovascular health indices. The traceability model achieved high accuracy during the training (100%) and validation phases (99.1%), with higher classification accuracy for wild-caught and pond-reared specimens, followed by coastal and Mid-Atlantic cage-reared specimens. Notably, this methodological approach identified key fatty acids, driving discrimination between groups, providing biologically meaningful markers likely linked to feeding regimes and production practices. Overall, fatty acid profiling coupled with machine learning provides a highly accurate framework for discriminating the production groups examined while delivering consumer-relevant nutritional information and supporting future seafood traceability applications. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Dependent development at the energy transition: placing lithium imaginaries in Neoliberal and Contentious Peru
Abstract: We examine lithium and development imaginaries in mining-dependent Peru, asking: What are these imaginaries? What narratives underpin them? Who articulates and shares them, and from where? What forms of state (in)action are envisioned in relation to them? The case study elucidates how alternative “imagined futures” coexist within a natural resource–dependent economy. The ruling national elites in Lima have a neoliberal imagination, treating lithium like any other mineral resource in the country. In contrast, professional elites in the mineral-rich but peripheral region of Puno adopt a resource nationalist view, advocating for direct state involvement in lithium industrialization and the transformation of the domestic energy system, shaped by beliefs on Bolivia's developmental pathway. Among rural community leaders as well as political and social leaders in the districts near lithium and uranium deposits, however, the prevailing idea is that of a social license. In this view, each community has the capacity to negotiate development terms with mining companies independently. In the broader imagination at the resource periphery of a peripheral national economy, the state is perceived primarily as a minimalist governmental actor, necessary only to oversee and ensure the enforcement of mine-community agreements and to provide basic infrastructure. Thus, elites at the political center and communities near expected resource developments converge in their immediate pursuit of rents promised by resource commodification. In the dominant discourses, environmental concerns are often subordinated to economic development goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Hydrazo Bridging Combined with Multiple Hydrogen-Bonding Network: A Strategy for Regulating Energy and Safety in Pyrazinyl Energetic Molecules
Abstract: Hydrogen bonding plays a pivotal role in the crystal engineering of energetic materials and provides an effective strategy for the synergistic regulation of structural stability and energetic properties. In this work, we used polysubstituted pyrazine as the parent skeleton, other six-membered aromatic rings as building blocks, and a hydrazo group as a bridging module to construct a series of symmetric and asymmetric hydrazo-bridged bicyclic pyrazinyl energetic molecules. A systematic evaluation of their geometric structures, electronic properties, detonation performance and safety was conducted by integrating theoretical calculations with experiments. Experimental and theoretical calculations have revealed a clear structure-property rule: as the number of ortho-NH2/NO2 modules increases, the hydrogen bond network gradually becomes more continuous and abundant, leading to improved detonation performance (Dv: 8023∼8414 m·s⁻¹), reduced mechanical sensitivity (IS: 8∼20 J) and improved thermal stability (Td: 223∼283 °C). It is worth noting that the enhancement of hydrogen bonding networks effectively eliminates the long-standing trade-off between energy and safety, while additional conjugation enhancement helps to improve thermal stability. This work establishes hydrazo-mediated multiple hydrogen bond network engineering as a universal and scalable strategy for achieving triple synergistic optimization, providing clear design principles for the next generation of high-performance, insensitive and thermally stable energetic materials. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Multi-omics profiling of muscle tissue reveals metabolic signatures associated with size variation in redclaw crayfish (Cherax quadricarinatus)
Source title: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology - Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
Abstract: The rising market demand for large, premium grade redclaw crayfish (Cherax quadricarinatus) highlights the need for improved production efficiency, yet the molecular characteristics associated with body-size variation remain poorly understood. This study employs an integrated multi-omics approach (untargeted metabolomics, targeted taurine analysis, and transcriptomics) to characterize the metabolic signatures associated with crayfish size variation. Untargeted analysis of 18,204 metabolite features identified 229 differentially abundant metabolites, including a 28-fold higher level of sucrose in large individuals (p = 0.025). Targeted analysis confirmed that taurine, a key osmolyte and antioxidant, was significantly elevated in larger crayfish. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed metabolic features associated with carbohydrate and purine metabolism that correlated with body-size variation. In contrast, smaller crayfish exhibited elevated purine turnover (xanthine/uric acid) and reduced levels of key anabolic metabolites. These findings provide a multi-omics characterization of metabolic states associated with growth phenotypes and identify candidate biomarkers for future studies investigating the potential of nutritional strategies to improve crayfish production. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Online direct-to-consumer channel introducing and ordering strategies of fresh supply chain considering disruption risks and yield constraints
Abstract: The rise of online direct-to-consumer (DTC) channels expands fresh producers’ distribution networks while intensifying competition with traditional retail channels. Meteorological disasters threaten the DTC channel's reliability, dynamically reshaping the coopetition between fresh producers and retailers. This study develops a theoretical framework to examine strategic interactions within a fresh supply chain, comparing a traditional monopoly model with an integrated distribution system that incorporates both DTC and traditional retail channels. Disruption risks and yield constraints faced by producers are considered. The findings suggest producers should introduce DTC channels during yield contraction but exercise caution in surplus periods. Despite disruption risks, DTC channels pressure retailers to accept higher wholesale prices and increase orders, enhancing the sales revenue of fresh produce with limited yield. However, rising disruption probabilities incentivize retailers to reduce order quantities strategically, leading to a higher risk of stagnation for fresh produce. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: Events under fire: Developing an urgent anthropology for events during armed conflicts
Abstract: This conceptual and methodological research note addresses event industry dynamics during armed conflicts, proposing an urgent anthropology approach to document transformations in real time. Using Ukraine as an example, we illustrate how event organizations have adapted to existential threats since the 2022 Russian invasion, demonstrating resilience through cultural initiatives, charitable events, and creative repurposing of resources. We argue that these practices have the potential to sustain cultural identity and to contribute to economic development, social cohesion and morale in conflict settings. To overcome the methodological and ethical challenges of traditional ethnography in war zones, we propose a novel citizen science framework within the urgent anthropology paradigm, leveraging digital technologies, social media, and participatory methods. This approach can decentralize knowledge production, mitigate researcher risk, and create longitudinal archives of industry adaptations. Our proposal supports SDG 16 by suggesting ways to link events and tourism research to peace, justice, and institutional resilience. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: EPIPTrack: Rethinking prompt modeling with explicit and implicit prompts for multi-object tracking
Abstract: Multimodal semantic cues, such as textual descriptions, have shown strong potential in enhancing target perception for tracking. However, existing methods rely on static textual descriptions from large language models, which lack adaptability to real-time target state changes and prone to hallucinations. To address these challenges, we propose a unified multimodal vision-language tracking framework, which leverages explicit and implicit prompts for dynamic target modeling and semantic alignment. Specifically, explicit prompts transform spatial motion information into natural language descriptions to provide spatiotemporal guidance. Implicit prompts combine pseudo-words with learnable descriptors to construct individualized knowledge representations capturing identity-related semantic attributes. Both prompts are dynamically adjusted through a pretrained vision-language text encoder to respond to changes in target states. Furthermore, we design a Discriminative Feature Augmentor to enhance visual and cross-modal representations. Extensive experiments on three public multi-object tracking benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing trackers across diverse scenarios, exhibiting robust adaptability and superior performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Carbon trading in community-based forest management: A bibliometric mapping of scientific publications from 2000 to 2025
Abstract: Carbon trading in community-based forest management (CBFM) has emerged as a promising mechanism for simultaneously addressing climate change mitigation and improving the welfare of rural communities. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of 203 scientific publications obtained from Scopus, covering the period 2000 to 2025, with an analytical focus on the period 2010-2024. Using VOSviewer v.1.6.20 and Scopus's built-in analysis, this study analyzes publication trends, author participation patterns, geographic distribution, journal sources, and thematic structure through author collaboration, co-occurrence of keywords, and bibliographic linking networks. Results show a sharp acceleration in publication growth following key climate policy milestones, including the Warsaw Framework for REDD+ (2013), the Paris Agreement (2015), and COP26 (2021), with a record 21 articles published in 2024. Nepal and Indonesia emerged as dominant knowledge producers, collectively contributing 42.4% of total publications. Thematic mapping identified three main research clusters: carbon governance in CBFM, carbon measurement and quantification, and multifunctional forest landscape ecology. A critical knowledge gap was identified: while the supply side of carbon measurement of forest carbon stocks and biomass has been well documented, the demand side of how communities access, negotiate, and fairly obtain benefits from carbon markets remains largely unexplored. These findings underscore the urgent need for interdisciplinary research that links technical carbon measurement with institutional, economic, and social dimensions of equity to promote fair and scalable carbon trading within the framework of community forest governance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Ethical considerations in establishing reference population DNA databases of Indigenous peoples in Southeast Asia
Abstract: Reference population DNA databases are essential for accurate forensic statistical calculations, yet Indigenous populations remain significantly underrepresented in most forensic genetic repositories, limiting the scientific accuracy of allele frequency distributions and population genetic parameters in affected countries. This gap is particularly acute in Southeast Asia, where Indigenous peoples comprise substantial populations but are largely absent from forensic databases. This paper reports ethical and governance principles that should be considered in establishing and maintaining Indigenous reference population DNA databases to generate empirically derived allele frequency distributions, characterize population structure, and calculate population-specific theta (θ) values for forensic applications. We propose that such databases should be governed by policies discussed with and approved by authorized Indigenous representatives, with independent academic or government institutions serving as custodians. Effective governance requires culturally informed ethical policies, defined organizational structures, standardized operational procedures, and well-trained staff. Drawing on international precedents from Singapore (Health Science Authority), Malaysia (Jabatan Kimia Malaysia), New Zealand (the New Zealand Institute for Public Health and Forensic Science), and the Philippines (Filipino Genomes Research Program, DNA Analysis Laboratory, Natural Sciences Research Institute, University of the Philippines Diliman), we demonstrate that reference population DNA databases can be successfully managed by universities or government agencies that maintain institutional independence from law enforcement while supporting calculations of random match probabilities and likelihood ratios. We identify critical ethical gaps regarding informed consent, community engagement and/or partnership, data ownership, and restrictions on secondary use. We recommend adopting dynamic consent models consistent with Indigenous data sovereignty and the CARE (Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility, Ethics) principles. The Philippines is presented as a case study, demonstrating how free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC) frameworks and stakeholder engagement enable the collection of Indigenous population genetic data while respecting Indigenous rights, albeit with their own challenges. Our findings demonstrate that ethical inclusion of Indigenous peoples in forensic database development is essential for generating accurate, population-specific genetic parameters and advancing forensic science that encompasses both broad general populations and smaller Indigenous communities. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Development and experimental evaluation of common rail direct injection methanol (MD97) fuelled compression ignition engine
Abstract: Methanol has emerged as a promising alternative to fossil fuels for powering internal combustion (IC) engines due to its higher fuel-to-oxygen ratio and lower tendency to form soot. Given the widespread use of compression-ignition (CI) engines in heavy-duty applications, there has been significant interest in adapting methanol for their operation. However, methanol’s inferior autoignition characteristics and longer ignition delay (ID) compared to diesel make its direct use in CI engines challenging. To overcome these limitations, engine modifications are essential to optimise the engine performance and ensure stable combustion. In this experimental study, a single-cylinder, four-stroke CI engine was modified by increasing its compression ratio (CR) and by incorporating an intake air preheating system to improve methanol ignition. The engine’s mechanical fuel injection system was replaced with a custom-built common-rail direct-injection (CRDI) system, and an in-house developed controller was utilised to inject methanol supplemented with an ignition improver (MD97: 97 % w/w methanol and 3 % w/w catalyst). The performance, combustion, and emission characteristics of MD97 were analysed and compared with baseline diesel (FIP 600 bar, SoI 14° bTDC). MD97 achieved stable ignition with a minimum ID of 7° CA, compared to the baseline diesel’s 7.5° CA. Injection timing was further optimised to achieve a balanced trade-off between the engine performance, combustion, and emission characteristics. Under optimised conditions (FIP 500 bar, SoI 13° bTDC), MD97 exhibited ∼40 % higher brake thermal efficiency (BTE), ∼88 % reduction in nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions, and almost negligible exhaust smoke; however, hydrocarbons (HC) and carbon monoxide (CO) emissions increased by ∼23 % and ∼52 %, respectively, compared to baseline diesel. Title: Co-firing of upgraded biomass towards flexible CO2 reduction for coal-fired power plants in China
Abstract: The increasing trend in CO2 emissions from fossil fuels has accelerated the renewable energy development, especially in China, the world's largest CO2 emitter, which targets carbon peaking by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. Co-firing of raw biomass is a promising carbon–neutral energy option in China, but its application is limited to only 10% incorporation with stable combustion performance. Therefore, in this study comprehensively assessed biomass upgrading methods, including torrefaction, pelletization, pyrolysis, and gasification, demonstrated that upgraded biomass exhibited significant potential as an attractive, feasible, and sustainable alternative fuel for a low-carbon approach to co-firing in existing PC power plants. The existing research work revealed that the recent Chinese energy policies support the co-firing of biomass, while biomass upgrading technologies are under development and need bioenergy-supported policies. The results showed that upgraded biomass enables higher co-firing ratios in PC boilers, achieving up to 50% substitution on an energy basis and reducing net CO2 emissions by up to 50% compared with full coal combustion. Co-firing of the upgraded biomass not only maintains the high efficiency of PC and CFB furnaces, but also has the potential to lower their carbon footprint and NOx emissions. Additionally, the effectiveness of the co-firing strategy for achieving carbon neutrality is evaluated. This review paper can assist in identifying the potential methods that can increase the biomass-to-coal ratio during direct co-firing in existing PC furnaces without requiring large modifications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xiao Y.; Liu Y.
Title: Intervention scope and crowd evacuation reliability under panic contagion
Abstract: Evacuation planning under exit failure is conventionally posed as a routing problem, in which the decision that matters is where each occupant is sent. This paper shows that once panic contagion couples crowd density to its own collapse, a control action becomes a load on the crowd it protects, and its reliability is decided by how many occupants it sets in motion. Three decisions that prior work confounds, the exit assignment, the release schedule and the scope of the repair applied when an exit closes, are varied independently in a validated social-force simulator with SIR-type contagion, across three station geometries with 40 paired seeds per cell. Metering the release into three batches is worth 20 to 36 percentage points. Redirecting only the occupants whose exit closed is worth 7.5 to 9.5 points on a linear-program plan and leaves the number of frozen occupants unchanged, whereas a re-solve that also releases the remaining crowd falls 43.5 to 43.9 points below that targeted repair wherever a cascade can develop. Optimizing the assignment yields no dependable gain. Every occupant ends the run evacuated, stranded or frozen, and the value of an intervention is its balance of stranding recovered against freezing induced. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Clemente A.; Penacchio O.
Title: Computational models of hedonic evaluation: An explanatory–predictive framework
Abstract: Hedonic evaluation underlies preferences across domains ranging from food and social stimuli to art. Increasing evidence suggests that these diverse judgements rely on common computational and neurobiological principles, motivating a unified perspective on how hedonic value is constructed. Computational modelling has become central to this endeavour by transforming conceptual theories into quantitative, testable accounts of how sensory information, prior experience, internal states and contextual factors give rise to subjective value. However, the rapid expansion of computational approaches has produced a heterogeneous landscape of models that differ in their assumptions, computational principles, explanatory ambitions and predictive performance. Here, we propose an explanatory–predictive framework for organising, comparing and evaluating computational models of hedonic evaluation. The framework characterises models according to two complementary dimensions: mechanistic explainability and empirical predictive performance. We also organise models into six broad families defined by their dominant computational principles. Finally, we argue that progress will depend less on competing modelling traditions than on integrating complementary computational principles into a general computational theory of hedonic evaluation. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Oxygen recovery in a long channel PEM fuel cell using side injection: Balancing uniformity, power density, and pressure drop
Abstract: Increasing the length of proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell channels attracts a lot of attention due to benefits such as enhanced reactant residence time, increased contact area and mass transfer path, and reduced edge effects. However, increasing the channel length may lead to a non-uniform distribution of the reactant along the flow path, which can result in performance degradation in the downstream regions. To compensate for this defect, the effect of side air injection into the cathode channel on the performance and oxygen concentration uniformity in a long PEM fuel cell is numerically investigated. A parametric study evaluating the impacts of the number and arrangement of injection ports on reactant distribution and overall cell efficiency of PEMFC was conducted and compared with case of without injection to finding the optimal configuration from point of view of power density and performance index. Results demonstrate that side injection effectively compensates for the oxygen concentration decline resulting from increased PEMFC channel length. Depending on the injection port arrangement, the power density enhancement relative to the no-injection case ranges from 27% to 158.96%. The highest power density was achieved with the eight-injection configuration (ports 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9), corresponding to a 158.96% increase. Furthermore, the six‑injection configuration (ports 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 9) emerges as the global optimum based on the performance index, which accounts for the trade‑off between hydrodynamic resistance and electrochemical performance, thus maximizing efficiency while avoiding excessive pressure drops. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Does artificial intelligence improve social stability risk performance in China?
Abstract: This paper examines whether and how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to improving the social stability risk level in China. Against the backdrop of rapid digital transformation and increasingly complex governance challenges, AI has been widely adopted in areas such as public security, social management, and risk monitoring. However, its actual effectiveness in mitigating social stability risks remains underexplored. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions in China, this study constructs an empirical framework to evaluate the impact of AI policy on social stability risk levels. The analysis integrates indicators of technological capacity, governance performance, and socio-economic conditions, and applies quantitative methods to identify both direct and indirect effects. The findings suggest that AI policy significantly reduces social stability risks by promoting digital economy development, increasing wage levels and investment in education. At the same time, the results reveal notable regional heterogeneity. The AI policy significantly reduces social stability risk in the central and western regions, and areas with moderate digital economy development, but has no statistically significant effect in economically developed and digitally advanced areas. The study also highlights potential challenges, including data governance concerns and uneven technological access, which may offset some of AI's benefits. This research contributes to the literature by linking technological innovation with social governance outcomes and provides policy implications for leveraging AI to promote social stability. It suggests that policymakers should not only invest in AI infrastructure but also address institutional and regional disparities to ensure inclusive and effective risk management. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Zhao Z.; Wu S.; Liu Y.; Cao Y.
Title: Biomass densification-assisted pyrolysis for bio-oil production: structural regulation, product distribution, and fuel-quality trade-offs
Abstract: Biomass pyrolysis is a promising route for producing bio-oil and value-added chemicals, but its practical application is limited by the low bulk density, unstable storage and transportation, poor feeding behavior, and structural recalcitrance of lignocellulosic feedstocks. Biomass densification provides an effective strategy to overcome these supply-chain constraints while also functioning as a structure-regulating pretreatment for subsequent pyrolysis. This review summarizes how compression-induced particle rearrangement, lignin softening and redistribution, pore reconstruction, hemicellulose disruption, and cellulose crystallinity variation affect heat transfer, volatile release, product distribution, and bio-oil quality. The synergistic roles of torrefaction, hydrothermal carbonization, steam explosion, biological and chemical pretreatments, and reactive co-densification are further discussed. These coupled strategies can improve feedstock uniformity and alter product distribution and bio-oil characteristics during subsequent pyrolysis. Their performance varies with feedstock properties, treatment intensity, densification conditions, and reactor operation, so the preferred route also depends on the desired product. Route selection must balance gains in liquid yield, bio-oil quality, or phenolic enrichment against the additional energy input and chemical or solvent recovery required by the process. This review highlights densification-assisted pyrolysis as an integrated pathway linking biomass supply, structural regulation, product-oriented conversion, and sustainable system design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Microbial contamination and hygiene practices in small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses in Vietnam: The effects of two interventions
Abstract: Foodborne diseases impose major health and economic burdens on low- and middle-income countries. In Vietnam, bacterial contamination is common along pork supply chains, particularly within traditional slaughterhouses. These facilities therefore represent key intervention points for improving food safety. This study evaluated the effects of interventions on microbial contamination and hygiene practices across small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses in four provinces of Vietnam. A controlled trial was conducted in 16 small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses. Eight slaughterhouses were first randomly assigned to receive a ‘Technique’ intervention (low-cost equipment and training), while the remaining eight served as no ‘Technique’ group. Within both groups, four slaughterhouses additionally received an ‘Incentive’ intervention (practice-rating program with monetary rewards). Microbiological and behavioral data were collected pre- and post-intervention through swabs of workers' hands (n = 128), pig carcasses (n = 192) and structured observation checklists (n = 192). The main effects of the ‘Technique’ and ‘Incentive’ interventions were evaluated using difference-in-differences mixed-effects models. The results revealed that Salmonella prevalence and mean total bacteria count on carcasses did not significantly change (37.5% and 5.4 log10 CFU/cm2 at baseline to 35.4% and 4.7 log10 CFU/cm2 at endline, respectively). Coliforms and Escherichia coli counts decreased across all groups, including the control, a pattern more consistent with seasonal and operational factors than the interventions. Neither intervention was associated with lower carcass contamination, and hygiene practice scores were not associated with contamination. Temperature, slaughtering capacity and workforce size showed mixed associations with microbial indicators. The ‘Technique’ intervention produced measurable improvements in hygiene practices, while the ‘Incentive’ intervention improved practices only in the short-term. While neither intervention reduced contamination, the study documents real-world slaughterhouse conditions and suggests that durable improvement will require sustained, multi-level strategies that combine behavioral change with structural and environmental upgrading. Title: Efficacy of group-based acceptance and commitment therapy in reducing anxiety and improving mental health among adults recovering from COVID-19: a quasi-experimental interventional study
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Background: Survivors of COVID-19 frequently encounter persistent psychological distress. While Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) aims to enhance psychological flexibility, its clinical utility and underlying mechanisms in post-pandemic recovery within diverse cultural contexts require further empirical investigation. Objective: This study evaluated the efficacy of a group-based ACT intervention in alleviating anxiety and promoting psychological well-being and mental health among COVID-19 survivors in Iran. Methods: This study employed a quasi-experimental interventional design with a pretest–posttest and 6-week follow-up assessment, including a control group. Individuals meeting the preliminary eligibility criteria were screened using the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) and the General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28). A total of 40 adults who had recovered from COVID-19 and exhibited clinically significant anxiety and reduced general mental health were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the ACT intervention group (n = 20) or the control group (n = 20). The intervention consisted of eight weekly 90-minute sessions focusing on the core processes of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). Outcomes were assessed using the BAI and GHQ-28 at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at a 6-week follow-up. Results: Analysis of the 36 participants who completed the protocol revealed that the ACT group demonstrated significant and sustained reductions in anxiety and somatic symptoms, alongside marked improvements in social functioning and overall mental health compared to the control group (p < 0.001). These gains were maintained at the 6-week follow-up. High intervention fidelity (90%) and attendance (87%) suggest the feasibility and acceptability of this approach in a post-viral clinical context. Conclusions: Group-based ACT is an efficacious and feasible intervention for addressing the long-term psychological sequelae of COVID-19. The findings support the integration of ACT into rehabilitation programs to enhance resilience and quality of life in survivors. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive

Title: Exposing rumor in online networks: A CP tensor-based detection framework
Abstract: With the proliferation of social media, the speed and scope of rumor dissemination have grown exponentially, posing significant challenges to information security and public governance, thus necessitating the development of robust rumor detection methods to address the increasingly complex online environment. Conventional rumor detection approaches, primarily relying on natural language processing or single-modal feature analysis, struggle to capture the complex user interactions and multi-dimensional contextual correlations in social networks, while graph neural network (GNN)-based methods, despite exploiting structural information, remain vulnerable to malicious manipulations and adversarial perturbations, resulting in limited generalization and detection performance. To address these challenges, this study proposes an adversarial training-based rumor detection framework, which integrates posts, authors, users, and comments into a fourth-order rumor feature tensor, leverages a multi-graph regularization joint optimization mechanism within the CP tensor decomposition framework, and incorporates four camouflage strategies under a min-max optimization framework to enhance the model's capability to model heterogeneous relationships and resist adversarial attacks. Experimental results on the PHEME and Weibo datasets show that the proposed framework achieves strong performance and improved robustness compared with the considered baselines. © 2026
