Title: LENS: A graph-based ciphertext semantic retrieval scheme with lightweight representations
Abstract: With the rise of cloud outsourcing and pre-trained language model-driven semantic retrieval, high-quality semantic search over encrypted data remains challenging. Existing schemes either depend on keywords or coarse representations that cannot capture complex semantics, or use high-dimensional dense vectors with linear scanning, causing prohibitive computation. Although tree indexes reduce latency, their rigid partitioning may miss neighbors. Meanwhile, encrypted graph indexes still lack explicit leakage characterization and security adaptation. To address these issues, we propose a ciphertext semantic retrieval scheme that jointly integrates robust semantic representation learning, lightweight vector compression, and graph-based navigation. Specifically, we construct low-dimensional compact semantic vectors for encrypted computation through hard-negative-driven sample construction, global-local collaborative optimization, and multi-level self-distillation. We then build an encrypted graph index whose retrieval workflow is isomorphic to hierarchical navigable small world graph (HNSW) search. We further characterize the leakage boundary of graph-based retrieval and prove chosen-keyword attack security under an IND-CPA secure inner-product primitive. Experiments on the TREC corpus demonstrate a better trade-off among query efficiency, retrieval quality, and scalability than scan-based and tree-based baselines. These results suggest that high-performance ciphertext semantic retrieval requires the joint design of representation learning, index topology, and security modeling. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: A perception-oriented framework for assessing wind turbine aerodynamic noise and operating-parameter effects with normal amplitude modulation
Abstract: To evaluate the effects of wind turbine operating parameters on residents’ perceived annoyance from aerodynamic noise in open rural areas, this study proposes a perception-oriented engineering framework that explicitly accounts for normal amplitude modulation (NAM). Initially, the ISO 9613–2:2024 propagation model is combined with empirical corrections to characterize attenuation across different azimuthal directions around the turbine. A directionally corrected Quasi-AM factor is then introduced to quantify variations in modulation depth under diverse propagation conditions and turbine operations. To better capture subjective human response, a power-law saturation penalty model is developed to adjust the conventional sound pressure level (SPL) by incorporating the contribution of NAM. The resulting NAM-corrected A-weighted sound level is subsequently employed in an annoyance model to evaluate residents’ perceived disturbance. The framework is validated through representative case studies in open rural areas, examining the effects of yaw angle, pitch angle, and rotational speed on the Quasi-AM factor, NAM-corrected A-weighted sound level, and perceived annoyance. Results demonstrate that the framework accurately captures the principal azimuthal variation of NAM, with a mean absolute error of approximately 0.38 dB, NAM-related corrections reach up to 3.60 dB in the main radiation region, indicating that NAM can substantially amplify perceived annoyance even when overall SPL changes are limited. The power-law saturation penalty model exhibits strong fitting performance (R2 = 0.9461), confirming its ability to represent the nonlinear contribution of NAM to annoyance. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that yaw angle, pitch angle, and rotational speed exert distinct effects on the spatial distribution of perceived annoyance. Overall, this framework provides a robust and practical tool for noise-oriented optimization of wind turbine operation and environmental assessment in rural wind farm settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Murai N.; Yamada T.
Title: Design of piezoelectric energy harvester with low frequency vibration via multiscale topology optimization
Abstract: Vibration energy harvester with piezoelectric material is expected as maintenance free power source for small electronic devices taking the advantages of compactness and high power density. Power generation capacity of the harvesters is not sufficient for applications especially at low frequency range. The basic strategy to improve the output power is matching the natural frequency of the harvester to the outer vibrations. However, change of the shape of the harvester to match the natural frequency to low frequency detract compactness of the piezoelectric harvesters. To address this trade-off, we consider a lattice-structured energy harvester and develop a multiscale topology optimization framework. The proposed method concurrently optimizes the macroscale structure and the microscale unit-cell structure by using the homogenization method to estimate the effective properties of the lattice. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Sun Q.; Wang R.; Wu J.; Ji F.; Peng J.; Chiclana F.
Title: Transforming noncooperative behavior with dynamic trust and weight incentives mechanism in social network group emergency decision making
Abstract: In emergency disaster response, resource allocation conflicts stemming from functional specialization often trigger noncooperative behaviors that severely compromise group decision-making efficiency. Existing social network group decision-making methods face two critical limitations: static trust models fail to capture the dynamic evolution of decision-makers’ credibility, and penalty mechanisms tend to provoke psychological resistance in high-pressure environments. To address these issues, this study develops an incentive-driven consensus framework. The approach integrates subjective trust relationships with objective behavioral similarity to construct a dynamically updated composite trust scoring mechanism, which enables adaptive allocation of decision makers’ weights. Furthermore, it introduces a harmony degree-based feedback mechanism incorporating a maximum individual cooperation willingness detection model to accurately identify noncooperative decision-makers. The core contribution lies in its weight incentive mechanism, which stimulates cooperation by increasing the decision weights of noncooperators, thereby transforming the traditional penalty paradigm into a reputation-based incentive paradigm. Case studies and comparative analyses demonstrate that the framework not only achieves consensus at lower adjustment but also effectively transforms noncooperative behavior into proactive collaboration while ensuring fairness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Ni J.; Chen L.; Yu N.; Xia S.
Title: Granular-ball graph coarsening for graph representation learning
Abstract: Graph coarsening provides an effective approach for improving the computational efficiency of Graph Neural Networks; however, existing paradigms often suffer from a connectivity-semantics gap, where rigid partitioning leads to a resolution mismatch that compromises structural integrity. To resolve these challenges, we propose GBC-GL, a novel granular-ball-based coarsening framework designed for high-fidelity graph representation learning. GBC-GL initiates with a connectivity-driven decomposition to safeguard the global topological skeleton. Building on this, we develop a structure-aware partitioning strategy that synergistically fuses PageRank-derived centrality with multi-scale features to map nodes into optimal granules. Crucially, a dynamic granularity control mechanism adaptively modulates aggregation scales based on local structural complexity, effectively mitigating information collapse in critical motifs while maximizing redundancy reduction. Extensive experiments across 16 benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of GBC-GL: it consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, yielding a 95.94% accuracy on Physics for node classification, 84.80% on YEAST for graph classification, and a 0.628 mean absolute error on ZINC for graph regression. Notably, GBC-GL delivers a 50-fold to 60-fold acceleration compared to spectral-based methods on representative graph classification benchmarks, effectively bridging the gap between high-efficiency graph compression and high-precision predictive modeling. Title: International supply chain drivers of forage-livestock conflicts in pastoral China
Abstract: China aims to eliminate forage-livestock conflicts (FLCs) in pastoral areas by 2035 to restore degraded grasslands and address related environmental, social, and economic issues. International trade affects grazing-induced FLCs in pastoral China through global economic supply chains. Here, we examine the crucial foreign consumption drivers, international supply chain paths, and global socioeconomic factors influencing FLCs in pastoral China from 2010 to 2020. The results show that foreign consumption caused two million tons of FLCs in pastoral China in 2020. During 2010–2020, foreign consumption contributed 0.1%–10.4% of FLCs in each pastoral province of China. Inner Mongolia, one of the vital ecological barriers against sandstorms in Asia, underwent a significant increase (92.0%) in its FLCs caused by foreign consumption over the decade. The final production sectors in critical international supply chain paths moved from non-pastoral provinces to foreign economies during 2010–2020. In addition, foreign economic structure transitions led to 660 kt of FLC increments during the decade, where foreign production structure transitions contributed 66.8%. Our findings highlight the importance of optimizing foreign production structures and fostering international cooperation to realize China's goal of FLC elimination. © 2026

Title: Semantic drift-resistant learning for robust multimodal sentiment analysis with incomplete information
Abstract: With the rapid growth of multimodal user-generated content, multimodal sentiment analysis in real-world applications is increasingly challenged by missing modality information. Existing methods mainly focus on missing information reconstruction or representation completion, while paying less attention to the disruption of cross-modal semantic consistency caused by incomplete information, which leads to latent representation shifts and further induces semantic drift. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Semantic Drift-Resistant Learning framework (SDRL) from the perspective of semantic drift mitigation. Specifically, SDRL models the representation relationship between complete and incomplete states through semantic consistency constraints to restrict the semantic deviation caused by missing information. Meanwhile, a reliability-aware proxy compensation mechanism is introduced to generate proxy semantic representations from non-text modalities and dynamically adjust the contribution of textual and proxy representations, thereby reducing the interference of unreliable information during cross-modal representation learning. Furthermore, a hierarchical consistency optimization strategy is designed to constrain the propagation of semantic drift from multiple perspectives, including local representations, global structures, and task responses. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SDRL consistently outperforms existing methods under different missing rates and various missing modality patterns on the MOSI, MOSEI, and SIMS datasets. The results verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in mitigating semantic drift and preserving semantic information in incomplete multimodal scenarios. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Shi P.; Chow C.-O.; Wong W.R.
Title: IAEF: Illumination-adaptive event-frame fusion framework for autonomous driving object detection
Abstract: Object detection for autonomous driving degrades under varying illumination. Traditional RGB cameras lose information in extreme brightness and darkness, and existing RGB-event fusion methods do not adapt to how information distribution shifts between modalities as lighting changes. We propose the Illumination-Adaptive Event-Frame Fusion Framework (IAEF), which combines RGB frames and event camera streams through three modules: an Adaptive Multi-modal Feature Extraction Network that cross-enhances features between modalities at multiple scales; an Illumination-aware Complementary-Unique Fusion module that separates unique and complementary features and weights them according to local illumination; and an Event-Frame Fusion Dynamic Detection Architecture that routes scenes through a lightweight or heavy detection path based on learned scene difficulty. On the DSEC-Det dataset, IAEF achieves 82.6% mAP50 and 52.3% mAP50:95, outperforming SFNet by 2.6% in mAP50 among RGB-Event methods and TSD-DETR by 4.2% among RGB-only methods. The gain is largest at night, where IAEF exceeds YOLO-FSE by 6.6% in mAP50, confirming that illumination-conditional fusion provides the greatest benefit when RGB features degrade most. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Tourism's temporal pathways: A deceleration framework
Abstract: This research introduces Tourism Deceleration as a theoretically grounded framework for understanding temporal recalibration in tourism. Building on social acceleration theory and consumer deceleration framework, we conceptualize tourism deceleration as a situated temporal negotiation through which travelers recalibrate pace, attention, mobility, digital connectivity, and presence. Using hybrid deductive-inductive qualitative content analysis supported by LLM-assisted coding and human validation, we analyze 367 unique Reddit posts and 21,554 comments related to slow travel and long-term travel. The findings show that decelerated travel is often negotiated through practical, social, and personal constraints rather than simply chosen as a preferred travel style. Episodic deceleration remains the most explicit form of decelerated travel, while extended duration often intersects with embodied practices, reduced mobility pressure, and selective negotiation of digital technologies. The research note contributes by distinguishing tourism deceleration from slow tourism and explaining how travelers manage time under conditions of choice, context, and constraint. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Ecological mechanisms and bifurcation dynamics in a mathematical model of African wild dogs
Abstract: The African wild dog (Lycaon pictus) is an endangered species, they live in cooperative packs led by alpha males and females, responsible for breeding and hunting. Young members disperse to maintain genetic diversity, while integration from other packs is welcomed. Pack size is crucial for survival: small packs struggle to hunt and face extinction, whereas large packs face challenges in feeding and raising pups. A mathematical model of predator–prey dynamics includes three roles within the predator population: pups and breeding helpers, active hunters, and dispersing individuals. The study demonstrates the fundamental role of social structure and cooperation in predator–prey dynamics. By incorporating Allee effects and dispersal, the model provides a more realistic representation of population viability in social carnivores and offers quantitative guidance for conservation of endangered cooperative species such as African wild dogs. Bifurcation analysis identifies critical thresholds separating steady and oscillatory regimes: Allee effects lower the threshold for oscillatory onset and amplify their intensity. At the same time, dispersal acts as a stabilizing force, delaying oscillatory behavior and enhancing population persistence. Numerical simulations reveal that Allee effects lengthen and amplify population cycles, particularly during socially dependent life stages, thereby increasing vulnerability at low densities. The existence of stable limit cycles confirms the persistence of oscillatory dynamics and enables detailed characterization of their periods. Furthermore, employing bifurcation analysis, which includes both Hopf and transcritical bifurcations, reveals critical transitions in system behavior as key parameters change. This analysis offers insights into the conditions necessary for stability. © 2026 International Association for Mathematics and Computers in Simulation (IMACS).

Title: Multiscale engineering of lignocellulosic materials: from hierarchical deconstruction to genetic reprogramming
Abstract: The widespread reliance on fossil-derived materials has enabled modern manufacturing but has also driven plastic pollution, carbon emissions, and end-of-life waste challenges. Lignocellulosic biomass offers a renewable and biodegradable alternative, yet its intrinsic heterogeneity has historically limited precise materials design. In this Review, we present a unified multiscale engineering framework for lignocellulosic materials, using wood as an archetypal system to illustrate how structure–property–function relationships can be deliberately programmed from the molecular to the macroscopic scale. We synthesize recent advances in hierarchical deconstruction (top-down processing of cell-wall polymers into micro-, nano-, and molecular building blocks) alongside emerging hierarchical assembly strategies enabled by genetic reprogramming of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin biosynthesis. This convergence enables unprecedented control over composition, anisotropy, interfaces, and transport pathways, yielding biomass-derived materials with tailored mechanical, optical, barrier, and electrochemical performance. We further discuss how these approaches reduce feedstock heterogeneity, improve process efficiency, and align materials development with circular-economy principles, carbon sequestration, and low-impact manufacturing. By linking molecular-level design and genetic modification to scalable processing routes and device-level functionality, this review positions engineered lignocellulosic materials as credible, high-performance alternatives to fossil-based plastics and composites, with transformative implications for energy, environmental, and sustainable manufacturing applications. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: The effects of resilience-oriented workspace interventions: combining social network analysis and organizational quality indicators
Abstract: Although it is known that workspace influences the performance of healthcare teams, there is scarce evidence regarding how to evaluate its implications for resilient performance. This study demonstrates an integrated approach for evaluating the effects of relocating three acute response teams responsible for the same patients – the rapid response team (RRT), medical on-call team (MOC), and nursing supervision (NS) – from separate rooms to a shared workspace. The intervention was evaluated using two complementary sources of evidence. First, social network analysis surveys were conducted before and after the intervention with the same 30 participants. The surveys mapped advice-seeking relationships from which 22 social network metrics were derived. Second, seven organizational quality indicators were analyzed before and after the intervention. Five quality and 12 network indicators showed statistically significant improvements; except for two social network metrics, all 27 indicators changed in the expected direction for improvement. Notably, reciprocity between teams, which is crucial for resilience, increased substantially – e.g., RRT↔MOC increased from 57.5% to 80.0%. Changes in collaboration patterns and quality indicators provided complementary evidence that the conditions supporting resilient performance were enhanced. The evaluation approach can be adapted to other resilience-oriented interventions in which relational dynamics and patient safety are crucial. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Cui J.; Wang S.
Title: Chemical proximity governs open-world infrared identification of microplastics using dual-evidence calibration
Source title: Spectrochimica Acta - Part A: Molecular and Biomolecular Spectroscopy
Abstract: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) classifiers can assign familiar polymer labels to spectra outside their training domain. We developed SPARC-FTIR to couple class-conditional conformal prediction with a calibrated distance gate for binary high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP) identification with rejection. Five spectral views were combined in a training-derived principal-component representation. The two gates distinguished label-set uncertainty from departure from the known feature domain and produced four evidence states. After auditing sample identifiers, 776 spectra were retained from an open ATR-FTIR collection; 689 HDPE/PP spectra supported training, calibration and testing, while 87 non-target spectra were withheld. On the primary test partition, closed-set balanced accuracy was 100%, 124 of 139 known spectra were accepted correctly, and 37 of 87 unknown spectra were rejected. Rejection was 29.4% for low-density polyethylene, 33.3% for mixtures and 100% for the 14 remaining unknown spectra. Across 30 group-preserving splits, mean known acceptance and unknown rejection were 92.8% and 36.3%, respectively. Matched spectral-library comparisons showed different subgroup trade-offs in acceptance and rejection. Frozen-model evaluation on two additional libraries showed acquisition-dependent acceptance and rejection. The calibrated decision states provide an auditable basis for reviewing spectra within a declared HDPE/PP scope; overlapping polyolefin spectra and cross-library transfer remain the principal constraints. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The evolving science of negotiation alternatives: New contexts, new perspectives
Abstract: We review the past decade (2016 – present) of empirical research on negotiation alternatives across multiple disciplines, including dyadic bargaining, international trade, and civil conflict interventions. Three themes emerged in our analysis: First, research has focused on how the effects of a negotiator's BATNA (best alternative to a negotiated agreement) are not person-invariant but are instead moderated by the characteristics of the party who “holds” the BATNA. Second, studies are establishing the conditions under which negotiation alternatives can backfire and hurt a negotiator's performance. Third, an emerging stream of research challenges our conventional understanding of BATNA by highlighting its perceptual nature and the possibility that it may exist on multiple levels within a given negotiation. We close by outlining future directions for each of these emerging themes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Nodding of virtual humans does not necessarily increase customer trust: a temporal analysis
Abstract: Virtual humans can potentially facilitate engaging customer interactions, but remain rarely used in customer service. Their embodiment enables virtual humans to use non-verbal listening cues like nodding. Nodding is theorized to increase trust in virtual humans, but literature on this effect is scarce, inconsistent, and only uses measurements after interactions. This study therefore aims to research how nodding of virtual humans influences customer trust, by (1) studying the following hypothesized mediation: nodding (social cue) triggers perceived responsiveness (social signal), which subsequently increases trust (social response); and (2) studying temporal trust dynamics within a customer interaction using exploratory analyses. An online experiment (N = 429) was performed, using a between-subjects design with two conditions: a virtual human either nodded during listening or did not. To isolate nodding optimally, participants watched a video of a customer interaction: a virtual human advised a customer on a wardrobe. While watching, participants used a slider scale to keep updating their temporal trust in the virtual human. Afterwards, participants answered questionnaires on trust and perceived responsiveness. Results showed that nodding did not increase trust or perceived responsiveness, nor did nodding build temporal trust. Temporal trust was built throughout the customer interaction, mostly when the virtual human was speaking. Exploratory analysis found that nodding increased anthropomorphism. Possibly, nodding did not influence trust because other social cues already caused trust-building. Virtual human developers should therefore be aware that nodding does not necessarily build customer trust. The temporal trust scale was useful for visualizing trust-building throughout customer interaction videos. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Building sustainable influencer partnerships within the creator economy
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Influencer marketing has become an integral part of retail branding strategies. As the creator economy continues to expand, influencer collaborations are now viewed as strategic partnerships rather than promotional activities. Despite this transition, sustaining authentic and long-term brand-influencer partnerships remains a significant yet underexplored challenge. Combining Social Exchange Theory (SET) and Self-Determination Theory (SDT) into a unified motivational-exchange framework, this research focuses on how brand practices operate simultaneously as relational exchange resources and as psychological need-satisfying inputs within influencer–brand partnerships. With a mixed-methods two-phase approach, this study exmains how brand ethical–purpose alignment, autonomy support, and AI co-creation are linked to influencers' sense of ownership and thriving, as well as citizenship behaviours and partnership continuity. In Study 1, 22 semi-structured interviews were conducted with professional influencers across four regions, intended to understand their lived partnership experiences. In Study 2, responses from 422 influencers were analysed using structural equation modelling and moderation analysis. The study also examines serial indirect pathways through which brand practices are associated with voluntary citizenship behaviours and partnership continuity via Collaboration Ownership and Influencer Thriving. The findings suggest that autonomy support, purpose alignment, and AI co-creation enablement are positively associated with influencers' ownership and thriving. These again are associated with higher levels of voluntary advocacy and intentions to continue partnerships. Therefore, the research positions influencer collaboration as relational rather than transactional and highlights the significance of autonomy, ethical-purpose congruence, and relational fairness in understanding sustainable relationships between influencers and brands. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Why skilled migrants stay or leave host countries: A belongingness theory perspective
Abstract: While skilled migrants have a high propensity to quit their jobs and leave host countries, little is known about why some skilled migrants leave while others stay. This paper draws on belongingness theory to examine the mediated effects of work and non-work sense of belonging between skilled migrants’ local language proficiency and host country exit, and the moderated effects of work and non-work social support from locals between local language proficiency and both belonging types. Regression analyses of time-lagged, multisource data collected from 159 foreign academics in Japan suggest that local language proficiency was positively related to work sense of belonging, which was subsequently negatively related to host country exit. Furthermore, the positive relationship between local language proficiency and work sense of belonging was stronger when work and non-work social support were high. This paper contributes to the literature by providing a novel perspective on skilled migrants’ host country experiences, shifting the focus from withdrawal cognitions to belongingness and host country exit, and integrating language proficiency into the theory of belongingness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Vulnerable narcissism outperforms grandiose narcissism as a predictor of social comparison orientation, motives, and affect
Abstract: Narcissism is often characterized by feelings of superiority over others, yet little research has directly tested its relationship with social comparison. Existing work has focused mostly on grandiose narcissism, leaving the role of vulnerable narcissism largely unexplored. Thus, it remains unclear how the two dimensions of narcissism contribute to social comparison processes. Across four correlational studies, we tested how facets of narcissism predict frequency of making social comparisons (Study 1, N = 176; Study 2, N = 217), motives for making comparisons (Study 2), tendencies to make upward and downward comparisons (Studies 3, N = 228; 4 N = 300), and affective responses to upward and downward comparisons (Studies 3 & 4). We also explored whether associations between narcissism and social comparison varied across measurement approaches, using three measures of narcissism. Across studies, vulnerable narcissism consistently predicted greater social comparison orientation, self-enhancement motives, higher directional comparison tendencies, and more negative affect following upward comparisons. In contrast, associations involving grandiose narcissism were weaker, inconsistent, and dependent on measurement approach. These findings indicate that vulnerable narcissism is a more robust predictor of social comparison processes than grandiose narcissism and should be centrally incorporated into future research on narcissism and self-evaluation. Authors: Liao Y.; Song M.
Title: When imperfect food meets joint consumption: a social influence perspective
Abstract: Drawing on social influence theory, this research examines the interaction effect of food appearance (imperfect vs. perfect) and consumption context (solo vs. joint) on consumers' preferences. Across five experiments, we show that a joint (vs. solo) consumption context exacerbates the reduction in consumers' purchase intention toward imperfect food. In addition, perceived risk and purchase embarrassment mediate this interaction effect on both purchase intention and willingness to pay (WTP). We further identify self-construal and discount information as boundary conditions. Regarding self-construal, for consumers with an interdependent self-construal, joint consumption amplifies the effect of imperfect appearance on perceived risk, purchase embarrassment, and purchase intention. In contrast, for those with an independent self-construal, these amplifying effects are not significant. In terms of discount information, when it is displayed, joint consumption amplifies the effect of imperfect appearance on perceived risk, purchase embarrassment, and purchase intention. When it is absent, however, only the effect on purchase intention remains, albeit attenuated. Finally, the presence of discount information shifts the underlying mechanisms of the interaction toward greater reliance on indirect pathways. This research offers practical guidance for promoting suboptimal food in joint consumption contexts. © 2026

Title: How homophily and sociality propensity influence stakeholder diversity in wildfire risk management networks: an ERGM analysis
Abstract: Recent wildfire management strategies emphasize stakeholder engagement in risk management and prevention as a means of enhancing systemic safety and operational reliability. Despite its growing importance, guidance on how to effectively implement such engagement remains limited. This study addresses this gap by combining Social Network Analysis (SNA) and Exponential Random Graph Models (ERGMs) to examine a sample of 256 stakeholders across seven wildfire management networks in different European countries. The objective is to identify the propensity of stakeholders to form ties, network diversity and structural dependency within wildfire risk management networks. The results make two key contributions to risk and resilience in crisis and emergency management body of knowledge. First, we show that sociality – the propensity of stakeholders to establish connections – is shaped by stakeholder profiles. Second, we find that homophily – the propensity of stakeholders to connect with similar others – emerges across multiple categories alongside structural network effects. We discuss the dual role of these mechanisms that facilitate engagement while simultaneously constraining the diversity of stakeholder types. The findings invite policymakers promoting stakeholder engagement and stakeholder diversity as strategies in risk management and crisis response to critically reflect about the mechanisms through which such engagement can be effectively fostered. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Performance assessment and multi-objective optimization of a novel vehicular power system integrating a direct borohydride fuel cell with an organic Rankine cycle
Abstract: In this study, a novel vehicular direct borohydride fuel cell (DBFC) power system integrated with an organic Rankine cycle (ORC) is proposed. The ORC subsystem recovers the waste heat generated by the onboard DBFC stack to produce additional electrical power. Given the limited engineering maturity of vehicular DBFC systems and low-temperature ORCs, the proposed system is investigated through steady-state theoretical and numerical analyses. The principal contribution of this work is the development of a DBFC-ORC system-level framework for vehicle-oriented power assessment, incorporating comprehensive 4E evaluation and multi-objective trade-off analysis in terms of energy, exergy, economic, and environmental performance.Numerical results show that the integration of the ORC subsystem effectively enhances system performance. At operating temperatures of 70, 75, and 80 °C, the maximum net output power of the integrated system is increased by 9.0%, 8.5%, and 8.0%, respectively, compared with that of the standalone DBFC stack. Moreover, the parametric analysis reveals that the 4E performance indicators cannot be simultaneously optimized through parameter adjustment alone. Therefore, multi-objective optimization is performed to obtain the Pareto-optimal solution set and the corresponding optimal operating parameters. Compared with the baseline case(current density of 10500 A/m2, an operating temperature of 353.15 K, a NaBH4concentration of 1 mol/L, an inlet pressure of 2 atm, anode stoichiometric ratios of 1.2 and cathode stoichiometric ratios of 1.2), the selected Pareto-optimal solution yields an 18.22% increase in net output power, a 14.52% reduction in the levelized cost of energy, and a 97.27% increase in exergy efficiency. These results are instructive for the design and implementation of DBFC as a power source for automotive applications. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yan Y.; Wu X.
Title: Can bigger cities be safer? Evidence from criminal indictment data in China
Abstract: This paper examines how city size affects the criminal indictment rate, drawing on panel data from Chinese cities spanning 2014-2021. The results show that bigger cities are associated with significantly lower criminal indictment rates. This finding remains robust after accounting for endogeneity concerns and conducting a series of robustness checks. Further analyses provide suggestive evidence that larger cities may reduce criminal indictments through higher opportunity costs, stronger punishment-related deterrence, and greater moral and social costs of crime. However, this crime-reducing effect is weakened by the presence of migrants, and supplementary evidence suggests that lower levels of migrant social integration in larger urban settings may help explain this moderating pattern. These findings highlight the importance of not only supporting urban development, but also ensuring stronger institutional capacity, effective public security governance, and more inclusive public-service provision. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Xu H.; Nguyen U.; Yang T.
Title: Bubble-cell native fluorescence imaging for high-sensitivity label-free protein quantification
Abstract: Quantification of low-abundance proteins is critical for biopharmaceutical development, proteomics, and biochemical research; however, existing methods often require trade-offs among sensitivity, sample consumption, and workflow simplicity. Ultraviolet (UV) absorbance at 280 nm remains the most widely used method for routine protein quantification because it is rapid, label-free, and reproducible, but its intrinsic sensitivity limits the analysis of dilute samples, particularly when only microliter sample volumes are available. Here we present a high-sensitivity, label-free method for protein quantification based on native fluorescence imaging (NFI) using a bubble-cell capillary, in which a short, enlarged section is incorporated into an otherwise uniform capillary to enhance fluorescence detection. The enlarged bubble-cell increases the optical interrogation volume, generating a localized fluorescence peak that enables robust peak-based quantification, signal-to-noise analysis, and direct visualization of proteins near the detection limit. Using only 1–2 μL of sample, the method achieved experimentally validated limits of detection of approximately 0.005 mg/mL for bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 0.0025 mg/mL for monoclonal antibodies, representing detection limits approximately one order of magnitude lower than literature-reported values for NanoDrop UV spectrophotometry, while preserving the simplicity of a rapid, label-free, and reagent-free workflow. Method validation demonstrated good reproducibility, satisfactory spike-and-recovery performance, negligible carryover, and reliable quantification over the validated working range. The method was further applied to monitor low-abundance fractions collected during monoclonal antibody charge-variant fractionation, enabling detection of minor protein populations that were not reliably detected using a conventional fluorescence plate reader. The combination of high sensitivity, validated analytical performance, minimal sample consumption, and simple peak-based detection demonstrates the potential of bubble-cell NFI as a practical platform for routine protein quantification and characterization, particularly when sample availability is limited or low-abundance protein species must be analyzed. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Arora L.; Jain S.
Title: Seeing through the mind: Explainable multimodal AI for depression detection—A review
Abstract: Depression detection using multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving, transitioning from traditional machine learning techniques to deep learning architectures built on pre-trained transformer encoders. These systems integrate textual, acoustic, visual, and physiological signal streams through early, intermediate, late, and hybrid fusion strategies to improve predictive performance. However, a significant gap persists in model interpretability: post-hoc attribution frameworks (such as SHAP and LIME) dominate recent work, accounting for over 70% of studies published in 2024–2025, while clinician-centered validation is reported in only about 18% of the full reviewed corpus. Consequently, existing explanations are rarely validated for explainability quality dimensions; for example, SHAP attributions are known to degrade under inter-modality collinearity, and reported systems frequently lack alignment with established diagnostic criteria (e.g., DSM-based or PHQ-9 symptom structures). To close the gap between predictive accuracy and clinical utility, this review jointly synthesizes multimodal datasets, feature extraction strategies, machine learning and deep learning taxonomies, fusion strategies, and explainability techniques across 72 included studies. Finally, we outline critical future directions, emphasizing standardized XAI benchmarks, clinician-in-the-loop validation studies, and knowledge-driven neuro-symbolic reasoning. © 2026

Title: Extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods promotes animal-friendly food choices
Abstract: Plant-based foods are essentially animal-friendly, yet they are rarely labelled as such. We examined whether extending animal welfare labels from only being displayed on animal-based foods, towards also being placed on plant-based products, would better integrate plant-based products into the set of options consumers consider animal-friendly. Across two studies in a simulated online supermarket, we hypothesised that extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods would promote animal-friendly choices via increased perceptions of physical opportunity to choose animal-friendly (i.e. availability of animal-friendly foods) and social opportunity to choose animal-friendly (i.e. social norms for choosing animal-friendly foods). We show that extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods not only promoted animal-friendly choices within the animal-based category, but also significantly increased the number of plant-based foods chosen by 28% compared to the control condition, and 33% compared to the condition in which only animal-based products were labelled. Furthermore, we show that the positive effects of extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods persisted even when consumers were exposed to multiple sustainability messages presented through a multidimensional label, which displayed animal welfare, biodiversity, and climate scores. The studies confirmed that label effects on animal-friendly choices were driven by increases in perceived physical and social opportunity to choose animal-friendly. Extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods is an effective strategy for encouraging animal-friendly food choices. Labels, it turns out, do more than inform: They reshape the physical and social context into a more supportive environment for plant-based choices. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Multi-objective design and optimization of modular methanol production systems integrated with renewable hydrogen and direct air capture
Abstract: A unified multi-objective optimization framework integrating renewable energy generation, electrolyzers, hydrogen-driven electrochemical CO2 capture systems (HECCS), methanol synthesis, and multiple storage technologies is developed to enable joint optimization of capacity configuration, operational scheduling, and flexibility allocation amid coupled electricity-hydrogen-carbon-methanol flows. The evolving roles of HECCS under supply-driven and demand-driven operating modes are evaluated. Under the supply-driven scenario, CO2 storage enables carbon-side buffering and partial temporal decoupling between carbon capture and methanol synthesis. At the minimum-total-annualized-cost Pareto solution, S2 with CO2 storage reduces the total storage requirement by approximately 41.3% relative to S1 without CO2 storage, while maintaining a nearly unchanged total annualized cost. This indicates that CO2 storage primarily restructures the inter-temporal regulation pathway rather than directly reducing system cost. Under the demand-driven scenario, HECCS achieves the lowest total annualized cost relative to conventional thermally regenerated direct air capture (DAC) technologies, demonstrating advantages in energy consumption and system integration. Further analysis shows that the fast response capability of HECCS does not necessarily lead to frequent dynamic operation. Under the economically optimal conditions, the system preferentially employs lower-cost storage to absorb renewable fluctuations and maintain stable operation of capital-intensive process units, whereas HECCS flexibility is activated mainly under storage-constrained conditions. The system-level process flexibility is thus governed by system constraints, economic trade-offs, and coordination among multiple flexibility resources rather than by intrinsic dynamic capability alone. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Suo B.; Jiang H.; Yuan S.; Zhang J.; Li B.; Lu K.; Song J.; Zhang C.
Title: Sequentially coupled numerical modeling of liquid-propellant-induced in-situ pyrolysis of oil shale
Abstract: The low thermal conductivity of oil shale restricts heat propagation during in-situ pyrolysis, while reservoir stimulation and heating are commonly treated as separate processes, making it difficult to capture the dynamic alteration of heat-transfer pathways after fracture creation. To address this issue, a sequentially coupled numerical framework integrating liquid-propellant deflagration pressure release, main-fracture propagation, discrete fracture-network construction and mapping, reservoir heat transfer, and kerogen pyrolysis was developed. Deflagration pressure was described using the JWL equation of state, main-fracture growth was driven by net pressure, and the resulting main and statistically generated branch fractures were mapped into a three-dimensional reservoir domain. Subsequent thermal and pyrolysis responses were calculated using Robin-type gas–rock wall heat transfer, bedding-anisotropic heat conduction, and distributed activation energy model (DAEM) kinetics, together with sensitivity analysis of the key thermal-boundary parameters and numerical verification of the heat-transfer implementation. For a single 3 kg charge, the peak gas and net pressures reached 83.78 and 77.73 MPa, respectively, and the main-fracture half-length stabilized at 1.49 m within approximately 0.3 s. The fracture network promoted preferential heat transfer from the hot gas into the reservoir, yielding 138.88 kg of cumulative primary shale-oil generation after 1800 s. Three-stage sequential deflagration substantially increased the axial thermal influence. Increasing the stage spacing from 2 to 8 m expanded the axial extent of the T ≥ 310 °C region from 12.12 to 24.12 m, whereas cumulative primary shale-oil generation decreased from 467.33 to 389.33 kg, demonstrating a trade-off between spatial coverage and inter-stage thermal overlap. These results reveal the sequential mechanism of short-duration fracturing, fracture-enhanced heat transfer, and early-stage pyrolysis, and indicate that liquid-propellant deflagration is better suited as a pre-fracturing and thermal-startup technique coupled with subsequent sustained heating rather than as an independent long-term heat source. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The persuasive power of video in hospitality: How guest-generated video reviews influence customer engagement
Abstract: Guest-generated video reviews are increasingly prevalent on online travel platforms, yet their effects and mechanisms remain underexplored. Drawing on media richness theory, this study is among the first to examine whether and how such reviews enhance customer engagement, measured by subsequent review volume. We adopt a multimethod approach that combines econometric analysis with a controlled experiment to establish causal inference and uncover underlying mechanisms. Using a 24-month panel of 4471 hotels on Ctrip.com, difference-in-differences results show that guest-generated video reviews significantly increase customer engagement, with stronger effects for higher-tier or large hotels. Experimental evidence further demonstrates that these effects operate through increased information diagnosticity and social presence. Additional video content analysis reveals that human presence, higher informational richness, better visual quality, and longer duration further amplify the positive effects. Authors: Qiu W.; Yu X.; Fu X.; Cheng M.; Zhang Y.; Yao T.
Title: How to move you? The persuasive effects of influencer narrative styles in recommending tourism activities
Abstract: Influencers exert significant promotional effects in tourism marketing; however, few empirical studies have examined how different types of tourism activities can strategically leverage these effects through influencer narrative style. To address this gap, this study draws on Heuristic-Analytic Theory to investigate how personal and professional narrative styles align with relaxing and challenging tourism activities to maximize influencers’ persuasiveness. The study analyzes secondary data from 1187 social media posts and conducts three scenario-based experiments with 1438 participants. Results show that personal narrative style is more persuasive for relaxing activities, whereas professional narrative style works better for challenging activities. Moreover, experience resonance and knowledge acquisition are identified as key underlying mechanisms. Notably, the study introduces temporal distance in travel decision as a moderator, highlighting the importance of dynamic temporal cues in influencer recommendations. The findings provide valuable theoretical contributions and practical implications for optimizing influencer marketing strategies in the tourism context. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ucus S.
Title: Prolonged participation AI-based mindfulness school programme in primary education: Implications for AI practices, schools and developers
Abstract: Background: Research on Artificial Intelligence (AI) -supported mindfulness programs in primary education remains limited, particularly in rural contexts where implementation conditions differ from urban settings. Aim: This study examines the effects of an AI-supported mindfulness intervention on rural primary school students' behavioral and socio-emotional outcomes, and on teachers' self-regulation and creativity, measured at pretest (T1), posttest (T2), and follow-up (T3). Method: The study used a quasi-experimental design with a control group across selected classrooms in four rural schools. The sample comprised an intervention group (N = 91) and a control group (N = 54), with 16 teachers participating in the intervention group. The intervention ran for ten weekly sessions across the fall and spring semesters. AI tools (ChatGPT and Gemini) supported teacher candidates in lesson planning and in the inquiry phase that followed each mindfulness practice. Implementation fidelity, assessed through mentor cross-rating, was 88.6% (SD = 9.7), with Cohen's κ = .86 in a sub-sample. Results: Split-plot ANOVAs showed significant Time × Group interactions favouring the intervention group on life skills (LSAS, η2p = .242), behavioural difficulties (SDQ total, η2p = .378), and teacher-student relationship quality (STRS total, η2p = .025). In the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), all five subscales were significant. The Closeness subscale drove the STRS effect; Conflict did not change. Nested analyses confirmed consistent effects across grade levels. Teachers showed gains on all nine TSRS subscales, and on the Social Value subscale of the TCS. Conclusion: The intervention was associated with improvements in students' life skills, behavioral functioning, and teacher-student closeness, as well as gains in teachers' self-regulation. The findings inform AI-supported mindfulness practice in rural primary education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Physics-informed neural network for predicting high-temperature flow stress of 3Cr-1Si-1Ni ultra-high-strength steel
Abstract: In this work, a first application of physics-informed neural network (PINN) to predict the high-temperature flow stress of an ultra-high strength steel is proposed, in which the accuracy, robustness and data efficiency are enhanced. Physical embedding and physical constraints are incorporated into the PINN as guiding physical principles, enabling superior generalisation ability and accuracy compared with the conventional artificial neural network (ANN) and the Johnson–Cook (J–C) model. The PINN also demonstrates significantly improved data efficiency when only small amounts of training data are available, requiring only three datasets for training. In terms of robustness, the PINN is shown to tolerate higher levels of random noise than the ANN. When the standard deviation of added random noise increases from 0 % to 10 %, the absolute prediction error of the PINN rises by only 5.5 MPa, compared with a 30.0 MPa increase for the ANN. These results demonstrate that PINNs provide a powerful framework for the development of constitutive models for metals with improved accuracy, data efficiency, and robustness. Furthermore, the proposed PINN can be extended by incorporating additional deformation-related physical constraints, offering a promising direction for constitutive modelling of metals. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Xiong C.; Lin W.; Huang H.; Mu Q.; Li K.
Title: Unified task profiling and performance interference-aware Makespan and energy scheduling for cloud robotics tasks driven by an improved genetic algorithm
Abstract: Cloud robotics systems offload heterogeneous, computation- and data-intensive tasks to shared cloud nodes, yet suffer from severe performance interference caused by co-located contention for shared physical resources. Such interference renders idealized execution times unreliable and degrades both Makespan and energy efficiency in conventional schedulers. To enable interference-aware scheduling, it is first necessary to quantitatively characterize the resource demands of diverse tasks and to measure how co-location affects their execution. Therefore, this paper proposes a unified task profiling approach that characterizes CPU, I/O, and memory demands and other key differentiating attributes of eight representative cloud robotics tasks spanning perception, planning, control, and execution. Lightweight, tunable benchmarks are then designed to emulate these resource-access patterns, enabling controlled co-location experiments that construct a quantitative interference-sensitivity matrix. On this foundation, an interference-aware integer programming model is formulated to minimize the weighted sum of Makespan and energy consumption. The main novelty lies in connecting task profiling, benchmark-calibrated interference measurement, and joint Makespan-energy scheduling into a unified interference-aware optimization method. To solve the resulting NP-hard problem, we propose an Improved Genetic Algorithm for Cloud Robotics Task Scheduling (IGA-CTS), which jointly searches task allocation and execution order over the interference-aware scheduling model. In benchmark-calibrated simulation experiments against seven evaluated baselines, no baseline simultaneously achieves lower median Makespan and energy consumption than IGA-CTS at any scale; although some baselines perform better on an individual objective, these advantages are accompanied by inferior performance on the other. An objective-weight sensitivity analysis further shows that this overall trade-off is largely maintained under varying optimization preferences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Wang L.; Guan B.; Zhu T.; Zhuang Z.; Chen J.; Bai Y.; Gao J.; Huang Z.
Title: Green methanol production under carbon constraints: pathways, system integration, and deployment conditions
Abstract: Green methanol links low-carbon carbon sources with renewable electricity while retaining liquid-fuel handling advantages. We reviewed 155 publications covering genuinely green routes based on renewable hydrogen and sustainable carbon (CO2 hydrogenation with renewable H2 and biomass- or waste-derived methanol), transitional low-carbon retrofits of fossil-based plants, and less mature electrochemical, photocatalytic, or methane-conversion routes. Retrofits are treated as transitional, not genuinely green, because their carbon remains fossil-derived unless the feedstock is replaced. Authors adopt different system boundaries and functional units, and assumptions about electricity, CO2 supply, plant scale, and cost are rarely identical. Our comparison places each pathway in its operating conditions and avoids ranking isolated performance values. It considers technical maturity, energy demand, life-cycle emissions, levelized methanol cost, feedstock supply, infrastructure, and operating flexibility, and examines when power-hydrogen-carbon integration is justified. The review provides four outputs: a protocol for checking the comparability of techno-economic assessment and life-cycle assessment (TEA/LCA) evidence, conditional rules for evaluating integration, a qualitative regional pathway-selection matrix, and a dynamic-validation gap analysis linking demonstrated performance to availability, load-following, capacity factor, and degradation. No route is universally preferred; a defensible choice depends on consistent accounting and on regional electricity, carbon resources, industrial assets, and end use. The integration comparison distinguishes H2-to-CO2 power-to-methanol (PtM), H2-enhanced biomass/waste conversion, retrofit/carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) in fossil methanol hubs, and multi-source industrial symbiosis, and shows that no archetype is universally superior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang Y.; Liu X.; Deng Y.; Xiao H.; Zhang Y.
Title: Gendering conversational AI in human–AI interaction: The role of interaction context and sexist ideology in shaping user evaluations
Abstract: As human–AI interaction becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, users often infer social identities from AI systems, including gender. Moving beyond the conventional view of AI gender as a static, designer-assigned attribute, this study conceptualizes AI gender as a user-constructed perception shaped by contextual cues. Integrating social role theory, the stereotype content model, and ambivalent sexism theory, we conducted a 2 (AI gender cues: male vs. female) × 3 (interaction context: service-oriented, warm-authoritative, vs. serious-authoritative) between-subjects experiment with Chinese participants (N = 833) to examine how interaction context, perceived AI gender, and sexist ideology jointly shape evaluations of AI competence, warmth, and trustworthiness. The results showed that interaction context significantly influenced gender attribution, with the serious-authoritative condition eliciting stronger gender categorization and a masculinization bias regardless of assigned gender cues. The evaluative consequences of perceived AI gender were also context-dependent: perceived femininity consistently linked with warmth, but was associated with competence and trustworthiness primarily in the serious-authoritative condition. Hostile and benevolent sexism further moderated these relationships in distinct ways. Title: Adaptive loss-based random Fourier filtering with complementary adaptation: Algorithm design and performance analysis
Abstract: Random Fourier features (RFF) based adaptive filtering provides an efficient tool for nonlinear modeling by approximating kernel mappings with finite-dimensional feature representations. However, existing RFF-based filters typically rely on quadratic loss functions and fixed adaptation strategies, making them vulnerable to non-Gaussian disturbances and limiting their ability to balance convergence speed and steady-state accuracy. To address these issues, a new adaptive filtering framework in the RFF domain is proposed. The framework incorporates an adaptive loss function with an adjustable shape parameter to improve robustness under non-Gaussian and impulsive noise environments. In addition, two RFF-based filters with complementary adaptation characteristics are combined through a convex combination strategy, providing a favorable trade-off between convergence rate and steady-state performance. The steady-state performance analysis of the proposed filtering framework is presented, which characterizes its steady-state behavior under mild assumptions. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method under various noise conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Li Y.; Yang M.; Liu S.; Liu L.-B.; Ouyang B.; Bian L.; Sun Y.; Luo J.-L.; Liu S.
Title: Phase-resilient in situ exsolution via thermal pre-stabilization of a double perovskite for high-efficiency solid oxide CO2 electrolysis
Abstract: Metal in situ exsolution endows perovskites with highly active and strongly anchored catalytic sites for high-temperature CO2 electrolysis. However, the concomitant lattice oxygen loss and B-site cation reduction often trigger detrimental phase transitions that compromise long-term durability. Here we demonstrate a chemically non-invasive thermal pre-stabilization strategy that fundamentally resolves this activity-stability trade-off. By elevating the calcination temperature of the double perovskite (DP) Sr1.95Ce0.05Fe1.3Ni0.2Mo0.5O6−δ (SCFNM) from 1100 to 1250 °C, we induce lattice contraction and enhanced BO6 octahedral ordering, which increase B-site cation oxidation states and metal-oxygen bond strength. This robust structure effectively suppresses the DP phase of perovskite transitioning to Ruddlesden-Popper phase during in situ exsolution, while preserving uniformly exsolved NiFe nanoalloys and retaining a higher oxygen vacancy concentration and a stronger CO2 adsorption capacity. As a result, the phase-pre-stabilized NiFe@SCFNM-1250 achieved a current density of 1.72 A cm-2, a maximum CO Faraday efficiency of 98.63% at 1.5 V and 850 °C and a markedly reduced degradation rate of 2.06 mA cm–2 h–1 over 100 h, which outperforming its non-stabilized counterpart by nearly twofold in durability. This work establishes thermal pre-stabilization as a universally applicable paradigm for balancing catalytic activity with structural stability in perovskite-based electrodes, offering a chemical-doping-free route toward durable CO2 electrolysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Sensing the path forward: AI as amplifier in sensory and consumer science
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how sensory and consumer data are collected, analyzed, and used. A common fear is that algorithms will displace trained panels and that predictive models will replace expert judgment. We argue the opposite: as AI automates what is easy to formalize, the value of what only humans can do (embodied sensing, cultural interpretation, ethical judgment, and meaning-making) rises. This paper is not a systematic review. It advocates a particular perspective (AI as amplifier of sensory expertise), informed by on-the-ground experience through the recent rise of large language models, including what has worked and what has not in practice. Three industry case studies from PepsiCo, Danone, and Kenvue support that perspective. The principles (knowledge management, automation, predictive modeling, people-centered adoption; humans in the loop; culture before algorithms) are meant to apply beyond large companies, including academia and smaller groups. That perspective also guided a selective literature reading focused on Food Quality and Preference and related journals, mainly from 2022 to early 2026. We clarify what AI is and is not, trace the path from chemometrics to neuromorphic sensing, and describe a four-pillar framework from a Pangborn 2025 industry workshop. Self-reported case outcomes include up to 50% faster analysis and a 75% reduction in reporting time; calculation details were not disclosed to us and the figures are not independently validated. The three organizations built the same capabilities in different orders and met the same barriers (culture, talent, IT collaboration). We also propose narrative-driven analysis with large language models and a near-term research agenda. Central message: when machines predict, humans must decide. © 2026

Authors: Hutchinson J.
Title: The therapy room is not a classroom: Why emotional safety in therapy belongs to the client
Abstract: Emotional safety in the therapy room is a clinical resource that belongs to the client. A growing number of clinicians, particularly those trained in social justice frameworks, feel empowered or obligated to correct clients' use of language deemed offensive. This paper argues that such practices are ethically indefensible and clinically counterproductive. Drawing on meta-analytic evidence on the therapeutic alliance, countertransference management, and core conditions of change, the evidence indicates that corrective responses to client language damage the alliance quality, increase the risk of premature termination, and suppress the very kind of honest disclosure that therapy requires. This paper further examines structural ideological bias in the profession, the contradictions between activist training frameworks and foundational ethics codes, and the misapplication of harm-speech theory to the clinical context. The fiduciary obligation of the therapist, the clinical evidence base, and every major professional ethics code converge on the same conclusion: the counseling room is not a classroom, and the client's psychological safety is not the therapist's to withdraw. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhou Y.; Wang J.; Gao J.; Wang K.; Lu H.
Title: An integrated analytical framework for natural gas pricing: combining multi-source drivers, forecast enhancement, and model interpretability
Abstract: With the global pursuit of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), accurate forecasting and mechanistic interpretation of natural gas pricing have become increasingly important. As a transition fuel in the shift toward a low-carbon energy system, natural gas plays a vital role in balancing energy accessibility and environmental sustainability. However, rising economic uncertainty and geopolitical risks present significant challenges to effective price forecasting and policy formulation. In response, we develop a data-driven analytical framework for natural gas pricing that integrates feature engineering and forecast enhancement to achieve accurate point-interval forecasts and investment timing. Leveraging advanced explainability techniques, the framework systematically uncovers the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in global gas market drivers. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional models in predictive accuracy and reveals important lag effects and interaction mechanisms among influencing factors. These findings validate the framework's ability to support pricing decisions and risk hedging for energy enterprises, and to provide scientific evidence for regional energy policymaking through quantification of heterogeneity. Ultimately, it offers key support for improving resource allocation efficiency and advancing the achievement of SDG targets. © 2026

Title: An agenda for plastics crisis research in the synthetic age
Abstract: This survey synthesizes insights from environmental social sciences to recast the plastics crisis as a structural feature of growth-dependent economies instead of a problem solvable by consumer choice or incremental technologies. Rather than a within-field review of ecological economics, it maps adjacent literatures to specify what this field could study and how, clarifying researchable questions, suitable methods, and tractable indicators. The synthesis foregrounds connections between expansionary political-economic dynamics, globally uneven socio-ecological burdens across the plastics life cycle, and the power and knowledge relations that shape what is produced, measured, and governed. It calls for comparative, mixed-methods, multi-scalar work and for open, standardized data on plastics flows to strengthen causal inference and comparability. Shifting attention upstream—from end-of-pipe fixes to the transformation of provisioning systems—the paper charts lines of inquiry capable of aligning social metabolism with biophysical limits and human needs, providing a roadmap for ecological economics to organize and accelerate research beyond consumer or techno-managerial framings. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Troath S.
Title: Deep sea mining, think tanks, and the politics of expertise
Abstract: Deep sea mining (DSM) is being contemplated in an environment of heightened geopolitical tensions. A confluence of factors has led to securitised framings of DSM, including the centrality of the Pacific as both a potential mining location and a perceived frontline of strategic competition, and the desire of western states to “derisk” from China when it comes to critical minerals. One of the factors shaping how strategic competition is understood and responded to is the role of experts. Within western states such as the US and Australia, think tanks play an important role in shaping narratives, perceptions, and policies relating to defence and foreign affairs. In this paper I will investigate how western security-related think tanks are approaching DSM.I will argue that think tanks are playing a significant role in contributing to narratives of necessity regarding DSM, and that security and strategic competition are the dominant framing of these narratives of necessity. Authors: Martin C.; Ishihara H.
Title: Trade-offs and transitions: A scoping review of structural and discursive power in post-growth interventions
Abstract: The dialectic relationship between the production of post-growth knowledge and ongoing construction of social reality is a complex one, but one that warrants attention. In this scoping review, we respond to the emergent interest in post-growth politics and theories of change. We aim to complement existing reviews of post-growth policy proposals and recommendations with an analysis of peer-reviewed studies on interventions – deliberate attempts by one state, market or civil society actor to influence another. Drawing on a socio-ecological systems leverage points perspective embedded within a political economy inspired mapping of social forces, we develop a conceptual framework for explaining strategic trade-offs made by actors to achieve various forms of depth.Our findings point to asymmetrical relationships between actors-executor pairs and a pattern of neoliberal subjectification in both intervention design and analytical focus. We also find that whilst post-growth interventions can readily achieve discursive depth, it is often accompanied by institutional shallowness and temporal fragility. We conclude with reflections on strategic implications for post-growth researchers and movements. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Intersectional justice as a guiding principle for feminist ecological economics
Abstract: Ecological economics focuses on provisioning for a good life for all within planetary boundaries. Feminist ecological economists have long highlighted the relevance of unpaid care work, times beyond linear clock time, and social-ecological provisioning towards this same end. In this article, we explore why and how intersectional justice should be a guiding principle for (feminist) ecological economics. Intersectional justice involves recognizing and redressing the discrimination that individuals or groups face due to overlapping social identities, which give rise to structural injustices that undermine the provisioning for a good life for all within planetary boundaries. Through three examples (global care chains, hidden ableist assumptions about ‘work’, and inequitable water access in India) we show that while many areas of feminist ecological economics lend themselves to intersectional analysis, operationalizing intersectional justice as a guiding principle is far from easy in practice. Learning from Black feminisms, disability studies, and feminist standpoint theory, we show how intersectional feminist perspectives can help challenge power structures and institutions that sustain injustices on both epistemic and material levels. This enables the kinds of collaborative action that can bring (feminist) ecological economics into broader acceptance, uniting struggles against various forms of oppression while building economic systems that prioritize the sustainability of life. Title: Modality effects in human–technology interaction
Abstract: This paper reviews emerging research on how different interaction modalities influence information processing and behavior when using new technological devices. A conceptual framework of modality effects is proposed which argues that different input (vocal, haptic) and output modalities (audial, visual) can trigger both cognitive and affective processes that alter users' downstream behaviors. Title: Designing wave farms to support mangrove restoration: A coupled hydro-morphodynamic and habitat suitability modelling approach
Abstract: Wave farms are increasingly proposed for hybrid coastal infrastructure, offering both renewable energy generation and shoreline protection. However, their potential to enable ecological restoration, particularly for mangrove restoration, remains underexplored. This study presents a novel framework for evaluating how wave farms can precondition coastal zones for mangrove restoration by attenuating wave energy, reducing erosion, and expanding areas of hydrodynamic suitability. Using a schematized coupled depth averaged (2DH) hydrodynamic, spectral wave and morphodynamic model in Delft3D, six wave farm configurations were tested under idealized conditions to quantify wave attenuation, sediment retention, and habitat suitability. Mangrove survivability was assessed through a novel drag-based (Type II) erosion-adjusted uprooting threshold. K-means clustering was applied to field-collected morphological traits to define three distinct seedling groups, enabling species-specific resistance modelling based on frontal area and anchorage. The results show that array layout strongly influences ecological and engineering performance. Some configurations enhanced erosion reduction and created more contiguous planting zones while others expanded the total area suitable for restoration. The proposed framework identifies zones preconditioned for restoration, which can be made viable for planting through interventions such as mud nourishment or raised platforms. This study provides a transferable methodology to support hybrid infrastructure design for climate resilience, ecosystem recovery, and local socioeconomic benefit. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Rapid microwave-assisted synthesis of ZnMn dual-atom nanozymes for cancer catalytic immunotherapy
Abstract: Catalytic nanomedicines face a persistent trade-off between structurally defined active sites and rapid synthesis. A microwave-assisted salt-flux conversion is developed that transforms a bimetallic metal-organic framework precursor within 3 min into nitrogen-doped carbon-supported ZnMn dual-atom nanozymes (ZnMn DAzymes). Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and dual-edge X-ray absorption fine structure analyses support adjacent Zn-Mn sites with an N-dominated ZnMn-N6-like coordination motif. Steady-state kinetics and density functional theory calculations suggest cooperative catalysis: Zn modulates H2O2 adsorption and O-O bond activation, whereas Mn provides stronger H2O2 chemisorption and redox flexibility, jointly enhancing catalase-, peroxidase-, and oxidase-like activities. The resulting cascade decomposes H2O2, relieves hypoxia, generates reactive oxygen species, and depletes glutathione, inducing mitochondrial dysfunction, immunogenic cell death, cGAS-STING-associated signaling, dendritic-cell maturation, and effector T-cell infiltration. Glutathione-responsive Mn2+ release additionally enables activatable T1-weighted magnetic resonance contrast. Combined with αPD-L1, ZnMn DAzymes suppress primary and distal tumors by approximately 90%, reduce lung metastases by 92%, and prolong survival in 4T1 models. This work provides a rapid route to ZnMn dual-atom nanozymes for catalytic immunotherapy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Coupled design of a bamboo-shaped cathode flow field and hybrid-porosity gas diffusion layer for enhanced performance and multiphysics transport in open-cathode PEMFCs
Abstract: The bamboo-shaped cathode flow field can enhance heat-mass transfer and improve the performance of open-cathode proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, its further engineering application faces two prominent challenges: 1) the effects of the key design parameters on cell performance and multiphysics transport remain unclear; 2) geometry-induced local convection enhancement may aggravate the inherent spatial nonuniformity of the physical fields within the porous electrode assembly and increase the risk of local degradation. To address these challenges, this study first studies the impacts of two key design parameters, the number of bamboo-joint units ( N ) and bamboo-joint indentation depth ( W ), on PEMFC performance and the associated heat and mass transfer in porous electrodes. Furthermore, the flow field is coupled with a hybrid-porosity GDL to improve physical field uniformity while retaining enhanced transport. The results show that moderate increases in N and W strengthen the periodic contraction–expansion effect of reactants within the bamboo-shaped configuration, thereby enhancing shear disturbance and lateral mixing. This promotes faster renewal of the thermal and concentration boundary layers in the flow field and porous electrode, thereby increasing the net water and oxygen transport fluxes and improving heat dissipation. Adjusting N and W contributes to superior open-cathode PEMFC performance by up to 8.10 % and 18.85 %, respectively. Increasing N and W also increases the ideal cathode air-supply power due to the relatively larger pressure drop under otherwise identical operating conditions, indicating a greater relative air-supply penalty. Accordingly, the flow field design requires a trade-off among performance improvement, ideal air-supply penalty, and the uniformity of key physical fields within the MEA. Guided by these mechanistic insights, a coupled design is developed by integrating the bamboo-shaped flow field with a hybrid-porosity gas diffusion layer (GDL). This novel design retains the transport and performance advantages of the bamboo-shaped flow field while further alleviating the inherent limitation of the non-uniform distribution of key physical fields within the porous electrode. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
