Title: Age-related emergence of behavioral deficits and amyloid pathology in the J20 mouse model of Alzheimer's disease
Abstract: Transgenic mouse models carrying familial Alzheimer's disease mutations are widely used in preclinical research, yet phenotypic variability across age and sex can complicate experimental design and interpretation. Here, we performed an age-stratified behavioral and pathological phenotyping of the hAPP-J20 mouse model using independent cohorts of female and male mice at 3, 6, and 9 months of age (n = 5–21 per group depending on the assay). Animals underwent a battery of cognitive and non-cognitive assays assessing well-being–related behaviors (nesting, splash test), locomotion and exploration (open field), anxiety-like behavior (elevated O-maze), working memory (Y-maze spontaneous alternation), and spatial learning and memory (Barnes maze). In parallel, amyloid pathology was quantified using ELISA measurements of Aβ1–40 and Aβ1–42 levels and histological assessment of hippocampal plaque burden. J20 mice exhibited early behavioral alterations detectable at 3 months, including impaired working memory, increased locomotor activity, and alterations in self-care behaviors. Spatial learning alterations were detectable from 3 months, whereas robust spatial-memory deficits became more consistently evident at later ages. Soluble and insoluble Aβ species increased progressively with age, whereas hippocampal plaque pathology was minimal at 3 months and rose markedly at 6 and 9 months. Analyses including sex as an independent factor identified endpoint-specific sex-related effects but did not support a consistent sex-specific trajectory. Overall, non-cognitive and working memory deficits emerge early, while spatial memory impairment and amyloid pathology dominate at later stages. This study provides a reference framework to guide age- and sex-appropriate experimental design in preclinical studies using the J20 model. © 2026

Title: Collective reinforcement learning and human–machine cooperation in multi-state stochastic games
Abstract: With the growing deployment of artificial intelligence agents in collaborative systems, understanding how they jointly shape cooperative behavior with humans under dynamic environmental conditions becomes essential. Stochastic games provide a natural framework for capturing how environmental feedback shapes behavioral choices and supports the emergence of cooperation. Building on this framework, we incorporate collective reinforcement learning dynamics (CRLD) into a multi-state stochastic game and develop a mixed human–machine population model to examine the emergence and stability of cooperation. Unlike existing models that mainly consider homogeneous learning populations or externally determined environmental states, this framework explicitly captures the feedback interaction among human behavioral responses, environmental state transitions, and machine learning dynamics. Our results show that environmental vulnerability, public-goods incentives, human cooperative inclination and its population share, as well as machine discounting, jointly determine the evolutionary path of cooperation. Cooperative humans increase the likelihood of favorable environmental states, lowering the threshold for machines to learn cooperative strategies. In contrast, defect-prone humans can disrupt numerically stable cooperative states and induce cooperation collapse. Increasing the proportion of cooperative humans also reduces the critical discount factor required for machines to sustain cooperation. These findings demonstrate that human behavior reshapes environmental state transitions and alters machine value evaluation, exerting essential influence on learning and strategy evolution. Overall, this study reveals the mechanisms that sustain cooperation in human–machine systems with variable environmental states and provides theoretical insights relevant to coordination in mixed-agent systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Rural occupational health in Colombia: policy–practice gaps among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca
Abstract: This study examines policy–practice gaps in occupational safety and health (OSH) protection among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca, Colombia. A multi-method design combined 14 semi-structured interviews and two focus groups with an adapted ILO Vision Zero Fund survey administered to 200 agricultural workers. Survey data were analyzed descriptively and through exploratory Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA), and qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated during interpretation. Findings showed multidimensional patterns involving occupational protection, working conditions, health-service availability, agricultural practices, and productive autonomy. These patterns coexisted with informal, seasonal, short-term, day-labor, and subsistence work, limited occupational risk coverage, discontinuous prevention and training, and fragmented institutional coordination. Qualitative findings further highlighted women’s combined productive and care roles, local and traditional knowledge, community participation, and heterogeneity across territorial settings and agricultural practices as relevant to prevention and decision-making. Conventional social protection and occupational risk arrangements centered on formal, contributory employment may not fully respond to dispersed and unstable rural work. Strengthening rural OSH requires integrated, territorially adapted, gender-sensitive strategies linking prevention, social protection, sustained training, institutional coordination, community participation, and productive autonomy. The findings support assessing differentiated and progressive protection pathways, including the feasibility of subsidized occupational risk coverage for more vulnerable workers and small productive units, combined with contributory mechanisms where work arrangements are more stable. By linking worker-level realities with institutional and policy-implementation gaps, this study provides evidence to inform more equitable rural OSH policies responsive to diverse territorial realities in Colombia. Title: Broken bodies in Domestic Spaces: Direct and Structural Violence in an Atypical Mortuary Dataset from Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: A major challenge for the understanding of violence in the past is that our main source of evidence comes from cemeteries, but a significant proportion of the victims of violence are not buried in cemeteries. Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia (c. 500 BCE–1050 CE) is infamous for its emerging warrior ideology and hegemony of violence. Yet, somewhat counter-intuitively, trauma rates have typically been found to be relatively low in cemetery populations. Not everyone was afforded formal burial in cemeteries, however. The BODY-POLITICS project examines a previously neglected mortuary dataset: disarticulated and semi-complete human remains deposited in and around domestic spaces such as longhouses, pits, wells, postholes, and hearths. We report on 12 individuals inscribed with 19 ante- and perimortem traumatic injuries, analysed through osteological, bimolecular and digital imaging methods. The unusual post-mortem history of these individuals, set within a historical context of raiding, enslavement, and ritual violence including potential ‘human sacrifice’, allows us to explore multiple scenarios for inflicted injuries: war-like events (extra-community violence), interpersonal and domestic violence (intra-community violence), and ritual violence. Finally, by integrating trauma patterns, mortuary treatment, and contextual information, we discuss the broader life histories of these individuals and argue that some may have been vulnerable to structural, ‘slow’ violence that compounded over the lifecourse. This study thus contributes to broader discourse on direct and structural violence towards potentially marginalised people, as well as connections between ritualised violence and divergent mortuary pathways. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Gümüştaş C.
Title: Masculine honor, social visibility, and safety non-compliance: intentions and approval judgments in high-risk sectors in Turkey
Abstract: Unsafe work in high-risk sectors cannot be explained only by knowledge deficits or weak safety management; workers may also attach reputational meaning to visible compliance. Drawing on honor theory and occupational-safety research on risk perception and social context, this study examined whether masculine honor values (hereafter honor values)—the belief that a man’s worth depends partly on a publicly defensible reputation—were associated with unsafe work intentions, lower perceived risk, and greater approval of safety-rule non-compliance among male workers in Turkish construction and shipbuilding. A worker survey (N = 244) was combined with a within-person vignette experiment in which the focal hazard was held constant while visibility was manipulated and audience identity and prior social comment varied orthogonally. Honor values were positively associated with unsafe work intentions (H1a) and approval of others’ violations (H1b), and negatively associated with perceived risk (H2). Perceived risk partially accounted for the honor–intention association (H3). The association between honor values and approval of non-compliance was stronger when the violation was public rather than private (H4), consistent with a reputational, visibility-contingent account. These findings identify a micro-level sociocultural pathway that complements knowledge- and risk-based accounts of safety decisions. They also suggest that safety communication and supervisory practice should address the social meaning of compliance, while the cross-sectional mediation and judgment-based vignette outcome limit causal and behavioral inference. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Viestad V.M.; Wintjes J.
Title: Teaching Through Making: |xam and !xun Material Culture of the Bleek and Lloyd Collection
Abstract: At Wits Art Museum (University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa) is a small collection donated to the former Wits Museum of Ethnology by Percival Kirby in 1952. A note in the accession register ties the items into the context of the renowned ‘Bushman researches’ of Wilhelm Bleek and Lucy Lloyd in Cape Town in the 1870s and 1880s, an unusual cross-cultural collaboration with a small group of |xam- and !xun-speaking people against the backdrop of the extreme oppression of San peoples across the southern African region. These objects represent a rare instance of historical material culture of San (‘Bushman’) origin in museum collections being associated with named persons or specific communities of origin. We examine them according to object type—spoon, head ornament, firestick, plaything, arrow and bullroarer—to assess their provenance and approach them ‘biographically’, exploring their community origins and coming into being as specific things, and their being gifted to Kirby by Wilhelm's daughter, Dorothea Bleek. Our ‘relocation’, documentation and contextualization of the Bleek-Kirby collection enables some of the material linkages to be restored, complementing the better-known narratives, making the case for the objects as active participants in the conversations, and enriching understanding of the Bleek and Lloyd Collection as a whole. We examine the significant cultural know-how embedded in these objects and emphasize the creative agency of the |xam and !xun people—|hanǂkass'o, !nanni, Tamme among others—as primary authors and producers of knowledge within the broader intellectual project. The bullroarers in particular reveal some of the affordances of this detailed work, assisted by the ongoing digitization and digital curation of the archive. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Crossing margins: Intersectional users’ ethical concerns about software
Abstract: Many modern software applications present numerous ethical concerns due to conflicts between users’ values and companies’ priorities. Intersectional communities, those with multiple marginalized identities, are disproportionately affected by these ethical issues, leading to legal, financial, and reputational consequences for software companies, as well as real-world harm for intersectional users. Historically, the voices of intersectional communities have been systematically marginalized and excluded from contributing their unique perspectives to software design, perpetuating software-related ethical concerns. This work aims to fill the gap in research on intersectional users’ software-related perspectives and provide software practitioners with a methodology for analyzing intersectional voices in software ethics discourse. We collected 36,777 posts from over 700 intersectional subreddits discussing software applications and utilized large language models to identify ethical concerns in these posts. We then applied regression models with counterfactual analysis to examine how intersectional identity dimensions shape the amplification or suppression of ethical concern expression across software genres, and conducted a time-series analysis to examine how concern expression varies over time in relation to real-world events. As a case study in the social media domain, we further demonstrate how identified ethical concerns can be prioritized to surface issues warranting timely developer attention, validated against survey-derived ground truth. Together, these analyses form the basis of a nascent feedback-driven framework for assessing whether software systems are meeting the needs of intersectional users. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Differential frontostriatal ΔFosB dynamics and behavioral flexibility in autism like VPA-exposed mice
Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves social impairments, repetitive behaviors, and behavioral inflexibility, defined as an inability to adapt behavior to changing contingencies, and is linked to frontostriatal dysfunction. How behavioral training modulates these circuits is unclear, but ΔFosB, a marker of sustained neural activity, may be useful to establish their relationship. The aim was to evaluate frontostriatal ΔFosB expression following prenatal exposure to valproic acid (VPA) and to determine how experience in the midsession reversal (MSR) task modulates posterior ΔFosB expression. CD-1 mice were prenatally exposed to VPA (500 mg/kg) or vehicle. Brains from postnatal day (PND) 30 mice were analyzed to quantify baseline ΔFosB + cells in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), dorsal striatum (DS), and ventral striatum (VS). In the second experiment, mice performed the MSR task for 13 days. Then, ΔFosB was re-evaluated at PND43 to assess experience-dependent changes. At PND30, VPA-exposed mice showed a significant increase in ΔFosB + cells in mPFC, OFC, DS, and VS, suggesting sustained activity-dependent engagement of the frontostriatal circuit. In the MSR task, mice adapted to contingency shifts using mixed strategies, including win-stay/lose-shift behavior and temporal estimation, whereas VPA mice showed less consistent strategy selection after reversal. After MSR, ΔFosB expression in the OFC and striatum of VPA mice normalized to control levels and remained persistently elevated in the mPFC at PND43. Thus, prenatal VPA induces long-term increases in neuronal transcriptional changes, suggesting activity-dependent plasticity in the frontostriatal circuit. Despite these neural alterations, behavioral flexibility was preserved, suggesting circuit-level adaptations underlying ASD-related strategies. Future studies could broaden these results by examining sex differences and characterizing the cellular and molecular changes dependent on frontostriatal ΔFosB dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Negotiation across the social sciences: An interdisciplinary review
Abstract: Psychological investigations have generated numerous insights into how two parties bargain. To build on this literature, we review recent research across multiple disciplines, focusing on aspects of negotiation that have received relatively little attention, namely individual differences, multiparty negotiations, and contextual factors. Insights into individual differences are observed in the developmental psychology, artificial intelligence, and social psychology literature. Investigations in these domains show that young children can think strategically about exchange, that individual differences shape the information negotiators obtain and how they utilize information, and that situational factors can constrain or facilitate the expression of individual differences. Insights into multiparty negotiations emerge from the social networks and political science literature. Investigations in these domains explore novel multiparty dynamics, highlighting the importance of structural position in bargaining, and demonstrating that relationship history can shape coalition formation. Insights into contextual factors emerge from the economic and public health literature. Investigations in these domains challenge assumptions about core negotiation concepts such as power and alternatives. Overall, an interdisciplinary perspective on negotiation complements and enriches psychological understanding, and provides implications for interventions, future theoretical development, and empirical research. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Folklore in learning and its implications for cultural literacy: A bibliometric study and systematic literature review
Abstract: The forces of globalization and digital transformation have intensified attention toward the need to strengthen cultural identity through education, including the use of folklore as a meaningful learning resource. However, existing studies on folklore in learning remain fragmented. While much of the literature focuses on either cultural preservation or specific educational applications, the gap lies in a systematic exploration of folklore's pedagogical role across different contexts and educational levels. This study addresses this gap by examining the development of research on folklore in learning and its implications for cultural literacy through a bibliometric approach combined with a systematic literature review. For the bibliometric analysis, metadata records of articles published between 2015 and 2025 were processed from the Google Scholar database. Data for the systematic literature review were collected from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, and the article selection process followed PRISMA procedures. A total of 41 articles met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final review. Bibliometric mapping was conducted using VOSviewer, while article identification and screening were supported by Publish or Perish. The bibliometric findings indicate a significant increase in publications over the past decade, accompanied by a thematic shift from cultural heritage preservation toward the integration of cultural values within educational contexts. The SLR findings show that the research is predominantly qualitative in nature, with folktales and legends as the most frequently used forms of folklore, and books and e-modules as the main learning media employed to strengthen cultural literacy. The findings suggest that folklore-based learning fosters students’ cultural awareness, internalizes values, strengthens identity formation, and deepens the understanding of local culture. This study contributes by providing a more integrated understanding of folklore as a pedagogical tool for cultural literacy, emphasizing its role in curriculum design. Future research should focus on expanding methodological diversity and exploring broader applications of folklore-based learning across various educational contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Han Z.; Zhao F.; Xu H.; Zhang Z.; Wu J.; Zhang Y.; Pan J.; Li M.; Hao Z.; Guan W.; Jiang P.; Luo Y.; Ma X.; Kuang H.; Liu Y.
Title: Machine learning algorithms empower traditional Chinese medicine: Breakthrough approaches from chemical component analysis to pharmacological mechanism research
Source title: Spectrochimica Acta - Part A: Molecular and Biomolecular Spectroscopy
Abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine studies are constrained by complex chemical components and multi-target biological interactions, making conventional analytical methods inefficient for mechanism exploration. As a data-driven technique, machine learning has been widely adopted to tackle diverse complex challenges in TCM research. Nevertheless, most existing reviews merely summarize individual algorithms or scattered application cases, lacking systematic task-based classification and unified operational standards. Based on literature published from 2022 to 2026, this review systematically classifies machine learning applications in TCM into four core research tasks. A task-oriented framework is constructed to match different algorithms with appropriate TCM research scenarios. This paper further establishes a complete standardized workflow covering algorithm selection, model construction and model evaluation to standardize ML applications in TCM research. This review also summarizes the applications of machine learning in TCM quality control, bioactive compound identification, processing analysis, and mechanism elucidation. Furthermore, major bottlenecks in current ML-based TCM studies are analyzed, and feasible optimization strategies are proposed. This review aims to provide clear and practical guidelines for the standardized application of machine learning in future TCM research. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: SR-MCUR: A scalable and robust CUR decomposition method for large-scale matrix approximation
Abstract: Matrix decompositions are powerful tools for analyzing and processing large-scale data in computer vision and pattern recognition applications. In particular, CUR decompositions offer several advantages over other factorizations, such as interpretability and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a robust and scalable CUR matrix decomposition, called SR-MCUR, based on deterministic sampling of rows and columns. It addresses the main limitations of a recently developed deterministic CUR method based on the discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM), as it does not require seeing the whole data matrix and only requires computing the singular vectors of a few observed data samples. Two versions of SR-MCUR, SR-MCUR(1) and SR-MCUR(2), are proposed based on selecting the rows and columns simultaneously and sequentially, respectively. We demonstrate that SR-MCUR(2) provides a more stable performance than the existing deterministic CUR methods and is less subject to ill-conditioning. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed methods. SR-MCUR methods dramatically outperform the existing deterministic CUR methods in terms of computational efficiency, enabling the handling of large-scale datasets on a single machine with limited computing and storage resources. Moreover, it provides a near-optimal approximation accuracy compared to deterministic CUR methods. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Wang X.; Zhong J.; Lin L.; Luo T.-J.; Li X.; Pei Y.; Lin Y.
Title: CROWN: Contract-theoretic resource optimization for welfare maximization in heterogeneous edge networks
Abstract: Efficient edge-assisted video streaming requires the synergistic orchestration of caching, computing, and transmission resources. However, this potential is practically impeded by the complex coupling of these heterogeneous resources and the information asymmetry regarding nodes’ private marginal operating-cost types. To address these challenges, we propose CROWN, a contract-theoretic incentive mechanism designed to support welfare-oriented resource coordination between the Content Provider and Content Delivery Network nodes A core modeling contribution of CROWN is a window-level multi-resource accounting formulation that translates the disparate constraints of storage, bandwidth, and computing into a tractable optimization framework while retaining their respective physical meanings. Building on this model and established discrete-screening results, we analytically derive a monotone contract menu that guarantees Individual Rationality and Incentive Compatibility under the stated static-screening and observability assumptions, thereby achieving a second-best welfare-maximizing solution under adverse selection. To ensure scalability in dense networks, we further develop a polynomial-time Primal–Dual Ironing procedure, implemented through scalar bisection and generalized PAVA ironing, to efficiently enforce allocation monotonicity. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of CROWN in balancing economic efficiency and service quality. Compared with the Stackelberg baseline at the representative network scale, CROWN yields a 9.31% improvement in total social welfare and sustains a 92.1% hit rate for long-tail content, demonstrating its effectiveness within the evaluated settings. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: How social media content shapes enrollment intention: Distinguishing firm-generated and user-generated effects through TPB and self-identity
Abstract: The increasing reliance on social media has transformed how prospective students gather and evaluate information when selecting universities. This study examines how firm-generated content (FGC) and user-generated content (UGC) influence students' behavioral intention to enroll in private universities through psychological mechanisms grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and self-identity. Specifically, the study investigates both direct and indirect effects of FGC and UGC on behavioral intention, mediated by attitude toward behavior, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and self-identity. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed, with data collected from 295 final-year high school students in Banten, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that FGC has a significant direct and indirect effect on behavioral intention, whereas UGC does not have a significant direct effect but appears to operate primarily through indirect pathways. Among the mediators, subjective norms emerge as the strongest predictor of behavioral intention, followed by attitude toward behavior and self-identity. In contrast, perceived behavioral control does not significantly influence behavioral intention. The findings suggest that FGC and UGC function through distinct mechanisms. While institutional content can directly shape behavioral intention, user-generated content primarily influences intention through social and psychological processes. These results highlight that the effectiveness of social media communication depends not only on information exposure but also on how information is cognitively evaluated, socially validated, and integrated into individuals' self-concept. This study contributes to the literature by distinguishing between different types of social media content and extending the TPB framework with self-identity in the context of higher education decision-making. The findings provide insights for understanding how digital communication influences complex behavioral decisions in contemporary educational environments. © 2027 Malque Publishing, All rights reserved.

Title: Extremely lightweight salient object detection in optical remote sensing images
Abstract: Existing salient object detection models in optical remote sensing images (ORSI-SOD) struggle to achieve a trade-off between saliency performance and computational efficiency. To address this issue, an extremely lightweight ORSI-SOD model is designed which operates independently of pre-trained weights. The proposed model incorporates an extremely lightweight trainable backbone, i.e. Octconv Backbone Network (OctNet) that is able to capture high-quality features. Different from commonly used lightweight ORSI-SOD models that introduce the MobileNet series as their backbone, the OctNet achieves this without relying on pre-trained weights. The high-quality features are subsequently fed into a multi-scale feature extraction module (MFEM) and a boundary enhancement module (BEM). The MFEM improves the feature extraction capability for multi-scale salient objects by introducing convolutions with diverse receptive fields. The BEM strengthens the capability in capturing intricate object boundaries within a dual-branch structure. The experimental results on three datasets consistently demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the existing state-of-art salient object detection models in terms of saliency performance and computational efficiency without relying on pre-trained weights. Furthermore, when the input data size is 288 × 288, the proposed model comprises merely 0.93 million parameters and requires only 3.25 billion floating-point operations (FLOPs). The corresponding code for the model proposed in this article can be viewed at https://github.com/blossom-lv/Lightweight_ORSI_SOD_Models/tree/master. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Cross cultural patterns of linguistic aggression and aggressive combat content enjoyment: A computational study of PUBG reviews across six continents
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: This study explores global patterns of linguistic aggression and appreciation for aggressive combat content as expressed in reviews of PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds (PUBG), analyzing over 18.7 million Google Play Store English language reviews from over 80 countries. Grounded in the General Aggression Model (GAM), it integrates media psychology, cross cultural communication, and computational social science to assess emotional expression in user generated content. Two indices, Aggression Score and Appreciation of Aggressive Content (AAC), were constructed using NLP, sentiment analysis, and lexicon-based tagging to capture hostile sentiment (anger) and positive reinforcement (joy, ratings, likes) in aggression-related reviews. Results reveal a significant increase in the average intensity of both scores over time, with reviews grouped under South America exhibiting higher average aggression and AAC scores within the dataset, while reviews grouped under Australia show comparatively lower levels of these measures. The study uses GAM as a conceptual lens to interpret large-scale, naturalistic expressions of aggression and enjoyment. Methodologically, it offers replicable framework for affective analysis; practically, it offers exploratory insights for game design and content moderation in digital environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: EGCG accelerates wound healing in diabetic mice by Notch pathway to enhance epidermis formation
Abstract: Keratinocyte proliferation delay was a prominent clinical manifestation of diabetes, significantly impeding the wound healing process in diabetic mice. The potential therapeutic role of (−)-epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) has been recognized due to its ability to enhance wound healing under diabetic conditions, but the underlying mechanism remained unclear. This study elucidates that EGCG expedited wound healing in diabetic mice by accelerating re-epithelialization and collagen deposition. Remarkably, we observed that EGCG promotes epidermal cell proliferation and enhances wound healing process in diabetic mice. We also discovered an overexpression of the Notch pathway in the epidermal cells of diabetic mice. Interestingly, EGCG effectively suppresses this overexpressed Notch pathway, suggesting a targeted mechanism for its therapeutic effects. Furthermore, the experiments with human immortalized keratinocytes (HaCaT) confirmed that high glucose levels activated the Notch signaling pathway, which was subsequently inhibited by EGCG treatment. In conclusion, our study reveals that EGCG improves wound healing in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic mice by targeting the Notch pathway in epidermal cells. These findings offered novel insights into therapeutic strategies for diabetic wounds and highlight EGCG as a promising candidate for treating chronic wounds. © National R&D Center for Edible Fungus Processing Technology 2026.

Title: How do sustainability capabilities create retail performance over time? dynamic evidence from U.S. and Chinese retailers
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines how sustainability-oriented technological innovation, sustainable supply chain management, and corporate social responsibility relate to environmental and manager-reported organisational performance in retail firms over time. Drawing on the natural resource-based view, institutional theory, and stakeholder theory, the study analyses a 12-wave monthly panel of 2410 retailers in the United States and China, comprising 26,998 firm-month observations. A multi-group hierarchical Bayesian continuous-time dynamic structural equation model estimates within-firm relationships, effects over one-, three-, and six-month intervals, time-varying mediation, and country differences. Technological innovation predicts environmental performance in both countries, but it strengthens sustainable supply chain management only in China. Sustainable supply chain management predicts organisational performance in both countries. Corporate social responsibility predicts environmental performance in both countries, while its direct short-run organisational effect is positive in the United States and negative in China. Environmental performance converts into organisational performance, and all three proposed indirect effects emerge, only in China during the focal six-month window. Exploratory analysis identifies integration-driven accelerators, evidence-driven pragmatists, and weakly-coupled drifters. The findings characterise retail sustainability as a dynamic conversion system with country-specific pathways to environmental and organisational outcomes; implications for individual customer responses require separate empirical testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Synergistic non-thermal plasma-catalytic reforming of toluene over hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 catalysts for efficient syngas production
Abstract: Biomass tar reforming is generally constrained by the high energy demand of conventional thermal processes because of the chemical stability of aromatic compounds. In this work, dielectric barrier discharge plasma was coupled with hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 catalysts for the steam reforming of toluene as a representative biomass tar compound. The effects of Ni loading, reaction temperature, and discharge power on toluene conversion, syngas formation, carbon recovery, and energy efficiency were systematically investigated. Among the catalysts, 15 wt% Ni/mHZSM-5 exhibited the best performance because of its favorable Ni dispersion, high proportion of surface chemisorbed oxygen, enhanced reducibility, and balanced acidity distribution. Among the operating conditions investigated, the best overall reforming performance was obtained at 75 W and 525 °C, achieving a toluene conversion of 99.2%, an H2 yield of 48.3%, a CO selectivity of 36.0%, and a gaseous carbon balance of 60.1%. In comparison, conventional catalytic reforming required substantially higher temperatures to achieve lower conversion and syngas production, demonstrating the promotional effect of plasma excitation on aromatic activation and subsequent surface reforming. The highest toluene conversion energy efficiency of 6.5 g·kWh−1 was obtained at 30 W, indicating a trade-off between conversion performance and energy input. The catalyst also maintained high activity during a 48 h stability test, although gradual deactivation occurred because of carbon deposition. Authors: Xiao P.-Y.; Li H.; Marwick B.
Title: Characterizing Core Morphology and Scar Patterning Within a Unified Spherical Harmonic Framework
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Lithic cores preserve the most direct evidence of past reduction strategies, yet their analysis still relies largely on typological classifications that are subjective and difficult to reproduce. Recent 3D methods quantify core attributes more precisely, but morphology and scar organization are handled in separate mathematical frameworks, precluding joint analysis of how the two relate. Here we present a unified framework based on spherical harmonics that encodes both core morphology (M-SPHARM) and scar patterning (SP-SPHARM) within a single rotation-invariant, landmark-free space, the latter being the first application of spherical harmonics to scar orientation data. Co-inertia analysis examines their covariation, and harmonic reconstruction renders statistical axes back into interpretable three-dimensional forms. While the methods are complementary, validation on ideal models and experimental cores shows that the scar pattern descriptor resolves finer distinctions among core types than existing metrics, most clearly the radial subtypes others cannot separate. The exploratory analysis on experimental and archaeological assemblages reveals no detectable covariation between morphology and scar organization. We identify core type as the principal factor structuring variation at Sandinggai (Hunan, China). The methods are released as an open-source R package (spharmlithic) with a fully reproducible workflow. More broadly, the framework supports understanding core variability as a continuous techno-morphological space rather than a set of discrete types. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Towards effective multimodal emotion recognition in conversations via joint multi-graph learning and self-distillation
Abstract: Emotion Recognition in Conversation (ERC) is a crucial component of empathetic dialogue systems, enabling conversational agents to comprehend users’ expressed emotions and respond appropriately. In recent years, ERC has increasingly evolved toward multimodal approaches, particularly graph-based ones, that leverage complementary signals to enhance effectiveness. Although these approaches show promise, they face challenges in effectively modeling relational structures, computing the contribution of each modality during fusion, and regularizing unimodal representations to prevent modality bias. In this study, we propose DiGemo, a novel multimodal ERC framework that employs Transformer-based contextual modeling and graph-based learning to jointly capture both sequential dependencies within conversations and complex inter-utterance relational structures across modalities. To effectively balance and exploit multimodal information, we employ an adaptive fusion approach based on the Gated Multimodal Unit to estimate the contributions of each modality. In addition, we integrate a self-distillation training strategy to regularize unimodal representations, allowing each modality to learn from the fused multimodal representation and achieve more stable learning. DiGemo achieves Weighted F1-scores of 74.44% and 65.92% on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets, respectively. These results validate the effectiveness of jointly modeling conversational context, cross-modal interactions, the adaptive contributions of modalities, and self-distillation for multimodal ERC. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: ThreatNet: A multi-class dataset and LLM-based framework with class-imbalanced fine-tuning for life threat detection
Abstract: Detecting life-threatening intent in online text is an increasing challenge as social media increasingly influence public conversation. Current models often face challenges related to insufficient data, class imbalance, and domain variability between platforms. This study proposes ThreatNet, a manually annotated multi-class dataset that contains a variety of linguistic indicators and different intensities of threats sourced from multiple online sources. Using this benchmark, we perform a comprehensive empirical evaluation of seven instruction-tuned LLMs (Flan-T5, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Gemma-3-4B-IT, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-Instruct-7B, Zephyr-7B-Alpha, Phi-3-Mini-3.8B) and four transformer baselines (BERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, DeBERTa). We analyze the impact of class imbalance mitigation strategies, few-shot prompting (0, 4, 8, 16 shots), and model scale. Title: Current research on catalysts and deactivation mechanisms for methane catalytic oxidation
Abstract: Focusing on the complex marine exhaust conditions with high water vapor, trace sulfur compounds and fluctuating operating loads, this work systematically summarizes the structure–activity relationships and anti-deactivation characteristics of mainstream catalysts for marine methane total oxidation. Among noble metal materials, Pd-based catalysts exhibit remarkable low-temperature catalytic activity, while Pt-based catalysts deliver superior sulfur tolerance under harsh flue gas environments. By contrast, the performance advantages of Rh catalysts are mainly effective for partial oxidation of methane. Beyond noble metals, low-cost transition metal oxides, perovskites, zeolites, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have also been comprehensively analyzed, with emphasis on their modification strategies tailored to improve low-temperature activity, hydrothermal stability and sulfur resistance. This review highlights the rational design and directional optimization of multifunctional catalysts targeting the actual demanding marine working conditions, providing theoretical guidance for the development of efficient and durable marine methane emission control technologies. Title: Social media reading engagement and critical reading proficiency among Vietnamese EFL learners: A correlational study
Abstract: Social media has become a routine source of English reading for university students, yet its contribution to critical reading proficiency remains empirically under-specified in EFL contexts. This study examines the extent to which social media reading engagement and learners’ critical reading orientation are associated with performance-based critical reading proficiency among Vietnamese undergraduate English majors. Adopting a cross-sectional correlational design, data were collected from 100 third-year English majors at a public university in Vietnam using a questionnaire measuring social media reading engagement and critical reading orientation, alongside a performance-based critical reading test targeting inference making, evaluative judgment, and credibility assessment. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson and Spearman correlations, and hierarchical regression. Results showed a moderate positive association between social media reading engagement and critical reading proficiency (r = 0.42), with engagement alone explaining 17.6% of the variance in test performance. When critical reading orientation was added to the model, the explained variance increased modestly to 20.7%, representing a small incremental gain (ΔR² = 0.031). Regression coefficients indicated that engagement accounted for the larger unique share of variance, whereas the contribution of orientation was statistically weaker and sensitive to threshold criteria. Overall, the findings suggest that social media reading functions as a supportive but conditional literacy environment: engagement with English texts on social media is associated with higher critical reading performance, yet its explanatory power remains bounded and insufficient to account for substantial individual differences. The study underscores the need for restrained pedagogical expectations regarding informal digital reading and highlights the importance of instructional mediation in fostering critical reading development in digitally saturated EFL contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: “How can I help you learn?” Incorporating emotions into parents' support of young children's self-regulated learning at home and school during prolonged crisis
Abstract: Background: Parents apply their knowledge of cognition, emotion, and behavior (metacognition, metaemotion, and metabehavior) to provide children external regulation to achieve learning goals. Aims: Two studies examined how parents' metaprocesses shape children's self-regulated learning (SRL) strategies through external regulation (other-regulation and co-regulation) in distance and in-school learning. Study 1 Method: Mothers (N = 357) were surveyed regarding their own and their 1st–3rd graders’ SRL in three cohorts: Cohort 1 (in-school learning; pre-COVID-19); Cohort 2 (distance learning; COVID-19 first lockdown); and Cohort 3 (in-school learning; post-lockdown). Results: Mediation coefficients were estimated for parent metaprocesses associated with their children's SRL, mediated through external regulation. In distance learning, parental metaemotion, metabehavior, and co-regulation were positively associated with their children's SRL. Co-regulation was positively associated with emotion SRL-reappraisal for Cohort 2 and Cohort 3. Study 2 Method: Parents (n = 311; 49% fathers) were surveyed while their 1st-3rd grade children were in distance learning (Time 1: COVID-19 third lockdown) and in routine in-school learning (Time 2) in a repeated-measures design. Their children (n = 143) reported on social, math, and language abilities at Time 2. Results: Cross-lagged models investigated Time 1 and Time 2 associations within- and across-time effects using complex mediation models. Metaprocesses were linked to SRL, math, and language skills through other-regulation, whereas metaprocesses were associated with SRL strategies and social skills through co-regulation. Conclusion: Parent metaprocesses were positively associated with prompts guiding their children's SRL strategies and learning outcomes. Title: Breaking the NOx-soot trade-off in compression ignition engines at mid-load with high-percentage n-Pentanol blends through charge cooling and oxygenation
Abstract: The quest for sustainable and environmentally friendly fuel alternatives has significantly increased interest in exploring higher alcohols, particularly n-pentanol, as a promising oxygenated biofuel option for internal combustion engines. This study meticulously analyzed the combustion, performance and emission characteristics of a 60% n-pentanol/40% n-dodecane blend, designated P60D40 , and n-dodecane, D100, utilizing computational fluid dynamics simulations. Here, n-dodecane was used as a surrogate for diesel fuel. The analysis was conducted under a variety of engine operation control parameters to ensure a thorough understanding of their behaviors. The results showed that under identical operating conditions, the indicated thermal efficiency of the P60D40 blend was 47.94%, which is higher than the 44.32% for D100. Furthermore, the equivalent indicated specific fuel consumption for the P60D40 blend was 169.89 g/kWh, in contrast to the 183.77 g/kWh of D100. This represents a 7.55% reduction in fuel consumption, highlighting the efficiency benefits of using n-pentanol as a fuel component. In addition to the performance improvements, the study also found significant reductions in harmful emissions. Specifically, emissions of soot, nitrogen oxides and carbon dioxide were reduced by 91.46%, 86.18% and 12.91%, respectively, compared to D100. The utilization of a 60% n-pentanol blend demonstrates considerable potential, as it not only meets the selected Euro VI reference limits of 0.4 g/kWh and 0.01 g/kWh for NOx and soot, respectively, but also offers excellent performance characteristics. Moreover, it shows the capability to effectively address the common trade-off between NOx and soot emissions, particularly under mid-load operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A dynamic fusion enhanced trajectory distillation framework for multi-view classification
Abstract: Multi-view classification incorporates multiple views to improve classification performance. However, in real-world scenarios, different views often exhibit unequal informativeness, which poses challenges to learning discriminative representations. Existing fusion methods mainly rely on weighting or attention mechanisms, which can mitigate redundancy but still lack explicit semantic guidance for discriminative representation learning. To address this issue, we propose a novel dynamic fusion enhanced trajectory distillation method for multi-view classification. Specifically, we develop a dynamic fusion module that enhances discriminative learning and adaptive multi-view fusion by incorporating label embeddings as explicit semantic guidance. Furthermore, we propose a trajectory distillation strategy to prevent the risk of inference-time label leakage while ensuring effective knowledge transfer, thereby enabling the student model to inherit the representation capability of the teacher model without relying on label information during inference. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently achieves superior performance and learns more discriminative representations for multi-view classification. Authors: Zhao H.; Ma J.
Title: Acceptability-driven adaptive migration promotes cooperation in human–machine hybrid population
Abstract: Sustaining cooperation in social systems is persistently challenged by the destabilizing influence of selfish behavior. In human–machine hybrid networks, interactions between artificial agents and human participants introduce both new obstacles and new opportunities for maintaining sustained cooperation. Social interactions are strongly influenced by individuals’ affective assessments of peer strategies. Here, “acceptability”—the degree to which an individual's strategy is supported by neighbors—drives emotion-based migration toward more favorable positions. By contrast, cooperative robots are unaffected by such emotional evaluations and instead base their migration decisions on either success-driven movement or random exploration. Inspired by this notion, the Acceptability-Driven Adaptive Migration (ADAM) model is proposed. Monte Carlo (MC) simulations demonstrate that the proposed ADAM model effectively fosters the emergence of cooperative strategies. In populations where ordinary nodes migrate according to acceptability, increasing the proportion of cooperative robots markedly enhances cooperation, while node density exerts minimal influence except at extremely high or low levels. When a greater share of robots follow the success-driven rule rather than random exploration, cooperation is further reinforced. Network-level average acceptability improves when robots constitute either a minority or a majority of the population. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Compitus K.
Title: Categorical exclusion: Speciesism as a neglected dimension of prejudice in cognitive behavioral therapy
Abstract: While CBT and ABA have recently begun to grapple with their own internal biases, the field's ethical framework remains stubbornly anthropocentric. Scholarship increasingly addresses systemic prejudice in research, yet speciesism—the hierarchical valuation of life based on biological category—is still largely ignored as a socio-political ideology. This is a significant oversight: psychometric evidence suggests that speciesism is not a fringe belief, but is cognitively rooted in Social Dominance Orientation (SDO), much like racism and sexism. Consequently, the discipline's human-centricity should not be viewed as a neutral default, but as an active ideological framework that prioritizes control over clinical insight. This is visible in the pathologization of vystopia. By framing the profound distress caused by industrialized animal exploitation as a cognitive distortion, clinicians commit a form of microaggression that can fundamentally weaken the therapeutic alliance. Furthermore, the behavioral emphasis on mastery and compliance uncomfortably echoes colonial power structures, treating sentient beings as mere variables rather than autonomous agents. To evolve, the field must adopt a socio-ecological model that recognizes the agency of both non-human animals and neurodivergent individuals alike. Decolonizing these frameworks does not dilute the efficacy of CBT; rather, it allows the discipline to function more fully as a science of liberation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Du S.; An D.; Zhang B.; Zhang K.
Title: Collective Action and Efficiency Loss? The Role of Kinship in Multi-Household Grassland Management on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau
Abstract: By facilitating cooperation, the multi-household management pattern (MHMP) enables some household members to engage in non-agricultural employment and is often assumed to enhance production efficiency. However, empirical evidence on its actual efficiency effects remains limited. Drawing on survey data from 156 herder households in Maqu County on the QTP collected between November 2021 and March 2022, this study applies an output-oriented Data Envelopment Analysis combined with Tobit regression to examine the impact of MHMP on production efficiency. The results show that participation in MHMP is associated with lower production efficiency. Labor reallocation from animal husbandry to non-agricultural activities explains this negative relationship. Moreover, strong kinship ties intensify the efficiency loss, as households embedded in close kinship networks tend to adopt more lenient norms regarding effort. While kinship-based cooperation facilitates collective action, it simultaneously reinforces relational norms that weaken performance-oriented incentives. These findings highlight a critical trade-off between social cohesion and production efficiency in collective pasture management. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Shi W.; Jin Y.
Title: THE VALUE OF RECOMMENDATIONS FROM SOCIAL MEDIA ANALYSTS IN ONLINE INVESTMENT COMMUNITIES
Abstract: This study examines the informational value of stock recommendations issued by social media analysts through the lens of Self-Determination Theory (SDT). Using comprehensive data from Seeking Alpha, we demonstrate that these recommendations significantly predict abnormal stock returns over a two-month horizon, with no subsequent reversal, suggesting that they convey incremental information not captured by sell-side analysts or textual sentiment. Guided by SDT, we further show that predictive accuracy varies systematically with analysts’ motivational contexts. Recommendations are more informative when issued by analysts identified as traders, whose direct financial stakes deepen the internalization of extrinsic incentives, and by analysts with high comment-section engagement, where interactive feedback supports needs for competence and relatedness. Conversely, predictive ability declines with longer platform tenure, consistent with motivational saturation as psychological needs become satisfied, and with higher posting frequency, where cognitive overload undermines need satisfaction. Finally, we find that both editorial selection and user-driven engagement effectively identify recommendations with greater ex-post informativeness. In an era of information abundance in online investment communities, our SDT-grounded analysis offers investors guidance for signal extraction and provides platform designers with principled insights for fostering higher-quality content ecosystems. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. Title: High-efficiency near-infrared TADF OLEDs with dipole moment selective matching and exciton management strategy for polar hosts
Abstract: Near-infrared organic light-emitting diodes (NIR-OLEDs) based on thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) are promising for optical communication, bioimaging, and biomedical sensing, but face a persistent trade-off between long-wavelength emission and device efficiency. Here, the previously reported NIR-TADF emitter APDC-DTPA is used to examine a dipole-moment-selective host-screening strategy together with energy-level matching and device-level exciton/charge management. Changing the host from BCP to PPF and DPEPO shifts the film PL maximum from 690 to 724 and 729 nm, while the corresponding photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY) are 28.87%, 24.89%, and 15.17%, respectively. These results show that host polarity can stabilize the charge-transfer excited state, whereas HOMO/LUMO alignment, triplet energy, and transport properties jointly determine device suitability. PPF therefore provides the most practical spectral-photophysical compromise and is selected for device optimization. Transient electroluminescence further reveals intermediate carrier-response dynamics for the PPF-based device. Subsequent insertion of CzSi/TSPO1 blocking layers and optimization of the hole-injection/transport architecture improve exciton confinement and charge balance. The optimized MoO3/TAPC:MoO3/TAPC device exhibits EL centered near 730 nm, a maximum luminance of 220 cd/m2, a maximum radiance of 4.86 W/sr/m2, and a measured peak EQE of 5.81%, corresponding to an approximately 175.4% increase relative to the initial PPF-based Pristine device (2.11%). Title: Comparing direct and indirect measures of attitudes toward health and sustainability in the perception of organic and ancient wheat labels
Abstract: Rising interest in organic and sustainable cereal-based foods necessitates clarifying how consumers' health and sustainability attitudes influence product experience. While attitudes are usually assessed through validated scales, such measures may suffer from social desirability bias, underscoring the value of complementary indirect techniques. This study investigates how consumer segmentation influences expectations and perception of organic crackers made from ancient (Verna) and modern (Altavista) wheat based on health and sustainability attitudes. Attitudes were measured through explicit scales and the indirect text highlighting (TH) method. Following a within-subjects design, one hundred and eighteen consumers evaluated the crackers under blind (only tasting), expected (only information: organic label alone vs. organic combined with the ancient wheat label), and informed conditions (tasting+information). Explicit scales identified two clusters, differing in broad general interest (high vs low) for both health and sustainability. Conversely, TH revealed a different context-specific segmentation based on information prioritization, distinguishing two groups, a health-oriented and a sustainability-oriented group. The two methods did not overlap, separating broad attitudinal traits (scales) from context-specific priorities (TH). Combined organic and ancient wheat cues generated higher expectations for liking, healthiness, sustainability, naturalness, and novelty than the organic label alone across consumer prioritizing health (TH) and both sustainability and health (attitudes) information. However, no assimilation toward expectations was found for liking, suggesting a misalignment between expectations and product experience. This research highlights the complementary value of indirect methods (TH) and underscores the need to align extrinsic cues with sensory characteristics to support more sustainable and healthier food choices. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Structure-aware optimization of recurrence thresholds for multi-sensor kinematic time-series image representations
Abstract: Recurrence plots (RPs) provide a nonlinear representation of time-series dynamics, but their structural characteristics are highly sensitive to recurrence-threshold selection. Conventional fixed-threshold and fixed-recurrence-rate strategies prescribe the recurrence condition without explicitly evaluating the structural properties of the resulting representation. To address this limitation, this work proposes a structure-aware recurrence-threshold optimization framework for multi-sensor kinematic time-series image representations. Rather than directly optimizing the absolute threshold ε, the target recurrence rate (RR) is formulated as a representation-design variable and evaluated using a normalized and regularized multi-metric Recurrence Quantification Analysis (RQA) objective. A kinematics-aware recurrence representation is constructed from acceleration magnitude, angular-velocity magnitude, jerk magnitude, and angular-acceleration magnitude to characterize both steady and transient motion dynamics. Experiments on UP-Fall show that the proposed formulation identifies a stable, non-boundary recurrence-density regime around the prior-informed RR≈0.08 region and produces systematic structural differences relative to fixed, nearest-neighbour, and stability-based threshold-selection methods, with large effect sizes for several RQA descriptors. Independent validation on SisFall confirms systematic RR dependence of the evaluated recurrence structures under different sensing and acquisition conditions, while demonstrating that the numerical operating regime is dataset-dependent rather than universally fixed. Downstream fall-versus-ADL validation further shows that the complete kinematics-aware representation achieves 85.58% accuracy, 88.89% recall, and 84.83% F1-score using RQA features, while direct KA-RP image classification achieves 0.9609±0.0089 accuracy and 0.9902±0.0044 AUC. Title: Integrative genetic analyses of circadian chronotype and autism highlight regional co-association at 17q21.31
Abstract: Chronotype and sleep problems are common in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but their genetic relationship remains uncertain. We integrated published cross-trait LD score regression (LDSC), brain eQTL-based summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), SNP-based two-sample MR, two-step mediation MR, secondary parallel SMR, and Bayesian colocalization using UK Biobank chronotype GWASs, the iPSYCH/Psychiatric Genomics Consortium ASD GWAS, and GTEx v8 brain eQTLs. The published LDSC estimate was negative for morningness-coded chronotype and ASD (rG = −0.199). Primary ASD-outcome SMR identified 50 gene-tissue pairs representing 24 genes at the exploratory multi-SNP PSMR < 0.001 threshold; none met Bonferroni significance. Fifteen candidates occurred in the LD-rich 17q21.31 inversion and are not independent gene discoveries. Secondary eveningness-outcome SMR tested all 24 candidates in matched tissues; 22 had PSMR < 0.05, but GTEx reuse made this descriptive. At 17q21.31, the prespecified p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁵ favored distinct variants (PP.H3 = 0.785) over one shared variant (PP.H4 = 0.126). H3 dominance strengthened at p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁶ and reversed only at the permissive p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁴, equal to p1 and p2. Authors: Wei M.; Zheng R.; Song R.
Title: Beyond the noise: Early identification of emerging technologies through weak signal prediction in higher-order networks
Abstract: The early identification of emerging technologies from weak signals is a critical strategic imperative. Existing network-based methods remain largely confined to lower-order representations and static, snapshot-based conceptualizations of weak signals, emphasizing retrospective detection over prospective prediction. Therefore, this study constructs a multi-source heterogeneous hypergraph with higher-order semantics, spanning the “Science-Technology-Industry” dimensions. By mapping the structural phase transitions of weak signals across an “Outlier-Mutation-Key Node” trajectory, we devise a quantifiable indicator system to shift the analytical paradigm from static retrospective detection to dynamic evolutionary tracking. Using a dataset of 145,316 papers, 79,050 patents, and 5941 project records from the New Energy Vehicle (NEV) fuel cell domain (2015–2024), we identify 226 candidate nodes exhibiting this trajectory. A two-round Delphi expert evaluation confirms 193 of these nodes as expert-confirmed weak signals, establishing Delphi-validated reference labels for subsequent model evaluation. We then employ Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Dynamic Hypergraph Convolutional Network (DHCN), and Large Language Models (ZS-LLM and ICL-LLM) to prospectively predict weak signals with disruptive potential. The ICL-LLM achieves the best predictive performance among the tested models, with a Macro-F1 score of 61.25%, outperforming the MLP (49.76%), DHCN (56.84%), and ZS-LLM (46.35%). This synergy between higher-order topology and semantic intelligence effectively filters stochastic noise and enables meaningful predictive capability of emerging technologies, providing an exploratory decision-support framework for technology foresight. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Smart and green solutions in the catering and hospitality: A review of the existing literature
Abstract: The integration of digital technologies and sustainability practices is reshaping the catering and hospitality industry, yet research on smart and green solutions remains fragmented. This study maps the intellectual and thematic development of this field through a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed publications using VOSviewer, Biblioshiny, and Microsoft Excel. The findings reveal substantial growth in research interest and increasing interdisciplinary contributions across countries, institutions, and authors. Keyword analysis identifies artificial intelligence, sustainability, digital transformation, and social media as dominant themes, while circular economy, Internet of Things (IoT), and customer behavior represent emerging areas. The analysis also highlights a relatively underexplored intersection of AI, IoT, and circular economy, suggesting important opportunities for future research. Authors: Yuan B.; Sun Y.; Sun H.
Title: RAGM-track: Typed graph memory for reliability-conditioned identity reasoning in RGB-T multi-object tracking
Abstract: Identity errors in RGB–thermal MOT can persist beyond the degraded frame because unreliable associations committed to memory distort later matching and identity recovery. Existing trackers encode history as homogeneous queues, prototypes, or track queries, limiting control over evidence retrieval and updating. We propose Reliability-Aware Graph Memory Tracking (RAGM-Track), which represents each identity as a persistent typed graph of identity, appearance, motion, reliability, occlusion, and hard-negative evidence. Reliability-derived degradation adapts the candidate-retrieval budget, while modality reliability and cross-modal conflict modulate association scores and protect memory writing, limiting error propagation and supporting re-entry recovery. On VT-MOT, RAGM-Track achieves 41.37 HOTA, 43.19 DetA, 42.76 IDF1, 50.83 MOTA, and 1124 identity switches. Among published results reproduced in our benchmark comparison, it reports the highest HOTA, DetA, and MOTA and the lowest identity-switch count, while its cross-pipeline IDF1 remains below PFTrack (47.25) and ACNTrack (48.04). Memory-slot-controlled ablations support the benefits of typed organization. On UniRTL-MOT, RAGM-Track improves AssA and IDF1 over untyped attention memory by 1.42 and 1.67 points with shared MCTrack detections, and 3.28 and 2.58 points with oracle boxes. These results show that governing memory evolution complements the interpretation of current observations in robust multimodal tracking. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Multiple pathways to social bonding through music
Abstract: Music is widely recognized for its ability to foster social bonding. Yet, while research has largely focused on interpersonal movement coordination, other ways in which music can connect people have received comparatively less attention. We argue that music-related social bonding extends beyond coordinated movement and emerges through multiple forms of imagined and shared social experience. We propose a conceptual framework comprising three interrelated pathways: interpersonal coordination, shared social experience without explicit behavioral coordination, and imagined social experience during solitary listening. Across these pathways, music recruits interacting mechanisms of temporal prediction, self-other integration, reward processing, and social-cognitive alignment that together promote social closeness, affiliation, and prosocial orientation. We further highlight how musical features and individual differences shape these processes. Title: Novel starch/agar smart bioplastic incorporated with dual-encapsulated anthocyanin for shrimp freshness monitoring
Abstract: A dual-encapsulation strategy for anthocyanins (as the active core) was proposed, using chitosan hydrochloride and carboxymethyl chitosan (90, 160, and 240 kDa) as the external shell and β-cyclodextrin as the internal shell. Color difference values of the bioplastics were confirmed as a reliable indicator of the edible quality of shrimp, and an artificial neural network model was successfully established between the color information (L*, a*, b*, color difference) and the related quality parameters (total volatile basic nitrogen content, pH) of shrimp. Authors: Zhang J.; Wang M.; Liu K.; Zhuang L.; Zhao Z.
Title: Assessment of horizontal ecological compensation in China based on ecosystem service flows
Abstract: Ecological compensation has been regarded as a key mechanism for promoting the coordinated development of regional social-ecological systems and addressing environmental justice. The scientific identification of compensation priorities and amounts is recognized as fundamental for the effective implementation of horizontal compensation schemes. The spatiotemporal dynamics of supply and demand for water, grain, and carbon ecosystem service values were assessed, together with coupling coordination and supply-demand balance. A national horizontal compensation framework for China integrated flow models for individual services, network topology analysis, and compensation accounting to link providers and beneficiaries across cities and estimate reference amounts. Supply generally increased, whereas demand rose for water and carbon but remained relatively stable for grain. Across 2000, 2010, and 2020, the average proportions of cities where local supply exceeded local demand were 80%, 86%, and 22% for water yield, grain production, and carbon sequestration, respectively. Substantial variations in network structure and node characteristics were observed among the compensation networks, with the number of modeled flow paths increasing for water and decreasing for grain and carbon. The numbers of ecological-provision and ecological-beneficiary cities decreased, while their respective average modeled net ecological benefits and net compensation payments were higher in 2020 than in 2000. Meanwhile, the number of cities with unresolved service deficits and no modeled compensation inflows or outflows increased. By linking supply-demand imbalances with flows of individual services, the framework provides a quantitative basis for identifying compensation partners and negotiating differentiated payment responsibilities using estimated amounts as references. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Qiao H.; Feng S.; Wang J.; Zhang F.; Li F.
Title: THDiff: Joint modeling of social and temporal factors in hyperbolic space for time-aware information diffusion prediction
Abstract: Information Diffusion Prediction (IDP) aims to forecast how information spreads among users on social platforms at a micro level. Most existing methods emphasize social relations while overlooking fine-grained temporal dynamics, even though both factors are essential to diffusion. Moreover, both social and temporal factors exhibit hierarchical and imbalanced structures, posing challenges for effective modeling via conventional Euclidean methods. In particular, our analysis of real-world diffusion data reveals highly irregular and heavy-tailed time-interval distributions, suggesting the need for refined representations that can accommodate such imbalanced patterns. While hyperbolic geometry has demonstrated strong capability in capturing hierarchical social influence, its potential for modeling temporal imbalances remains largely unexplored. Motivated by these observations, we propose a novel time-aware hyperbolic diffusion prediction model (THDiff) that jointly models social and temporal factors within a unified hyperbolic framework. Specifically, THDiff uses a rotation-assisted hyperbolic embedding to construct user representations that encode global hierarchical social influence. Building on these representations, it leverages hyperbolic attention to construct cascade representations from both social and temporal perspectives and fuses them through a hyperbolic Hawkes process, enabling comprehensive modeling of complex dynamic diffusion dependencies. By jointly modeling social and temporal factors, THDiff effectively predicts not only who will be activated but also when diffusion events are likely to occur. Extensive experiments across four real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing methods, achieving up to 8.2% and 10.9% improvements in Hits@1 and MRR, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Sun S.; Ma W.; Dai X.; Liu G.; Zhu X.; Zhang J.
Title: A Q-guided offline reinforcement learning framework for incentive mechanism optimization in spatial crowdsourcing
Abstract: Spatial crowdsourcing platforms require effective incentive mechanisms to recruit distributed users for location-dependent tasks while jointly considering platform revenue, user participation, and budget constraints. Existing heuristic and game-theoretic approaches often depend on simplified assumptions about user rationality and system information, whereas online reinforcement learning methods require repeated interaction with the environment, making them costly and risky for practical deployment. To overcome these limitations, we propose QG-DiffIRL, a Q-guided diffusion offline reinforcement learning framework for incentive mechanism optimization. Learning from constructed offline interaction records derived from real mobility traces, QG-DiffIRL integrates a diffusion-based policy for complex continuous action generation, critic-guided value refinement for high-quality incentive decisions, and prospect-theory-based user modeling for boundedly rational acceptance behavior. Extensive experiments on multiple spatial crowdsourcing datasets demonstrate that QG-DiffIRL consistently improves platform utility, utility per accepted task, and budget efficiency while achieving competitive or superior social welfare over representative baselines, highlighting its value for robust and data-driven incentive design in spatial crowdsourcing platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Multifunctional polyurethane enabled by halloysite nanotubes: Combining robust self-healing, high recyclability, and superior wear resistance
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Developing advanced intelligent materials that integrate long service life, high reliability, and sustainable recyclability remains a critical unresolved challenge in the field of high-end equipment. Conventional polyurethanes, constrained by their intrinsic molecular structures, struggle to reconcile mechanical performance with self-healing capability. Guided by a molecular-nanoscale multiscale structural design paradigm, this study designs and fabricates a novel polyurethane composite through a ternary synergistic strategy involving dynamic covalent bonds, multiple hydrogen bonds, and rigid nanotubes. Incorporation of dynamic disulfide bonds and guanidine-functionalized halloysite nanotubes (M-HNTs) enables the construction of a reversible adaptive chemo-physical network architecture. Through the cleavage and recombination of dynamic disulfide bonds and multiple hydrogen bonds, this material exhibits robust self-healing capability (efficiency > 94%), excellent wear resistance (wear rate 2.6 × 10−14 mm3/(N m)), and remarkable recyclability (> 90% mechanical retention after 6 cycles), along with good shape memory function (recovery rate > 96%). Authors: Yao L.; Ma Q.; Yan M.
Title: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COIN: CLICKBAIT’S INFLUENCE ON CONSUMER PURCHASE INTENTION IN SOCIAL MEDIA
Abstract: As social media increasingly operates within algorithm-driven attention economies, clickbait has become a pervasive engagement tactic. However, prior research has not fully explained the psychological mechanisms linking clickbait to downstream consumer behavior. Existing studies have also largely treated clickbait as an isolated persuasive cue, overlooking its dynamic interactions with other elements in social media ecosystems. Drawing on psychological reactance theory (PRT) and uses-and-gratifications theory (UGT), this study develops an integrated framework to examine when clickbait harms versus facilitates consumer responses. Across four experiments, we test a sequential mediation model in which perceived intrusiveness and advertising avoidance transmit the effects of clickbait on purchase intention. We further introduce message appeal congruence as a key boundary condition. The results indicate that clickbait does not uniformly produce negative outcomes. When headline-induced motivations align with the gratifications delivered by the content, perceived intrusiveness and reactance are attenuated. When they are misaligned, advertising avoidance increases and purchase intention declines. This research advances the clickbait literature by shifting attention from static credibility judgments to dynamic goal-directed processing and by identifying gratification fulfillment as an upstream regulator of psychological reactance in social media contexts. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. Title: Semantics-aware truth discovery based on semi-supervised representation refinement
Abstract: Data scientists are facing the urgent need to build a robust data integration pipeline for heterogeneous data from multiple sources. Existing truth discovery algorithms consider textual values as categories, ignoring semantic ambiguity. This work seeks to answer the Semantics-aware Truth Discovery problem: How to incorporate semantic information into truth discovery methods? We tailor an off-the-shelf tabular representation method for multi-source observations as a Basic Representation Model (BRM). However, as an unsupervised model, BRM falls short in dealing with inadequate local semantic information in multi-source observations. To mitigate this issue, we construct a semi-supervised hyperparameter search strategy for representation refinement. We also propose warm start and pruning strategies to accelerate hyperparameter search. Empirical evaluation on three real world datasets shows that S3TD outperforms existing truth discovery state-of-the-art algorithms by 3.07% on average, and can enhance the performance of existing truth discovery algorithms by up to 8.17%, both in absolute error rate. Moreover, S3TD can obtain such performance gains using as few as 5% labeled data, and reduce time costs without performance loss. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Stepwise salting-out and freeze-thaw strategy enables robust conductive polyvinyl alcohol hydrogels via interfacial synergy for multifunctional wearables
