Abstract: To address the intrinsic trade-off between mechanical robustness and ionic conductivity in polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogels arising from structural heterogeneity, this work presents a stepwise salting-out and freeze-thaw cycling strategy to fabricate high-performance composite hydrogels with synergistic interfacial interactions. By integrating sodium alginate-dispersed liquid metal with lignosulfonate mediation, we establish a multi-scale crosslinking network governed by hydrogen bonding, metal-coordination, and electrostatic effects. Crucially, the stepwise process mitigates the excessive densification typical of conventional methods, facilitating the homogeneous infiltration of additives and refining PVA microcrystalline domains. Title: Domain-specific risk tendencies show little association, directly or indirectly, with domain-specific self-esteem
Abstract: Both risk taking and self-esteem have traditionally been considered general traits that apply across domains of behaviors, although each has separately been considered as multidimensional or domain specific at times. The domain specificity of both constructs is debated, though, and the theoretical relationships between self-esteem and risk-taking remain unclear. The present study (N = 191) looked at relationships across both domain specific self-esteem and domain-specific risk taking, as well as a theoretically hypothesized possible moderating variable of relative state (perceived ability/need). General self-esteem and general risk taking were assessed concurrently. Specific domains of self-esteem and risk taking were mostly correlated with, yet distinct from, the general constructs with a few notable exceptions. General self-esteem was not correlated with general risk taking, and—although social and physical appearance self-esteem differentially associated with evaluations of their relative state in those areas—domain specific self-esteem was largely not correlated with specific types of risk taking. Moderation analyses did not support an indirect relationship between self-esteem and risk taking. Better measures for the relative state model of risk and more firmly grounded theoretical models of self-esteem and risk taking may be needed in order to better understand if and how they are related. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: van Kleef G.A.; Cohen-Chen S.

Title: Social consequences of emotional expressions in negotiation
Abstract: Negotiation is integral to social life. Whether we focus on exchanges between individuals, groups, organizations, or nations, negotiation is the most common and constructive way of making deals and solving disputes. Negotiations can spark intense emotions, which in turn shape negotiation processes and outcomes. Here, we review research on the social consequences of emotional expressions in negotiation. We summarize evidence regarding specific single emotions (e.g., anger, happiness, disappointment, sadness, fear, guilt, shame, pride, hope) as well as alternative (patterns of) emotional responses (e.g., empathy, emotional ambivalence, mixed emotions, alternating emotions, indifference) across levels of analysis (interpersonal, intragroup, intergroup). Our review indicates that emotions can have both favorable and unfavorable consequences, depending on critical moderators (e.g., information processing, perceived appropriateness) and the focal criterion (e.g., monetary gains, social outcomes). The richness of the empirical record underlines the importance of investigating discrete emotions (rather than positive vs. negative affect) and defies simple conclusions about the (dys)functionality of emotions. Emotional expressions can help or hurt negotiators’ outcomes depending on goal prioritization (e.g., maximizing individual outcomes vs. maintaining positive relations) and the social context. We call for research outside the lab to gain insight into real-world consequences of emotional dynamics in (intergroup) negotiation, mediation, and diplomacy. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: ASD-FCGCN: A biologically interpretable graph convolutional network for ASD diagnosis from rs-fMRI
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition traditionally diagnosed through subjective behavioral assessments. Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) provides a potential pathway for objective neuroimaging biomarker discovery; however, existing deep learning methods often struggle to integrate neurobiological priors with data-driven representations. This study aimed to address these limitations by developing a biologically interpretable graph-learning framework for rs-fMRI-based ASD classification. Methods: We propose ASD-FCGCN, a biologically informed graph convolutional network validated on 871 subjects from the ABIDE dataset. The method systematically integrates neurobiological priors with graph learning. Specifically, prior-weighted functional connectivity matrices are constructed to generate hemisphere-specific representations. A Pairwise Association Encoder (PAE) is employed to estimate inter-subject phenotypic relationships, transforming similarity weights into channel-wise gating signals to dynamically regulate graph convolution. Furthermore, a corpus callosum-inspired interaction mechanism is introduced to enable bidirectional information exchange between hemispheres, thereby synthesizing whole-brain features for classification. Conclusion: The results indicate that integrating neurobiological priors, phenotype-guided convolution, and cross-hemispheric coordination can improve subject-level rs-fMRI-based ASD classification. Title: How could redistribution be possible? Effects of national identity and communion among Chinese youth
Abstract: Previous studies in Western countries demonstrated that the relationship between national identity and redistribution preferences was inconsistent, and few studies addressed the cross-cultural consistency about this relationship. Title: When service environments signal ideology: Customer responses to ideological cues

Abstract: Service environments increasingly contain visible cues that communicate political engagement, religious identities, LGBTQ + affiliation, environmental advocacy, and other collective values. Although servicescape research has traditionally emphasized atmospheric, aesthetic, and functional cues, less is known about how customers interpret ideological cues embedded within routine service encounters. Drawing on servicescape research and social identity theory, this research examines how ideological servicescape cues are associated with customer discomfort, avoidance intentions, and stated store-choice decisions. Study 1 shows that political cues generate greater discomfort than environmental and lifestyle cues, although they do not differ significantly from religious or LGBTQ + cues. Study 2 shows that matching political cues displayed across employee and environmental touchpoints generate greater discomfort than political cues displayed through a single source, while perceived authenticity does not account for this association. Study 3 shows that political cues are associated with lower stated store choice than environmental cues, particularly when matching political cues appear across employee and environmental touchpoints. Across studies, customer discomfort statistically accounts for part of the association between ideological cue conditions and avoidance intentions or stated store-choice decisions. The findings extend servicescape scholarship by showing that politically charged symbolism may shape customer responses through both cue content and cue-source configuration. Title: Machine Learning-Assisted optimization of acetylene Dual-Fuel combustion using Copper oxide (CuO) Nano-Enhanced waste Plastic Oil in Compression Ignition (CI) Engine

The proposed approach integrates waste-to-energy fuel utilization, catalytic nano-additives, high-reactivity gaseous combustion, and data-driven predictive modelling within a unified sustainable combustion framework. Among all tested fuel combinations, A5WPO10Cu100 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a maximum brake thermal efficiency of 33.12 %, corresponding to an 8.27 % improvement over diesel, together with a 21.03 % reduction in brake specific energy consumption. The optimum fuel also reduced HC, CO, and smoke opacity by 41.46 %, 47.62 %, and 43.58 %, respectively, while A10WPO10Cu100 produced the highest combustion intensity with a peak heat release rate of 68.9 J/°CA, maximum cylinder pressure of 90.5 bar, and minimum ignition delay of 8.75 °CA, indicating enhanced premixed combustion and catalytic oxidation. Although NOx emissions increased under higher acetylene induction due to elevated combustion temperatures, the overall combustion efficiency and emission trade-off were significantly improved. To further establish predictive capability, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models were developed using the experimental dataset. Among these, the Random Forest model demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy with R2 values ranging from 0.995 to 0.999 and prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, confirming its robustness in predicting nonlinear combustion, performance, and emission characteristics. The integrated experimental and machine learning framework demonstrates that CuO nano-enhanced WPO coupled with acetylene induction is a promising strategy for improving CI engine efficiency while simultaneously advancing intelligent combustion optimization for sustainable transportation applications. To further enhance predictive capability and intelligent engine diagnostics, advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) were developed using experimentally measured combustion, performance, and emission parameters. The Random Forest model demonstrated superior nonlinear prediction capability with prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, coefficient of determination (R2) approaching 0.995–0.999 for major engine responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Serema B.
Title: The Influence of Tswana Cosmological worldview and Sacred Beliefs on the Spatial Organization of Traditional Settlements: A Study of the Setswana Traditional Space kgotla
Abstract: This study examines how Tswana cosmology and sacred beliefs shaped the spatial organization, social structure, and geography of traditional settlements, focusing on the Setswana kgotla as the central sociopolitical, ritual, and spiritual space. Although the kgotla has undergone substantial functional and physical transformation through colonization, modernization, and contemporary planning, its historical development provides important insight into the principles underlying Tswana settlement planning. Using an interpretive qualitative approach based on historical documents, classic ethnographic literature, comparative spatial analysis, field observations, and oral accounts from six historically significant Tswana villages in Botswana—Kanye, Mochudi, Molepolole, Maun, Serowe, and Ramotswa—this study investigates the sacred and social principles governing settlement organization, including the location of the kgosi’s ward, the centrality of the kgotla, geographic setting, cardinal orientation, hierarchical ward structure, spatial configuration, and threshold treatments. The findings show that traditional Tswana settlements were shaped not only by practical and defensive needs but also by a cosmological order in which authority, ancestry, community, environmental relationships, and protection were expressed through space. Rather than serving solely as a traditional court, the kgotla functioned as the symbolic center where the moral, political, and sacred dimensions of Tswana society converged. The study argues that Tswana spatial organization is best understood as a dynamic system shaped by cosmology, environmental knowledge, and historical change rather than as a fixed symbolic structure. It further demonstrates that precolonial Tswana settlement planning embodied an Indigenous system of spatial knowledge rooted in concepts of hierarchy, enclosure, ecology, and social affiliation. Reconsidering the cosmological foundations of the kgotla therefore provides valuable insights into Indigenous settlement planning and contributes to broader discussions of culturally grounded, context-responsive approaches to spatial organization. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: The viral deviation: a quantitative analysis of social media engagement metrics on non-compliant flight deck behaviors
Abstract: Background Normalization of Deviance (NoD) is a well-documented organizational failure mode in aviation, yet its propagation through digital ecosystems remains unexplored. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) highlights a critical mentorship vacuum due to pilot retirements, and social media platforms increasingly serve as informal training environments. This study introduces the concept of Algorithmic Normalization of Deviance- ANoD, hypothesizing that recommendation algorithms systematically reward and amplify “gray-zone” cockpit behaviors that erode sterile flight deck protocols. Method We conducted a stratified netnographic analysis of 150 high-visibility aviation videos (N = 150) across Instagram Reels, split between algorithmically recommended content (n = 100) and curated influencer content (n = 50). A novel coding framework operationalized compliance (Compliant vs. Gray Zone vs. Deviant) and incentive structures. Engagement metrics were analyzed to quantify the algorithmic advantage of non-compliant behavior. Results The analysis reveals a directionally consistent “Viral Deviation” pattern rather than a statistically decisive one. Gray-zone recordings (i.e., technically legal but procedurally borderline) comprised 57% of the sample and attracted higher engagement than compliant content, although this difference was small and did not reach conventional significance (d = 0.24, p = 0.11). The clearest signal emerged between content sources: algorithmically surfaced posts showed significantly higher interaction rates than curated influencer posts (d = 0.31, p = 0.029), a small but statistically significant per-view advantage for content promoted directly by the recommendation system. Structural incentive analysis further indicates that monetization pressures co-occur with increased gray-zone production, structurally analogous to a parallel, shadow curriculum associated with conditions that may facilitate drift. Conclusion The study identifies statistical associations, not causal relationships, and the downstream behavioural impact on pilots is hypothesised from the algorithmic-pattern evidence rather than directly measured. Within those bounds, social media algorithms constitute a structurally unmonitored distribution channel whose observed associations with gray-zone content amplification are consistent with a normalisation-of-deviance feedback mechanism operating beyond current regulatory oversight — an association that warrants urgent empirical validation and proactive governance. We propose a shift from prohibition to risk-stratified governance, recommending that regulators distinguish between handheld (high-risk) and mounted (managed-risk) devices, and integrate digital algorithmic literacy into ab-initio pilot training to counter this new systemic threat. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Chen Y.; Zheng T.; Luan Y.; Feng Y.; Jiang K.; Li W.; Wang M.; Liu Z.; Lu G.
Title: Automatic design of flow channel for PEMFC based on space-weighted topology and multi-objective optimization
Abstract: To address the severe concentration polarization in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) under high current density, caused by oxygen transport limitation and water management imbalance, this study proposes a three-dimensional automatic flow channel design framework integrating topology optimization and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). A multi-physics coupled model is established, with average current density, current density variance, and pressure drop selected as optimization objectives. The weight space is systematically explored through Latin hypercube sampling combined with simplex mapping, and a BP neural network surrogate model is trained based on COMSOL-MATLAB high-fidelity simulation data to enable efficient global optimization. The results reveal a pronounced nonlinear trade-off among the three objectives. Single-objective optimization improves current density but significantly increases pressure drop, while conventional empirical weighting schemes fail to achieve balanced performance. The optimal compromise solution (w1 = 0.571, w2 = 0.286, w3 = 0.143), identified using the TOPSIS decision-making method, achieves a 5.04 % increase in peak power density compared to the conventional structure, while significantly enhancing oxygen distribution uniformity and water management capability. Furthermore, the lateral flow intensity ratio demonstrates a fundamental transition of oxygen transport from diffusion-dominated to convection–diffusion coupled mechanisms. This study provides a systematic and data-driven optimization framework that eliminates empirical bias in weight selection, enables automatic generation of complex flow channel structures, and the optimal structure’s discovery mechanistically reveals the embryonic form of single-channel optima, offering new insights for designing high-performance PEMFC flow fields. Authors: Li X.; Yu N.; Chang X.; Zhang H.; Hu G.; Zhao H.; Dong Z.
Title: Spectral graph filter bank fusion for multimodal rumor cascade representation and detection
Abstract: Rumor detection on social media is inherently a multi-source information fusion problem that involves heterogeneous signals from textual content, user interactions, and temporal dynamics. Existing approaches often underexploit the global structural patterns encoded in rumor propagation graphs. In this work, we propose a unified multimodal fusion framework, termed Rumor Graph Filter Net (RGFN), which integrates multimodal representations with learnable spectral graph filtering. Specifically, post content embeddings derived from a pre-trained language encoder, user social relation representations obtained via self-supervised contrastive learning, and propagation timestamps are jointly transformed into the graph spectral domain using the Graph Fourier Transform (GFT). To adaptively capture discriminative propagation characteristics, we design channel-wise graph filter banks based on Chebyshev polynomial approximations, enabling frequency-selective enhancement and noise suppression. The filtered spectral responses are projected back to the spatial domain through the inverse GFT, followed by a simplified hierarchical multi-view graph pooling mechanism to obtain robust graph-level representations across scales. The final classifier operates on fused multilevel features for rumor identification. Experiments on two real-world rumor datasets, Twitter and Weibo, show that RGFN achieves the highest F1-score among the baselines and performs competitively on other metrics. Specifically, RGFN outperforms the best baselines on Twitter and Weibo by 4.9% and 1.4% on F1-score, respectively. The proposed framework offers a principled integration of graph signal processing and multimodal information fusion for social media credibility assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Decoding entrepreneurial intention: A systematic review, theoretical framework synthesis, and research trajectories
Abstract: Entrepreneurial intention (EI) is a critical psychological construct for understanding the precursors of entrepreneurial behavior. Despite a surge in empirical research over the past decade, the literature on EI remains fragmented across theoretical frameworks, methodological approaches, and contextual applications. This study systematically reviews 53 peer-reviewed articles on entrepreneurial intention published between 2018 and 2025 to synthesize theoretical frameworks, methodological patterns, key findings, and future research directions. Guided by the PRISMA approach, the review reveals the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) as the predominant model, frequently integrated with constructs from Social Cognitive Theory, Technology Acceptance Model, and moral or contextual frameworks. Quantitative cross-sectional designs dominate the methodological landscape, often involving university student samples and the use of structural equation modelling techniques for hypothesis testing. Findings consistently confirm the central role of attitude, perceived behavioral control, and self-efficacy in predicting EI, while more recent studies highlight the growing significance of emotional intelligence, cultural influences, institutional support, and entrepreneurship education. However, the review identifies key limitations, including the overreliance on student-based samples, a lack of longitudinal and experimental designs, and limited generalizability to actual entrepreneurial behavior in real-world settings. Additionally, contextual diversity across emerging and developed economies remains underexplored. In response, the study proposes five future research trajectories: theoretical expansion beyond dominant models, increased adoption of behavioral and longitudinal approaches, broader contextual and demographic inclusion, pedagogical innovation in entrepreneurship education, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration. By mapping evolving trends and gaps in EI research, this review provides a foundation for more dynamic, inclusive, and practically relevant scholarship in entrepreneurship studies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion with Graph-Aware Dual Contrastive Learning for drug–drug interaction prediction
Abstract: Accurate prediction of drug–drug interactions (DDIs) is vital for patient safety and therapeutic efficacy. Recently, DDI prediction methods based on graph neural networks and multi-source heterogeneous drug information have made progress. However, most existing multimodal DDI prediction methods still fail to fully integrate multi-source heterogeneous drug information and effectively exploit the complementary information across different modalities, making it difficult to fully capture the sequential, structural, and semantic characteristics of drugs, thereby limiting the quality of drug representations and DDI prediction performance. To address these limitations, we propose MHGCL, a Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion with Graph-Aware Dual Contrastive Learning framework, designed for DDI prediction. Initially, we construct a comprehensive drug representation by integrating four modalities: drug SMILES sequences, protein target sequences, molecular graphs, and a biomedical knowledge graph (KG) to holistically capture and incorporate the sequential, structural, and semantic information of drugs. Next, we design a graph-structure-aware adaptive subgraph extraction strategy that selects the optimal sampling method based on the structural properties of the KG, and propose a dual contrastive learning mechanism to enhance the quality of feature representations for both molecular graphs and KGs. Finally, we construct a cross-modal self-attention fusion module that achieves dynamic interaction and deep integration of heterogeneous modality features. Experimental results on three real-world drug datasets demonstrate that MHGCL significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, validating its effectiveness for DDI prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Ensemble of deep architectures for SWARM AI-based decision-making
Abstract: This work studies how an artificial agent can participate in swarm-based decision-making alongside human experts by learning collective decision dynamics. We formulate this problem as a multimodal sequential prediction task that combines two complementary sources of information: (i) spatiotemporal interaction traces generated by experts through the HANS web platform and (ii) the corresponding image. We propose a hybrid architecture with an LSTM branch for interaction sequences and a WideResNet branch for image encoding, followed by feature fusion and joint optimisation. The model predicts the evolution of the collective decision at each time step, thereby acting as an autonomous swarm AI agent that receives the same evidence as a human participant. We evaluate the approach on four use cases from environmental microscopy and biomedical imaging: diatoms, cyanobacteria, HER2 and Ki67. The analysis considers interaction-level prediction error, measured by RMSE, and decision-level metrics, including precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score and balanced accuracy under Top-k settings. Across the datasets, the model achieves low interaction error and strong balanced accuracy, while the temporal analysis shows that it captures meaningful convergence patterns in expert consensus. These results support the feasibility of hybrid multimodal models for embedding artificial agents in collaborative decision environments. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: HAD-TAM: Health insurance anomaly detection via truncated affinity maximization with degree-normalized scoring
Abstract: Substantial financial losses are incurred annually as a result of medical insurance fraud, driven by subtle behaviors such as false diagnoses and over-prescription. Although heterogeneous graph structures can be exploited by existing graph neural network-based methods, they often rely on manually selected meta-paths, and the identification of structural anomalies remains a persistent challenge. To address these challenges, Health insurance Anomaly Detection via Truncated Affinity Maximization (HAD-TAM) is proposed as a health insurance fraud detection method, wherein degree-normalized anomaly score-guided meta-path selection is first combined with dual-threshold edge pruning to capture structural anomalies. First, the meta-graph with the highest degree-normalized anomaly score is selected by the model to highlight structures potentially indicative of fraud. Second, non-homophily edges are iteratively pruned by the model using both global and local thresholds to suppress noise and preserve meaningful structure. Finally, the neighborhood affinity of normal nodes is maximized by the model to better separate them from anomalies and improve fraud detection accuracy. Experimental results show that HAD-TAM outperforms eleven advanced baseline methods on two real-world medical insurance datasets, achieving a 2.41% improvement in AUROC and a 1.06% improvement in AUPRC. Furthermore, it exhibits good generalization to public datasets such as Amazon and Reddit. © 2026

Title: Overcoming Digital Twin Blindness: An event-triggered edge–cloud architecture using quantized TinyML
Abstract: Maintaining synchronization between physical assets and their Digital Twin (DT) typically requires continuous data transmission, which becomes challenging in bandwidth- and energy-constrained Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. Continuous data transfer introduces a trade-off between update frequency, state accuracy, and communication overhead. To address this challenge, an edge–cloud cooperative architecture is proposed for event-triggered DT synchronization using a quantized Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) model. An ultra-lightweight INT8-quantized separable convolutional autoencoder is deployed at the edge. This model performs on-device sensor fusion and triggers synchronization when significant deviations in the physical state are detected. During periods without edge transmissions, a cloud-hosted forecasting model predicts and maintains the DT state. The proposed approach is evaluated using the SKAB, CMAPSS, and MNIST datasets. Micro-benchmark results show that the TinyML gatekeeper is compressed to 10.77 KB and consumes only 0.0058 mJ per inference, resulting in an 11.9 times reduction in memory footprint and a 45 times improvement in Age of Information compared to conventional synchronization methods. Cloud-side experiments further show that predictive state reconstruction preserves DT fidelity while reducing communication overhead by more than 85%. End-to-end evaluations show that the proposed framework significantly extends the Pareto frontier of DT synchronization. The system operates at a low bandwidth utilization of approximately 54.2%, reduces univariate synchronization error by over 71%, and achieves a perfect synchronization for multivariate anomaly tracking with RMSE of zero for 8-dimensional data. Overall, the framework mitigates the Digital Twin Blindness problem inherent in static polling approaches and provides a scalable synchronization strategy for next-generation IIoT systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Achieving superior piezoelectric temperature stability in Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3-based piezoceramics via mixed phase boundary engineering
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: A long-standing challenge for Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3 (BNT)-based ceramics is that constructing a single morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) makes it difficult to simultaneously achieve high piezoelectric constant d 33 and superior piezoelectric temperature stability, which hinders their industrial applications. Herein, a novel strategy is proposed to mitigate the above trade-off by designing a mixed phase boundary strategy that integrates the multi-MPB components (abbreviated as M-BNT) to construct polymorphic polar domains. By this strategy, the M-BNT ceramic not only possesses a high d 33 of 180pC/N and a large depolarization temperature T d of 145°C, but also exhibits outstanding thermal stability of in-situ d 33. The competitive residual stress related to the mismatch of shrinkage rate and coefficient of thermal expansion during sintering and cooling, provides the driving force for the development of polymorphic polar domains. Our work offers a viable strategy for developing BNT-based piezoceramics that simultaneously exhibit a high d 33 and superior piezoelectric temperature stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Determination of discount rates in business valuation and public project evaluation: A systematic review from the perspective of international finance and financial theory
Abstract: The discount rate plays a central role in business valuation and public project appraisal because it links risk to the valuation of future cash flows and guides the efficient allocation of resources. However, the global literature lacks methodological consensus and shows significant divergences between private and social approaches, as well as between developed and emerging economies. The present study aims to synthesize the main theoretical and empirical approaches used to determine discount rates from the perspective of international finance. A systematic literature review was conducted following the prisma protocol. Searches were conducted in scopus, web of science, sciencedirect, ssrn, and jstor, using boolean search strings related to “discount rate”, “wacc”, “capm”, “social discount rate”, and “country risk premium”. Studies published from 2000 to 2025, in english and spanish, were included. Only studies with a clear methodological foundation in finance and economics were considered. The analysis was carried out through a qualitative thematic synthesis. The reviewed literature indicates the predominance of the wacc and asset pricing models as the primary references for estimating private discount rates, and reports the increasing use of multifactor models and country risk premiums in the international context. For public projects, the literature identifies two main approaches: the social rate of time preference and the social opportunity cost of capital. The studies also suggest substantial heterogeneity across countries, with generally higher discount rates in emerging economies. No single discount rate is universally applicable; instead, its estimation depends on the local institutional context, the objectives of the investment, and the nature of the risks being evaluated. Title: BCF-CDAN: bidirectional cross-modal fusion and conditional domain adversarial network for multimodal cross-subject emotion recognition with EEG-fNIRS
Abstract: Emotion recognition is essential for affective brain-computer interface (BCI), yet poses significant challenges. Specifically, emotion processing involves complex temporal dynamics and spatial brain networks. Therefore, it’s difficult to decode human emotions. Furthermore, individual differences limit the generalizability of cross-subject emotion recognition. In addition, the feasibility of EEG-fNIRS for fine-grained emotion recognition remains underexplored. To address the above issues, this study proposed an interpretable multimodal cross-subject emotion recognition model—the bidirectional cross-modal fusion and conditional domain adversarial network (BCF-CDAN). The proposed framework explicitly exploited the high temporal resolution of EEG and the high spatial resolution of fNIRS. Specifically, modality-specific convolutional neural networks were first employed to emphasize the temporal information of EEG and the spatial information of fNIRS. A multi-stream module and a one-stream module were then designed to achieve cross-modal fusion. The multi-stream module employed bidirectional cross-attention to capture interactive correlations between EEG temporal features and fNIRS spatial features, while the one-stream module used self-attention to learn a global discriminative representation. Subsequently, a conditional domain adversarial network (CDAN) combined with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss was applied to achieve cross-subject distribution alignment. Results on the two self-collected EEG-fNIRS datasets, TMVED3 (three-class task) and TMVED8 (fine-grained eight-class task), showed that BCF-CDAN achieved cross-subject accuracies of 80.14% and 53.13%, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, the interpretability analysis revealed cross-modal dependencies between EEG temporal features and fNIRS spatial features. Overall, the approach leveraged modality-specific strengths, offering a generalizable and interpretable strategy for brain signal integration. Title: Effect of walking slope on cognitive performance. Electrophysiological evidence of dual-task interference
Abstract: The neural basis of cognitive–motor dual-tasking (CMDT), which involves the simultaneous performance of motor and cognitive tasks, has received increasing attention. However, the electrophysiological impact of walking complexity on concurrent cognitive performance remains unclear. This study examined how walking slope modulates cognitive performance and event-related potentials during a visuomotor discrimination task requiring a simple manual keypress response to target stimuli while walking on a treadmill. Twenty healthy adults (20–36 years) completed the task under three slope conditions (downhill −11%, flat 0%, uphill +11%) while electroencephalogram was recorded. Behavioral results showed preserved accuracy across conditions, with slower response times during downhill walking relative to uphill walking. Early sensory processing was strongly affected by locomotor complexity: both uphill and downhill walking elicited larger P1 amplitudes and reduced N1 amplitudes relative to flat walking. In contrast, late cognitive processing indexed by the P3 was largely preserved, although the differential P3 was selectively reduced during uphill walking, suggesting selective redistribution of resources under the highest energetic and cognitive load, consistent with a possible capacity-sharing account. Uphill walking was perceived as the most physically and cognitively demanding condition, while the lowest mean state-anxiety score was observed after uphill walking. Authors: Chen W.; Yuan H.; Li S.; Ye M.
Title: DMoA: Dynamic Mixture of Adapters with Feature-Enhanced Fusion for UAV Visible-Infrared Object Detection
Abstract: Visible-infrared (RGB-IR) object detection has attracted significant attention in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based applications, such as disaster search and rescue, intelligent surveillance, and battlefield target tracking. However, the quality of RGB and IR modalities may vary substantially under different environmental conditions, causing one modality to become unreliable and leading to suboptimal feature enhancement and fusion. To address this challenge, we propose the Dynamic Mixture of Adapters (DMoA), a novel modality-aware enhancement framework that dynamically refines multi-modal features before semantic fusion through a Mixture of Experts (MoE) mechanism. Applied across multi-scale feature layers, DMoA consists of three key components. First, a Cross-Modality Feature Pre-Enhancement (CMFPE) block exploits complementary information to compensate for weak modality features. Second, the Dynamic Feature Enhancement (DFE) block employs separate four-expert pools and gating networks for RGB and IR at each scale, with no parameter sharing across modalities or scales. Each gating network sparsely activates the top two lightweight experts for input-adaptive feature refinement, thereby limiting computational overhead. Finally, a Semantic Information Fusion (SIF) block promotes cross-modal semantic consistency through mutual information optimization while suppressing redundant feature responses. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that DMoA consistently achieves competitive detection performance and a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off, highlighting its effectiveness for UAV-based RGB-IR object detection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Generating synthetic citation networks with communities
Abstract: Generating realistic synthetic citation, patent, or component dependency networks is essential for benchmarking community detection, graph visualisation, and network data mining algorithms. We present a systematic comparison of generators of directed graphs that are nearly acyclic and have a ground-truth community structure. We evaluate 12 methods across 7 real citation networks and 26 metrics. We propose the practice of reversing the directions of edges in static generators to break cycles and induce a citation-like flow, which markedly improves the performance of a degree-corrected Stochastic Block Model. Our methodological approach to evaluating community detection benchmarks distinguishes between endogenous and exogenous mesoscopic similarities, with the latter proving more important. This distinction reveals that high-parameter models gain much of their advantage by memorising planted community statistics, which limits their fidelity when the evaluation is blind to those labels. Finally, we introduce the Citation Seeder (CS) algorithm, an iterative generator grounded in the Price-Pareto model of citation networks, with interpretable parameters and O(N+E) generation. CS achieves competitive results against the best-performing baselines while using up to four orders of magnitude fewer parameters, providing an interpretable account of a network's structure and, on a temporal hold-out, extrapolating its future in-degree distribution more faithfully than descriptive baselines. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Arıcak O.T.; Boz C.
Title: Development and validation of an ICD-11–based problematic social media use scale
Abstract: The present study aimed to address conceptual and measurement challenges in assessing problematic social media use by developing a scale grounded in the ICD-11 diagnostic framework for behavioral addictions. Item generation was based on core features including impaired control, prioritization of the behavior, continuation despite negative consequences, and functional impairment. Following expert review and pilot testing, data were collected in multiple phases. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a multidimensional structure consistent with ICD-11 criteria. Measurement invariance was established across gender (female vs. male) and age groups (emerging adults vs. adults) in separate Multigroup Confirmatory Analyses. Item Response Theory analyses showed that the scale demonstrates higher discrimination at low to moderate levels of problematic use, highlighting its sensitivity for early detection. Overall, the findings suggest that the scale is a theoretically grounded and psychometrically sound instrument for assessing problematic social media use, with potential applications in research, screening, and early intervention contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: ECG-based NSR, CHF, and ARR classification: Tradeoff between classical feature engineering and TCN-based deep features
Abstract: Accurate and efficient automatic classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for scalable cardiac monitoring and timely clinical decision making. Herein, we focus on classifying Arrhythmia (ARR), Congestive Heart Failure (CHF), and Normal Sinus Rhythm (NSR). In particular, this study compares a classical feature-based pipeline that includes time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-scale features with a modern deep feature extractor employing the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). For this, MATLAB simulations were conducted on ECG signals from the MIT-BIH database to evaluate the classification performance and quantify practical trade-offs by reporting wall-clock training times, inference latency, and hardware requirements. The results showed that the Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieved classification accuracies of 88%, 91%, and 100% for ARR vs NSR, ARR vs CHF, and NSR vs CHF, respectively, when trained and tested on the classical features. On the other hand, the TCN achieved an overall accuracy of 99.4% to distinguish between the three classes. Furthermore, the TCN yielded superior raw predictive performance but offered reduced interpretability compared with the classical feature-based pipeline, at the expense of requiring substantially greater computational resources. These results demonstrated that well-engineered classical descriptors remain competitive for low-resource deployment, while data-driven TCNs deliver higher accuracy when computational budgets permit. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Yu Y.; Zhang S.; Xu Y.; Wang P.
Title: DMJP: Diffusion and multi-model joint perturbation for enhanced facial privacy
Abstract: Face recognition technology has been adopted in public safety, social platforms, and other domains. However, unauthorized identity recognition poses privacy risks, exacerbating concerns about the misuse of personal data and thus calling for robust privacy protection methods. Current face privacy protection techniques often encounter challenges such as limited transferability or noticeable image distortion. To tackle these issues, this paper introduces DMJP, a framework that integrates Latent Diffusion Models with a multi-model joint perturbation optimization mechanism. The method encodes an input image into the latent space, applies gradient-based multi-model perturbations, and generates a protected image via Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model sampling. Gradients from multiple white-box face recognition models are combined to guide common feature manipulation, while different adversarial attack algorithms are merged to form a unified perturbation direction, enhancing transferability against black-box FR models. In addition, an adaptive perturbation strategy dynamically adjusts perturbation strength according to the diffusion timesteps and reconstruction errors, balancing protection effectiveness and image quality. Experiments on CelebA-HQ and FFHQ demonstrate a favorable trade-off between Protection Success Rate and image quality, with competitive PSNR/SSIM and substantially improved Fréchet Inception Distance. Further experiments evaluate computational efficiency through sparse injection and demonstrate target-free anonymization and robustness to preprocessing and DDIM purification. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Li W.; Liao H.; Teng M.
Title: Extreme weather and human capital formation: evidence from Qing China
Abstract: Weather shocks can constrain educational investment and human capital formation. In Qing China, education spending rose and fell with weather-sensitive farm income. Using a two-century panel (1646–1904) covering 234 prefectures, we find that a drought occurring one year before the examinations and additional droughts within the past five years reduce jinshi (the highest degree in the imperial examination system) density by approximately 6 % and 2.6 % per period, respectively. Adaptive measures such as the introduction of sweet potatoes, savings from surplus years, and flexible pricing mechanisms prove effective in mitigating drought effects. For robustness, we proxy regional recording capacity with the word count of meteorological entries and augment the baseline with controls for social unrest and epidemic shocks, with results remaining stable. By bringing long-run historical evidence to bear, this study enriches the literature on how extreme weather affects human capital formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Sun Y.; Zhang H.; Xu Z.; Guo Z.; Yuan L.; Zhang R.; Liu C.; Li T.
Title: STR-LBSN: Spatio-temporal Role-based Heterogeneous Hypergraph Embedding for location-based social networks
Abstract: Location-based social networks (LBSNs) contain rich social, spatial, and temporal information. However, most existing embedding methods overly simplify the underlying hypergraph structure, represent each user with a single static embedding, and fail to model the coupling between social relationships and mobility behaviors. To address these limitations, we propose STR-LBSN, a Spatio-temporal Role-based Heterogeneous Hypergraph Embedding framework for Location-Based Social Networks. STR-LBSN models users’ temporally evolving behavioral roles as hidden states in a Hidden Markov Model and constructs a role-centric hypergraph from the decoded role assignments. Based on this structure, STR-LBSN learns multi-role representations through biased random walks and heterogeneous sampling in cosine space, while balancing social contexts and spatio-temporal mobility patterns. Extensive experiments on seven real-world LBSN datasets demonstrate that STR-LBSN achieves the highest mean performance among twelve state-of-the-art baselines in nearly all settings. Specifically, for friend recommendation, STR-LBSN achieves substantial relative improvements across four evaluation metrics, including Precision, Recall, F1-score, and NDCG, with particularly large gains on sparse datasets. For POI recommendation and activity recommendation, it delivers average performance gains of about 5% to 30% in terms of Hit@5, Hit@10, and Hit@20. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation studies and parameter sensitivity analyses support the effectiveness of the main modeling components and examine the robustness of STR-LBSN to key hyperparameters. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Academic self-handicapping in education: reconceptualizing it as a central psychological mechanism through a systematic review
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: This study synthesizes empirical findings on academic self-handicapping (ASH) in educational contexts using a systematic literature review (SLR) of 30 articles retrieved from major international databases. The review aims to identify antecedent factors, examine the role of ASH as a psychological mechanism, and analyze its impact on academic and psychological outcomes. The findings indicate that ASH is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon shaped by the interaction of psychological, motivational, and contextual factors, including academic anxiety, low self-control, performance-avoidance orientation, weak self-regulation, and social pressure. More importantly, ASH operates as a core psychological mechanism that links antecedent variables to outcomes, functioning as a psychological bottleneck that constrains positive resources and as a risk-amplifying mechanism that intensifies negative academic and psychological consequences. Although intervention-based research remains limited, preliminary intervention evidence suggests that cognitive- and emotion-focused approaches, including CBT, REBT, and ACT, may help reduce academic self-handicapping; however, the limited number of intervention studies precludes firm comparative conclusions. This study contributes by shifting the understanding of ASH from a variable-based construct toward a process-oriented psychological mechanism within the academic system. The findings highlight the need for future research to develop contextually grounded and intervention-focused approaches that explicitly target ASH to improve students’ academic success and psychological well-being. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive

Title: Understanding conflict in protected areas: integrating justice considerations with economic perspectives
Abstract: Despite broad agreement on the urgency of sustainability transitions that protect biodiversity, conservation conflicts continue to rise. This paper examines environmental conflicts in protected areas (PAs), highlighting the overlooked link between conflict and justice. Existing frameworks often fail to distinguish between conflict manifestations and determinants, or to integrate justice theories with economic perspectives. This study provides a comprehensive review of the literature to support the analysis of PA conflicts and develops a robust framework that integrates justice considerations with the economic perspective. Conflicts are viewed as inherent to complex social–ecological systems, shaped by social relations and rights over ecosystem services. The framework is structured around three analytical axes: substance (what the conflict is about), process (how it unfolds), and relation (who is involved with-whom). It differentiates between how conflicts appear (i.e., manifestation) and what causes them (i.e., determinants), framed through distributive, procedural, and recognition justice. This perspective challenges linear assumptions that conflicts always stem from injustices, emphasizing their potential to drive institutional change. The framework offers a novel approach to assessing justice-conflict dynamics in PAs governance, providing comprehensive toolkit for promoting equitable conservation strategies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: From half-cell to heavy-duty: a critical review of MXene catalysts for PEMFC cathodes
Abstract: MXenes have emerged as promising cathode catalyst supports for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) due to their high conductivity and tunable surface chemistry. However, despite numerous reports of exceptional half-cell oxygen reduction reaction activity, MXene-based catalysts have not yet been demonstrated to translate into practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) performance, especially under combined heavy-duty automotive conditions. This review critically evaluates the gap between the rotating disk electrode and single-cell performance of Pt/MXene, MXene-carbon, non-precious, and single-atom catalysts. We systematically benchmark MEA-level metrics, peak power density under H2/air, high-current–density polarization, electrochemical surface area retention under accelerated stress tests, and Pt utilization against commercial Pt/C and heavy-duty targets. We identify key unresolved barriers: MXene oxidation under acidic and oxidative cathode conditions, nanosheet restacking-induced oxygen transport resistance, and the lack of standardized MEA validation. Finally, we provide an engineering-oriented roadmap that integrates termination engineering, hybrid architectures, and AI-assisted design to bridge the half-cell-to-heavy-duty gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Significantly enhancing the strength of aluminum while preserving excellent electrical conductivity via single-walled carbon nanotubes reinforcement
Abstract: The inherent trade-off between the strength and electrical conductivity has long constrained the development of advanced aluminum (Al) conductors, and the potential of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) to break this dilemma remains critically underexplored, largely due to their dispersion difficulties. Herein, SWCNTs reinforced Al matrix nanocomposites are fabricated via friction stir processing (FSP) and followed by hot extrusion, and the strength-electrical properties are systematically evaluated. Microstructural analysis confirmed the well dispersion of SWCNTs without micro-sized aggregations. The smaller diameter and much higher specific surface area of SWCNTs enables the formation of a greater number of clean and strong bonded interfaces with the Al matrix under the thermo-mechanical conditions of FSP, which is the key for enhancing strength and maintaining electrical conductivity of Al. As a result, the ultimate tensile strengths of the SWCNTs/Al nanocomposite reached 201.1 MPa, representing an increase of 113.0% over the unreinforced Al. Remarkably, the SWCNTs/Al nanocomposite retained a high electrical conductivity (∼62.3% IACS) and good elongation (∼12.5%). This combination of more than doubled strength with uncompromised conductivity highlights the advantage of SWCNTs over conventional CNTs reinforcements in achieving strength-electrical conductivity synergy. Our findings establish that SWCNTs, despite their processing challenges, serve as exceptionally efficient reinforcements for overcoming the long-standing strength-conductivity trade-off, positioning them as a highly promising reinforcement for next-generation high-performance Al conductors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Synthesis-structure-property-performance economic value creation relationships in biomass-derived carbon materials for hydrogen storage: Implications for green finance and sustainable development
Abstract: The transition toward a hydrogen-based economy requires innovative storage materials that simultaneously enhance hydrogen performance, promote resource efficiency, and generate long-term economic value. Biomass-derived porous materials have emerged as a promising solution by transforming abundant agricultural, forestry, and industrial biomass residues into high-value hydrogen storage media, thereby supporting the principles of the circular bioeconomy and sustainable resource management. This study examines the economic value creation potential of biomass-based hydrogen storage technologies and evaluates their implications for green finance, low-carbon investment strategies, and sustainable development. It highlights how biomass valorization reduces dependence on expensive conventional storage materials while creating new revenue streams through waste utilization, carbon reduction, and renewable energy integration. The analysis demonstrates that biomass-derived activated carbons, biochars, carbon aerogels, and hierarchical porous carbon nanostructures possess favorable physicochemical properties, including high specific surface area, tunable pore architectures, lightweight characteristics, and excellent adsorption performance, making them attractive candidates for efficient hydrogen storage systems. From an economic perspective, these technologies improve supply-chain resilience, lower production costs, stimulate rural economic development, and encourage investment in sustainable manufacturing industries. Furthermore, biomass-based hydrogen storage aligns closely with green finance mechanisms by attracting environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investments, facilitating access to green bonds and climate finance, and supporting national decarbonization policies designed to achieve net-zero emissions. The study also discusses the integration of biomass-derived storage materials within emerging hydrogen value chains, emphasizing their contribution to carbon neutrality, renewable energy storage, and energy security. Despite challenges related to commercialization, feedstock standardization, scalability, and investment uncertainty, continued advances in material engineering, policy incentives, and financial innovation are expected to accelerate industrial deployment. Overall, biomass-derived hydrogen storage represents a strategically important intersection between sustainable materials science, green finance, and circular economic development, offering significant opportunities to create environmental, economic, and social value while supporting the global transition toward resilient and sustainable energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Actionable Weather Communication Recommendations for Hard-to-Reach Populations Using Topic Modeling and Thematic Analysis
Abstract: Language barriers, geographic isolation, and limited digital access are some of the obstacles that hard-to-reach populations in the United States face when trying to access weather and climate information. These conditions restrict equitable access to the public benefits mandated by federal weather policy and public warning systems. We identified actionable, evidence-based strategies for strengthening hazard communication for these populations. We conducted topic modeling on 7,705 peer-reviewed article abstracts and an in-depth thematic analysis of 129 peer-reviewed studies documenting effective approaches for engaging groups with differentiated information needs. The thematic analysis produced four integrated recommendations: community-embedded communication, hybrid and redundant communication systems, cross-sector coordination, and inclusive and actionable communication. Across these themes, studies emphasized strategies such as mobile service delivery, low-tech communication channels, culturally specific messages, trusted messengers, and participatory design. The results show how broader federal priorities for improving forecast communication and public response can be advanced and hazard communication improved through practices validated in health and social services. When taken as a whole, these insights provide communicators, emergency managers, and legislators with scalable ways to create more resilient and inclusive hazard information systems.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Wu Y.; He Z.; Wang S.
Title: Carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS): From technology advances to carbon neutrality pathways in energy and industrial sectors
Abstract: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is critical for hard-to-abate sectors including steel, cement, chemicals, and power generation. This review systematically synthesizes recent advances across the full CCUS chain, covering emerging electrochemical and membrane-based direct air capture (DAC), AI-enhanced monitoring, verification, and risk management with digital twins, and synergistic coupling with green hydrogen and power-to-liquid synthetic fuels. Mature capture technologies and utilization pathways are assessed alongside geological storage in saline aquifers, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, and coal seams. Operational data from million-tonne demonstration projects are distilled to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial implementation. The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects CCUS playing a key role in global emissions reductions by 2050, while the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) emphasizes its critical role in ambitious climate stabilization pathways. A conceptual system integration framework is proposed to clarify the distinct roles of CCUS in energy conversion versus industrial production. Despite persistent challenges, including high costs, energy penalties, infrastructure deficits, and regulatory gaps, future directions prioritize low-energy materials, AI-driven optimization, industrial clustering, cross-border networks, and policy incentives. Through innovation and cooperation, CCUS is transitioning from demonstration to commercial-scale deployment to support global climate goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Safety concepts through a memetic lens
Abstract: Within safety practice and science there are countless ideas, approaches and concepts to manage safety. Some of these safety concepts are picked up, discussed widely and spread, while others do not. Little is known about this subject. This paper provides a unique perspective on the development and adoption of safety concepts by using an evolutionary framework to explore reasons why. As a case, this paper traces the historic development of one of safety’s most influential and iconic safety concepts, the accident triangle, over nearly a century through successive cycles of replication, variation, and selection. Knowledge of factors that influence the adoption of safety concepts can contribute to the design of more effective concepts that attract attention and of social and organisational environments that are receptive of these concepts. In the end, provided the concepts in question are useful, this can contribute to enhancing safety and reducing harm. In addition, the insights gained in this paper can help safety professionals and academics to critically reflect on the development of safety concepts, to help them better understand how safety concepts evolve and can change meaning leading to various interpretations and reflect on what this means for their own adoption of concepts and eventually their practice. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Collaborative multi-instance feature aggregation for visual privacy protection
Abstract: The rapid advancement of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) has dramatically shaped numerous domains of modern society. With the increasing emphasis on high-quality and personalized data, safeguarding visual privacy and preventing information leakage have become urgent research priorities. Traditional privacy-preserving strategies predominantly rely on isolated instance-level manipulations, such as artificial noise injection or pixel-level obfuscation, to achieve de-identification. Yet, these independent sample-level approaches inevitably face an inherent trade-off: slight alterations provide inadequate protection, whereas aggressive modifications severely distort task-relevant semantics and compromise downstream accuracy. To overcome this dilemma, we introduce a novel visual privacy protection framework driven by multi-instance feature-level aggregation. Unlike conventional methods that perturb a single isolated instance, our approach constructs anonymized representations by collaboratively aggregating identity-discriminative feature fragments drawn from multiple data instances. Instead of relying on external noise to conceal identity, this collaborative aggregation synthesizes protected data, effectively weakening the deterministic link between the original identity and the visual representation. Comprehensive experiments on diverse visual identity recognition benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework delivers superior results, achieving both robust perceptual anonymization and high downstream task utility compared with prior state-of-the-art techniques. © 2026

Title: Effects of psychosocial interventions on emotional health outcomes in parents within one year after paediatric intensive care: A systematic review and meta-analysis
Abstract: Background: Post-intensive care syndrome in paediatrics affects the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social health of children and their families. Although psychosocial interventions are increasingly advocated, evidence regarding their effects on parental emotional health after paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission remains uncertain. Objectives: To determine the effects of psychosocial interventions on emotional health outcomes in parents of critically ill children within one year after PICU discharge. Research methodology and design: This systematic review and meta-analysis included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating psychosocial interventions for parents of children admitted to a PICU. Five databases were searched from inception to January 2026. Eight RCTs were included, and all eight contributed PICU-specific data to at least one meta-analysis. Outcomes included post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, anxiety, and stress. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Setting: Studies were identified through searches of PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, and CINAHL from database inception to January 2026. Main outcome measures: Parental PTSD, depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms assessed within one year after PICU discharge. Results: Eight RCTs involving 470 participants contributed PICU-specific data to the quantitative synthesis. Psychosocial interventions were associated with small reductions in PTSD symptoms (eight studies, n = 467; SMD = −0.30, 95% CI −0.53 to −0.07, p = 0.017) and depression symptoms (seven studies, n = 448; SMD = −0.13, 95% CI −0.24 to −0.02, p = 0.029). The pooled effect on anxiety was not statistically significant (eight studies, n = 470; SMD = −0.08, 95% CI −0.28 to 0.12, p = 0.380). General stress was reported by one study and was not pooled. Conclusion: Psychosocial interventions may produce small reductions in PTSD and depression symptoms in parents after their child's PICU admission, whereas the anxiety estimate remained compatible with benefit and no effect. Interpretation is limited by the small number and size of trials, variation in intervention characteristics, and risk of bias. Implications for clinical practice: Accessible evidence-based psychoeducational support, distress screening with appropriate referral pathways, and planned follow-up may help address parental emotional distress after PICU admission. Authors: Tong K.; Xu D.; Lu X.; Wang Q.; He H.; Tan Y.; Wang H.
Title: Gut-joint axis mediates susceptibility to osteoarthritis in female adult offspring rats with prenatal caffeine exposure
Abstract: Prenatal caffeine exposure (PCE) is closely associated with the susceptibility to adult osteoarthritis, but the mechanisms underlying the gut microbiota remain unclear. In this study, the postnatal weeks (PW) 12 and 36 PCE female offspring rats showed decreased articular cartilage mass, increased modified Mankin's score, decreased matrix synthesis, elevated local inflammatory factors in articular cartilage, and increased matrix degradation. Furthermore, the gut microbiota of PCE female offspring rats was disturbed, which was primarily characterized by decreased butyric acid-producing bacteria (such as Butyricimonas and Romboutsia). The short-chain fatty acid metabolic profile also confirmed that decreased serum butyric acid levels in the PCE group were significantly correlated with the expression of essential genes of the osteoarthritis phenotype. The fecal microbiota transplantation experiment confirmed that the altered gut microbiota in PCE offspring rats induced osteoarthritis phenotype. Supplementation with sodium butyrate can alleviate the osteoarthritis phenotype caused by PCE in female adult offspring rats. © 2026

Authors: Lee J.J.; Andonopoulos V.
Title: Influencer beware: The buffering role of sponsor–influencer fit in the commercialization-authenticity trade-off
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As social media influencers (SMIs) increasingly commercialize their online presence through sponsored content, understanding how sponsorship intensity shapes consumer responses has become important. Drawing on attribution and congruence theories and the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how sponsorship levels influence audience engagement and purchase intentions through perceived personal authenticity (PPA) and whether these effects depend on sponsor–SMI fit. Three experimental studies were conducted to test the proposed relationships. The results show that higher sponsorship levels reduce consumers’ intention to follow influencers and share their content. Sponsor–SMI fit attenuates the negative effect of sponsorship intensity on PPA. Thereby mitigating its adverse effects on consumer engagement and purchase intentions. We further demonstrate that sponsorship level affects consumer responses indirectly through PPA and that this indirect effect is contingent on sponsor–SMI fit. These findings advance the influencer marketing literature by applying the ERC framework to distinguish the different authenticity types and their impact on consumer behavior. The study also extends attribution and congruence theories by explaining how and when commercialization influences consumer responses and offers practical guidance for balancing monetization and authenticity in influencer marketing. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Beyond the lecture: Creative and innovative pedagogies in management education – An integrative conceptual review
Abstract: Management education has been criticised for over-reliance on transmission-oriented pedagogies poorly suited to developing the competences contemporary business graduates require. The case for moving beyond the lecture is strengthened by generative artificial intelligence, which performs the analytical and reproductive tasks underpinning conventional assessment, shifting educational value toward judgement, situated decision-making, and reflection. This integrative conceptual review of creative and innovative pedagogies draws on literature published principally between 2013 and 2026, organising the field into six clusters: experiential and simulation-based learning; game-based and gamified approaches; arts-based methods; design-based pedagogies; problem-based learning; and student-generated multimodal artefacts. For each cluster it examines theoretical foundations, evidence strength, and implementation challenges, distinguishing outcomes with stronger evidence (engagement, motivation) from those with weaker evidence (durable transfer). Three cross-cutting themes are identified: the centrality of learner agency, the neglect of structured reflection, and institutional conservatism as a barrier to change. The review contributes a typology of creative pedagogy organised by locus of creation and mode of engagement, which is used to make explicit the trade-offs each configuration entails and where institutional conservatism constrains change, together with implications for programme design, assessment and facilitation, and a research agenda spanning longitudinal measurement, equity, programme-level integration, and generative AI. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Shahmohammadian A.; Ghafory-Ashtiany M.
Title: Navigating housing system complexity – Part II: Quantitative analysis of the Housing System Abstraction Hierarchy (HSAH)
Abstract: Housing is a key component of urban systems, playing an essential role in shaping sustainable development and enhancing the resilience of cities. To achieve adequate housing, governments must adopt a systemic, integrated perspective on the housing system's structure, considering its complex interdependencies. Part I of this two-part study (the accompanying paper) introduced the Housing System Abstraction Hierarchy (HSAH), a conceptual framework for capturing the structural complexity of housing systems. Part II quantifies the HSAH, consisting of 176 nodes and 7822 interconnected links, using advanced network analysis metrics to identify the most influential components of the housing system and their functional dependencies. The results reveal that nodes with high Eigenvector Centrality, primarily within the economic, environmental, and technical domains, represent the most structurally influential parameters, whereas governance and social-related nodes with high Betweenness Centrality act as critical bridges facilitating cross-sectoral coordination within the housing system. Understanding these leverage points and network hubs provides policymakers with targeted entry paths for improving housing outcomes and driving system-wide transformation. Furthermore, the analysis traces cascading effects and systemic vulnerabilities, demonstrating how weaknesses in lower-level functional parameters can propagate and influence the system's higher-level objectives. Finally, the study highlights key insights from the policy paper on achieving adequate housing in Iran, developed based on the HSAH analysis, offering transferable insights for other developing and rapidly urbanizing contexts worldwide. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Hu G.; Jiang Z.; Ma J.; Wang M.; Han Y.; Du W.; Qian F.
Title: Modelling, intelligent optimisation and techno-economic analysis of post-combustion carbon capture for ethylene production under variable loads
Abstract: Thermal cracking furnaces in ethylene plants are the dominant source of CO2 emissions in the petrochemical industry, making the integration of carbon capture plants critical for decarbonization. However, the coupling behaviours between the thermal cracking furnace and the capture plants, particularly under different operating conditions, pose significant challenges to system optimization. To address this, this study proposes a comprehensive integrated simulation and intelligent optimization framework for a 60 kt/yr industrial thermal cracking furnace coupled with a Monoethanolamine (MEA)-based carbon capture process. Firstly, a high-fidelity coupled thermal cracking furnace model (based on Zone Method and COILSIM1D) is established to accurately predict flue gas characteristics under varying fuel gas flowrates. Secondly, a rate-based post-combustion carbon capture plant model is developed in Aspen Plus®, validated against pilot scale experimental data from the Technology Centre Mongstad (TCM), and scaled up to match the flue gas from the industrial scale thermal cracking furnace. Genetic Algorithm (GA) is implemented in MATLAB to interact with process simulations, enabling the global optimization of energy consumption and carbon capture costs. Optimization results reveal a previously unidentified divergence between technical and economic performance: the lowest specific reboiler duty occurs at 82–84% capture level, whereas the lowest cost consistently lies at 86–90%. We demonstrate quantitatively that this 4–6 percentage point gap arises from the trade-off between the change of capital cost caused by economies of scale and the exponential rise in regeneration energy, which is established for the first time for low carbon ethylene plants—— the optimal capture level shifts towards higher values as fuel gas flowrate decreases. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang Z.; Yin Y.; Wei F.; Wu J.; Lv H.; Yang W.
Title: Psy-DMTL: Psychology-guided dynamic multi-task learning for LLM-based personality detection
Abstract: Personality detection aims to infer individuals’ psychological traits from user-generated text and has broad applications in user profiling, personalized services, and human–computer interaction. Recent LLM-based methods have shown strong potential for this task by providing rich semantic representations. However, most existing methods still face three limitations: coarse-grained long-history encoding may dilute sparse personality cues, shared user representations may entangle heterogeneous evidence across personality dimensions, and cross-dimension dependencies are often modeled implicitly without psychology-inspired structural guidance. To address these issues, we propose Psy-DMTL, a psychology-guided dynamic multi-task learning framework for LLM-based personality detection. Psy-DMTL first encodes posts independently with a frozen LLM and uses a gated hierarchical context encoder to capture user-level dependencies while preserving fine-grained cues. It then introduces orthogonal dimension-attention pooling to extract dimension-specific representations for different MBTI dimensions. Finally, a psychology-guided dynamic modulation decoder models directional cross-dimension interactions through FiLM-based feature modulation. Experiments on the Kaggle and Pandora benchmarks show that Psy-DMTL achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of average Macro-F1 on both datasets. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for long-history personality detection. Supplementary experiments on the Italian Personal-ITY dataset further support the model's competitive performance. Our model is publicly available at https://github.com/qaswzh/Psy-DMTL. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Pan S.; Zhan P.; Chen W.; Wu L.; Cai R.
Title: Causal-inspired knowledge tracing via class-conditioned latent representation learning
Abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) plays a foundational role in smart education by modeling students’ evolving knowledge states from historical learning interactions. Existing deep KT architectures predominantly mine statistical correlations from individual interaction sequences, neglecting group-level educational contexts (e.g., class). Such contextual heterogeneity forces models to rely on spurious correlations, leading to error next-response predictions. Guided by advanced educational philosophies, causality offers a principled lens to characterize the underlying data-generating process of student learning. Nevertheless, comprehensive contextual signals are inherently complex and largely latent. To bridge this gap, we propose CLR4KT, a causal-inspired plug-in framework for Class-Conditioned Latent Representation Learning in KT. CLR4KT introduces an identifiable Variational Autoencoder (iVAE) style architecture to capture the data-generating mechanism, leveraging class-level contextual information as an observed group-level conditional signal to assist in identifying and resolving the complex, latent context representations. By conditioning both the latent prior and the variational posterior on class labels, CLR4KT learns class-conditioned latent representations. These enhanced latent states are seamlessly integrated into mainstream KT backbones via temporal modeling. Extensive experiments across four benchmark datasets demonstrate that CLR4KT consistently boosts predictive capability. Ablation and visualization analyses confirm the effectiveness of class-conditioned latent representation learning module of our method. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Debiasing scene graph generation with Context-Aware Peer Networks
Abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects and infer their pairwise relationships, but long-tailed predicate distributions cause models to over-predict frequent predicates and under-recognize informative tail relations. We propose Context-Aware Peer Networks (CAPN), a plug-and-play framework for unbiased SGG. CAPN replaces a single relation predictor with multiple collaborative peers and introduces a context-aware encoder with Context-to-Peer (CPE) and Context-to-Predicate (CPR) modules. CPE adaptively weights peer contributions according to scene context, while CPR modulates predicate logits to improve context-consistent prediction and alleviate head-predicate dominance. Experiments on Visual Genome and Open Images V6 show that CAPN improves the mR-R trade-off across Motifs, VCTree, and Transformer backbones, achieving a weighted score of 45.1 on OI-V6 and a mean score of 49.0 on VG PredCls.
