Title: The impact of digital marketing on consumer attitudes and behavioural responses: The role of perceived value and financial considerations in the decision-making process
Abstract: Digital technologies influence consumers across need recognition, information search, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase activity. This study examines how six features of digitally mediated promotion—informativeness, personalisation, interactivity, entertainment, credibility, and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM)—shape attitudes and subsequent behavioural responses among Albanian consumers. It also evaluates attitude as a mediator, media literacy as a moderator, and differences across decision-journey stages. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey yielded 487 valid responses from adults residing in Albania who had recently used online channels in purchase-related activity. The conceptual model integrates the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, the Theory of Planned Behaviour, and the customer-journey perspective. Measurement and structural relationships were assessed using partial least squares structural equation modelling with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples; supplementary analyses tested mediation, moderation, age-group differences, and stage-specific effects. Results: Credibility was the strongest predictor of attitude (β = 0.291), followed by positive eWOM (β = 0.245) and informativeness (β = 0.230). Attitude positively predicted purchase intention (β = 0.597), online engagement (β = 0.467), and recommendation intention (β = 0.517), while purchase intention predicted self-reported purchasing (β = 0.553). Attitude mediated the effects of all six promotional features on purchase intention. Media literacy strengthened the informativeness–attitude relationship (β = 0.109), whereas age-group differences were not significant. Influence was greatest during information search and alternative evaluation. Conclusion: Effective online communication depends more on usefulness, credibility, and authentic social evidence than on entertainment alone. The findings extend evidence from a Southeast European setting and show that favourable attitudes translate into purchases only when perceived value, affordability, payment, and delivery conditions permit conversion. Managers should therefore combine transparent information and trustworthy reviews with financially clear offers and sustained post-purchase support. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Determinants of membrane sensitivity to the Mastoparan-1 peptide from Polybia Paulista
Source title: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
Abstract: The membrane-disrupting peptide Mastoparan-1 (MP-1), derived from the wasp Polybia paulista is known to possess antimicrobial properties, and exhibits enhanced activity against a number of cancer cell lines relative to healthy cells. Due to the mechanism of action of MP-1 it is likely that differences in plasma membrane lipid composition arising from cancer associated mutations, such as localisation of phosphatidylserine (PS) lipids to the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane, are involved in driving that enhanced activity. Rapid screening of MP-1 mutants in a combined approach using model membrane and cell-based biological assays, has led to the identification of a number of derivative peptides with enhanced selectivity for cancer-like membrane models and breast cancer cell lines and provided insights into the mechanism of membrane disruption and cell death. Notably, the morphology of the membrane perturbations observed by Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) and activity in cell model systems can change considerably in response to single-point mutations in the MP-1 sequence, indicating a complex structure-activity relationship. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Duong T.X.
Title: River tourism based on community participation and regional linkages for sustainable livelihoods: The case of Can Tho City, Vietnam
Abstract: This study examines the role of community-based river tourism and regional linkages in supporting sustainable livelihoods in Can Tho City, Vietnam. A convergent mixed-methods approach was employed, combining surveys of 385 tourists, 47 local households, and 18 tourism officials and community representatives with 36 semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), cluster analysis, and multiple regression, while qualitative data were integrated through thematic coding, triangulation, and SWOT analysis. The findings indicate that community-based river tourism contributes to livelihood diversification, income generation, skill development, and social capital formation. Participating households reported relatively high livelihood stability (mean = 3.87) and moderate government support (mean = 3.59), whereas regional linkage participation remained low (mean = 1.79). EFA results revealed a common factor linking government support, regional cooperation, and livelihood outcomes, with factor loadings ranging from -0.64 to -0.51. For tourism officials and community representatives, EFA identified two governance dimensions—regional coordination and community-enterprise synergy—which explained 84.83 of the total variance. Tourists reported high overall satisfaction (mean = 4.35), strong community interaction (mean = 4.61), positive perceptions of cultural preservation (mean = 3.71), and willingness to pay for tourism services (mean = 3.98). Regression analysis showed that cultural preservation perception was the only statistically significant predictor of tourist satisfaction ( β = 0.146, p = 0.004 ). Open-ended responses highlighted key development priorities, including reducing crowding ( 29.6 ), increasing the availability of tour guides ( 26.8 ), enhancing cultural activities ( 23.9 ), and extending tour duration ( 19.7 ). Overall, sustainable livelihood outcomes depend not only on community participation but also on effective governance, cultural preservation, and stronger regional integration. The findings provide empirical evidence and practical implications for sustainable tourism planning in riverine destinations of the Mekong Delta. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Authors: Zhang Y.; Xu H.; Li H.
Title: Toward a relational typology: Mapping social entrepreneur-resident interactions in community-led tourism social entrepreneurship
Abstract: Research on tourism social entrepreneurship has focused on exogenous models while overlooking host communities' agency. The aim of this study was to examine interactions between social entrepreneurs and residents in the context of community-led tourism social entrepreneurship. The exploratory qualitative study design involved three fieldwork phases. We used two dimensions—the initiator's primary motivation and the embeddedness forms in the responder's actions—to identify four relationship types: traditional bonding ties, instrumental ties, patron–client ties, and value-congruent alliances. The social action and embeddedness theories guided our examination of relational formation. Findings further reveal a model of power shift and relationship dynamics. This model suggests that a power shift involves three principal stages centered around dependence. In summary, we provide here a typological framework for analyzing social entrepreneur–resident interactions and offer practical insights into sustainable community development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A bibliometric review of farmer livelihood resilience in Indonesia: A two-decade study
Abstract: Farmer livelihood resilience is crucial given the sector's contribution to the national economic resilience, particularly in Indonesia. Despite its importance, a comprehensive synthesis of how this field has evolved over the past two decades remains limited. The objectives of this study are to provide an overview of the circumstances and challenges related to farmer resilience by examining research on farmer livelihood resilience in Indonesia. Employing a hybrid methodology that combines bibliometric analysis with a systematic literature review (SLR) guided by PRISMA protocols, this research analyzed 184 articles, 94 conference papers, and 2 review papers indexed in the Scopus database from 2005 to 2025. VOSviewer software was utilized to visualize co-occurrence networks and publication patterns. The results demonstrate a substantial increase in academic interest over the last decade, with a significant peak in publications after 2015. The analysis identified five dominant thematic clusters: (1) Smallholder Farmers’ Climate Change Adaptation in Indonesia; (2) Sustainable Agriculture and Land Conversion Policy; (3) Social Capital and Collective Action for Sustainable Agriculture; (4) Livelihood Strategies of Oil Palm and Agroforestry Farmers; (5) Sustainability of Palm Oil Smallholders. This study fills a critical research gap by bridging quantitative mapping with qualitative insights, offering a strategic roadmap for future scholarly inquiry. The findings emphasize that strengthening farmer resilience in Indonesia requires integrated policy frameworks that prioritize institutional support and optimized social capital. Ultimately, these results provide vital evidence for policymakers to design more inclusive and sustainable agricultural development strategies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Authors: Ma C.-X.; Peng F.-L.; Li Z.-J.; Qiao Y.-K.
Title: Spatial cognitive patterns of underground public spaces from a stimulus-organism-response perspective: evidence from LLM-empowered social media data mining
Abstract: Current underground public space (UPS) renewal prioritizes engineering-oriented physical upgrades, neglecting users’ multidimensional cognitive experiences. Existing studies on underground space perceptions rely on small-sample surveys and fail to capture joint co-occurrence patterns among multiple stimuli. This study integrated the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework with large language models to decode spatial cognitive patterns. It drew on 76,078 social media reviews from 64 UPSs in 19 Chinese cities (2005–2024). DeepSeek extracted 27 spatial stimuli and their sentiments, serving as public perceptions. Generalized ordered probit regressions showed that management quality, environmental conditions, and atmospheric experiences exhibited the strongest associations with overall ratings. Negative perceptions showed stronger negative associations with ratings than positive perceptions showed positive associations. Association rule mining uncovered co-occurrence patterns across genders, city clusters, and review periods. Dissatisfaction was associated with shorter, more concentrated patterns of negative stimuli, whereas satisfaction was associated with the co-occurrence of positive functional and experiential perceptions. Co-occurrence patterns varied markedly across organismic attributes. Males showed simpler, function-oriented networks, while females displayed more complex, multi-dimensional ones. Regional expectation thresholds differed across contexts. Temporal patterns shifted from physical defects to operational management. These findings support a cognition-driven renewal paradigm, shifting from engineering-oriented interventions to weakness prioritization, multifunctional experience design, and inclusive context-specific strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The psychology of AI-mediated communication across languages
Abstract: Communication across languages is increasingly mediated by artificial intelligence (AI). This creates opportunities for people with different language backgrounds to communicate in their respective native languages. AI-mediated communication can therefore reduce cognitive effort, disfluency, and social stigma associated with speaking a non-native language. At the same time, non-native language use influences cognitive, emotional, and social processes that go beyond the accurate transmission of meaning. By affecting these processes and introducing new cues, AI-mediated communication could also have unintended effects on communication effectiveness and social evaluations between interlocutors. We examine the conditions under which these effects may help or hinder cross-linguistic interactions and identify directions for research on the psychology of cross-linguistic communication as AI language tools become prevalent. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Beyond Technology Readiness Levels: Developing and Evaluating an Industry 5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework for Regulated Life Sciences Manufacturing
Abstract: Purpose: Regulated life sciences manufacturing organisations face increasing pressure to adopt Industry 5.0 (I5.0) innovations while maintaining patient safety, product quality, data integrity, and regulatory compliance. Existing assessment models provide useful perspectives on technical maturity, expectation dynamics, and organisational innovation capability, but do not fully assess whether an innovation is ready to progress responsibly in a regulated, multi-stakeholder environment. This paper develops an I5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework and presents a preliminary practitioner-informed evaluation of its use in regulated life sciences manufacturing. Methods: This paper uses design science research structured through the Double Diamond process. The framework was developed through literature review, advisory feedback, subject matter expert input, practitioner workshops, case-based application, surveys, and thematic analysis. Evaluation was conducted with a small, purposively selected cohort of 16 practitioners from a single educational-industry programme. Results: The framework comprises three linked tools: the Innovation Maturity Assessment, Innovation Maturity Rubric, and Innovation Readiness Levels. Across two exploratory workshops involving 16 experienced practitioners, participants reported that the framework supported clearer discussion of readiness and improved visibility of adoption risks. Title: Tuning donor–acceptor interactions via electronic modulation in Ga-doped ZnO for carbon chain growth from syngas
Abstract: Higher alcohol synthesis from syngas over conventional CuZn catalysts often encounters a trade-off between total alcohol selectivity and C2+ distribution. Here, we show that Ga-doped ZnO enables precise electronic modulation to balance donor and acceptor reactions through controlled Ga doping. Electron-deficient Znδ+ sites serve as key active centers, facilitating non-dissociative CO adsorption and CO insertion for carbon chain growth. At low doping, substitutional Ga acts as a donor, promoting C-O bond activation. At 1 mol% Ga, substitutional Ga and the resulting electron-deficient Znδ+ sites effectively balance the electron donation-acquisition relationship, achieving 63.5% liquid C2+ alcohol content. Excessive doping (13 mol%) causes Ga clustering and electron-rich states, over-dominating acceptor reactions and suppressing CO insertion. This work establishes that balancing donor–acceptor reactions via electronic modulation is key to overcoming this trade-off, offering a design principle extendable to other electronically tunable catalytic systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang J.; Kong D.
Title: Gravity-inspired key node identification in complex networks using entropy-weighted shortest path analysis
Abstract: Identifying influential nodes is an important issue in analyzing complex networks. This paper proposes Gravity-Inspired Entropy-Weighted Shortest Path Analysis (GEWSP), a multidimensional strategy for identifying influential nodes in complex networks. GEWSP can consider node interactions as gravitational forces based on the law of gravity, providing a more faithful representation of structural influence. A network weighting strategy is introduced to account for path diversity and structural heterogeneity. Meanwhile, GEWSP integrates multiple weighted shortest-path features to characterize node importance from different structural perspectives. Information entropy is then employed to adaptively determine the weight of each dimension, enabling a more balanced integration of different structural influences. In addition, GEWSP adopts a semi-local perspective by jointly considering the intrinsic properties of each node and the characteristics of its nearby neighborhoods within a predefined range. This configuration enables the model to exploit information from different structural scales without imposing substantial computational overhead. The proposed framework is evaluated on several networks by the Susceptible–Infected–Recovered (SIR) spreading model. Experimental results show that GEWSP consistently outperforms existing methods in epidemic spreading simulations. It achieves higher identification accuracy and stronger discrimination among influential nodes, demonstrating its effectiveness for key node identification in complex networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Fietz K.
Title: Do workers value formal jobs? Evidence from Brazil
Abstract: Informal employment, and the resulting lack of social insurance coverage, remains widespread in low- and middle-income countries. This paper contributes to the debate on the determinants of informality by estimating workers’ willingness to pay (WTP) for a formal job using a sample of 4997 Brazilian dependent workers. On average, workers are willing to forgo 15.1% of their wages for a signed work card, with higher WTP among formal and highly educated workers. Predicted eligibility for non-contributory social assistance lowers WTP, while predicted eligibility for contributory social insurance increases it. A simple calculation suggests that workers’ WTP may not fully offset employer contributions if passed on through lower wages. Providing additional information on formality raises WTP, but mainly among those already having a higher valuation of formality. © 2026 The Author

Title: A comprehensive review on ammonia-hydrogen synergistic combustion technology for engine applications: a utopia or still a challenge?
Abstract: Amid the global pursuit of carbon neutrality and energy transition, the decarbonization of engines has become an inevitable trend. Ammonia, featuring zero-carbon content and high hydrogen density, offers advantages such as easy storage and transport, a mature industrial chain and low cost, making it a promising alternative fuel for carbon–neutral energy systems. However, the inert combustion of pure ammonia severely limits its direct application in engines. Given the physicochemical differences between hydrogen and ammonia, blending highly reactive hydrogen can create novel combustion schemes for ammonia-hydrogen synergistic fuels. Notably, a critical gap remains between current fundamental reaction kinetics of ammonia-hydrogen systems and their engineering application in macro-scale engines. Therefore, this paper systemically reviews the latest technological advancements in ammonia-hydrogen synergistic fuels for internal combustion power systems, focusing on reaction kinetic mechanisms, mixture formation, advanced combustion mode adaptability, and emission generation and control strategies. In engineering applications, the realization of online hydrogen production through vehicle-mounted catalytic cracking is essential for establishing a single-fuel ammonia power system. New combustion methods, such as jet ignition and spark-assisted compression ignition, show great promise in improving the efficiency of ammonia-hydrogen combustion and reducing nitrogen-based emissions. However, ammonia-hydrogen combustion systems still face several challenges, including incomplete combustion mechanisms, unreliable materials in the injection and cracking systems, low catalytic cracking efficiency and the difficulty of controlling nitrogen-based emissions. In summary, ammonia-hydrogen synergistic combustion is a vital technical approach to achieving zero-carbon combustion in engines, but its commercial application necessitates continuous technological innovation and development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A trustworthy evidential transformer with linear fusion and Gram-matrix distillation for efficient optic disc and cup segmentation
Abstract: Accurate glaucoma screening relies on the vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR), but automation remains challenging. A critical trade-off between computational efficiency, segmentation accuracy, and model trustworthiness hinders clinical deployment. Vision Transformers offer global context but suffer from quadratic complexity (O(N2)), while standard Convolutional Neural Networks lack explicit mechanisms for uncertainty quantification (UQ). To bridge this gap, we propose EviG-Former (Evidential Gram Transformer), a highly efficient student network trained via Teacher-Student distillation. Our framework combines Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) with Linear Multi-Scale Token Fusion (L-MSTF). We designed an Uncertainty-Gated Feature Fusion (UGF) module that uses epistemic uncertainty to guide gradient flow, focusing on ambiguous regions like faint vessel boundaries. Additionally, Gram-Matrix Consistency Distillation ensures the lightweight student maintains topological integrity. We validated EviG-Former on RIM-ONE-r3, Drishti-GS, ORIGA, and REFUGE datasets. It achieved highly competitive Optic Cup segmentation Dice scores (0.9004, 0.9423, 0.8916, and 0.9005, respectively) when evaluated against thirteen leading baselines. Crucially, this performance requires only 0.69M parameters (up to 178× fewer than recent high-capacity networks) while sustaining real-time processing (≈60.7 FPS). Furthermore, the estimated VCDR mean absolute error falls below the 0.05 clinical threshold on three datasets. Title: Examining perceptual spillover effects in social media influencer marketing effectiveness: A PLS-SEM and fsQCA approach

Abstract: Social media influencers (SMIs) play a pertinent role in shaping brand evaluations, yet how influencer-level perceptions translate into brand-level evaluations and SMI marketing effectiveness remains unclear. Drawing on spillover effects as a theoretical lens, a two-stage quantitative approach was adopted. Results from the Stage 1 serial mediation model suggest that SMI social attractiveness is directly associated with purchase intention and indirectly associated with purchase intention through brand attitude. Contrary to prevailing assumptions, perceived SMI authenticity does not mediate the relationship between social attractiveness and purchase intention. Consistent with a spillover interpretation, perceived SMI authenticity serves as an evaluative facilitator associated with brand-level evaluations rather than directly with purchase intention. Authors: Hung H.-K.
Title: When passion breeds silence: How coworkers’ work passion elicits envy and employee silence in hospitality workplaces
Abstract: While work passion is well-studied as an intrapersonal motivational construct, its interpersonal consequences for coworkers remain underexplored. Drawing primarily on the Social Functional Theory of Emotions, we examine how employees' observed work passion functions as a social signal that elicits coworker envy and, in turn, shapes silence behaviors. Across four studies (three experiments and a multi-source dyadic field study with hotel employees), we find a robust asymmetric pattern: harmonious passion primarily elicits benign envy, which is associated with prosocial silence, whereas obsessive passion primarily elicits malicious envy, which is associated with deviant silence. Cross-path effects were weaker and less consistent across studies. An exploratory field-study finding suggests that obsessive passion may occasionally relate to benign envy, although this association did not emerge in the experiments and warrants replication. This research extends passion theory by highlighting its interpersonal signaling effects and reframes silence as a strategic emotion-regulation response. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Investigations of the cascading effect of hotel entrepreneur's optimism on employees’ work behaviors and customers evaluations in small and medium hospitality enterprises
Abstract: Given the significant proportion of small and medium hospitality enterprises (SMHEs) in the hospitality and tourism industry, this study focuses on the influential role and the power of entrepreneurs. Integrating optimism theory and social learning theory, we delineate how the entrepreneur's attributes and leadership exert a cascading effect across hierarchical levels, impacting both employees and customers. A multisource field study (248 entrepreneurs, 681 employees, and 1179 customers) shows that an entrepreneur's optimism drives adaptation to new leadership styles, i.e., e-leadership and green leadership, crucial for achieving the organization's goals regarding digital transformation and sustainability. An entrepreneur's e-leadership positively affects employees’ creative performance, while green leadership has a crossover effect on employees’ green behaviors, ultimately increasing customer satisfaction and ratings. Title: How punishment sensitivity affects delay discounting: The mediating role of functional connectivity between the left dorsal medial prefrontal cortex and right postcentral gyrus
Abstract: Punishment sensitivity refers to an individual's tendency to perceive and respond to punishment and other negative outcomes. Delay discounting refers to that an individual tends to devalue the subjective worth of future rewards as the waiting time increases. Previous findings suggest that punishment sensitivity may be related to delay discounting, but direct evidence for this association and the neural mechanisms underlying this relationship remain unclear. To address this question, we combined behavioral measurements, voxel-based morphometry (VBM), resting-state fMRI, and mediation analysis to investigate their brain-behavior mechanisms. Behaviorally, punishment sensitivity negatively correlated with delay discounting. Furthermore, VBM analysis found that the gray matter volume (GMV) of the left dorsal medial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC_L) is positively associated with punishment sensitivity, and neuroimaging results revealed that the functional connectivity between the dmPFC_L and the right postcentral gyrus (PCG_R) was positively associated with punishment sensitivity. More critically, mediation analysis showed that this functional connectivity exhibited a partial mediation with a statistical suppressor effect in the association with delay discounting. These results suggest that the functional connectivity between the dmPFC_L and PCG_R may represent a neural correlate of this association, providing new insights and a neurobiological interpretation for this association. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Federated knowledge graph-driven multimodal neuroinformatics for early diabetes-related cognitive risk prediction
Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to cognitive decline and neurodegeneration through intertwined metabolic, vascular, and neuroinflammatory mechanisms. Despite growing clinical evidence, early identification of diabetes-related cognitive risk remains challenging due to the heterogeneous, longitudinal, and distributed nature of healthcare data. Existing predictive models typically rely on centralized, static learning paradigms, which limit scalability, privacy preservation, and adaptability to evolving patient trajectories. In this paper, we propose CNEC, a Continual federated knowledge graph-driven multimodal Neuroinformatics framework for Early diabetes-related Cognitive risk prediction. CNEC integrates heterogeneous multimodal data–including EHRs, metabolic biomarkers, lifestyle factors, and IoMT signals–into a diabetes-aware knowledge graph that explicitly models metabolic, vascular, and neurocognitive interactions. A relation-aware graph neural network is employed to learn interpretable representations, while continual learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting under longitudinal data shifts. Federated learning enables privacy-preserving collaborative training across distributed healthcare institutions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CNEC consistently outperforms various baselines, achieving up to a 6.1% improvement in AUC and significantly enhanced robustness under continual updates, with less than 1.5% performance degradation in federated settings. These results indicate that CNEC provides an effective, scalable, and interpretable solution for proactive cognitive risk assessment in populations with diabetes. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: From rejection sensitivity to phubbing: Self-compassion and self-uncertainty as serial mediators and a self-compassion writing intervention
Abstract: Phubbing—attending to one's smartphone in another person's presence—is widespread, yet its dispositional and intrapersonal correlates remain poorly understood. Drawing on the cognitive-affective model of rejection sensitivity (RS) and a self-regulatory resource framework, we examined whether RS is associated with phubbing through two intrapersonal processes: reduced self-compassion and heightened self-uncertainty, operationalized as low self-concept clarity. Across three studies with Chinese university students, we combined a cross-sectional survey (Study 1, N = 1202), an experiment crossing measured high- versus low-RS groups with a social-context recall manipulation (Study 2, N = 197), and a four-week randomized self-compassion expressive-writing intervention with one-month follow-up (Study 3, N = 87 completers). In Study 1, RS was positively associated with phubbing, with statistical indirect associations via self-compassion, self-uncertainty, and their serial combination. Study 2 replicated these indirect associations and showed that social context moderated the indirect pathway through self-compassion: relative to a neutral condition, it was larger after rejection recall and smaller after acceptance recall. In Study 3, self-compassion writing, relative to neutral writing, produced larger gains in self-compassion and larger reductions in phubbing, sustained at follow-up. The findings identify intrapersonal responses to rejection as correlates of phubbing and provide preliminary evidence for a targeted writing intervention. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Fusion techniques of time frequency-based images to predict the outcome of rTMS depression therapy
Abstract: Depression is a mental condition that can lead to suicide and self-harm. Predicting the outcome of depression treatment is one of the most difficult tasks for clinicians. Among various treatment options, repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) is a widely used non-invasive method. Predicting rTMS response using Electroencephalogram (EEG) data is difficult because of high inter-subject variability and limited features from single-domain analysis. We introduce two fusion techniques, montage and blending, to overcome these limitations and extract richer features from EEG-derived Time-Frequency (TF) images. We then propose a lightweight custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on fused TF representations. We use a primary dataset of 15 patients and a secondary dataset of 46 patients. We run two sets of experiments. The first set uses segment-level 10-fold cross-validation. In this setup segments from the same patient can appear in both training and testing. The Montage CWT_ST fusion reaches 99.90% accuracy on the primary dataset and 91.90% on the secondary dataset. The second set uses strict subject-disjoint cross-validation. All segments of a patient stay in one fold and no patient appears in both training and testing. Performance collapses. We test four time–frequency methods, six fusion mechanisms, and fourteen model architectures. With one exception, every configuration on both cohorts falls between AUC 0.31 and 0.54 and every 95% confidence interval contains 0.5. A patient-level permutation test on the best standalone method returns p = 0.703. The best subject-level result is Montage CWT_ST on the primary cohort, which reaches AUC 0.874 ± 0.183 and 82.7% accuracy. The same fusion strategy on the same pair of methods reaches 0.514 on the secondary cohort, so the mechanism behind this difference is not yet established and we identify it as the main target for follow-up work. The gap between the two experimental setups is the main result. Segment-level validation raises accuracy from chance to near-perfect on this data. Similar figures in the EEG literature should therefore be read together with the fold construction used to produce them. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Enhancing Agricultural Extension Access: The Role of Different Extension Media in Climate-Vulnerable Areas of Bangladesh
Abstract: Enhancing rural productivity and resilience depends heavily on agricultural extension services, which support farmers in climate-vulnerable regions. This research examines how different farmer characteristics affect access to agricultural information through three channels: individual, group, and mass media. A cross-sectional survey of 820 farm households across the High Barind Tract and the southwest coastal and southeastern hilly regions of Bangladesh used random sampling for data collection. Researchers then analyzed the data with descriptive statistics and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) and Tobit regression models to identify determinants across the three communication channels. Age negatively influenced engagement, while farming experience enhanced contact. The majority of farmers relied on informal networks, including progressive farmers and neighbors, but showed minimal interaction with official extension agents and digital resources. Older and less-educated participants displayed restricted use of mass media. The study establishes that effective extension strategies require educational development, organizational engagement, and demographic adjustments. The successful delivery of agricultural information requires both formal service expansion and digital literacy education, as well as reinforcement of community-based learning platforms in climate-vulnerable regions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Wuwei Huanglian Wan inhibits Helicobacter pylori and alleviates associated gastritis: host metabolic remodeling and altered IL-6/STAT3 signaling
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Wuwei Huanglian Wan (WWHLW) is a traditional Tibetan medicine formula developed by Tibetan physician Takpe Pingcuo and officially documented in the Ministry of Health Drug Standards for Tibetan Medicines (Volume I, 1995). It has long been used for the treatment of gastrointestinal disorders, particularly conditions associated with gastrointestinal discomfort and inflammation. Given the overlap between its traditional indications and the clinical manifestations of H. pylori-associated gastritis (HAG), WWHLW represents a promising candidate for the management of H. pylori infection and related gastric inflammation. In addition, several constituent herbs of WWHLW have demonstrated anti-H. pylori and anti-inflammatory activities, providing a pharmacological basis for further investigating its therapeutic effects. Aim of the study: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the therapeutic effects of WWHLW against H. pylori infection and HAG, and to explore the biological processes associated with these effects through integrated multi-omics and experimental validation. Materials and methods: The therapeutic effects of WWHLW were evaluated through in vitro antibacterial assays and an H. pylori-infected mouse model. UHPLC-HRMS/MS was employed for chemical profiling and identification of serum-absorbed constituents. Serum metabolomics, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, network pharmacology analysis, molecular docking analysis, and molecular biological analyses were integrated to investigate the metabolic, microbial, and signaling changes associated with its therapeutic activity. Results: WWHLW exhibited anti-H. pylori activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of 0.2-0.5 mg/mL against both standard strains and multidrug-resistant clinical isolates. At MIC concentrations, WWHLW treatment altered the expression of multiple virulence-associated genes and reduced gastric H. pylori colonization by 93.8% in infected mice. UHPLC-HRMS/MS analysis putatively annotated 121 compounds in the WWHLW extracts, of which 10 prototype constituents were detected in serum after oral administration. Integrated metabolomics and network pharmacology analyses revealed alterations in lipid and amino acid-related metabolic pathways following WWHLW treatment. Gut microbiota analysis showed that WWHLW was associated with less pronounced alterations in microbial diversity and composition than antibiotic treatment. Correlation analysis further revealed statistical associations between microbial taxa and lipid and amino acid-related features. Experimental validation showed that WWHLW reduced inflammatory cytokine expression and suppressed STAT3 phosphorylation, consistent with altered IL-6/STAT3-related molecular changes. Conclusions: WWHLW exhibits therapeutic potential against H. pylori infection and HAG through combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory effects. The protective activity of WWHLW was associated with reduced IL-6/STAT3 signaling, providing pharmacological evidence supporting its traditional use in gastrointestinal disorders. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: From facial synchronization to social conformity: A computational analysis of emotional contagion in online co-viewing
Abstract: This study examines emotional contagion and social conformity in online co-viewing environments, where viewers can observe one another's facial expressions during shared media experiences. Using a 2 (group size: 3 vs. 8) × 3 (emotional valence: happy, neutral, mixed) between-subjects experiment, we applied deep learning–based facial expression analysis (DeepFace) to capture participants' emotional responses on a frame-by-frame basis. Emotional contagion was operationalized as frame-by-frame facial expression synchronization between participants and co-viewers. The results showed that facial expression synchronization was significantly higher in smaller groups and in the happy-valence condition, suggesting that emotional contagion occurred even without direct interpersonal interaction. Contrary to predictions based on classic conformity research, synchronization was stronger in smaller groups, indicating that visual social cues may operate differently in online co-viewing than in face-to-face settings. Time-lag analyses further showed that facial expression synchronization was strongest with no temporal delay and declined as the lag increased, suggesting that emotional contagion emerged rapidly during online co-viewing. These findings extend current understanding of emotional contagion and social conformity in video-mediated communication by showing that visually mediated emotional cues can shape shared affective responses in ways that differ from established patterns of face-to-face social influence. Methodologically, this study illustrated the usefulness of AI-based facial expression analysis for examining dynamic emotional processes during shared media experiences. The findings also provide practical implications for designing online co-viewing platforms that leverage visual social cues to enhance shared viewing experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: hnRNPU regulates the sorting of exo-miR-125a-5p in colon epithelial cells and its role in realgar-induced central nervous system toxicity
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Elucidating the mechanisms underlying realgar-induced toxicity is essential for the early prevention and treatment of arsenic-related adverse effects and for reducing the associated healthcare burden. Aim of study: Owing to its poor solubility, realgar preferentially accumulates in the intestine after oral administration. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which realgar regulates exosomal miR-125a-5p (exo-miR-125a-5p) sorting in colonic epithelial cells and to investigate the role of exo-miR-125a-5p in realgar-induced central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Materials and methods: A chronic realgar-exposed mouse model was established and combined with AAV9-mediated hnRNPU knockdown, miR-125a-5p-enriched exosome administration, and probiotic intervention. Complementary in vitro studies were performed using YAMC cells subjected to hnRNPU silencing or co-treatment with realgar and L-cysteine sulfinic acid (LCSA). Small RNA sequencing, 16S rDNA sequencing, quantitative proteomics, untargeted metabolomics, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), miRNA pull-down, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), Western blotting, and other molecular biological approaches were integrated to systematically investigate the molecular mechanism underlying realgar-regulated exo-miR-125a-5p sorting in colonic epithelial cells and its contribution to realgar-induced CNS toxicity. Results: Realgar exposure induced dose-dependent colonic injury, altered the exosomal miRNA profile of colonic epithelial cells, and significantly reduced the secretion of exo-miR-125a-5p. Mechanistically, the RNA-binding protein hnRNPU directly bound mature miR-125a-5p, enhanced its post-transcriptional stability, and promoted its nuclear retention, thereby limiting its loading into exosomes. Realgar-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis reduced the abundance of Lactobacillus and the level of its metabolite, LCSA, resulting in aberrant upregulation of hnRNPU. The consequent reduction in circulating exo-miR-125a-5p relieved repression of the STAT1 signaling pathway, leading to activation of the microglial STAT1–NLRP3 inflammasome axis and exacerbation of realgar-induced CNS toxicity. Conclusion: Realgar induces both colonic and central nervous system toxicity. Mechanistically, realgar disrupts gut microbial homeostasis, depleting Lactobacillus-derived LCSA, which promotes hnRNPU expression and enhances the nuclear retention of mature miR-125a-5p. This process suppresses miR-125a-5p sorting into exosomes, reduces circulating exo-miR-125a-5p levels, and consequently activates the microglial STAT1–NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, thereby aggravating CNS toxicity. These findings identify a previously unrecognized gut microbiota–metabolite–RNA-binding protein axis governing exosomal miRNA sorting and establish exo-miR-125a-5p as a critical mediator linking intestinal injury to neuroinflammation. This study provides new mechanistic insights into realgar-induced colonic and CNS toxicity and expands our understanding of gut–brain axis-mediated toxicological mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Teaching methods for civic and moral education in Vietnam: Implications for pre-service teacher education and competence-based pedagogy
Abstract: Civic and Moral Education (CME) is important in developing students’ moral judgement, civic responsibility, legal awareness, critical thinking, and the ability to participate in society responsibly. In Vietnam, CME is mainly embodied in the school subject of Giáo dục công dân, which is located at the intersection of moral education, citizenship education, legal education, values education and social responsibility. The competence-based General Education Curriculum of Vietnam has brought new pedagogical expectations to this subject. Instead of mainly focusing on the transmission of moral principles and legal knowledge, CME is increasingly expected to engage students in reasoning, dialogue, reflection, problem-solving and the application of civic-moral knowledge to everyday situations. This narrative literature review synthesises Vietnamese and international scholarship on pedagogical approaches relevant to CME, with particular focus on their implications for pre-service teacher education. Five main pedagogical directions are discussed: discussion-based and critical thinking-oriented learning; case-based and problem-based learning; experiential and service learning; reflective pedagogy and professional ethics education; digital pedagogy for civic participation. The literature reviewed indicates that these approaches may provide students with valuable opportunities to analyse civic-moral dilemmas, take different perspectives, link knowledge with lived experience, and take responsible action in both physical and digital communities. However, their realisation is highly dependent on the pedagogical design, dialogic facilitation, ethical judgement, reflective practice and assessment competence of teachers. In Vietnam, there is a persistent gap between competence-based curriculum expectations and teacher preparation to implement participatory and practice-oriented pedagogy. Hence, this review suggests an integrated framework for pre-service CME teacher education that links civic-moral content knowledge, pedagogical design, dialogic facilitation, experiential practice, ethical reflection, digital responsibility, and competence-based assessment. The review concludes that it is important to strengthen teacher preparation to translate curriculum reform into meaningful civic-moral learning while being sensitive to Vietnam’s cultural, institutional, and educational context. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Li Z.; Zhao Q.; Xu J.; Jiang J.; Zhang J.; Li J.
Title: Identifying key regions in spatial networks via regular hexagonal grids
Abstract: Spatially embedded complex systems are often disrupted at the regional level rather than by isolated node or edge failures, making key region identification a challenging combinatorial problem. Existing partition-based approaches either suffer from overlap and coverage trade-offs with circular regions or rely on square grids that may inadequately capture spatial influence and accessibility in real-world settings. We adopt a non-overlapping regular hexagonal grid and propose Key Region Identification with Graph Neural Networks using Regular Hexagonal Grids (KRIG-H). The framework treats each grid cell as a region node and constructs a region graph through geometric mapping between original edges and grid cells. Trained on synthetic spatial networks, KRIG-H generalizes to unseen real-world networks. Using the fraction of removed regions as a normalized evaluation scale, we compare KRIG-H with six region-centrality baselines under both hexagonal and square decompositions, with random region removal as a control. On real-world networks, KRIG-H reduces AUC by 24.88 % relative to its square counterpart, while hexagonal partitioning lowers the overall average AUC across methods by 21.77 %. Results on synthetic and real infrastructure and road networks show that KRIG-H achieves effective, robust, and transferable region-based vulnerability analysis with limited additional computational cost. © 2026

Title: Sociotechnical imaginaries and acceptance of artificial intelligence in education: A longitudinal social media analysis
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a site of public debate on social media concerning the future of education, raising broader societal questions about human behavior, judgment, and accountability. However, how educational AI is publicly interpreted and contested in everyday digital discourse is still underexplored. Addressing this gap, this study examines how AI in education is publicly discoursed through a longitudinal mixed-methods analysis of user comments responding to TED Talk videos on YouTube that circulate influential public narratives about technological and educational futures between December 2022 and November 2025. The study traces changing public orientations towards educational AI and the future visions underpinning them. Multilingual sentiment analysis reveals a fluctuating three-year trajectory, with sentiment becoming more positive in the middle period before negative sentiment rose again in 2025. Thematic analysis of the public discourse further identifies three sociotechnical imaginaries through which commenters articulate competing visions of educational futures: (1) human-centered education in an age of cognitive displacement, where concerns focus on preserving critical thinking and human judgment; (2) educational transformation through literacy, governance, and accountability; and (3) teachers as mediators of competing AI-powered educational futures. The study contributes to existing scholarship by demonstrating how acceptance and resistance toward AI in education are socially and discursively constructed through competing visions of desirable educational futures in digital public spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Rebesco P.; Akimowicz M.
Title: Know its worth? Factors affecting the social acceptability of water reuse: A mixed methods planned behavior model
Abstract: Due to strong demographic pressure, rapid urban development, and climate change, water demand is increasing while usable freshwater supplies are being depleted. The reuse of treated wastewater (RTWW) is one of the avenues currently being explored to ensure the quantitative and qualitative security of the water supply. The interests for social acceptability emerged with risk management approaches and the subsequent debates on the role of technical progress, the implementation of major development projects, and their consequences for the environment between the late 1970s and early 1980s. The purpose of this article is to identify the factors that influence the building of RTWW acceptability. This study was carried out in southern France. It combines a quantitative survey on behavior related to engaging in RTWW, based on Ajzen's theory of planned behavior, with a qualitative socioeconomic study aimed at understanding representations and beliefs regarding RTWW. The findings show that a lack of knowledge about RTWW and the implementation of only a few RTWW projects result in a normative gap and a perceived lack of control. In addition, trust in managers and public authorities, the quality of treatments, as well as risks perceptions – particularly those relating to health – significantly influence intentions to engage in RTWW. Lastly, several factors such as emotions, types of uses, and environmental awareness play an underlying role by helping build perceptions of water reuse, trust in relevant stakeholders, and more accurate perceptions of risks. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Assessing the viability of urban rooftop photovoltaic systems under new regulatory frameworks in Brazil via an evolutionary real options approach
Abstract: The transition towards decentralized and sustainable urban energy systems requires robust decision-making frameworks that account for policy changes, market uncertainties, and investment flexibility. This study applies an Evolutionary Real Options Approach (EROA) to evaluate the economic viability of residential photovoltaic (PV) systems in Brazil under the New Mark of Distributed Generation (NMDG), a regulatory change that alters incentives for net metering. By incorporating stochastic volatility models, such as the Heston model and Geometric Brownian motion (GBM) with jumps, this work quantifies the impact of regulatory changes on investment timing and system sizing decisions. Results indicate a significant reduction in financial returns and a delay in investment decisions under the new regulation. The introduction of the new regulation has led to reductions in returns of approximately 18% and 23% for the Heston and GBM with jumps models, respectively. In terms of decision sequences, the Heston model presents increased opportunities for phased investment due to its greater flexibility. On the other hand, the GBM with jumps model encourages immediate investment in a complete solar system. The new regulation results in a delay of 6 to 12 months at entry points, regardless of the chosen model. These findings contribute to the understanding of urban energy transitions, policy impacts on decentralized generation, and investment dynamics in sustainable urban infrastructure. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Lean limit extension Aspects of gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine with hydrogen fraction
Abstract: An experimental investigation was conducted on a spark-ignition gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine equipped with hydrogen port fuel injection (PFI) to investigate the effects of hydrogen enrichment on combustion characteristics, thermal efficiency, and exhaust emissions under lean-burn operation. Gasoline–hydrogen blends with different hydrogen mass fractions were tested at varying equivalence ratios, while spark timing was adjusted between 14° and 35° bTDC to compensate for hydrogen’s higher flame speed. The results showed that hydrogen addition accelerated combustion, shortened combustion duration, and significantly extended the lean operating limit. However, hydrogen enrichment generally increased nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions because of higher in-cylinder combustion temperatures. Under homogeneous combustion conditions, hydrogen was supplied through port fuel injection (PFI) in the intake manifold with a start of injection (SOI) of 210° during the suction stroke, while the gasoline direct injection (GDI) SOI was set at 330° during the engine suction stroke. With a spark timing of 22° bTDC, 5.17% hydrogen by mass fraction reduced nitric oxide emissions by 0.29 g/kW-h and improved the hydrocarbon–NOx emission trade-off. Stable engine operation was achieved at an equivalence ratio of 0.55. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Parreño E.B.
Title: The Filipino attitudinal framework for academic success and well-being: Exploring the role of attitudes toward lesbians and gay men and social interest on psychological well-being and perceived academic performance
Abstract: Extant knowledge has established associations among the psychological constructs attitudes toward lesbians and gay men (ATLG), social interest (SI), psychological well-being (PW), and perceived academic performance (PAP). However, these studies for the most part have been compartmentalized. Very few, if not none, have explored the plausible complexity underlying the interactions among these constructs. Using a correlational cross-sectional research design covering 932 students (between 16 to 26 years old) in a public university, I hypothesized that ATLG, SI, and PW interact to play an enabling role in the pursuit of academic excellence. I likewise hypothesized that sex (SE), sexual orientation (SO), gender identity (GI), and gender expression (GE) as possessing moderating effects on ATLG and SI. A structural equation model (SEM) on the interaction of all of the aforementioned variables was posited. The results of the SEM revealed that ATLG and SI are directly associated to PW and PAP. Moreover, PW mediates the relationship between ATLG and PAP, and that of SI and PAP. However, SE, SO, GI, and GE were found to have no moderating effects on ATLG and SI. Likewise, SI does not mediate the relationship between ATLG and PW, and that of ATLG and PAP. Consequently, a proposed model is derived, referred to as Parreño’s Filipino Attitudinal Framework for Academic Success and Well-being or PAFIFAB, with model fit indices APC = 0.199, P < 0.001 and ARS = 0.136, P < 0.001. The present study contributes to integrative theory building as it underscores the importance of employing a gendered lens and having progressive attitudes and compassion in achieving positive mental and academic outcomes, thus allowing academic institutions to bring to fruition the global mandate of promoting well-being, advocating gender equality, and advancing quality education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Hoang Q.
Title: Factors influencing language choice of the Chơ Ro ethnic minority in Southern Vietnam: A socio-structural analysis
Abstract: This study examines the structural and socio-psychological factors shaping the language choice of the Chơ Ro— an indigenous community of fewer than 30,000 members in Southeast Vietnam—to identify the determinants of linguistic persistence amidst rapid industrial expansion. In the context of industrialization in Vietnam, ethnic minority communities navigate significant challenges related to language maintenance. This paper argues that Chơ Ro language choice reflects a phenomenon of language persistence, in which internal cultural motivations and communal networks function as determinants against the pressures of language shift. Utilizing a convergent mixed-methods design, the study analyzed quantitative data from 472 bilingual participants in Dong Nai, triangulated with qualitative data from 30 semi-structured interviews conducted with village elders and cultural custodians. The regression model yielded an adjusted R2 of.862, indicating that the independent variables account for 86.2% of the variance in language choice. Results indicate a predictive hierarchy: Cultural motivation (CM) emerged as a determinant predictor (β = 0.271, p < 0.001), followed by Endogamous social networks (ESN) (β = 0.225, p < 0.001) and Domain functional expansion (DFE) (β = 0.195, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that the Chơ Ro language remains a functional medium in domestic and communal domains, supported by Intergenerational Transmission Strength (ITS) (β = 0.171) and Institutional Support (IS) (β = 0.166). Qualitative themes reinforce these results, identifying a gendered buffering mechanism where domestic socialization counteracts external industrial pressures. This research provides an empirical framework for policy interventions aimed at addressing ethnolinguistic vitality through the reinforcement of community-based linguistic assets. By documenting the resilience of a small-scale minority, the study contributes to a comparative theory of bilingualism in urbanizing contexts, emphasizing that internal conviction and communal structures are necessary to mitigate linguistic attrition in high-density economic zones. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: A novel tetrafluoroborate with giant birefringence assembled from biocompatible adenine
Abstract: Birefringent crystals with large optical anisotropy are indispensable for the achievement of optical devices miniaturization. Due to structural diversity, organic-inorganic hybrid crystals have emerged as promising platforms for modulating birefringence. However, achieving ultraviolet (UV) transparency and large birefringence simultaneously still remains a challenge due to intrinsic trade-off. Herein, a strategy that combines a biocompatible planar π-conjugated cation with non π-conjugated anion is proposed. Adenine (ADE, C5H5N5) is employed as a new birefringence-active unit and assembled with tetrafluoroborate [BF4]− anions, yielding a new fluoroborate crystal (C5H6N5)BF4 (ADE-BF4). The anhydrous two-dimensional structure, sustained by intermolecular hydrogen bonding and π-π interactions, endows ADE-BF4 with high thermal stability up to 213 °C. It features a giant birefringence of 0.439@546 nm, and the limited electron delocalization of ADE and [BF4]− endows it with a wide transparency range extending into the UV region (cutoff edge at 289 nm). Theoretical calculations disclose that the coplanarity of the planar ADE moieties contribute to the significantly enhanced birefringence. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Chen J.; Wang S.; Ke W.; Zhang J.
Title: When culture speaks through E-commerce chatbots: How collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles shape impulsive buying
Abstract: E-commerce chatbots increasingly provide product advice during online shopping, yet it remains unclear how culturally framed recommendation language shapes impulsive buying. Drawing on cultural dimensions theory, cultural priming theory, and constructivist interpretation, this study conceptualizes collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles as message-level cultural language cues rather than as measures of consumers’ stable cultural orientation. Across four experiments with 880 participants, we show that a collectivistic persuasive style increases impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as socially supported and behaviorally acceptable choices, which strengthens social conformity. By contrast, an individualistic persuasive style reduces impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as choices requiring confirmation against personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit, which strengthens self-referencing. The findings further identify two boundary conditions. Human labeling strengthens the collectivistic pathway through social conformity by making group-oriented language more likely to be treated as socially relevant advice, whereas AI labeling shifts source perception toward algorithmic advice and strengthens the individualistic pathway through self-referencing by increasing attention to personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit. Low algorithm accessibility strengthens the collectivistic pathway, whereas high algorithm accessibility strengthens the individualistic pathway. These findings show that chatbot recommendations do more than transmit product information. They shape how consumers interpret the perceived source, social relevance, and personal applicability of recommendations, thereby influencing whether recommendations are quickly accepted as purchase decisions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: High-performance thin film nanocomposite membrane prepared from 2D ZIF-67 nanosheets and Pebax for natural gas dehydration
Abstract: Thin film nanocomposites (TFNs) fabricated with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are considered as promising alternatives for natural gas (NG) dehydration. However, it remains difficult to realize both high water permeance and selectivity at the same time. The ultrathin selective layer of the TFN structure inherently provides higher permeance than traditional membranes. In this research, TFN membranes were fabricated via incorporating ultrathin ZIF-67 nanosheets into a Pebax 1657 polymer matrix with polyacrylonitrile (PAN) porous support. The 2D ZIF-67, characterized by their leaf-like morphology, create well-defined molecular sieving channels while maintaining excellent interfacial compatibility. A key innovation of this work is the achievement of exceptionally high separation performance. The optimized membrane with 12.5 wt% ZIF-67 loading demonstrated exceptional separation capabilities, a remarkable 38,356 GPU in water vapor permeation along with H2O/CH4 separation factor of 18,235 was documented, which surpasses most reported membranes for NG dehydration. The synthesized membranes also exhibited exceptional stability of 10 days. This work demonstrates that 2D MOF nanosheets can overcome the typical permeability-selectivity trade-off, advancing membrane based NG dehydration toward practical applications. Copyright © 2026. Title: Mapping the Global Technology Landscape and Dynamic Evolution of Artificial Intelligence-assisted Drug R&D Based on Patent Analysis
Abstract: Purpose: This study investigates the global development trajectory, thematic evolution, and technological life cycle of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled drug research and development (R&D). It aims to clarify the evolutionary trajectory of the field, the leading countries and technological domains, and the current life cycle stage of the technology. Methods: Drawing on global patent data, the study integrates bibliometric analysis, social network analysis (SNA), technology life cycle (TLC) modeling, and a cross-time Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model. A Logistic growth model is applied to estimate developmental stages and long-term saturation, while cross-time LDA identifies major technological themes and their temporal evolution. Results: Patent activity has increased sharply since 2013. The United States (40.19%) and China (32.20%) dominate global filings, with China surpassing the U.S. in annual applications by 2022–2023. India has emerged as a rapidly growing contributor. TLC analysis suggests the technology entered the growth stage in 2022 and is projected to mature around 2030, with a projected saturation of approximately 21,875 patents by 2048. Topic modeling identifies 19 themes, with dominant areas including therapeutic use prediction, physicochemical modeling, retrosynthesis prediction, multitarget drug design, and personalized medicine. The technological focus has shifted from early computer-aided design to deep learning and clinical optimization. Conclusion: The findings reflect accelerating technological convergence between AI methods and pharmaceutical innovation, pointing to strong long-term growth potential. The quantitative TLC staging and cross-time LDA provide descriptive insights that may support strategic R&D planning, investment prioritization, and policy formulation. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: The rise of religious influencers and their impact on social communication in Asia: A systematic review of Da’wah, preaching, and public discourse
Abstract: This systematic review examines how digital platform ecosystems have reshaped Islamic da’wah, contemporary preaching practices, and public-facing religious engagement in Asian contexts through the growing prominence of online faith-based opinion leaders. The review synthesizes studies indexed in Scopus covering the period 2020–2025. Using a qualitative thematic synthesis approach, the article analyzes recurring patterns related to authority transformation, platform-specific communication strategies, credibility and authenticity, youth engagement, religious moderation, gender participation, ethical risks, media literacy, and institutional adaptation. The findings show that religious authority in digital environments is increasingly negotiated through visibility, engagement, relatability, and algorithmic circulation rather than through formal institutional credentials alone. Religious communicators successfully expand access to religious learning by adopting short-form video, live interaction, collaborative content, and personalized storytelling, particularly for younger audiences. At the same time, the review identifies substantial risks, including interpretive oversimplification, misinformation, commercialization pressures, gendered constraints on legitimacy, and the amplification of polarizing content by platform logics. The study further demonstrates that sustainable digital religious communication requires hybrid governance arrangements that combine theological stewardship, operational content standards, media literacy interventions, and strategic collaboration between scholars, institutions, and digital communicators. Overall, the review highlights that the digitization of da’wah is not merely a technological shift, but a structural transformation in how religious authority, trust, and public moral discourse are produced, circulated, and contested across Asian societies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Flexible ambition: How to make bold first offers without backlash
Abstract: One of the most vexing dilemmas negotiators experience is whether to make the first offer—and how ambitiously to do so. Although research finds that ambitious first offers lead to better outcomes on average, they can also incite extreme boomerang counteroffers, impasses, and resentment. We call these countervailing effects the first-offer double bind: Modest first offers produce poor economic outcomes, but ambitious first offers risk economic and relational backlash. To overcome the first-offer double bind, negotiators need to present their ambitious first offer in ways that invite conciliatory rather than competitive reactions. In this article, we introduce a generalizable solution to the first-offer double-bind: present ambitious first offers that signal flexibility. We highlight several strategies for producing flexible ambition: (a) frame ambitious proposals as offers vs. requests, (b) highlight how one's ambitious offer benefits the other side vs. oneself, (c) propose an ambitious range vs. point value, and (d) present ambitious multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (MESOs) vs. a single package offer. Each strategy preserves or strengthens the first-offer anchor, tethering counteroffers to the first offer, while guiding receivers to see ambitious offerers as less aggressive and more cooperative. We close by considering two research frontiers. First, we propose that the flexible ambition approach can mitigate other double binds more broadly, including the gender, social class, and low-power double binds; preliminary evidence suggests that MESOs work equally well for high and low power negotiators and for men and women. Second, we explore how ambitious and flexible first offers should be. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Development of an immersion-type hydrogel-integrated microfluidic glass fiber-based analytical device and its application to smartphone-assisted glucose colorimetric assay
Abstract: Microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs) are attractive platforms for on-site analysis; however, quantitative analysis remains challenging because sampling strongly influences analytical performance. Existing sampling methods often require precise volumetric sampling or operator-dependent handling, which involves an inherent trade-off between analytical simplicity and quantitative reliability. To overcome this limitation, herein, we propose the concept of a quantitative assay using an immersion-type hydrogel-integrated microfluidics glass fiber-based analytical device (IHμGFAD). The IHμGFAD consisted of a reagent-encapsulated hydrogel for reaction/detection with a glass fiber channel for sampling. The combination of the hydrogel with the glass fiber channel was realized by exploiting the self-adhesive property of hydrophobic patterns fabricated using a liquid crystal display 3D printer. The immersion-based quantitative assay using the IHμGFAD was demonstrated with a glucose oxidase/horseradish peroxidase-based glucose colorimetric assay as a model system. The limit of glucose detection (3σ) was estimated to be 68 μM. Title: Platform abandonment through push–pull–mooring: Trust, commitment, and generational patterns in U.S. social media
Abstract: Generational frameworks frequently explain platform adoption, but rarely platform abandonment. Through a stratified survey of 990 U.S. adults, this study examines how age cohorts (digital natives vs. digital immigrants) respond to platform change and what predicts abandonment across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, and TikTok. Using the push-pull-mooring (PPM) framework, we found that cohort labels did not predict exit in pooled models. Distrust was the strongest pooled push predictor. Affective and normative commitment reduced abandonment odds, whereas need-based commitment increased them. Generation did, however, structure post-exit destinations: among Twitter/X leavers, digital natives were more likely to name Instagram and TikTok, and older cohorts were more likely to name Facebook. Abandonment is better explained by institutional distrust and multidimensional attachment than by cohort labels, but generation remains consequential for where users go next. Title: Hierarchical diagnosis and operating-condition tracing of energy-efficiency abnormalities in crude oil distillation units
Abstract: Dynamic energy-efficiency abnormalities in crude oil distillation unit (CDU) are difficult to diagnose because process variables are strongly coupled and abnormal operating conditions may affect multiple process sections. This study develops a hierarchical diagnostic framework that progressively narrows the diagnostic scope from process-level abnormality monitoring to process-section localization and finally to operating-condition tracing. First, slow feature analysis (SFA) is employed to monitor the dynamic energy-efficiency state and detect deviations from normal operation. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is then used for process-section classification to narrow the diagnostic scope to a specific process section. Subsequently, a convolutionally encoded heat-map strategy based on sliding-window feature extraction is applied to characterize temporal deviations among variables within the localized section and trace the associated abnormal operating condition. Eight abnormal operating conditions are simulated for the CDU, with 2400 samples generated for each condition at a 2-min sampling interval. Using 21 selected process variables, the CNN achieves average precision, recall, and F1 scores of 99.84 %, 99.90 %, and 99.87 %, respectively, under the reported experimental setting. SFA achieves an average recall of 99.54 %, a false-positive rate of 0.39 %, and a fault detection delay of 7 min, compared with 98.79 %, 2.26 %, and 15.25 min for PCA. Two industrial operating cases are further analyzed to examine the practical applicability of the proposed diagnostic workflow. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework for hierarchical energy-efficiency abnormality detection and operating-condition tracing in CDU processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Lin K.; Coutellier L.
Title: Impact of parvalbumin interneuron inhibition during adolescence on social behaviors
Abstract: Adolescence is an important period for the maturation of prefrontal circuits and the complex behaviors it regulates, including social interactions. A major component of this developmental process is the maturation of parvalbumin-expressing (PV) interneurons, which regulate excitation-inhibition balance and contribute to the refinement of cortical networks. Although PV neurons have been implicated in social behaviors, their role during adolescence in shaping social behavior development remains unclear. To address this question, we chemogenetically inhibited prefrontal PV interneurons in male and female mice during either adolescence or adulthood and assessed long-term changes in PV network characteristics and social behavior. Adolescent PV inhibition produced persistent reductions in detectable PV neurons and increased PNN labeling surrounding PV cells, as well as reduced social motivation in males following prolonged food deprivation. In contrast, adult inhibition did not alter detectable PV neurons or PNN association, but reduced cFos expression in PV-targeted cells in the prelimbic cortex in response to a social interaction and produced changes in female social interaction patterns and sex-dependent changes in anxiety-like behavior. These findings suggest that PV interneuron activity contributes to the regulation of prefrontal inhibitory circuitry and social behavior, with disruption during adolescence producing lasting changes in PV network characteristics and social motivation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Incentivizing continuous personal health data sharing: A multidimensional contract model incorporating privacy concerns and health service needs
Abstract: Sustained health data sharing provides a critical foundation for digital health platforms to deliver proactive health management and personalized services. However, the multidimensional heterogeneity of users in terms of healthcare needs and privacy concerns, together with behavioral biases arising from platform bounded rationality, poses substantial challenges to the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. This study develops an incentive contract comprising a data-sharing duration and a task-based reward. Under the assumption that user types are unobservable, we derive the optimal contracts for two alternative objectives: platform profit maximization and social welfare maximization. We further incorporate reference dependence and loss aversion to characterize platform behavioral biases and compare the resulting contracts under expected utility theory and prospect theory. The results show that user heterogeneity, platform governance objectives, and boundedly rational behavior jointly shape the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. First, this study identifies how multidimensional user heterogeneity can be characterized and screened under information asymmetry. The marginal rate of substitution between users’ demand for health services and their privacy concerns enables the platform to map multidimensional user attributes onto a unified type ordering and induce self-selection through a differentiated menu of contracts. Second, the findings reveal the role of platform governance objectives in shaping incentive mechanisms. Profit maximization and social welfare maximization follow distinct resource-allocation logics, thereby generating different data-sharing durations, task-based rewards, and welfare-distribution structures. Third, this study uncovers the mechanism through which platform bounded rationality affects contract design. Loss aversion does not invariably strengthen or weaken incentives, rather, its effect varies with the platform’s governance objective. Under a profit-oriented objective, loss aversion may lead to an expansion of the incentive contract, whereas under a welfare-oriented objective, it tends to result in a more restrictive contract. Numerical analyses and robustness checks provide further support for these theoretical findings. By examining the information, governance, and behavioral mechanisms underlying incentive design, this study explains how incentives for sustained health data sharing are formed. It enriches the literature on incentive mechanism design for digital health platforms and provides theoretical guidance for platform governance and incentive decisions under information asymmetry and bounded rationality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: HyFora: Hyperspherical representation and frustration quantification for community structure discovery in complex information networks
Abstract: Complex information networks encode rich associative structural information about group organization, cross-group interactions, and information diffusion, making community structure discovery an important task in information science. However, existing methods mostly rely on Euclidean proximity or local structural features, making it difficult to balance global community separation with local relational consistency measurement. To address this issue, this paper proposes HyFora, a hyperspherical frustration-aware framework for community structure discovery in complex information networks. HyFora first constructs a background-corrected relation operator to distinguish community-relevant structural deviations from degree-driven connectivity patterns. Based on this operator, node relations are represented on the unit hypersphere, where directional consistency and angular separation jointly characterize intra-community cohesion and inter-community distinction. HyFora further quantifies the mismatch between local relations and global community organization as structural frustration, providing an interpretable consistency measure for community readout and boundary-node analysis. Experimental results show that HyFora achieves maximum relative improvements of approximately 21.2%, 27.3%, 15.4%, and 14.0% in terms of NMI, ARI, ACC, and modularity Q[jls-end-space/], respectively, while ablation, sensitivity, and node-ranking analyses verify the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed components.
