Title: Hydrogen production from municipal solid waste via oxygen–steam gasification for a Riyadh application: process simulation, sensitivity analysis, and techno-economic screening
Abstract: This study develops an Aspen Plus thermodynamic screening framework for hydrogen production from municipal solid waste (MSW) in a Riyadh application through oxygen–steam gasification, staged water–gas shift (WGS), surrogate contaminant removal, and surrogate pressure swing adsorption (PSA). MSW was represented on an as-received basis using literature-derived proximate and ultimate analyses. Gasification was modeled using an equilibrium reactor coupled adiabatically to decomposition, with the industrial-purity oxidant flow solved for the target temperature. The 100 kg h−1 reference case produced 6.775 kg h−1 of product hydrogen (67.75 kg H2 per metric ton of as-received MSW). Hydrogen production decreased across the 10–60 kg h−1 steam sweep at 900 °C. Response-surface analysis of 15 distinct simulations ranked 25 kg h−1 steam, an 800 °C gasifier temperature, and a 180 °C low-temperature WGS temperature highest within the studied domain; two cases excluded from regression showed interpolation errors below 0.074 %. A comparison case at 27 kg h−1 steam, 800 °C and 180 °C (Case A) produced 7.083 kg h−1 hydrogen, with specific compressor work of 5.911 kWh kg-H2−1 and an oxidant demand of 36.841 kg h−1. A 1200 °C refuse-derived fuel benchmark with reconstructed steam input reproduced four major wet-gas fractions within 0.76 percentage points. Two fluidized-bed comparisons at 850 °C showed substantial departures in gas ratios, and hydrogen yields at 800–900 °C remain unvalidated. Under three capital scenarios, the preliminary minimum hydrogen selling price for Case A was US$4.10–5.51 kg-H2−1. The results define conditional operating trade-offs and priorities for local feed characterization, kinetic, separation, heat-integration, and equipment-level studies. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Uncovering heterogeneity in students’ metacognitive ability within social-emotional learning: A rasch measurement analysis
Abstract: This study aims to uncover the heterogeneity of students' metacognitive ability within the framework of Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) using the Rasch measurement model. While previous studies have tended to treat metacognitive ability as a homogeneous construct, limited attention has been given to latent individual variability through modern psychometric approaches. This study employed a descriptive quantitative design involving 536 secondary school students in Bali, Indonesia. Data were collected using a metacognitive ability scale and analyzed using the Rasch Rating Scale Model to estimate individual abilities and item difficulty on a common logit scale. In addition to person and item calibration, the analysis included reliability indices, rating scale diagnostics, principal component analysis of residuals, differential item functioning by gender, and person-item mapping through the Wright Map. The findings indicate that students' metacognitive ability is heterogeneously distributed and forms multiple distinct ability strata. The instrument demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and was capable of differentiating levels of student ability meaningfully. Visualization through the Wright Map shows that student abilities are continuously distributed from low to high levels, without clustering in a single category. Furthermore, some students exhibited ability levels that exceeded the difficulty of most items, suggesting the need to develop more challenging items to enhance measurement precision. This heterogeneity may reflect variations in self-regulation development, learning experiences, and socio-emotional factors. In addition, some observable gender-related patterns emerged, although these tendencies should be interpreted cautiously and within their sociocultural context. Overall, the findings highlight the contribution of Rasch measurement in revealing latent variations that are often obscured by aggregate scores and provide empirical support for differentiated learning strategies aimed at fostering reflective, autonomous, and adaptive learners. Title: Designing the future of consciousness: A components framework and speculative implications
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: As technologies increasingly converge with users’ psychophysiology and mental states, perception and mind-altering are emerging as plausibly designable components of user experience. This gives rise to emergent phenomena of digitally induced altered states of consciousness (DIAL) that find application not only in therapeutic and mental health contexts but also in communication and leisure. Modern consciousness-altering technologies primarily exist as early prototypes, and their empirical research tends to constrain the context of use to instrumental functionality. Fictional narrative analysis proposes to push these limitations by considering concepts of technology in imaginary contexts, thereby examining the experiences, social rituals, and ethical issues associated with their use far beyond traditional technical scenarios. This article employs a reflexive thematic analysis of popular science fiction narratives to expand our understanding of how ASCs are integrated into HCI, considering broader sociocultural and sociotechnical contexts. As a result, we identify key aspects of interaction (purpose and context) and combine their subcategories into a framework that facilitates rethinking traditional HCI, revealing potentials that remain inaccessible within clear consciousness. This framework was used to construct five themes, highlighting that the benefits of mitigating cognitive load and deepening technology-mediated communication with DIAL might entail sacrificing identity and autonomy and increasing the pressures of the modern, overcompetitive, hyper-individualistic lifestyle. Thus, the article contributes to the HCI agenda by expanding existing paradigms of interaction with mind-altering technologies and by demonstrating the use of science fiction as a powerful avenue for exploring the design space and critical inquiries about these types of interactions. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Yi H.; Ding L.; Yang R.; Guo C.; Zhang B.; Li M.
Title: HeRaKT: Heterogeneous bidirectional modeling for response-aware knowledge tracing
Abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) aims to predict future performance of learners by modeling the evolving knowledge states from historical interactions. Existing methods typically do not distinguish the semantic roles of responses and encode them in a unified structure, thereby overlooking the heterogeneous semantics between correct and incorrect interactions. In this paper, we conduct empirical analyses revealing that responses with the same correctness label as the prediction target contribute positively to performance, whereas those of the opposite type introduce semantic noise. Motivated by this finding, we propose a novel Heterogeneous bidirectional modeling framework for Response-aware Knowledge Tracing (HeRaKT). To explore the underutilized semantic heterogeneity of learner responses, we design a path-separated architecture for handling heterogeneous signals with distinct inductive biases. To further enrich each path with broader bidirectional response-level signals, we devise a cloze-style training strategy which aggregates both past and future responses without label leakage. Extensive experiments on multiple public KT benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, validating the importance of explicitly modeling response heterogeneity and leveraging bidirectional response contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Renewable energy infrastructure in desert-gobi-arid zones: A review of physical-ecological transformations and ecosystem resilience
Abstract: Desert-Gobi-Arid (DGA) zones are key regions for large-scale photovoltaic and wind-energy development and represent fragile dryland ecosystems with strong water limitation and slow ecological recovery. This paper critically reviews the ecological impacts of renewable-energy infrastructure in DGA-type landscapes, using China’s DGA bases as the main empirical context and evidence from ecologically comparable drylands for comparison. It examines how photovoltaic and wind facilities affect surface environments, ecological processes, and carbon cycling. Existing studies indicate that these facilities influence local microclimate, soil conditions, vegetation dynamics, and carbon exchange through shading, surface disturbance, airflow alteration, and hydrothermal redistribution. These impacts are site- and scale-dependent and are jointly controlled by facility layout, disturbance intensity, surface substrate, vegetation background, climate conditions, and management practices. Under low-disturbance design and effective management, they may support soil moisture retention, vegetation recovery, soil carbon accumulation, and ecosystem resilience, while higher disturbance may increase ecological risks such as water stress and habitat fragmentation. This review links direct emission reductions with indirect ecological effects and governance considerations and provides a case-based reference for assessing renewable-energy development in fragile dryland environments. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Music in early childhood: Perception, action, and social experience
Abstract: Research on early musical development has expanded beyond perceptual abilities to encompass movement, social interaction, and broader developmental processes. This Opinion article highlights three themes that illustrate this evolution: the relation between rhythm perception and movement, the role of music in caregiver–child interaction and social communication, and the developmental significance of active musical engagement. Authors: Li C.; Xi Z.; Yu B.; Yu X.; Wang H.; Dong R.; Zhao S.; Yang S.
Title: Dynamic temporal modeling and distribution-calibrated fusion for multimodal sentiment analysis
Abstract: Existing multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) methods still lack dynamic modeling of unstable emotional information. Emotional expressions in audio and visual modalities often exhibit different temporal rhythms, while most existing recurrent state update mechanisms propagate hidden states at fixed temporal progression scales. In addition, some cross-modal associations merely reflect statistical co-occurrence patterns, and such incidental correlations do not always correspond to genuine emotional dependencies. Moreover, the reliability and contribution of each modality may dynamically vary across real-world scenarios. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multimodal sentiment analysis framework based on dynamic temporal modeling and distribution-calibrated fusion. Specifically, adaptive temporal modeling is performed on audio and visual sequences through dynamic temporal granularity selection, enabling the model to capture both short-term emotional fluctuations and long-range emotional dependencies while estimating temporal confidence. Furthermore, Gaussian distribution modeling and perturbation consistency constraints are introduced to characterize uncertainty in modality representations, thereby preventing over-reliance on unreliable associations during fusion. Temporal confidence and distributional uncertainty are further combined into a unified modality confidence, which dynamically regulates cross-modal fusion and representation alignment to improve semantic consistency of fused representations. Experimental results on the CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Extending the operating range of HCCI engines with the rhombic drive mechanism: A novel concept
Abstract: Homogeneous charge compression ignition (HCCI) engines offer high thermal efficiency and very low nitrogen oxides (NOx) and soot emissions, but they have significant challenges such as a limited operating range, knocking at high loads, and misfiring at low loads. In this study, the use of a rhombic drive mechanism as an alternative to the conventional crankshaft mechanism was numerically investigated for the first time to extend the operating range of HCCI engines. A total of 301 computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed using CONVERGE CFD, employing an HCCI engine model validated with experimental data. The simulations were conducted at engine speeds of 800–2600 rpm, within a λ range of 1.3–3.4, using fuels with research octane numbers of 20 and 40 (RON20 and RON40). The results showed that the rhombic drive mechanism extended the compression phase, allowing the piston to remain near top dead center (TDC) for a longer duration. This increased the average cylinder temperature, facilitating auto-ignition and enabling stable HCCI combustion near the low-load limit at higher engine speeds. With the rhombic drive mechanism, heat release was more concentrated around TDC, the combustion duration was shortened, and the combustion process approached a constant-volume character. The principal contribution of the rhombic drive mechanism was extending the upper engine-speed limit of naturally aspirated HCCI operation. The low-load improvement was secondary, while higher MPRR under identical engine-speed and lambda conditions showed no direct extension of the high-load limit at a fixed speed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang P.; Jiang N.; Wei Z.; Hui P.
Title: Exploring socioeconomic associations of crisis information processing via large language models and explainable AI
Abstract: Social media evolution has restructured corporate crisis communication, yet extracting regional intelligence from unstructured data remains a significant computational challenge. This study proposes an integrated AI-Spatial Information Framework to analyze provincial-level discourse patterns during a major corporate crisis. Using the DeepSeek R1 671B model with few-shot learning, we classified 225,515 social media comments from Douyin into five theory-driven categories and an “Other” category, achieving an overall accuracy of 85.67% against stratified human reference labels (Cohen’s kappa = 0.828). We then employed LASSO-based feature selection and FDR-corrected OLS regression to examine associations between provincial-level socioeconomic indicators and consumer discourse patterns across 31 Chinese provinces. Statistical results suggest that provincial socioeconomic factors account for a substantial portion of the observed variation in digital discourse. Life expectancy was positively associated with brand anthropomorphism, while tertiary education showed a tentative negative association with health risk perception. More importantly, these associations suggest that regional variation in brand-supportive discourse is closely related to socioeconomic conditions and is theoretically consistent with cognitive buffering processes. By integrating theory-driven LLM classification with spatial analysis, the proposed framework connects computational linguistics and spatial social computing, providing a replicable approach for examining regional heterogeneity in digital crisis discourse. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Tang Z.; Zhang Z.
Title: Technological paths for enhancing renewable energy integration: Modeling, optimization, and practical prospects
Abstract: Against the backdrop of global dual-carbon goals and China's energy transition, the large-scale integration of wind and solar power faces an integration bottleneck due to their inherent intermittency and insufficient grid flexibility. This paper systematically reviews mainstream modeling methods for renewable energy integration-including system constraint modeling, time-series production simulation, and optimal scheduling-with a comparative analysis of their core logic, applicable scenarios, and solution strategies. From five key dimensions-power-side regulation, grid-side flexible interconnection and grid-forming control, energy storage coordination, multi-energy complementarity, and market-oriented mechanisms-this study analyzes the optimization pathways and technical achievements in enhancing renewable energy integration. It also summarizes typical domestic and international practices and identifies core challenges such as limited model adaptability, trade-offs between system security and integration efficiency, weak grid support, and regional imbalances. Future research directions are proposed, including AI-assisted dispatching, digital twin applications, distributed integration technologies, localization of international experiences, electricity-carbon market linkage, and differentiated urban-rural development paths. This review aims to provide theoretical and practical insights for overcoming integration bottlenecks and advancing the construction of new power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zeng Z.; Wu J.; Zhang X.; Kong X.; Wan H.; Li G.; Lin Q.; Luo M.; Cambria E.
Title: Learning from incomplete signals: Multi-view knowledge distillation for robust harmful micro-Video detection
Abstract: As hateful and misleading content continues to proliferate on social media platforms, detecting multimodal harmful content in micro-videos has become increasingly important. While recent advances in this area have shown promise, existing methods often assume complete access to all modalities, including video, audio, and textual descriptions. This assumption fundamentally limits their robustness in real-world settings, where micro-videos are frequently modality- and segment-incomplete due to upload artifacts, platform-level compression, or missing metadata. To bridge this gap, we introduce three real-world benchmarks that systematically capture varying degrees of incompleteness at both the modality and segment levels. We further propose MVKD , a multi-view knowledge distillation framework tailored for robust harmful micro-video detection under incomplete and uncertain conditions. MVKD (1) adaptively distills modality-specific knowledge through confidence-aware guidance, (2) enhances sample- and domain-level representations via contrastive alignment, and (3) integrates complementary cues using a multi-view mixture-of-experts strategy. Extensive experiments show that MVKD consistently outperforms strong baselines in both accuracy and robustness across diverse missingness patterns, and generalizes effectively to previously unseen domains. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Adult-only: When excluding children reveals a flaw in hospitality management approach
Abstract: This research note explores social servicescape in hospitality settings, considering recent regulatory debates questioning the exclusion of children. Although children are often positioned as either sovereign consumers or a marginalised group, their impact on guest satisfaction remains largely unexplored. Drawing on 90,045 TripAdvisor reviews from 72 international resorts, we applied advanced natural language processing techniques, including BERT-based sentiment analysis and child-reference classification using a local Large Language Model to examine whether references to children influence customer evaluations. By comparing satisfaction scores across reviews that mention or omit children, we explore whether these differences reflect broader managerial, academic, and policy-related challenges. This study contributes to ongoing debates on adult-only vs inclusive hospitality by highlighting how children's presence is addressed in guest feedback, and by raising questions about the potential limitations in current hospitality management practices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Xiao M.; Tian J.; Chen Y.; Dai W.; Zheng A.; Chen X.; Liu X.; Han J.; Liu Y.; Chen H.
Title: How is self-defeating humor associated with perceptions of the physical self? A large-sample resting-state fMRI study
Abstract: Self-defeating humor (SDH), characterized by self-ridicule to gain social approval, has been consistently linked to the body-image disturbance. However, its neural underpinnings remain poorly understood. The present study investigated the neural mechanisms linking SDH to negative physical self-perceptions in a large sample ( N = 1668). Participants completed measures of humor style and negative physical self, and resting-state functional MRI. Behaviorally, SDH was positively correlated with all dimensions of negative physical self. Whole-brain fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations analyses revealed that SDH was associated with decreased activity in the right parahippocampal gyrus, left caudate, right posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), and right precuneus (PCUN), but increased activity in the right postcentral gyrus (PoCG). Resting-state functional connectivity analyses showed SDH was negatively associated with caudate–occipital and PCC–PCUN connectivity but positively associated with PCC–occipital and PCUN–occipital connectivity. Mediation analyses identified a negative indirect effect through PoCG activity, and a positive indirect effect through PCUN activity in the associations of SDH with negative evaluations of general appearance and fatness, respectively. These findings highlight the role of brain regions involved in self–other information processing in linking SDH to maladaptive self-perceptions, thereby advancing our understanding of the neural pathways through which humor styles influence psychological health. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Understanding work well-being: A systematic review and future research agenda on multilevel influences
Abstract: Work well-being has become an important topic in organizational research, as it is beneficial to employee performance and job satisfaction. Although studies on work well-being have increased recently, existing literature remains fragmented, with prior reviews predominantly focusing on general employee well-being or single-level analyses. This limitation constrains both theoretical clarity and the development of targeted organizational interventions. In particular, there is a need to systematically review how individual, group, and organizational factors shape employees’ well-being at work. To address this gap, the present study conducts a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing evidence from 53 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025, retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. This study has two key implications: It identifies knowledge gaps in the literature and supports evidence-based decision-making. By synthesizing findings across the individual, group, and organizational levels, this review develops a broad and integrated understanding of the drivers of work well-being. The findings suggest that work well-being is driven by the dynamic interaction between individual and social resources, and broader organizational conditions. These factors operate in combination rather than independently, shaping employees’ psychological experiences across work contexts. This study contributes to the literature by providing a structured and integrative multilevel framework, clarifying conceptual boundaries of work well-being, and identifying underexplored research areas. It also offers a more analytically grounded synthesis that advances theoretical development and informs evidence-based organizational practices. In addition, the study highlights directions for future research, offering valuable insights for policymakers, managers, and scholars seeking to promote work well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Cities under pressure: Tourism intensity and the erosion of social capital in Italy
Abstract: This research note reconceptualizes tourism intensity as a structural stressor capable of undermining the social capital that sustains urban life. Drawing on a 15-year longitudinal panel data of 42 Italian cities (2009-2023) and employing a dynamic System GMM estimator, our study analyses how varying levels of tourism intensity affect social capital, operationalized through a multi-indicator civic engagement index. The results reveal a non-linear erosion process, where social capital remains stable at low and moderate levels of tourism intensity but declines sharply once cities surpass high-intensity thresholds. Our findings provide a quantifiable basis for understanding overtourism as a threshold-based social phenomenon, extending beyond resident perceptions to the structural weakening of civic cooperation, trust, and engagement. The present study advances theoretical debates by positioning tourism intensity as a civic destabilizer and highlights the need for governance models that protect social capital as a critical urban asset. Without such safeguards, cities risk transitioning from vibrant, participatory communities into socially depleted Non-places. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Suriano R.; Paonessa L.P.
Title: Science takes more than belief: Epistemic and cognitive predictors of scientific reasoning
Abstract: Belief in science and scientific reasoning represent related but conceptually distinct aspects of individuals' engagement with science: the former reflects an epistemic orientation toward science, whereas the latter concerns the ability to evaluate evidence, methods, and inferences. We examined actively open-minded thinking (AOT) and cognitive reflection (CRT) as theoretically complementary characteristics, representing an epistemic disposition and a reflective cognitive component, respectively. In a sample of 333 Italian participants, we examined the incremental associations of belief in science, AOT, and CRT with scientific reasoning and whether AOT and CRT showed similar or differentiated associations with belief in science and scientific reasoning. Belief in science was positively but weakly associated with scientific reasoning. AOT and CRT accounted for additional variance in scientific reasoning beyond sociodemographic characteristics and belief in science. AOT was associated with both belief in science and scientific reasoning, whereas CRT was associated with scientific reasoning but not significantly with belief in science. Overall, the findings indicate partly differentiated patterns of association across the two constructs. Given the cross-sectional design, no causal or temporal conclusions can be drawn. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Guan Y.; Cao S.
Title: A dynamic graph query-based data pricing method via multi-armed bandits
Abstract: Graph query-based data pricing is promising for pricing answer subgraphs in graph databases according to diverse buyer queries. However, existing methods provide limited support for adaptive price updates when the broker must balance transaction revenue with transaction success rate under incomplete buyer-valuation information. To bridge this gap, we propose GQPRM, which includes: (1) a vertex-edge pricing mechanism that prices a first-time queried answer graph through non-negative atomic prices; (2) a multi-armed bandit (MAB)-based strategy that discretizes repeated-query prices into candidate actions and uses historical acceptance/rejection records for exploration and exploitation; (3) an entropy-weighted feedback update that allocates the observed subgraph-level price variation to vertices and edges in a demand-sensitive manner, rather than assuming that binary feedback uniquely identifies a single overpriced element; and (4) a smart contract-based incentive allocation mechanism that records ownership and supports auditable reward allocation between the data broker and data owners. Experiments on three typical datasets demonstrate that GQPRM improves cumulative transaction value and transaction success rate over the static baseline under the evaluated settings. © 2026

Authors: Fan G.; Deng Z.; Fang H.
Title: EXPLORING THE HEALTH KNOWLEDGE CO-CONSTRUCTION ON SHORT VIDEO PLATFORMS
Abstract: Short video platforms have become an important channel for doctors to conduct health science popularization. This study aims to explore the factors influencing health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms. Based on arousal theory, we develop an empirical model to examine the effects of video vividness, video complexity, emotional attitudes, and doctor popularity on health knowledge co-construction. We collected data from the largest short video platform in China, comprising a total of 4,009 videos and 1,040,230 comments for empirical analysis. This study combined machine learning, large language models, and econometric models to test the theoretical model. The results show that: (1) video vividness has a significant positive effect on health knowledge co-construction; (2) video complexity has a negative effect on health knowledge co-construction; (3) there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between emotional attitude and health knowledge co-construction; (4) doctor popularity positively moderates this curvilinear relationship. This study contributes to the literature on knowledge co-construction, expands the understanding of health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms, and provides practical guidance for platform managers and doctors. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. Title: Reinforcement learning with experience sharing promotes collective cooperation on higher-order networks
Abstract: As a central form of prosocial behavior, collective cooperation is the cornerstone of social prosperity, and elucidating how it emerges among the self-interested population is of significant theoretical and practical importance. However, existing research of cooperative evolution on higher-order networks typically assumes that agents update decisions exclusively based on their own experiences, overlooking the pervasive diffusion of information within groups. In reality, decision-making is shaped not only by individual experience, but also by experiences acquired from neighboring agents. To this end, we develop a hypergraph-based reinforcement learning framework that integrates individual and neighborhood experiences to investigate how information sharing affects cooperation under higher-order interactions. Specifically, we utilize hypergraphs to characterize the interaction topology, within which agents update their strategies according to the Q-learning algorithm. Extending the standard learning paradigm, we introduce an experience sharing mechanism, where neighborhood information is aggregated to form a shared experience and subsequently fused with individual experience to guide decision-making. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that an intermediate level of experience sharing can significantly enhance the collective cooperation, particularly under severe social dilemmas, increasing the final cooperation level by up to approximately 0.43. In contrast, excessive experience sharing leads to behavioral homogenization among agents, thereby undermining the relative advantage of cooperation. Moreover, higher learning rates coupled with moderate discount factors are most conducive to cooperation. These findings shed new light on how experience sharing shapes cooperative dynamics in higher-order networks. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Efficient stability-preserving model order reduction for vibro-acoustic systems with complex configuration of porous and poro-elastic materials
Abstract: Recent developments in digital twins have led to a renewed interest in efficient transient vibro-acoustic finite element simulations, which can be combined with limited measurements to bridge the gap between the model and the physical world. To this end, stability-preserving model order reduction (spMOR) is a rapidly emerging topic to enable large-scale finite element models, which can reduce the size of these models but preserve their high fidelity and stability. Notably, the spMOR for vibro-acoustic systems with different porous materials was recently addressed by introducing additional variables. The trade-off is that the size of the resulting full-order models increases significantly with the complexity of porous materials, such as the frequency range and dimensions. Consequently, substantial computational resources are required for the offline generation of the reduction basis. Hence, an efficient approach is proposed in this paper to improve the offline stage efficiency of the spMOR for vibro-acoustics with a complex configuration of porous and poro-elastic materials, which adopts a two-step strategy to generate stable reduced-order models. Firstly, a higher-order Krylov subspace method based on Taylor’s theorem is applied to the frequency-domain model, leading to an intermediate reduced-order model. This process ensures the preservation of system matrix properties and positive realness of the frequency-dependent parameters. Secondly, leveraging these key properties, the spMOR for vibro-acoustics with porous and poro-elastic materials is applied to the intermediate reduced-order model to give a compact time-domain model. The proposed method is demonstrated on a simple cubic cavity and a more involved sedan car cabin. The proposed method significantly accelerates the calculation of the reduction basis and reduces memory usage. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Li Z.; Zhou H.; Wu Q.
Title: An adaptive-problem structure framework for survival relevance in temporal processing
Abstract: Research on survival-relevant cues and subjective time often groups stimuli into immediate-survival, reproductive, and social categories. These labels do not explain why cues within one category recruit different temporal processes across contexts and perceivers. The Adaptive-Problem Structure (APS) Framework characterizes the adaptive problem indicated by a cue through two separable appraisals: ecological urgency, the time sensitivity and cost of delaying a response, and interpretive indeterminacy, the extent to which adaptive meaning and the appropriate response remain unresolved. APS predicts when these appraisals recruit established arousal, attention, information-sampling, and memory processes, how diagnostic context changes those links, and which personality differences strengthen them. Temporal consequences depend on the timing paradigm, interval, and response format. We outline independent ratings, selective within-domain manipulations, process measures, and staged construct validation. Five predictions specify task conditions, personality mappings, comparison baselines, and non-supporting outcomes. APS offers testable constraints on mechanism recruitment and prediction for new stimuli; the framework itself remains to be empirically validated. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: QLRUN: Integrating Q-learning and covariance matrix learning into Runge–Kutta optimization for engineering design problems
Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid metaheuristic Q-learning Runge–Kutta Optimization (QLRUN) for solving complex, high-dimensional, rotated, and constrained engineering optimization problems. The proposed framework integrates the gradient-guided search mechanism of the Runge–Kutta Optimization (RUN) algorithm with the adaptive decision-making capability of Q-learning to achieve dynamic regulation of exploration and exploitation behaviors during the optimization process. In QLRUN, the optimization state is characterized using convergence and population-diversity indicators, while the Q-learning agent adaptively selects search operators according to a fitness-improvement-driven reward policy that is iteratively updated throughout the search process. To further enhance rotational robustness and maintain population diversity, a lightweight Covariance Matrix Learning (CML) mechanism is incorporated to construct adaptive eigen-coordinate systems aligned with the fitness landscape's geometry. Unlike the full covariance adaptation employed in CMA-ES, the proposed CML strategy acts as an efficient coordinate-transformation mechanism with low computational overhead. The effectiveness of QLRUN is comprehensively validated using the 23 classic standards, the CEC2020, and CEC2022 benchmark suites, which include unimodal, multimodal, hybrid, composition, shifted, and rotated functions, as well as seven constrained engineering design problems. Comparative evaluations against the original RUN and nine state-of-the-art metaheuristics demonstrate that QLRUN consistently achieves competitive convergence accuracy, improved solution stability, and faster convergence characteristics. Quantitatively, QLRUN achieves the top Friedman mean rank across all three benchmark suites, attaining scores of 1.70 on 23 classic standards, 1.40 on CEC2020, and 1.17 on CEC2022, thereby substantially outperforming the original RUN and the competing optimization methods. Moreover, on constrained engineering design problems, QLRUN obtains highly competitive best-known solutions, including a pressure vessel design cost of 5.88536×103 and a tension/compression spring weight of 1.26660×10−2. Beyond p-value-based significance, practical superiority is further confirmed through consistent top-one Friedman rankings and Wilcoxon Rank-Sum win/tie/loss results against RUN of 17/5/1, 8/1/1, and 9/2/1 for the 23 classic standards, CEC2020, and CEC2022 benchmark suites, respectively. Statistical analyses using the Wilcoxon Rank-Sum, Friedman, ANOVA, and Kruskal–Wallis tests confirm the robustness and practical significance of the proposed approach. The results demonstrate that QLRUN constitutes a robust, computationally efficient optimization framework suitable for challenging applications in power systems, energy engineering, and multidisciplinary design optimization. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Halali E.
Title: Two automatic motivations, two control systems: A neuroscience framework for negotiation
Abstract: Negotiation often involves a recurring tension between self-interest and social preferences such as fairness, trust, honesty, and reciprocity. A central debate concerns which motive, self-interest or social preferences, constitutes the automatic default and which requires cognitive control to be expressed. Understanding these automatic processes is important because negotiations often tax cognitive resources, increasing reliance on automatic responses. Yet, the evidence remains contradictory: in some contexts, self-interest appears spontaneous and social concern effortful, whereas in others the reverse holds. This review argues that the inconsistency stems from a flawed premise. Drawing on converging evidence from social, affective, and decision neuroscience, I propose that both self-interest and social preferences are automatic motivational processes, driven by distinct motivational systems and regulated by separate prefrontal control mechanisms. The right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (rDLPFC) is proposed to regulate reward-seeking motivation, facilitating prosocial behavior such as fairness and reciprocity, whereas the right ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (rVLPFC) is proposed to regulate socio-emotional responses, facilitating self-interested choice, together forming a proposed double dissociation within this motivational conflict. This dual-control framework reframes the central question from which motive is automatic to which automatic motivational system dominates a given context. It reconciles conflicting findings and explains why subtle situational shifts can reverse the apparent automatic response. The review considers emerging hormonal, neuromodulation, and hyperscanning evidence from dynamic interactions and discusses how changing circumstances may alter not only which motivation dominates, but also which form of control is needed to act in accordance with one's goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The role of citizen science in engaging older adults with age-friendly green spaces
Abstract: This project addresses the global challenges of an ageing population and rapid urbanisation by exploring how citizen science can support the engagement of older adults in shaping age-friendly green spaces. Conducted in the City of Unley, South Australia, the study engaged 30 older residents (aged 60+) as citizen scientists to trial a multi-format audit tool and co-reflect on its use in practice for creating age-friendly environments, generating practical insights for future research and design practice. Integrating audits into participants’ daily routines and everyday life spaces ensured that findings reflected lived experiences. Citizen science was not merely a data collection tool but a sustained dialogue, with regular workshops and informal café sessions supporting motivation, peer learning, and collaborative analysis. Participants reported challenges such as sustaining long-term motivation, but also highlighted opportunities for empowerment, confidence-building, and strengthened community ties. Importantly, many older adults described shifts in how they experienced their environments—becoming more observant, extending their walking habits, and growing more confident in voicing ideas. Several participants continued their civic engagement beyond the project, illustrating the lasting impact of participation. The study contributes methodological insights into designing inclusive citizen science initiatives, offering guidance on recruitment, tool development, and engagement strategies tailored to older populations. Overall, this study demonstrates the power of citizen science not only to generate grounded data but also to empower older adults and co-produce inclusive urban knowledge. Findings provide process-focused insights into age-friendly engagement and illustrate the broader potential of citizen science in shaping equitable, community led public spaces. Overall, this research demonstrates how citizen science can move beyond data collection to become a co-creative process that empowers older adults and informs age-friendly urban transformation. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Rethinking institutional support for migrant businesses in Sweden: A strategic management– oriented scoping review
Abstract: Migrant entrepreneurship has become an increasingly important contributor to Sweden’s economic and social landscape; however, the institutional environment supporting migrant-owned businesses remains fragmented and difficult to navigate. This study conducts a scoping review to map existing knowledge on the opportunities, barriers, and systemic gaps affecting migrant entrepreneurs in Sweden. The review draws on peer-reviewed journal articles, policy reports, and grey literature published between 2020 and 2026, identified primarily through the Scopus database and complementary manual searches. A total of 18 studies met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using a thematic synthesis approach. The findings reveal that migrant entrepreneurs contribute significantly to job creation, innovation, and regional development, particularly in sectors such as retail, hospitality, and services. However, they face persistent barriers including limited access to finance, bureaucratic complexity, language constraints, and weak integration into institutional support networks. The analysis further shows that although Sweden possesses a wide range of support mechanisms, these are often poorly coordinated, resulting in duplication, inefficiencies, and limited accessibility for migrant entrepreneurs. Guided by the resource-based view (RBV) and contingency theory, this study develops a strategic pathways model consisting of three interrelated pillars: resource mobilization, adaptive strategy, and collaborative alignment. The model provides a conceptual framework for enhancing institutional effectiveness and improving the inclusiveness of entrepreneurial support systems. The study highlights the need for a more integrated, flexible, and strategically coordinated support ecosystem. It also identifies critical gaps in empirical research and calls for future studies to test the proposed model in real-world institutional settings. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Herbal medicine among vulnerable populations in Cameroon: a systematic review and meta-analysis with clinical, mechanistic, and global health perspectives
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Herbal medicine (HM) is widely used in Cameroon, yet its prevalence, clinical evidence, and the pharmacological mechanisms supporting its use among vulnerable populations have not been comprehensively synthesised.Aim of the study: To systematically review and meta-analyse HM use among women, adolescents, and children in Cameroon, summarise the available clinical and mechanistic evidence for commonly reported medicinal plants, and identify challenges relevant to policy and global health. Materials and methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, multiple databases were systematically searched. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled HM proportion. Also, a PubMed search for clinical evidence (randomised controlled trials, RCTs) and bioactive compounds/mechanistic insights was conducted to support the folkloric use of the identified plants. Results: Sixteen studies involving ∼15,000 individuals were included. The pooled proportion of HM use was 46.9% (95% CI 30.7 – 63.4%), with subgroup estimates of 52.1% (95% CI 33.6 – 70.4%) in women and 26.4% (95% CI 0.0 – 85.0%) in children. A total of 93 plant species belonging to 79 genera and 44 families were identified. Anaemia, digestive problems, labour, and cancer were the main reasons for HM. Cordia platythyrsa and Entandrophragma candollei were classified as vulnerable/endangered by the IUCN. RCT evidence was available for only 19 plant species, including 6-shogaol (Zingiber officinale) and annonacin (Annona muricata) for cancer, quercetin-3-rhamnoside (Alchornea cordifolia) for anaemia, and oleic acid (Phoenix dactylifera) for labour. Mechanistic studies indicated that these bioactive compounds act through multiple pathways (e.g., shogaol - upregulated STAT3 pathway, reactive oxygen species generation, and cell cycle arrest in cancer cells). Conclusions: Nearly one in two individuals in these vulnerable populations reported HM use, despite limited high-quality clinical evidence supporting most medicinal plants. Strengthening epidemiological surveillance, clinical research, conservation of threatened medicinal species, and integration of traditional medicine into health systems could improve the safe and evidence-based use of HM in Cameroon and similar settings. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Anchoring sustainability: A new paradigm for maritime clusters
Abstract: The environmental footprint of maritime transport, combined with growing social and regulatory pressure to tackle pollution, has brought the shipping industry to the forefront of the sustainability agenda. The role of industry clusters is becoming increasingly relevant to this discourse, given their influence across all dimensions of sustainability. Surprisingly, although this profound relationship is well documented, it has not received sufficient scholarly attention. This study analyses the highly fragmented literature on maritime clusters and sustainability using a novel combination of bibliometrics and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven thematic analysis. On this basis, a framework is developed that captures the interaction between clusters and the key components of sustainability. The findings suggest that sustainability should not be treated as an isolated strategic initiative or the outcome of regulatory pressure, but as a key dimension of cluster competitiveness. Additionally, it emerges that digital innovation acts as a cross-cutting enabler of sustainability in maritime clusters, linking the economic, social/governance, and environmental pillars of the proposed framework. Overall, this study provides actionable insights for maritime practitioners and policy makers alike. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Techno-economic analysis of biogas production: a literature review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: The accelerating global energy transition and the development of the circular economy have established biogas as a key renewable energy source that can reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve waste management, and contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals. From this perspective, the techno-economic performance and sustainability of biogas systems have attracted growing attention in both academic and policy domains. This review aims to provide a comprehensive assessment of global research on biogas production and its techno-economic analysis, focusing on scientific dynamics, technological advances, analytical methods, and methodological challenges. An integrative review approach was applied, combining a systematic literature review with bibliometric analysis. A total of 287 Scopus-indexed publications were analyzed using VOSviewer to identify key research trends, collaborations, and thematic clusters. The qualitative synthesis explores advancements in anaerobic digestion technologies, biogas upgrading, and techno-economic analysis frameworks, with an emphasis on key performance indicators, cost metrics, modeling approaches, and uncertainty analysis. The results indicate a substantial increase in publication activity, from 3 publications in 2015 to 64 in 2024, accompanied by expanding international research collaboration. The analysis also reveals a methodological evolution from conventional cost-based evaluations toward integrated frameworks that combine technical, economic, environmental, and uncertainty assessment components. Recent studies reflect progress in co-digestion optimization, microbiological enhancement, life cycle-based assessments, and AI-driven modeling. However, significant gaps remain, including limited data reliability, regional inconsistencies, and the absence of harmonized methodologies for techno-economic analysis. The review highlights the need for standardized, transparent, and policy-oriented frameworks to strengthen the role of biogas in sustainable energy transitions. Future efforts should concentrate on improving the robustness of data, integrating environmental and socio-economic dimensions, and aligning techno-economic analysis practices with national and international energy strategies. Bibliometric analysis identified 5 major thematic research clusters covering anaerobic digestion, feedstock and waste management, environmental assessment, process engineering, and resource recovery. The review further demonstrates that recent advances in co-digestion, pretreatment technologies, microbiological enhancement, and biogas upgrading have contributed to improved methane yields and enhanced process performance. In order to increase the efficiency of the production system, careful consideration must be given to the choice of feedstocks, the production processes, and the legal framework for biogas production. Efforts must be focused on improving the technological and commercial efficiency of biogas to ensure good sustainability. In this context, appropriate investments and policies could play a key role in energy diversification. © 2026 The Authors. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of KeAi Communications Co. Authors: Wang L.; Jia J.; Zhou L.; Li S.
Title: Perceived placeness in creative tourism: Conceptualization, scale development and implications for transformative experiences
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Creative place-making combines cultural heritage, spatial design, creative symbolism, and experiential affordances to cultivate distinctive destinations, yet what tourists holistically perceive in these places remains underexplored. Drawing on atmospheric aesthetics theory, this study conceptualizes perceived placeness in creative tourism as tourists' holistic perception of the environmental and atmospheric qualities that make creative tourism destinations experientially distinctive. To operationalize this construct, content analysis was used to identify its dimensions and initial items. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses refined these items into a 20-item, five-dimensional scale comprising environmental qualities, historical-cultural embeddedness, creative-symbolic ambiance, restorative affordance, and emotional affordance. The nomological relevance of the scale was further established by examining its implications for transformative experiences via authenticity. Theoretically, this study positions perceived placeness as an integrative perceptual field between place-making and tourists’ psychological responses, and contextually elaborates atmospheric aesthetics theory in creative tourism. Practically, the scale provides a timely tool for evaluating and planning creative place-making efforts and curating meaningful tourist experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Lexicon-guided representation learning with self-attentive transformer models: Enhancing offensive language detection in low-resourced languages
Abstract: Detecting offensive language in online social platforms is essential yet challenging in low-resourced, morphologically rich languages such as Turkish. This study presents an engineering-driven and innovative approach for offensive language detection in Turkish. The proposed method directly injects offensive lexicons collected from local sources by domain experts into transformer self-attention mechanisms. In particular, it leverages lexicon-guided representation learning within Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) variations to enhance attention toward offensive linguistic cues. DistilBERT and XLM-RoBERTa are enhanced with a lexicon mask that reweights attention toward lexicon-matched tokens by a factor of five, while maintaining end-to-end fine-tuning without architectural modifications. Using the OffensEval Turkish dataset (35,284 annotated tweets), the proposed method is evaluated against traditional baselines (MLP, CNN, SVM, LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU) as well as vanilla transformer models. The proposed Lexicon-Guided XLM-RoBERTa achieves an F1-score of 0.87, while Lexicon-Guided DistilBERT attains 0.85, outperforming vanilla XLM-RoBERTa (0.78), DistilBERT (0.76), and non-transformer baselines (0.66–0.72). Additionally, LIME is employed to provide local and model-agnostic explanations for both offensive and non-offensive predictions, demonstrating that lexicon-guided attention enhances the detection of morphologically complex and implicit offensive cues while reducing false positives in neutral contexts. The proposed method offers practical and multidisciplinary contributions through a lightweight plug-in attention mechanism based on linguistic resources, achieving state-of-the-art performance in Turkish offensive language detection while providing interpretable outputs beneficial for content moderation, human-centered AI, and computational social science. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Sounding different: Exploring attitudes towards digital voice personalization in a conversational setting
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of voice generation and conversion technologies, the application of voice personalization in everyday communication is becoming increasingly possible. However, current studies on voice personalization have largely focused on tool design, while relatively little is known about the impact of these technologies on self-presentation and social interaction. To explore this, we conducted a qualitative study with 14 pairs of participants (28 in total, 15 females and 13 males) that integrated a voice personalization tool into natural conversation. In pairs, participants first engaged in a conversation using their original voices, and then reflected on this experience. After that, they personalized their voices using a voice modification tool and took part in a second conversation with the same partner in which they heard each other’s modified voices in real-time. Finally, they participated in follow-up interviews. Our findings show that voice personalization prompted participants to reflect on their original and modified voices, to negotiate between authenticity and desired traits, and to consider both benefits and risks of voice personalization in different contexts. These insights indicate that voice personalization is intricately linked to self-perception while simultaneously functioning as a malleable social signal. Overall, this study contributes empirically grounded findings on how voice modification affects self-perception and impression management, and offers design directions for future personalization tools. © 2026 The Authors. Title: What motivates landowners to use prescribed fire in a wildfire prone landscape? Evidence from California, USA
Abstract: The use of prescribed fires on private lands is important to achieving landscape and community resilience goals, yet private landowner adoption remains low. This study examines the factors shaping non-industrial private forest and rangeland owner intentions to use prescribed fire in California. Using the Theory of Planned Behavior framework and Likert scale questions, we administered a survey to 4000 landowners, yielding 509 usable responses. We used multinomial logistic regression to model adoption intention (yes, maybe, and no) and binary logistic regression to examine preferred implementation approaches among landowners open to burning. Results indicate that 27% of respondents were willing to burn, 42% remained uncertain, and 31% were unwilling. Social norms were the strongest predictor of adoption intention. Past wildfire exposure, perceived wildfire risk, landholding size, perceived benefits of prescribed fire, and attitudes toward cultural burning positively impact adoption likelihood. Capacity to conduct burns strongly differentiated the willing adopters from uncertain ones, while prohibitive cost was the most consistent barrier across groups. Among landowners open to burning, community cooperative burning was the most preferred implementation approach, followed by agency-assisted burning, with preferences shaped by trust, liability concerns, and landholding size. Findings suggest that in California, making prescribed fire more visible may matter as much as making it feasible. Effective outreach should prioritize peer-based demonstration strategies, reduce cost and liability barriers, and build local burning capacity to bridge the gap between interest and action. Policy interventions supporting community burn networks and technical assistance could accelerate prescribed fire adoption on private lands. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Greenhouse gas emission under a dual-disposability approach: Assessing environmental technical efficiency in the airline industry
Abstract: This study provides a robust analysis of environment-adjusted airline efficiency under a dual-disposability assumption for undesirable output. It employs also a two-stage methodology to investigate the complex and heterogeneous relationships between airline operational profiles and their environmental efficiency. Technical efficiency is estimated in the first step using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) based on the Directional Distance Function (DDF) under both assumptions of the technological characterization of gas emissions, contractible versus non-contractible. In the second step, to analyze the factors influencing the estimated efficiency scores, a Tobit second-stage regression is employed. Results show that efficiency scores under strong disposability are systematically and significantly higher than those obtained under weak disposability, with an average difference of 11.9 percentage points. The findings also indicate a positive and statistically significant relationship between the LCC variable and technical efficiency, implying that airline groups with LCC subsidiaries achieve higher efficiency levels. Based on their specific trade-off between operational and environmental inputs, the analysis of technical efficiency elasticities classifies airlines into five groups. These range from “Strong Proactive Environmental Performers” to “Low Efficiency High-Cost” groups, whose efficiency improvements are structurally linked to either an optimization or a deterioration of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions performance. The technical efficiency elasticity with respect to revenue share and to fuel efficiency are parallel across all airlines, while the elasticity for GHG consistently exhibits the opposite sign. We provide one of the few systematic comparisons of efficiency scores under weak versus strong disposability. This comparison allows us to quantify the systematic contraction in measured efficiency that occurs when greenhouse gas emissions are modeled as a technologically costly output rather than a costless byproduct. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Nitrogen-doped graphene composite with optimized pyridinic/pyrrolic configurations for high-performance NH4+ storage
Abstract: Graphene has emerged as a crucial class of electrode materials for aqueous ammonium-ion batteries (AAIBs). However, pristine graphene suffers from severe restacking and lacks sufficient redox-active sites, fundamentally limiting its practical application. Herein, we employ a two-step temperature-controlled pyrolysis strategy using melamine as both a nitrogen source and a self-sacrificing template to synthesize a nitrogen-doped graphene/g-C3N4 composite (g–CN@G-700) that features both a high proportion of redox–active pyridinic and pyrrolic nitrogen configurations and an optimal graphitization degree, thereby resolving the trade-off among conductivity, specific surface area, and active nitrogen content. Consequently, the material demonstrates a high reversible NH4+ storage capacity of 202 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1, favorable rate capability, and satisfactory long-term cycling stability with no significant capacity decay after 5,500 cycles at 4 A g−1. By using X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, we reveal a highly reversible synergistic charge storage process involving the active nitrogen species and carbonyl groups with NH4+. Finally, combined with theoretical calculations, we propose a synergistic NH4+ storage mechanism where pyridinic-N and pyrrolic-N provides primary redox-active sites, and graphitic-N maintains structural integrity. This work provides a pathway to design and synthesize high-performance carbon-based materials for AAIBs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Graphene and MXenes: performance–scalability trade-offs and application-driven materials selection in two-dimensional technologies
Abstract: Graphene and MXenes are leading two-dimensional (2D) materials, yet their selection for emerging technologies remains limited by the lack of quantitative comparison between intrinsic performance, scalability, and cost. This review introduces a practical performance–scalability assessment framework based on a multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) approach. In this regard, material-performance, synthesis-scalability, and techno-economic indicators were normalized and integrated to calculate the final material-selection score. The evaluated criteria include electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, mechanical strength, electrochemical capacitance, synthesis yield percentage, maturity status, price per unit mass of precursors, specific energy utilization, and oxidation resistance capability. Graphene exhibits higher thermal conductivity (2000–4000 W m⁻1 K⁻1), mechanical strength (∼130 GPa), and oxidation stability, supporting its use in performance-critical electronics and structural applications. MXenes provide higher electrochemical capacitance ( 300–1500 F g⁻¹), higher reported synthesis yields (80–99%), tunable surface chemistry, and lower estimated laboratory-scale cost (US$10–50 g⁻1), favoring energy storage, sensing, electromagnetic interference shielding, and water-related applications. The novelty of this review lies in combining property-level performance, synthesis maturity, scalability indicators and cost-performance mapping, into a single comparative framework, enabling rational, application-specific selection of graphene, MXenes, and their hybrid systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Zhang P.; Yang Z.; Chen R.
Title: Going green to compete: Male-biased operational sex ratio, status motivation, and men's relative green product preference
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Motivating men to choose environmentally preferable products remains an important challenge. Across six studies, this research examines how operational sex ratio (OSR), defined as the ratio of reproductively available men to women, is associated with men's relative preference for green products over conventional alternatives. OSR can characterize a broader demographic environment or serve as a population cue in a local social setting. A cross-level analysis in China showed that men living in provinces with more male-biased OSRs assigned greater priority to environmental protection, whereas women showed no corresponding association. Randomized experiments showed that perceived male-biased OSR increased men's relative green product preference; perceiving a female-biased OSR did not produce a corresponding increase among women. Among men, the subsequent studies provided complementary evidence consistent with mediation by status motivation, linked male-biased OSR cues more closely to intrasexual competition motivation than to mate-attraction motivation, and showed that audience publicness moderated the indirect effect through status motivation. These findings extend sustainable-consumption research by identifying population composition as a social-environmental condition relevant to men's green product evaluations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Recognition of individual angry versus happy faces in 6- and 9-month-old infants
Abstract: With mixed evidence from adults, children, and infants suggesting either anger or happiness superiority in emotion detection, emotion recognition, and recognition of individual faces posing emotional expressions, the current research was undertaken to determine if one or the other emotion would result in higher recognition of individual faces by 6-month-old and 9-month-old infants. The infants were familiarized with an angry or happy face and then given a novelty preference test pairing the familiarized face with a novel face posing the same emotion. Recognition performance of both age groups in each emotion condition was above chance; however, recognition of angry faces was reliably higher than for happy faces. A simple exposure-frequency account of the findings is unlikely because infants experience more happy than angry faces. In addition, lower-level interpretations based on differences in salience, complexity, and discriminability were not supported by image analyses, infant looking times during familiarization, or adult ratings. An account based on the processing of facial expressions as social or communicative signals by infants is discussed, with a possible role for an early negativity bias. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Digitalising waqf for sustainable development growth: Investigating user intentions through technology readiness and ethical commitment
Abstract: The digitalisation of cash waqf represents a promising avenue within Islamic social finance, offering substantial potential to enhance the welfare and socio-economic development of Muslim communities. Through digital platforms, cash waqf can be collected, managed and distributed more efficiently, transparently and widely compared to traditional methods. Despite these advantages, the level of public participation and contributions to digital cash waqf platforms remains significantly below expectations. This gap highlights the need to better understand the factors that influence individuals’ willingness to adopt digital channels for charitable giving. This study aims to explore the determinants that influence individuals’ intentions to contribute to cash waqf via digital platforms by employing the Technology Readiness framework. Specifically, the study examines the roles of optimism, innovativeness, insecurity, discomfort, and moral obligation in shaping users’ behavioural intentions toward online waqf contributions. Data were collected through an online survey involving 211 Muslim respondents in Malaysia who have experience with digital financial services. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The findings reveal that optimism, insecurity, and moral obligation have a positive and significant influence on individuals’ intentions to donate cash waqf through digital platforms. In contrast, discomfort demonstrates a significant negative effect, indicating that feelings of technological anxiety and lack of confidence in using digital systems may discourage adoption. Given the limited empirical research on digital cash waqf, this study contributes valuable insights into the psychological and behavioural factors influencing online donation behaviour. The findings provide practical implications for waqf institutions and policymakers to design strategies that reduce technological barriers while strengthening moral and religious motivations, thereby encouraging wider adoption of digital cash waqf platforms, particularly in developing countries with similar socio-economic environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Müller R.-A.; Coffie I.S.
Title: Experiential and symbolic pathways to luxury fashion brand equity: The contingent role of brand attachment and subjective norm
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The study develops and tests an integrated moderated mediation model to explain how emotional attachment, shaped by experiential and symbolic brand stimuli, is associated with consumer-based brand equity (CBBE) in the luxury fashion context, and the role of consumers’ social environment, drawing on Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour. Data were collected from 544 luxury fashion consumers and were analysed using Hayes' PROCESS Model 15. Both brand experience and brand mystery were positively associated with brand attachment. Brand attachment was also positively associated with CBBE and significantly mediated the indirect associations between experiential and symbolic brand resources and CBBE. Furthermore, subjective norm moderately weakens the positive relationship between brand attachment and CBBE, indicating that while subjective norm weakens the relationship between emotional attachment and consumers' evaluations of luxury fashion brands, it does not replace it. This study advances luxury branding research by showing how an identity-based relational mechanism is associated with broader CBBE, with experiential encounters and symbolic meanings relating to brand equity through emotional attachment. By integrating Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour within a unified framework, the study shows that experiential and symbolic brand resources are associated with luxury brand equity through complementary relational pathways. © 2026

Authors: Zhang G.; Cui X.; Liu H.; Wang Y.; Zhao S.
Title: ResGAT: A residual graph attention network for technology transfer prediction in Chinese universities
Abstract: University patent transfer in China remains sparse, and only a small fraction of university patents are licensed or assigned. Technology-transfer offices must still judge which patents are worth promoting and which enterprises are plausible recipients. Existing matching methods rely on content similarity, collaborative filtering, or shallow heterogeneous graphs. They rarely model patent–patent, patent–entity, and entity–entity relations together with patent attributes when positive transfer labels are extremely scarce. This study proposes a residual graph attention network (ResGAT) for technology-transfer object recognition. Built on three meta-paths, ResGAT uses relation-specific attention together with a shared feature transformation. It stacks residual graph-attention layers on the homogeneous branches to limit over-smoothing, and it uses a shallow cross-type branch to pass entity information to patents. A two-stage procedure then estimates transfer probability and ranks candidate transferees by dot-product similarity. On a civil-engineering patent graph from a Chinese university, and on seven strategic-emerging-industry subsets, ResGAT outperforms heuristic, linear, and multi-relational graph baselines under the same 10-fold protocol. The model also returns ranked enterprise lists for high-potential patents, so transfer offices receive a concrete shortlist rather than only a transfer score. © 2026

Title: Energy, exergy, and direct engine-out emission impact assessment of an ethyl acetate–diesel dual-fuel engine under different EGR rates
Abstract: This study experimentally investigates the energy, exergy, and direct engine-out emission impacts of ethyl acetate (EA)–diesel dual-fuel operation under exhaust gas recirculation (EGR). Tests were conducted on a single-cylinder direct-injection diesel engine at 1800 rpm and 25–100% loads. EA injection durations of 1, 2, and 3 ms and EGR rates of 0%, 5%, 10%, and 20% were investigated. Energy and exergy balances were established, and direct emission impact was calculated from CO, CO2, HC, and NOx mass-flow rates derived from the measured exhaust-gas concentrations and intake-air flow. At full load, EA(2 ms) + 20% EGR increased energy and exergy efficiencies by 39.1% and 38.4%, respectively, and reduced exergy destruction by 42.5% relative to diesel operation without EGR, representing the thermodynamically preferred condition. EA(3 ms) without EGR produced the maximum pointwise direct emission-impact reduction of 72.5% at 25% load, whereas EA(3 ms) + 20% EGR provided the greatest average reduction of 35.8%. Condition-mean ANOVA showed that engine load accounted for 84.81%, 84.61%, and 91.70% of the variations in energy efficiency, exergy efficiency, and direct emission impact, respectively. Load-resolved TOPSIS identified EA(2 ms) + 20% EGR as the highest-ranked balanced compromise, with a mean closeness coefficient of 0.7781; however, EA(3 ms) + 20% EGR became preferable when direct emission impact received greater weight. The results demonstrate metric-specific optima and support load-dependent coordination of EA injection and EGR. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Orgs G.
Title: The neuroaesthetics of liveness
Abstract: Live theatre, dance and music pervade to human culture. Building on a rich theoretical debate within theatre, performance and media studies, this review sketches out a psychological approach to understanding live experiences. It distinguishes physical liveness (presence in a here and now) from social liveness (sharing experiences with others). Recent mobile EEG studies on live dance performances and music concerts demonstrate that audience engagement during live performances is measurable as dynamic brain synchrony between co-present audience members or between audience members, music and movement. Differences in audience engagement between live and recorded performances (physical liveness) are measurable as looser or tighter slow wave neural synchrony. Conversely, social liveness can increase audience arousal, indexed by reduced power in the EEG alpha band during collective viewing of both live and recorded dance. These findings suggest that variable performance content and stable performance context engage dissociable neural mechanisms, attention and arousal respectively. Research on liveness originates in the performing arts but can be extended to the visual arts and to sport events. Physical and social liveness may facilitate those rare, memorable and transformative aesthetic experiences that are difficult to produce in lab-based environments. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Tuberculosis Patients’ Preferences for Improving Tuberculosis Care in Chitwan District, Nepal: A Discrete Choice Experiment
Abstract: Objectives Patient-preferred tuberculosis (TB) care is integral for the patient-centric approach to TB care delivery. This study aimed to ascertain the aspects of TB care that people with TB value most, to inform improvements in TB care in Chitwan District, Nepal. Methods A discrete choice experiment (DCE) survey was developed to elicit the care preferences of TB patients in Chitwan District. The DCE included 6 attributes (patient card, sex of healthcare worker, transport incentive, provision of psychosocial support, waiting time, and type of TB care provider), which were developed through literature review, expert consultations, and patient interviews. Participants were randomly selected from the TB care centers and interviewed face-to-face to complete the survey. Six choice sets were presented to each participant and asked to choose preferred option from 2 hypothetical TB care models labeled as TB Care A and TB Care B. A conditional logit regression model was used to quantify the preference of TB patients. Results Among 133 patients who participated in DCE (97% response rate, mean age of 47 years, 71% male), 83% had pulmonary bacteriologically confirmed TB, and 32% were in the intensive phase of treatment. Patients highly valued TB care services that have the provision of psychosocial support (β = 0.62, P < .001), followed by improved patient card (β = 0.50, P < .001), and the waiting time for TB care within half an hour (β = 0.25, P = .002). Conclusions People with TB preferred to be supported by psychosocial interventions, improved patient card, and reduced waiting time in current TB treatment strategy. This study provides evidence for current/future TB control program package to align with the patient’s preferences. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Meaning in the age of AI: Experiencing less, needing more
Abstract: What does it mean to be human when artificial intelligence (AI) can simulate human thought and creative labor with increasing fidelity? Unlike AI, humans experience meaning in life. Yet AI may create a paradox for meaningfulness. AI may reduce people's ability to experience meaning by disrupting selfhood (loss of effort and self-efficacy), social relationships (reduced mattering and connection), and culture (erosion of value and stability). At the same time, it may heighten people's need for meaning by challenging human exceptionalism and increasing the need for coherence amidst upheaval. This paradox—experiencing less while needing more—is what we term the AI Meaning Gap. Yet meaninglessness is not inevitable. If developed and used intentionally, AI could become a tool for reflection, understanding, and self-growth, thereby enhancing meaning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
