Title: Experimental Study on Smart Sloped Rolling-Type Bearings Integrated with Early Prediction of Peak Velocity
Source title: International Journal of Structural Stability and Dynamics
Abstract: The use of sloped rolling-type bearings (SRBs) to protect critical equipment from seismic damage has been widely adopted. However, maintaining SRB displacement responses within safe limits often requires a large damping force, which results in unacceptable accelerations. This highlights the trade-off in seismic isolation: reducing displacement typically comes at the cost of increased acceleration, and vice versa. Although previous numerical studies have shown that adjusting the SRB damping force based on peak velocity (PV) predictions from an earthquake early warning (EEW) system enables better control over acceleration and displacement responses, experimental validation is necessary. This study employs magnetorheological (MR) dampers to apply the damping force determined by the predicted PV. Performance tests are conducted to characterize the physical properties of the MR dampers and develop their mathematical representation. Numerical simulations incorporating the MR damper and SRB models under seismic conditions are used to establish a control law that correlates PV with the voltage required by the MR dampers. To predict PV, the first few seconds following primary seismic wave (P-wave) detection undergo a multi-scale short-term Fourier transform (STFT) to generate a spectrogram. After feature enhancement, it is fed into a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model, which predicts the impending earthquake’s PV. This prediction, alongside the established control law, enables rapid adjustment of the SRB damping force shortly after P-wave detection. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evaluated through shake table testing. Results indicate that the approach significantly mitigates isolation displacement responses under major earthquakes, demonstrating its potential for improving seismic isolation performance. 2026 © The Author(s)

Title: STGCM: Sign-aware triple graph collaborative model for recommendation
Abstract: Recommendation systems, as a core technology for mitigating information overload, play a crucial role across many fields. In recent years, graph neural networks (GNNs) have significantly improved recommendation performance by modeling user-item interactions as a graph structure. However, most existing sign-aware methods directly partition the user-item interaction graph into separate positive and negative graphs for modeling. While this local modeling approach can distinguish different feedback types, it disrupts the global topology of the original graph. This impairment exacerbates data sparsity and weakens the propagation of signed information. To address this, we propose STGCM, a Sign-aware Triple Graph Collaborative Model for Recommendation. STGCM employs a multi-perspective graph convolution embedding learning framework, which preserves the complete topology of the original graph while thoroughly excavating local preference features from both positive and negative feedback. Building on this, a two-stage hierarchical attention fusion mechanism is designed to achieve a global-information-supplemented, synergistic fusion of multiple perspectives, thereby enhancing the model's information complementarity capability. The experimental results provide compelling evidence that STGCM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across three real-world datasets. Authors: Kashiwa M.; Nishikawa T.
Title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Anamorelin and Olanzapine for Cancer Cachexia in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients in Japan
Abstract: Objectives Cancer cachexia significantly impacts quality of life and prognosis in patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Anamorelin and olanzapine have demonstrated efficacy in improving appetite and body weight in clinical trials. However, their cost-effectiveness within the Japanese healthcare system is unclear. This study assesses the cost-effectiveness of anamorelin and olanzapine for cancer cachexia in patients with non-small cell lung cancer from the perspective of Japanese healthcare payers. Methods A Markov model with 7 health states was developed using clinical trial data (ONO-7643-04 for anamorelin and OlAnCa for olanzapine) and real-world cost and survival data from the Japan Medical Data Center claims database. The time horizon was 60 months, with 4-week cycles (65 cycles). Costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were discounted at an annual rate of 2%. One-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted using 1000 Monte Carlo simulations. Results The incremental cost-effectiveness ratios were 7 405 419 Japanese yen (JPY)/QALY for anamorelin and 6 737 715 JPY/QALY for olanzapine compared with placebo. Both exceeded the willingness-to-pay threshold of 5 million JPY/QALY. At the 7.5 million JPY/QALY threshold, cost-effectiveness probabilities were 63.7% for anamorelin and 93.2% for olanzapine. One-way sensitivity analysis identified utility values and healthcare costs as the most influential parameters. Conclusions Both anamorelin and olanzapine exceeded conventional cost-effectiveness thresholds in Japan. Given the limitations of pharmacotherapy in improving physical function, multimodal cachexia management incorporating nutritional counselling, exercise therapy, and rehabilitation warrants consideration. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Fear of missing out, entertainment, and social presence: A stimulus-organism-response model of impulse buying in Chinese live-stream commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines the drivers of impulse buying behavior in China's rapidly expanding live-stream e-commerce environment. Building on a Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, it investigates how key live-stream features — including entertainment value, host interactivity, perceived scarcity of product offers, and social presence — influence consumers’ internal reactions (emotional arousal and fear of missing out) and ultimately their impulse purchase intentions. Survey data were collected from a representative sample of 580 Chinese consumers with recent live-stream shopping experience. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), the results show that entertainment and scarcity stimuli significantly increase arousal and FOMO, both of which in turn are associated with higher impulse purchase intention, while social presence relates directly to impulsive buying. Multi-group analyses indicate significant demographic differences in some pathways. The fsQCA reveals distinct configurations of conditions associated with high impulse purchase intention, highlighting the crucial roles of scarcity cues and community engagement. The findings offer new theoretical insights into digital retailing and practical guidance for designing engaging live-stream shopping experiences that balance consumer excitement with brand objectives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: When ads look worth keeping: Screenshotable design increases ad saving and Facebook ad liking
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As social media advertising increasingly competes in fast-scrolling feed environments, an important but understudied question is whether some ads succeed by functioning less as transient persuasive messages and more as saveable information objects. Drawing on affordance theory and uses and gratifications reasoning, this research examines whether screenshotable ad design increases preservation-oriented engagement by making ads seem useful for later use. Across five studies, including controlled online experiments and a naturalistic simulated-feed experiment, screenshotable ads were associated with higher ad saving intention and Facebook ad liking relative to non-screenshotable ads. The results are consistent with perceived future utility as a mediating mechanism: screenshotable design increased perceived future utility, which in turn was associated with higher saving-related responses and Facebook ad liking intention. The process was stronger when consumers anticipated a future rather than immediate need, such that perceived future utility translated more strongly into ad saving and liking under future-need conditions. In addition, screenshotable design more strongly increased perceived future utility when information density was high rather than low, indicating that saveable structure is most effective when the ad contains enough substantive content to justify preservation. The findings contribute to consumer research on digital advertising response by identifying screenshotable ad design as a distinct visual structure that can shape consumers’ interpretation of an ad as a later-use resource, and they offer guidance for managers designing social media ads intended to be kept, revisited, and positively engaged with over time. © 2026

Title: The benefits of reading narrative fiction
Abstract: The benefits of reading are well-known and have been well-established by research. But does it matter what we read? Are there unique benefits to reading narrative fiction: stories about people, their goals, challenges, emotions, and interactions? Focusing on research published in the past few years, we review the empirical evidence of the benefits associated with reading fiction. This includes a wide range of domains, including language abilities, our ability to understand others, early social development, intergroup prejudice, meaning in life, cognition, longevity, and well-being. Several remaining research questions are also presented. Authors: Lai A.; Wu J.; Cao Y.; Lin T.
Title: Corporate environmental credit rating and social stability: Evidence from capital-labor conflicts in China's polluting industries
Abstract: Mitigating capital-labor conflicts is essential for maintaining social stability. Using China's Enterprise Environmental Credit Evaluation System (EECES) as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the impact of corporate environmental credit rating on capital-labor conflicts. The results indicate that EECES reduces capital-labor conflicts in polluting industries by approximately 17.63%, although its effect weakens over time. Channel tests show that EECES mitigates capital-labor conflicts by reducing workers' pollution exposure risk, improving corporate environmental information transparency, and enhancing social trust in corporations. Moreover, in cities with weaker social governance capacity, EECES exerts a stronger restraining effect on capital-labor conflicts, suggesting that it effectively compensates for deficiencies in social governance. Further analysis reveals that although EECES reduces industrial output, it significantly promotes economic transformation. Overall, these findings highlight EECES as an effective policy tool for safeguarding social stability. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Subsample averaging for non-periodic microstructures: Bias reduction, dispersion increase, and practical trade-offs in computational micromechanics
Abstract: The computation of effective properties of random microstructured materials via representative volume elements (RVE) is affected by both bias and dispersion. For non-periodic microstructures (snapshots), which naturally arise in experiments and imaging-based studies, the bias decays slowly, rendering standard homogenization approaches inaccurate, significantly biased, and therefore unreliable. Recent theoretical results suggest that subsample averaging – evaluating the apparent properties only on a strictly interior subdomain – can significantly reduce the bias. In this work, we investigate the practical performance of subsample averaging for linear elastic particle-reinforced composites using large-scale numerical experiments and FFT-based computational micromechanics. We first demonstrate that subsample averaging must respect the Hill–Mandel condition to improve the convergence behavior of the bias, i.e., both stress and strain fields must be subsample averaged. In particular, the naive approach of subsample averaging the apparent stress alone may reduce the magnitude of the bias, but does not improve its convergence rate. When applied consistently, subsample averaging reduces the magnitude of the bias and produces a more favorable decay trend for the investigated non-periodic microstructures. However, this bias reduction comes at the cost of an increased dispersion due to the reduced sampling domain, resulting in only marginal improvements of the total error when used in isolation. To overcome this limitation, we combine subsample averaging with variance reduction via optimized volume fraction (OVF), which significantly improves overall accuracy and reliability for matrix-inclusion composites. The presented strategy is straightforward to implement and can be readily applied within existing computational frameworks without modifying the underlying solver. These results reveal a fundamental bias–dispersion trade-off associated with subsample averaging and provide practical guidance for computing the effective properties from non-periodic microstructure samples, including samples obtained experimentally. © 2026

Authors: He X.; Choi Y.; Su Y.; Fan D.; Cui L.; Lei J.
Title: Beyond the accession event: Joint regional membership duration and completion of cross-border acquisitions
Abstract: Cross-border acquisition (CBA) completion is often hindered by institutional barriers, imposing substantial costs on deal participants. While regional integration aims to reduce such barriers, prior research predominantly treats regional integration as a discrete accession event, leaving post-accession adaptation dynamics and their underlying mechanisms underexplored. Drawing on new institutional economics and social learning theory, we argue that joint regional membership duration increases CBA completion likelihood, with country-dyadic M&A stock serving as the mediating carrier via the sequential pathways of institutional alignment and social learning. We further examine how initial regulatory distance and cultural distance condition this mechanism. Using a sample of 8009 announced CBAs across the European Union (2010–2022), we find support for the mediation pathway and show that both regulatory and cultural distance weaken this indirect effect. This study advances the literature by moving beyond discrete event-based integration framing and refines the understanding of cross-national distance within integrated regional blocs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
Abstract: Hierarchical text embedding models offer variable-length representations, while quantization reduces numerical precision; both aim to improve computational efficiency. This work is an empirical benchmark study of how these two orthogonal, already-established techniques interact. We evaluate 38 tasks from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) using four transformer-based embedding models, covering 1D and 2D hierarchical representations combined with 32-bit, 8-bit, and binary quantization, for 168 configurations per task. We report each efficiency dimension separately: theoretical per-vector storage and end-to-end evaluation time. Under a Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc analysis, int8 quantization is statistically indistinguishable from float32 for pair classification and re-ranking and costs at most 1.5 percentage points overall, whereas binary quantization is significantly worse across every task category. Halving the embedding dimension once is not statistically detectable above m=16; two successive halvings always are. Combining an 8× dimensionality reduction with int8 yields a 32× reduction in per-vector storage at 94.4% of baseline effectiveness. Because evaluation times were measured once, we treat them as indicative: we find no evidence that quantization speeds up evaluation, whereas sampling from intermediate layers shortens it substantially. Retrieval degrades far faster than every other category, so we report findings per task category. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Chen M.; Li R.; Hu T.; Dong J.
Title: Community participation intensity on asynchronous biodiversity and human well-being responses to ecological restoration in global drylands
Abstract: Ecological restoration serves as a key strategy for addressing desertification and ecosystem degradation in global drylands. However, achieving synergistic benefits for both biodiversity and human well-being remains a significant challenge for sustainability. Although community participation is increasingly promoted, quantitative evidence remains limited on how participation intensity is associated with measured ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. A dataset encompassing 744 effect sizes from 41 independent studies across global drylands was constructed to conduct a meta-analysis. The synthesis indicated positive benefits relative to degraded baselines, while composite biodiversity and composite human well-being showed asynchronous responses across community participation intensity. For composite biodiversity, the pooled mean estimate corresponded to an average increase of 122.11% relative to degraded baselines. Limited community participation was associated with long-term positive patterns in the composite biodiversity (159.35%) and composite human well-being (130.71%), whereas extensive community participation showed an evidence-limited and marginally supported positive tendency in composite human well-being in the short term. Eventually, we propose an adaptive framework in which livelihood-support components may be emphasized during early restoration, followed by lower-disturbance stewardship considerations as biodiversity recovery stabilizes. Overall, our findings provide exploratory quantitative evidence for discussing how community participation may affect asynchronous ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Fukubayashi N.; Fuji K.
Title: From overloaded to unsatisfied: The short- and long-term effects of online career media exposure
Abstract: The contemporary career landscape is increasingly influenced by digital technologies. The widespread availability of online career information and the daily exchange of content via social media not only facilitate autonomous career development but also expose individuals to a vast array of career options. Although this abundance reflects greater self-determination, it may also lead to psychological challenges through choice overload. In this study, the possibility that online exposure to career information and options increases career choice overload, which, over time, may reduce overall career satisfaction, is examined. Using a combined contemporaneous and cross-lagged effects model, we found that greater online exposure to career information was associated with increased career choice overload, which was captured across three dimensions: career choice avoidance, disengagement from one's current career, and impatient career idealism. Longitudinally, elevated career choice overload predicted lower overall career satisfaction, and conversely, lower satisfaction contributed to greater overload, which suggests a potential negative spiral. Our findings provide empirical evidence that routine online media exposure can generate both conscious and unconscious career choice overload, which highlights the occurrence of choice overload in high-stakes career contexts and its multidimensional nature. © 2026

Title: Unveiling research trends in artificial intelligence adoption based on the UTAUT: A bibliometric analysis supporting SDGs and future outlook
Abstract: The development of AI adoption across disciplines has become a major global concern, especially with the UTAUT model that runs concurrently. This study aims to map research trends on AI adoption within the UTAUT model in conceptual, intellectual, and social structures. The research utilises a bibliometric approach from the Scopus database for the period 2018-2025 on related topics. Data analysis was conducted descriptively using Biblioshiny (Rstudio). The study found a very positive and significant development in research on AI adoption within the UTAUT model across various disciplines, aligning with the SDGs, particularly points four, nine, and seventeen. The countries that contributed most were China and the USA. Interesting themes for studying the development of UTAUT model implications include social influence, performance expectancy, behaviour, perceived risk, digital literacy, and AI anxiety. In SDG 4, the adoption of AI in higher education is crucial by incorporating perceived risk and digital literacy to achieve effective personalised learning. In SDG 9, organisational and corporate levels within managerial structures are important for combining structural and psychological factors that influence AI adoption. AIMDSS in the healthcare sector is essential for supporting health innovation and infrastructure. Meanwhile, for SDG 17, discovering best practices for AI adoption across various fields needs to be accelerated, particularly in Africa, South America, and most of Eastern Europe. The implications of this research point to the development of institutional guidelines for AI adoption and the exploration of the UTAUT model. By highlighting the evolving role of contextual, ethical, and governance-related factors, this study provides a foundation for aligning AI adoption strategies with sustainable development objectives and informs future empirical and policy-oriented research. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Mapping the evolution of communication research in aquatic conservation: A systematic literature review of emerging patterns and research opportunities (2015–2025)
Abstract: This review examines the development of communication research in aquatic conservation through a systematic literature review. Although communication is increasingly recognized as crucial for environmental governance, promoting aquatic conservation remains underexplored and often treated instrumentally. Using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, this review analyzed eleven articles (n = 11) published between 2015 and 2025, drawn from Scopus and Web of Science databases. Findings indicate that existing studies are predominantly presented in the Global North and tend to emphasize media representation, message framing, and individual behavioral change. These patterns suggest that communication is often conceptualized as a tool for disseminating information rather than as a broader social process. Most of the research described is qualitative, further strengthening the exploratory nature of the evidence. This review identifies limited engagement with systemic perspectives in understanding how communication shapes environmental responses. To address this, this study introduces Niklas Luhmann's social systems theory as an analytical lens for reinterpreting communication in aquatic conservation. From this perspective, communication is understood as a process of systemic resonance in which environmental issues are selectively interpreted across different social systems. This study contributes to the field by providing an exploratory synthesis of existing research and highlighting the need for more methodologically robust, geographically diverse, and theoretically grounded studies. The findings also underscore the importance of shifting from instrumental approaches to a more systemic understanding of environmental communication. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Authors: Alalwan T.A.; Perna S.
Title: Maternal diet and offspring ASD and ADHD: A critical narrative review of dietary patterns, choline, and polyphenol-related exposures
Abstract: Maternal diet may influence fetal neurodevelopment through nutrient availability, placental function, and maternal–fetal metabolite signaling. This critical narrative review used a structured, purposive search to organize human evidence on prenatal dietary patterns, choline, and polyphenol-related exposures according to outcome directness: diagnosed autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), related dimensional traits, and general neurodevelopment. Whole-diet studies provide the most direct human evidence, but diagnostic findings are cohort-dependent and vulnerable to residual familial and genetic confounding. Choline trials and cohorts mainly address attention-related traits or general cognition; they do not establish prevention of diagnosed ASD or ADHD. Polyphenol evidence is limited to food proxies and one trimester-specific cohort of estimated intake, without diagnostic or biomarker-based studies. Preclinical data support biological plausibility—particularly for choline in BTBR, maternal immune-activation/CHRNA7, and Ts65Dn models and for resveratrol in valproate-exposed rodents—but remain model-specific. The evidence is therefore best treated as an organizing framework rather than a confirmed causal hypothesis. Clinical translation should prioritize achieving recommended dietary adequacy and balanced dietary patterns; evidence does not support high-dose single-nutrient or concentrated-polyphenol supplementation for ASD/ADHD prevention. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Extracts of Coriaria nepalensis ameliorate MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behaviors via regulation of neurotransmitter imbalance and neuroinflammation
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Coriaria nepalensis Wall. is a traditional ethnomedicine used by the Dong ethnic group in Guizhou Province, China, for the treatment of schizophrenia. However, its pharmacological effects and the bioactive constituents responsible for its therapeutic efficacy remain largely unknown. Aim of the study: To evaluate the anti-schizophrenic effects of C. nepalensis extracts and investigate their underlying mechanisms and potential bioactive constituents. Materials and methods: An MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like Sprague–Dawley rat model was established to evaluate the therapeutic effects in the blank control group, model group, positive drug group, and different dose groups of C. nepalensis extracts (EA-H, EA-M, EA-L, SJ-H, SJ-M, and SJ-L). Schizophrenia-like behaviors were assessed using the open-field, Y-maze, three-chamber social interaction, and prepulse inhibition (PPI) tests. Neurotransmitter levels in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex were determined by LC-MS, inflammatory cytokines were quantified by ELISA, and the expression of signaling pathway-related proteins and glutamate decarboxylase 67 (GAD67) was analyzed by Western blotting. Plasma-absorbed constituents of the active extract were characterized using HPLC-MS/MS. Results: C. nepalensis extracts alleviated MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities to different extents, including altered locomotor activity, impaired spatial working memory, and social deficits. Among all treatments, the low-dose ethanol extract (EA-L) produced the most pronounced effects. EA-L significantly improved sensorimotor gating deficits in the PPI test and showed a stronger ameliorative than risperidone under the present experimental conditions. Mechanistically, EA-L restored neurotransmitter homeostasis in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, attenuated neuroinflammatory responses, regulated the abnormal activation of inflammation-related signaling pathways, and normalized GAD67 expression. These changes were associated with improvements in schizophrenia-like negative symptoms, cognitive deficits, and sensorimotor gating impairment. Chemical profiling identified 251 constituents in the ethanol extract, of which 57 were detected in rat serum after oral administration, suggesting that these absorbed compounds may contribute to the observed pharmacological activity. Conclusion: Extracts of C. nepalensis, particularly EA-L, ameliorated MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities by restoring neurotransmitter homeostasis and suppressing the aberrant activation of neuroinflammation-related signaling pathways. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Multimodal fusion for precision livestock behavior monitoring: A systematic review of deep learning, pose estimation, and sensor integration strategies
Abstract: Animal behavior analysis is a cornerstone of precision livestock farming, providing non-invasive insights into health, welfare, and productivity through continuous behavioral monitoring. Traditional approaches, including manual observation, sensor-based systems, and rule-based modeling, are limited by labor intensity, observer subjectivity, and low temporal resolution. This systematic review (PRISMA 2020; 2020-2026 literature) presents a comprehensive synthesis of deep learning and multimodal artificial intelligence approaches for animal behavior recognition in precision agriculture. Deep learning architectures, including convolutional, recurrent, and transformer-based models, achieve reported accuracies of 85-99% across livestock species, with transformer-based models reaching a mean of 94.4% (95% CI: 91.96-96.76%). Critically, multimodal fusion systems demonstrate a mean accuracy gain of 10.3 percentage points over single-modality baselines in an exploratory analysis of four independent source-level comparisons (95% CI: 4.9-15.8%; paired t(3) = 6.01, p = 0.009, Cohen’s d = 3.01), with peak detection sensitivities exceeding 90% for health-critical conditions, including lameness and metabolic disorders. This review evaluates early, late, and hybrid fusion strategies; the role of pose estimation in fine-grained movement analysis (with 94-100% accuracy in lameness detection); and the contribution of wearable and environmental sensors to continuous monitoring. Explainable AI methods are assessed for their role in improving model transparency and stakeholder trust. Key challenges, including data scarcity, annotation heterogeneity, multimodal synchronization, and limited cross-domain generalization, are critically discussed, along with six directions for future research. This review uniquely positions adaptive multimodal fusion as the central paradigm for next-generation, deployable precision livestock behavior monitoring systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chung Y.-S.; Huang H.-P.
Title: Expand or carve up? Evaluating market dynamics of premium airline entry with extended synthetic control methods: Evidence from STARLUX airlines
Abstract: This study examines the effects of STARLUX Airlines' entry as a newly established premium full-service carrier on Taiwan's international air transport market. Using the synthetic control method (SCM) and an extended SCM framework, the analysis evaluates changes in passenger demand following the airline's entry, encompassing both single and multiple treated units, including individual routes and interconnected markets. A conditional growth model was subsequently employed to distinguish market expansion from demand redistribution. Results indicate that although only 9 out of 24 treated markets showed statistically significant expansion, STARLUX's entry still revealed latent demand and contributed meaningfully to overall market growth despite the relatively small size of STARLUX as compared to its primary competitors, China Airlines and EVA Airways. This effect was particularly evident in business-oriented and transfer-focused segments, while some tourism-driven and politically sensitive markets saw limited or negative responses. This study contributes to the literature by highlighting the demand-side influence of premium airline entry, extending SCM to multi-unit and network-based applications, and providing a replicable framework for evaluating airline market interventions in liberalized environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: DRNet: Parallel two-branch network with fusion-enhancement and channel-pixel attention for color image steganalysis
Abstract: Image steganalysis is a hot topic in the field of information security, and researchers have recently proposed a series of methods. However, existing color image steganalysis methods tend to extract features indiscriminately from different channels and regions, which fails to focus on steganographically relevant channels and texture-rich areas where stego signals are concentrated. In addition, most methods lack effective mechanisms to aggregate and amplify steganographic information across the three color channels, leaving weak stego signals dispersed and undetected. To address these issues, we propose a parallel two-branch network with fusion-enhancement and channel-pixel attention for universal color image steganalysis. In the main branch, we design a stego signal fusion-enhancement block that performs multi-channel information fusion and first introduces detail-enhanced convolution to amplify weak stego signals. In the auxiliary branch, we design a channel-pixel attention mechanism that jointly performs attention across channel and pixel dimensions, enabling precise localization of steganographic regions via multiplication-based fusion with main branch features. Experiments on the Alaska II dataset demonstrate that the proposed network achieves superior detection accuracy and generalization over state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each component, and visualizations confirm that the channel-pixel attention mechanism effectively guides the model to focus on steganographic regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Kassouri Y.
Title: Mobile internet connectivity and climate change literacy in Africa
Abstract: Addressing climate change requires individual behavioral shifts and a deep understanding of its impacts, yet the role of information and communication technologies (ICT), a powerful driver of social movements and cultural shifts, in shaping climate change literacy remains underexplored. This study addresses a critical gap by exploring how ICT, particularly mobile Internet connectivity, influences climate change literacy in Africa. I provide the first systematic evidence on the impact of mobile Internet connectivity on climate change literacy by exploiting variations in peer-based Internet connectivity in an instrumental variable strategy. Using newly georeferenced individual-level data on climate change literacy from over 42,000 respondents across 31 African countries, I show that mobile Internet connectivity has a modest yet robust effect on climate literacy, raising it by approximately 0.57 points for a typical adopter. Heterogeneity analysis shows that mobile Internet access primarily enhances the knowledge-based dimensions of climate literacy, particularly climate awareness and understanding, while also improving risk perceptions to a lesser extent. This suggests that mobile Internet contributes to climate literacy mainly by expanding access to factual information and knowledge about climate change. Suggestive evidence reveals that Internet connectivity can help close climate-related information gaps, among socio-economically disadvantaged groups, such as women, farmers, and those without formal education. Although Internet connectivity increases the frequency of using Internet and social media for news, there is no strong evidence that these platforms serve as channels linking Internet connectivity to climate literacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A graph-based friend recommendation system in social networks using Q-Deep Learning Network
Abstract: The growth of social networks heavily depends on effective user connectivity. In such networks, users typically establish connections through cascading diffusion models. This allows them to expand both their friend circles and the overall reach and scalability of the network. However, due to the overwhelming number of users, identifying potential friends with similar interests and experiences can be challenging. To address this, friend recommendation systems aim to suggest similar users based on individual features and activities on social platforms. This task becomes even more difficult under the “cold start” condition, where no prior user information is available. Given the dynamic nature of social networks, user preferences are continuously changing. For this reason, using adaptive machine learning models is essential. Reinforcement learning, which adapts through interaction with the environment and user behavior, presents a promising solution for dynamic friend recommendation. In this paper, we propose a Graph-based Friend Recommendation system using a Q-Deep Learning Network (GFRQLN). Our method leverages standard social network datasets stored as adjacency matrices. It uses graph centrality metrics—degree, closeness, and betweenness—as input features. Each state in the proposed model includes a user and their immediate friend circle, while the action corresponds to adding a new user to this circle. The reward mechanism is based on modularity: if the modularity increases, a positive reward is given; otherwise, a penalty is applied. Experimental results demonstrate that GFRQLN outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, it shows improvements in accuracy and precision of approximately 12 % and 24 % on the Facebook dataset, 10 % and 13 % on DBLP, 11 % and 10 % on IMDB, and 20 % and 17 % on Yelp. Additionally, our model achieves significant reductions in MAE and RMSE, with improvements of about 43 % and 48 % on the Ciao dataset, and 35 % and 28 % on the Epinions dataset, respectively. © 2026

Title: Fat body transcriptomic responses to dietary macronutrient balance and Metarhizium infection in the desert locust, Schistocerca gregaria
Source title: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology - Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
Abstract: Dietary macronutrient balance influences immunity and disease outcomes in most organisms, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. We investigated how dietary protein-to-carbohydrate ratio shapes the fat body transcriptomic response of an insect, the desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria), following infection with the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium robertsii. Our earlier research showed that a carbohydrate-biased diet extends better survival from infection. We hypothesized that this was due to enriched immune functions, potentially due to more readily accessible energy to support immune responses, and/or because the fungal growth was slowed due to reduced availability of protein or other nutrients. RNA sequencing of fat body tissue collected 96 h post-infection followed by differential expression analysis showed that infection elicited a core transcriptional response, whereas direct dietary effects remained limited. Infection substantially enriched all immune pathways (humoral, cellular, and recognition and signaling) regardless of diet. These results provide support against the hypothesis that differences in survival among dietary treatments are due to differences in host immune pathway activation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Should generative AI be responsible to users? Developing and validating the user-generative AI psychological contract scale
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As GenAI becomes increasingly embedded in AI-enabled service interactions, users' evaluations of AI are extending from functional performance to expectations regarding responsibility and obligation. Drawing on Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) theory and psychological contract theory, this study defines the user–generative AI psychological contract (AIPC) as users' beliefs about the responsibilities and obligations GenAI should fulfill toward them during ongoing interaction and develops a corresponding scale. Study 1 used purposively recruited interviews (N = 26) to identify the construct content domain. Study 2 used two nonprobability online-panel samples of active GenAI users (N = 507 and N = 506) to develop the items and examine the factor structure, reliability, and construct validity. Study 3 used the same 506-case sample employed for structural validation in Study 2 to provide an initial test of the nomological network among AIPC, AI anthropomorphism, and co-creation intention. Results indicate that AIPC consists of three dimensions—the functional support contract, relational collaboration contract, and ethical safety contract—and forms a 16-item scale. Users reported the strongest expectations regarding ethical safety. Anthropomorphism was indirectly associated with co-creation intention through functional support and relational collaboration, but not through ethical safety. The findings extend psychological contract theory to user–AI relationships and provide a measurement tool for studying responsibility expectations toward GenAI. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Factors affecting public transport adoption in Riyadh- case study
Abstract: Riyadh's greenhouse gas emissions and urban climate risks are likely heightened by accelerated urbanization and profound dependence on private cars. Despite the government's investment in public transportation, societal resistance to giving up private cars and using public transit persists due to cultural and traditional factors. Within the Gulf context, this study is the first to investigate the unique socio-cultural and urban context of Riyadh to understand university students' mobility behavior, identify four factors that significantly are associated with their travel choices, and quantitatively rank the relative influence of these factors. Surveys (n = 710) were used to assess four key factors, analyzed via multiple regression, chi-square, and t-tests. Results indicate that, in descending order of influence, psychological factors (explaining 23% of the variance) have the most significant association with students' willingness to switch to public transport in Riyadh, followed by trip characteristics (13%), urban factors (12%), and socioeconomic and demographic factors (12%). The result suggests that, alongside infrastructure improvements, coordinated strategies are required to change social norms, enhance environmental awareness, and create culturally responsive incentives. The findings support the implementation of place-based policies for sustainable mobility. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A cross-disciplinary reflection on the role of Indonesian traditional fermented foods in strengthening sustainable science education
Abstract: Traditional fermentation practices in Indonesia embody biocultural knowledge by linking food production, microbial processes, ecological adaptation, and community traditions. Nevertheless, industrialization, urbanization, and diminished intergenerational knowledge transfer have increasingly marginalized these practices, resulting in the underutilization of their educational potential for sustainable science learning. This study argues that the deliberate incorporation of Indonesia’s traditional fermentation practices into sustainability-focused STEM education, guided by culturally responsive pedagogy, can directly foster scientific literacy, promote sustainability, and strengthen local cultural connections. Such integration addresses the underutilization of biocultural knowledge in fermentation and underscores its unique potential at the intersection of science and culture. A systematic narrative literature review was conducted utilizing Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Publications from 2000 to 2025 were included. Eligible sources comprised peer-reviewed articles or academic works addressing fermentation, science education, sustainability, and indigenous knowledge. Studies were analyzed using thematic content analysis and inductive-deductive coding. The review further assessed conceptual clarity, empirical rigor, contextual depth, and educational relevance. The findings indicate that traditional fermentation serves as a living laboratory, connecting microbiology, biochemistry, ecological knowledge, and sociocultural practice. Five themes emerged: indigenous ecological knowledge; microbiological and nutritional aspects; cultural transmission and identity; food security and sustainability; and STEM pedagogy integration. Although many studies provide strong cultural and conceptual insights, fewer offer robust empirical evidence regarding classroom implementation or measurable outcomes. This study presents a framework for incorporating traditional fermentation into science education. By prioritizing contextual, interdisciplinary, and community-based approaches, the framework demonstrates how local knowledge can enhance scientific literacy, sustainability, and cultural resilience. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Politeness negotiation in English refusals: Evidence from Javanese EFL learners and Native Speakers of English
Abstract: This study examines how politeness is negotiated in English refusal speech acts produced by Javanese Learners of English (JLEs) and Native Speakers of English (NSEs) across situations characterized by variations in power relations and social distance. Data were collected through a set of written discourse completion tasks (WDCTs) consisting of nine scenarios representing interpersonal, academic, and professional contexts. The study employs a comparative qualitative design, with refusal strategies identified using an established taxonomy and systematically coded using Atlas.ti. The results show that refusal is consistently realized as a sequence of pragmatic moves rather than a single illocutionary act. Among JLEs, the most frequent pattern is layered mitigation, characterized by the combination of apology, appreciation, and indirectness prior to the main refusal. This pattern becomes more prominent in situations involving greater interlocutor power and greater social distance. In contrast, NSEs tend to employ concise mitigation combined with clearer expression intent, often limiting negotiation and reducing ambiguity. Indirectness in JLEs frequently functions to maintain relational harmony and prolong interactional openness, whereas in NSEs, it operates within a more bounded and situationally oriented framework. The study also revealed that direct refusal emerges selectively in equal-power relationships, with differing orientations toward politeness marking between the two groups. Theoretically, this study contributes to the literature on interlanguage pragmatics by positioning politeness in refusal as a dynamic negotiation process shaped by the interaction of cultural orientation, social variables, and sequential organization of speech. These findings highlight the need to conceptualize refusal not as a fixed strategy type but as a context-sensitive pragmatic practice. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: A systematic review of emerging bioenergy pathways: Comparison of economic viability and greenhouse gas emissions
Abstract: To capture the recent technology improvements in advanced biofuels, this review conducted a systematic review of post-2015 publications and synthesized 116 techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), and social LCA studies to analyze the economic viability and environmental and social impacts. Capital costs, feedstock prices, operational expenses, and minimum fuel selling prices (MFSPs) were benchmarked alongside carbon emissions to enable direct comparison. This review finds key technical advancements emerged from new catalysts, enzymes, and chemicals, and optimized processes in pretreatment, conversion, and integrated system models. Results indicate that biomethane from anaerobic digestion of agriculture waste is the most cost-effective and climate-friendly option, with capital investments often below $10 million, MFSPs under $2/gal, and WTW emissions consistently below 30 g CO2-eq/MJ. Biodiesel from waste oils can achieve MFSPs below $2/gal when co-products (e.g., electricity, glycerol) are valorized, though emissions vary with feedstock and land use change impacts. For cellulosic ethanol, advances in pretreatment, enzyme efficiency, and lignin valorization have reduced MFSPs to $2.3–$3.2/gal and achieved 70–90% GHG reductions relative to gasoline. Overall, waste-based feedstocks consistently outperform crop-based systems in cost and emission metrics. Process optimization and co-product valorization help with improving resource efficiency, reducing production costs and lowering environmental impacts. The social LCA studies find advanced bioenergy deliver broad societal benefits, with employment as the most consistently reported positive outcome. The review highlights the importance of standardized TEA/LCA/social LCA frameworks, recommending targeted policy incentives to accelerate the deployment of low-carbon bioenergy technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Deterministic modeling of infection dynamics under Far-UVC irradiation: a cumulative-exposure framework and its mathematical relation to infectious quanta
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Far-UVC irradiation (200–235 nm) is a promising photonic intervention for suppressing the environmental transmission of airborne pathogens in occupied spaces. However, establishing a robust physical and mathematical framework to quantify these dynamic pathogen-host interactions remains challenging, as direct verification using mammalian models is experimentally demanding and cost-prohibitive. Here, we present a controlled in vivo biophysical model system—utilizing zebrafish and Yersinia ruckeri —to quantitatively examine the macroscopic survival dynamics of a host population under varying environmental pathogen loads. We observed a distinct, threshold-like transition in macroscopic host survival near a critical pathogen density (106 CFU/mL for a 0.25-day exposure duration), above which infection-induced mortality sharply increased. Far-UVC irradiation reduced the viable pathogen density as a function of UV dose, systematically driving the system below this critical threshold and demonstrating effective physical pathogen attenuation. To elucidate the underlying dynamics, we introduced a deterministic, multistep Susceptible-Infectious-Removed (SIR) model governed by a system of coupled differential equations. The theoretical model revealed that the final macroscopic state of the system is governed by a cumulative exposure parameter, Λ=β0ρτ, where β0 is the infectivity coefficient, ρ is the bacterial density, and τ is the exposure duration, rather than by instantaneous bacterial density alone. Crucially, the cumulative exposure parameter Λ derived from this aquatic infection model shares the same exponential cumulative form with the infectious quanta in the Wells-Riley model for predicting airborne transmission. Therefore, this in vivo platform validates a quantitative physical framework specifically for evaluating ultraviolet (UV) disinfection dynamics. These findings provide a theoretical basis for designing precise photonic irradiation algorithms that maintain cumulative environmental exposure below critical pathogenic thresholds. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Art as a scaffold for social cognition
Abstract: The idea that art connects us to others is culturally compelling, yet empirical evidence linking art engagement to social cognition remains mixed across paradigms, methods, and timescales. We develop the thesis that art functions as a scaffold for social cognition, rather than a direct intervention on social-cognitive abilities. From this perspective, art structures the conditions under which social cognition unfolds by shaping whether individuals engage with socially meaningful content, how deeply they become involved, and whether they return to similar experiences over time. The scaffold model identifies three interrelated components: a motivational gate, qualities of engagement, and reinforcement and habit formation. By integrating previously disconnected literature, the scaffold model reframes art's social-cognitive impact as a recursive process that creates repeated opportunities for social-cognitive practice across contexts, media, and timescales. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Ultrasonic vocalizations in mice and rats: New applications and recent developments from sender to receiver
Abstract: Mice and rats emit ultrasonic vocalizations (USV) above the human hearing range. Such USV are widely regarded as reliable indicators of the animal's affective state. Moreover, USV serve important communicative functions. Given their prominent role in social communication, this review adopts a reciprocal framework that considers both sender and receiver, with particular emphasis on the production and perception of USV. The review focuses on sex differences and subtype variations in the sender, and explores the communicative value of USV through playback studies, revealing their role in regulating social interactions from the receiver's perspective. It also examines recent applications, including the use of isolation-induced USV during the homing test, USV as measures of expectation, and their relevance in modeling mania and emotional contagion. Furthermore, this review takes into account advancements in sender identification and live tracking in semi-natural environments, which have enhanced our understanding of USV. Title: Neural and endocrine correlates of extinction of conditioned sexual incentive salience in male rats
Abstract: Conditioned sexual arousal (CSA) can develop when initially neutral social cues acquire sexual incentive value through associative learning. In male rats, pairing the D2-type receptor agonist quinpirole (QNP) with cohabitation with an almond-scented juvenile male induces a conditioned sexual response toward that stimulus. Here, we examined how this response changes following repeated nonreinforced exposure to the conditioned social cue. Adult male rats underwent three conditioning trials followed, in the extinction-training groups, by three additional drug-free exposures to the almond-scented juvenile male. Conditioned responding was subsequently assessed toward both a receptive female and the juvenile male. QNP-Paired males showed robust juvenile-directed non-contact erections (NCEs), whereas QNP-Extinction males showed markedly reduced NCE responding. Genital investigation also showed a significant Partner × Treatment interaction, while the remaining behavioral measures did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Free testosterone did not differ significantly among treatments. Exploratory Fos-immunoreactivity (Fos-IR) analyses revealed treatment-related differences in several brain regions; however, no direct QNP-Paired versus QNP-Extinction regional comparison remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Thus, repeated nonreinforced exposure to the conditioned social cue was associated with a marked reduction in conditioned sexual responding. Because the Paired and Extinction conditions differed in elapsed time and additional experience, this reduction is compatible with extinction but cannot be attributed uniquely to extinction learning. The endocrine and Fos-IR findings should be considered exploratory. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Mapping the intellectual structure of floating photovoltaics research, trends and emerging frontiers: a hybrid bibliometric review and content analysis
Abstract: This study presents a hybrid bibliometric–content analysis integrating scientific publications, patent activity, and deployment statistics to map the evolution, intellectual structure, and emerging research priorities of floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems. A dataset of 1716 publications spanning 2004–2025 was analysed using Bibliometrix, and the resulting thematic structure was used to organize a technical synthesis. Four interconnected domains were identified. Structurally, FPV deployment spans three aquatic environments, three principal floating concepts, and four station-keeping families, confirming that design requirements vary fundamentally with site conditions and environmental loading. Reported FPV energy-yield differences relative to land-based PV range from −3.84% to +19.68%, demonstrating that thermal benefits are strongly dependent on climate, geometry, and ventilation. Environmental studies commonly assess approximately 10% reservoir coverage, while scenarios reaching 25–30% indicate increasing trade-offs between water conservation and ecological uncertainty. Techno-economic evidence reports FPV capital-cost premiums of approximately 25–30%, with operating-cost estimates commonly 2–4% higher than land-based PV, although assumptions vary substantially. These findings demonstrate that FPV is a coupled water–energy–infrastructure system whose reliability, environmental sustainability, and bankability cannot be evaluated independently. Future research should prioritize long-term structural monitoring, transferable performance models, ecosystem-scale assessment, standardized reporting, and uncertainty-aware life-cycle economic frameworks for commercial-scale deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The role of mnemonic discrimination in symptom severity and treatment response of obsessive-compulsive disorder
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Mnemonic discrimination, the ability to differentiate novel stimuli from highly similar past ones, has been evidenced as a compelling factor for fear overgeneralization in anxiety disorders. However, very limited research has examined mnemonic discrimination in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). The current study provided an initial examination of the relationship between mnemonic discrimination to OCD symptoms and treatment response. Patients (N = 48) in an intensive partial hospital/residential treatment program for OCD completed the Mnemonic Similarity Task at admission and discharge, along with self-report measures of OCD severity, trait worry, intolerance of uncertainty, and threat estimation. Results showed no significant relationship between mnemonic discrimination and baseline OCD symptom severity. Over the course of treatment, mnemonic discrimination did not change significantly, nor was it associated with OCD symptom reduction. Notably, however, there was a significant interaction between poor mnemonic discrimination and high trait worry to predict more severe OCD symptoms at baseline. Findings suggested that while mnemonic discrimination alone might not be a risk factor for OCD severity or impact treatment response, it could be a potential transdiagnostic risk factor that exacerbates internalizing symptoms when co-present with other cognitive vulnerabilities. Title: Digital influences on green economic participation: The role of eWOM in shaping circular consumption among young vietnamese consumers
Abstract: Circular business models (CBMs) are increasingly recognized as a strategic mechanism for advancing sustainable consumption and supporting green economic growth, particularly in emerging economies where rising consumption intensifies pressures on natural resources and waste management systems. Concurrently, the rapid expansion of social media and digital commerce has elevated electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) to a central role in shaping how young consumers interpret, evaluate, and normalize sustainability-oriented business practices. Despite this growing intersection, limited empirical evidence explains how specific attributes of eWOM translate into consumers’ intentions to participate in CBMs, especially in developing-market contexts such as Vietnam. Addressing this gap, the present study adopts a quantitative approach using survey data from 1,142 young Vietnamese consumers to examine how core dimensions of eWOM influence information acceptance and, subsequently, participation intentions in CBMs within the retail sector. A rigorous multi-stage analytical procedure was employed, including reliability testing, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to validate the measurement model, and structural equation modeling (SEM) to assess the structural relationships among latent constructs. The results indicate that all four eWOM attributes positively influence information acceptance, which in turn significantly drives participation intention. Among these factors, relevance emerges as the most influential attribute, suggesting that sustainability-related messages are most effective when aligned with consumers’ personal needs, values, and decision contexts. The findings also confirm the mediating role of information acceptance in translating eWOM quality into behavioral intention. By validating both the measurement and structural models, this study enhances the robustness of IAM-based explanations in the context of circular consumption and extends the literature on digital influence in emerging markets. Practically, the study highlights the importance of designing relevant, credible, and comprehensive sustainability communication strategies. Nevertheless, the findings should be interpreted with caution due to the cross-sectional design and non-probability sampling approach. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: A production-ready machine learning system for inclusive employment: Requirements engineering and implementation of AI-driven disability job matching platform
Abstract: Employment inclusion of people with disabilities remains critically low in Italy, with only 3.5% employed nationally despite mandatory hiring quotas. Traditional manual matching processes require 30–60 min per candidate, creating bottlenecks that limit service capacity. Our goal is to develop and validate a production-ready machine learning system for disability employment matching that integrates social responsibility requirements while maintaining human oversight in decision-making. We employed participatory requirements engineering with Centro per l'Impiego di Villafranca di Verona professionals. The system implements a seven-model ensemble with parallel hyperparameter optimization using Optuna. Multi-dimensional scoring combines semantic compatibility, geographic distance, and employment readiness assessment. The system achieves a 90.1% F1-score and sub-100 ms response times while processing 500,000 candidate–company combinations in under 10 min. Qualitative expert validation with employment center professionals suggests potential for 60%–100% capacity increases for employment centers. The LightGBM ensemble shows optimal performance with 94.6-second training time. Our findings indicate that advanced AI systems can successfully integrate social responsibility requirements without compromising technical performance. The participatory design methodology provides a replicable framework for developing ethical AI applications in sensitive social domains. Title: When loyalty points become donations: The effects of redeemability, point expiration, and descriptive norm information
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Although loyalty programs and checkout charity are widely implemented across retail industries, the integration of reward point donations into online checkout charity remains rare, and consumer behavior in this context is not yet fully understood. While a few studies have explored reward point donations and generally reported positive consumer responses, to the best of our knowledge, little research has examined how reward point characteristics and situational factors influence consumers' willingness to donate. To address this gap, the present research examines, across three studies, the effect of point redeemability on consumers’ donation intention through online checkout charity, as well as the moderating roles of point expiration and descriptive norm information. Study 1 shows that consumers exhibit higher donation intention when their reward points are non-redeemable than when they are redeemable. Study 2 demonstrates that the interaction between point redeemability and point expiration significantly influences donation intention, while Study 3 shows that the interaction between point redeemability and descriptive norm information also significantly affects donation intention. Authors: Chenhao Z.; Hongying T.
Title: Res-PGDnet: A time frequency fusion model with physiologically constrained adversarial training for PPG-based valence–arousal state classification
Abstract: Accurate valence–arousal assessment is crucial for affective computing applications. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is a promising, practical modality for this task, but it poses challenges: signals are noise-prone, the physiological affect mapping is complex and subject-specific, and models generalize poorly. Existing methods often focus narrowly on temporal features, employ physiologically unconstrained robustness strategies, or suffer from a severe performance–efficiency trade-off. We propose Res-PGDnet to address these issues via synergistic time frequency fusion and physiologically constrained adversarial training. Its core innovations are (i) applying adversarial perturbations constrained by physiological priors to model parameters to ensure robust, plausible learning and (ii) hierarchically integrating DCT attention modules to jointly enhance temporal and spectral feature representations. On the DEAP-PPG dataset, Res-PGDnet achieves 93.47% intra-subject accuracy and 92.46% Macro-F1 score, with strong robustness (metric: 0.920) and 85.1% cross-subject accuracy. The model is efficient (12.5 M parameters, 1250 FPS), demonstrating potential for wearable-based valence–arousal classification in settings like mental health monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Palma-Lopez M.; Galindo-Mendez L.R.
Title: Urine culture contamination in a tertiary hospital: Demographic predictors and direct economic impact
Abstract: Background Pre-analytical sample contamination is a significant pre-analytical error that hinders diagnostic efficiency and increases laboratory costs. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical-demographic factors associated with contamination and quantify its direct economic impact in a tertiary hospital. Methods An observational, retrospective study was conducted on 2835 urine cultures processed between January and June 2025. Contamination was defined according to CLSI PRE05 guidelines. Direct costs (reagents and consumables) were calculated. Data normality was assessed using Q–Q plots, and cost distributions were compared using the non-parametric Kruskal–Wallis test. Results Of the total samples, 31.4% were positive, 64.7% negative, and 3.8% contaminated. Multivariable analysis identified age ≥ 60 years and female sex as independent predictors of urine culture contamination. Patients aged ≥60 years accounted for 44.9% of all contaminated samples. ESKAPE pathogens represented 81% of positive isolates. The total cost for urine cultures was $37,728 USD, with contamination representing a direct loss of $873 USD (2.3% of the urine culture budget). Kruskal-Wallis analysis confirmed that contamination costs constitute a significant and avoidable financial burden ( p < 0.0001). Conclusions Older adults (>60 years) and female patients had a higher risk of urine culture contamination. Although the absolute cost of contamination may appear marginal, it reflects a preventable diagnostic inefficiency that delays treatment in a clinical setting dominated by ESKAPE pathogens. Implementing assisted collection protocols for geriatric patients is a necessary cost-effective strategy to optimize institutional resources and patient safety. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Riveted Fe–N5 moieties confined in curved graphitic carbon enable a triple-protection mechanism for robust acidic oxygen reduction electrocatalysis
Abstract: Fe–N–C exhibits exceptional catalytic activity and stands as a prominent representative of single-atom catalysts (SACs). However, the activity and, especially, the stability of its active sites pose a formidable challenge for practical applications. Therefore, we first performed DFT predictions on active site structural models featuring curvature and axial coordination, revealing that the curved Fe–N5 configuration simultaneously boosts both the activity and stability. Then we adopt an O-Tolidine molecular-induced strategy to construct the curved graphitic carbon layers, which anchor Fe single atoms in a bent and axial N-coordinated configuration. The molecular-assisted effect facilitates micropore formation, accelerates the graphitization process, and simultaneously provides additional nitrogen coordination sites, ultimately achieving the curved Fe–N5 configuration. The curved Fe–N5 motifs establish a triple protection mechanism: resistance to Fe dissolution, suppression of carbon corrosion and shielding against H⁺ attack, thus alleviating the long-standing activity–stability trade-off in SACs. Benefiting from these structural merits, the as-obtained catalyst delivers outstanding durability in H2-O2 fuel cell, achieving a high peak power density of 1.37 W cm−2 with only 10.2% performance degradation after 10,000 square-wave cycles—far lower than the 29.8% loss of conventional Fe–N–C. Under H2-Air conditions at 0.65 V, it retains 74.3% of its initial current density over 200 h. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: An AI-driven clinical decision support system for coronary artery disease prediction in T2DM patients using clinical laboratory parameters and deep fusion learning
Abstract: This article presents an intelligent clinical decision support system that integrates graph-based modelling and deep fusion learning for coronary artery disease (CAD) risk prediction using a clinical Laboratory and validated dataset. Title: Ultrasonic vocalizations as markers of anxiety and depression in rodent models of neurotrauma
Abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) and traumatic brain injury (TBI) are severe events that cause lasting sensorimotor and autonomic impairments. Both injuries often also lead to psychological and somatosensory dysfunctions such as anxiety, depression, or pain. Preclinical assessment of anxiety and depression in rodents often relies on locomotion-based behavioural tests confounded by motor deficits and pain-related changes. Because rodents cannot self-report sensory or emotional experiences, behavioural outcomes are limited to observable proxies of anxiety and depression. Ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) offer a complementary, non-locomotor tool that may capture anxiety- and depression-relevant context not detected by behavioural tests. Despite extensive USV research in stress, reward, and social behaviour, applications to neurotrauma remain underexplored, with no studies directly examining USVs in relation to anxiety- or depression-like outcomes after SCI. Even so, evidence from related fields and the limited neurotrauma literature suggests that USVs warrant further exploration as affective readouts after TBI and particularly SCI. USVs may complement behavioural testing by providing socioaffective context without relying on locomotor performance, potentially helping distinguish post-injury anxiety- and depression-like phenotypes from pain-related and other injury-associated changes. By integrating behavioural, neural, and pharmacological evidence, we highlight how USV features may reflect affective dimensions relevant to post-injury anxiety- and depression-like states and outline methodological considerations for validity and specificity. Machine-learning approaches further enable high-throughput, objective detection of subtle affective shifts. With development of collaborative datasets, these methods could reveal consistent affective vocal patterns and lay groundwork for a rudimentary ‘lexicon’ of rodent affect. Integrating USV analysis into neurotrauma and CNS disease research may refine preclinical models of affective dysfunction and improve triangulated evaluation of treatments targeting chronic mental health outcomes. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Gipperth J.
Title: Epistemic justice and deep-sea mining: UNCLOS’s facilitation of epistemic diversity the International Seabed Authority’s decision-making process
Abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. The paper reflects on epistemic justice in energy- and ocean governance, and asks whether and how United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) facilitates that such justice is sought in the regulatory process of deep sea mining by focusing on procedural rules for the International Seabed Authority (ISA) and the representation of different knowers in the decision-making process, including its Council's structure, authority, and composition. It concludes that a very small number of individuals has the power to bring about a very large change in deep sea mining regulations, currently without legal requirements to include experiential, traditional or other forms of knowledges beyond the scientific method in the decision-making process. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zawada-Tomkiewicz A.
Title: A unified micro–macro stochastic framework for tool wear evolution and lifetime prediction
Abstract: Tool wear results from the interaction of numerous micro-scale contact regions subjected to mechanical, thermal and tribological loading. This paper proposes a physics-informed micro–macro stochastic framework linking contact-scale degradation processes with engineering-scale prediction of wear evolution and tool life. At the micro-contact level, tool degradation is represented by a population of interacting contacts undergoing wear, load redistribution and local instability. Model reduction leads to a state-dependent stochastic differential equation whose drift and diffusion terms describe macroscopic flank-wear evolution, while a jump component represents intermittent degradation events. Abrasion/ploughing, adhesion/BUE, thermal–oxidative and diffusion–chemical wear are represented as dominant degradation mechanisms, whereas coating protection and edge instability are treated as latent degradation states. Tool life is formulated as a first-passage problem with respect to a prescribed wear limit. Model parameters are identified from experimentally reconstructed wear increments, with different tribological systems represented using the same stochastic formulation through coefficient calibration. Validation is performed at three complementary levels: predictive assessment of wear evolution, statistical evaluation of degradation dynamics and independent physical validation. The framework reproduces nonlinear wear evolution and increasing degradation variability, while the inferred mechanism hierarchy and latent degradation states are qualitatively supported by independent experimental evidence. The proposed methodology bridges tribological processes at the micro-contact scale and stochastic reliability assessment at the engineering scale, integrating wear evolution, mechanism interpretation and tool-life prediction within a unified physics-informed framework. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Elidrissi R.; Kertechian K.S.
Title: Technostress in the age of digital transformation and AI: A bibliometric–systematic literature review for HRM research
Abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are reshaping human resource management through algorithmic recruitment, automated evaluation, predictive analytics, and generative tools. While these systems improve efficiency, they also intensify technostress through opacity, surveillance, reduced control, and digitally intensified work arrangements. Responding to a fragmented literature spanning both AI-enabled and broader digital work systems, this study provides a B-SLR that maps technostress in digital transformation while identifying AI-specific stressors as a key emerging stream for HRM research. Drawing on 194 Scopus-indexed articles, we combine performance analysis and science mapping to identify publication trends, dominant themes, and intellectual structures. The review shows how AI-specific stressors extend established technostress mechanisms and shift attention toward transparency, control, fairness, and responsible HRM design. We conclude with actionable implications for researchers and practitioners aiming to design more transparent, responsible, and sustainable digital and AI-enabled HRM systems. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Li X.; Meng H.
Title: The allure of imperfection: How ugly-cute aesthetics drive purchase intentions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The rise of social media has increased both aesthetic diversity and consumer attention to product appearance and emotional appeal. This research examines the commercially successful yet under-researched “ugly-cute” aesthetic, exemplified by products like Pop Mart's LABUBU. Moving beyond traditional approaches that treat beauty (or ugliness) and cuteness as separate dimensions, we investigate their interactive effects through four studies: one field experiment and three online experiments, involving participants from both China and the United States. Our findings show that the combination of ugly-cute configurations can attenuate the purchase-intention disadvantage associated with ugliness-related aesthetic deviation, with this effect explained by perceived social value and moderated by consumption setting (public vs. private). Specifically, this effect is more pronounced in public consumption settings, where consumers are more likely to seek social approval and positive evaluation from others, thereby amplifying perceived social value in purchase decisions. These results advance the literature on product design and consumer aesthetics by identifying a psychological explanation underlying consumer responses to atypical aesthetics, and provide practical insights for designing products that generate perceived social value (e.g., feeling accepted, gaining approval, or being positively regarded by others). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Beyond the hotspots: Identifying public opinion blind spots and agenda-setting dynamics in crisis information generation
Abstract: During sudden crises, a structural mismatch between social media attention and governance value often marginalizes key crisis issues, creating public opinion blind spots that undermine effective emergency management. Using the 2021 Henan rainstorm as a case study (N = 40,160), this study proposes an integrated framework to identify public opinion blind spots and examine their agenda-setting dynamics.
