Bootstrap estimation further assesses the association between blind spots and agenda-setting effects. Results show that blind spots vary dynamically across the 4R phases, with Prevention Education, Disaster Causation, and Review and Improvement recurring most frequently. Bidirectional agenda-setting effects can emerge at a 1-hour resolution, and stronger agenda guidance from authoritative users is associated with blind-spot mitigation. Ultimately, these findings offer practical implications for optimizing crisis information supply and strengthening social resilience. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Gas-solid interfacial photoelectrocatalysis for toluene mineralization with concomitant hydrogen peroxide generation

Abstract: The abatement of gaseous volatile organic compounds (VOCs) such as toluene is constrained by sluggish mass transfer and the trade-off between adsorption and oxidation activity in conventional liquid-phase systems. In situ tests confirm the complete mineralization without accumulation of toxic intermediates, and theoretical calculations elucidate the increased electron density near the Fermi level, which significantly enhances the adsorption of both toluene and O2. Title: Adsorption performance of radial-flow contactors for direct air capture: A computational study
Abstract: The need for efficient direct air capture (DAC) is increasing as the global mean temperature continues to rise and a large fraction of CO2 emissions cannot be addressed by conventional CO2 capture technologies. For adsorption-based DAC, the geometry of the gas-solid contactor is an important design parameter because it determines pressure losses, sorbent utilisation, and the efficiency of the process. This study investigates the adsorption stage in a centripetal Z-type radial-flow adsorber for DAC. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model is adopted to simulate the gas flow through the porous bed of adsorbent particles adsorbing CO2 from the gas with the help of the linear driving force model and the Toth isotherms. The material properties are experimentally obtained for a commercial amine-functionalised resin. Twelve different configurations of the contactor are analysed with various bed aspect ratios and radius ratios while keeping the bed volume constant. The simulations indicate that the geometry strongly affects the flow distribution, pressure drop, and adsorption time, which affect the specific energy requirement and productivity of the adsorption stage of the DAC process. Configuration selection represents the trade-off between low energy requirements (at high bed aspect ratio and radius ratio), low space requirements, and construction material costs (at low bed aspect ratio and radius ratio). Title: Divergent relationships between moral disengagement and cyberbullying bystander response behaviors: Examining the amplifying roles of humor and anonymity
Abstract: While bystander response behaviors are pivotal for cyberbullying (CB) intervention, prior research has yielded inconsistent findings regarding their correlates, partly because it has often treated diverse bystander responses as a monolithic construct and failed to distinguish constructive defense from aggressive defense. Furthermore, few empirical studies have examined how digital affordances interact with individual factors in relation to diverse bystander responses within a Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) framework. To address these gaps, this study examined the main and interactive associations of individual moral disengagement (MD), perceived anonymity, and humor of CB with four distinct online bystander responses (constructive defense, aggressive defense, inaction, and reinforcement). A final analytic sample of 1201 Chinese secondary school students, selected via multi-stage random sampling, completed a survey assessing MD, CB contexts, and real online bystander responses. Multilevel analysis indicated that MD, perceived anonymity and humor were consistently and negatively associated with constructive defense but positively associated with inaction. Conversely, MD and anonymity were positively associated with aggressive defense, whereas humor showed no significant link. Regarding reinforcement behaviors, perceived anonymity and humor were positive predictors, whereas MD exerted a non-significant association. Moderation analyses revealed that anonymity strengthened MD's positive associations with inaction and reinforcement, whereas humor amplified MD's association solely with reinforcement. Title: Deep spectral unmixing unfolding network for multispectral and hyperspectral image fusion
Abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) comprise tens to hundreds of contiguous narrow spectral bands, imposing substantial computational demands on HSI processing. However, the strong similarity between adjacent bands creates considerable redundancy, whose reduction is essential for computationally efficient processing. We propose a multispectral and hyperspectral image fusion (MHIF) framework, termed the Deep Spectral Unmixing Unfolding (DSUU) network, from a matrix factorization perspective. DSUU exploits sparsity priors through a spectral unmixing model to reduce information redundancy. It then applies proximal gradient optimization and unfolds its iterations into a deep network, improving the efficiency of conventional model-driven optimization. The proximal operators for endmembers and abundances use 1D- and 2D-DWT-based blocks to mitigate errors arising from inaccurate initialization. To capture spatial-spectral correlations overlooked by matrix factorization, we introduce a Spatial-Spectral Refinement Block (SSRB) comprising a multiscale spatial module and a spectral attention module. Experiments on three benchmark datasets show that DSUU achieves a more favorable trade-off between fusion quality and computational complexity than state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. By integrating data-driven learning with model-driven optimization, DSUU retains an interpretable algorithmic structure while achieving efficient and high-quality fusion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Gaussian Splatting for real-time scene reconstruction: Methods, systems, and trade-offs
Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) allows for high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis. Title: Enhancing situational awareness in health systems: A scoping review of technologies and cross-industry insights
Abstract: Background: Situational awareness technologies are increasingly utilised in healthcare systems to facilitate timely and coordinated decision-making. Reported implementation considerations include data quality, governance, and integration into everyday workflows. Objective: This scoping review aimed to map technologies, systems, and methods used to enhance situational awareness in health service delivery and to identify approaches used in other industries that could be adapted for healthcare, particularly in regional and remote settings. Methods: We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance for scoping reviews. Electronic databases (PubMed and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between January 2000 and October 2025. Reference lists and citation searches in Google Scholar were also examined. Records meeting the inclusion criteria were screened and reviewed, with key data extracted using a structured charting form and synthesised into seven application domains. Results: Searches identified 744 records, of which 23 studies were included. These covered diverse technologies such as dashboards, forecasting models, alert systems, and geospatial decision environments. Most studies were from high-income countries (n = 19). Studies reported potential benefits for visibility, coordination, and decision-making. However, most evidence was descriptive, with limited evidence of whether these systems improve service delivery. Recurrent implementation challenges included data fragmentation, limited interoperability, and misalignment between governance and workflow. Conclusions: This review highlights the need for more rigorous and context-sensitive evaluations of technologies used to enhance situational awareness in healthcare, especially in regional and resource-limited settings. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

Authors: Xiang M.; Gao Z.; Fu W.; Wang C.; Yang F.; Zhou W.; He M.; Wang X.; Deng Y.; Bai J.; Ma S.; Zhang W.; Zhou J.; Su Y.
Title: Breaking selectivity-conversion trade-off for CO2-glycerol carbonylation via constructing ternary active-sites in zeolite-based catalyst
Abstract: Directly converting glycerol (GL) and CO2 into glycerol carbonate (GC) offers a pivotal solution to valorize biodiesel by-products while mitigate greenhouse gas emmissions. However, the chemical inertness of CO2 and the inherent complexity of GL molecular structure pose a significant challenge in balancing activity and selectivity for this reaction. Herein, Lewis and Brønsted acid sites were constructed on the inherent Lewis basic sites within ETS-10 zeolite, leading to the formation of a ternary-active-sites Zn(Otf)x/ETS-10 catalyst for overcoming the long-standing trade-off between activity and selectivity in CO2-GL carbonylation. The tailored Lewis and Brønsted acid sites synergistically anchor GL molecules and provide a novel mode for their targeted activation, resulting in an intriguing 11-membered ring-shaped Zn-GL* intermediate. Subsequently, the direct cyclization with the adjacent bi-COO* species formed by CO2 activation on Lewis basic sites promotes GC production while suppressing the side reactions that consume both GL and GC. Ultimately, by using CaC2 as a solid dehydrating agent, a 95.2% of GC selectivity and 40.9% of GL conversion were achieved within the regular and enlarged 12-membered ring (12-RS) of the ETS-10 framework. This work offers valuable insights into the rational design of active sites for highly active and selective carbonylation catalysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang W.; Dong L.; Fang Y.; Yang X.; Chen Z.; Li Z.; Chen G.; Ning S.
Title: Multi‑objective optimisation and experimental validation of a compact energy‑efficient active regeneration burner for diesel particulate filter regeneration
Abstract: Active regeneration burners are essential for diesel particulate filter (DPF) regeneration. However, they are often constrained by low flow utilisation, excessive gas velocity, and inadequate mixing between combustion products and exhaust gas, leading to poor thermal efficiency and degraded regeneration performance. To tackle these challenges, this study focused on achieving a compact and lightweight burner design via iterative and dimensional optimisation. A multi‑objective optimisation framework incorporating Response Surface Methodology (RSM), Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III), and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was then established to enhance the combustion performance. The effectiveness of this optimisation approach was verified through regeneration experiments. The optimised design reduced burner volume and mass by 57.7 % and 39.5 %, respectively, while maintaining outlet velocity uniformity above 97 % across three investigated exhaust-flow conditions. Outlet temperature uniformity increased from 82.8 % to 92.2 %, the maximum measured outlet temperature at the five-point thermocouple plane increased from 865 °C to 970 °C, and thermal efficiency increased from 38.8 % to 51.1 %. The time required for the DPF upstream temperature to reach 600 °C decreased from 200 s to 172 s, while the regeneration efficiency increased from 92 % to 94 %. Smoke opacity, HC, and CO decreased from 3.9 % to 3.1 %, 28 ppm to 8 ppm, and 0.205 vol% to 0.100 vol%, respectively; however, NOx increased from 104.5 ppm to 117.0 ppm, indicating a trade-off between oxidation completeness and NOx formation. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the burner for compact and energy-efficient diesel aftertreatment systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Automated analysis of prosodic and conversational speech markers for autism spectrum disorder screening and severity estimation
Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with clinically meaningful differences in speech, prosody, and reciprocal communication; however, these markers are difficult to quantify consistently during routine screening. This study investigates whether automatically extracted acoustic, prosodic, and conversational speech markers can support objective ASD screening and severity estimation. We present SpectrumNet, a speech-marker modeling framework designed to analyze communication-relevant features rather than replacing clinical diagnosis. The framework combines a multi-scale acoustic encoder, a prosody encoder, and a conversational-dynamics encoder to represent voice quality, rhythm, intonation, speech rate, pause behavior, and turn-taking patterns. A cross-domain feature disentanglement module separates ASD-relevant communication markers from speaker identity and emotional variation, while a hierarchical attention mechanism identifies patterns across short-, medium-, and longer-range temporal scales. The model was evaluated using five publicly available datasets, with ASDSpeech serving as the primary clinical benchmark and ADOS-2 scores used for severity estimation. On ASDSpeech, SpectrumNet achieved 93.10% accuracy, 92.80% F1-score, and 95.50% AUC for ASD versus typically developing classification. Severity estimates were strongly associated with ADOS-2 scores, including a Pearson correlation of 0.891 for the total score. Cross-dataset testing on AV-ASD showed 78.43% zero-shot accuracy and 85.20% accuracy after minimal fine-tuning, suggesting partial generalizability across recording settings. These findings support the potential value of speech-based computational markers as an adjunctive screening aid for communication-disorder assessment, while highlighting the need for larger, clinically diverse, and prospectively validated cohorts before diagnostic deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Polyethylene gasification in a bubbling fluidized bed: Operating-parameter effects on syngas, tar and soot formation
Abstract: Plastic gasification offers a route to recover polymer carbon as synthesis gas; changes in operating conditions affect both syngas properties and the partitioning of carbon among gaseous, condensable, and solid products. This study investigates these effects during polyethylene gasification in an electrically heated lab-scale bubbling fluidized bed. Experimental series varied temperature (750–850 °C), equivalence ratio (ER; 0.20–0.30), and steam-to-carbon ratio (S/C; 0.25–0.75), with additional tests assessing the influence of feed rate and oxygen enrichment. Raising temperature increased H2 and CO yields, doubled gas yield from 0.90 to 1.74 Nm3/kgdaf, and raised carbon conversion efficiency to 93%, while shifting condensables from aliphatics toward aromatics/PAHs. Increasing ER to 0.30 lowered condenser-collected tar but increased soot sixfold and produced less favourable methanol-relevant stoichiometry, showing a trade-off between tar reduction, soot formation, and syngas quality. Steam addition suppressed soot by almost one order of magnitude, but H2, CO, and gas yields peaked at S/C = 0.50, with limited further conversion benefit at higher S/C. Oxygen enrichment from 30% to 72%, with additional steam moderating bed temperature, maintained gas-phase carbon conversion with only a minor reduction in cold-gas efficiency. Paired in-reactor and downstream sampling tracked gas evolution through the freeboard, showing continued olefin conversion and H2 formation consistent with kinetic-model predictions at an imposed 850 °C. C2H4 in the product gas accounted for 25–35% of feed carbon under all conditions. Further hydrocarbon conversion, contaminant removal, and H2 adjustment would therefore be required before the syngas could be used for methanol synthesis. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Conflict expression: A decade of group conflict research
Abstract: The conflict expression framework was developed to generate new practical and theoretical insights into how conflict communication affects group processes and negotiated outcomes. The framework proposes that conflict expressions vary along two dimensions: directness and oppositional intensity. The framework suggested that the effects of different types of conflict on group processes and outcomes likely depend on how the conflict is expressed, that conflict within groups is likely perceived differently by different members of the same social unit, and that conflict affects negotiation processes dynamically through reciprocated statements and responses. We review research building on the framework – including empirical tests of the main propositions, methodological advances, and as a theoretical foundation for conflict communication research more broadly – and identify directions for the future. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Tang R.; Men X.; Gu Y.; Bi L.
Title: Proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cells with La0.5Sr0.5Fe0.75X0.25O3 (X=Co,Ni, Cu) cathodes: a comparative study
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: To enhance the cathode performance of La0.5Sr0.5FeO3 (LSF) in proton‑conducting solid oxide fuel cells (H‑SOFCs), different transition metal elements (Co, Ni, Cu) are introduced at the Fe site, forming the composition La0.5Sr0.5Fe0.75X0.25O3 (X = Co, Ni, Cu). Ni doping is the most effective in promoting oxygen vacancy formation, oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity, and proton migration. H-SOFCs employing the Ni-doped LSF cathode achieve higher power output and lower polarization losses than those using Co- or Cu-doped counterparts. Furthermore, the Ni-doped LSF material is evaluated in composite cathodes. A trade-off exists between the ORR activity of the Ni-doped LSF cathode and the proton conduction provided by the proton conductor. The optimal composition was found to contain 10 wt% proton conductor, yielding a peak power density of 1456 mW cm−2 at 700 °C. This result represents a substantial improvement in the performance of LSF-based cathodes for H-SOFCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A learning-based robust framework for chest X-ray pneumonia classification: Privacy-preserving deep learning with adversarial training
Abstract: Chest X-ray classifiers must protect patient data without sacrificing diagnostic utility or robustness to adversarial perturbations. We propose a multi-objective framework that integrates differential privacy with adversarial training through sample-adaptive gradient clipping, dynamic privacy-budget allocation, and structure-aware adversarial sample generation. Experiments on ChestX-ray14 and the COVID-19 Radiography Database evaluate clean accuracy, adversarial accuracy, and resistance to membership inference attacks. At a privacy budget of ε=1.0, the proposed method achieves 87.3% clean accuracy, 65.1% adversarial accuracy, and a membership inference attack success rate of 54.1%. Ablation results show that each adaptive component contributes to the observed privacy–utility–robustness trade-off. An exploratory diabetic-retinopathy experiment further examines transfer to a different imaging modality. © 2026

Title: Encountering the “familiar stranger”: Activating latent cultural identification among Vietnamese tourists in China
Abstract: Tourism studies have largely examined cultural identification through encounters with difference, while paying less attention to culturally proximate travel contexts. Drawing on schema theory, this study examines how latent cultural identification (LCI) emerges when sedimented cultural meanings become perceptible and interpretable during travel. Based on interviews with 41 Vietnamese tourists traveling in China, the findings indicate that material, social, and mediated cues make routinized meanings noticeable, while internalized cultural schemata help tourists interpret them in relation to their cultural self-understanding. Affective resonance amplifies this process by intensifying the salience and self-relevance of interpreted meanings. Behavioural responses vary across compliance, inquiry, reinterpretation, and co-creation, reflecting different degrees of self-reflection and social embeddedness. By highlighting the role of cultural schemata in LCI, this study extends tourism identity research and shows how LCI can help tourists locate their own culture within the wider world-cultural landscape, enrich personal meaning-making, and foster intercultural exchange. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mn-doped polysaccharide-derived calcium-based sorbents with enhanced CO2 capture and cyclic stability
Abstract: Rapid CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel combustion have intensified the demand for efficient carbon-capture technologies. Calcium looping (CaL) is considered a promising option because of its high theoretical capacity and low material cost; however, severe sintering of CaO-based sorbents during repeated carbonation–calcination cycles results in rapid performance degradation. Mn-doped polysaccharide-derived CaO-based sorbents (Mn-PDCA) were prepared through a microtitration–wet-impregnation route to improve their cyclic CO2-capture performance. Among the prepared sorbents, 15Mn-PDCA exhibited the best overall performance, achieving an initial CO2 uptake of 0.474 g/g and retaining 0.417 g/g after 15 cycles under mild conditions, corresponding to a capacity retention of approximately 87.97%. Its initial uptake was 65.73% higher than that of Mn-free 0Mn-PDCA. Comprehensive experimental characterization indicated that the enhanced performance originated from the coordinated effects of Mn-associated surface regulation, Ca–Mn mixed-oxide pinning, XG-directed porous-structure formation, and residual-carbon confinement. Mixed Mn valence states and defect-associated oxygen species contributed to favorable surface chemical environments for CO2 adsorption, while thermally stable CaMnO3 and Ca4Mn3O10 phases acted as interfacial or grain-boundary barriers that restrained CaO crystallite migration and coalescence during cycling. Meanwhile, XG directed precursor nucleation and promoted the formation of porous microspheres, with the retained carbonaceous species providing an additional spatial-confinement effect. Excessive Mn loading at 20% caused Mn-rich aggregation, partial pore blockage, and dilution of active CaO, revealing a capacity–stability trade-off. These findings demonstrate a coordinated template–metal regulation strategy for developing sintering-resistant CaO-based sorbents for calcium-looping CO2 capture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Experimental investigation of different CO2 injection schemes to enhance oil recovery in sandstone reservoir
Abstract: Application of carbon dioxide injection to enhance oil recovery is one of the best strategies to achieve a balance between energy security and reduced atmospheric emissions. Several injection schemes can be adopted to implement carbon dioxide-enhanced oil recovery. Injected CO2 mobilizes trapped oil by developing partial or full miscibility through diffusion, oil swelling, and viscosity reduction, but mechanisms such as viscous fingering, gravity override, and early gas breakthrough limit recovery efficiency. This study presents an experimental investigation of four different CO2 injection schemes, including continuous gas injection (CGI), cyclic injection (huff-n-puff), water-alternating-gas (WAG), and polymer-assisted WAG (PWAG) for enhancing oil recovery. Core was characterized for mineralogy, porosity, permeability, and wettability, while density, API gravity, rheology, and safety–critical properties of crude oil were evaluated. Core-flooding experiments were conducted at 70 °C and 800 psi overburden pressure, beginning with secondary waterflooding followed by tertiary CO2-EOR. Waterflooding recovered 47.47 % of the original oil in place (OOIP), leaving 52.53 % OOIP as the target for EOR method. CGI, cyclic, WAG, and PWAG injection schemes using CO2 resulted in significant incremental recovery. The results highlighted the critical role of mobility control in improving sweep efficiency, incremental oil recovery, and effective CO2 utilization by establishing a clear performance hierarchy: PWAG ' WAG ' CGI ' cyclic injection. Title: Unlocking reversible hydrogen storage in penta-hexa-hepta graphene through lithium functionalization
Abstract: A newly proposed two-dimensional carbon allotrope, penta–hexa–hepta graphene (PHH-Gr), is systematically investigated as a potential hydrogen storage medium using first-principles calculations. The thermodynamic, dynamical, and thermal robustness of PHH-Gr are verified through cohesive energy evaluation, phonon spectrum analysis, and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. Lithium decoration is found to be energetically favorable, with Li atoms strongly anchored at heptagonal hollow sites and minimal clustering tendency due to large Li–Li separations and high diffusion barriers. Electronic structure analysis demonstrates substantial charge transfer from Li to the PHH-Gr substrate while preserving metallic characteristics. Hydrogen adsorption on pristine PHH-Gr is weak, whereas Li functionalization markedly enhances H2 binding through polarization and charge-transfer effects. Each Li species can adsorb up to four hydrogen molecules, yielding a maximum gravimetric and volumetric hydrogen storage capacities of 10.75 wt% and 91.2 g L−1, respectively. Thermodynamic analysis using differential adsorption energies reveals that while the maximum storage capacity requires cryogenic temperatures or elevated pressures, a practical working capacity of approximately 6–8 wt% is achievable under reversible cycling conditions (298 K, 30 bar for uptake; 373 K, 3 bar for release). AIMD simulations also verify that the weakly bound fourth H2 molecule per Li site desorbs at room temperature under ambient pressure. These results highlight Li-decorated PHH-Gr as a robust and efficient material for reversible hydrogen storage applications with a working capacity exceeding DOE targets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Positive emotion dispositions and human values in a Brazilian sample: Structural evaluation and exploratory network analysis
Abstract: Understanding how positive emotions relate to broader motivational systems across cultural contexts is essential for clarifying their underlying structure. In this study, we examined the organization of positive emotions and their motivational correlates in Brazil, contributing to ongoing debates about the structure and foundations of positive emotions across cultures. Analyzing responses to the Dispositional Positive Emotions Scales (DPES; Shiota et al., 2006 ) in a Brazilian sample ( N = 435), we found mixed fit and reliability across individual scales, but neither the full seven-factor solution nor a previously reported six-factor model adequately fit the data. Following stability-based item pruning, EGA yielded four exploratory communities based on 18 items that cut across the original categories: Social Recognition, Awe & Happiness, Compassionate Caregiving, and Self-Contentment & Growth. We examined how these emergent communities mapped onto values as indicators of motivational goals. Value associations differed across communities, particularly between Compassionate Caregiving and Social Recognition. Overall, the findings identify exploratory item communities showing differentiated associations with several human values in this sample. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yasar D.; Öktem Erkartal P.
Title: Between indeterminacy and intervention: A field-based typology and design framework for interstitial Urban voids
Abstract: Urban voids are increasingly discussed as opportunities for urban transformation, yet they are often treated as a homogeneous category despite their diverse spatial, perceptual, and social characteristics. This study adopts a field-based qualitative research design that combines walking-based observation, standardized field coding, photographic documentation, and matrix-based comparative analysis to examine interstitial urban voids as heterogeneous spatial conditions. Using this research design, 61 interstitial micro voids were documented across four dense urban corridors in Istanbul. Data were recorded through a standardized protocol integrating morphological features, visibility and accessibility, informal use traces, sensory conditions, and perceived safety. The coded variables were then comparatively analysed to construct a typology and to support context-sensitive transformation decisions. Based on the combined evaluation of these variables, six void types were identified: circulation leftover, back-of-house void, residual structural gap, visual relief void, unintentional social pocket, and infrastructure-related void. Findings indicate that transformation potential differs across types and cannot be interpreted through a single factor. Unintentional social pockets and selected visual relief voids were associated with observed social or perceptual value, supporting preservation or light-touch intervention as analytically derived options rather than intensive formalization. By contrast, back-of-house voids and infrastructure-related voids combined poorer maintenance, negative sensory conditions, weaker public integration, and lower observer-based perceived safety, indicating a stronger need for safety-oriented redress before public activation. Circulation leftovers and residual structural gaps occupied an intermediate position, where transformation potential depended on access, visibility, ownership, maintenance, and existing use conditions. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins system: SHAP-coupled entropy-energy-economic analysis and ANN-assisted multi-objective optimization
Abstract: A green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins (MTA/MTO) system offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization and reduce emissions in coal-based chemical production. However, the key variables and subsystem-level contributions affecting overall performance are not fully understood, and achieving efficient, feasible multi-objective optimization is challenging. This study develops an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted multi-objective optimization approach based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-coupled entropy-energy-economic (3E) analysis. The approach integrates ANN-based Pareto region identification with hierarchical Aspen Plus re-evaluation and repair to improve both optimization efficiency and solution feasibility. SHAP-coupled 3E analysis clarifies the roles of decision variables and subsystems in thermodynamic, economic, and energy performance, and highlights trade-offs among entropy generation rate, annual energy cost, and net present value. Results indicate that methanol-related and proton exchange membrane electrolyzer operations primarily influence overall 3E performance, while electrolyzer operation and methanol separation variables are most significant for objective trade-offs. Utilizing an ANN-assisted parallel NSGA-II, a promising Pareto region is identified in surrogate space within 132 s. Following rigorous re-evaluation and SHAP-coupled 3E-informed repair, all ANN-guided solutions converge in the rigorous model, with the relative errors between rigorous objective values and ANN predictions below 1.00 %. Compared to the baseline, the selected compromise solution increases the net present value by 28.48 %, while reducing the overall entropy generation rate by 1.52 % and the annual energy cost by 0.13 %. Title: Contesting Interests Between Institutional Pluralism and People-Centred Development in Natural Resource Management: Lessons from Selous Niassa Wildlife Corridor in Tanzania
Abstract: The debate on institutional pluralism (IP) in relation to natural resources management and people-centred development has become significant in Tanzania and many other developing countries. Mostly, the debates are related to the challenges of balancing conservation goals with people-centred development pathways in natural resources management. The theory of Self-Governance explains how the central government manages resources in community-owned areas. Data were gathered from national- and local-level government, non-governmental, and private-sector institutions relevant to the study, particularly those predominantly involved in natural resources management. The study utilized key informant interviews (KIIs), focus group discussions (FGDs), and household surveys in villages within the Selous-Niassa wildlife corridor (SNWC). The KII and FGD data were analysed using content analysis, and descriptive statistics were computed for the household interview data using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS). The results indicate that the evolution of institutional pluralism progressed through distinct stages, both before and after independence. During the pre-independence period, indigenous knowledge and practices for managing natural resources were destroyed, giving the colonial government power, even though it did not ensure sustainable management. This remained the same until the 1990s, when decentralization and Community-Based Resource Management were established (1990s - present). Tanzania saw increased recognition of the role of institutional pluralism in natural resource management. However, the increased recognition did not align with the current management status of natural resources in the SNWC, where degradation is accelerating due to increased human development. This paper concludes that natural resource management under institutional pluralism is influenced by communities’ development ambitions. This paper calls for strategies that balance the goals of natural resource management and development and recommends natural recovery measures. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Gao B.; Gao S.; Wang X.; Xiang L.; Yuan Y.; Liu Y.
Title: A SIQOR dynamical model for rumor propagation in online social networks with coupled banning and debunking
Abstract: Online social networks (OSNs) often face a counterintuitive challenge during rumor outbreaks: regulatory suppression, such as node-level banning, can paradoxically amplify dissemination. Existing models largely neglect these cascading behavioral responses. To accurately simulate this dynamic and provide a mechanistic interpretation of the Streisand effect, the SIQOR rumor propagation model is proposed in this paper. Moving beyond traditional frameworks, the SIQOR model captures the interaction between platform-level intervention and user behavioral responses, specifically emphasizing how banning stimulates a state of heightened willingness to disseminate the rumor and curiosity among neighboring users. Following theoretical analysis of the system’s dynamic behavior, the model is validated through numerical experiments on synthetic scale-free networks and empirically verified using four real-world Twitter datasets. The results faithfully reproduce the peak scale and long-tail decay of actual rumor outbreaks. Crucially, while raising the baseline banning rate monotonically suppresses the peak scale of active spreaders, aggressive early-stage interventions subject to capacity limits conditionally trigger a non-monotonic surge in propagation desire among neighboring users, demonstrating that raising the banning probability mechanically triggers a non-linear surge in propagation desire, thereby proving that the Streisand effect is a predictable dynamical outcome rather than a mere behavioral anomaly. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Liu Y.; Shi Y.; Bu W.; Liu S.
Title: A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
Abstract: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Existing research indicates that approximately 80% of strategic initiatives fail due to employee resistance to change or capability deficits. Furthermore, nearly three-quarters of middle managers and staff exhibit resistance toward such transformations. This alarming trend raises a fundamental question: how can the hospitality industry navigate the inherent tension between high-touch emotional labor and digital depersonalization to transform employee resistance into proactive adoption? While traditional research frequently focuses on hotel management as change promoters, this study shifts the analytical focus to hotel employees as change recipients. Guided by cognitive appraisal and social information processing theories, within the context of hotel service scenarios, this research constructs models of resistance mitigation and antecedent condition linkages across individual, organizational, and managerial levels. Through an empirical analysis of 545 survey responses from various hotel categories and the application of fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study systematically explores the mechanisms of resistance alleviation and the synergistic effects of the identified influencing factors. Regression results indicate that digital literacy, digital strategy consensus, and perceptions of digital technology warmth and capability are negatively associated with hotel employee resistance to digital transformation. Additionally, organizational strategic flexibility and digital leadership positively moderate the relationships between these individual factors and resistance. The fsQCA results further identify two primary equifinal patterns sufficient for fostering a state of low resistance, demonstrating how strong digital leadership serves as a social cue that effectively compensates for the absence of organizational strategic flexibility. Ultimately, this research deepens the understanding of human-centered digital transformation in the hospitality sector and offers theoretical frameworks for managers to mitigate employee resistance to digital initiatives, thereby facilitating successful strategic implementation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhao X.; Huang H.; Bai N.; Chen Y.; Zhang Y.; Wang M.; Lu Y.
Title: From perceived attractiveness to visitation: Multi-scale measurement and influencing factors across 143 Chinese historic cities
Abstract: Effective tourism management requires understanding how attraction attributes and supporting factors shape tourists’ perceived attractiveness, and how these in turn translate into visitation. We develop a tourist-centered framework using 610,136 reviews across 2128 heritage attractions in 143 cities, measuring multi-scale perceived attractiveness with a large language model pipeline and visitation with review volume, then identifying the factors that influence both metrics using XGBoost and SHAP. Results show that (1) perceived attractiveness and visitation share a multi-core spatial structure, while visitation displays a polarized long-tail distribution; (2) attraction attributes, especially official designation, visual quality, and ticket pricing, dominate both metrics but shape them differently; (3) positively perceived social, economic, scientific, historic and aesthetical values increase visitation, whereas political value is negatively associated; and (4) accessibility and spatial agglomeration also contribute positively. Practically, multi-scale benchmarking identifies underperforming attractions, while attraction-scale value profiles and the identified influencing factors guide targeted strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effect of hemp protein isolate on the quality and in vitro digestion of high moisture plant-based meat
Abstract: Plant-based meat (PBM) offers high protein, low fat, and cholesterol-free benefits, yet optimizing its nutritional and functional quality remains a challenge. This study incorporated hemp protein isolate (HPI) into soy protein–wheat gluten blends to produce PBM via high-moisture extrusion, examining HPI effects on quality, structure, digestibility, and bioactivity. Results showed that HPI improved mechanical properties, color, and fiber formation; at 40% HPI, disulfide bonds peaked, enhancing water-holding capacity and network density. During in vitro digestion, HPI reduced α-helix/β-sheet ratios and increased random coils, facilitating enzyme access. Protein digestibility peaked at 30% HPI (48.47% gastric, 84.52% intestinal), yielding more small peptides. Although total peptide counts dropped, 28 unique HPI-derived peptides appeared, with six predicted in silico as potential α-glucosidase inhibitors. Moderate HPI addition thus improves PBM quality and digestibility while offering potential bioactivity, providing a theoretical basis for functional PBM development. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhao H.; Shi R.
Title: Why disaster experience does not always improve Preparedness: The role of disaster learning and heterogeneous effects
Abstract: The frequency and severity of natural disasters and public emergencies have continued to increase worldwide. Household preparedness plays a vital role in disaster risk reduction, yet the effect of disaster-related experience on preparedness remains inconclusive. Using survey data from 5,862 residents in China, this study separately examines the associations of past disaster experience and disaster learning with household preparedness. Conventional regression models and a causal forest approach are used to estimate average associations and explore heterogeneous effects across individuals. The results show that disaster learning, rather than past disaster experience, is positively associated with preparedness behavior, highlighting the importance of capacity building. In addition, both past disaster experience and disaster learning exhibit heterogeneous effects across individuals. Feature importance analysis further indicates that social capital, emergency awareness, and community infrastructure are important influential factors associated with preparedness behavior. By introducing a causal forest approach to distinguish the differential effects of past disaster experience and disaster learning, this study provides a more nuanced understanding of household preparedness and offers useful insights for developing more targeted household disaster risk reduction strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Rapid inter-individual vocal interactions in freely behaving rats revealed by acoustic source localization
Abstract: Ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) in rodents have been widely used as indicators of affective states; however, their role in rapid temporal exchange between individuals remains largely unexplored, primarily due to technical limitations in identifying vocalizing individuals during free social interactions. Here, we combined acoustic source localization (USVCAM) with markerless multi-animal tracking to examine the temporal structure of vocal interactions in freely behaving rat dyads. In three dyads with sufficient vocal output, inter-individual vocalization intervals exhibited a clear peak at approximately 50–250 ms, indicating fast temporal exchanges of vocalizations between individuals. To test whether this pattern could arise from independent vocal production, we performed Monte Carlo randomized simulations based on empirically observed intra-individual intervals. The simulated distributions failed to reproduce the empirical peak and instead showed a concentration at shorter intervals, resulting in a significant distributional difference. These results reject the null hypothesis of independent vocal generation and suggest that the observed temporal structure reflects the influence of one individual's vocalizations on those of the other individual. Together, these findings extend the potential applications of rodent USVs, in addition to their established use as affective indicators, by providing a proof-of-principle demonstration of rapid inter-individual vocal exchanges and a tractable experimental framework for investigating the temporal dynamics of social vocal communication. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Shared regulatory systems in memory suppression and fear extinction: An ALE and MACM meta-analysis
Abstract: Memory suppression and fear extinction both reduce the influence of past experiences on current cognition and behavior, but they are typically studied within separate research traditions. The present study examined whether these two processes recruit partially overlapping neural systems involved in the regulation of unwanted memories and previously threat-associated cues. We conducted a preregistered coordinate-based meta-analysis of fMRI studies using activation likelihood estimation (ALE) and meta-analytic connectivity modeling (MACM). The analysis included 63 experiments involving 1452 participants and focused on contrasts commonly used to index retrieval suppression in the Think/No-Think paradigm and threat-cue processing during extinction learning. ALE revealed convergent activation in bilateral inferior frontal gyrus/anterior insula and right inferior parietal lobule. MACM further showed that these regions were embedded within broader executive-control and attention-related coactivation networks. These findings suggest that memory suppression and fear extinction partially converge within broader control- and attention-related systems involved in controlling task-relevant memory and threat representations. At the same time, partly distinct medial temporal and affective-learning patterns point to important domain-specific differences between intentional episodic retrieval suppression and extinction-based threat–safety updating. Overall, the findings help bridge research on memory control and fear extinction by identifying partially overlapping regulatory systems while preserving important theoretical distinctions between the two processes. This framework highlights how control- and attention-related neural systems may contribute to the regulation of unwanted memories and conditioned fear responses through their interactions with memory, threat-learning, and contextual updating processes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Comparing neural signatures of risky decision-making and guaranteed reward processing using a modified Balloon Analogue Risk Task and multi-echo imaging
Abstract: Risky decision making is a fundamental human behavior involving multiple cognitive processes. Understanding how these processes are represented in the brain offers critical insights into decision-making, development, and vulnerabilities to psychopathology. However, functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) research of decision-making under risk and reward often does not clearly distinguish between risky decision processes and response to guaranteed reward and has limited sensitivity to deep subcortical regions, constraining our contributions. In this study, we present a modified Balloon Analogue Risk Task completed under a multi-echo fMRI protocol meant to enhance subcortical signal. Forty-eight participants inflated virtual balloons across three conditions: risky reward, guaranteed reward, and neutral. GLM analyses revealed increased signal in orbitofrontal cortex, anterior insula (AI), striatum and a brain stem nuclei, ventral tegmental area (VTA), during risky reward decision versus guaranteed rewards conditions. Multivariate analysis identified the AI as a key predictor of the risky decision condition, outperforming striatal and VTA contributions. These results suggest risky decision-making shows greater recruitment of reward-relevant regions and illuminates putative neurobiological mechanisms associated with risky decision making relative to guaranteed and non-contingent reward. The study also provides a new tool to enhance the resolution of human neuroscience research on risk-taking across the lifespan and vulnerabilities to psychopathology. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang S.; Tu R.; Zhang W.; Gao Q.; Chen W.; Sun Y.; Xie W.; Li Z.; Tang Y.; Pan F.; Gao G.; Li L.; Ju W.; Jiang E.; Xu X.
Title: Interface-tuned Janus-type high-entropy heterostructures for cascade electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
Abstract: High-entropy materials (HEMs) hold great promise for electrocatalytic applications owing to their tunable electronic structures, particularly in complex reactions involving multiple intermediates. However, HEMs prepared by conventional methods often suffer from a trade-off between site diversity and reaction specificity, resulting in limited catalytic efficiency. In this study, we address this challenge by developing a Janus-type high-entropy alloy/high-entropy layered hydroxide (HEA/HELH) heterostructure with synthetically controllable interfaces via Fe3 +-mediated topochemical reconstruction with precisely controlled reconstruction times of 30–120 min. Leveraging the Fe3+/Fe2+ redox-driven carbon-confined galvanic replacement reaction, we achieved epitaxial interfacial growth and formed a built-in electric field (BIEF) with a work-function difference of 0.54 eV, which lowered the potential required to reach 10 mA cm⁻² by 240 mV. The optimized HEA/HELH heterostructure delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 93.5% for FDCA at 1.55 V vs. RHE and retains more than 90% of its current response over 100 h, comparing favorably with recently reported HMFOR electrocatalysts. Mechanistic studies suggest that interfacial charge redistribution associated with the BIEF facilitates the formation and utilization of high-valence Co/Ni/Fe species, thereby promoting cascade oxidation from HMF to FDCA. Furthermore, the controllable HEA/HELH demonstrates significant potential for broader adaptability in multistep electrocatalytic oxidation. This work provides an interfacial engineering strategy for designing high-entropy catalysts for electrocatalytic biomass valorization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Mapping the global landscape of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship: A bibliometric review (2000–2025)
Abstract: Mentorship is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of women’s entrepreneurial participation and success. However, existing scholarship remains fragmented, conceptually inconsistent, and unevenly distributed across global contexts. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship, examining peer-reviewed literature published between 2000 and 2025 globally. To enhance methodological robustness and address limitations associated with narrow keyword selection, a multi-stage search strategy was employed using the Scopus database. A total of 878 records were identified through the Scopus database. The final dataset includes 621 articles, allowing for a detailed analysis of publication trends, geographic distribution, authorship patterns, and thematic development within the field. The findings reveal a significant concentration of research output in the Global North, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom, with comparatively limited representation from developing regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa. Thematic analysis indicates strong clustering around mentorship, coaching, entrepreneurial ecosystems, and capacity building, highlighting both conceptual convergence and fragmentation. Furthermore, the results show that mentorship is frequently embedded within broader entrepreneurial support frameworks rather than examined as a standalone construct. In response, this study advances a Gendered Social Capital and Learning framework to provide a more integrated understanding of mentorship processes in women’s entrepreneurship. The study contributes to the literature by offering a robust, data-driven overview of the field, identifying key gaps in geographic and theoretical coverage, and highlighting the methodological implications of keyword selection in bibliometric research. The findings provide valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to design more inclusive and contextually relevant mentorship interventions for women entrepreneurs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Evaluating Mild Cognitive Impairment using large language models: A comparative analysis
Abstract: This study evaluates whether fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) can support preliminary screening of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) from transcribed Chinese speech. Using the Chinese subset of the TAUKADIAL/TalkBank connected-speech dataset, we compared Llama3, Gemma, Qwen, and Qwen1.5 models under supervised fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, different quantization settings, automatic speech recognition systems, and prompt styles. The experiments were evaluated with subject-level five-fold cross-validation and reported with mean and standard deviation for accuracy, F1-score, precision, and recall. Among the tested configurations, Llama3-8B with 4-bit QLoRA achieved the strongest performance, with accuracy and F1-score of approximately 0.86. To place these results against transparent alternatives, we added the official TAUKADIAL feature-based benchmarks, which use acoustic eGeMAPS features and interpretable linguistic measures such as token count, type count, type–token ratio, lexical density, and verb and pronoun ratios. Because the official benchmark uses a different multilingual train/test protocol, it is treated as an external reference rather than a head-to-head ranking. The findings suggest that LLM-based transcript analysis may be useful as a low-cost prescreening aid, but the small, language-specific dataset and lack of matched external validation require cautious interpretation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Unraveling the multi-stage damage evolution in architected SiC/SiC composite claddings via quasi-in-situ X-ray computed tomography
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: While multi-layered SiC/SiC composites are essential for accident-tolerant fuels, linking structural architecture to damage evolution remains critical. This study evaluates hoop tensile failure across single-layer, duplex, and triplex claddings using quasi-in-situ XCT, Raman, and EBSD. Results reveal that macroscopic failure is governed by spatial defect distribution, residual stresses, and interlayer. Single-layer claddings exhibit flaw-sensitive failure influenced by the distribution of radially aligned pores. Duplex claddings achieve the highest strength via disrupted defect continuity, favorable compressive residual stresses, and polymorphic (6H/2H-SiC) boundaries that force tortuous crack pathways. Conversely, the triplex architecture exhibits a distinct mechanical trade-off: inner tensile stresses and a thickened PyC interlayer slightly reduce peak strength but trigger extensive interfacial debonding, yielding remarkable pseudo-ductility and damage tolerance. These insights highlight that managing structural architecture and residual stress is critical for optimizing multi-layered SiC/SiC composite claddings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Birdsong with gentle wind selectively benefits stimulus interference but not response or multisource interference: Evidence from EEG
Abstract: Despite the growing threat of urban noise pollution to cognitive health, empirical evidence regarding the cognitive benefits of natural sounds remains mixed. The Specificity Hypothesis addresses this by proposing that such benefits are selective, benefiting only those cognitive functions that are highly matched with directed attention. Interference control is a cognitive function closely linked to directed attention and comprises three types: stimulus interference, response interference, and multisource interference. These types differ in their relationship with directed attention. However, whether natural sounds produce differential effects on distinct types of interference control remains unclear. The present study employed electroencephalography to examine the effects of natural sounds such as birdsong with gentle wind on distinct types of interference control. Thirty-nine participants performed the multi-source interference task while listening to either birdsong with gentle wind or an urban sound dominated by machine noise, with electroencephalography recorded simultaneously. Behavioral results showed no significant differences between the two sound stimuli across any type of interference control. Neurophysiological results revealed that birdsong with gentle wind significantly enhanced alpha oscillations, N200, and N450 amplitudes in the stimulus interference condition, whereas no significant changes in any neural measure were observed in the response interference or multisource interference conditions. Exploratory correlation analyses suggested that the enhancements of N200 and N450 were correlated with behavioral improvement in stimulus interference. These findings indicate that birdsong with gentle wind selectively supports the resolution of stimulus interference, while it does not significantly modulate response interference or multisource interference in the current experimental conditions. This finding suggests that future soundscape design should reconsider the general utility of this type of natural sound and pay more attention to the alignment between the cognitive demands of the task context and its benefits. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Shared value vs plural values. Contesting renewable energy projects of the Enel Group
Abstract: The energy transition triggers urgent questions about what values are important, who controls transitional processes, and who has the power to define the answers to the climate crisis. Energy companies claim their central role in the development of renewable energy as the ultimate solution. However, communities affected by large-scale renewable energy projects have extensively raised environmental and social justice concerns and denounced the industry's poor practices and abuses.In this article, we analyse 15 socio-environmental conflicts around renewable energy projects owned by the Enel Group, one of the world's largest energy utilities, through the values and valuation languages of the affected communities. We map them onto five dimensions: environmental, health-related, socio-economic, ontological, and political. We build on environmental justice and ecological economics literature on valuation languages and employ counter-accounting to gather bottom-up evidence of grievances.We argue that, while the company claims that RE is the ultimate solution and the ‘Creating Shared Value’ approach is beneficial to all parties, those impacted by Enel's projects question the corporate model of energy transition and defend a plurality of values embedded in relational worldviews that are systematically misrecognised. We eventually criticise the corporate self-attributed moral and value-centred mandate in the energy transition and call for inclusive research about desirable energy futures rooted in plural and relational value systems. Authors: Wang Y.; Li X.
Title: Adaptive PSO for consensus optimization oriented to trust-consensus inconsistency correction and personalized guidance
Abstract: In social network group decision-making (GDM) based on fuzzy preference relations (FPR), trust among decision-makers (DMs) dominates the efficiency of opinion convergence. Traditional particle swarm optimization (PSO) has inherent drawbacks when applied to the consensus reaching process (CRP), and existing research has three limitations: static trust weights lack quantitative correction methods for trust-consensus inconsistency, unified consensus guidance fails to generate differentiated adjustment targets based on preference similarity and dynamic consensus contributions, the personal historical optimum of classical PSO becomes invalid, and undifferentiated global guidance easily traps the algorithm in local optima. This paper adopts PSO instead of other algorithms because of its one-to-one particle-DM correspondence, interpretable updating rules and good compatibility with multi-round CRP iterations. To retain PSO’s strengths and address the local optimum problem, a three module collaborative optimization framework is proposed, including the trust-consensus inconsistency correction mechanism, consensus-oriented adaptive weighted aggregation mechanism, and reconstructed improved PSO. The first module identifies inconsistent trust via bidirectional ranking of trust degrees and consensus levels to ensure trust weights match the consensus reliability of DMs. The second module constructs a dual aggregation structure driven by similarity and consensus to produce exclusive personalized guiding opinions for each DM. The third module reconstructs the PSO updating paradigm and adopts consensus progress adaptive inertia weights and learning factors to balance global exploration. The three modules operate in closed-loop collaboration: calibrating trust weights, generating customized guidance, and adaptively updating preferences. Experimental results indicate that the proposed framework achieves faster consensus convergence and lower adjustment costs under the tested settings, providing a promising intelligent solution for complex decision-making tasks in social network analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: X-MCB-Net: Explainable multimodal Cyberbullying Detection Network using Swin Transformer
Abstract: Cyberbullying on social media represents a persistent digital safety concern, often conveyed through the interplay of offensive text and images. Existing detection systems largely treat visual and textual modalities independently and offer limited interpretability, hindering deployment in accountable content-moderation workflows. This study presents X-MCB-Net, an explainable multimodal cyberbullying detection framework that integrates the Swin Transformer for visual feature extraction with XLM-RoBERTa and a bidirectional GRU for textual analysis. A dynamic intermodal attention mechanism fuses visual and linguistic representations to capture implicit and context-dependent cues for abuse. The core novelty lies in the joint design of adaptive cross-modal fusion and explainability-aware attribution, enabling both high detection performance and transparent decision support for human moderators. Evaluated on 5790 annotated image–text pairs from the Multimodal Cyberbullying Detection Dataset, X-MCB-Net achieved 98.8% accuracy and 96.6% F1-score under stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Explainable AI (XAI) visualizations identify the image regions and text tokens that drive each classification decision, supporting auditability and moderator trust in automated online safety systems. Title: Non-progressive influence maximization in temporal social networks
Abstract: The influence maximization (IM) problem involves identifying a set of key individuals in a social network who can maximize the spread of influence through their network connections. In this paper, we focus on the temporal non-progressive IM problem, which considers the temporal nature of real-world social networks and the special case where the influence diffusion is non-progressive, i.e., nodes can be activated multiple times. While influence diffusion in many real-world social network scenarios is non-progressive, such as in marketing campaigns promoting updated products and public health campaigns promoting healthier lifestyle choices, this problem has received limited attention in prior research. We first extend an existing diffusion model to capture the non-progressive influence diffusion in temporal social networks. We then propose a method, named TNIMRL, which employs deep reinforcement learning and temporal graph embedding to solve the temporal non-progressive IM problem. In particular, we propose a novel algorithm that effectively leverages temporal graph embedding to capture the changes in temporal social networks and seamlessly integrates with deep reinforcement learning. The extensive experiments on different types of real-world social networks demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Ltd. Title: ACOPI-QGen: Implicitness-aware joint quintuple extraction for aspect-based sentiment analysis via contrastive and graph-based modeling
Abstract: In social media and online reviews, sentiments are often expressed implicitly through contextual, figurative, or indirect language, making them difficult to capture using traditional Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) techniques. Many prior studies on ABSA treat implicit aspects and opinions as auxiliary cases or evaluation subsets, limiting their role during learning. To address this limitation, we propose ACOPI-QGen, a joint structured framework that extracts a five-element sentiment quintuple (Aspect Term, Aspect Category, Opinion Term, Polarity, Implicitness). Rather than treating implicitness as a post-hoc attribute, we model it as a supervised four-class variable: EAEO, EAIO, IAEO, and IAIO, where A/O denote aspect/opinion and E/I denote explicit/implicit realization. The proposed framework combines BERT-based contextual encoding, Supervised Contrastive Implicit Learning, and a Relational Graph Attention Network guided by a Surrogate Aspect-Opinion Dependency Tree to support implicit sentiment modeling when aspect or opinion spans are missing. A non-autoregressive set decoder uses parallel tuple queries to predict multiple candidate sentiment quintuples while preserving aspect-opinion alignment. We curate three datasets for quintuple extraction (Restaurant-ACOPI: 2584; Laptop-ACOPI: 4376; and Shoes-ACOPI: 3896 instances). ACOPI-QGen achieves Exact Match F1 scores of 55.68, 48.43, and 60.49 on Restaurant-ACOPI, Laptop-ACOPI, and Shoes-ACOPI, respectively, with corresponding improvements of 2.92, 2.53, and 5.45 absolute F1 points over the best-performing state-of-the-art models across the three domains. Authors: Acierno S.G.; Apuzzo C.; Lancia A.; Erto A.
Title: Critical assessment of the multifaceted impact of in-situ water removal on CO2 hydrogenation to methanol in membrane reactors
Abstract: The thermodynamic limitation of CO2 hydrogenation to methanol remains a bottleneck for intensified e-methanol production. A kinetic–thermodynamic analysis assessed the potential of in-situ water removal for enhancing methanol synthesis and whether the theoretical benefits of selective dehydration can be preserved under realistic membrane-separation conditions. A catalytic packed-bed reactor (PBR) was adopted as a reference system, followed by an idealized point-wise water-removal benchmark and zeolite membrane-assisted reactor configurations with different transport characteristics. The reaction system was described using a one-dimensional pseudo-homogeneous plug-flow coupled with the Vanden Bussche–Froment kinetic model for methanol synthesis over a Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalyst. Membrane-assisted configurations combined reaction kinetics on the retentate side with permeance-based membrane transport. A highly water-selective NaA membrane and a steam-selective SOD-type membrane with appreciable reactant co-permeation were considered to evaluate the impact of non-ideal permeation and reactant losses. The reference PBR exhibited the trade-off between increasing CO2 conversion and enhanced CO formation at higher temperatures. The idealized benchmark showed that selective dehydration can relax equilibrium constraints and enhance methanol yield, particularly at high water-removal levels. However, comparison with realistic membrane-assisted systems revealed that these gains depend on the balance between water removal and reactant retention. The NaA membrane provided the best performance, achieving a methanol yield of 23.8% at 250 °C and ΔP = 30 bar, whereas SOD-based configurations suffered from H2 and CO2 co-permeation losses that partially offset benefits of water extraction. Overall, membrane-assisted methanol synthesis is advantageous only when water-removal capacity is balanced by sufficient reactant retention within the catalytic environment. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Evolution and Uses of Rock Art Sites: Contribution of Morphogenic Mapping of Rock Walls
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: In this article, we present a new method for investigating rock art within the framework of site morphogenesis. Although numerous surveys of paintings and engravings have been conducted in archaeology since the twentieth century, few have taken into account the geomorphological characteristics of rock surfaces and their morphogenic evolution. Yet the processes responsible for these transformations directly interact with rock art. This approach therefore raises several questions: have the sites and their rock surfaces always been accessible? If not, from when until when were they accessible? Beyond parietal paintings and engravings, are there other traces of human activity? How are these related to the rock art? The method developed, based on the general geomorphological ground mapping’s codes, has been adapted for the analysis of painted and engraved rock walls at different spatial scales. The results demonstrate the relevance of such morphogenetic analysis of rock walls for the understanding of painted and engraved archaeological sites. At Rocher du Château (France, Savoie), phases of the rock wall’s evolution have been identified, which enable discussions about Neolithic and proto-historic frequentations contemporaneity with rock paintings, and their accessibility through time. At Bruguier rock shelter (France, Gard), seven phases of human activity, that are not visible on the ground, and numerous modifications were identified on the rock wall. The methodological and cartographic framework presented in this paper is grounded in an integrative approach to the study of evolving rock walls. Geomorphological analysis sheds light on the physical changes affecting the rock wall before, during, and after (pre)historic human occupation, while the cartographic framework is intended to be further developed through interdisciplinary collaboration. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Adaptive time-period discretization for multi-period scheduling of gaseous energy systems in steel enterprises
Abstract: Multi-period scheduling of gaseous energy systems in steel enterprises commonly relies on Equal Time-Period Discretization (ETPD), which involves an inherent trade-off between discretization accuracy and computational efficiency. Coarse discretization may accumulate storage deviations and cause safety violations, whereas fine discretization significantly increases the computational burden. To address this issue, this study proposes Adaptive Time-Period Discretization (ATPD), a time-representation and inventory-safety enhancement framework that adaptively partitions continuous-time supply–demand parameters based on cumulative storage deviation. Specifically, ATPD decouples the adaptive parameter grid from the uniform decision-variable grid and incorporates the deviation bound as a compensation margin in the storage safety constraints, thereby directly linking discretization accuracy to physical safety. The proposed method is validated through a case study on oxygen and byproduct gas scheduling using real-world data from a steel enterprise. Compared with ETPD, ATPD achieves more accurate parameter fitting, eliminates storage safety violations via deviation-bound compensation, and improves computational efficiency by over tenfold while maintaining a comparable model size. The results demonstrate that ATPD effectively balances discretization accuracy, storage safety, and computational efficiency in gaseous energy scheduling. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Beyond technological determinism: A multidimensional framework and research agenda for consumer trust in blockchain applications
Abstract: Blockchain technology is increasingly integral to domains such as finance, supply chain, commerce and tourism, yet consumer trust remains a pivotal barrier to its widespread adoption. Studies on trust in blockchain contexts have significant conceptual and contextual limitations that inhibit a holistic understanding of trust formation. In this study, we draw on the antecedents, decisions, outcomes and theory, context, methods (ADO-TCM) framework to systematically review 53 high-quality multidisciplinary studies. We identify three critical issues: (1) technological determinism that conflates technical capability with consumer trust, marginalising psychological, social and institutional factors; (2) theoretical convergence around acceptance models that obscures blockchain-specific trust phenomena; and (3) a narrow geographic and domain scope that creates self-reinforcing knowledge hierarchies limiting generalisability across applications and cultures. To address these gaps, we propose a multidimensional trust framework integrating three dimensions: technological architecture trust, information source trust and social actor trust, reflecting blockchain's sociotechnical structure. Central to this framework is a four-paradigm typology that classifies trust into interpersonal, technology, institutional, and sociotechnical perspectives, revealing that the prevalence of technological determinism reflects theoretical inertia rather than genuine consensus. We complement this with three research themes: multi-level theoretical integration, innovative methodologies and contextual expansion. This study contributes to the information systems discourse by providing a theoretical foundation for understanding trust in complex sociotechnical systems beyond acceptance models. By conceptualising consumer trust as a dynamic, multidimensional construct shaped by interactions between users, technology, and institutions, we offer a research agenda with actionable directions for advancing blockchain trust theory and practice. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Leveraging concept-cognitive learning to identify maximum s-defective cliques in network systems
Abstract: Detecting maximum s-defective cliques and cohesive subgraphs tolerating up to s missing edges is crucial for analyzing noisy and dynamic networks, but due to its NP-hardness, it remains challenging, leading to poor time efficiency and difficulties in dynamic scenarios. To address this problem, this study introduces a novel framework that leverages Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) under the paradigm of Concept-Cognitive Learning (CCL). This paper presents a theoretical proof that any maximum s-defective clique can be derived by expanding an equiconcept, which refers to a clique structure with equal intension and extension, and with at most s vertices, thereby ensuring detection completeness. Based on this, we develop two algorithms: a static method SFDC and an incremental method IFDC. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach typically achieves 10x to 100x speedups over state-of-the-art methods in both static and dynamic settings, with particularly strong performance in high-defect and dynamic environments. A case study further illustrates the practical utility of our method in extracting meaningful cohesive structures from real networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: The dark side of disrespect: How workplace incivility breeds service sabotage and turnover
Abstract: This study examines how different sources of workplace incivility affect frontline hotel employees. Drawing on Conservation of Resources Theory and Social Identity Theory, Study 1 compares the effects of employee incivility (originating internally) and customer incivility (originating externally) on emotional exhaustion. Based on a scenario-based experiment with 263 participants, the results show that employee incivility causes greater emotional exhaustion than customer incivility. Study 2 further differentiates in-group sources by their hierarchical level—supervisor, same-level colleague, and subordinate—and examines their specific impacts on emotional exhaustion, which, in turn, affects sabotage and turnover intentions. Using survey data from 302 respondents, the findings reveal that same-level colleague incivility has the strongest negative impact, followed by supervisor, subordinate, and customer incivility. Perceived organizational support buffers these effects. The study contributes to workplace incivility research in collectivist and high power-distance cultures and offers practical implications for hotel management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: ViLID: Multimodal misinformation detection with complementary input- and rationale-level inconsistency signals
Abstract: Multimodal misinformation on social media platforms often exploits subtle inconsistencies between text claims and accompanying images, such as repurposing authentic images out of context. Traditional vision–language models (VLMs) optimized for similarity can overlook these discrepancies. To address this challenge, we introduce ViLID, a vision–language inconsistency detector that combines a raw multimodal pathway with complementary rationale-derived signals rather than relying on rationales alone. ViLID employs two complementary signals: an embedding-level inconsistency score and a rationale-level inconsistency score, derived from structured rationales generated by large language models (LLMs) for both text and images. This approach integrates explicit inconsistency features with fused multimodal representations and incorporates an alignment regularization term that reduces inconsistency on truthful pairs. We evaluate ViLID on Fakeddit and MMFakeBench. The full model achieves the strongest overall performance, while the ablation results indicate that rationale-derived signals primarily improve error balance and the preservation of truthful samples by reducing the over-flagging of benign mismatches. Lastly, we translate our model's scores into practical moderation operating points, illustrating relevant precision/recall/workload trade-offs that inform effective deployment strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
